# Internal Architecture

## System Overview

The Slack Channel Router is a two-way bridge between Slack and Claude Code sessions via Socket Mode + MCP HTTP (StreamableHTTP). The server runs the persona configuration last applied (`config.json.last-applied`, a byte copy of `config.json` recorded when it was applied; `config.json` itself at a start with no record) and holds one Slack connection per persona: a Socket Mode client plus a Web API client, built from that persona's own credentials file by the connection manager (`src/persona-connections.ts`). Each persona runs one Claude Code instance under agent-director, `cscb_<key>`, in its own working directory. Each Claude Code session connects to its own MCP Server instance and is matched to one persona by its working directory. One server runs every persona; a persona that can't come up stays down on its own while the others serve.

The server-wide switch `allow_invited_channels` picks one channel mode for every persona (README [Channel modes](../README.md#channel-modes)). In declarative mode (the switch absent or `false`) a persona serves the channels its `channels` lists, at each entry's `delivery`, and its destination is `permission_prompts`. In fungible mode (`true`) it serves every public or private channel its Slack app is a member of that is not externally shared, at the channel delivery its agent stores with `set_channel_delivery` (`channel-delivery.json`; `mentions` when nothing is stored), and its destination is `invited.permission_prompts` (`"dm"` when absent).

**Layering (b.deo SRI-1003).** CSCB never touches tmux, and never replicates agent-director: sessions, liveness, spawn and resume are agent-director's, and the server reaches a session only through it. There is one Claude session per persona, however many channels it serves, in either mode: fungible mode adds no session, no tmux, no agent-director call and no channel-membership lookup.

## Module Map

```
cli.ts                          CLI entry point — start/stop/clean_restart/credentials/clear-latch subcommands; the usage text is `CLI_USAGE_LINES`, one entry per subcommand, `clear-latch`'s being `CLEAR_LATCH_USAGE_ENTRY`. `start`, `stop` and `clean_restart` take every setting they use and their persona set from the configuration the server runs, through `readAppliedPersonaConfig` (`reload.ts`): the last-applied record beside the configuration file (`resolveServerConfigPath`, state directory from `resolveServerStateDir`) when it exists, else the configuration file. The CLI never writes a reload file or the retired-key record (`retired-keys.json`; it builds no retired-key store), never reads, writes, creates or removes the stored-choice file (`channel-delivery.json`; `cli.ts` imports nothing from `channel-delivery.ts` directly, b.deo SRI-401), and its process reads no Slack token and no credentials file (b.av2 SR-8.7 as amended by b.deo SRI-403, SRI-407; b.av2 SR-10.2). `credentials <persona>` (b.av2 SR-12 as amended by b.deo SRI-1101 to SRI-1110; the setup wizard's credentials command) finds the persona by name or key (`resolvePersonaTarget`) in the configuration file as it stands (`loadPersonaConfig`, never the record, so a persona declared but not yet confirmed is found), prints the persona and its `credentials_file`, and runs the packaged `scripts/write-credentials.sh` (`CREDENTIALS_SCRIPT_PATH`) with `bash` for that path on the operator's terminal (stdio inherited; SIGINT and SIGQUIT ignored while it runs, as a shell does for a foreground job), exiting with the script's status. It reads no configuration file or record, builds no agent-director client and writes or removes no file. `start` checks only that the config file or its last-applied record exists, spawns the daemon and waits for its startup outcome (see [start command](#start-command)). `stop --stop-bots` and clean_restart share a `teardownBots(personas, exit_timeout)` closure that runs one pause/status/kill teardown per persona of the config (SR-11 Event 12), addressing each persona's instance directly as `cscb_<key>` (`personaInstanceId`); log lines name the persona as its JSON-quoted name with its key (`renderPersonaRef`). `teardownPersona` answers the persona's outcome (`PersonaTeardownOutcome`, `cli-teardown.ts`) and never throws for an agent-director answer: it decides its `status` reads with `stateReadVerdictOf` and each `pause` answer by class with `pauseVerdictOf` (b.jg5 SRJ-903), makes its kill through `teardownKill` (b.jg5 SRJ-904, SRJ-702, SRJ-110): one bounded retry (`runKillRetry`, `kill-retry.ts`) whose every try is one checked kill (`checkedKill`, `checked-kill.ts`) under `TEARDOWN_KILL_OPTIONS` (a GONE answer is a non-success), seeded with the state the path last read, its `status` read between tries mapped by `teardownKillReadOf`, a CONFIG read ending the tries whatever state was last read (`TEARDOWN_KILL_RETRY_OPTIONS`, `configReadEndsTries`), its lines through `console.error` (stderr; `clean_restart.log` for `clean_restart`, which has redirected it) with the prefix `[slack] teardownBots: persona <ref>`, and its result mapped to the persona's outcome by `teardownKillOutcomeOf`. Only UNAVAILABLE is tried again: the three store names (`ErrSchemaMismatch`, `ErrSchemaMigrationRequired`, `ErrStoreOpen`) are UNCLASSIFIED and fail at once, never retried. It waits for the pause's tries, its poll and the kill's tries on the injected clock (`CliDeps.now`, `CliDeps.sleep`; b.jg5 SRJ-908), so a teardown ends within `teardownBoundMs`; it latches nothing, checks no latch before the kill (b.jg5 SRJ-503) and reads or writes no record. `teardownBots` waits for every persona to settle (`Promise.allSettled`), maps a teardown that rejects all the same to a failed outcome (`teardownRejectedOutcomeOf`), answers the outcomes in configuration order and never throws. `reportTeardown` then walks them in configuration order (b.jg5 SRJ-907, SRJ-909): each persona's report (`personaTeardownReportOf`, `cli-teardown.ts`) is printed, then appended to `server.log` (`CliDeps.appendServerLogLine(line, at)`, timed by `CliDeps.now`), then recorded in `startup-errors.log` (`CliDeps.recordStartupErrorEntry(classLabel, message)`), each write best effort: a failed write prints one `[slack] <command>: could not …` line, never changes the exit status and never blocks the other destinations. In production the two seams write `server.log` (`appendLogLine`, `logging.ts`) and `startup-errors.log` (`recordStartupError` with `logDir` and `omitStderr`) in `resolveServerStateDir()`; the server is stopped at that point, so the CLI writes `server.log` itself. A failed initialization or precheck stops neither the server nor any persona: the command prints its lines, the last `<command>: nothing was stopped`, and exits 1. Only after a passed precheck is the server stopped, then every persona torn down. `stop --stop-bots` never starts the server: a failed persona exits 1 with the server left stopped (b.jg5 SRJ-905). `clean_restart` starts the server when every persona stopped; after a failed teardown it first checks that agent-director answers (`agentDirectorAnswers`: one `directorList()` within `PRECHECK_TRIES` tries `PRECHECK_TRY_SPACING_MS` apart, any error a failed try) and starts the server if it does, or, if not, prints, appends to `server.log` and records one not-restarted alert (`cleanRestartNotRestartedAlert`, class `clean-restart-not-restarted`) with no start, then the last line and exit 1 either way (b.jg5 SRJ-906; [clean_restart](#clean_restart-sr-11-event-12) step 8). The precheck's tries, the pause's tries and the answer check share the exported `callWithCliTries(call, retry, sleep)`, the CLI's one "3 calls 2 s apart" loop on the injected clock. The CLI reads rows without latching, recording or clearing: it installs no conflict latch, configured-persona query or retired-key store, and neither the precheck's adapters nor the teardown's apply the row-read rule (b.jg5 SRJ-114, SRJ-115, SRJ-801). `createDirectorOps(getClient)` builds the six `director*` adapters (`DirectorOps`) over `getClient().get/readPane/status/pause/kill/list` (`DirectorClient`); `directorGet` and `directorStatus` answer null only for `ErrSpawnNotFound`, recognised by class (`isAdErrorInstance`); `directorReadPane`, `directorPause` and `directorKill` pass every error through, `ErrSpawnNotFound` included, for the precheck or the teardown to classify. `directorKill` makes one plain `kill` with `{ claude_instance_id }` alone, never with agent-director's finished-row option, and answers its result as given (`kill_sent` true, false or absent), so the teardown's checked kill is the one place that decides what a kill answered. `directorList` makes one `list` filtered by `SERVICE_LABEL` (`service=cscb`, `persona-identity.ts`) alone, answers its rows and passes every error through. The production init is the exported `initProductionClient(callTimeoutMs, gateOptions?, gateDeps?)`: `runStartupGate(gateDeps, { ...gateOptions, callTimeoutMs })`, throwing `StartupGateFailedError` with the outcome's class label, message and `refusalKind` on failure. `CliDeps.initClient(callTimeoutMs, gateOptions?)` takes `InitClientGateOptions` (every `StartupGateOptions` field but the call timeout); only `stop --stop-bots`'s call passes any, `{ skipPhase1Floor: true }` (b.jg5 SRJ-203, SRJ-902), and `clean_restart`'s passes the call timeout alone, so it runs the whole gate. `stop --stop-bots` decides an initialization failure by `refusalKind` alone (`isClientTooOldRefusal`: a `StartupGateFailedError` whose kind is `REFUSAL_KIND_CLIENT_TOO_OLD`), never by its class label or message: on the client's too-old refusal it stops the server alone and ends with `onlyServerStoppedLine()`; any other failure stops nothing. The same `clientFor` and the applied-persona lookup (`getAppliedPersona`) go to the notifier, the MCP tools, the permission poller, the event router's click path and the archive's per-persona name resolver. Right after it, one destination hold (`personaDestinationHold`, `createPersonaDestinationHold` from `persona-destination-hold.ts`) is built at module scope over that resolver, `getAppliedPersona`, `clientFor` and the real clock, also side-effect-free (no Slack call, no timer), and goes to both as `destinationHold`, so one persona's prompts and notices share one failure episode; shutdown drops its held notices and timers with `cancelAll()`. one try, since the run read the row dead) and answers its outcome, latching the persona on a CONFLICT or an UNUSABLE NAME (see Auto-Restart step 4), the reconnect adapter (`_buildReconnectSessionAdapter`) defers a `working` row while `isLaunchInFlight(key)` or while its one `read-pane` of the row gives no proof (it probes no tmux session for any row: its prompt-row verdict also reads the row through one one-line `read-pane`), and a `pending` row through `deferPendingRow` (see Auto-Restart step 3); each of its escalate-dead answers (the reconnect's `dead-session`, `escalateRowWithNoPane`'s `working`, `waiting` and prompt-row verdicts, and the prompt row's 10-minute sweep with `row-read-finished`) carries the verdict it swept with (`escalateDeadWith`, `ReconnectEscalateDead`, b.jg5 SRJ-611), and `main()`'s `initRestart` `launchSession` binding passes that verdict on to the session manager's `launchSession` as `{ canLaunch, deadEvidence }`, and the liveness adapter (`_buildIsSessionAliveAdapter`) answers a liveness reading (`live`, `pending`, `dead` or `unknown`, `liveness-reading.ts`; a `pending` reading carries the row's raw launch start when the `status` result shows one), not a boolean, deciding `status` errors by class (see Auto-Restart step 3); it and the reconnect adapter apply the session manager's own-row `status` step (`applyOwnRowStatusStep`) after their own `status` call, and an answer that latched the persona (a configured persona's own row reading `pending` with no launch start included, b.jg5 SRJ-513) reads `unknown` at the liveness adapter and makes the reconnect adapter answer `'transient'` with nothing typed and no `deferPendingRow` hand-off. `deferPendingRow(key, launchStartedAt?, appliedPersona?, options?)` (exported `@internal`, async) is the `pending` deferral (b.jg5 SRJ-314, SRJ-409, SRJ-411, SRJ-410): it logs one line, naming the launch start when one was read, then, for the applied persona with the key, runs the session manager's `readAndStepPendingRow` (one `get`, then a covered or undecided row armed pending-only, an uncovered one sent through the live-row sequence), logs one line for a row read in another state, no row or a refused read, and answers `'pending'`, with nothing typed and nothing counted ([Auto-Restart](#auto-restart), **`pending` rows**). Only at a retry of the persona's timer (`isInsideTimerRetry`) and unless `DeferPendingRowOptions.mayRunRule` is false (the reconnect adapter's deferral), a covered row gets the pending-row rule's one run (`runPendingRowRuleAtRetry`), and a row the rule or the step's `get` reads `ended`, `missing` or gone makes it answer that `DeadRowRead` with one line (`deferringPendingRowGoneLine`; `DeferPendingRowAnswer` is `'pending' | DeadRowRead`). `_buildReconnectSessionAdapter` takes the same applied-persona lookup as its third argument (default `getAppliedPersona`) and hands it to the deferral. `main()` wires `RestartDeps.armRetryTimer` to the UNAVAILABLE retry controller's `arm` with the `read-error` cause, `RestartDeps.deferPendingRow` to `deferPendingRow`, returning its answer, passing the reading's launch start, the retry action's `stepPendingRow` to the session manager's `retryPendingRowStep(key, getAppliedPersona(key))`, and adds to `onCapReached` the stop of the persona's retry timer with `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_CAPPED` (b.jg5 SRJ-305), after the cap notice and the unclassified-error episode's end, each isolated. At module scope the server keeps two in-flight bindings (b.jg5 SRJ-303, SRJ-315, SRJ-401): "blocks a retry", `isPersonaRetryBlocked(key)` (true exactly when the session manager's `personaRetryBlockCause(key)` names a cause: a launch call, a running live-row sequence, b.jg5 SRJ-706, or an old-life wait step for a hold the persona waits on, b.jg5 SRJ-811), which `main()` gives the UNAVAILABLE retry controller as `isInFlight`, with `personaRetryBlockCause` as `retryBlockCause` (the ErrInvalidFlags hold's retry at once passes it to `runRestartRetry` too); and "in flight for P", `isPersonaWorkInFlight(key)`, built from it (`isPersonaRetryBlocked(key) || isDialogApproverRunning(key)`), which goes to the health tick's in-flight member, the lost-message routing's read gate (`isWorkInFlight`) and the `tmux-unavailable` retry check (`armMissingTmuxUnavailableRetry`). The kill adapter and the reconnect verdicts keep `isLaunchInFlight`: they act on rows that are not `pending`. Right after the UNAVAILABLE retry controller, `main()` builds the one live-row sequence registry (`createLiveRowSequenceRegistry`, `live-row-sequence.ts`, b.jg5 SRJ-706) over `buildLiveRowSequenceDeps` (the retry controller as its arm, the system clock, `console.error` and the applied configuration read at each call) with `runDetachedRecoveryAttempt` as its attempt runner, keeps it in the module holder `liveRowSequences` and installs it in the session manager (`setLiveRowSequenceRegistry`) before the start pass; a no-launch request (the old-life wait) runs through its `runOutsideAttempt`, `runOutsideAttempts`. Right after that install, `main()` installs the pending-row rule (`setPendingRowRule`, b.jg5 SRJ-410): `createPendingRowRule(buildPendingRowRuleDeps({ appliedPersona: getAppliedPersona, episodes: <the notice episodes>, log }))` with `serialize: personaLifecycle.run` and `gate: retryRunGate` (the one `RetryRunGateDeps` object whose six bindings, applied persona, relaunch gate, cap, shutdown, latch and `ErrInvalidFlags` hold, are spread into `createFullModeRetryAction`), before the start pass ([The pending-row rule](#the-pending-row-rule-bjg5-srj-410)). Right after it, `main()` installs the old-life wait's bindings (`setOldLifeWaitBindings`, b.jg5 SRJ-811, SRJ-812, SRJ-1512): the retry controller as the waiting personas' arm, the system clock, the server log, the applied configuration read at each call, the one kill-failure alerts instance, `recordStartupError` and the wait's own unclassified-error episodes (`createOldLifeWaitUnclassifiedErrors`, built just before over the alert threshold in effect and kept in the module holder `oldLifeWaitUnclassifiedErrors`, which shutdown closes; b.jg5 SRJ-313). The `/clear-latch` route (`CLEAR_LATCH_ROUTE`, after `/interject` and before the 404) likewise calls `handleClearLatch` (`clear-latch.ts`) with the caller's address, the applied persona config and `clearByHand`, the one `clearByHandOf(latchRecheck)` `main()` builds right after `bindLatchRecheck` (b.jg5 SRJ-510; see [POST /clear-latch](#post-clear-latch)).     ├── config.ts               The persona configuration loader — load, validate, defaults, tilde expansion. SR-4.1 agent_director_poll_interval_ms field. b.jg5 SRJ-213 `agent_director_call_timeout_ms` field, server-wide only: a positive integer in [`MIN_AGENT_DIRECTOR_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS`, `MAX_AGENT_DIRECTOR_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS`] = [1000, 3 600 000], default `DEFAULT_AGENT_DIRECTOR_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS` (60000); anything else is rejected with `agent_director_call_timeout_ms must be a positive integer in [1000, 3600000].`, the poll interval's range check (`checkPositiveIntegerInRange`) with its own bounds. `agentDirectorCallTimeoutMsOf(config)` is the pure accessor: the configuration's value, or the default when the configuration is null or undefined. SR-4.2 unknown-field rejection; `describeUnknownKeys` names an unknown key only when it matches `ECHOABLE_KEY_NAME_RE` (letters and underscores, up to 48 characters) and counts the rest, so a pasted token is never echoed (b.av2 SR-10.3 as amended by b.deo SRI-901 to SRI-906). **The channel modes (b.deo SRI-101 to SRI-105).** `allow_invited_channels` is a server-wide boolean (`ServerSettings`, default `false`), validated with the other server-wide settings before any persona (`allow_invited_channels must be a boolean.`). `CHANNEL_MODES` (`declarative`, `fungible`) and `ChannelMode` name the modes, and `channelModeOf(config)` is the one mode accessor: `fungible` exactly when the switch is `true`, `declarative` otherwise and when there is no configuration; every consumer reads the mode through it from the configuration in effect at each use. A persona entry's fungible section is `invited` (`PersonaInvitedInput`; its keys `PERSONA_INVITED_KEYS`, `permission_prompts` alone). Each configuration's entries are validated by the mode its own switch picks, candidate, record and start alike: declarative validation is the 0.11.1 rules and never looks at `invited`; fungible validation checks `invited` (shape, keys, `invited.permission_prompts` as `"dm"` or a channel ID, and the `dm` destination rule, worded "by default" when the value is absent) and never parses `channels` or the top-level `permission_prompts`; the cross-persona rules are the same in both modes. The resolved `Persona` carries the section in force: `channels` (empty in fungible mode), `permission_prompts: string | undefined` (undefined in fungible mode) and `fungible_destination` (the resolved `invited.permission_prompts`, `"dm"` when absent; undefined in declarative mode), plus `sections` (`PersonaSections`: the three section keys as written, unvalidated, in both modes). A destination is read from these fields only through the one destination rule (`personaDestinationOf`, `persona-destination.ts`), and `sections` only by the reload plan. The persona loader (b.av2 SR-1) is the only loader; the pre-persona keys appear only in the conversion-error check (`PRE_PERSONA_KEYS`). `parsePersonaConfigBytes(bytes, source, configDir, { home?, record? })` is the one validating JSON-parse path: it parses and validates the exact bytes that were read, so the bytes the reload controller records or applies are the bytes it checked (b.av2 SR-8.7 as amended by b.deo SRI-403). Record mode (`record: true`, used for the last-applied record) skips only the real-path collision step (b.av2 SR-1.5 as amended by b.deo SRI-104). The cross-persona rules include the prefix-related key rule (b.1ix follow-up): no persona's key may start with another's, checked by `personaKeysPrefixRelated`, with a new name for the persona with the shorter key from `suggestNonPrefixingName` (both exported, both pure); see the persona config section. `readPersonaConfigBytes` reads a file once and throws `PersonaConfigReadError` (with the errno code when it is safe to echo) on failure. It is stat-first, with the credentials check's rule: it opens the path read-only and non-blocking, stats the descriptor and reads only a regular file through it, so a FIFO or device at the configuration file or the record never hangs the start or the CLI. A directory fails with code `EISDIR`, any other non-regular file with `not a regular file` (`CONFIG_NOT_REGULAR_FILE_CODE`). It enforces the 64 KiB size cap (`MAX_RELOAD_FILE_BYTES`, worded `MAX_RELOAD_FILE_SIZE_TEXT`; code `EFBIG`, `FILE_TOO_LARGE_CODE`), shared with `readCredentialsFile`; its third argument, `ReadPersonaConfigBytesOptions` (`{ uncapped?: boolean }`), lifts the cap for three reads only: the file guard's, the retired-key record's (`loadRetiredKeyStore`) and the stored-choice file's (`loadChannelDeliveryStore`, b.deo SRI-403). See Configuration, Reload files, Size cap. `configReadFailurePredicate(code)` is the one wording of a read failure after a file's name (`does not exist`, `is larger than the 64 KiB limit`, or `cannot be read (<code>)`), used by the start's messages, the record error, the invalid candidate and the stale-confirmation line. Its file-system seam is `PersonaConfigFs` (default `DEFAULT_PERSONA_CONFIG_FS`), which lets tests fake a FIFO or a failing call; `loadPersonaConfig(path, home?)` is that read plus a default-mode parse. `configFileReadFailureMessage` builds the start's message for a configuration file that does not exist, is larger than the cap or cannot be read, and `isMissingConfigCode` says whether a read failure means the file is absent (ENOENT, ENOTDIR). A malformed-JSON error names the file and the line and column where the text stops being JSON (`json-position.ts`) and echoes none of the text. See "Persona config" under Configuration. `resolveServerStateDir(home?, env?)` and `resolveServerConfigPath(home?, env?)` are the one definition of the state directory (`SLACK_STATE_DIR` made absolute, else `<home>/.claude/channels/slack`) and of `config.json` inside it, read at call time; `server.ts` and `cli.ts` both use them, so the CLI and the server read one configuration file and one last-applied record beside it. `resolveDefaultCronTablePath(configDir, home?, env?)` is the one definition of the crontable's default, used when `cron_table_path` is absent or `null` (bug b.avm; the loader then sets `cron_table_path_defaulted`, a resolved-only flag that is never a configuration key, true exactly then and false for any path written, the default's own included): with `SLACK_STATE_DIR` unset, `<XDG config dir>/cscb/crontab`, where `resolveXdgConfigHome(home?, env?)` is an absolute `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (an empty or relative one is ignored), else `<home>/.config`, so `~/.config/cscb/crontab`, outside `~/.claude`; with it set, `legacyCronTablePath(configDir)`, `<config dir>/crontab`, the pre-b.avm default, so an install isolated by `SLACK_STATE_DIR` keeps its schedules with the rest of its state. The loader (`resolvePersonaConfig` and `parsePersonaConfigBytes`, whose environment is `ResolvePersonaConfigOptions.env`, `process.env` by default) and `main()`, for the start's crontable preparation (`cron-table-migration.ts`), both resolve the default and the old path through these, touching no file; the cron log's default stays `<config dir>/cron.log`. Exports `resolveRealPath` (b.av2 SR-1.5 as amended by b.deo SRI-104), the shared real-path-with-lexical-fallback comparison used by the persona collision rules (loader and bring-up checks), the stop-hook personal-config-dir refusal, the MCP session matcher and the file guard; see the persona config section. `SERVER_PATH_SETTINGS` is the one list of path-valued server-wide settings (`mcp_config_path`, `append_system_prompt_file`, `message_archive_db`, `claude_config_dir`, `cron_table_path`, `cron_log_path`): `resolveServerPaths` expands exactly these (a `satisfies` check keeps the two in step), and the reload change plan compares exactly these by real path. `tryResolveRealPath` is the same real-path lookup without the lexical fallback (undefined when realpath fails, never throws); `resolveRealPath` delegates to it, and `compareRowToPersona` (`session-manager.ts`) uses it to tell when a persona's working directory has no real path (b.av2 SR-6.4). `resolveRealPathStrict(path, fs?)` (bug b.g57) is the one for a persona's effective `claude_config_dir`, which may not exist yet: the real path when it resolves, else the nearest existing ancestor's real path plus the missing components when each fails with `ENOENT` and the first missing component does not exist either (with no symlink on the path that is the lexical form); a first missing component that exists (a symlink that points to nothing), any other error code (`EIO`, `ENOTCONN`, `ENOTDIR`, `ELOOP`, …) or no resolvable ancestor is unresolvable, returned with the errno code and never as the lexical form (realpath and lstat injectable, `StrictRealPathFs`; never throws, opens nothing). Also exports `credentialsFilesToProtect(appliedPersonas, configPath, home?)` (b.av2 SR-5.2), which lists every applied persona's `credentials_file` plus every `personas[i].credentials_file` named by the config file currently on disk (read through `readPersonaConfigBytes` with `uncapped`, one of the three reads the size cap does not cover, so an oversized unapplied file's paths are still protected; parsed tolerantly and not validated; an unreadable, non-regular or unparseable file adds nothing; never throws); the reload controller's `protectedCredentialsFiles()` calls it for `assertSendable` to refuse. The config-file half is `referencedCredentialsPaths(bytes, home?)`: every string `personas[i].credentials_file` in the given bytes or text, in declaration order with duplicates kept, tilde-expanded and made absolute; parsed but not validated, so a file that fails validation still names its paths, and unparseable JSON or a missing `personas` array yields none. Pure and never throws. It is the one extraction of referenced credentials paths, shared by the file guard and the reload detection tick's fingerprint, and the one documented exception to parsing only through `parsePersonaConfigBytes`: its parse is tolerant, discards any parse error rather than reporting it and returns only paths, so nothing it reads is recorded, applied or echoed. `replySettingsOf(config)`: the three server-wide reply settings (`ack_reaction`, `reply_chunk_limit`, `reply_chunk_mode`) of a config, defaults when absent or when the config is null; pure. `server.ts`'s `getReplySettings()` delegates to it.

see Configuration, Reload files). `createReloadController(deps)` takes every dependency injected, as `createCronScheduler` does: `paths`; `lifecycle`, whose `startBringUp(applied)` (the start pass), `teardown(persona)`, `updateInPlace(change)`, `reconnectCredentials(persona, applied)`, `refreshTemplate(applied)` and `bringUp(persona, applied, options?)` are all required (the default bodies of apply steps 2–6 call the last five; production binds them to `persona-lifecycle.ts`); `log` (the server log); `write` (default `durableWriteFileSync`); `remove` (default `durableUnlinkSync`, the durable delete of `config.json.pending` and `config.json.apply`); `retiredKeys` (the server's retired-key store, `retired-keys.ts`: production passes the one store `main()` loaded at start, which writes through `durableWriteFileSync`, the default `write` too, so a test builds it over the writer it gives here; `dryRun`; `heldCredentialsDigest(key)` (production binds the bring-up controller's `credentialsDigest`; without it credentials never count as changed); `bringUpState(key)` (production binds the bring-up controller's `state`; `credentialsFs` (the seam for the tick's credentials reads); `workingDirectoryFs` (the seam for the working-directory check of an added persona; the real file system by default); `checkConfigDir(persona)` (the `claude_config_dir` check of an added persona; production passes the session manager's `checkLaunchConfigDir`, the check the bring-up controller and every launch use, so the preview resolves the directory as the bring-up will; default `checkPersonaConfigDir` against `home` and the real file system); production never sets it, so the controller runs `lifecycleApplySlots` over `lifecycle`); and `home`. The handle has `resolveStart()` (synchronous, once: the start-time choice between the record and the configuration file, writing the record when there was none; see Server-Managed Startup step 2a), `runStartBringUp()` (once, after an applied start: `lifecycle.startBringUp` over the applied set), `startDetection()` (arms the detection tick once, and only after an applied start's bring-up pass has returned; returns whether it armed it), `stopDetection()` (stops it at shutdown; idempotent), `applied()` (the applied config, the exact bytes it was validated from and whether they came from the record or the file; after a confirmed apply's step 1, the confirmed candidate with source `config`) and `protectedCredentialsFiles()` (the SR-5.2 file guard's source; see Security Model). The detection tick (b.av2 SR-8.2, SR-8.3; b.av2 SR-8.7 as amended by b.deo SRI-403, SRI-407), the `config.json.pending` lifecycle, confirmation processing (SR-8.5) and the step runner of the confirmed apply (`applyConfirmed`, SR-8.6 as amended by b.deo SRI-805) live here; see [Reload Detection Tick](#reload-detection-tick-bav2-sr-82-sr-83). `configInEffect(startTime, applied)` (pure) is the configuration the server runs from an applied configuration, after an apply (`onApplied`) and for the start bring-up pass (`startBringUp`): the applied persona set and the applied `allow_invited_channels` switch over every other server-wide setting of the start-time configuration, so the switch is the one server-wide setting applied in place, from the step-1 swap (b.deo SRI-201, SRI-203), and any other changed server-wide setting takes effect only at the next start (the top-level `claude_config_dir` and `stop_hook_bootstrap` reach the personas only as inherited defaults, already resolved into each persona). The start-time configuration can differ from the controller's applied one in `cron_table_path` alone, when the start runs on the old crontable (bug b.avm, `cronTablePathForStart`); the controller's configuration is left as resolved, so detection compares `config.json` with it and never sees that difference. `readAppliedPersonaConfig(configPath, home?, fs?)` is the CLI's read-only resolver over the same rules: the record when it exists, else the configuration file; a record that exists but cannot be read or validated throws with the deletion hint and never falls back to the file. Each detection pass builds the change plan (`buildChangePlan`, `reload-plan.ts`) from the facts it gathered and writes and logs the preview rendered from it; the plan alone decides whether a credentials change is pending. `RELOAD_DIAGNOSTIC_CLASSES` (`reload-record-write-failed`, `reload-nothing-pending`, `reload-preview`, `reload-invalid`, `reload-applied`, `reload-noop`, `reload-stale-confirmation`) is the reload class list, kept apart from `PERSONA_DIAGNOSTIC_CLASSES`; `RELOAD_PREVIEW` and `RELOAD_INVALID` are defined in `reload-plan.ts`, and `RELOAD_APPLIED`, `RELOAD_NOOP` and `RELOAD_STALE_CONFIRMATION` in `reload-apply.ts`, all re-exported here. Importable without side effects (b.av2 SR-13.1): importing it creates no timer or Slack client, reads no file or environment variable and logs nothing, and the controller reads, writes and logs nothing until `resolveStart`, except `protectedCredentialsFiles()`, which reads the configuration file on each call (at any phase), uncapped, and writes and logs nothing; the detection tick reads, writes and logs only after `startDetection`. The record, the configuration file, the pending file and the confirmation are read only through `readPersonaConfigBytes` (the `configFs` seam), so a non-regular file cannot hang the start or a tick. Every one of those reads is capped except `protectedCredentialsFiles()`'s (see [Size cap](#reload-files-configjsonlast-applied-configjsonpending-configjsonapply)). The record is written only at a start without one and by a confirmed apply's step 1. Step 1 is one synchronous stretch over both stores (`applyConfirmed`): first, when a key the plan brings up (`added` or `destructive`) has an unwritten stored-choice drop, it writes the stored-choice record once (`writeUnwrittenDrops`; b.deo SRI-408), and a failed write logs `reloadChannelDeliveryWriteFailedLine(channelDeliveryPath, lastAppliedPath)` (class `reload-record-write-failed`) and applies nothing, so the change stays pending; then it records the retired keys, stops their approvers and rewrites the record as below, begins the old-life holds, drops the stored choices of every removed and destructively modified key in one batch with the reason `retired by a confirmed change` (b.deo SRI-406; a failed write is the store's own line and never fails the apply), marks each destructive modify's key as retiring (b.deo SRI-502), and swaps the applied set (`onApplied`). Step 2 then runs alone through `runApplySteps`, the retiring marks are cleared in a `finally` once it has settled, and steps 3–6 follow in a second `runApplySteps` call. A switch change alone puts no persona in any step: every session is kept (b.deo SRI-203). `retiredKeysToRecord(plan, store)` (reads only the store's queries) is the batch step 1 records: each removed persona's key (a key-changing rename's old key included) as `removed`, each destructive modify's key as `destructive-modify`, and each added persona's key (a key-changing rename's new key included) that the store holds only in memory, with the cause it holds; empty when there is none. `oldLifeHoldsToBegin(plan, applied)` (pure; b.jg5 SRJ-809) is the old-life holds step 1 begins once the last-applied rewrite has succeeded: one per removed persona's key (a rename's old key included) and destructive modify's key whose old declaration `applied` holds, in the plan's order, on `cscb_<key>` at the old declaration's working directory with the cause `apply-step-1`; the controller's required `oldLifeHolds` (`Pick<OldLifeHoldSet, 'begin'>`, production `main()`'s one set) begins them, a throw logged as `[slack] reload: beginning the old-life hold of <id> failed: <thrown value> (b.jg5 SRJ-809)`. The start resolution records no retired key. The start reads no credentials file; the detection tick reads each referenced one through `readCredentialsFile` (`persona-credentials.ts`), outside dry run. Beyond those reads, a pass runs the working-directory and `claude_config_dir` checks of each added persona and resolves the real path of a path written differently in the two configurations; it makes no Slack call itself (a confirmed apply's bring-ups do, through the lifecycle operations). Its lines go to the server log only, never to Slack.
    ├── reload-plan.ts          b.av2 SR-8.4 (as amended by b.deo SRI-803, SRI-804) / SR-8.6 (as amended by b.deo SRI-802) / SR-10.3 (part; as amended by b.deo SRI-901 to SRI-906); b.jg5 SRJ-1510 / SRJ-1511 (as amended by b.deo SRI-802) the change plan and the pending-change preview. `buildChangePlan(applied, candidate, facts)` classifies a candidate against the applied configuration in the terms of the SR-8.6 table (as amended by b.deo SRI-802): personas added (with why each cannot come up), removed, destructively modified, modified in place, with changed credentials, with next-launch changes (own or inherited) and unchanged, plus the changed server-wide settings (an inherited default lists the personas that inherit it). **By channel mode (b.deo SRI-802 to SRI-805).** A persona change is classified by the candidate's section in force (`channelModeOf(candidate)`), never the applied mode. When both configurations are in the same mode, the section in force is compared by resolved values (declarative: the set of channel IDs, a kept channel's `delivery` and `permission_prompts`; fungible: `fungible_destination`, so an absent `invited.permission_prompts` equals `"dm"`); when the switch changed, the keys of the section it turns on are compared as written (`sections`). A changed key of the section in force is in place (`IN_PLACE_SETTINGS`: `channels`, `delivery`, `permission_prompts`, `invited.permission_prompts`, `dm.enabled`, `dm.contact`; the `dm` keys in both modes). A changed key of the other section (`RECORDED_SECTION_KEYS`: `channels`, `permission_prompts`, `invited`; `RecordedSectionKey`) goes into `ValidChangePlan.recorded` (`RecordedPersonaChange`), never into an apply step: it counts in no header term, `noEffectiveChange` ignores it, a persona with recorded changes only stays in `unchanged`, and a recorded-only confirmation logs `reload-noop`. The switch (`MODE_SWITCH_SETTING`, `allow_invited_channels`; absent and `false` are equal) is a server-wide change carrying `ServerSettingChange.mode` (the mode it turns on) and `.personas` (every persona present in both configurations); a change of the switch alone modifies no persona. The candidate is a valid configuration, an invalid one with the loader's error, or a missing or unreadable configuration file. Every fact that needs I/O is injected as `facts`: `realPath` (required, the SR-1.5 comparison form (as amended by b.deo SRI-104)), `home` (for the default config dir), `dryRun`, the current and held credentials digests, `credentialsProblem(path)` (why the new credentials content is not locally valid, token-free), the bring-up state, the added personas' can't-come-up causes and `configDirProblem(persona)`, why a persona's changed effective `claude_config_dir` can't be resolved (asked only for a persona whose `claude_config_dir` changed, own or inherited, a destructive modify included). Such a persona carries `configDirUnresolvable` (the problem, or `FACT_UNKNOWN`), and its line warns, as an added persona's does, without refusing anything: a next-launch line and a changed top-level `claude_config_dir` line end `; but at that launch <it|the inheriting personas> cannot come up: <problem>`, a `DESTRUCTIVE:` line `; but it cannot come up: <problem>` (bug b.g57). A credentials change carries `credentialsBroken`, `retrying` and `problem`, and its line states the real effect for each state. A fact the caller could not gather is passed as `FACT_UNKNOWN` and carried as unknown (an added persona's `cannotComeUp`, or a credentials change's `credentialsBroken` and `retrying`, is undefined), and the preview says it could not be checked. `isCredentialsBroken(state)`, re-exported from `persona-bringup-controller.ts`, is the SR-6.4 credentials-broken rule the plan applies to the bring-up state; the apply's steps 4 and 6 use the same rule. A persona whose first Slack attempt is still in flight (no outcome yet) counts as `retrying`. `configDirsChanged` tells the apply to refresh the agent-director template (SR-8.6 step 5 as amended by b.deo SRI-805); the apply selects step 5 whenever it is true, even for a plan with no effective change (`applyStepsFor`, `reload-apply.ts`). It is not rendered. The plan holds persona keys, names, entry positions, paths and setting names only, never a digest. `DESTRUCTIVE_SETTINGS`, `IN_PLACE_SETTINGS` and `NEXT_LAUNCH_SETTINGS` name each field's effect, `stop_timeout` and `exit_timeout`, the server-wide settings only the CLI uses, get their own server-wide line (the CLI takes them from the record once applied, `CLI_RECORD_SETTINGS`), and `agent_director_call_timeout_ms`, used by both the CLI and the server, gets a third (the CLI takes it from the record once applied, and the running server uses it from its next start, `CLI_RECORD_AND_SERVER_START_SETTINGS`); `addedPersonas(applied, candidate)` lets a caller gather facts about the added personas before building the plan. Renderers, all from the plan and never from a second diff: `changePlanCounts` and `renderChangePlanCounts` (the header's counts), `renderPreviewLines` and `renderPreview` (the body of `config.json.pending`), `renderPreviewLogLines` (the `reload-preview` log form) and `renderInvalidLogLine` (the one `reload-invalid` line). `modeSwitchLine(mode, personas)` renders the switch's own line (the mode turned on, applied in place at once, from the next event, tool call, prompt and notice, for each persona present in both configurations, or `no persona is affected`), and `recordedLine(p)` a recorded change's line (the keys changed in the section not in force, recorded with no effect until the switch selects that section); the preview puts recorded lines after the other affected personas and before the server-wide settings. `removedLine(persona)` and `destructiveLine(change)` render the two `DESTRUCTIVE:` lines (unescaped; `renderPreviewLines` escapes), each saying the persona will be retired: its session stopped and never resumed, and a destructive modify's brought up fresh, from the fixed clauses `REMOVED_RETIRED_CLAUSE` and `DESTRUCTIVE_RETIRED_CLAUSE` after `DESTRUCTIVE_PREFIX` (b.jg5 SRJ-1510), held in the import-free `reload-preview-clauses.ts` and re-exported here unchanged; no preview line says "destroyed". Defines `RELOAD_PREVIEW` and `RELOAD_INVALID`. Pure and deterministic (b.av2 SR-13.1): no file, Slack, agent-director, timer, log or state, nothing at import; the same plan always renders the same text. The reload detection tick builds the plan every pass (see [Reload Detection Tick](#reload-detection-tick-bav2-sr-82-sr-83)); a confirmed apply acts on the plan that pass built from the confirmed bytes, never a second diff, and its `reload-applied` line reuses the counts, so what is applied is what was previewed.

Imports nothing, and must stay so: the /ci-live runner loads it on the host, where importing `reload-plan.ts` would load the Slack SDKs (pinned by the source audit in `tests/ci-live-docker.test.ts`).

step 1 (write the stored-choice record when a key brought up has an unwritten drop, record the retired keys, stop their approvers, rewrite the record, begin the old-life holds, drop the retired keys' stored choices, mark the retiring keys, swap the applied set; a body that throws is reported to `onFailure` and the next step still runs; it never rejects. `applyStepNumber(step)` gives a step's SR-8.6 number (as amended by b.deo SRI-805) for log lines. `fanOutPersonas(personas, operation, onFailure)` runs one operation per persona at once and settles once every one has settled, never failing fast; a failure is an `ApplyPersonaFailure`): step 2 fans `teardown` out over `removed` and `destructiveOld`, step 3 fans `updateInPlace` out over `inPlace` (each an `InPlaceApplyInput`: the persona as confirmed, its previous declaration and the changed settings; one update per persona key), step 4 fans `reconnectCredentials` out over the credentials-changed personas (`credentials` and `credentialsBroken`) that are not credentials-broken when step 4 runs, step 5 calls `refreshTemplate` once with the confirmed configuration, and step 6 fans `bringUp` out over `added` and `destructiveNew` and, with `{ recovery: true }` (`ApplyBringUpOptions`), over the credentials-changed personas that are credentials-broken when step 6 runs and that step 4 did not reconnect, all with the confirmed configuration. "Credentials-broken now" is asked of `credentialsBrokenNow(key)` (`CredentialsBrokenNowQuery`) when each step runs; with no answer, the plan's split decides. A reconnect that resolves `{ kind: 'credentials-broken' }` (`CredentialsBrokenAtReconnect`) is left to step 6. A persona with only next-launch changes is in no body's input: step 1's swap is all it needs. Defines `RELOAD_APPLIED`, `RELOAD_NOOP` and `RELOAD_STALE_CONFIRMATION`. Pure (b.av2 SR-13.1): it reads and writes no file, calls neither Slack nor agent-director, arms no timer and logs nothing, and nothing runs at import; `runApplySteps` and the fan-outs only call and await the injected bodies, members and queries. Its only state is the default bodies' per-apply set of the personas step 4 reconnected, which step 6 reads. No output holds a token, credentials content, a digest or a fingerprint.

A content is the exact bytes or the `FINGERPRINT_MISSING` / `FINGERPRINT_UNREADABLE` marker, and a marker never equals any bytes, an empty file included. Every write writes the whole record held in memory through `durableWriteFileSync`, and the record in memory changes only once the write succeeded; on a `DurableWriteUnsyncedError` the bytes the file held before are written back (or the file, absent before, removed), best effort. Two changes stay in memory after a failed write, flagged unwritten and carried by the next write that succeeds: the keys a failed batch recorded with the `absent-at-start` cause (`isHeldInMemory`; re-recording such a key writes the record even though it has no mark) and a failed mark. Directories are compared by real path at query time (`realPath`, `resolveRealPath` by default), the lexical path when it cannot be resolved. Imports nothing from agent-director; importable with no side effect.

A missing file is an empty, readable record. A file that cannot be read, parsed or validated is left in place, logs one `channel-delivery-unreadable` line (`channelDeliveryUnreadableLine(path, cause)`) and gives a store that is unreadable for the run (`readable` false): no stored choice applies, nothing is written or dropped, and the tool is refused; every member synchronous, so no two writes interleave): `path`, `readable`, `storedChoice(key, channel)`, `storedChannels(key)` (sorted), `record()`; `set(key, channel, delivery, declaration)` refuses a bad input or an unreadable store with no write, otherwise writes the whole record with the change through the writer and changes memory only once the write succeeded, answering `ChannelDeliverySetResult` (`CHANNEL_DELIVERY_SET_STORED`, `_UNREADABLE`, `_INVALID` with its `ChannelDeliverySetInvalidField`, `_WRITE_FAILED`); a drop only ever moves a channel toward `mentions`. `applyStartRules(start)` (`ChannelDeliveryStart`: the applied personas as `ChannelDeliveryAppliedPersona` and the retired-key store as `ChannelDeliveryRetiredKeyView`, its `isRecorded` and `isMarked` alone) drops, in one batch, the entries of a key that is not an applied persona's, then of a key whose recorded declaration differs from the applied one (`name` exactly, each path as written or by `resolveRealPath`), then of a key the retired-key record holds without its mark, each key once with its first reason, and runs nothing on an unreadable store. The bring-up lines are listed under Logging, Persona bring-up lines.
    ├── persona-credentials.ts  b.av2 SR-1.4 persona credentials-file reader, step 1 of the SR-6.1 bring-up. The file has a fixed shape: a JSON object with exactly two string keys, `bot_token` (prefix `xoxb-`) and `app_token` (prefix `xapp-`); each value has at least one character after its prefix and contains no whitespace or control character. `checkPersonaCredentials` finds it locally valid when it exists, is readable, parses and has that shape, and its real path is no other applied persona's credentials file. Checks run in this order: a real-path collision (`resolveRealPath`, lexical fallback) with another applied persona's credentials file makes the persona credentials-broken as `persona-credentials-invalid`, naming the other persona, and is checked first so the other persona's tokens are never parsed or used (the file is still read, stat-first, but only to hash it for the digest below); a missing path (ENOENT/ENOTDIR) is `persona-credentials-missing`; the path is then opened once, read-only and non-blocking (following symlinks), so opening a FIFO never waits for a writer, and the type check and the read both go through that one descriptor, so the file checked is the file read; anything but a regular file (a directory, FIFO, socket or device) is `persona-credentials-unreadable` and is never read, so a FIFO cannot block the read and a device cannot feed it for ever; a regular file over the size cap is `persona-credentials-unreadable` too (`credentials file is larger than the 64 KiB limit`; see Configuration, Reload files, Size cap), so its digest is the unreadable marker at bring-up and in the reload tick alike; the descriptor is always closed, and a close failure is ignored; permission denied or any other open, stat or read error is also `persona-credentials-unreadable`; content that is not JSON, not an object, lacks a key, has a non-string or wrongly prefixed value, a value with nothing after its prefix, a value containing whitespace or a control character, or any extra key is `persona-credentials-invalid`, with every problem listed. Causes name a bad token by its key and rule only; a parse failure is described generically and extra keys are counted, not named. Success returns a `PersonaSlackTokens` value that redacts itself when JSON-serialised, string-converted or inspected. All file access goes through an injectable seam (`openFile`, `fstatFile`, `readFileFd`, `closeFile`, `realpath`), with the real file system as the default; the names differ from the working-directory check's `stat` and `access` so an override of one in the combined bring-up seam never reaches the other. Nothing runs at import, and it reads no environment variable, writes nothing and checks no file mode. It is the server's only token source: step 1 of each persona's start bring-up (`checkPersonaLocalSteps` in `persona-start.ts`, run by the bring-up controller), which hands the tokens to the connection manager. It is read once per persona at start; bring-up retries reuse that read. Reader and digest (b.av2 SR-8.3): the stat-first open, type check and read above is its own export, `readCredentialsFile(path, fs?)`, returning the exact bytes or a missing/unreadable failure with its token-free cause; the seam's `readFileFd` returns bytes, decoded as UTF-8 only for validation. `credentialsDigest(read)` turns a read into what is held for it: `sha256:<hex>` over the exact bytes, or `CREDENTIALS_MISSING_MARKER` / `CREDENTIALS_UNREADABLE_MARKER`, which never equal a digest. `checkPersonaCredentialsAndDigest` returns the check's result beside the digest of what it read, valid or not. A real-path collision returns the digest too: the persona's own path is read stat-first and hashed, never parsed, and no token is taken from it, so re-saving the file can make a change pending for that persona once the collision is gone. `checkPersonaCredentials` is that check without the digest. The reload detection tick reads each referenced file through the same `readCredentialsFile`, so a FIFO or device never blocks a tick either. `credentialsReadProblem(read)` runs the content check over a read the caller already holds and returns the cause, worded as `checkPersonaCredentials` words it (the same `credentials file is invalid: ` prefix for bad content), or undefined when the file is locally valid; it skips the real-path collision rule and returns no token. The tick uses it to preview whether an added persona can come up without reading its file twice. A digest is held in memory only and never logged.
    ├── persona-bringup.ts      b.av2 SR-6.1 steps 1 and 2 as pure checks. `checkPersonaWorkingDirectory` (step 2) requires the working directory to exist, be a directory (after following symlinks), be readable and searchable, and have a real path that is no other applied persona's working directory. A missing path is `persona-directory-missing`; anything else, including a real-path collision (named with the other persona), is `persona-directory-unusable`. It reads no credentials file, so a dry-run bring-up can call it alone. `checkPersonaLocalBringUp` always runs both the credentials check and the directory check before returning, so when both fail both causes are reported: it returns both outcomes plus the failure list (credentials first) and, with an injected logger, emits each failure line exactly once. It also returns `credentialsDigest`, the digest or marker of the credentials bytes step 1 read, whatever step 1's outcome; for a real-path collision the persona's own file is only hashed, never parsed. It reuses `persona-credentials.ts`'s real-path collision and errno helpers rather than duplicating them. No Slack or agent-director call, no environment access, no writes, no timers, nothing at import; file access goes through an injectable seam (stat, access, realpath), and the combined check's seam also covers the credentials check's descriptor-based open, stat, read and close. The server runs them as steps 1 and 2 of each persona's start bring-up (`checkPersonaLocalSteps` in `persona-start.ts`, called by the bring-up controller): the combined check normally, the directory check alone in dry run. The controller also calls `checkPersonaWorkingDirectory` alone for each directory re-check. `checkPersonaConfigDir(persona, { home?, fs?, log? })` (bug b.g57) is the pre-launch check of the persona's effective `claude_config_dir` (none means `<home>/.claude`) through `resolveRealPathStrict`: `{ ok: true, realPath }` (a directory not created yet under a resolvable parent passes, with the real path it will have) or a `persona-config-dir-unresolvable` failure naming the configured directory and the errno code; it never throws. A failure also carries `problem`, its cause without the held persona's consequence (`claude_config_dir cannot be resolved to a real path (<errno>[: a symlink on its path points to nothing])`), which the reload preview words itself. The session manager runs it before every launch (`checkLaunchConfigDir`), the bring-up controller runs it right before each Slack step (bring-up and directory retry) and re-checks a held persona with it, and the reload detection tick runs it on each added persona.
    ├── persona-slack-validation.ts  b.av2 SR-3.2 classifier for a persona's Slack token validation: `auth.test` checks `bot_token`, opening Socket Mode checks `app_token`. Three outcome classes: up, Slack-unreachable (retried for ever with backoff) and credentials-broken. `botIdentityFromAuthTest` returns up only when `auth.test` gave both the bot user ID and the bot ID (SR-3.1); a result lacking either is Slack-unreachable. `classifySlackValidationError(error, check)` maps a thrown or rejected value to one of the two failure outcomes. Slack-unreachable (`persona-slack-unreachable`) covers a network, DNS or request-timeout error, a non-200 HTTP status (429 included), a rate-limited error, a `start()` whose WebSocket phase was abandoned after 10 s (the `SlackStartTimeoutError` marker, SR-3.3), no WebSocket URL, a socket closed before `hello`, any other Socket Mode error, any unrecognised value, and a `PlatformError` of `internal_error`, `fatal_error`, `service_unavailable`, `request_timeout` or `ratelimited`. A `PlatformError` whose Slack error code is missing, empty or not a short lower-case identifier is also Slack-unreachable (reason `unknown`): the library builds such errors itself from a 200 answer that isn't JSON, such as a proxy page. Only a `PlatformError` carrying a well-formed Slack error code outside those five is credentials-broken (`persona-credentials-refused`), carrying the key and the Slack error code. The "no WebSocket URL" reason applies only to the library's plain, code-less error from the Socket Mode open; any other code-less failure is reported as an unrecognised failure (reason `unknown`, still Slack-unreachable). An unreachable outcome carries a reason kind, plus the HTTP status, the transient Slack error code or `retryAfter` where they apply, and, when the thrown value had a message (an error's `message`, or a thrown string), that message rendered by `describeLogMessage` as `message`: `message="…"`, redacted by `redactSlackLogText`, on one line, capped at 300 characters (the rendering every other persona error line uses). CSCB's own timeout markers carry none. The cause text never holds error text. Library errors are recognised by their `code` field, never by `instanceof`, so stub errors classify the same way. The classifier never throws. `slackRetryAfterSeconds(error)` reads the `retryAfter` a rejected Web API call carries (the library's rate-limited error, or a platform error whose code is `ratelimited`), copying nothing else; the classifier and the destination hold both use it. Waits come from `persona-retry-schedule.ts` (5 s doubling to 300 s, no cap, never shorter than `retryAfter`) and log lines from `persona-slack-episodes.ts`. Pure and injectable (SR-13.1): no timers, clock, Slack client, I/O or environment access, nothing at module scope. The connection manager (`persona-connections.ts`) calls it for every attempt. `classifyWebApiAuthFailure(error, method)` (bug b.ujn) is the running-persona counterpart used by `persona-web-api-watch.ts`: a refused outcome of the `web-api` check (`bot_token`) only for a platform error whose Slack error is exactly `invalid_auth`, `token_revoked`, `account_inactive` or `not_authed`, undefined for anything else. Its cause names the method when it matches `SLACK_METHOD_NAME_RE`, e.g. `bot_token refused by a Web API call (chat.postMessage): Slack error token_revoked`. It copies nothing from the error but the Slack error code.
    ├── persona-retry-schedule.ts  b.av2 SR-3.2 backoff for the Slack-unreachable class. `createPersonaRetrySchedule` returns one independent schedule per persona and retry purpose; it holds only its own failure count. `nextDelayMs(retryAfterSeconds?)` records a failure and returns the next wait in milliseconds: 5 s doubling to a 300 s ceiling (5, 10, 20 … 300 s), with no attempt cap. When a `retryAfter` is given the wait is never shorter than it, clamped only at the largest delay a JavaScript timer honours (about 24.8 days). `reset()` returns to 5 s once the cause clears. The arithmetic is `backoff.ts`'s stateless `doublingBackoffDelay`; the session-restart counters (keyed by persona key), 900 s ceiling and 5-failure cap are not used. Returns waits only: no timers or clock, so the caller schedules through its injected timers (SR-13.1). The connection manager (`persona-connections.ts`) keeps one per persona for bring-up retries and Socket Mode reopens, and one per pending credentials reconnect, the bring-up controller (`persona-bringup-controller.ts`) one per persona for working-directory re-checks, and the destination hold (`persona-destination-hold.ts`) one per persona for destination retries.
    ├── persona-slack-episodes.ts  b.av2 SR-10.3 (as amended by b.deo SRI-901 to SRI-906) cause-start / cause-clear latch for Slack validation log lines, so `persona-slack-unreachable` is logged when the cause starts and when it clears, not on every attempt. `createSlackEpisodeTracker` takes one persona (name, key, entry position, credentials-file path, optional logger) and `record(outcome)` returns the lines it produced; `end(reason)` closes an open episode without an outcome (the attempts it covered were abandoned, such as a cancelled credentials reconnect) with one line carrying its class label and the cause `cleared: <reason>`, and does nothing when none is open. An episode is a run of outcomes of one class. When an episode starts it emits one line (`persona-slack-unreachable`, or `persona-credentials-refused` naming the key, check and Slack error code). When it ends, because the persona comes up or the class changes, it emits one cleared line with the same class label and a cause starting `cleared: `. A change of reason within Slack-unreachable stays in the same episode. A third episode kind, connection lost, opens when a connection that was up drops: it emits one `persona-connection-lost` line, absorbs every Slack-unreachable reopen outcome without a line, and closes with one `persona-connection-restored` line when the persona is up again; a refusal during it ends it silently and emits the `persona-credentials-refused` line in place of the restored line. Lines are built by `formatPersonaDiagnostic` from the outcome's own fields; a `persona-slack-unreachable` start line ends with the outcome's redacted `message` after the cause when it has one, and no cleared, lost or restored line carries one. With an injected logger each is emitted exactly once. No module-scope state or timers, so two personas' trackers are independent. The connection manager (`persona-connections.ts`) drives it, one tracker per persona plus one for each pending credentials reconnect, and is the only emitter of these lines for its personas, except that the bring-up controller logs a later refusal of a reconnect left retrying (see [Credentials change](#credentials-change-bav2-sr-86-step-4-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-805)). A connection stopped and brought up again gets a fresh tracker.
    ├── persona-slack-clients.ts  b.av2 SR-3.3 / SR-13.1 Slack client factory and option sets for persona connections. Three client kinds, each built through the injectable `PersonaSlackClientFactory`: the long-lived Socket Mode client (app token); a short-lived validation Web API client used only for `auth.test` (bot token); and the long-lived Web API client every posting path uses (bot token), including `reply` uploads and `download_attachment`. Settings, in prose: library auto-reconnect is off on the Socket Mode client. The Socket Mode client's own Web API calls and the validation client make no retries, time out after 10 s and reject rate-limited calls instead of waiting. The long-lived Web API client times out each attempt after 30 s and keeps the library's default retry policy (ten retries with randomised backoff over about 30 minutes) and its rate-limit waiting. None of the three attaches the original request to its errors. Library loggers: the Socket Mode client gets `socketModeSlackLogger(persona, log)` in place of the library's console logger; it drops every line except an explicit list of the library's fixed-text connection-health lines (ping and pong timeouts, and `Failed to send ping to Slack` with its error detail dropped), which it hands to the connection manager's `log` as `[slack] persona Socket Mode: personas[<i>] "<name>" (key=<key>): <text>`, at or above the level the library sets (default INFO); a throwing sink is swallowed. The socket client's own `clientOptions` (for `apps.connections.open`) carry no logger, so that client inherits the socket's. The validation and long-lived Web API clients get `redactingSlackLogger()`, which writes to the console as the library's console logger does (`[LEVEL]  web-api:WebClient …`, default INFO) after replacing URL-like substrings with `<redacted-url>` and token-like ones with `<redacted-token>` in every argument (non-strings via `util.inspect`); `redactSlackLogText` is the redaction, and its token pattern is deliberately wide. Why: the library defaults reconnect and retry on their own (the socket client retries opening up to 100 times), set no request timeout, and attach the raw request error, Authorization header included, to request errors; under Bun the socket library prints a failed WebSocket handshake's error text, which holds the WebSocket URL with its connection ticket, at its default level into `server.log`; and a Web API client's failed-request line on a 429 holds the request URL, which for a `filesUploadV2` upload is Slack's short-lived upload URL. Each option builder returns a fresh object, so no option object is shared between clients or personas. `PRODUCTION_SLACK_CLIENT_FACTORY` is the only place a token is handed to a Slack library, and it passes the token and options through unchanged. Also holds the 10 s `start()` bound and the 10 s / 30 s request-timeout constants. Also holds the integration suite's Slack API base URL override (see `CSCB_SLACK_API_URL` under Environment Variables): `resolveSlackApiUrlOverride(env, log)` reads it and `loopbackSlackApiUrl` decides whether it is honoured; each option builder takes an optional `slackApiUrl` and, given one, adds it and changes nothing else (the socket client carries it inside its `clientOptions`). Nothing is constructed, read or logged at import; the environment is read only through the `env` passed to `resolveSlackApiUrlOverride`, and the loggers built here write only when a client calls them.

    ├── persona-connections.ts  b.av2 SR-3.1 (module part) / SR-3.2 / SR-3.3 / SR-3.4 / SR-10.3 (as amended by b.deo SRI-901 to SRI-906) / SR-13.1 supervised per-persona Slack connection manager. Per persona, `createPersonaConnectionManager` validates, then connects: a short-lived validation client runs `auth.test` and is discarded, then one long-lived Web API client and one long-lived Socket Mode client are built. The three client kinds and their settings are in the `persona-slack-clients.ts` entry. A persona is up only once `auth.test` returned both the bot user ID and the bot ID and the socket's `start()` resolved. The manager bounds a bring-up's `auth.test` at 10 s on its injected clock (`SLACK_AUTH_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS`), because the validation client's own request timeout starts only once the connection is made and so does not cover a DNS or TCP-connect stall; on expiry the call is abandoned and the attempt is Slack-unreachable (`SlackAuthTestTimeoutError`, reason `timeout`). Each `start()` bounds its WebSocket phase at 10 s; one that never settles is abandoned and counts as Slack-unreachable, not broken. Slack-unreachable is retried with the `persona-retry-schedule.ts` backoff; a refusal leaves the persona credentials-broken. Reopen: when an up persona's socket drops and the manager didn't close it, the first reopen attempt is immediate and later ones use the same backoff; a credentials error on reopen leaves the persona disconnected and credentials-broken. **Revoked bot token while running** (bug b.ujn): the socket runs on the app token, so a revoked bot token would leave it up while every Web API call fails. Every long-lived Web API client the manager hands out is therefore wrapped by `watchWebClientAuth` (`persona-web-api-watch.ts`). The first call on it rejected with `invalid_auth`, `token_revoked`, `account_inactive` or `not_authed` latches that client, and, when it is still the persona's current client (a client replaced by a reconnect swap, `replaceRetryTokens` or a fresh bring-up marks nothing) of a persona neither stopped nor already broken, marks the persona like a refused reopen, synchronously in that rejection's handler (`markRefusedWhileRunning`): its retry timer and any attempt in flight are cancelled, its live socket is detached (it forwards nothing more), one `persona-credentials-refused` line is logged with cause `bot_token refused by a Web API call (<method>): Slack error <code>`, and its status becomes `broken` (phase `running`). None of that waits for the per-persona serializer, so a lifecycle operation holding the persona's turn cannot delay it; only the detached socket's network close is submitted through the injected `serialize`, never awaited (`stop` closes it at once if its turn has not come). From then on the persona is not serving, so the server's client lookup (`createPersonaClientLookup`, `persona-start.ts`) hands out no client, and a call on a client already handed out is refused locally by the latch (`WebApiCallRefusedLocallyError`), never sent. The persona is not up, so the up predicate, the relaunch gate, MCP admission, the permission poller and `/interject` all refuse it. A pending credentials reconnect is left to finish; its swap brings the persona back up. Every event reaches the handler tagged with its persona's key, and a handler throw affects no other event or persona. All state lives in one entry per persona: no lock, queue or timer spans two personas, and no handling path reads another persona's connection. Dry run (SR-3.4) calls no factory method, needs no credentials and makes no Slack call: each persona is up at once with a distinct placeholder identity derived from its key (`dryRunPersonaIdentity`: `U000DRY_<key>` / `B000DRY_<key>`), and no Web API client exists. The Slack client factory, clock and timers are injected, as `createCronScheduler` takes its clock; nothing is created, read or scheduled at import. `server.ts` constructs one manager in `main()` with the event router as `onEvent`, the dry-run flag, the lifecycle serializer's `run` as `serialize` and a status listener composed of the up-flush listener and the bring-up controller's `onConnectionStatus` (reached through the module-scope `bringUps` holder, because the controller is built over the manager and so after it; the holder is set before anything connects), and each persona is brought up through the bring-up controller (`persona-bringup-controller.ts`) at start, or at a confirmed apply for an added persona. `stop(key, endReason?)` closes one persona's connection: its retry is cancelled, its clients closed, its status becomes `stopped` and its entry is forgotten. A persona teardown calls it with no reason, so nothing is logged for an open episode: no lost, restored or unreachable line (b.av2 SR-6.5 as amended by b.deo SRI-307). With `endReason` (the bring-up controller's `claude_config_dir` hold, which brings the persona up again later on a fresh connection and tracker), the persona's own open episode (`persona-connection-lost`, `persona-slack-unreachable` or `persona-credentials-refused`) first ends with one line of its class and the cause `cleared: <endReason>`, so its start line gets an end; with no episode open it logs nothing. Shutdown closes every connection with `stopAll()`. **Credentials reconnect** (b.av2 SR-8.6 credentials row, as amended by b.deo SRI-201, SRI-203, SRI-406, SRI-408, SRI-502, SRI-802, SRI-805; b.av2 SR-3.1, SR-3.3): `reconnectCredentials(key, tokens, onLaterOutcome?, beforeSwap?)` opens a second connection for a persona that has been up, with a new token pair, through the same attempt code: a new validation client and `auth.test`, a new long-lived Web API client, and a new Socket Mode client whose `start()` is bounded at 10 s like every other start. Every client is built through the factory with the SR-3.3 option sets. Identity is re-read from the new `auth.test`, with no check that the app is the same. Only when the new socket reaches `hello` does the persona switch to the new tokens, identity, Web API client and socket together; then any reopen of the old connection is cancelled and the old socket is closed as the manager's own close, with no lost line. Until then the old connection keeps its normal supervision, and both sockets forward events (the routing's dedupe delivers a message once); SR-3.1 allows two sockets and two Web API clients per persona only during this overlap. The first attempt resolves as a `PersonaReconnectOutcome`: `swapped`, `refused` (the new clients are discarded and the old connection is untouched), `retrying` (Slack unreachable, a `start()` abandoned at 10 s included: the old connection stays in use and the new one retries on its own SR-3.2 schedule and its own episode tracker, so its unreachable start and cleared lines are logged afresh), or `cancelled` (dry run, an unknown or stopped persona, or superseded). A later swap or refusal of a reconnect left retrying goes to `onLaterOutcome`; a refusal ends its retries. `beforeSwap` runs right before every swap, at the first attempt or later, while the persona still reports its old status, so no status listener sees it up on the new connection before the hook has run; a throw (or a rejected promise) is logged as a `credentials reconnect before-swap hook` failure and the swap goes ahead. A new reconnect, `stop` and `stopAll` cancel a pending one; its open Slack-unreachable episode then ends with one cleared line (the tracker's `end`), cause `cleared: the new connection of its confirmed credentials change is no longer retried: a later confirmed credentials change replaced it` or `…: the persona's connection was stopped`, so its start line always gets an end. `replaceRetryTokens(key, tokens)` is the retrying case instead: a persona whose bring-up is Slack-unreachable and retrying (or whose first attempt is in flight) takes the new pair for every later attempt; an attempt in flight with the old pair is cancelled and a new one starts, and the SR-3.2 schedule and episode logging carry on. It returns false for any other state, since a persona that has been up is reconnected instead. The held token pair is replaced only by a swap or by `replaceRetryTokens`.

It reaches the destination and its setting only through the resolver (`destinations.destinationOf`, and `destinationSettingFrom`), over the configuration in effect at each attempt, and keeps no destination and no mode; an episode records only the destinations it named, by setting and value (`NamedDestination`), so a switch change that keeps the value logs one fresh opening line (b.deo SRI-702, SRI-906).
