See Permission Relay, [Destination hold](#destination-hold-bav2-sr-71-failures-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-702-sri-703).
    ├── persona-event-router.ts  b.av2 SR-3.1 / SR-4.1 (as amended by b.deo SRI-301) / SR-7.1 (as amended by b.deo SRI-701 to SRI-703) / SR-13.1 the handler every persona connection forwards its events to. `createPersonaEventRouter({ routing, clientFor, getPersona, log, handleClick?, emitTrail? })` returns the connection manager's `onEvent` handler, called with the receiving persona's key, the event name and the library's listener argument. `message` and `app_mention`: one RAW line, `[slack] RAW <event> event persona=<key>: <first 300 chars of the event JSON>`, then the event and its `ack` go to persona-routing's `receive` with the receiving persona as the only receiver and, as its fourth argument, the envelope's `is_ext_shared_channel` flag exactly as received (`true`, `false`, another value, or undefined when the envelope has none or there is no body; the private `envelopeFlagOf`, read from the envelope, never from the event; b.deo SRI-301). The RAW line is the same in both modes. `interactive`: the payload's channel, message `ts` and clicking user are read once; for each action `cscb.block_action.received` is emitted and `handlePermissionClick` runs with `receivingPersonaKey` set to the receiving persona's key, stopping at the first handled action. A throw while handling one action is logged as `[slack] persona=<key>: interactive action <i> of <n> handling failed: <describeThrownValue>` and the remaining actions still run. The payload is acked exactly once, after handling, on every path: when an action is handled, when none is, and when an action throws. Any other event name is logged, acked and ignored. A throw while handling one event is logged as `[slack] persona=<key>: <event> event handling failed: <describeThrownValue>` and never reaches the manager. No other persona's key, connection or client is consulted. Nothing runs at import.
    ├── persona-start.ts        b.av2 SR-6.1 / SR-3.1 / SR-3.4 / SR-7.2 / SR-13.1 the per-persona start procedure and the connection seams the server reads. The procedure's steps, in order: (1) the local credentials check and (2) the working-directory check, both evaluated before either stops the bring-up so both causes are reported (`checkPersonaLocalBringUp`; in dry run only `checkPersonaWorkingDirectory` runs and no credentials file is read); (3) Slack validation and connection through the connection manager's `bringUp(persona, tokens)` (no tokens in dry run); (4) the launch, only when step 3 reports the persona `up`. This module exports steps 1–3 as separate functions and runs none of them itself: `checkPersonaLocalSteps` (steps 1–2, returning each failure, the tokens read and the credentials digest (`credentialsDigest`, whatever step 1's outcome, a real-path collision included; none in dry run), logging only when given a logger), `connectPersonaSlack` (step 3, handing the persona and the tokens it is given to the manager) and `personaSlackStatusFailure` (the step-3 failure for a status other than `up`). A failure's step (`PersonaBringUpStep`) is `credentials`, `working-directory`, `slack` or `claude-config-dir`, the last for a persona held because its `claude_config_dir` cannot be resolved (bug b.g57), before its Slack step or at a later launch. The bring-up controller (`persona-bringup-controller.ts`) runs the server's start through them and keeps each persona's outcome; the start pass launches a persona that is `up` at start, and the controller launches one that reaches `up` through a retry. Steps 1–2 log through the local checks and step 3 through the manager; a throw from `bringUp` is the only line `connectPersonaSlack` adds (`[slack] persona <ref> not brought up: Slack bring-up threw: <describeThrownValue>`), and it resolves a `slack` failure of class `error`. Nothing here posts to Slack, records a startup error or counts a failed spawn. Seams, built over the manager and the applied-config getter: `isPersonaClientServing(status)` (true for `up`, `lost` and `retrying` in its `reopen` phase; false while connecting, retrying its bring-up, broken, stopped or unmanaged), `createPersonaClientLookup` (`clientFor`: the manager's long-lived Web client for a serving applied persona, else nothing, and always nothing in dry run), `createPersonaIdentityLookup` (the serving persona's bot identity; the placeholder identity in dry run) `createPersonaUpFlushListener(notifier)` (a status listener: flush exactly that persona's held notices on every transition to `up`), `composePersonaStatusListeners(...listeners)` (several status listeners as the manager's one; each is called even when an earlier one throws), `createPersonaUpPredicate(connections, outcomes)` (`isPersonaUp(key)`, b.av2 SR-6.4: true only while `isPersonaClientServing` holds for the persona's status and its bring-up outcome is `up`; false for a persona the manager or the controller does not know; logs nothing; the one "is this persona up" check behind MCP session admission (Session Lifecycle, Connection), the permission poller's skip (Permission Relay, Per-tick flow) and `/interject`'s 503) and `createPersonaRelaunchGate(connections, log, outcomes?)` (`canRelaunch(key)`: decides through the same private check as `createPersonaUpPredicate` (`isPersonaUpGiven`), over one status read it also uses to word its log line, so the gate and the predicate can't drift: true only while `isPersonaClientServing` holds for the persona's status and, when `outcomes` is given, its bring-up outcome is `up`; false for a persona the manager does not know, such as one that failed its credentials or working-directory check; every brought-up persona is `up` in dry run). The server passes the bring-up controller as `outcomes` and hands the gate to restart (`RestartDeps.canRestart`), the restart launch and the health check's work list; see Auto-Restart. When it answers false it logs one of two lines, once per persona per reason: a repeat for the same reason is silent, and being eligible again re-arms it. While the connection is not serving: `[slack] persona=<key>: not relaunched — its Slack connection is <state>; eligible again once it is up`, with `<state>` one of `not brought up` (the manager does not know the persona), `connecting`, `retrying its bring-up`, `retrying`, `broken` or `stopped`. While the connection is serving but the bring-up outcome is not `up`: `[slack] persona=<key>: not relaunched — its bring-up has not succeeded; eligible again once it is up`. A key outside the applied set (`PersonaUpQuery.isApplied`, production: the bring-up controller's `isApplied`; b.av2 SR-8.6 as amended by b.deo SRI-201, SRI-203, SRI-406, SRI-408, SRI-502, SRI-802, SRI-805) is refused first, whatever its status: `[slack] persona=<key>: not relaunched — it is no longer in the applied configuration`; the up predicate answers false for it too. Each line carries only the key and the reason. Tokens exist only in memory: for the call, in the manager, and in the bring-up controller's entry for the persona (kept from the first read for later directory retries; see the next entry). Nothing runs at import.
    ├── persona-bringup-controller.ts  b.av2 SR-6.1 (outcomes) / SR-6.4 / SR-7.2 (part) / SR-10.3 (part; as amended by b.deo SRI-901 to SRI-906) / SR-13.1 per-persona bring-up outcomes and retries. `createPersonaBringUpController({ connections, launch, dryRun, log, clock?, ... })` (`connections` is the connection manager's `bringUp`, `status` and `stop`, all required; `stop` closes a persona's connection when a `claude_config_dir` hold starts for it) returns `bringUp(persona, applied)`, `onConnectionStatus(key, status)` (the manager's status listener), `isUp(key)`, `isApplied(key)` (whether the key is in the applied set now, from the optional injected `appliedPersonas()` getter, which production binds to `personaConfig`'s personas; true for every key without it; see the applied-set guard under Server-Managed Startup step 5), `state(key)` (outcome and causes, never a token), `credentialsDigest(key)`, `changeCredentials(persona, applied, connections, hooks?)`, `holdForConfigDir(persona, failure)`, `cancel(key)` and `cancelAll()`. `credentialsDigest(key)` (b.av2 SR-8.3) is the read-only query behind the reload detection tick's credentials comparison: the digest or marker of the bytes the persona's bring-up read, or of its last confirmed credentials change, which is what it connected with, is retrying with or broke with. No retry re-reads the file, so it changes only at a confirmed credentials change. `changeCredentials` is apply step 4's per-persona body (see [Credentials change](#credentials-change-bav2-sr-86-step-4-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-805)). Beside the held content, each entry keeps the content its own connection uses (`live`: tokens and digest), set at bring-up, at every swap of a credentials reconnect (at once or later) and when a retrying persona takes a change; a refused change holds `live` again, so the change is pending. `isCredentialsBroken(state)`, exported here, is the SR-6.4 rule it, the change plan and the apply steps share. A persona broken by a credentials file another applied persona shares holds the digest of its own path's bytes (read only to be hashed, never parsed). It is undefined in dry run (no file is read) and for an unknown or cancelled persona. It is never logged. `bringUp` logs the persona's `persona-start` line, runs steps 1–2 (`checkPersonaLocalSteps`), then step 3 (`connectPersonaSlack`) when both pass, and resolves once the persona has an outcome: `up`, `broken` or `retrying` (see Server-Managed Startup step 5 for the cause mapping). It launches nothing itself at start. Causes are kept apart (credentials, directory, Slack, config dir). A directory-broken persona is re-checked on its own timer with its own `createPersonaRetrySchedule` (5 s doubling to 300 s, no cap), never through `backoff.ts`; a re-check is scheduled only once the previous one has finished. The tokens read at the persona's bring-up (or at its last confirmed credentials change) are held in its entry and handed to the manager when a directory retry reaches Slack; no retry re-reads the credentials file. A persona that reaches `up` through a retry is launched once through the injected `launch` (the server's `spawnForPersona`): when a directory retry's Slack step leaves the persona's outcome `up` (the manager's status is `up`, `lost` or `retrying` in the `reopen` phase), or when `onConnectionStatus` sees `up` right after `retrying` in the `bring-up` phase. An `up` after `lost` or a reopen launches nothing. The `claude_config_dir` hold (bug b.g57): the injected `checkConfigDir` (production: `checkLaunchConfigDir`) runs once steps 1 and 2 pass, right before step 3, at bring-up and when a directory retry reaches Slack; an unresolvable directory opens the hold there, so the persona never connects. `holdForConfigDir` (the session manager's hook, installed with `setConfigDirUnresolvableHook`) opens it for a persona whose later launch found the directory unresolvable, and closes its Slack connection (the manager's `stop` with the end reason `the persona's Slack connection was closed while its claude_config_dir cannot be resolved`, so an open lost, unreachable or refused episode ends with one cleared line; a failure logs `closing its Slack connection for its claude_config_dir failed: <error>`), so the persona leaves up (below) and its MCP session is dropped. Either way its outcome is `retrying` with a `configDir` cause and no connection, its instance and row are kept, and its notices are held by the notifier. The failure line is logged once when the episode starts, and the directory is re-checked on the persona's own timer and `createPersonaRetrySchedule`, outside the restart counter and cap, each attempt through the serializer. Once it resolves: one cleared line (`…; continuing the bring-up`), Slack validation and connection with the held credentials, then the launch (`up after its claude_config_dir resolved — launching`), which resumes the row through the collision ladder; Slack-unreachable then retries and launches on `up`. A persona Slack had refused when the hold started keeps that refusal as its cause and stays `broken` after the cleared line. A confirmed credentials change while held takes the new content (held and live) and opens no connection; the persona connects with it on its return. It returns false for a persona the controller does not know or has cancelled, and the caller then logs the line itself. An `up` right after `broken` (a pending credentials reconnect swapped in for a connection Slack had refused meanwhile) launches the persona the same way, logging `up after its confirmed credentials change — launching`. Each retry attempt, through to the launch it triggers, runs through the optional injected `serialize` (the server's lifecycle serializer, b.av2 SR-6.6): a directory re-check with its Slack step and launch, and the launch after a Slack retry reached `up`. Their checks (cancelled, no longer applied, already launched) run when the attempt starts, and the launch is awaited inside the attempt. `launchAfterRetry` also waits for up: it launches nothing unless the persona's outcome is `up` when its turn comes, so a Slack launch queued behind an operation that held the persona for its `claude_config_dir` (closing its connection) does nothing, even if the directory resolved by then; the hold's recovery launches it after the reconnect. The controller never submits `bringUp` itself; the apply bring-up does. `cancel(key)` (a persona teardown, or shutdown's `cancelAll()`) forgets the persona's entry and clears its timer, so retry work still queued for it does nothing. Each persona's state, timer and in-flight flag live in its own entry; nothing spans two personas. Lines go through the injected logger only (never `startup-errors.log`), and nothing here posts to Slack. Dry run reads no credentials file and makes no Slack call, but the directory check and its retry run as in a real start. Leaving up (b.av2 SR-6.3, SR-6.4): each time a persona's outcome changes from `up` to `broken` or `retrying` (a refused reopen of a running persona, or a Web API call refused for its bot token, bug b.ujn, both of which make it `broken`; or a `claude_config_dir` hold, which makes it `retrying` and closes its connection), the optional injected `onLeftUp(persona, state)` is told once; a persona that was never up is not reported, and a lost connection being reopened (`lost`, `retrying` in the `reopen` phase) stays `up` and is not reported. A throw or rejection from the listener is logged as `[slack] persona "<name>" (key=<key>): handling its change from up to <outcome> failed: <error>`. The module also exports `describePersonaNotUp(state)`, the token-free reason a persona is not up used by the refusal and drop lines (`<outcome>: <first cause>`, credentials before directory before Slack before config dir; `its bring-up has not run` with no state; `its Slack connection is not serving` when the outcome is `up` but the connection is not), and `createNotUpSessionDropper({ drop, log })`, the `onLeftUp` listener the server installs (Session Lifecycle, Disconnection). Clock, logger, checks, file-system seam, manager, launch, serializer and leaving-up listener are injected; nothing is created, read or scheduled at import or at construction.
    ├── persona-serializer.ts   b.av2 SR-6.6 / SR-13.1 per-persona lifecycle serialization. `createPersonaSerializer()` returns a `PersonaSerializer`: `run(key, operation)` (`PersonaSerialize`) starts the operation only once every operation already submitted for that key has settled, and resolves or rejects with the operation's own result; `whenIdle(key)` resolves (never rejects) once everything submitted for the key before the call has settled. Per key it holds one promise chain and nothing spans two keys, so one persona's operation never waits on another's. A rejected operation doesn't stop the next one for its key; its rejection goes to its submitter. Re-entrancy rule: an operation running for a key must never await `run` or `whenIdle` for the same key. What goes through it: Session Lifecycle, [Per-persona serialization](#per-persona-serialization-bav2-sr-66). No dependencies. Importable without side effects: importing it or calling the factory creates no timer, and an instance holds nothing until the first `run`. `server.ts` builds the one production instance at module scope.
    ├── persona-lifecycle.ts    b.av2 SR-6.1 / SR-6.2 / SR-6.5 (as amended by b.deo SRI-307) / SR-6.6 / SR-8.6 (as amended by b.deo SRI-802, SRI-805) / SR-13.1; b.jg5 SRJ-715 / SRJ-1507 (as amended by b.deo SRI-307) the per-persona operations a confirmed apply runs. `createPersonaLifecycle(deps)` returns a `PersonaLifecycle`: `teardown(persona)`, the persona teardown of apply step 2 (b.av2 SR-6.5 as amended by b.jg5 SRJ-1507 and b.deo SRI-307: it stops the approver, the live-row sequence and the retry timer first, kills the row with the bounded retry and keeps it, with no delete), which never rejects; `bringUp(persona, applied, options?)`, the bring-up at apply of step 6, which resolves with the bring-up outcome once an `up` persona's launch has settled, and with `{ recovery: true }` is the recovery bring-up of a credentials-broken persona whose credentials file changed; `reconnectCredentials(persona, applied)`, the credentials change of step 4, which resolves with the controller's `PersonaCredentialsChangeResult` once an up persona's first reconnect attempt has settled; `updateInPlace(change)`, the in-place update of step 3 (an `InPlaceApplyInput`), which never rejects, logs `[slack] persona "<name>" (key=<key>): updated in place (<settings>); its instance, Slack connection and MCP session are kept` with the changed settings in `IN_PLACE_SETTINGS` order (`invited.permission_prompts` among them), and forgets the persona's cached DM conversation when any of the exported `DM_DESTINATION_SETTINGS` (`permission_prompts`, `invited.permission_prompts`, `dm.enabled`, `dm.contact`) changed, saying so on that line (b.deo SRI-701); and `refreshTemplate(applied)`, the template refresh of step 5 (`refreshSlackChannelBotTemplate`, `agent-director-template.ts`), which never rejects and, belonging to no persona, is not serialized. The four per-persona operations are submitted through the injected serializer and never submit to it again from inside; none touches another persona. Every `teardown` cancels the persona's launch wait for a `working` row as soon as it is submitted (`cancelLaunchWait`, b.f2b). `teardown` also serves the old half of a destructive modify (its key still applied): it then also cancels the persona's bring-up retries and restart timer, and stops its UNAVAILABLE retry timer, at submit, before its serializer turn; `bringUp` serves the new half. Every `teardown` registers its submit with the notifier (`submitTeardown`, ended once by `settleTeardown`), and its serializer turn forgets the key's outage flags and opens the notifier's teardown window (`openTeardownWindow`) before its first step, closing it (`closeTeardownWindow`) when it completes, whatever a step throws, so every notice raised for the key meanwhile is written to the server log and a startup-errors entry (b.jg5 SRJ-1003); each CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME answer its kill reports is raised through the notifier's `notify` with the text `teardownKillRefusalNoticeText(instanceId, refusal)` (exported; b.jg5 SRJ-1002, SRJ-1003), and a standing non-success that no kill-failure alert, try-time refusal notice or outage onset written in the window records is raised the same way with the text `teardownKillNotSucceededNoticeText(instanceId, outcome, tries)` (b.jg5 SRJ-110; both builders live in `checked-kill.ts`). A persona with only next-launch changes gets no operation. the destination resolver's `forget` (teardown, an in-place update that moves the DM destination, a credentials change right before its new connection comes into use, and a recovery bring-up); the destination hold's `cancel`; the notifier (`forget`, and, optional in the type so hand-built fixtures stay valid, `notify`, `submitTeardown`, `settleTeardown`, `openTeardownWindow` and `closeTeardownWindow`; production passes the one notifier); `appliedPersonas()` (the teardown's Stop-hook pass, whether a teardown's key is still applied, and whether an in-place update's key is still applied); `dryRun`; `isShuttingDown` (the server's `shuttingDown` flag, read at each use);     ├── delivery-decision.ts    b.av2 SR-4.2 (as amended by b.deo SRI-303 to SRI-309) / SR-4.3 / SR-4.4 (as amended by b.deo SRI-306) / SR-13.1 the one place inbound delivery is decided, in both channel modes (b.deo SRI-303, SRI-305, SRI-306, SRI-308, SRI-309). `decideDelivery(event, persona, applied, fungible?)` takes one raw `message` / `app_mention` event, the receiving persona P (key, bot user ID, bot ID, channel entries and `dmEnabled`, P's `dm.enabled`) and every applied persona's key and channel entries, and returns deliver with `via`, or drop with a reason (`non-message`, `no-author`, `own`, `dm-disabled`, `group-dm`, `channel-not-configured` with an `unclaimed` flag, `not-mentioned`). What it covers: the deliverable subtypes (none, `file_share`, `bot_message`, `thread_broadcast`, `me_message`); an author must be present (`user` or `bot_id`); self-exclusion by P's bot user ID or P's bot ID, where an author with no `user` (a webhook or integration) is identified by its bot ID; the conversation kind (a DM is `channel_type` `im`, or, as a defensive fallback for an event without `channel_type`, a conversation ID starting with `D`; a group DM is recognised only by `channel_type` `mpim`), where a DM delivers with `via` `dm` when `dmEnabled` is on and is `dm-disabled` when it is off, an `mpim` event is always `group-dm`, and neither reaches the channel rules (an `app_mention` in a group DM has no `channel_type` and a `G…`/`C…` ID, so it takes the channel rules); channel membership; `delivery: all`; and `delivery: mentions`, which delivers on P's own user mention (`<@P>` or `<@P|label>`) or on `<!here>` / `<!channel>`, with or without a label. `<!everyone>` and user-group mentions do not count. An empty or unknown bot user ID or bot ID never matches. Self-exclusion is the only filter on the author: nothing arbitrates, counts or throttles exchanges between personas. `via`, first match wins: `dm`, `mention`, `broadcast`, `receive_all_shared`, `receive_all`. `receive_all_shared` needs at least one other applied persona with `delivery: all` in that channel, whether or not that persona is up; only a DM produces `dm`. All of the above is declarative mode's, and the decision is exactly that when `fungible` is absent or its `mode` is `declarative`. **Fungible mode.** `FungibleDecisionInputs` (`mode`, the envelope flag `isExtSharedChannel` as received, `channelIdPattern`, and from `ChannelDeliveryInputs` the applied personas' `fungibleDestinations`, `PersonaFungibleDestination`, and the optional `storedChoices`, `StoredChoices`: `readable` and `storedChoice(key, channel)`, which the stored-choice store satisfies) are read at the call. The message-shape, author, self-exclusion and conversation-kind steps are the same as above (a DM by `dmEnabled`, an `mpim` event `group-dm`); a channel event then meets the five conditions of `FUNGIBLE_REFUSALS`, in order, and the first it fails gives a drop with reason `fungible-refused` and its `refusal` (`FungibleRefusal`): `channel_type` is `channel` or `group` (`not-a-channel`), the channel ID matches the pattern (`channel-id-malformed`), the flag is present (`flag-missing`), a boolean (`flag-not-boolean`) and `false` (`externally-shared`). On the path, P's channel delivery is `channelDeliveryFor(key, channel, inputs)` (`ChannelDeliveryResult`: `delivery` and `heldByLoopGuard`): `mentions`, held, when the channel is another applied persona's fungible destination (the loop guard; a `dm` destination holds nothing and P's own destination is never held), else P's stored choice when the store is readable, else `mentions`. Then `via` is `mention`, then `broadcast`, then, at `all`, `receive_all_shared` when any other applied persona's `channelDeliveryFor` for the channel is `all`, else `receive_all`; otherwise a `not-mentioned` drop. No persona's channel entries are read, and whether any persona lists the channel plays no part. Every outcome on the fungible path carries `fungible` (`FungiblePath`: `channelType`, `public` or `private`, and `channelDelivery`). Also exports `stripPersonaMention`, which removes P's own mention token (both forms) from the text and leaves other mentions and broadcasts. Pure: imports types only, keeps no state and has no side effects on import. `decideDelivery`'s only caller is the persona pipeline in `persona-routing.ts`; `channelDeliveryFor`, the one copy of the channel-delivery and loop-guard rule, is also called by `set_channel_delivery` (`registry.ts`) for its result.
    ├── persona-routing.ts      b.av2 SR-4.1 (as amended by b.deo SRI-301, SRI-302) / SR-4.2 (as amended by b.deo SRI-303 to SRI-309) / SR-4.3 / SR-4.4 (as amended by b.deo SRI-306) / SR-4.6 / SR-7.3 / SR-10.3 (as amended by b.deo SRI-902, SRI-903) / SR-13.1; b.jg5 SRJ-1011 / SRJ-1501 / SRJ-1509 inbound delivery per persona, in both channel modes (b.deo SRI-301 to SRI-309, SRI-902, SRI-903). `createPersonaRouting(deps)` returns `receive(event, ack, personaKeys, isExtSharedChannel?)` (one key or a list; the event router passes the receiving persona's key alone and the envelope flag as received), `forget(key)` and `heardChannels(key)`: intake acks the event first, then, for each receiving persona key, writes the archive through the injected archive seam (in both modes, before any decision) and runs that persona's pipeline, each run isolated (a throw is logged naming the persona and never stops another persona's run). After the archive write the channel mode is read once for the event (`channelModeOf` over the configuration in effect, `PersonaRoutingConfig` carrying `allow_invited_channels`); in fungible mode an `app_mention`, a group-DM one included, ends there, with no dedupe record, decision, line, dispatch, reaction or report, since the `message` event carrying the same mention decides (b.deo SRI-302). A `message` event refused on the fungible path logs one `unclaimed-channel` line with the refusal's reason (`fungibleUnclaimedChannelCause`). It owns the per-persona dedupe: one `inbound-dedupe.ts` store per persona key, created on first use and kept until `forget(key)` drops it together with the key's heard set, other keys' stores and sets untouched (a persona teardown, which stops the persona's connection first, since another event for the key would create a new store); the key is the event's (channel, ts), or (channel, ts, edited.ts) when the event carries a top-level `edited.ts` (read by the private `editedTs`; a `message_changed` event nests its edit under `message` and keeps the two-part key), and a duplicate key stops after the archive write with no decision and no log line. It also owns the b.kvq no-session branch and the b.9cj streamless branch (the private `handleLostMessage`): it feeds `decideLostMessageState` (`lost-message.ts`) the persona's inputs, each asked with its key at that time, and fires the human-triggered `scheduleRestart` only when `firesHumanTriggeredRestart` says so (`starting-now`). Every Slack client, the persona config, the bot identity, the name resolver, the archive writer, the ack-reaction source, the notice sink (`notify`), the logger and (optionally) the dedupe clock, the up predicate and the lost-message state inputs are injected; the session lookup, restart guards and outage flags use the real registry, restart, backoff and outage state. Slack-call failures are logged through `describeSlackCallFailure`.

An absent optional query answers false (an absent `isNotUp` counts the persona as up), so with none given the decision is the four-query one. `decideEarlyLostMessageState` is exported so a caller that must know whether states 1 to 5 apply asks the same code. `firesHumanTriggeredRestart(state)` is true only for `starting-now` (b.jg5 SRJ-1501). `STATE_WORDING` is the frozen, exported map of each state's one `Recovery:` line; tests import it and the order and keep no copy. `buildLostMessageNotice(senderLabel, state)` builds the one-line notice body: a message from the sender was lost, not delivered, not saved and won't be delivered later, plus the recovery state. The body carries no message text, no mention and no persona name; the notifier adds the persona reference. Pure: no state, I/O, timers or logging, nothing at import. Its only caller is `persona-routing.ts`, which feeds the queries (see that entry) and raises the notice through the per-persona notice sink.

It is not idempotent: escaped text is escaped again. Its callers are `lost-message.ts` (the sender label) and `outage-state.ts` (agent-director's description quoted in the `ad-config-malformed` onset). `unescapeSlackControlCharacters(text)` undoes it (`&lt;` and `&gt;` first, `&amp;` last, so `&amp;lt;` becomes `&lt;`) and changes nothing else; its caller is `persona-notifier.ts`, whose persona teardown window writes text built for Slack to the server log and `startup-errors.log` instead (b.jg5 SRJ-1003). Pure: no imports, no module-scope state, nothing runs at import.
    ├── inbound-dedupe.ts       b.av2 SR-4.1 (as amended by b.deo SRI-302) / SR-13.1 one persona's inbound dedupe store. `createInboundDedupeStore(now?)` returns a store whose `record(conversationId, ts, editedTs?)` answers `new` (and records the key), `duplicate`, or `unkeyable` (`conversationId` or `ts` missing, empty or not a string; nothing recorded, and the caller treats the event as new). The key is (`conversationId`, `ts`, `editedTs`) when `editedTs` is a non-empty string, and (`conversationId`, `ts`) otherwise; the parts are joined with a separator no Slack ID or ts contains, so a two-part and a three-part key never collide. A key is remembered for `INBOUND_DEDUPE_RETENTION_MS` (10 minutes) from its first sighting; a duplicate does not extend it. Each `record` first prunes expired keys, so memory stays bounded with no timer. It knows nothing about personas, Slack or config and limits nothing: distinct keys are always new. State is in memory only. Clock injected (default `Date.now`); nothing at import. Its only caller is `persona-routing.ts`, which keeps one store per persona.
    ├── registry.ts             Persona-keyed MCP session registry (b.av2 SR-6.3), per-session MCP Server factory with the persona-scoped Slack tools, transport routing. A session is identified by its `roots/list` working directory, compared by real path; `matchPersonaByRootsPath` maps it to exactly one applied persona (a directory matching more than one persona matches none, with one log line). `decideSessionAdmission(rootsPath, personas, { isPersonaUp, describeNotUp?, ... })` wraps the match and answers `admitted`, `unmatched` or `not-up` (b.av2 SR-6.4); it logs the refusal line for `not-up` and registers, removes or closes nothing itself (see Session Lifecycle, Connection). Before any persona is matched it asks the optional held-directory query (`heldDirectory?: (rootsRealPath) => SessionHeldDirectory | undefined`, `{ directory, instanceIds }`; b.av2 SR-6.3 as amended by b.jg5 SRJ-1505, SRJ-810) with the roots real path and answers `held` (`{ kind: 'held', directory, instanceIds }`) for a held directory, whichever persona names it, a query that throws counting as held with no id, with one line (`sessionHeldRefusalLine(directory, instanceIds, failure?)`); with no query nothing is held. `closePendingSession(pendingId, transport, { removePending, stopKeepAlive })` disconnects a pending session that won't be registered: it removes the pending entry, stops the SSE keep-alive, then closes the transport and ignores a close error; `server.ts` uses it for every such branch (see Session Lifecycle, Connection). `dropPersonaSession(key)` drops the session registered for a persona: it removes the persona's MCP session-ID mappings and registry entry first, marks the entry not connected, then closes its transport, so the close restarts nothing; it resolves whether a session was registered and logs nothing (see Session Lifecycle, Disconnection; a persona teardown drops the session the same way). The registry holds one session per persona key (`getSessionByPersona`); a newer session for a persona replaces the older one, and a stale close of the replaced session leaves the newer one registered. A pending session's entry stub is promoted in place, so its tool handlers read the persona key it was matched under. Each session lists six tools: the five Slack tools (`reply`, `react`, `edit_message`, `fetch_messages`, `download_attachment`) and `set_channel_delivery` (`SET_CHANNEL_DELIVERY_TOOL`, re-exported from `channel-delivery.ts`), in both modes. Every tool first resolves the session's persona at call time; a session with no persona key gets `sessionNotMatchedRefusal(tool)`, and a key that is not an applied persona's gets `personaNotAppliedRefusal(tool, key)`, the two refusals all six share. The posting-scope check `checkPersonaTarget(persona, target, action, mode?)` (b.av2 SR-5.1 as amended by b.deo SRI-601; the mode from `SessionToolDeps.getChannelMode`, read at each call with the persona; absent is declarative) sorts the target with the module-private `classifyPersonaTarget` (a channel, a `D…` DM conversation ID, a `U…`/`W…` user ID, or other): a channel is a configured channel `id` in declarative mode and any `CHANNEL_ID_RE` value in fungible mode, where the persona's `channels` is not read and Slack enforces membership; a channel is allowed always, a `D…` conversation only while the persona's `dm.enabled` is on, and a user ID only for a `post` action (`reply`) while `dm.enabled` is on, in both modes; any other target is refused as not a configured channel in declarative mode and with `FUNGIBLE_TARGET_REFUSAL` in fungible mode. Each Slack tool's target argument and action are in the private `TOOL_TARGET` map (see Outbound). A pure check: no Slack call, log or state. In fungible mode a Slack call on a channel target that fails gives the tool error `slackRefusalToolErrorText(tool, persona, channel, code)` (b.deo SRI-602). **`set_channel_delivery` (b.deo SRI-501 to SRI-507).** Its handler (`setChannelDelivery` in `createSessionServer`) never calls `checkPersonaTarget`, reads no client, makes no Slack call and has no dry-run branch. After the shared resolution it also refuses, with `personaNotAppliedRefusal`, a key the stored-choice store marks retiring and a session that is not the one the registry holds for its key, dropped or replaced (`getSessionByPersona(key) !== entry`), then applies `SET_CHANNEL_DELIVERY_REFUSALS` in order (`SetChannelDeliveryRefusal`; builders `channelDeliveryDeclarativeRefusal`, `channelDeliveryUnreadableRefusal`, `channelDeliveryValueRefusal`, `channelDeliveryChannelRefusal`, which echo a channel only when it matches `ECHOABLE_CHANNEL_RE` and a delivery only when it matches `ECHOABLE_KEY_NAME_RE`), stores the choice through the store's `set` (`SessionChannelDeliveryStore`, the members it uses), logs one `persona-channel-delivery-set` line through `SessionToolDeps.log` and answers `channelDeliverySetResultText`, or a failure text (`channelDeliveryWriteFailedText`, `channelDeliveryNotStoredText`), all with no await between resolving the persona and the write. Its descriptions are `SET_CHANNEL_DELIVERY_DESCRIPTION`, `SET_CHANNEL_DELIVERY_CHANNEL_DESCRIPTION` and `SET_CHANNEL_DELIVERY_DELIVERY_DESCRIPTION`. Its inputs are the optional `SessionToolDeps` members `getChannelMode`, `getChannelDelivery`, `heardChannels`, `getAppliedPersonas` and `log`; the path is in Data Flow, Outbound. The MCP instructions (`MCP_INSTRUCTIONS`, exported as the exact string `createSessionServer` hands every instance, one text for both modes, which the shipped-description audit in `tests/shipped-docs.test.ts` covers) describe the `<channel>` tag (their example tag carries `source="slack-channel-router"`, the MCP server name the harness renders) (including the author's `user_id`, or `bot_id` for an author without a user, and the `via` values), say that `<@ID>` in text mentions a Slack user or another persona and is how to address another persona, say that a message without `via` is an injected prompt, state where the tools may act (with invited channels off, the channels the persona is configured into; with them on, any channel its Slack app is a member of, where Slack refuses the others; and with DMs on a DM conversation or, for `reply`, a user ID), say in one sentence what `set_channel_delivery` sets and that it works only with invited channels on, and describe the tools; they carry no reload or `clear-latch` wording. No session-id discovery (AD owns it).

Also defines the CSCB-synthetic `ErrSpawnCapReached` (never emitted by the AD library; minted by the restart cap path — remediation hint "restart the server to retry — automatic restarts are suspended for this persona"), whose `errName` is `ERR_SPAWN_CAP_REACHED_NAME` (`'SpawnCapReached'`); the remediation hint recognises it by its class.
    ├── ad-description-phrases.ts  b.jg5 SRJ-1303 agent-director's description words that CSCB matches (ADSRD SR-1.4). No imports. String constants: the unusable recorded session name (`UNUSABLE_RECORDED_NAME_PHRASE`), the nine CONFLICT case words (`CONFLICT_*_PHRASE`, "another agent-director store" (`CONFLICT_ANOTHER_STORE_PHRASE`) among them), the description words that ride beside a case phrase, on a kill failure, or on an UNAVAILABLE (`ErrTmuxUnresponsive`) or ENVIRONMENT (`ErrTmuxNotAvailable`) error and are not case phrases ("the new row was ended" also rides on a plain spawn's `ErrTmuxUnresponsive` or `ErrTmuxNotAvailable` after "duplicate session" whose re-lookup could not answer, beside a retry with `reuse_finished`, HO rev 26; CSCB keys no behaviour on it there) (the plain spawn's label wordings `PLAIN_SPAWN_LABEL_NAMES_THIS_ID_PHRASE` and `PLAIN_SPAWN_LABEL_NOT_THIS_ID_PHRASE`, `NEW_ROW_ENDED_PHRASE`, `NOTHING_WRITTEN_PHRASE`, `PANE_NOT_ADOPTED_PHRASE`, `NO_KILL_SENT_PHRASE`, and every kill failure's `RETRY_KILL_LATER_PHRASE` and `NEVER_DELETE_ROW_PHRASE`), the different tmux server (`DIFFERENT_TMUX_SERVER_PHRASE`), the launch timeout (`LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_PHRASE`) and a row still stopping or still starting (`STILL_STOPPING_PHRASE`, `STILL_STARTING_PHRASE`). Besides the words it holds one pattern and its helper, the only definition of a kill failure's survivor-naming form (b.jg5 SRJ-702, SRJ-1303, SRJ-1007): the survivor clause's words (`SURVIVOR_CLAUSE_ONE_PHRASE`, "another process of a pane of the labelled session", and `SURVIVOR_CLAUSE_MANY_PHRASE`, "other processes of panes of the labelled session"), `SURVIVOR_PID_PATTERN`, built from them, which matches the clause followed by "(pid S)" for one survivor or "(pids S1, S2)" for several (no `g` flag; group 1 the one pid, group 2 the list), and `survivorPids(description)`, every pid the description's survivor clause names, in order, empty when it has none. The form is checked against agent-director 0.11.0 (tag `v0.11.0`, `pkg/api/kill_errors.go`). The worker's own pid, written "the agent process (pid N)" after the kill exit wait (joined with " and " to the survivor clause when both outlived it) or "while its agent process still runs (pid N)" when no session or pane of the launch was found, carries none of the clause's words, so the pattern never matches it and `survivorPids` never returns it. Reading survivor pids from the description is interim: a description is text for humans, agent-director's structured `survivor_pids` is on the `ad.kill.called` trail, and CSCB has asked agent-director for the survivor pids on the error itself (SRJ-702). The words are copied from agent-director so CSCB matches exactly what it writes; CSCB only looks for them in a description it has received and never uses one to build a command. The module sets no order in which the CONFLICT case words are checked, and the order of its declarations means nothing. The test stub's error builders take their descriptions from here; the error classifier (`ad-error-class.ts`) matches `UNUSABLE_RECORDED_NAME_PHRASE` and `DIFFERENT_TMUX_SERVER_PHRASE` from here, and its launch-timeout predicate (`isLaunchTimeoutError`, b.jg5 SRJ-407) matches `LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_PHRASE`; and the conflict latch (`conflict-latch.ts`) is the consumer of the nine CONFLICT case words, which it checks in the order it defines. No other module matches the other words.
    ├── ad-error-class.ts       b.jg5 SRJ-104 the one classifier of agent-director errors, and the `ErrInvalidFlags` step beside it. `classifyAdError(value)` maps any value thrown by an agent-director call to exactly one of ten classes (`AD_ERROR_CLASSES`, labels `AD_ERROR_CLASS_*`, type `AdErrorClass`), recognising each class the client declares by `instanceof` (the classes `agent-director-errors.ts` re-exports) and an `ErrUnknownErrorName`, decided before those classes, by its `unknownName`; an instance of a class the table names takes that class's answer whatever its `errName` (the order is under [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)); pure and never throws. `isAdErrorInstance(value, errorClass)` is the one never-throwing by-class check a site uses to tell one agent-director error class from another (a STATE class's meaning is set per site): true when `value` is an instance of `errorClass` (`AdErrorConstructor`: a client class imported from `agent-director-errors.ts`, or CSCB's own subclass). A base `AgentDirectorError` whose `errName` merely equals a class's name is not an instance of it. `AD_GONE_ERROR_CLASSES` lists the GONE classes; `goneErrNameOf(value)` answers the name of the GONE class a value is an instance of (one of `AD_GONE_ERR_NAMES`, log labels only). `isInvalidFlagsError(value)` is `isAdErrorInstance`'s use for `ErrInvalidFlags`, and narrows the value to `InvalidFlagsError`. `isDifferentTmuxServerError(value)` (b.jg5 SRJ-1021) answers whether a value is the re-bound-socket form of ENVIRONMENT: true only when `classifyAdError` gives ENVIRONMENT and its `errDescription` contains `DIFFERENT_TMUX_SERVER_PHRASE` from `ad-description-phrases.ts`; a missing or non-string description answers false. Recognition is by class (through `classifyAdError`) plus phrase; it never throws. `outage-state.ts`'s `raiseTmuxUnavailable` uses it to pick the onset. `describeAdErrorClassification(c)` renders a classification for a log line. `conflictDescriptionOf(value)` (b.jg5 SRJ-501, SRJ-507) answers the raw `errDescription` of a value that `classifyAdError` classes CONFLICT, an `ErrTmuxSessionConflict` instance, and `undefined` for a value of any other class (an `ErrUnknownErrorName` included, whatever its `unknownName`, and a base `AgentDirectorError` merely named `ErrTmuxSessionConflict`), for a missing or non-string description and when a read throws; it never throws. The CONFLICT classification itself carries no description, so `describeAdErrorClassification` never logs that raw text; the reader (`conflict-latch.ts`) redacts it before it is stored or logged. `killFailedDescriptionOf(value)` (b.jg5 SRJ-110) answers the raw `errDescription` of an `ErrTmuxKillFailed` instance, and `undefined` for any other value (an `ErrUnknownErrorName` whose `unknownName` is `ErrTmuxKillFailed` included: it is UNAVAILABLE and never a kill failure), a non-string description or a read that throws; the kill outcome (`checked-kill.ts`) carries it raw and every log line renders it redacted. `unclassifiedClassificationOf(value)` is the UNCLASSIFIED classification, reported name and rendered message included, of a value a site takes as UNCLASSIFIED although the classifier gives it another class (at a kill, a class SRJ-110 has no row for); it is pure and never throws. `CSCB_UNKNOWN_ERROR_NAME` (`'UnknownError'`) is the `errName` of CSCB's own `UnknownError` wrapper, by which the classifier recognises it, UNAVAILABLE. `classifyWithInvalidFlagsRecheck(value, trigger?)` is the `ErrInvalidFlags` step: one immediate version re-check through `triggerAdVersionRecheck` (`ad-version-gate.ts`), then UNCLASSIFIED; it answers an `AdErrorStepAnswer`, or for an `InvalidFlagsError` argument an `AdInvalidFlagsStepAnswer` whose `recheck` is not optional. `describeAgentDirectorFailure(err)` renders a failed call for a log line (a safe `errName`, then the redacted description; `permission-poller.ts` re-exports it). `describeReportedAdFailure(err)` (b.jg5 SRJ-104) renders a failed call naming what agent-director reported: an UNCLASSIFIED, UNUSABLE NAME or CONFIG error as `<reported name> message="<agent-director's description>"` (an `ErrUnknownErrorName`'s `unknownName` and the envelope's `err_description`, not the client's own text; the name or the message alone when the other is unsafe or empty; redacted, on one line), and every other value through `describeAgentDirectorFailure`; it never throws. The CLI precheck (`cli-teardown.ts`) describes its failures with it. `describeAdFailureForLog(err)` (b.jg5 SRJ-104, SRJ-1014) is the server-log describer: `describeReportedAdFailure`'s rendering when the classifier gives a reported name, else `describeAgentDirectorFailure`'s; it never throws. The server's refusal lines use it (the CONFLICT and UNUSABLE NAME lines at a launch, the own-row read, the reconnect and the dialog approver, a launch's other refusal lines, the pane-read and pending-row descriptions), so an agent-director error name the client does not know shows as the reported name, never the client's placeholder. **Verbs (b.jg5 SRJ-307, SRJ-310).** `AD_VERBS` (type `AdVerb`) lists every agent-director verb a wrapped call declares. A wrapped call declares an `AdCall`: its verb, or for `kill` an `AdKillCall` (`{ verb: 'kill', rowReadLive }`; `AD_CALL_KILL_ROW_READ_LIVE`, `AD_CALL_KILL_ROW_NOT_READ_LIVE`, `adKillCall(rowReadLive)`), since only the site knows whether it kills a row it read live. The tmux-touching set is `TMUX_TOUCHING_VERBS`: `spawn` (plain or reuse), `resume`, `read-pane`, `send-keys`, `pause`, and `kill` of a row read live. `isTmuxTouchingCall(call)` answers for a declared call (a `kill` only when `rowReadLive` is exactly true) and `adCallVerb(call)` gives its verb; both never throw. `AD_LAUNCH_VERBS` is `spawn` and `resume`, and `isLaunchCall(call)` answers for a declared call: a successful launch call leaves its row `pending`, which the wrapper passes as the condition end's reading. `AD_READ_VERBS` is `status`, `get` and `list`, the arming predicate's read verbs. `find-missing`, `delete`, `get-permission` and `decide` are in none of these sets. b.jg5 SRJ-407: `launchTimeoutFormOf(value, call)` names the form in which a value ends a declared launch call as a launch timeout (`LaunchTimeoutForm`: `LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_FORM_CALL_TIMEOUT`, `ErrCallTimeout`; `LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_FORM_TMUX_UNRESPONSIVE`, an `ErrTmuxUnresponsive` instance whose description contains `LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_PHRASE`), or `undefined` for any other value (an `ErrUnknownErrorName` carrying `ErrTmuxUnresponsive` included) or a call that is no launch call; `isLaunchTimeoutError(value, call)` is its boolean. By class plus phrase, pure, never throws; both forms keep the UNAVAILABLE class. See [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104).
    ├── checked-kill.ts         b.jg5 SRJ-110 / SRJ-701 / SRJ-703 a kill's outcome, its class, whether the caller's next step may run, one checked kill and its log rendering. No server-only import (no notifier, outage state, Slack client, latch, episodes or server module), no state and no version re-check of its own, so a CLI process can use it too. `KillOutcome` is a success (`KillSuccess`) or a non-success (`KillFailure`). The successes: `killed` (`KILL_OUTCOME_KILLED`, the call resolved; `killSent` is the result's `kill_sent`, true or false, absent from a result with no boolean `kill_sent`, read through the client's `KillResult`), `row-gone` (`ErrSpawnNotFound`), `session-gone` (a GONE answer, `ErrTmuxSendKeys` or `ErrTmuxCaptureFailed`, its name kept: for `kill`, gone is success, b.jg5 SRJ-104) and `row-finished` (`KILL_OUTCOME_ROW_FINISHED`, with its `read`), which only the bounded retry (`kill-retry.ts`) gives, when a `status` read between tries finds the row finished, or, for an old-life wait's kill, when its hold ended while the tries ran (`KILL_ROW_FINISHED_HOLD_ENDED`, read `hold-ended`; b.jg5 SRJ-702, SRJ-811). The non-success is `not-killed` with one of `KILL_FAILURE_CLASSES`: UNAVAILABLE (`killFailed` true for an `ErrTmuxKillFailed` instance, with its raw `killFailedDescription` from `killFailedDescriptionOf`; false for an `ErrUnknownErrorName` carrying that name), CONFLICT, UNUSABLE_NAME, CONFIG, ENVIRONMENT or UNCLASSIFIED; the thrown value is kept as `error` and never logged raw. A class SRJ-110 has no row for (`KILL_UNLISTED_CLASSES`: LAUNCH FAILURE, a STATE name other than `ErrSpawnNotFound`, `ErrInvalidFlags` included, and DIRECTORY) is UNCLASSIFIED with that class kept as `unlistedClass`; `recheck` is the answer kind of the `ErrInvalidFlags` version re-check a caller made, never set here. `killOutcomeOf(settled)` maps a settled kill (`{ result }` or `{ thrown }`) to its outcome by class through `ad-error-class.ts` (`classifyAdError`, `isAdErrorInstance`, `goneErrNameOf`, `killFailedDescriptionOf`); it is pure and never throws. `checkedKill(instanceId, kill, options?)` makes exactly one call of the injected `kill` with `{ claude_instance_id }` alone (`PlainKillParams`, a plain kill) and answers its outcome; it never throws, rejects or retries. `CheckedKillOptions.goneIsFailure`, which only the CLI teardown passes (`TEARDOWN_KILL_OPTIONS`, `cli-teardown.ts`), makes a GONE answer the GONE non-success (`KillFailureGone`: `not-killed`, class GONE, its name kept) in place of `session-gone`; `killOutcomeOf(settled, options?)` takes the same option. Overloads keep a call with no options answering a `KillOutcome`, so no server site's outcome type holds the GONE non-success; `AnyKillFailure` and `AnyKillOutcome` are the forms with it. `killLetsNextStepRun(outcome)` is the next-step predicate: true only for a success form, false for every non-success and for any value that is not a kill outcome. `isKillOutcome(value)` and `killOutcomeStopsServer(value)` (a non-success whose `recheck` is `stop`) never throw. `describeKillOutcome(outcome)` renders one log line's fragment: `outcome=killed kill_sent=<true|false|absent>`, `outcome=row-gone (ErrSpawnNotFound)`, `outcome=session-gone (<GONE name>)`, `outcome=row-finished read=<read>` or `outcome=not-killed class=<class> …` (with `from=<class>` and `recheck=<kind>` for an unlisted class; `class=GONE <name>` for the GONE non-success), every description through the shared redaction and no raw thrown value. Beside it, the two notice texts built from a kill's outcome where nothing latches on it (b.jg5 SRJ-1002, SRJ-1003, SRJ-110), both unescaped and never throwing: `teardownKillRefusalNoticeText(instanceId, refusal)` (a `KillRefusal`: `at` `KILL_REFUSAL_AT_KILL` or `KILL_REFUSAL_AT_READ`, a CONFLICT or UNUSABLE_NAME `errorClass`, the thrown value), `agent-director kill of <id> refused at a try: <outcome>` or `… refused at a status read between its tries: <outcome>`, and `teardownKillNotSucceededNoticeText(instanceId, outcome, tries)`, `agent-director kill of <id> did not succeed after <n> kill(s); the row is kept: <outcome>`. Its callers: `killPersonaInstance`, the start sweep's `sweepKill` and the old-life wait's kill tries (`session-manager.ts`), the bounded retry (`kill-retry.ts`), the restart work (`restart.ts`), the restart kill adapter (`server.ts`), the persona teardown (`persona-lifecycle.ts`), the CLI teardown's kill (`teardownKill`, `cli.ts`), and the old-life wait's notice text (`old-life-wait.ts`, `teardownKillRefusalNoticeText`).
    ├── kill-retry.ts           b.jg5 SRJ-702 / SRJ-110 the bounded retry of a live row's kill. No server-only import (no notifier, outage state, Slack client, latch, episodes or server module) and no state, so a CLI process can use it too; every wait is injected (`KillRetryWait`: a clock with `setTimeout`, the shape `createFakeClock` satisfies, or a sleep function; `KILL_RETRY_SYSTEM_CLOCK` is the production clock), and every wait is awaited, so no timer is left pending once a call settles. `runKillRetry(options)` (`KillRetryOptions`: `instanceId`, the site's single-try `kill`, its between-try `read`, `wait`, the seed `lastRead`, optional `keepGoing`, `configReadEndsTries`, `budget` and `holdEnded`, `log` and `logPrefix`) makes up to `KILL_RETRY_TRIES` (3) tries `KILL_RETRY_SPACING_MS` (2 s) apart, never throws or rejects, and answers a `KillRetryResult`: the `outcome` that stands, how the tries ended (`end`: `settled`, `exhausted`, `budget-spent`, `row-finished`, `read-config`, `read-latched`, `stopped`, or `hold-ended` for an old-life wait's kill whose hold ended while its tries ran: asked after each wait between tries, before the keep-going check, after a read that did not find the row finished and when a try's UNAVAILABLE outcome would stand, it ends the tries as the `row-finished` success, read `hold-ended`, with no further kill or read, and a survivor named by those tries gives the `survivor` decision; b.jg5 SRJ-702, SRJ-811, option A), the counts of `tries` and `reads`, the `alert` decision (`KillRetryAlert`: `none`, `survivor` with `survivorDescription`, or `ordinary` with `lastKillFailedDescription` and/or `earlierSurvivorDescription`, each raw for the caller to redact) and, under `configReadEndsTries` on a `read-config` end only, `configRead` (the CONFIG read's error, raw). `configReadEndsTries` (off by default, so every server site keeps the `pending`-only CONFIG rule) makes a CONFIG read between tries end them whatever state was last read; only the CLI teardown sets it (`TEARDOWN_KILL_RETRY_OPTIONS`, `cli-teardown.ts`). The seed (`KillRetrySeed`: `killRetrySeedOfState(state)`, `KILL_RETRY_SEED_LIVE_UNREAD`, `KILL_RETRY_SEED_NOT_LIVE_VALUE`) is the row state the path last read; `killRetrySeedIsLive` is true for a known-live seed or a state other than `ended` and `missing`. A read answers a `KillRetryRead` (`state`, `no-row`, `latched` or `failed` with its error). `createKillRetryPassBudget()` is the start sweep's pass budget; `killRetryStopped(result)` is true when a latching read or the keep-going check ended the tries; `namesSurvivor(description)` is `survivorPids` (`ad-description-phrases.ts`) found non-empty, the only survivor detector. `runKillRetry` is generic over its tries' outcome form (`KillRetryOptions<O>`, `KillRetryResult<O>`, `O` a `KillOutcome` by default or an `AnyKillOutcome`), so a caller's GONE non-success is a failure end, logged and decided as one. Its users: the server's kill sites and the CLI teardown's kill (`teardownKill`, `cli.ts`, waiting on `CliDeps.sleep`). Its lines come from `killRetryTryLine`, `killRetryReadLine`, `killRetryStopLine`, `killRetryHoldEndedLine` and `killRetryEndLine`, every description redacted. Behaviour: [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104), **The bounded kill retry**.
    ├── kill-failure-alert.ts   b.jg5 SRJ-704 / SRJ-1007 / SRJ-1013 the kill-failure alert's texts and its route selection. Pure: no module-scope state, no environment or file access, no server-only import (no notifier, Slack client, latch, episodes, outage state or server module) and nothing at import, so any process that kills a row can build the same texts. Two versions (`KILL_FAILURE_VERSION_ORDINARY`, `KILL_FAILURE_VERSION_SURVIVOR`): `killFailureOrdinaryBody` (*Kill failed*) quotes the descriptions the bounded retry's `ordinary` decision carries (the last kill failure's, the latest survivor-naming one, or both in SRJ-1007's two-description form, the last kill failure's first) and leaves the "agent-director said" sentence out when it has none; `killFailureSurvivorBody` (*Process outlived kill*) quotes the latest survivor-naming description and lists the pids its survivor clause names, "pid S" each, joined with ", " (`killFailureSurvivorPidList`, which reads them only through `survivorPids`, `ad-description-phrases.ts`, so never the worker's own pid), and names no command. Every quoted description, the session and the instance id go through `renderLogMessageText` (redacted, one line, capped at 300 characters, b.jg5 SRJ-1001); a text built `forSlack` is then escaped once (`escapeSlackControlCharacters`), and a log line or entry is not. The closing sentences are the `KILL_FAILURE_*_CLOSING` constants, picked by `killFailureClosingSentence(version, closing)` from the rows `destination`, `destination-latched` (ordinary only; the survivor version takes its destination sentence), `cli-teardown` and `log-only`. `killFailureAlertText(content, closing, forSlack)` is the body, a space and the closing sentence; `killFailureAlertEntryText(ref, context, text)` is the log-line and entry form `<ref> (<context>): <text>`; its context (`KillFailureAlertEntryContext`) is one of `KILL_FAILURE_CONTEXTS` or, for a CLI teardown, `killFailureCliTeardownEntryContext(command)`, rendered by `renderKillFailureAlertEntryContext` as `CLI teardown, <command>` (`stop --stop-bots` or `clean_restart`, passed in as a plain string: the module imports neither `cli.ts` nor `cli-teardown.ts`). The contexts are `KILL_FAILURE_CONTEXTS`, in SRJ-1007's order: `start sweep`, `CLI teardown`, `persona teardown`, `old-life wait`, `stuck-launch abort`, `recovery`. `selectKillFailureAlertRoute({ version, context, configured, latched })` answers SRJ-704's route, first match wins (an overload types the `CLI teardown` context's answer as `KillFailureCliTeardownRoute`: log-only, printed, always with its class), with its class (`PERSONA_KILL_FAILED_LABEL`, `persona-kill-failed`; `PERSONA_KILL_SURVIVOR_LABEL`, `persona-kill-survivor`, for the survivor version on every route that writes an entry; `PERSONA_TEARDOWN_NOTICE_LABEL`, `persona-teardown-notice`, the persona teardown's, exported as the one constant that `persona-notifier.ts` imports and re-exports, since this pure module may load no notifier), whether the text is printed, whether it opens the persona's episode and its closing sentence; it is pure and never throws. Its callers: the kill-failure alerts (`persona-episodes.ts`), the start sweep (`session-manager.ts`) and the CLI teardown's report plan (`personaTeardownReportOf`, `cli-teardown.ts`). Behaviour: [The kill-failure alert](#the-kill-failure-alert-bjg5-srj-704-srj-1007).
    ├── live-row-sequence.ts    b.jg5 SRJ-705 / SRJ-706 / SRJ-717 / SRJ-710 the live-row sequence: the one way a persona's live row `cscb_<key>` (`pending` included) is replaced. `runLiveRowSequence(request, deps, stop)` runs one sequence and answers its outcome (`LiveRowSequenceOutcome`); it never throws or rejects and leaves no timer of its own pending once it settles. The request (`LiveRowSequenceRequest`) carries the key, the instance id, the state the starter last read, the entry step (`LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_ENTRY_KILL`, 1, or `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_ENTRY_GET`, 2, for a starter that made the first kill itself), the keep-conversation and retired-key flags, whether it ends in a launch (false is the no-launch form) and the kill-failure alert's context (one of `KILL_FAILURE_CONTEXTS`). `createLiveRowSequenceStop()` builds the stop signal (reasons `latched`, `teardown`, `shutdown`, `not-up`, and `hold-ended` for a no-launch request whose old-life hold ended, which, like `latched`, drops no answer). The pure `decideLiveRowLaunchKind` decides step 6's kind and reason; `liveRowLaunchSucceeded` reads a launch result against `LIVE_ROW_LAUNCH_SUCCESS_ACTIONS` (`fresh-retired` among them, b.jg5 SRJ-806 as amended by b.deo SRI-407); the pure `liveRowSequence*Line` builders build every line it logs, under `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_LOG_PREFIX` (`[slack] live-row-sequence:`). The pace and caps are exported: `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_RUN_SPACING_MS` (5 s), `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_STEP4_PAUSE_MS` (5 s), `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_STEP3_RUNS` (3), `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_MAX_RUNS` (`LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_STEP3_RUNS` + 1, step 3's runs and step 4's one: 4; b.jg5 SRJ-705), `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_MAX_KILLS` (2), `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_GRACE_REARM_MS` (5 s), the wait before step 2's G wait is armed again after the G accessor threw or answered NaN (never an early end; `liveRowSequenceWaitArmFailedLine`, and the armed line's `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_GRACE_UNREADABLE_TEXT` and `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_GRACE_NEVER_ENDS_TEXT`), and `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_GRACE_REARM_LOG_SPACING_MS` (60 s), the least time between two arm-failed lines of one wait whose description did not change. Every agent-director call, the latch, the alerts, the retry arm and the clock come through `LiveRowSequenceDeps`, which the session manager's `buildLiveRowSequenceDeps` binds: the checked kill inside the bounded retry (`retryPersonaKill`), the kill-failure alerts and their episodes, the shared own-row `get` and `status` reads, the bypassing `find-missing` entry, the G accessor and the sequence-launch entry; the wait arms through `armPendingRowWait` (`pending-row.ts`, never early) on the injected clock, with the raw launch start the step-2 `get` read. It holds no module-scope state, runs nothing at import, and loads neither the session manager, the server, the notifier nor any Slack module; it arms through its own cause names (`LIVE_ROW_ARM_NOT_JUDGED`, `LIVE_ROW_ARM_ENDED`, `LIVE_ROW_ARM_COLLISION`, `LIVE_ROW_ARM_LOST_RACE`), which the dependency builder maps to `unavailable-retry.ts`'s labels. Step 6's not-launched reasons include three for a `resume` that answered `ErrSpawnNotResumable`, after the entry's one re-read of the row (b.jg5 SRJ-710, never a second sequence): `not-resumable` (`LIVE_ROW_NOT_LAUNCHED_NOT_RESUMABLE`, a lost race, arming `LIVE_ROW_ARM_LOST_RACE`), `not-resumable-pending` (`LIVE_ROW_NOT_LAUNCHED_NOT_RESUMABLE_PENDING`, a launch in progress, arming `LIVE_ROW_ARM_ENDED`) and `not-resumable-latched` (`LIVE_ROW_NOT_LAUNCHED_NOT_RESUMABLE_LATCHED`, which the sequence ends as stopped for the latch, nothing armed). The registry, `createLiveRowSequenceRegistry({ deps, runAttempt, runOutsideAttempt? })` (b.jg5 SRJ-706, SRJ-811), is one per server and holds its state in the returned object: entries keyed by instance id, each recording its key and whether it ends in a launch. `start(request, options?)` starts a sequence without awaiting it and answers `started` (`LIVE_ROW_START_STARTED`; the sequence's first call comes after the answer), `already-running` (`LIVE_ROW_START_ALREADY_RUNNING`: a sequence already runs on that instance id, or, for a request that ends in a launch, another such request runs for that persona; nothing started) or `closed` (`LIVE_ROW_START_CLOSED`, after `close`), a refusal logging `liveRowSequenceNotStartedLine`; it never throws. A no-launch request (the old-life wait) is refused only by its instance id, so waits keyed by an old key never refuse a persona's own sequence on another id, and one wait runs per held id. `LiveRowSequenceStartOptions` lets a start give its own dependencies (`deps`, the wait's `buildOldLifeWaitDeps`) and an end handler (`onSettled`, told the outcome after the entry is dropped; a throw is ignored). `stop(key, reason)` sets the stop signal of that persona's sequence that ends in a launch before it returns, logs `liveRowSequenceStopAskedLine`, and resolves true once the sequence has settled (its call in flight returned, its end line logged), false at once when none runs; it never stops a no-launch request. `stopNoLaunch(instanceId, reason)` stops only the no-launch request on that id (the hold's end, `hold-ended`), never a sequence that ends in a launch; `stopAll(reason)` stops every one; `close()` stops every one, no-launch requests included, with `shutdown` and refuses every later start; none rejects. `isRunning(key)` is true from the start's answer until a sequence keyed by `key` settles, its step-6 launch included (a wait on a persona's own `cscb_<key>` counts), and `isNoLaunchRunning(instanceId)` while a no-launch request runs on that id; `_whenSettled(key)` and `_whenSettledOn(instanceId)` are test-only. Each sequence that ends in a launch runs inside the injected attempt runner (`LiveRowSequenceAttemptRunner`; production `runDetachedRecoveryAttempt`, `unavailable-retry.ts`), its own recovery attempt for the persona, detached from its starter's; a no-launch request runs through `runOutsideAttempt` (`LiveRowSequenceOutsideAttemptRunner`; production `runOutsideAttempts`), outside every attempt. An entry is removed when its sequence settles, whatever the outcome. Its production starters, both in `session-manager.ts` and both through `startLiveRowSequence`, answer `sequence-waiting`: the collision ladder's replace step (`replacePersonaRow`, b.jg5 SRJ-707): at a ladder site whose row cannot be kept (`resume_enabled` false, a `cwd` mismatch, a `config_dir` mismatch) and whose last-read state is live (`pending` and an unreadable state included), and at a retired key's old life (b.jg5 SRJ-805), it starts a sequence with that state as its seed, entry at step 1, the conversation not kept, the retired-key flag set for a retired key, ending in a launch, alert context `recovery`; and the ladder's not-resumable step (`spawnNotResumableAtLadder`, b.jg5 SRJ-710, SRJ-611): a `resume` that answered `ErrSpawnNotResumable` on a path holding dead evidence, whose re-read finds the row in a known live state other than `pending` (`AGENT_DIRECTOR_LIVE_STATES`), starts the same request seeded with the re-read state and with the conversation kept, so its step 6 is a `resume` when the row allows one. The abort of CSCB's own stuck launch (`startStuckLaunchAbortSequence`, b.jg5 SRJ-412) starts one more, entry at step 2 after its own kill, seeded `pending`, the conversation kept, alert context `stuck-launch abort`, and answers "sequence started". The no-launch form's one entry is the session manager's `ensureOldLifeWait` (b.jg5 SRJ-811), which the old-life hold step calls when it holds a launch back (b.jg5 SRJ-810). `LIVE_ROW_LAUNCH_CALL_SUCCESS_ACTIONS` names the successes that are a launch call's own, and `liveRowSequenceEndArmText(outcome)` is the end line's account of the retry timer (b.jg5 SRJ-301, SRJ-409). Behaviour: [The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717).
