    ├── ad-version-gate.ts      b.jg5 SRJ-201 / SRJ-202 / SRJ-208 / SRJ-204 / SRJ-205 / SRJ-206 / SRJ-211 / SRJ-212 CSCB's own Phase 1 floor for the agent-director binary, the two version refusal messages, the runtime version re-check and the host-version decision. No value import from `agent-director` (errors are classified by their `errName`, else `name`, read as a string; fields are read structurally), no child process and no file read; a stop holds no Slack sink and reaches only the injected `recordStartupError` and `stop` (b.jg5 SRJ-1002); nothing is armed, read or logged at import. `PHASE1_FLOOR_VERSION` is the floor (currently 0.11.0), the Phase 1 agent-director release's version, confirmed from the 0.11.0 release (tag `v0.11.0`; npm `agent-director@0.11.0`, the client `package.json` pins); code and tests read it from the constant, never a literal. `meetsPhase1Floor(version)` parses the version with the same strict rule as the installed client's parser (`major.minor.patch` with an optional `-prerelease`, no leading `v`, no `+build` metadata, no whitespace trimming), refuses a version that does not parse (fail closed), and compares major, minor and patch numerically against the floor's; the pre-release suffix is ignored, so `<floor>-rc.N` counts as `<floor>`. There is no development override: the client's `0.0.0-dev` sentinel compares as `0.0.0` and is refused. `PHASE1_RUNBOOK_SECTION_TITLE` is the title of the README runbook section for switching over to agent-director Phase 1; every message, test and doc that names the section takes the title from it. `PUBLISHING_HOST_BLOCK_HEADING` is the heading of that section's block "The publishing host" (b.jg5 SRJ-211, SRJ-1108), which covers the host that publishes the release and a host with no agent-director; the README's block heading equals it, and the install check's not-found message and `/publish`'s not-found and below-client-minimum diagnostics name it, as publishing-host contexts (the startup gate's not-found message does not: the gate runs on a bot host, where the binary may only be missing from the launcher's HOME or PATH beside a live store and workers) (tests import it from here). `PHASE1_REQUIRED_PHRASE` ("this CSCB release requires agent-director Phase 1 or later") is carried by every `ad-below-phase1-floor` entry (b.jg5 SRJ-1013); `PHASE1_SWITCH_OVER_INSTRUCTION`, that phrase followed by the instruction to follow the switch-over runbook in the README, is the startup gate's. A runtime re-check's entry of either class names the debug skill instead: `DEBUG_SKILL_RUNTIME_STOP_POINTER`, built from `DEBUG_SKILL_PATH` (`skills/debug-slack-channel-bots/SKILL.md`) and `DEBUG_SKILL_RUNTIME_STOP_SECTION_TITLE` ("Found while the server was running"), with no instruction to upgrade or install agent-director (b.jg5 SRJ-205, SRJ-208). `buildBelowPhase1FloorMessage({ foundVersion, binaryPath }, foundBy?)` and `buildSystemInstallTooOldMessage({ foundVersion, binaryPath, requiredVersion }, foundBy?)` build the `ad-below-phase1-floor` and `ad-system-install-too-old` messages; their startup form (the default, `FOUND_BY_STARTUP_CHECK`) is described under [Server-Managed Startup](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1) step 1. The runtime form (`FOUND_BY_RUNTIME_RECHECK`) replaces the floor message's "found by the startup check" with `RUNTIME_RECHECK_PHRASE` ("found by a runtime re-check while the server was running") plus ", so the server stopped", and adds the same clause after the too-old message's binary path; the startup forms never contain the phrase. The runtime floor message ends `Note: <PHASE1_REQUIRED_PHRASE>; <DEBUG_SKILL_RUNTIME_STOP_POINTER>.` and the runtime too-old message `This CSCB release and agent-director Phase 1 are installed together; <DEBUG_SKILL_RUNTIME_STOP_POINTER>.`, so neither names the switch-over runbook or the install skill; the startup forms keep the runbook (and the startup gate appends the install-skill block to the too-old one). **Host-version decision (SRJ-211).** `decideHostAdVersion(result, clientMinimum)` is the one decision on the host's agent-director binary against the installed client's minimum. Its inputs are one settled call of an injected `resolveSystemBinary()` (`HostVersionCallResult`: `resolved` with the result, or `rejected` with the thrown value) and the client's `min_binary_version`, which the caller reads (`readClientMinVersion` in `install-check.ts`); the module has no resolver of its own and reads no file. Both callers settle their one call with `settleHostVersionCall(resolve)`, which returns the resolved value or the thrown value (a synchronous throw counts as a rejection) and never rejects. The decision is pure and never throws. Rejections are read by name (`errName`, else `name`): `ErrSystemInstallNotFound` fails `not-found`; `ErrSystemInstallTooOld` fails `below-client-minimum` from the error's `actualVersion`, `requiredVersion` and `binaryPath`; `ErrSystemInstallUnreachable` (any reason) fails `version-unreadable`, carrying a `reason` word: the error's own reason when it is a short safe word (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens), else `unknown` (`UNREACHABLE_REASON_UNKNOWN`, not one of agent-director's reasons); any other named error or non-error throw fails `other` with the re-check's token-free description. For a resolved call: a client minimum that does not parse fails `client-minimum-unreadable`; a missing version, or one the client's strict rule cannot parse (a leading `v` included), fails `version-unreadable` with reason `unparseable-version` (`UNREACHABLE_REASON_UNPARSEABLE_VERSION`); a version below the minimum fails `below-client-minimum`; a version at or above the minimum passes (`pass`) when it meets the Phase 1 floor (`meetsPhase1Floor`), else passes below the floor (`pass-below-floor`: `0.10.0`, or the sentinel `0.0.0-dev`). The outcome kinds are the `HOST_VERSION_OUTCOME_*` constants and the failure kinds the `HOST_VERSION_FAIL_*` constants. Two helpers are shared with the install check: `readField(value, key)` reads one property of any value without throwing (`undefined` for a non-object, a missing property or a throwing getter), and `redactToOneLine(text)` returns the text as one token-free line (token- and URL-like text redacted by `redactSlackLogText`, each run of `\r`, `\n`, U+2028 and U+2029 collapsed to one space); the decision's own path and version texts go through it too. The minimum comparison follows the client's own order, `compareAdVersions(a, b)` (-1, 0, 1, or `null` when either does not parse): `CLIENT_DEV_SENTINEL_VERSION` (`0.0.0-dev`, mirroring the client's `DEV_SENTINEL_VERSION`) ranks above every version, cores compare numerically, a release ranks above its own pre-release and pre-release tags compare as strings. So `0.0.0-dev` is above every client minimum yet below CSCB's floor, which gives it no sentinel treatment. A `pass-below-floor` outcome carries a note, which each caller builds. `buildPhase1HostNote({ foundVersion, binaryPath })` builds `/publish`'s: the version and path, the floor (release candidates included), `PHASE1_HOST_NOTE_PHRASE` ("this CSCB release needs agent-director Phase 1 on the host"), that the binary meets the client's minimum so it is accepted, and the runbook section's title from `PHASE1_RUNBOOK_SECTION_TITLE`; no upgrade instruction, command or link. `buildInstallCheckPhase1Note(foundVersion)` builds the install check's (SRJ-212): the version, the floor (release candidates included), `INSTALL_CHECK_PHASE1_NOTE_PHRASE` ("the server refuses to start on it until agent-director Phase 1 is installed") and the runbook section's title; no upgrade instruction, command or link. The decision has two callers: `/publish`'s preflight check `scripts/ad-version-check.ts` (gate SR-2.5) and `runInstallCheck()` in `install-check.ts` (see there). `/publish`'s script (publish-time only, not shipped) reads the client minimum first and exits 15 without calling the resolver when it cannot be read; otherwise it makes one resolver call and applies the decision: a pass writes one `SR-2.5 (preflight)` line to stdout and exits 0, a pass below the floor adds the note on stderr as `SR-2.5 (preflight) NOTE: <note>`, and a failure writes one `SR-2.5 (preflight)` diagnostic naming the runbook section to stderr and exits 15 (`AD_VERSION_CHECK_FAIL_EXIT_CODE`). The not-found and below-client-minimum diagnostics' recovery is to follow the section's block "The publishing host" (`PUBLISHING_HOST_BLOCK_HEADING`), then rerun `/publish`; no diagnostic advises installing or upgrading agent-director, or editing `package.json`'s agent-director version. Its `runAdVersionCheck(deps)` takes the resolver with no default; only its `main()` passes the client's `resolveSystemBinary`. `scripts/preflight.sh` runs it and exits 15 on any non-zero status, writing its own diagnostic (naming the runbook section) when the status is not 15. **Runtime re-check (SRJ-204, SRJ-205, SRJ-206).** `decideAdVersionRecheckOutcome(result)` maps one settled `resolveSystemBinary()` call to one outcome: a version that meets the floor passes (it becomes the last version seen); a version below the floor or one that does not parse (`0.0.0-dev` included) stops as `ad-below-phase1-floor` with the runtime floor message; a rejection named `ErrSystemInstallTooOld` stops as `ad-system-install-too-old` with the runtime too-old message built from the error's `actualVersion`, `requiredVersion` and `binaryPath`, which points to the debug skill and has no install-skill block; anything else (`ErrSystemInstallUnreachable`, `ErrSystemInstallNotFound`, any other error, a non-error throw, the time limit) could not run, and nothing changes; its token-free description is the error's name (for `ErrSystemInstallUnreachable` also its reason and binary path, as `ErrSystemInstallUnreachable (reason <reason>, binary at <path>)`), the thrown value's type (`a thrown string`, `a thrown null`, `an error with no readable name`) or `no answer within the 30 s time limit`. `createAdVersionRecheck(deps)` builds the timer over an injected clock (`AdVersionRecheckClock`, real timers by default): a serialized, self-re-arming `setTimeout` chain (never `setInterval`) whose first re-check runs `AD_VERSION_RECHECK_INTERVAL_MS` (120 s) after `start()` and each next one `AD_VERSION_RECHECK_INTERVAL_MS` after the previous one ends, so no two checks are acted on at once and at most one call is awaited. It is independent of `health_check_interval`, `0` included. Each call is bounded by `AD_VERSION_RECHECK_TIME_LIMIT_MS` (30 s) on the same clock; a call past it counts as could not run and is abandoned, not ended: it may still be running when a later check makes the next call, and its answer is ignored. `resolveSystemBinary` has no default here: `main()` passes it in, with the startup gate's `adVersion` as the baseline. A stop ends the chain (every timer cleared, a call in flight never acted on), calls `recordStartupError(classLabel, message)` once, then the `stop` callback once with `AD_VERSION_RECHECK_STOP_EXIT_CODE` (1). Could not run (SRJ-206): the server keeps running and the re-check keeps its schedule; the first could-not-run result after `start()` or after a passing re-check (timed or triggered) starts a run of failures and writes one server-log line, `buildAdVersionRecheckCouldNotRunLine(description)` (prefix `AD_VERSION_RECHECK_COULD_NOT_RUN_LOG_PREFIX`); the rest of the run writes nothing, and the next pass ends the run. It is never a `startup-errors.log` entry and never a Slack post. A pass whose version differs from the last version seen (the baseline is the startup gate's `adVersion`) makes it the last version seen and then runs each version-changed listener once, in registration order, with the previous and the new version; a listener that throws or rejects is logged as one line and the rest still run. `trigger()` runs one re-check at once through the same call, decision, failure run and stop path and answers with the outcome it acted on (passed with the version and path, stopped, could not run), or `not-running` (`RECHECK_OUTCOME_NOT_RUNNING`) with no call before `start()`, after `dispose()` or after a stop, and at once when the re-check is disposed while the check it joined is in flight (without waiting for the call, whose later answer is never acted on); it never rejects. The timer and every trigger share one check in flight: a trigger during a timed or triggered check joins it, and a timed re-check that comes due during a triggered check joins it too, then arms the next 120 s timer and runs the tick listeners as usual; either way one call is made and its outcome is acted on once. A trigger never moves the pending timer and runs no tick listener. After each timed re-check that did not stop (could-not-run ones included) the next timer is armed and then the tick listeners run; never on a stopping tick or after `dispose()`. A listener that throws or rejects is logged as one line and the chain carries on. The tick hook's consumer is the re-read of agent-director's timing settings (`installAdSettings`, `ad-settings.ts`, b.jg5 SRJ-209), so that file is read again at each timed re-check that did not stop, whatever `health_check_interval` is (`0` included), and never on a stopping tick, on a trigger or after `dispose()`. Module-level wiring for `server.ts`: `installAdVersionRecheck(deps)` builds and starts the one re-check with the listeners registered through `onAdVersionRecheckTick(listener)` and `onAdVersionChanged(listener)` (each returns its unsubscribe and may register before or after the install); a second install, or one after dispose, is a logged no-op. `triggerAdVersionRecheck()` triggers the installed re-check and answers `not-running` when none is installed, it was disposed or it already stopped. Its caller is the `ErrInvalidFlags` step in `ad-error-class.ts`, which the reuse spawn (`reuseSpawnForPersona`, whose re-check answer decides the `ErrInvalidFlags` hold, b.jg5 SRJ-207), the `resume` at either `resume` site, every plain spawn (`plainSpawnOutcomeAt`), the shared read-pane and the reconnect's `send-keys` (`session-manager.ts`) and the click handler's `decide` (`permission-click-handler.ts`) run on an `ErrInvalidFlags` (see [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)). Its consumer is the `ErrInvalidFlags` hold (`invalid-flags-hold.ts`, b.jg5 SRJ-207): `main()` registers one `onAdVersionChanged` listener that ends every hold whose version differs from the new one, or that began under none, and retries each ended persona at once ([The `ErrInvalidFlags` hold](#the-errinvalidflags-hold-bjg5-srj-207-srj-1008)). `lastAdVersionSeen()` answers the installed re-check's last version seen (its baseline until a pass changes it), or `undefined` when none is installed, it was disposed or a stop ended it (the instance's `isRunning()` answers whether it runs); a hold begins under it when the reuse spawn's immediate re-check could not run or was not running. `disposeAdVersionRecheck()` (idempotent) disposes it (a trigger waiting on its check in flight answers `not-running` at once) and blocks any later install. `resetAdVersionRecheckForTests()` disposes the installed re-check and clears the handle, the disposed flag and both listener registries.

Constants only, no state and no I/O, so the CLI teardown (`cli-teardown.ts`) names the file without importing the settings reader; `ad-settings.ts` re-exports the path and `cli-teardown.ts` the display name.
    ├── ad-settings.ts          b.jg5 SRJ-209 agent-director's timing settings, read the way agent-director reads them. agent-director offers no interface that reports its effective timing values, so CSCB reads `~/.agent-director/config.toml` itself (`AD_SETTINGS_RELATIVE_PATH`, defined in `ad-config-file.ts` and re-exported here) under the server process's HOME: `productionAdSettingsHome()` is `process.env.HOME` at read time, else `os.homedir()` when `HOME` is unset. It reads the nine `[tmux]` keys (`AD_TMUX_KEYS`, in the fixed order the rule checks them: `pending_grace_seconds`, `stopping_window_seconds`, `starting_session_seconds`, `sweep_budget_seconds`, `query_timeout_ms`, `action_timeout_ms`, `create_timeout_ms`, `pipe_close_wait_ms`, `kill_exit_wait_ms`) and `[pause] timeout_seconds`. The file goes through `readPersonaConfigBytes` (`config.ts`, the stat-first reader with the 64 KiB cap, so a FIFO or device never hangs a read), is decoded as strict UTF-8 and is parsed only with `smol-toml` (pinned exactly in `package.json`) with integers as `BigInt`, so a float such as `60.0` is not an integer; CSCB never parses TOML by hand, and every value is kept as the `bigint` read. The defaults (`DEFAULT_AD_SETTINGS`: 60, 90, 300, 15, 1500, 2000, 5000, 100 and 5000 in key order, and `pause` 30 s) and the minimums (`AD_SETTING_MINIMUMS`: `starting_session_seconds` 60, `stopping_window_seconds` 30, and `pending_grace_seconds` the larger of 30 and ⌈(`create_timeout_ms` + `pipe_close_wait_ms`) / 1000⌉ + 20, `pendingGraceMinimumSeconds`, so 30 at the defaults and 61 with `create_timeout_ms` 40000) are named constants that live only in this module; no other module in `src/` holds one. `kill_exit_wait_ms`'s 5000 is the 0.11.0 release's default: its release notes list the key under the `[tmux]` settings, and the value is `DefaultKillExitWaitMs` in agent-director's `internal/config/tmux.go` at tag `v0.11.0`. **The rule.** A missing file (ENOENT only) gives every default; a missing key, or 0, gives that key's default; the other six keys have no minimum. A read is refused when the home getter throws (reason `the home directory cannot be found`; the line's path is then `~/.agent-director/config.toml`), when the file exists but cannot be read (a directory, a non-regular file, over the cap, a permission or I/O error, a path component that is not a directory), is not valid UTF-8 or not valid TOML, when `tmux` is not a table, or when one of the nine keys is not a TOML integer (a string, a float, `60.0` included), is negative, is above `AD_SETTING_INTEGER_MAX` (2^63 − 1, the top of Go's `int64`, which agent-director's nine `[tmux]` fields use; agent-director's TOML parser refuses the whole file for a larger integer, while `smol-toml` reads one as a `BigInt`, so CSCB checks the bound itself; reason `[tmux] <key> is too large for agent-director`), or has an effective value below its minimum (the grace minimum is computed from the read's effective `create_timeout_ms` and `pipe_close_wait_ms`, a refused value of either counting as its default). The reason is the first broken rule in key order. Other keys and tables are ignored, so a misspelt key leaves its default in force. `[pause] timeout_seconds` has its own rule and never refuses the read: missing (or no file) gives 30, a positive integer up to `AD_SETTING_INTEGER_MAX` is used as given, and 0, a negative value, an integer above `AD_SETTING_INTEGER_MAX` (the top of Go's `int` on agent-director's 64-bit builds), any other kind or a `pause` that is not a table is "not used" (`AdPauseTimeout` `not-used`, with `found` describing it by integer, as `an integer too large for agent-director`, or by kind only). **The reader.** `createAdSettingsReader({ home, fs?, log })` returns an `AdSettingsReader`: `read()` never throws and answers `accepted` (the values replace those in effect and end a run of refused reads) or `refused` with a token-free reason (nothing changes); `valuesInEffect()` answers the last accepted read's values, else `DEFAULT_AD_SETTINGS_IN_EFFECT`. The reader's first accepted read (a missing file included), and each later accepted read whose nine `[tmux]` values differ from those in effect, writes the values line (`buildAdSettingsValuesLine`: the path and the nine values in `AD_TMUX_KEYS` order, each with its unit from `adTmuxKeyUnit`, `s` or `ms`); an accepted read that changes only `[pause] timeout_seconds`, or nothing, writes none, and a throwing log sink changes no value. The first refused read after start or after an accepted read writes one log line (`buildAdSettingsRefusedReadLine`, see [Logging](#agent-director-settings-lines-bjg5-srj-209)); the rest of the run writes nothing. No reason carries the parser's message, the file's text or a string value: a parse failure is reported by line and column, a read failure by its errno code (or `not a regular file`), a wrong-typed value by its kind. The read makes no agent-director call, raises no outage, records no startup error and posts nothing. **Wiring.** `installAdSettings(deps?)` builds the server's reader (production dependencies unless given), runs the startup read and registers `read()` on the version re-check's tick hook (`onAdVersionRecheckTick`, `ad-version-gate.ts`); it arms no timer of its own, and a second install is a logged no-op returning the installed reader. `main()` calls it once (see [Server-Managed Startup](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1)). `adSettingsInEffect()` answers the installed reader's values, else the defaults; `resetAdSettingsForTests()` removes the tick listener and forgets the reader. **The derived waits (b.jg5 SRJ-210).** From a values record the module derives three waits, in milliseconds: G, the grace period (`adGraceMs`), is `pending_grace_seconds`; the alert threshold (`adAlertThresholdMs`) is the longer of `stopping_window_seconds` and `starting_session_seconds`, plus `AD_ALERT_THRESHOLD_ADDEND_SECONDS` (60 s); B, CSCB's launch bound (`adLaunchBoundMs`), is the later of `DIALOG_READY_TIMEOUT_MS` (300 s, B's floor, defined in this module; `session-manager.ts` imports it from here and re-exports it) and G plus `AD_LAUNCH_BOUND_GRACE_ADDEND_SECONDS` (60 s). At the defaults G is 60 s, the threshold 360 s and B 300 s; with `pending_grace_seconds` 120, `stopping_window_seconds` 30 and `starting_session_seconds` 120 they are 120 s, 180 s and 300 s; with `pending_grace_seconds` 300, B is 360 s. Each wait is computed exactly from the `bigint` values and is a millisecond `number` only when it is at most `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`; a longer one is `AD_WAIT_NEVER_ENDS` (`Infinity`), never a rounded-down number. `adGraceMsInEffect()`, `adAlertThresholdMsInEffect()` and `adLaunchBoundMsInEffect()` derive from `adSettingsInEffect()` each time they are called, so a wait is checked against the values in effect when it is checked (a plain `elapsed >= wait` comparison, which never holds for `AD_WAIT_NEVER_ENDS`); nothing keeps a copy from the start. `wholeMinutes(ms)` renders a derived value for a notice in whole minutes, rounded down (360 s gives 6, 359 s gives 5). The alert threshold's consumer is the `tmux-unresponsive` condition's alert check (`persona-episodes.ts`): it waits on `adAlertThresholdMsInEffect` through the never-early wait below and states the minutes with `wholeMinutes` ([Its three posts](#its-three-posts-bjg5-srj-308-srj-309-srj-1006)). **The never-early wait.** A runtime timer longer than `MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS` (2^31 − 1 ms, about 24.8 days; imported from `persona-retry-schedule.ts`, not redefined) fires almost at once, so `armNeverEarlyWait(clock, startMs, waitMs, callback)` (`waitMs` is `NeverEarlyWaitLength`: a fixed number, or a getter such as `adLaunchBoundMsInEffect`) arms a derived wait on the caller's injected clock (`NeverEarlyWaitClock`: `now`, `setTimeout`, `clearTimeout`) as a chain of timers, one pending at a time, none longer than that maximum. When a timer fires the callback runs once only if `clock.now() - startMs` has reached the wait in effect; otherwise the helper re-arms for the smaller of the time left and `MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS`, so a setting too large for the runtime's timers never makes a wait end early. A fixed number is the wait for the whole arm. A getter is read at the arm and again at every timer fire, so the wait is checked against the values in effect at each fire, never a copy from the arm: a value raised while armed never ends the wait at the old deadline, and a lowered value is seen at the next fire (the callback runs then if the lowered deadline has passed, otherwise the next timer ends exactly at it), so a lowered wait ends at most `MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS` after it was lowered. While the getter answers `AD_WAIT_NEVER_ENDS` (or NaN, or throws, at a fire, which counts as never-ends for that fire, silently) the helper keeps one `MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS` timer pending and checks again. The callback always runs from a timer, never during the arm call; a fixed `AD_WAIT_NEVER_ENDS` arms nothing; the returned cancel is idempotent; a non-finite `startMs`, a NaN fixed `waitMs` or a getter whose value at the arm is NaN throws a `RangeError` before anything is armed, and a getter that throws at the arm throws out of the call. These waits are CSCB's own bounds only: wherever agent-director gives its own answer, that answer decides, whatever the settings say. The read arms no timer; the helper's timers are the only ones this module arms, on the clock its caller passes. **The ceilings and the need (b.jg5 SRJ-213).** agent-director's verb ceilings (ADSRD SR-13.2 is their single source) are computed exactly from the `bigint` values in effect, in milliseconds (`adVerbCeilingsMs`), with Q, A, C, W and E the `[tmux]` keys `query_timeout_ms`, `action_timeout_ms`, `create_timeout_ms`, `pipe_close_wait_ms` and `kill_exit_wait_ms`, and B `sweep_budget_seconds` times 1000: `kill` max(2Q + 2A + E + 4W, 3Q + 2A + 5W); `read-pane` 3Q + A + 4W; `send-keys` 3Q + 2A + 5W; `pause` 3Q + 2A + 5W plus `[pause] timeout_seconds` times 1000 when that value is used (without it when it is not used); `resume`, `spawn-with-reuse` and `plain-spawn` max(Q + C + 2A + 4W, 2Q + C + 3W); `find-missing` and `expire` B + Q + W. At the defaults: 12.4, 6.9, 9, 39, 10.9 and 16.6 s. `AD_CEILING_VERBS` lists the verbs in table order, each marked with whether CSCB calls it (every verb but `expire`). The need (`adCallTimeoutNeed`) is the largest ceiling among the verbs CSCB calls plus `AD_CALL_TIMEOUT_NEED_MARGIN_MS` (15 s: the store's 10 s busy timeout and 5 s to start agent-director's CLI), a named constant that lives only in this module; a tie names the earlier verb in table order, so the launch row's `setBy` is `resume`, and the warning line names that row by its three verbs, `resume/spawn-with-reuse/plain-spawn` (`AD_LAUNCH_CEILING_VERBS`). It is 54 s at the defaults (set by `pause`), 60.9 s with `create_timeout_ms` 40000 and `pending_grace_seconds` 61 (`setBy` `resume`; the line names `resume/spawn-with-reuse/plain-spawn`) and 84 s with `[pause] timeout_seconds` 60. When `[pause] timeout_seconds` is not used, `pause` counts without its wait and the need's `setBy` is `unused-pause-value`, carrying the token-free `found` of `AdPauseTimeout`. **The startup check.** `checkAdCallTimeoutAtStartup(callTimeoutMs, { log, valuesInEffect? })` computes the need from the values in effect and writes `buildAdCallTimeoutWarningLine`'s line, if one is due (see [Logging](#agent-director-settings-lines-bjg5-srj-209)): when the setting is at or below the need (compared exactly: ⌈setting⌉ ≤ need, NaN counting as at or below), or, whatever the setting, when `[pause] timeout_seconds` is not used, one line naming the unused value where it would name the verb. It writes at most one line, never throws (the build and the log sink are both guarded), never stops the start, changes no value, arms nothing and registers nothing. The server runs it once per start (Server-Managed Startup step 2c), never on the 120 s tick. **Imports.** At run time the module imports only `node:os`, `node:path`, `smol-toml`, `config.ts`, `ad-version-gate.ts` (`onAdVersionRecheckTick`, `PHASE1_RUNBOOK_SECTION_TITLE`) and `persona-retry-schedule.ts` (`MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS`), plus the `PersonaConnectionClock` type from `persona-connections.ts` and the `ServerSettings` type from `config.ts` (type-only). It loads none of the agent-director package, client, outage-state, notifier or Slack modules, directly or through the modules it imports. It does not import `session-manager.ts`; `session-manager.ts` imports this module for the dialog approver's waits, so there is no cycle. Nothing is read, armed or logged at import. No other module reads the derived waits or the never-early wait helper: `server.ts` imports this module for `installAdSettings`, `adAlertThresholdMsInEffect` (handed to the `tmux-unresponsive` condition) and, in its call-timeout start step, `adSettingsInEffect` and `checkAdCallTimeoutAtStartup`; `persona-episodes.ts` imports `armNeverEarlyWait` and `wholeMinutes`; `pending-row.ts` imports `armNeverEarlyWait` for `armPendingRowWait`, the arm of every wait on a `pending` row ([Launch pending](#launch-pending-bjg5-srj-406-srj-408)); and `session-manager.ts` imports, for the dialog approver, `DIALOG_READY_TIMEOUT_MS`, `adLaunchBoundMsInEffect` (B), `adGraceMsInEffect` (G) and `armNeverEarlyWait` (see [Pre-session dialog approval](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1)), and binds `adGraceMsInEffect` as the live-row sequence's G; `live-row-sequence.ts` imports `AD_WAIT_NEVER_ENDS` and the clock type for its step-2 wait, which it arms through `armPendingRowWait` with the G accessor itself, so G is read from the settings in effect at the arm and at every timer fire and the wait never ends early ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717)).
    ├── shutdown-deadline.ts    b.jg5 SRJ-205 the bounded fallback exit for a runtime version re-check stop. `armShutdownDeadline({ exitCode, exit, log, deadlineMs?, clock? })` arms one timer on the injected clock (`ShutdownDeadlineClock`, real timers by default) after `deadlineMs` (default `SHUTDOWN_DEADLINE_MS`, 30 s, the CLI `stop`'s default `stop_timeout`, so a re-check stop gets the same grace a signal stop gets before SIGKILL) and returns an idempotent cancel (a cancel after expiry does nothing). On expiry it logs one token-free line, `buildShutdownDeadlineLine(deadlineMs, exitCode)` (`[slack] Shutdown did not complete within 30 s — exiting with code 1` as `main()` arms it), then calls `exit(exitCode)` once; a logger that throws does not stop the exit. Nothing is armed, read or logged at import. `main()` arms it with `process.exit` and the re-check's exit code from the re-check's `stop` callback, then sets `process.exitCode` to that code, before calling `shutdown`; signals arm none (see [Graceful Shutdown](#graceful-shutdown-sr-11-event-11)).
    ├── install-skill-pointer.ts   SR-4.5 / SR-9.3 manual-skill-install instructions block. Renders a multi-line string containing the GitHub URL of `skills/install-cscb/SKILL.md` (derived from `package.json` `repository.url`), the target path `~/.claude/skills/install-cscb/SKILL.md`, and the invocation command `/install-cscb`. The startup gate appends this block to the three `ad-system-install-*` typed-error failure messages only — never to `ad-below-phase1-floor`, `ErrBunVersionTooOld`, the three `ad-shim-*` branches, or the same-user check. The skill walks the operator through the diagnosis: for `ad-system-install-not-found` it names the README switch-over runbook section's block "The publishing host" (after the startup gate's refusal on a bot host, that section's step 1 version check instead), and for `ad-system-install-too-old` the section, and runs nothing; it runs no agent-director install, reinstall or upgrade and offers no such command (b.jg5 SRJ-208).
    ├── install-check.ts           b.jg5 SRJ-212 the agent-director install check. `runInstallCheck(deps?)` reads the installed client's minimum with `readClientMinVersion()`, makes one call to the injected resolver (`InstallCheckDeps.resolveSystemBinary`, default the client's own `resolveSystemBinary`; tests pass a stub) and applies the host-version decision `decideHostAdVersion` from `ad-version-gate.ts`, shared with `/publish`'s check; it classifies agent-director errors by name through that decision, never `instanceof`, and never throws. Outcomes: a binary that meets CSCB's Phase 1 floor passes; one at or above the client's minimum but below the floor (`0.10.0`, the client's `0.0.0-dev` sentinel) passes with the success result's optional `note` (`buildInstallCheckPhase1Note`, naming the runbook section); any other outcome fails with one of four class labels: `ad-system-install-not-found`, `ad-system-install-too-old` (below the client's minimum, message from `buildSystemInstallTooOldMessage`, which names the runbook section and advises no upgrade), `ad-system-install-unreachable` (an `ErrSystemInstallUnreachable` of any reason, with the decision's reason word, so a reason that is absent or not a short safe word reports `unknown`; a resolved version that does not parse as reason `unparseable-version`; or any other failure as reason `other`, described by its name or type and never its own message) and `ad-version-floor-unreadable` (the client's `dist/version-floor.json` cannot be read, or its `min_binary_version` is missing or not a version). A failure's `detail` keeps the thrown error's structural fields, each text as one token-free line through `redactToOneLine`: an unreachable error's `diagnostic` and `signal` (`null` when not a string; `exitCode` kept only when a number, else `null`), a not-found error's `checkedLocations` (each entry copied as `{ kind, detail }`, both texts redacted; an empty list when the field is not a list) and a failed floor read's `underlying` (the thrown value's message, else `null`). A binary that passes with the note is still refused by the startup gate (`ad-below-phase1-floor`). Side-effect-free: no `process.exit`, no disk writes, no stdout/stderr. Consumed by `scripts/install-check.ts` (the `bun run install-check` diagnostic, which prints the note as the last line of its OK block, under `INSTALL_CHECK_NOTE_LABEL`), the install-cscb skill (through that script, relaying the note) and the npm postinstall probe (`postinstall.ts`). `readClientMinVersion(deps?)` returns the installed client's `min_binary_version` (or the `ad-version-floor-unreadable` failure, one per failure mode: the subpath cannot be resolved, the file cannot be read, it does not parse as JSON, or the field is missing or not a non-empty string). Its optional `ClientMinVersionDeps` are `resolveFloorUrl` (default `import.meta.resolve` of `agent-director/dist/version-floor.json`; a throw is the resolve failure, a non-`file:` URL a read failure) and `readFile` (default `readFileSync` as UTF-8; a throw is the read failure). With no deps, or an empty deps object, the value or the failure is cached (`resetCacheForTests` / `setFloorForTests` reset and seed the cache in tests); a call with any dep injected bypasses the cache, neither returning the cached value nor storing its own result; `/publish`'s preflight check `scripts/ad-version-check.ts` reads it too. The class-label constants and the `InstallCheckClassLabel` type live in `install-check-labels.ts` and are re-exported here. **Remedy texts (b.jg5 SRJ-208, SRJ-212, SRJ-1101).** Three exported constants carry every remedy that names the README's switch-over runbook section, and the startup gate's messages use two of them: `RUNBOOK_SECTION_POINTER` (the section by its title; the startup gate's not-found message names it with its step 1 version check), `PUBLISHING_HOST_BLOCK_POINTER` (its block "The publishing host", in the install check's not-found message only, "which covers a host with no agent-director") and `CLIENT_PACKAGE_REMEDY` ("Check the agent-director npm package installed with CSCB; see" the section, in the five `ad-version-floor-unreadable` texts). The unreachable message says to diagnose with the install-cscb skill and names the section; the `other` failure names the section or says to file a bug. No message advises installing, reinstalling, upgrading or removing anything. The startup gate does not call `runInstallCheck()`: it builds the client with `Client.create()` and applies the Phase 1 floor itself, and imports only the class-label constants, so both emit the same strings.
    ├── install-check-labels.ts    The agent-director class labels (`AD_SYSTEM_INSTALL_NOT_FOUND`, `AD_SYSTEM_INSTALL_TOO_OLD`, `AD_SYSTEM_INSTALL_UNREACHABLE`, `AD_VERSION_FLOOR_UNREADABLE`, `AD_BELOW_PHASE1_FLOOR`, `AD_SHIM_CATALOG_INCOMPLETE`) and the `InstallCheckClassLabel` type (the first four, which the install check writes; the not-found, too-old and unreachable labels are shared with the startup gate, and the last two only the startup gate writes). A leaf module with no imports, so `ad-version-gate.ts` takes its labels from here and never imports `install-check.ts` (which imports `agent-director`); `install-check.ts` re-exports all of it.
    ├── agent-director-template.ts SR-3.1 / SR-3.2 / b.av2 SR-8.6 step 5 (as amended by b.deo SRI-805) — builds the slack-channel-bot MakeTemplateParams and calls client.makeTemplate({ overwrite: true }). `installSlackChannelBotTemplate(personaConfig, deps?)` is the boot install: fatal on any rejection (records `ad-template-install` and exits 1), and it resolves `InstalledTemplate`, agent-director's result plus the `params` it installed. `refreshSlackChannelBotTemplate(applied, installed, { getClient, log, home? })` is the apply-time refresh: `installed` with its memory-read `allow` rules derived afresh from `applied` (`deriveMemoryReadAllowRules`, the boot derivation, so never a config-dir root) and every other field, `claude_args` included, as the boot install wrote it. It never rejects and never exits: it logs one `[slack] template refresh:` line and resolves `{ kind: 'refreshed', path }` or `{ kind: 'failed' }`; nothing retries it. Importable without side effects.
    ├── session-manager.ts      SR-1 in full — startupSessionManager (one bring-up and one spawnForPersona per persona), spawnForPersona (SR-1.4 collision-then-act, persona-keyed; its first spawn is plain, with no reuse flag, b.jg5 SRJ-711, and an `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` at any launch is one counted launch failure that kills nothing and makes no spawn in its place, b.jg5 SRJ-602; its `resume`'s outcomes follow b.jg5 SRJ-113 and its `ErrSpawnNotResumable` b.jg5 SRJ-710), launchSession (restart relaunch by persona key), reconcileOrphans (the persona-keyed start sweep, b.av2 SR-6.3, b.jg5 SRJ-116: one `list`, its latch pass `latchFromListedRows`, the `absent-at-start` recording `recordAbsentPersonaKeys`, then the kills of live strays, each checked and none followed by a delete (`killStartSweepRow`), one post-kill findMissing over every row given a kill (`runStartSweepPostKillFindMissing`) and the summary line (`startSweepSummaryLine`); b.jg5 SRJ-714, SRJ-1506; Server-Managed Startup step 4), reconnectMcp/waitForWaitingAndReconnect. The reconnect (`reconnectMcpWithCause(key, lastRead, ref?)`, with the row state its caller last read; `reconnectMcp` answers its outcome alone) makes exactly one `send-keys` of `/mcp reconnect`, never retries, starts no tmux server and makes no tmux call of its own (b.jg5 SRJ-118, SRJ-609); for a persona whose own `cscb_<key>` is held for an old life (`isOwnRowOldLifeHeld`, b.jg5 SRJ-810) it makes none, arms the persona's timer with `held-for-old-life` and answers `transient` (`reconnectHeldLine`). It decides its answer by class through `ad-error-class.ts`: `ReconnectOutcome` is `ok`, `dead-session` with a `DeadSessionCause` (`tmux-gone`, `row-not-interactive` or `row-absent`), or `transient` (nothing typed, never counted, no spawn-failure notice; marked `latched` when it latched or found the persona latched, `stopping` when its `ErrInvalidFlags` re-check stopped the server). Its lines come from exported builders (`reconnectStartLine`, `reconnectLatchedLine`, `reconnectGoneLine`, `reconnectNotInteractiveLine`, `reconnectRowAbsentLine`, `reconnectConflictLine` with `RECONNECT_NOT_THIS_LAUNCH_NOTE`, `reconnectUnusableNameLine`, `reconnectInvalidFlagsLine`, `reconnectTransientLine`), and the ladder's line for a `transient` one from `transientReconnectLine`; `escalateDeadVerdictOfCause` gives the escalate-dead verdict for each cause (see Server-Managed Startup step 5, the `waiting` branch). Dead evidence (b.jg5 SRJ-611; [Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611)): `DEAD_SESSION_CAUSES` and `ESCALATE_DEAD_VERDICTS` list every `DeadSessionCause` (the reconnect's three, plus `row-read-finished` for the launch wait's finished-row read and `prompt-row-ladder-gone` for the ladder's prompt-row GONE) and every `EscalateDeadVerdict`; `isDeadEvidence(source)` decides each by an exhaustive switch, true only for the GONE-based ones and false, fail safe, for any other value, `undefined` and `DEAD_EVIDENCE_NONE`; `carriedDeadEvidenceOf` builds the `CarriedDeadEvidence` (`{ source, evidence }`) a path carries, `CARRIED_DEAD_EVIDENCE_NONE` for none (the type carries a type-only brand that only these two supply, so a value built by hand fails the typecheck, and `evidence` is always `isDeadEvidence(source)`); `describeDeadEvidence` renders it for the lines; `waitForWaitingAndReconnectWithCause` gives the launch wait's `dead-session` with its cause (`WaitDeadSession`); `launchSession(key, config, { canLaunch?, deadEvidence? })` and `spawnForPersona(persona, config, isStartup?, hooks?, deadEvidence?)` take the escalate-dead verdict the restart path's relaunch carries, which the ladder keeps for its run until a read of the row as finished or gone, or a reconnect's `row-not-interactive`, voids it (`voidDeadEvidence`, one `deadEvidenceVoidedLine` per voided piece; [Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611), **Dead evidence covers one life**); the line builders are `deadSessionRouteLine`, `waitRowFinishedLine`, `waitRowAbsentLine`, `promptRowSweepFinishedLine` and `joinedLaunchDropsDeadEvidenceLine`. At start, `startupSessionManager(config, { bringUp, isShuttingDown })` runs each persona through the b.av2 SR-6.1 procedure: steps 1–3 (the bring-up controller's `bringUp`, `persona-bringup-controller.ts`) for every persona at once, then the launch (`spawnForPersona`) for each persona that is `up`, through a first-in, first-out launch pool of at most `concurrency` (default 3; a value below 1 is treated as 1), in the order the personas become ready, so no persona's Slack connection waits behind another persona's launch; the pool asks `isShuttingDown` (the server passes `() => shuttingDown`) right before starting each launch, and once it answers true (a throw counts as true) starts none: each persona still queued makes no agent-director call, gets `not-launched-shutdown` (`NOT_LAUNCHED_FOR_SHUTDOWN`) in `perPersona` and one line (`startLaunchNotStartedForShutdownLine`), and is counted in no count and never failed (b.jg5 SRJ-205); `bringUp` is the controller, and the server always passes it (without it each persona is launched directly, in config order through the same pool, which only launch-ladder unit tests do). A `broken` or `retrying` persona takes no pool slot and is counted in `notBroughtUp` and as a `not-brought-up` entry with its `outcome` and failures in `perPersona`; it records no startup error, raises no notice and is not a failed spawn. Every launch result is counted once, in its own `StartupSessionManagerResult` count (b.jg5 SRJ-1015), and the pass's one summary line is `startupSummaryLine(personaCount, counts)` (`StartupSummaryCounts`), whose ending from `failed` on is `startupSummaryEnding(counts)`, held in the import-free `startup-summary-ending.ts` and re-exported here unchanged. `launchSession(key, config, { canLaunch?, deadEvidence? })` (restart) runs the launch only; it asks `canLaunch` (the server passes the relaunch gate) before looking the persona up, and when that answers false (not up, or a key no longer applied) it launches nothing, runs no trust patch or reply-guard step and returns `'skipped'`. `spawnForPersona` is the one launch entry point and allows one in-flight launch per persona key: a second call for a key whose launch is still running joins it and gets its result, and `isLaunchInFlight(key)` reports whether one is running (a launch call only: it answers false while only the launch's dialog approver runs); `whenLaunchSettled(key)` resolves once that launch has settled, whatever its outcome (never rejects, starts nothing, does not wait for the approver), for a persona teardown. `readPersonaRowState(key)` is the UNAVAILABLE retry timer's row read (b.jg5 SRJ-303, SRJ-115): one `status` call for `cscb_<key>` through `withOutageDetection`, with no findMissing sweep and no other call; it answers an `UnavailableRetryRowRead` (`unavailable-retry.ts`): `state`, the row's state as agent-director reports it, or `absent` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_ROW_ABSENT`) for `ErrSpawnNotFound` (by class, `isAdErrorInstance`), and, on a `pending` row only, `launchStartedAt`, the result's raw launch start (`pendingLaunchStartOf`; absent when it shows none). It throws every other error (inside a recovery attempt the wrapper has already reported it, so it arms the timer) and logs nothing. `killPersonaInstance(key, { context, rowReadLive? })` makes one checked kill of `cscb_<key>` (`checkedKill`, `checked-kill.ts`) through `withOutageDetection` and answers its `KillOutcome`, `kill_sent` included (b.jg5 SRJ-110, SRJ-701): it never throws, never retries, logs nothing, records no startup error, raises no notice and latches nothing, so each caller acts on the outcome by its own context. `context` is required (`KillPersonaInstanceOptions`): `KILL_CONTEXT_ATTEMPT` (the live-row sequence's kills and the restart path's kill, inside their attempt) lets the wrapper report the error as for any call in the attempt, and an outcome of a class the kill has no row for (`unlistedClass`) is then reported as UNCLASSIFIED through `reportUnclassifiedAtSite` with `unclassifiedClassificationOf`'s classification, which arms the retry timer and feeds the unclassified-error episode; `KILL_CONTEXT_TEARDOWN` (each try of the persona teardown's kill, `killPersonaInstanceForTeardown`) passes the wrapper's `armsNothing` option with the configured-persona query. In either context an `ErrInvalidFlags` gets one immediate version re-check (`recheckKillOnInvalidFlags`), its answer kind kept as the outcome's `recheck`; an outcome whose re-check decided that the server stops is not reported as UNCLASSIFIED, and its caller does nothing more (b.jg5 SRJ-205). `rowReadLive` is true only for the live-row sequence's kills, of a row read live. With `deferUnavailableReport` (`KILL_CONTEXT_ATTEMPT` only; one try of `retryPersonaKill`) the wrapper does not report an UNAVAILABLE answer, so only the outcome that stands is reported (b.jg5 SRJ-702). `retryPersonaKill(key, { rowReadLive, lastRead, site, ref, clock, keepGoing? })` (`PersonaKillRetryOptions`) is the bounded retry of a persona's kill inside an attempt (`runKillRetry`, `kill-retry.ts`): each try is one `killPersonaInstance` with `deferUnavailableReport`, the read between tries is the shared own-row `status` read (what `status read between kill tries`), the keep-going check is false once the persona is latched or, through the query `main()` installs (`setPersonaKillKeepGoingQuery(query)`, `PersonaKillKeepGoingQuery`: `isPersonaUp(key)`, `isShuttingDown()`; with none installed only the latch is asked), once it is not up or the server is shutting down, and, when the caller passes its own `keepGoing` (the live-row sequence's: not stopped and not latched), once that answers false or throws; after a failure end that no stop ended it reports the outcome that stands once (`reportDeferredUnavailable`), and it answers the retry's result, its alert decision included. The restart kill adapter and the live-row sequence's kills call it, and each then raises that decision through `raisePersonaKillFailureAlert(key, retried, site, ref, context?, alerts?)` (b.jg5 SRJ-704), which hands it to the given kill-failure alerts, by default the installed ones (`setKillFailureAlerts(alerts)`, `main()`'s; with none it logs one line carrying the decision), with the context `recovery` unless given (the sequence passes its request's context), `latched` (a read between tries latched the persona, or it is latched now) and `stopped` (the keep-going check stopped the tries while it is not latched, or the last outcome's version re-check decided that the server stops). Every own-row read that reads the row `ended` or `missing`, or answers `ErrSpawnNotFound` (`readPersonaOwnRow`, `applyOwnRowStatusStep`), ends the persona's kill-failure episode (`endKillFailureEpisodeOnRead`); on the replacing path these are the collision ladder's `get` and the live-row sequence's `get`s and between-try `status` reads, so a row seen gone there ends it; see [The kill-failure alert](#the-kill-failure-alert-bjg5-srj-704-srj-1007). The collision ladder makes no kill and no delete: a row it cannot keep goes through the replace step (`replacePersonaRow`, b.jg5 SRJ-707; Server-Managed Startup step 5), which decides on the row state the path last read. A finished row (`ended`, `missing` or no row) gets one reuse spawn of the same id through the finished-row branch (`reuseFinishedRow`), whose first collision re-runs the ladder's get-then-act once (`ladderGetThenAct`) and whose second arms `collision` and answers `retrying` (`SPAWN_ACTION_RETRYING`, uncounted); a live row (`pending` and an unreadable state included) starts the live-row sequence and the ladder answers `sequence-waiting`. A replacement at the resume step (`replaceAtResumeSite`: `resume_enabled` false, a `config_dir` mismatch) whose path last read the row live but holds no dead evidence re-reads the row first and never starts the sequence itself (b.jg5 SRJ-609, SRJ-611). Every plain spawn goes through one exported handler, `plainSpawnOutcomeAt(site)` (b.jg5 SRJ-111; [Plain spawn](#plain-spawn-bjg5-srj-111)), given a `PlainSpawnSite` (the persona, `isStartup`, `ref`, the params, `what`, the row state last read, `marksDirectoryCounted`, the site's success line and its collision row `collided`): the ladder's first spawn (`what` `spawn`), its retry spawn after the collision `get` answered `ErrSpawnNotFound` (`retry-spawn`) and `plainSpawnAfterResumeNotFound` at both `resume` sites (`fresh spawn after ErrSpawnNotFound on resume`). It runs the reply-guard steps, makes the one spawn through `launchCallWithWindow`, and on success runs `afterLaunchSucceeded`; an `ErrInstanceIdCollision` (by class) undoes the reply-guard steps and answers through `collided`; anything else goes to the private `plainSpawnFailedAt`, whose `ErrInvalidFlags` goes through the private `invalidFlagsUnclassifiedAt` (shared with `resumeFailedAt`: one immediate version re-check, then UNCLASSIFIED), whose only spawn-failure notice is for LAUNCH FAILURE, and whose STATE or GONE names the plain spawn gives no meaning take the UNCLASSIFIED row. A later plain spawn's collision inside get-then-act goes to the private `plainSpawnCollisionAtLadder`: the first re-runs `ladderGetThenAct` once (`LadderRun.plainSpawnCollisionRerun`, kept apart from `reuseCollisionRerun`), and one in that re-run arms `collision` through `reportReuseCollisionAtSite` and answers `retrying`, each with one `plainSpawnCollisionLine(what, ref, rerun, armed)`. A resume's `ErrSpawnNotResumable` takes the not-resumable step (`notResumableStep`, b.jg5 SRJ-710): one re-read of the row through the shared own-row read (the private `rereadPersonaRow`, answering `PersonaRowReread`: `latched`, `refused`, `finished` (`ended`, `missing` or no row), `pending`, `live` (`ROW_REREAD_LIVE`: a known live state other than `pending`, one of `AGENT_DIRECTOR_LIVE_STATES`) or `unknown` (`ROW_REREAD_UNKNOWN`: any other state, an unreadable one included, which never leads to a kill), rendered by `describePersonaRowReread` as `state=<state>`, `state=unreadable` for a state that could not be read) and the pure decision on it, `decideNotResumable(reread, deadEvidence, sequenceBarred)` (`NotResumableDecision`: `latched`, `pending`, `live-row-sequence` or `lost-race`). At the ladder (`spawnNotResumableAtLadder`) a `pending` row goes to the ladder's `pending` step (`ladderPendingRowStep`), a known live state other than `pending` on a path holding dead evidence starts the live-row sequence with the conversation kept, and anything else, an unknown or unreadable state included, is the lost race (`lostRaceAtLadder`): no kill, delete or launch, the retry timer armed with `spawn-not-resumable-lost-race`, `retrying`. The live-row sequence's final launch is `launchForLiveRowSequence(persona, config, { kind, lastRead, stop })` (b.jg5 SRJ-705 step 6), a launch call registered in the in-flight launch map (it waits for a launch already in flight for the persona to settle, or for the sequence's stop signal, whichever comes first, never joining or overlapping it, so `isLaunchInFlight` and `whenLaunchSettled` cover it; once the signal is set it makes no call, registers nothing and answers not launched, `stopped` (`LIVE_ROW_NOT_LAUNCHED_STOPPED`), with one line, b.jg5 SRJ-706; it is exempt from the `sequence-waiting` gate below), run as a launch attempt after the latched gate, the `claude_config_dir` check and the dry-run check: a `resume` of the id through the one `resume` handler (`resumeAtSite`, shared with `resumeOrFreshSpawn`; b.jg5 SRJ-113), whose `ErrNoSessionId`, `ErrJsonlMissing` and `ErrJsonlNeverWritten` (by class) go on to the no-transcript step (`noTranscriptReuse`: after `ErrJsonlMissing` the lost-transcript diagnosis, then the reuse once), whose `ErrSpawnNotResumable` takes the not-resumable step with the sequence barred (the private `sequenceNotResumable`, b.jg5 SRJ-710: one re-read, never a second sequence) and answers not launched (`not-resumable-latched`, `not-resumable-pending` or `not-resumable`), whose `ErrSpawnNotFound` makes one plain spawn of the same id from `buildSpawnParams` with no spawn-failure notice for the `ErrSpawnNotFound` (its collision answers not launched, `spawn-collision`, `LIVE_ROW_NOT_LAUNCHED_SPAWN_COLLISION`, through the private `sequenceSpawnCollision`), and whose every other failure ends by class through the private `resumeFailedAt` with no further call; or the reuse spawn (below), whose collided answer becomes not launched (`reuse-collision`, `LIVE_ROW_NOT_LAUNCHED_REUSE_COLLISION`); a `resume` answering `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` also arms the persona's retry timer at once in pending-only mode (`armPendingOnlyAfterLaunchFailure`, `outage-state.ts`; the result's `pendingOnlyArmed`). A success runs the after-launch step (`afterLaunchSucceeded`). The entry counts its launch's result once, as `launchSession`'s reading does, through `recordLaunchResultOutsideRestartWork` (`restart.ts`; b.jg5 SRJ-112, SRJ-113, SRJ-602): a success records a success; a `failed` result not marked stopping that carries `countedClass` (LAUNCH FAILURE or DIRECTORY; `sequenceLaunchCounted`) is one counted failure (the cap notice at the cap); any other failure and a retrying, stopping, latched, held, deferred or not-launched answer record nothing. A call that joins its launch gets every failure not marked stopping, and a not-launched answer, as `retrying`, so the failure is counted at most once, by the entry. It never removes a row and never throws. The reuse spawn, `reuseSpawnForPersona(persona, config, { isStartup, lastRead, trustPatchRan? })` (`ReuseSpawnOptions`; b.jg5 SRJ-112, SRJ-708), is the one launch that brings a persona up fresh on its own instance id: after the `claude_config_dir` check (`deferred`, with no call, when the directory does not resolve) it sends `buildSpawnParams`'s params with only `reuse_finished: true` added (the client's `SpawnParams`), runs the trust patch once unless its caller ran it in this attempt (`trustPatchRan`), and calls through `launchWithReplyGuard`; a success logs its `reuse-spawned` line (no earlier life kept when its caller last read no row), runs the after-launch step with `LAUNCH_VERB_REUSE_SPAWN` and answers `spawned`. The private `reuseSpawnFailedAt` decides every failure by class through `src/ad-error-class.ts` (the collision by `ErrInstanceIdCollision`, through `isAdErrorInstance`). It answers a `ReuseSpawnResult`: a launch result, or the collided answer (`REUSE_SPAWN_COLLIDED`, `reuse-collided`, type `ReuseSpawnCollided`, told apart by `isReuseSpawnCollided`), which is no launch result, so no caller counts a collision. A LAUNCH FAILURE or DIRECTORY failure carries `countedClass`, and a counted `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` result also carries `pendingOnlyArmed` (`SpawnPersonaResult`) when it armed the retry timer in pending-only mode. Its callers are the sequence-launch entry and the no-transcript step (`noTranscriptReuse`), which the collision ladder's `resume` and the sequence-launch entry's `resume` leg share. Outcomes: [Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708). `buildLiveRowSequenceDeps({ killFailureAlerts?, retryArm, clock, log, appliedConfig })` (`LiveRowSequenceDepsInput`) binds the sequence's production dependencies (`LiveRowSequenceDeps`, `live-row-sequence.ts`) to these entries: each `get` through `readPersonaOwnRow`, each run through `bypassingFindMissingSweep` with the persona's key as its next-step `get` and read with `readFindMissingRow`, each kill through `retryPersonaKill` with the sequence's keep-going check and wait, the latches through `latchOnKillOutcomeAt`, both alerts through the given kill-failure alerts with the request's context, `adGraceMsInEffect` as G, the persona's applied `resume_enabled` and `compareRowToPersona` for step 6 (a deferred `cwd` check counts as a match, and an unresolvable `config_dir` gives no mismatch), the sequence-launch entry, and the retry arm with `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_SEQUENCE_NOT_JUDGED`, `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_SEQUENCE_ENDED` or `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_COLLISION`; it reads nothing and starts nothing when called; `main()` calls it once, for the live-row sequence registry. The registry installer `setLiveRowSequenceRegistry(registry)` (b.jg5 SRJ-706; production: `main()`'s one registry, installed before the start pass; test seam `_resetLiveRowSequenceRegistry()`) holds the server's registry. Its start entry, `startLiveRowSequence(request)`, the one way a starter reaches it (a step-2 entry is the same call with entry step 2), answers the registry's answer, or `not-installed` (`LIVE_ROW_START_NOT_INSTALLED`) with one line when none is installed; the running query `isLiveRowSequenceRunning(key)` and `stopLiveRowSequence(key, reason)` forward to it (false, and nothing stopped, with none installed). With both a registry and a latch with `addSetObserver` installed, one more set observer on the latch, `stopSequenceOnLatch`, stops a latched persona's running sequence with the reason `latched`, whichever installer ran second. While a sequence runs for a persona that is not latched, `spawnForPersona` answers `sequence-waiting` right after its held gate, before the in-flight join, with one line and no agent-director call, trust patch, reply-guard step, record or arm; `launchSession` maps it to the uncounted `'refused'`, and the start pass counts it in its `sequenceWaiting` count, neither as failed nor as succeeded. Its production starters are the collision ladder's replacement sites, through the replace step (b.jg5 SRJ-707): a live row there (`pending` included) starts a sequence entering at step 1, with the conversation not kept, the retired-key flag set for a retired key's old life, a launch at the end and the alert context `recovery`; the pending-row step's read-and-step entry (`readAndStepPendingRow`, b.jg5 SRJ-411), which starts the same request for an uncovered `pending` row found by the restart path's deferral or a pending-only retry; and the ladder's not-resumable step (`spawnNotResumableAtLadder`, b.jg5 SRJ-710, SRJ-611), which starts the same request with the conversation kept when the path holds dead evidence and the re-read finds the row in a known live state other than `pending` (a state CSCB does not know, an unreadable one included, is the lost race). `killPersonaInstanceForTeardown(key, { clock, ref? })` is the persona teardown's kill (b.jg5 SRJ-715, SRJ-110, SRJ-702): `runKillRetry` over one `killPersonaInstance` with `KILL_CONTEXT_TEARDOWN` per try, seeded `KILL_RETRY_SEED_LIVE_UNREAD`, its read between tries one `status` through `withOutageDetection` arming nothing with no own-row step (`readTeardownKillRow`), so it latches nothing, applying only the retired-key entry clear (`decideRetiredEntryClear`, site `persona teardown kill: status read between tries`); no keep-going check, nothing reported after the tries, its lines prefixed `[slack] persona teardown kill for <ref>`. It answers a `PersonaTeardownKillResult`, the retry's result plus `refusals` (`PersonaTeardownKillRefusal`: each CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME answer met, `at` `KILL_REFUSAL_AT_KILL` or `KILL_REFUSAL_AT_READ`, `src/checked-kill.ts`), never throws, and makes no delete: no export of the session manager deletes a persona's row; the ladder itself is the private `runPersonaLadder`. The ladder's row guards and the sweep's `cwd` condition go through `compareRowToPersona` (see Server-Managed Startup steps 4 and 5). It also reports `workingDirectoryResolved` (the persona's working directory has a real path, `tryResolveRealPath`) and `cwdCheckDeferred`: the working directory has no real path and the row's `cwd` has none either (absent, missing, a dangling symlink's old target) or equals the configured `working_directory` lexically. For such a row neither the sweep nor the ladder acts on `cwd` grounds (b.av2 SR-6.4): the sweep keeps the row and defers the check to the launch, and the ladder keeps the row and fails the launch. A row whose `cwd` resolves to an existing directory elsewhere isn't deferred: it is still swept or replaced as a `cwd` mismatch, so a persona can't adopt another persona's directory. Raises its persona notices (b.av2 SR-7.2) through one installed sink, `setSessionNotifier(notify)`, which production sets to the per-persona notifier's `notify` (`persona-notifier.ts`); with no sink installed (unit tests, the integration driver) a notice is logged, not posted. `notifySpawnFailure(key, error, isStartup)` raises the spawn-failure notice, whose text `spawnFailureNoticeText(error)` builds: the error label (the `errName` when it is a safe identifier, else the stack-free `describeThrownValueWithoutStack` description without its `message` field), agent-director's description through `renderLogMessageText` (redacted, on one line, capped at `MAX_LOGGED_MESSAGE_LENGTH`) and then `escapeSlackControlCharacters`, and the remediation hint, decided by class in the private `remediationHint`, which has no collision branch; no collision reaches it (b.jg5 SRJ-713), and a `resume`'s collision goes to the private `resumeCollisionAt`, which logs the exported `resumeCollisionLine(ref, failure, armed)`; when a startup notice's post fails (at its first failed attempt; a notice the destination hold keeps can still post later) it records the `spawn-failure-post` startup error with a token-safe cause from `describeDestinationFailureCause` (a failed DM open names the step and code, `conversations.open code=<code>`; a failed post gives the rejection's description), and outside startup it logs the same cause. `notifyRestartCapReached(key)` is the cap-notice function restart's `onCapReached` calls: a non-startup spawn-failure notice carrying `ErrSpawnCapReached`, whose body is the exported, pure `restartCapReachedNoticeText()`. `notifyPersonaNotConnected(key, notice)` (b.f2b) raises the not-connected notice through one latch per persona (`notConnectedNoticeRaised`), so at most one of its texts is posted per episode: `blocked-on-prompt` (*Waiting on a prompt*: the session waits on a prompt or dialog, which CSCB never types into), `auto-restart-disabled` (with `session_restart_delay` 0 nothing will reconnect the persona: *Not connected* when its MCP session is not connected, *Not receiving messages* when it is connected but its message stream is gone) or `unproven-idle` (*Not connected*, at any delay: its row reads `working` and CSCB, unable to prove the session idle, has held back from it for `UNPROVEN_IDLE_NOTICE_AFTER_MS`, 10 min, from the first deferral; `noteWorkingRowDeferral(key, autoRestartDisabled)` counts the run of deferrals, `endWorkingRowDeferral(key)` ends it). The health check raises the latter through `notifyDisconnectedWithAutoRestartDisabled(key, cause)` (`cause` `disconnected` or `streamless`). The texts are built by the exported, pure `buildNotConnectedNotice(key, notice)` (six renderings: *Waiting on a prompt* and the `unproven-idle` *Not connected*, each with and without auto-restart disabled, and the `auto-restart-disabled` *Not connected* and *Not receiving messages*); every one names the exact attach (`tmux attach -t =slack_bot_<key>`, `tmuxExactSessionTarget`) and `/mcp reconnect`, so its second line ends with SRJ-1001's human-only sentence (`CONFLICT_NOTICE_HUMAN_ONLY_LINE`, `conflict-latch.ts`; b.jg5 SRJ-1001). `forgetNotConnectedEpisode(key)` ends the episode, silently, clearing the latch, the restart path's idle evidence and the run of deferrals: the server calls it when the persona's MCP session registers, the health check on every tick that finds the persona alive, connected and with its stream, and the persona teardown. The b.f2b stale-`working`-row evidence lives here too: the pure `classifyWorkingPane` (pane: `prompt`, `busy`, `blank` or `idle`) and `foldWorkingPaneRun` (the positive-idle rule, over a `TranscriptReading` from `session-transcript.ts`), `STALE_WORKING_WINDOW_MS` (60 s), `WORKING_ROW_READ_INTERVAL_MS` (5 s, the launch wait's read cadence) and `UNPROVEN_IDLE_NOTICE_AFTER_MS` (10 min), each with `_set…` / `_reset…` test seams, the clock seam `_setNow` / `_resetNow`, and the restart path's per-persona run behind `checkWorkingRowPane(key, pane, { persona?, latchedNow? })` (the fold on a pane its caller read; it makes no `read-pane` of its own), `hasPendingWorkingRowEvidence(key)` and `forgetWorkingRowEvidence(key)`. `checkWaitingRowPane(key, latchedNow?)` is the restart path's one pane read of a `waiting` row, answering `reconnect`, `defer`, `gone` (`WAITING_ROW_PANE_GONE`) or `absent` (`WAITING_ROW_PANE_ABSENT`); `EscalateDeadVerdict` names why the restart path escalated a persona as dead, and `ESCALATE_DEAD_EVIDENCE` gives each verdict's one evidence text for the escalate-dead line (`ESCALATE_DEAD_WAITING_ROW_PANE_GONE`, `ESCALATE_DEAD_ROW_ABSENT_AT_PANE_READ` name the two pane-read verdicts), and `PROMPT_ROW_STATES` names `ask_user` and `check_permission`. `checkPromptRowDeferral(key, state)` (b.jdc) keeps the restart path's run of deferrals on such a row whose one-line `read-pane` answered a pane or was taken as alive (UNAVAILABLE, CONFIG or UNCLASSIFIED): from `PROMPT_ROW_SWEEP_AFTER_MS` (10 min) after its first deferral, each one runs the memoized findMissing sweep and reads the row again, and a row then `ended` or `missing` escalates (`promptRowSweepFinishedLine`; the adapter's escalate-dead answer carries the cause `row-read-finished`, a row read and not dead evidence); a persona latched once that sweep is done answers `latched`, with no row read. Every findMissing call goes through one memoized, single-flight core (`sharedFindMissingSweep`, module-private, b.m4r, b.jg5 SRJ-120): its callers all make ordinary runs; `bypassingFindMissingSweep(key, logPrefix, nextStepGetKey?, call?)` is the exported bypassing entry (a new call whatever is memoized or in flight, its result memoized for later ordinary callers; the live-row sequence's runs and the old-life wait's are its two callers, the wait's passing `call`, a `FindMissingCallOptions`: wrapper options that arm nothing for the old key and a failure sink); `readFindMissingRow(result, id, stateBefore)` is the pure reading of one row of a result (`marked-missing`, `judged-left-live`, `not-judged` for a `pending` row in neither list, `judged-alive`); `FIND_MISSING_MEMO_TTL_MS` (10 s) is the exported memo window, measured on the clock seam `_now`. After a run the server makes, each configured persona's own row in `unverified_ids` is read once through `readPersonaOwnRow`, the reads running concurrently (`readListedPersonaRows`), except an already-latched persona's (`personaLatchedNow`), which is skipped with no `get` and no latch call; a caller whose own row's read failed with a refusal gets `FIND_MISSING_REFUSED` (`postRunGetRefusal`), and a caller whose persona is latched once the sweep is done gets `FIND_MISSING_LATCHED` (see Server-Managed Startup step 5, the b.m4r note). `cancelWorkingRowWait(key)` cancels a launch's wait for a `working` row (or a wait its launch in flight has yet to start) for a persona teardown. The wait's lines and notices are built by exported pure builders: `waitRowAbsentLine` (an absent row, at the poll or the timeout), `waitPollStatusErrorLine` (a failed poll `status` read), and, for a wait that ends `not-reconnected`, a `WaitEndedReport` (`waitEndedOnStateReport`, `waitTimedOutLiveReport`, `waitTimedOutUnreadReport`; the module-private `waitEndedNotice` picks the notice) turned into its one line by `waitEndedDisconnectedLine` for the restart delay in effect. The start pass parks a launch that waits for a `working` row (`launchOrPark`, over `spawnForPersona`'s `LaunchHooks.onWorkingRowWait`), so it returns without waiting it out; see Server-Managed Startup step 5. The lost-history and inconclusive-history notices of `diagnoseJsonlMissing` go through the same sink; their texts are the exported, pure `jsonlTranscriptLostNoticeText`, `jsonlRowAbsentInconclusiveNoticeText` and `jsonlCandidatesInconclusiveNoticeText`, which quote the text taken from agent-director's description or row through `renderLogMessageText` (redacted, one line, capped at `MAX_LOGGED_MESSAGE_LENGTH`; b.jg5 SRJ-1001) and then escape it, with the CSCB-worded reason, for Slack (`escapeSlackControlCharacters`), while the log line and the startup-errors entry carry it as given, unescaped. The reason for a row whose `started_at` is absent or unparseable quotes that `started_at` through `renderLogMessageText` too (`(none)` when it renders blank), in the notice, the log line and the startup-errors entry alike. `diagnoseJsonlMissing` reads the channel mode of the configuration it is given (`channelModeOf`) for the archive evidence (`personaArchiveEvidenceScope(persona, mode)`, `jsonl-persistence-check.ts`; b.deo SRI-704): in fungible mode the evidence is inconclusive, never `lost`, and its reason is `unattributableZeroReason(mode)`. Every launch first runs `checkLaunchConfigDir(persona)` (`checkPersonaConfigDir` with the spawn home and the `_setConfigDirFs` test seam); an unresolvable directory makes no agent-director call, goes to the one installed hook (`setConfigDirUnresolvableHook`; production: the bring-up controller's `holdForConfigDir`; with none, or when it does not hold the persona, the line is logged here) and returns `deferred` with the cause as `deferredBy` (step `claude-config-dir`), which `launchSession` maps to `'skipped'` and the start pass counts as `not-brought-up` `retrying` with that cause. Spawn-path log lines name the persona as `"<name>" (key=<key>)`; key-only helpers log `persona=<key>`. A `resume` answering `ErrInvalidFlags` goes through the `ErrInvalidFlags` step (`classifyWithInvalidFlagsRecheck` in `ad-error-class.ts`) with its default re-check trigger; when the re-check decides the stop, the `failed` result is marked `stopping` and no notice is posted. Every collision ladder a `spawnForPersona` call starts runs as a launch attempt (`runInAttempt(key, 'launch', …)`, b.jg5 SRJ-301); a joining call, the claude_config_dir deferral and dry run are none. A `failed` result whose attempt's last agent-director error armed the persona's UNAVAILABLE retry timer (the trigger sink answered that the persona has a timer after the call) is answered as `retrying` (`SPAWN_ACTION_RETRYING`, through `retryingWhenArmed`; a `failed` marked `stopping` stays as it is), which joiners get too. A CONFLICT at any spawn or `resume` the ladder makes latches the persona through the installed latch (`setConflictLatch(latch)`, production: the server's one latch, installed before the start pass; with none installed nothing is latched and the site still answers `latched`; the installer also registers one set observer on the latch, `stopApproverOnLatch`, so a latch of P set by any site stops P's running dialog approver with the reason `latched`) and answers the action `latched`; see [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)). `launchSession` maps `deferred`, `latched`, a `held` launch (the persona is held on `ErrInvalidFlags`) and a `stopping` failure to `'skipped'` (the latch or the hold stops the retry timer, b.jg5 SRJ-305), `retrying` and `sequence-waiting` to `'refused'` (nothing recorded, and a retry that meets one re-arms the timer, SRJ-302; b.jg5 SRJ-1015), `fresh-retired` and every other success to `true`, and any other failure to `false`. `readPersonaOwnRow(key, at)` (b.jg5 SRJ-114; `OwnRowReadSite`: `site`, `what`, optional `ref`, for its log lines) is the one read of a persona's own row at the collision `get`, the `ErrJsonlMissing` diagnosis `get`, the transcript `get` and the `get` after a findMissing run's `unverified_ids` (b.jg5 SRJ-120): one `get` of `cscb_<key>` through `withOutageDetection`, then `row-read-rules.ts`'s decision; Which keys count as configured comes from one installed query (`setConfiguredPersonaQuery(query)`, type `ConfiguredPersonaQuery = (key) => boolean`; production: `main()`'s query over `getAppliedPersona`); with none installed (unit tests, the integration driver) no key counts and no note latches, while the CONFLICT and UNUSABLE NAME latch entries latch as for a configured persona (`latchEntryConfigured`, which also latches a removed persona inside its open teardown window); tests remove it with `_resetConfiguredPersonaQuery()`. With none installed (unit tests, the integration driver, the CLI), or an `isMarked` that throws, no key counts as recorded or marked, nothing is cleared and every launch path launches as for a key that is not retired; tests remove it with `_resetRetiredKeyStore()`. `oldLifeWaitUnclassifiedNotReportedLine(ref)` is the line of an UNCLASSIFIED answer met with no episodes bound, and `oldLifeWaitNotAppliedLine(key)` the line of a waiting persona outside the applied configuration;
