See [A launch's window and the read after a timeout](#a-launchs-window-and-the-read-after-a-timeout-bjg5-srj-407). **The latch re-check (b.jg5 SRJ-505, SRJ-506, SRJ-502).** `buildLatchRecheck(input)` (`LatchRecheckInput`: `latch`, `clock`, `serialize`, `appliedConfig`, `log`, `episodes`, optional `canRelaunch`, `isAtCap` and `resetRestartFailures`, the last handed to `clearAndRecover` only) composes the re-check timers over the round and the clear hand-off, and answers the controller with the one clear entry and the after-clear sequence over it (`LatchRecheck`: the controller, `clear`, `clearAndRecover(key, reason)`); `main()` and the recovery harness both call it. `runLatchRecheckRound(key, deps)` (`LatchRecheckRoundDeps`: `latch`, `appliedConfig`, `clearHandOff`, optional `runRestartDecision`, `canRelaunch` and `isAtCap`, `log`) is one round inside the re-check's scope (`runInLatchRecheck`): step 1's read at the sites `LATCH_RECHECK_STATUS_READ_SITE` and `LATCH_RECHECK_GET_READ_SITE`, the decision, then the one call: the probe or the lap `read-pane` through the wrapper with the one-line count, a launch through its one handler (`plainSpawnOutcomeAt`, `reuseSpawnForPersona`, `resumeAtSite`) registered as the persona's launch in flight, the finished-row retry's `get` (`LATCH_RECHECK_FINISHED_ROW_GET_SITE`) and launch, or one run of the restart path's decision (`runRestartWorkInTurn`) with the re-check's permit, which `latchGateReadingOf` honours, so every gate built on `personaLatchedNow` and `spawnForPersona`'s launch gate pass it. Inside the scope the handlers clear the latch before their after-launch step and before a definite failure's class handling (`clearLatchBeforeOutcome`, `isDefiniteLaunchAnswer`), the live-row sequence's start entry clears it for a permitted run, a collision gives no information (`latchRecheckCollided`), an UNAVAILABLE launch makes no `get` (`afterLaunchUnavailable`), a relatch records the state the re-check last read (`recordedRowState`), and `launchSession` answers a `failed` launch of a still-latched persona `'skipped'` and revokes the run's permit. A re-check's launch is counted by `countLaunchOutsideRestartWork`, shared with the live-row sequence's final launch. A persona at the restart cap (`isAtCap`, asked first; b.av2 SR-6.3) gets the round's reads only: no launch, no cleared probe's `find-missing` and no run of the restart path's decision, one `latchRecheckAtCapLine` and the answer `LATCH_RECHECK_AT_CAP`. A probe that finds the condition cleared is followed in the round by one bypassing `find-missing` and the single retry (`latchRecheckClearedProbeRetry`, over the pure `decideClearedProbeRetry`), and a "this row's own id" single retry refused again drops the probe (`setProbeDropped`). Outside the scope, a launch's CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME for a persona latched elsewhere during its call sets nothing (`latchedElsewhereDuringCall`). **After a clear (b.jg5 SRJ-506).** The round's hand-off (`createLatchRecheckClearHandOff`) calls the clear entry; after a clear that launched nothing (`RECHECK_CLEARS_THAT_LAUNCHED_NOTHING`) it hands the after-clear run to the round's operation (`runLatchRecheckRoundThenOwed`), which runs it right after the round in the same serializer turn. `runLatchClearSequence(key, reason, deps, options?)` (`LatchClearSequenceDeps`: `clear`, `appliedConfig`, `serialize`, optional `retryAtOnce` and `resetRestartFailures`, `log`; `LatchClearSequenceOptions.findMissingFirst`) is the clear by hand and the same sequence after it: one job submitted through the persona's serializer, whose first step is the clear, so nothing is cleared before the persona's turn comes; a clear that clears a latch then resets the persona's restart failure count (`resetRestartFailures`, a throw logged by `latchClearRestartResetFailedLine` and swallowed); it answers in two parts (`LatchClearSequenceAnswer`): `cleared` (whether the persona was latched, once the clear, and that reset, have run in that turn) and `done` (`LatchClearSequenceOutcome`, `LATCH_CLEAR_SEQUENCE_*`: `not-latched`, `not-applied`, `find-missing-refused`, `relatched`, `retried` with the retry's outcome, `retry-failed`). `clearByHandOf(recheck)` (b.jg5 SRJ-510, SRJ-1005) is the one clear-by-hand binding over `LatchRecheck.clearAndRecover`, with `LATCH_RECOVERY_REASON_CLEARED_BY_HAND`, answering only `cleared`; `main()` applies it once to its re-check for the `/clear-latch` route, and the recovery harness to its own. See [The re-check](#the-re-check-bjg5-srj-505) and [How a latch clears and relatches](#how-a-latch-clears-and-relatches-bjg5-srj-506-srj-1005). **The forced-launch seams (b.jg5 SRJ-1306 as amended by b.deo SRI-1402 to SRI-1404; b.jg5 SRJ-1401).** `_forceResumeForPersona(persona, config)` and `_forceReuseSpawnForPersona(persona, config)` are test seams for `tests/integration/fixtures/fmk-driver.ts` only; no production path calls them. Each forces one launch of the persona's own id (`cscb_<key>`), whatever its row reads, with nothing of the row read first (`NOTHING_READ`), through CSCB's own launch path and classification. `runForcedLaunch` wraps both as every launch outside the restart work is wrapped: a launch of the persona already in flight in this process is joined with no call; a `claude_config_dir` that does not resolve goes to the deferral hook (`deferred`) and a dry run answers `no-op`, each with no call; otherwise the earlier row's idle evidence and deferrals are forgotten, one line is logged, and the call runs as a launch attempt (`runInAttempt`, `retrying` in place of `failed` when the attempt armed the retry timer) registered as the persona's launch in flight, its result counted by `countLaunchOutsideRestartWork`. The forced `resume` runs the pre-launch trust patch and then the one `resume` handler (`resumeAtSite`, with the plain spawn's parameters and the head `[slack] forced-launch:`): `ErrSpawnNotResumable` arms the lost-race cause and answers `retrying`, with no re-read and nothing counted or posted, as at the latch re-check's `resume`; a no-transcript answer goes on to the no-transcript reuse (`noTranscriptReuse`), and `ErrSpawnNotFound` to the handler's plain spawn. The forced reuse spawn is `reuseSpawnForPersona` with `lastRead` `NOTHING_READ`, so a CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME latches after the one latch-time `status` read and every other answer takes SRJ-112's outcome table. A collision of the reuse or of the plain spawn ends the launch (`forcedLaunchCollided`): the collision cause armed, `retrying`, nothing counted or posted. Both seams hand the reuse the forced launch's name (`ReuseSpawnOptions.forcedWhat`, through `NoTranscriptReuseOptions.forcedWhat` after the forced `resume`), so its success line gives the forced launch as the reason nothing was read. Each answers a `ForcedLaunchOutcome`: `called` (false when it joined a launch in flight, deferred or ran dry), `result` (the production path's answer), `error` (the forced call's own error, when it threw, as a `ForcedLaunchError`: `name`, `errorClass` from `classifyAdError`, `description` through `renderLogMessageText`, and `unknownName` for an `ErrUnknownErrorName`), `counted` (one counted launch failure) and `latched`. The error comes from a per-persona observer that `launchCallWithWindow` tells how each launch call settled (`tellForcedLaunchObserver`); only `runForcedLaunch` sets one, for the length of its launch, and it keeps the first call's. Neither seam adds an agent-director call to those its path makes. They run in the process that calls them (the driver), not in the bot server, and log the lines of [Forced-launch seam lines](#forced-launch-seam-lines-bjg5-srj-1306-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-1402-to-sri-1404-bjg5-srj-1401).

Imports nothing, and must stay so: the /ci-live runner loads it on the host, where importing `session-manager.ts` would load the agent-director client and `bun:sqlite` (pinned by the source audit in `tests/ci-live-docker.test.ts`).
    ├── session-transcript.ts   b.f2b a persona's Claude Code transcript as the positive idle signal for a stale `working` row. `locateTranscript(row, configDir)` (pure) returns the row's `jsonl_path` when its file name is `<claude_session_id>.jsonl`, else `<configDir>/projects/<cwd slug>/<claude_session_id>.jsonl` through `resolveJsonlPath` (`cozempic.ts`), or undefined when neither can be had; a path from an earlier session is never read. `readTranscriptTurnState(path)` opens the file read-only and non-blocking, `fstat`s it, reads only a regular file and only its last `TRANSCRIPT_TAIL_BYTES` (256 KiB), and returns a `TranscriptReading`: `ended` or `open` with a `TranscriptSnapshot` (path, device, inode, size, mtime; compared by `sameTranscriptSnapshot`), or `unreadable` with a fixed, token-free reason; it never throws. `transcriptTailTurnState(tail, fromStart)` is the pure rule: scanning back past entries that are not part of a turn (every type but `user`, `assistant` and `queue-operation`, and a completed local command's three `user` lines), the first other entry decides: an `assistant` entry whose stop reason is `end_turn`, `stop_sequence` or `refusal` and which holds no `tool_use` block is `ended`, and so is an interrupt marker (a `user` entry whose only content block is the text `[Request interrupted by user]` or `[Request interrupted by user for tool use]`: Claude Code fires no Stop for an interrupted turn); anything else is `open`. An `attachment` that records a Stop hook keeping the turn going (`hook_additional_context` or `hook_blocking_error` with `hookEvent` `Stop`) is `open` too, where it comes after the last `assistant` entry. Importable without side effects.

Owns the live LivePermission map, keyed on the composite `(claude_instance_id, request_token)` pair, consumes AD's plural `permission_requests` projection, resolves each listed row's persona from its `persona` label (b.av2 SR-7.1 as amended by b.deo SRI-701, SRI-702; the `channel` label is never read), posts one Slack message per open row to the persona's destination through that persona's client (`PollerDeps.clientFor` / `getPersona`) and the shared destination hold, the destination resolved at each attempt by the one destination rule over the configuration in effect (`personaDestinationOf`, through the resolver; b.deo SRI-701, SRI-702): its `permission_prompts` in declarative mode, its `invited.permission_prompts` (`"dm"` when absent) in fungible mode, a channel or its DM with `dm.contact`, opened if needed.     ├── liveness-reading.ts     b.jg5 SRJ-314 (C12) the four liveness readings and the row-state mapper. Pure: no I/O, clock, module state or log line. `LIVENESS_LIVE`, `LIVENESS_PENDING`, `LIVENESS_DEAD`, `LIVENESS_UNKNOWN` (`LIVENESS_KINDS`, type `LivenessKind`); a reading (`LivenessReading`) is an object whose `kind` names it, with the frozen values `LIVENESS_READING_*`. `livenessReadingForState(state)` maps a row state: `pending` → `pending`, another state in `AGENT_DIRECTOR_LIVE_STATES` → `live`, one in `AGENT_DIRECTOR_DEAD_STATES` (`ended`, `missing`) → `dead` carrying that state, anything else → `unknown`. `livenessKindOf(reading)` answers a reading's kind, and `unknown` for any value that is not a reading; it never throws. A `pending` reading (`PendingLivenessReading`) carries `launchStartedAt`, the row's launch start raw as agent-director wrote it, when the `status` result showed one (b.jg5 SRJ-115); nothing here parses or ages it. `pendingLaunchStartOf(result)` reads it from a `status` result (a non-empty `launch_started_at` on a `pending` row only, else absent); `pendingLivenessReading(launchStartedAt?)` builds the frozen reading (`LIVENESS_READING_PENDING` when there is none); `livenessReadingForStatus(result)` is `livenessReadingForState` over the result's state, with a `pending` reading carrying the launch start; `launchStartOfReading(reading)` answers the launch start a probe's answer carries. A `dead` reading (`DeadLivenessReading`) may carry `source` `LIVENESS_DEAD_SOURCE_INSTALL_GONE` (`install-gone`): `LIVENESS_READING_DEAD_INSTALL_GONE` is the `dead` reading from `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`, which reads no row, and `isInstallGoneDeadReading(reading)` tells it apart from a row read's `dead`, for the slow-recovery count (b.jg5 SRJ-610). A row read's `dead` reading carries what it read as `rowRead` (`DeadRowRead`: `ended`, `missing`, or `no-row` for `ErrSpawnNotFound`; `LIVENESS_READING_DEAD_ENDED`, `LIVENESS_READING_DEAD_MISSING`, `LIVENESS_READING_DEAD_NO_ROW`), which the restart path's no-kill line names (the kill follows none of them: no kill is sent for a row just read `ended`, `missing` or gone, b.jg5 SRJ-110, SRJ-314); `LIVENESS_READING_DEAD` is the `dead` reading with no row state read. `deadRowReadOf(reading)` answers a `dead` reading's `rowRead` (none for any other answer) and `deadLivenessReading(rowRead?)` builds the frozen reading. None of them throws. The `status` result is typed through `ad-phase1-types.ts` (a type-only import). `AGENT_DIRECTOR_LIVE_STATES` and `AGENT_DIRECTOR_PENDING_STATE` live here; `session-manager.ts` re-exports the live set. Only `dead` leads to a launch, and only its `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` form to a kill before it; see Auto-Restart steps 3 and 4.

No imports, no timers/I/O; in-process state, lost on server restart by design. Also exports the stateless `doublingBackoffDelay(base, priorAttempts, ceiling)` = min(base·2^priorAttempts, ceiling), unit-agnostic and finite for any attempt count; `nextBackoffDelay` delegates to it with the 900 s ceiling and returns the same values as before. The persona Slack-unreachable policy (`persona-retry-schedule.ts`) is also per persona but reuses only the arithmetic: it counts different failures and shares no state with the session-restart counters. The UNAVAILABLE retry timer (`unavailable-retry.ts`) is the other caller of `doublingBackoffDelay` outside this module: it keeps its own refusal count and never reads or writes the failure counter or the cap latch.
    ├── unavailable-retry.ts    b.jg5 SRJ-302 to SRJ-306 (and SRJ-301's code line) per-persona retry timer for a persona that agent-director refuses (UNAVAILABLE). `createUnavailableRetryController({ log, action, clock?, onRetryFire? })` builds one controller (`onRetryFire(key, firedAt)` observes every retry before its action, a skipped one included; production binds the `tmux-unresponsive` onset check at a retry. `onStopped(key, reason)` observes every real stop of a timer, after its stopped line and before its hand-off, a timer dropped because its re-arm failed included (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_RUN_FAILED`), but not a no-op stop, a failed first arm or a pending-only stop that yielded; production binds the condition's `cancelAlert`, then the unclassified-error episodes' `retryStopped` (b.jg5 SRJ-313), each isolated so one that throws does not skip the other. `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_TERMINAL_STOPS` names the stop reasons after which that alert check is never armed again: torn down, not applied, shutdown), which keeps at most one timer per persona key; clock and timers are injected (`SYSTEM_PERSONA_CONNECTION_CLOCK` by default), each controller holds its own entries, and no persona state is kept at module scope (the attempt context below holds only running attempts), so nothing spans two personas or two controllers. Nothing is armed, read or logged at import or creation. The controller's exports: `arm(key, cause)` (full mode; answers true when the persona has a timer after the call, false after `close` or when the first timer could not be set), `armPendingOnly(key)`, `conditionEnded(key, condition, reading?)` (called by the `tmux-unresponsive` condition's end and by each real clear of the `tmux-unavailable` outage, through the outage state's cleared-flag observer; both bound in `main()`), `stop(key, reason)`, `stopAll(reason)`, `close(reason)` (the server's shutdown: stops every persona and refuses every later `arm`), and the read-only `view(key)` (its phase, due time, wait, refusal count, causes, `mode` and `lastRow`), `isArmed`, `armedKeys` and `whenRunSettled`. `createFullModeRetryAction(deps)` is the server's retry action for both modes, over `runRestartRetry` and `readPersonaRowState` (`FullModeRetryDeps.readRow`, answering an `UnavailableRetryRowRead`: the row's `state` and, on a `pending` row, its raw `launchStartedAt`; the action acts on the state only). Its gate before any call is the exported `retryRunGateStop(deps, key)` over `RetryRunGateDeps` (`isShuttingDown`, `appliedPersona`, `isLatched`, `isHeld`, `canRelaunch`, `isAtCap`, in that order; answers the first `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_*` reason that holds, or nothing), which the pending-row rule's run at a dialog approver's stop asks too (`PendingRowRuleInstall.gate`). Its optional `isLatched(key)` (b.jg5 SRJ-303, SRJ-305; production: the server's latch's `isLatched`) stops a latched persona's timer before any call, in either mode, with `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_LATCHED` (`the persona is latched`, not a terminal stop), the same stop the latch's hold uses; a query that throws counts as latched (one line naming what it threw). Its optional `isHeld(key)` (b.jg5 SRJ-207, SRJ-303, SRJ-305; production: the server's `ErrInvalidFlags` hold's `isHeld`), asked right after it, stops a held persona's timer the same way with `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_HELD` (`the persona is held on ErrInvalidFlags`, not a terminal stop), the stop the hold's set reaction uses, and a full-mode retry whose work answers `held` stops with it; a query that throws counts as held (one line naming what it threw). Its optional `isSessionConnected`, `hasSessionStream` and `endTmuxUnresponsive(key, reading)` let a retry that finds the persona healthy end its `tmux-unresponsive` condition ([The tmux-unresponsive condition](#the-tmux-unresponsive-condition-bjg5-srj-307-srj-310)) and, as `main()` binds the hook, clear its `tmux-unavailable` outage with the same reading (b.jg5 SRJ-311, SRJ-312); absent, a retry ends and clears nothing. `main()` builds the controller with it on the system clock and installs it as the outage state's trigger sink before the start pass. The waits come from `doublingBackoffDelay` over `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_BASE_S` (30 s) and `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CEILING_S` (300 s); stop reasons and again-reasons are the `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_*` and `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_AGAIN_*` labels. `runNow(key, cause, why)` runs a persona's retry at once (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_RUN_NOW_RAN`, `_ARMED`, `_RUNNING`, `_CLOSED`; the hold-ended label `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_RUN_NOW_HOLD_ENDED`, `old-life-hold-ended`; its one line built by the exported `unavailableRetryRunNowLine`; b.jg5 SRJ-810), and `sequenceWaitingAgainReason(cause)` names a `sequence-waiting` run's again-reason (`old-life-wait-in-flight` when an old-life wait step blocks a retry, else `live-row-sequence-waiting`). "Blocks a retry" names its cause (`RetryBlockCause`: `RETRY_BLOCK_LAUNCH`, `RETRY_BLOCK_LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE`, `RETRY_BLOCK_OLD_LIFE_WAIT`; `FullModeRetryDeps.retryBlockCause`, read through `readRetryBlockCause`, a throw or an answer that is not a cause counting as not known): `retryBlockAgainReason` maps it to the again-reason (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_AGAIN_LAUNCH_IN_FLIGHT`, `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_AGAIN_SEQUENCE_IN_FLIGHT` `live-row-sequence-in-flight`, `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_AGAIN_OLD_LIFE_WAIT_IN_FLIGHT` `old-life-wait-in-flight`; `launch-in-flight` when not known) and `retryBlockSkipText` to the restart retry's skip-line words; the action passes the query on to `runRestartRetry`. The live-row sequence arms with its four causes, `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_SEQUENCE_NOT_JUDGED` (`sequence-not-judged`), `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_SEQUENCE_ENDED` (`sequence-ended-without-launch`), `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_COLLISION` (`collision`, a collision at its final launch: the reuse spawn's, or the plain spawn's after its `resume`'s `ErrSpawnNotFound`) and `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_LOST_RACE` (`spawn-not-resumable-lost-race`, its final `resume`'s `ErrSpawnNotResumable` whose re-read found a lost race), none ever counted ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717)). The collision ladder arms `collision` too, on a reuse spawn's second collision (in the one re-run of get-then-act the first gave) and on a plain spawn's collision in the one re-run of get-then-act a plain spawn's collision gave (b.jg5 SRJ-111; [Plain spawn](#plain-spawn-bjg5-srj-111)), and `spawn-not-resumable-lost-race` on a lost race: a resume's `ErrSpawnNotResumable` whose re-read found no reason to act, or a resume site's replacement whose re-read found the row in a known live state other than `pending`, or in a state CSCB does not know, on a path with no dead evidence (b.jg5 SRJ-710, SRJ-609), both through the outage state's site entries (`reportReuseCollisionAtSite`, `reportLostRaceAtSite`) and never counted. Behaviour (modes, the retry action, the outcome map, stop rules, condition ends) is in Auto-Restart, [UNAVAILABLE retry](#unavailable-retry-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305) and [Pending-only mode](#pending-only-mode-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305-srj-306); every line it logs is in docs/engineering-guide.md, Log Messages. **What arms a timer (b.jg5 SRJ-301).** A launch attempt (a run of a persona's collision ladder, whoever starts it) and a recovery attempt (a run of its restart work, adapters included) run through `runInAttempt(key, 'launch' | 'recovery', fn)`, an attempt context carried on `AsyncLocalStorage` across the attempt's awaits and timers; it holds only the running attempts, never a persona's state between them. Attempts nest (a restart's relaunch is a launch attempt inside the recovery attempt), and the innermost one for the key records the error. A new attempt links to the nearest attempt still running, and a continuation that outlives its attempt (a timer the attempt set) is outside it, so an attempt started after another has closed is not nested in it. `fn` is handed an `AttemptView` of its own attempt (`key`, `kind`, and a live `lastError`: the last agent-director error met in that attempt, not in one nested in it, with its verb, its cause kind and whether it armed); `isInsideAttempt(key)` reads the context. `runOutsideAttempts(fn)` runs `fn`, and everything it starts, outside every attempt (`AsyncLocalStorage.exit`): the registry starts the dialog approver through it, so the approver is part of no launch or recovery attempt (b.jg5 SRJ-401). It leaves the retry marker too. The retry marker (b.jg5 SRJ-410): `createFullModeRetryAction`'s action runs each retry inside `runInTimerRetry(key, fn)`, in both modes; `isInsideTimerRetry(key)` answers whether the current call is inside an open retry for that persona, and `claimTimerRetryRuleRun(key)` grants the pending-row rule's one run per retry ([The pending-row rule](#the-pending-row-rule-bjg5-srj-410)). The live-row sequence registry also runs a no-launch request (an old-life wait) through it, so nothing the wait meets arms a timer for its old key by the attempt rule (b.jg5 SRJ-811, SRJ-1512). `runDetachedRecoveryAttempt(key, fn)` runs `fn` as a recovery attempt of its own for the persona, outside the caller's (`runOutsideAttempts`, then `runInAttempt`): the live-row sequence registry's attempt runner (b.jg5 SRJ-706), so an error a sequence meets arms by the attempt rule there and never turns its starter's launch into `retrying`. `reportAttemptError(key, value, verb, sink)` is the one reporting step, reached through `reportAgentDirectorError` in `outage-state.ts`; its second half, `reportAttemptCause(key, cause, verb, sink)`, takes a cause the caller decided itself, under the same context rule (the outage state's site entry `reportUnclassifiedAtSite` passes the `unclassified` cause for the resume path's `ErrInvalidFlags`, the reconnect's, and a kill's outcome of a class the kill has no row for inside an attempt). The arming predicate `unavailableRetryCauseFor(value, verb)`, over the classifier, answers the cause, in this order: `unavailable` for an UNAVAILABLE outcome from any verb, `kill-failed` when that outcome is an `ErrTmuxKillFailed` instance (told apart by class through `isAdErrorInstance`; an `ErrUnknownErrorName` carrying that name is `unavailable`), `environment` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_ENVIRONMENT`) for an ENVIRONMENT answer (`ErrTmuxNotAvailable`) from any verb, `kill` and the read verbs included, `config` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_CONFIG`) for a CONFIG answer (`ErrConfigMalformed`) from any verb, `kill` and the read verbs included, `unclassified` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_UNCLASSIFIED`, b.jg5 SRJ-313) for an UNCLASSIFIED answer from any declared verb but `status`, `get` and `list` (a call with no known verb arms nothing; `ErrInvalidFlags` is STATE here), `read-error` for any other error from `status`, `get` or `list` except `ErrSpawnNotFound` (each site keeps its meaning) and an UNUSABLE_NAME answer, and nothing otherwise. The `environment` and `config` causes (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_ANY_CONTEXT_CAUSES`) arm in any context (b.jg5 SRJ-311, SRJ-316), so a persona that met a CONFIG answer is retried whatever `session_restart_delay` and `health_check_interval` are: inside an attempt for `key`, inside another persona's attempt, or outside every attempt (the health tick, the permission poller and click handler, the JSONL safeguard, the dialog approver). A persona teardown's kill, each try and each `status` read between its tries, is the one call outside an attempt that arms nothing: it passes the wrapper's `armsNothing` option (`outage-state.ts`; b.jg5 SRJ-110, SRJ-715, hatch A3). The start sweep (`reconcileOrphans`) calls agent-director outside the outage wrappers, so it reports nothing and arms nothing. A bounded kill retry inside an attempt (b.jg5 SRJ-702, `retryPersonaKill`) arms once per retry, not once per try: each try's UNAVAILABLE answer is held back (the wrapper's `deferUnavailableReport`), and only the outcome that stands is reported, once, through `reportDeferredUnavailable` (so `kill-failed` for an `ErrTmuxKillFailed` that stands); a try's other answers are reported at once, as they stand at once. Every other cause arms only inside an attempt for `key`; outside one it arms nothing. A stray `environment` or `config` arm (a torn-down persona, one not in the applied configuration or not up) stops at its first retry through the pre-call checks, with no agent-director call. One armed during a persona teardown (by a launch in flight, or an earlier call) does not wait for that: the teardown stops the persona's timer again once its launch in flight settled and once more after its kill ([Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-307) steps 3 and 8; the kill itself arms none), which matters for a destructive modify's old half, whose key stays applied and would pass those checks. A cause goes once to the trigger sink (`UnavailableRetryTriggerSink`, which the controller implements through `arm`, and through `armPendingOnly` for the sink's optional member of that name), so a trigger while armed keeps the due time. Inside an attempt for `key` the innermost attempt records the error as its last. It is recorded as armed only when the sink answers true, that is when the persona has a timer after the call; a sink that answers anything else, or throws, armed nothing, and the step never throws. A launch answers `retrying` (session-manager entry, `SPAWN_ACTION_RETRYING`) only from an error recorded as armed. A second arming path is the restart work's arm hook, `RestartDeps.armRetryTimer` (wired in `main()`): it arms the persona's timer with the `read-error` cause (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_READ_ERROR`) on every `unknown` liveness reading at the restart work, the re-probe's included, whatever made it `unknown` (a probe that throws included, which the arming predicate does not arm on; a probe whose own read latched the persona, an UNUSABLE_NAME answer or its own row reading `pending` with no launch start, stops at the work's latch check first and never reaches the hook, b.jg5 SRJ-512, SRJ-513; a CONFIG `status` has already armed the `config` cause through the reporting point, and a trigger while armed keeps the due time); see Auto-Restart, step 3. A third is the health tick's arm hook, `HealthCheckDeps.armRetryTimer` (wired in `main()`): a persona held off on its raised `tmux-unavailable` outage that the tick reads but does not find healthy, with no timer armed (`isRetryArmed` answers false), is armed with the `environment` cause, since a retry that stopped as not up, on a declined launch or on a failed run leaves the flag raised with no timer (see [Health-Check Poller](#health-check-poller) step 1). A fourth is the outage state's launch-failure arm (`armPendingOnlyAfterLaunchFailure`, `outage-state.ts`): inside a launch or recovery attempt for the persona, a launch's `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` (a plain spawn's, a reuse spawn's or a `resume`'s, in the collision ladder and the live-row sequence alike) arms its timer at once in pending-only mode through the sink's `armPendingOnly` (cause `pending-row`), recording no attempt error, so the counted failure stays counted (b.jg5 SRJ-112, SRJ-113, SRJ-301, SRJ-409). A fifth is the outage state's pending-row arm (`armPendingOnlyForPendingRow`), in or outside an attempt, for a covered or undecided `pending` row (b.jg5 SRJ-301, SRJ-409). An `armPendingOnly` during a running retry cancels no condition end deferred to that run; only a full-mode `arm` does (`armIn`). `FullModeRetryDeps.stepPendingRow?(key)` is the pending-only retry's pending-row step, called inside a recovery attempt when its `status` read shows `pending` (production: the session manager's `retryPendingRowStep`), whose answer decides (`pendingStepAnswer`: `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_PENDING_STEP_KEPT`, `…_SEQUENCE_STARTED`, `…_LATCHED`, `…_ROW`); `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_AGAIN_SEQUENCE_STARTED` (`live-row-sequence-started`) is the again-reason of a retry that started the live-row sequence for an uncovered row (b.jg5 SRJ-411) or through the abort of CSCB's own stuck launch (b.jg5 SRJ-412). `currentAttemptLastError(key)` (read-only, b.jg5 SRJ-407) answers the innermost running attempt's last recorded error, which the session manager's step after a launch's UNAVAILABLE outcome reads before its `get` replaces it, to answer `retrying` when the launch's error armed the timer. **The latch re-check scope (b.jg5 SRJ-505).** `runInLatchRecheck(scope, fn)` (`LatchRecheckScope`: `key`, the latch's `isLatched`, an optional `permit`, `LatchRecheckPermit` with `holds()`) is a third context beside the attempt context and the retry marker, carried the same way; `latchRecheckScopeOf(key)` answers the caller's scope object back, `isInsideLatchRecheck(key)` whether the current call is inside a re-check of `key` and the persona is still latched (a throwing query counts as latched), and `holdsLatchRecheckPermit(key)` whether its scope carries a permit that still holds. While `isInsideLatchRecheck`, the reporting step arms nothing for any cause in any context, and the controller's `arm` and `armPendingOnly` arm nothing, logging `[slack] unavailable-retry: persona=<key> not armed (<cause>) — inside its latch re-check, an answer gives no information`. `runOutsideAttempts` leaves the scope too.
    ├── outage-state.ts         Persona-scoped outage-flag state machine — tracks four orthogonal classes (`ad-unreachable`, `cwd-unreachable`, `tmux-unavailable`, `ad-config-malformed`; the last added by b.jg5 SRJ-316) per persona, keyed by persona key (b.av2 SR-6.3), and emits onset / all-clear notices through an injected `notify(key, text, options?)` hook. Production wires the hook to the per-persona notifier, so each notice goes to that persona's destination and names the persona; the `cwd-unreachable` detail is the persona's working directory. The `ad-unreachable` onset says the outage affects every persona, since the binary is host-wide, and its remedy points to the README's switch-over runbook section by its title (`PHASE1_RUNBOOK_SECTION_TITLE`, imported from `ad-version-gate.ts`), with no install, reinstall or upgrade command (b.jg5 SRJ-1001); the generic `tmux-unavailable` onset speaks for the one persona (agent-director cannot reach tmux for this persona), since the flag is raised and cleared per persona, and keeps its "install or repair tmux" remedy. Each notice carries `OutageNoticeOptions` (b.jg5 SRJ-1002, SRJ-1003): `{ outage: { phase: 'onset', classes: [<its class>] } }` or `{ outage: { phase: 'all-clear', classes: [<every class it lists>], allClearOf } }` (`allClearOf(classes)` renders the all-clear of a subset of those classes over the same bad-stretch snapshot, so the notifier can split it), which `main()` passes on to the notifier, so the all-clear of an outage whose onset a persona teardown's window wrote is written the same way, whenever it comes (the `persona-notifier.ts` entry). `server.ts` calls `initOutageState` at boot and, outside dry run, `resetAllToHealthy` with the applied persona keys before any persona is brought up, and a persona teardown calls it with that persona's key alone, once, right before its notice window opens (silent: no all-clear notice; a flag raised in the window is kept past the teardown); AD verb calls run inside `withOutageDetection` / `withSpawnDetection`, which raise a flag on a typed error (`tmux-unavailable` for class ENVIRONMENT, `ErrTmuxNotAvailable`, and `ad-config-malformed` for class CONFIG, `ErrConfigMalformed`, both decided through the classifier) and clear flags by these rules (b.jg5 SRJ-312): `ad-unreachable` and `ad-config-malformed` clear on any successful wrapped call (no error answer clears `ad-config-malformed`, `ErrSpawnNotFound` and GONE included); `tmux-unavailable` clears only when the declared call is tmux-touching (`isTmuxTouchingCall`, see [The tmux-unresponsive condition](#the-tmux-unresponsive-condition-bjg5-srj-307-srj-310), Declared verbs) and it succeeded or threw a GONE error, so a successful `status`, `get`, `list`, `find-missing`, `delete`, `get-permission`, `decide` or kill of a row not read live never clears it, because tmux did not answer them; `cwd-unreachable` clears on a successful `withSpawnDetection` call only. A GONE error is still rethrown unchanged: the all-clear its clear can emit goes out through the isolating step (`notifyIsolated`), so a `notify` that throws or rejects is logged once (`[slack] outage-state: all-clear notice for persona=<key> failed: <error> — the flags stay cleared; the notice counts as posted`) and never replaces the GONE error the wrapper rethrows. The all-clear is still one per bad stretch: it posts only when a clear empties the persona's flag set. `clearOutageFlag(key, cls, reading?)` tells the optional cleared-flag observer (`OutageStateDeps.onFlagCleared(key, cls, reading?)`) of each real clear, a flag that was raised, after the state change and any all-clear; a throwing observer is swallowed, and `resetAllToHealthy` (boot, teardown) never calls it. `main()` binds it so a `tmux-unavailable` clear calls the retry controller's `conditionEnded(key, 'tmux-unavailable', reading)` (see [Pending-only mode](#pending-only-mode-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305-srj-306), Condition ends). The `reading` is the row reading the clear brought: `pending` from a successful launch call (`isLaunchCall`), the live reading of a health tick or retry that found the persona healthy, and none from any other tmux-touching success or a GONE error. Outside the wrappers, `tmux-unavailable` is cleared only by the health tick's healthy branch ([Health-Check Poller](#health-check-poller) step 4) and a retry that finds the persona healthy (the `unavailable-retry.ts` entry); the liveness adapter clears `ad-unreachable` and `ad-config-malformed` only. Every error a wrapped call throws is then reported once, before the rethrow, through `reportAgentDirectorError(key, err, call)` (b.jg5 SRJ-301), which two other places also call: the liveness adapter in `server.ts`, for its bare `status`, and a persona that joined a shared `find-missing` sweep another caller started (`session-manager.ts`), under its own key. The wrappers take the call's verb as a declared argument, `withOutageDetection(key, dir, call, fn)` and `withSpawnDetection(key, dir, call, fn)`, with `call` an `AdCall` (`ad-error-class.ts`: the verb, and for `kill` whether the site kills a row it read live), so typecheck makes every wrapped call site declare it; `fn` gets the plain client. `withOutageDetection` takes an optional fifth argument (`OutageDetectionOptions`): with `armsNothing: { personaConfigured }`, used only by a persona teardown's kill (b.jg5 SRJ-110; hatch A3), the error is not reported (no retry timer is armed, no `tmux-unresponsive` condition is started, nothing reaches the unclassified sink), and an ENVIRONMENT or CONFIG answer raises `tmux-unavailable` or `ad-config-malformed` only when `personaConfigured()` answers true (a throw counts as false); the `ad-unreachable` raise and the clears are unchanged. With `deferUnavailableReport: true`, used only by one try of a bounded kill retry inside an attempt (b.jg5 SRJ-702), an UNAVAILABLE error (by class, `ErrTmuxKillFailed` included) is not reported: it arms no retry timer, starts no `tmux-unresponsive` condition and is not recorded as the attempt's last error; every other value, and a success, is handled as without it. The retry's caller then reports the outcome that stands once through `reportDeferredUnavailable(key, err, call)`, which reports an UNAVAILABLE value through `reportAgentDirectorError` with the kill's declared call and does nothing for any other value (its try reported it); it never throws. The report goes to the optional `triggerSink` in `OutageStateDeps` (see the `unavailable-retry.ts` entry): production installs the server's UNAVAILABLE retry controller there, and with none installed nothing is armed. An ENVIRONMENT or CONFIG error arms the persona's timer in any context (except under `armsNothing`); every other cause arms only inside a launch or recovery attempt for the persona. The same step starts or continues the persona's `tmux-unresponsive` condition through the optional `conditionSink` (`TmuxUnresponsiveSink`, production the condition built in `main()`): inside a launch or recovery attempt for the persona, for a tmux-touching call whose error the arming predicate answers with the `unavailable` cause (never ENVIRONMENT or CONFIG). The wrappers also end the condition, in any context, when a tmux-touching call succeeds or throws a GONE error, with the reading `pending` when the call was a successful launch (`isLaunchCall`) and no reading otherwise. With no condition sink installed nothing starts or ends. The same step also reports an UNCLASSIFIED error (b.jg5 SRJ-313) once to the optional `unclassifiedSink` (`UnclassifiedErrorSink`, production the unclassified-error episodes built in `main()`, see `persona-episodes.ts`): inside a launch or recovery attempt for the persona, from any declared verb, the reads included; outside an attempt, or from a call with no known verb, nothing is reported. `reportAgentDirectorError(key, err, call, { reportUnclassified: false })` keeps a value from that sink with its arming unchanged: the liveness adapter passes it for `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`, which keeps its `dead` reading. `reportUnclassifiedAtSite(key, err, call, classification)` is the site entry for an outcome a site classifies itself (the resume path's `ErrInvalidFlags` after its re-check, the reconnect's `send-keys` answering `ErrInvalidFlags`, and a kill in an attempt whose outcome is of a class the kill has no row for, `ErrInvalidFlags` after a re-check that did not stop included: `killPersonaInstance`, b.jg5 SRJ-110): inside an attempt it arms the persona's timer with the `unclassified` cause (`reportAttemptCause`) and reports the outcome with the site's classification; outside one it does nothing. The reuse spawn uses it too, for a name it gives no meaning; its `ErrInvalidFlags` reports nothing here (unless the re-check stops the server, it holds the persona, b.jg5 SRJ-207). `armPendingOnlyForPendingRow(key)` (b.jg5 SRJ-301, SRJ-409) is the pending-row arm: it asks the installed trigger sink's optional `armPendingOnly` to arm the persona's timer in pending-only mode, inside an attempt or outside every one, records no attempt error and starts no condition, answers whether the sink was asked, and never throws; the caller decides whether the persona may be armed (the session manager's `armPendingRowWatch` never arms a latched one). `armPendingOnlyAfterLaunchFailure(key)` (b.jg5 SRJ-112, SRJ-113, SRJ-409) is the launch-failure arm: for a launch's `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` (a plain spawn's, a reuse spawn's or a `resume`'s; the session manager's `launchFailureResult` calls it) it arms the persona's retry timer at once, with no `get` first, in pending-only mode through the trigger sink's optional `armPendingOnly`, only inside a launch or recovery attempt for the persona (a timer already in full mode stays in full mode); it records no attempt error, so the counted failure never becomes `retrying`, answers whether the sink was asked, and never throws. An UNCLASSIFIED outcome touches no flag (`ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` still raises `ad-unreachable` in the wrappers). Flags, notices and the rethrown error are unchanged by any sink. `tmux-unresponsive` is not one of its classes: see [The tmux-unresponsive condition](#the-tmux-unresponsive-condition-bjg5-srj-307-srj-310). State mutates before every emit (SR-V-2.x state-before-emit); no timestamps by design. **The `tmux-unavailable` onset (b.jg5 SRJ-1021).** Every site that raises `tmux-unavailable` on an ENVIRONMENT answer (the wrappers, the liveness adapter's bare `status` in `server.ts`, and a joiner of a shared `find-missing` sweep in `session-manager.ts`) raises it through the one entry `raiseTmuxUnavailable(key, err)`, never through `setOutageFlag`. The onset has two forms, chosen there at raise time from the raising error `err`: `tmuxServerChangedOnset()` (the *tmux server changed* text, which sends a human to agent-director's README "Operator actions", says no bot acts on it, and carries no tmux install or repair advice) when `isDifferentTmuxServerError(err)` (`ad-error-class.ts`) holds, and `ONSET_TEMPLATES['tmux-unavailable']` (*tmux unavailable*) otherwise. The choice is not stored: no detail is recorded for the flag, so the bad-stretch history and the all-clear (`ALL_CLEAR_TEMPLATE`, naming `tmux-unavailable` with no detail) are the existing ones, and agent-director's description never reaches Slack. The same-flag dedupe holds: the first raising error of a bad stretch picks the onset, and a second error of either form while the flag is raised posts nothing. Either form changes nothing else: no kill, delete or launch follows from it, and the flag clears by the rules above. `setOutageFlag` and `raiseTmuxUnavailable` share one private raise step (`raiseFlag`), so state still mutates before the emit. **The `ad-config-malformed` outage (b.jg5 SRJ-316, SRJ-1018).** agent-director refuses its config file: a CONFIG answer (`ErrConfigMalformed`, an `ErrUnknownErrorName` recognised by its `unknownName`, see [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)) from any wrapped call, in or out of an attempt, from the liveness adapter's bare `status`, or from a joiner's shared `find-missing` sweep raises it through the one entry `raiseAdConfigMalformed(key, err)`, never through `setOutageFlag`. It is handled as `ad-unreachable` is: the same destination, one onset per episode and the one all-clear. The flag is set first, then one raise line is logged (built from the classification's fields only, `describeAdErrorClassification`), then the onset (`adConfigMalformedOnset(err)`, `ONSET_TEMPLATES['ad-config-malformed']`) is posted, quoting the classifier's rendered message (redacted, one line, capped at `MAX_LOGGED_MESSAGE_LENGTH`) with Slack's control characters escaped after the cap (`escapeSlackControlCharacters`, `slack-text-escape.ts`), so a description cannot mention `@channel` or a user and no entity is cut; the raise line quotes the same message redacted but unescaped. A value with no description drops the quoting sentence. The onset goes out through a private isolating step (`notifyIsolated`): a `notify` that throws, or returns a promise that rejects, is logged once (`outageNoticeFailedLine`: `[slack] outage-state: onset notice for persona=<key> failed: <error> — the flag stays raised; the notice counts as posted`) and the onset counts as posted, so it is not posted again this episode and `raiseAdConfigMalformed` never throws. A wrapper raising it from its catch block therefore still reports the CONFIG value through `reportAgentDirectorError` (arming the retry timer) and rethrows that value, not the notify failure. No detail is ever recorded for the class, so the all-clear lists it bare and agent-director's text appears only in the onset. A second CONFIG answer while the flag is raised logs and posts nothing. It clears on any successful wrapped call and, at the liveness adapter, on a `status` success or `ErrSpawnNotFound` (each shows agent-director loaded its config and read its store); a real clear logs one line before any all-clear. `version` and `help` never clear it: CSCB never wraps them, and the version re-check touches no flag. Its clear stops no timer: the cleared-flag observer is told of it, but `main()` passes only `tmux-unavailable` clears to the retry controller. No action follows the outage: the site that met the answer refuses (see [Refusals at the launch and recovery sites](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)), and the retry timer retries the persona. CSCB's own read of `~/.agent-director/config.toml` (`ad-settings.ts`) never raises it; only agent-director's answers do. **Class order.** `OUTAGE_CLASS_ORDER` is the exported, frozen stable order (`ad-unreachable`, `cwd-unreachable`, `tmux-unavailable`, `ad-config-malformed`) in which the all-clear lists the resolved classes; tests iterate it. `_resetOutageState` is test-only. Its classes are outage flags only: the once-per-episode latches of the per-persona notice kinds live in `persona-episodes.ts`, which holds no `OutageClass`, except that the `ad-config-malformed` kind's latch is this module's `ad-config-malformed` flag. `endTmuxUnresponsiveForLaunchRow(key, reading)` (b.jg5 SRJ-310, SRJ-407) is the end entry of SRJ-310's third rule: it asks the installed condition sink to end the persona's `tmux-unresponsive` condition with `TMUX_UNRESPONSIVE_END_LAUNCH_ROW_LIVE` and the live state read, answers whether a sink was asked, works in any context and never throws; the session manager's shared own-row reads decide when it applies. It names no command. **The launch start not recorded** (b.jg5 SRJ-513). `launchStartNotRecordedSetInput(key, rowState)` is pure and builds the `set` input for a persona whose own row reads `pending` with no launch start: case `launch-start-not-recorded`, refused operation `none`, the given row state (`pending`), the session `slack_bot_<key>` and no description, since a row read carries none. `setLaunchStartNotRecorded(key, rowState)` is `set` with that input. Its trigger is the row-read rule's launch-start decision (`row-read-rules.ts`), acted on by the session manager's shared own-row `get` read and own-row `status` step, which, holding only `set`, pass the input to `set`. **The launch-start-not-recorded notice** (b.jg5 SRJ-1020). `launchStartNotRecordedNoticeText(key)` is pure and builds one line from the exported fixed parts (`LAUNCH_START_NOTICE_HEAD`, `LAUNCH_START_NOTICE_SESSION_END`, `LAUNCH_START_NOTICE_POINTER`, `LAUNCH_START_NOTICE_HOLD`, joined by `LAUNCH_START_NOTICE_SEPARATOR`) and the CONFLICT notice's human-only line: *Held: launch start not recorded*, why agent-director will not act on the row's session, the quoted session `"slack_bot_<key>"` (rendered and escaped as the CONFLICT notice renders a session), the pointer to the "Operator actions" section of agent-director's README, what CSCB does meanwhile, and the human-only line. It names no command. **Recognition.** `recogniseConflictCase(description)` is pure: the first entry of `CONFLICT_CASE_ORDER` whose phrase the description contains decides, and a description with none of the words, or a value that is not a string, is `unrecognised`. `CONFLICT_CASE_ORDER` is the one order, a frozen list of `{ latchCase, phrase }` over the phrase constants of `ad-description-phrases.ts`: `conflicting-labels` ("conflicting labels"), `pane-not-found` ("the agent's pane was not found"), `not-this-launch` ("not this launch's session"), `leftover` ("left over from an earlier life", the pre-spawn scan's leftover and the "duplicate session" leftover alike), `never-reported-in` ("never reported in"), `own-id` ("this row's own id"), `no-valid-id` ("no valid instance id"), `different-id` ("a different instance id"), `another-store` ("another agent-director store"), then unrecognised text. `never-reported-in` stays a distinct case in the record but is handled as unrecognised text: `takesUnrecognisedHandling(latchCase)` answers true for it and for `unrecognised` (`UNRECOGNISED_HANDLING_CASES`); its words come from a call CSCB never makes. The plain spawn's label wordings are not case phrases. **The CONFLICT notice** (b.jg5 SRJ-1004). `conflictNoticeText(source)` (`ConflictNoticeSource`: `sessionName`, `latchCase`, optional `description`, taken from a CONFLICT latch's record) is pure and builds the body from the exported fixed lines (the `CONFLICT_NOTICE_*` constants, joined by `CONFLICT_NOTICE_LINE_SEPARATOR`) and the case sentences (`CONFLICT_CASE_SENTENCES`, frozen, one per recognised case but `never-reported-in`; `conflictCaseSentence(latchCase)` answers `undefined` for `unrecognised`, `never-reported-in` and a hold case); the persona notifier adds the persona prefix. Its lines, in order: the first line, naming the quoted session, with the case sentence for a recognised case and none for unrecognised text or `never-reported-in`; the description line, quoting agent-director's description, left out when the source has none; then, for `different-id`, its must-not-be-ended line in place of the pointer line, for `another-store` its must-not-be-ended line followed by the pointer line, and for every other case the pointer line alone (the pointer sends a human to the "Operator actions" section of agent-director's README); then the `list` line, which names the session without its quotes; then the human-only line. The quoted description is redacted and capped (`renderLogMessageText`, the record's form, so a no-op on a record's description) before it is placed, then escaped once for Slack (`escapeSlackControlCharacters`, `slack-text-escape.ts`); the session name is rendered and escaped the same way in the first line and the `list` line. Log lines stay unescaped. CSCB's own lines never spell a label option's name (agent-director's quoted description may) and never name a session-ending command. **The recovery notice** (b.jg5 SRJ-1005). `conflictRecoveryText(sessionName, reason)` builds the CONFLICT latch's recovery body (naming the quoted session), `holdRecoveryText(reason)` the body for a hold latch (naming no session), and `latchRecoveryText(kind, reason, sessionName)` picks one by latch kind (`LatchKind`: `LATCH_KIND_CONFLICT` or `LATCH_KIND_HOLD`; `latchKindOf(latchCase)` answers the hold kind for a hold case and the CONFLICT kind otherwise); all are pure and built from the exported heads and tail (`CONFLICT_RECOVERY_HEAD`, `CONFLICT_RECOVERY_REASON_LEAD`, `HOLD_RECOVERY_HEAD`, `LATCH_RECOVERY_TAIL`). The reason (`LatchRecoveryReason`, one `LATCH_RECOVERY_REASON_KIND_*` kind each) is one of five: the row reads a state (`latchRecoveryReasonRowReads(state)`), the row is gone, a retry of the refused operation was not refused, the row finished and a relaunch was not refused, or cleared by hand (the frozen `LATCH_RECOVERY_REASON_*` values); `latchRecoveryReasonText(reason)` renders it from `LATCH_RECOVERY_REASON_ROW_READS_HEAD` and `LATCH_RECOVERY_REASON_TEXTS`, the state rendered and escaped as a quoted description is. The clear entry posts it. **The clear** (b.jg5 SRJ-506, SRJ-1005, SRJ-1016). `createLatchClear({ latch, episodes, stopTimer, log })` (`LatchClearDeps`) builds the one clear entry, `LatchClear` (`(key, reason) => boolean`): for a latched persona it removes the record (`forget`, its forget observers told), stops the re-check timer, posts `latchRecoveryText` for the record's latch kind once under `LATCH_RECOVERY_MARK` in the episode of that kind (begun first if none is open; nothing after the episodes' `close`), ends every latch-kind episode silently, and logs `latchClearedLine(key, record, reason, posted)`; an unlatched persona gets nothing and the answer is false. Each step is isolated (a throw logs `[slack] conflict-latch: persona=<key> clear step failed (<step>): <error>`); it never throws. It has two callers, both through `buildLatchRecheck`'s `LatchRecheck`: the re-check's clear hand-off, and the clear by hand of the `/clear-latch` route (`clearByHandOf` over `clearAndRecover`, the reason "cleared by hand", as the first step of the after-clear sequence's job, `runLatchClearSequence`, `src/session-manager.ts`). `RECHECK_CLEARS_THAT_LAUNCHED_NOTHING` names the re-check clears after which the persona is retried at once. **The notice's episode** (b.jg5 SRJ-508, SRJ-1016). `createConflictNoticeObserver(episodes)` (`ConflictNoticeEpisodes`, the `begin` and `post` of `PersonaEpisodes`, and its optional `end`) is a set observer: a `latched` or `relatched` set with a CONFLICT case or unrecognised text begins the persona's CONFLICT episode with the record's case (kept when its case is the same, a new episode for a new case) and posts the notice in it at most once, so a first latch posts once and a relatch with a new case posts once more; a `same-case` set keeps the episode and posts nothing; a hold case begins or keeps the episode of its own kind (`HOLD_NOTICES`, one `HoldNotice` per hold case: its episode kind and its text builder) and posts that text in it at most once, never the CONFLICT notice (`unusable-recorded-name` posts `unusableNameNoticeText`; `launch-start-not-recorded` posts `launchStartNotRecordedNoticeText`); before either, a `latched` or `relatched` set ends the persona's open episodes of the other latch kinds silently (`LATCH_NOTICE_EPISODE_KINDS`, `latchNoticeEpisodeKindOf`), so a relatch back posts once more; after the episodes' `close` it begins and posts nothing. The post goes through the episodes' sink, never straight to Slack, and the observer reads no other notice's latch, so no not-connected notice already posted (b.f2b's `unproven-idle` or `blocked-on-prompt`, under `notConnectedNoticeRaised`) holds it back. It ends no episode of the record's own kind. `bindConflictNotice(latch, episodes)` adds it to a latch and answers its removal. **The holds** (b.jg5 SRJ-305, SRJ-310, SRJ-313, SRJ-502). `createConflictLatchHoldObserver(holds, log)` (`ConflictLatchHolds`: `stopRetryTimer(key)`, `endTmuxUnresponsive(key)`, `endUnclassifiedError(key)`, and the optional `endSlowRecovery(key)` and `endStuckLaunch(key)`) is a second set observer: on every set, of all three outcomes and whatever the case, it stops the persona's retry timer, then ends its `tmux-unresponsive` condition silently, then ends its unclassified-error episode, then resets its slow-recovery count and ends its slow-recovery episode silently (b.jg5 SRJ-610, SRJ-1016; `main()` binds the tracker's `endForLatch`), then ends its stuck-launch episode silently (b.jg5 SRJ-1016; `main()` binds `endStuckLaunchEpisodeForLatch`, `pending-row.ts`, over its notice episodes), in that order; each step is isolated, and one that throws logs `[slack] conflict-latch: persona=<key> hold failed (<hold>): <describeThrownValue>` (`<hold>` is `retry timer stop`, `tmux-unresponsive end`, `unclassified-error end`, `slow-recovery end` or `stuck-launch end`) and the next still runs. A same-case set runs them too, since a refusal met while the persona was already latched may have armed its timer again. `bindConflictLatchHolds(latch, holds, log)` adds it to a latch and answers its removal. Observers run in the order they were added, and `main()` binds the holds before the notice, so every hold is done before the notice is posted (see [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)). No module-scope state, no agent-director call and nothing run at import or creation (the only timers are the re-check controller's, on its injected clock), so a test builds a fresh instance and needs no reset seam. `main()` in `server.ts` builds the server's one instance, binds its holds, then its CONFLICT notice, then its re-check timers (`bindLatchRecheck` over `buildLatchRecheck`'s controller) to it, and installs it in the session manager (`setConflictLatch`) and as the latched query of the restart work, the retry action and the health tick (see [Server-Managed Startup](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1)), keeping no module-scope handle to it. A latch is set by these callers: the collision ladder, through `setFromConflict`, on a CONFLICT at a spawn, reuse spawn or `resume` it makes; the restart path's kill adapter (through the session manager's `latchOnRestartKillOutcome`) and the live-row sequence's kills on a CONFLICT at a kill, with the refused operation `next-check-or-recovery` for a kill (b.jg5 SRJ-110), and the session manager's own-row read (`readPersonaOwnRow`), through `set`, on a `provenance_conflict` note on a configured persona's own row (case `conflicting-labels`, refused operation `bring-up`, the session `slack_bot_<key>` and no description, so its CONFLICT notice has no description line); and, on an UNUSABLE_NAME answer, the session manager's `unusableNameAt`, its shared own-row reads and its own-row `status` step, through `set` with `unusableNameSetInput`'s input (the liveness and reconnect adapters in `server.ts` reach it through that step); and, on a configured persona's own row that reads `pending` with no launch start, the session manager's shared own-row `get` read and its own-row `status` step, through `set` with `launchStartNotRecordedSetInput`'s input ([Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502), [Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)). The persona teardown (`runTeardown`, `persona-lifecycle.ts`) calls `forget` for its key through the injected `forgetConflictLatch`, after the launch in flight settled and right before it forgets the persona's notice episodes, which ends the CONFLICT episode too (b.jg5 SRJ-504); a process that ends drops every latch. The re-check's step-1 reads and retries latch through the same session-manager entries, and the clear entry is the only other path that drops a latch. **The re-check** (b.jg5 SRJ-505; [The re-check](#the-re-check-bjg5-srj-505)). `LATCH_RECHECK_INTERVAL_MS` (120 000). Step 1's reading, `LatchRecheckReading` (`RECHECK_READING_*`: a state, with `notePresent` for a `get`; no row; a failed read). `decideLatchRecheck({ record, reading, retiredKeyRecorded })` (pure) answers a `LatchRecheckDecision` (`step`, `action` and `call` from the `RECHECK_STEP_*`, `RECHECK_ACTION_*` and `RECHECK_CALL_*` identifiers; `clear`, with the recovery reason, when the reading clears; `unmatched` for a pair no row matches); `decideFinishedRowLaunch(reading, hasSessionId, retiredKeyRecorded)` (pure) the finished-row retry's launch; `decideLatchRecheckProbe(latchCase, answer)` and `decideLatchRecheckPendingReadPane(latchCase, answer)` (pure) the verdicts (`RECHECK_VERDICT_*`) on one `read-pane` answer (`LatchRecheckPaneAnswer`: the pure mapper's `PANE_READ_*` kind and, for a CONFLICT, its case). The clear hand-off's type, `LatchRecheckClearHandOff` (`LatchRecheckCleared`: `by`, one of `RECHECK_CLEARED_BY_*`, the record and the recovery reason); a probe that finds the condition cleared is no clear and is not handed off. `decideClearedProbeRetry(record, reading, retiredKeyRecorded)` (pure) the single retry after a cleared probe. The timers: `createLatchRecheckController({ clock, isLatched, serialize, round, log, intervalMs? })` (`LatchRecheckControllerDeps`, `LatchRecheckClock`) answers a `LatchRecheckController` (`observer`, `arm`, `stop`, `stopAll`, `isArmed`, `armedKeys`, `whenRoundSettled`) and imports nothing from the session manager; `bindLatchRecheck(latch, controller)` adds its set observer and a forget observer that stops the persona's timer, and answers their removal. A clock that throws logs `[slack] conflict-latch: persona=<key> re-check timer could not be set: <error> — not armed`, a rejected round `[slack] conflict-latch: persona=<key> re-check round failed: <error>`. `latchRecheckRoundLine(ref, latchCase, call, answer)` (pure) builds the round's one line. The round itself, which makes the calls, is the session manager's (`runLatchRecheckRound`, composed by `buildLatchRecheck`). See [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104).
