```
    ├── interject.ts            b.av2 SR-9.1 / SR-9.2 / SR-13.1 `/interject` request handler. `handleInterject(req, remoteAddress, deps)` validates the request (method, localhost, `INTERJECT_BODY_CAP_BYTES` 32 KB cap, JSON, `persona` and `message` fields), resolves the persona by name or key with `resolvePersonaTarget`, refuses a persona that is not up with 503 (b.av2 SR-6.4), looks up its session, and sends one `notifications/claude/channel` with meta `user` and `ts` only. Injected dependencies: `getPersonaConfig` (the applied persona config, or null), `isPersonaUp` (production: the server's `createPersonaUpPredicate`), `getSessionByPersona`, and optional `now` and `log`. No import-time side effects: it reads no file, environment variable or config, binds nothing and never imports `server.ts`. Also exports `DEFAULT_INTERJECT_SENDER` (`interject`); `cron-dispatch.ts` imports the body cap. See [POST /interject](#post-interject).
    ├── crontable.ts            cscb_cron parser — `parseCrontable(text)` turns crontable text (5-field cron expression + prompt-file path + optional comma-separated persona list, each entry a persona name or key, space-delimited) into in-memory `{schedules, errors}` records. Pure module, no I/O, no timers (backoff.ts precedent); expression validity is delegated to the bundled zero-dependency `croner` library. Tolerant parse (PD-6): `#` comments and blank lines are skipped silently, each bad line becomes a structured parse-error record `{lineNumber, rawLine, reason class}` for the caller to log while sibling lines survive, and it never throws for content reasons. Duplicate lines are both kept; targets are kept verbatim, duplicates included, and are neither resolved nor validated here — name-to-key resolution and deduplication happen at fire time in `cron-dispatch.ts`. Each schedule carries identity `cscb-cron:<prompt-file-basename-without-extension>` (PD-1), the verbatim prompt path, its 1-based `lineNumber` in the source text (comments and blank lines counted, so it is the line the operator edits; the scheduler's load warning names it), and a `targets` union (all-bots marker vs. explicit list of targets as written). Parse-error reason classes keep their channel-list names (`wildcard-channel-list` for a literal `*`, `malformed-channel-list`, `path-with-spaces`).
    ├── cron-bootstrap.ts       cscb_cron boot-time crontable creator — `ensureCrontableExists(path)` guarantees a crontable file exists, returning `created` / `already-exists` / `failed(cause)`. Exclusive-create only: writes the template header with `{ flag: 'wx' }` when the path is absent, never write-then-rename and never mkdir's a missing parent: the default location's directory is made before the scheduler starts by the start's `prepareDefaultCronTable` (`cron-table-migration.ts`, bug b.avm), and nothing makes the directory of a `cron_table_path` the operator chose, even one naming the default's file. EEXIST is swallowed as `already-exists` (a human or another bot winning the create race is normal, not an error); a pre-existing file is left untouched byte-for-byte. Non-EEXIST errors surface as a `failed` outcome — never thrown, never `process.exit` — so a bad path can't crash boot. The module itself never logs; callers own log level and wording — `cron-scheduler.ts` uses it on both paths: an INFO line for the first-install create at `start()`, and, after a runtime deletion, a distinct re-created INFO line following the latched vanish WARN. D-Q1 invariant: this create is the server's ONLY write to the crontable, ever — the server never rewrites, reorders, normalizes, or prunes its content. The `#`-comment template header is exported as the shared constant `CRONTABLE_TEMPLATE_HEADER` (consumed by E6 bot discoverability); its documented line format tracks `crontable.ts`'s parser.
    ├── cron-table-migration.ts bug b.avm the start's preparation of the crontable's default location, and the move of a crontable left at the old default. `prepareDefaultCronTable(paths, deps)` (`CronTablePaths`: `inEffect`, the start-time configuration's `cron_table_path`; `defaulted`, whether the loader filled it in, `cron_table_path_defaulted`; `defaultPath` and `legacyPath`, from `config.ts`'s `resolveDefaultCronTablePath` and `legacyCronTablePath`; `CronTableMigrationDeps`: `log` and an optional partial `fs`, `CronTableMigrationFs`, over the real file system `NODE_CRON_TABLE_MIGRATION_FS`) runs once per start (Server-Managed Startup step 2a-ter) and answers a `CronTableMigrationOutcome`. It acts only when `defaulted` is true and `inEffect` is the default, and the default is not the old path: otherwise `not-default` (any `cron_table_path` the operator wrote, even one naming the default's own file: nothing created, moved or linked, D-Q1) or `legacy-is-default` (`SLACK_STATE_DIR` set). It then makes the default's directory (`mkdir -p`) and compares the two paths: nothing, or a dangling link, at the old path is `no-legacy`; two regular files that are one inode (a hard link, left by a move that stopped after placing the file) are finished as `moved` `resumed`; any other pair that names one file with links followed (the same device and inode, whichever way the links point) is `already-migrated`, logged by nothing, so a re-run is a no-op; a regular file at the old path and nothing at the new one is `moved`. The move first makes a symbolic link to the new path beside the old path under a temporary name, so an old directory that cannot take it stops the move before anything changed; it then hard-links the file to the new path (`via` `link`) or, when a hard link can't be made (`EXDEV`, `EPERM`, `ENOTSUP`, `EOPNOTSUPP`, `EMLINK`), copies it with its mode to a temporary name beside the new path and hard-links the copy into place (`copy`), but only when the old file's device, inode, size and modification time are the same before and after the copy (otherwise the copy is removed and the move fails with `CRON_TABLE_CHANGED_DURING_COPY_CAUSE`); finally it renames the temporary link over the old path. A link at the old path to a regular file elsewhere, with nothing at the new path, gives the new path a link to that file's real path and leaves the old link (`linked`); anything at both paths that is not one file is `both-exist` (the new one used, the old one untouched); anything else at the old path is `not-regular`. A failed step is `failed` with its `step` and cause. `mkdir`, `move` (placing the file, the stale copy included) and `unexpected` (a path that could not be looked at) change nothing, and the pure `cronTablePathForStart(paths, outcome)` then answers the old path, which `main()` makes the crontable the start runs on; `swap` (the file in place, the old name not replaced) runs on the new path, and the next start finishes it as `resumed` while both names are one inode. Whenever the start runs on the new path after a move, a link or a failed swap, the module carries the prompts. A directory at `<old dir>/prompts`, with nothing at `<new dir>/prompts`, is moved there: a symbolic link to the new name is made beside it under a temporary name, the directory is renamed, and the link is renamed to the old name. A rename that fails with `EXDEV` links `<new dir>/prompts` to the old directory instead; an old `prompts` that is itself a link to a directory gets the new name linked to its real path, the old link left; a taken new name is left alone. It then reads the crontable at the new path (`parseCrontable`) and, for each line whose relative prompt path (resolved with `cron-dispatch.ts`'s exported `resolvePromptPath`, against each crontable path as given) named an existing file before the move and names none after it, logs one WARN naming the absolute path to write; no line is ever rewritten. It never writes crontable content (the bootstrap's create stays the server's only write of it) and never overwrites the new path: both hard links and the symbolic link fail on an existing file, and only its own temporary names are ever removed. It never throws: every outcome but `no-legacy`, `already-migrated`, `not-default` and `legacy-is-default` logs one line of its own (each prompts step and each relative-path WARN add theirs), information lines prefixed `CRON_MIGRATE_LOG_PREFIX` (`[slack] cron-migrate:`) and WARNs `CRON_MIGRATE_WARN_PREFIX` (`[slack] Warning: cron-migrate:`), built by the exported `cronTable*Line` and `cronPrompts*Line`/`cronRelativePromptMovedLine` builders. The builders whose line quotes a file-system error are the lines listed for this module in `tests/secrecy-audit.test.ts`'s `RAW_ERROR_ALLOWED`. No module-scope state and nothing run at import.
    ├── cron-log.ts             cscb_cron log writer — the single writer of the dedicated cron log at `cron_log_path`. `createCronLog(path, { maxBytes?, write? })` returns a handle whose `outcome`/`summary`/`info`/`warn` methods funnel through one internal append: per-(fire,target) outcome entries whose target field holds the target as written in the crontable, per-fire summary lines, info lines, and warn lines (the latter two are line kinds, not outcome classes). Write failures are swallowed (one `[slack] cron-log` console.error, fd dropped, self-heals next append) — they never propagate into dispatch. With `maxBytes` set it caps the log by dropping the oldest whole lines (`write` is the rewrite's test seam); without it the log is append-only. See [cron.log](#cronlog-cron_log_path) and [Pruning](#pruning-cron_log_max_bytes). Pure half (record types, line formatting and `cronLogPruneOffset`, the prune's cut) is I/O-free.
    ├── cron-dispatch.ts        cscb_cron fire/delivery path — `createCronDispatcher({port, cronLog, cronTablePath, resolveTarget})` returns a handle whose `fire(schedule)` delivers ONE matched schedule; it logs every outcome and never throws. The scheduler's tick (`cron-scheduler.ts`) is the only caller — it hands the minute's matches to the dispatcher. The module imports nothing from server.ts, holds no timer, and reads no crontable. Each schedule delivers independently: every match becomes its own `/interject` POST and its own outcome line, so N schedules matching the same minute produce N separate messages. Fixed internal shape (E4's seam, do not collapse): resolve-targets → all-bots deferral branch → target-origin-agnostic per-target delivery. Targets resolve from the schedule's explicit persona list at FIRE time (`resolveDeliveryTargets`, pure): each written target goes through the injected `resolveTarget` (name or key → persona key, so a changed persona set applies at the next fire), then targets are deduplicated on the value to be POSTed in first-seen order — a persona named twice, by name or key, is delivered once; a target that resolves to nothing is POSTed as written, once per distinct text, so the handler answers 404. Each delivery target keeps the first-written text as its log target field. The all-bots marker is deferred to E4 — no read, no POST, one `fanout-deferred` outcome (target `-`) plus a `delivered=0 failed=0` summary (the target set is undefined until E4, and a no-match minute logs nothing, so 0/0 cannot read as quiet success). The prompt file is resolved and fresh-read every fire (never cached): leading `~` via `config.ts` `expandTilde`, absolute as-is, relative anchored to the CRONTABLE's directory — a deliberate divergence from system cron's $HOME convention so a prompt can colocate as `prompts/foo.md` and stay stable (E6's format reference carries this rationale). Missing → `prompt-missing`, unreadable → `prompt-unreadable` (errno), each target `-`, then a `failed=<targets>` summary and no POST. D-Q5 skip-never-truncate: the oversize predicate is UTF-8 byte length of the EXACT serialized `{persona, message, sender}` body > 32768 (`INTERJECT_BODY_CAP_BYTES`, imported from `interject.ts`), byte-identical to the /interject handler's own check — the measured string IS the sent string, so a 413 is structurally impossible; over-cap targets log `prompt-oversize` (size, cap) and are skipped, never truncated, never POSTed. Under-cap targets POST the measured body to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/interject` AS-IS (decision 7 — no extraction, no internal call) with `sender` = schedule identity (D-Q4 — else senderLabel defaults to `interject` and fires are indistinguishable from peer-bot traffic). Status → outcome: 200 `delivered`, 503 `no-session` (decision 1 — NO retry, no queue, no scheduleRestart), 404 `unknown-persona`, else/network error `http-error`. Sequential loop attempts every target; exactly one outcome line per (fire,target) plus one per-fire summary (`failed` = targets whose intended delivery did not happen). Known limitation (recorded, unsolved): a single non-loopback `bind` leaves no loopback listener, so every fire fails connection-refused → `http-error`; no loopback detection is added.
    ├── cron-scheduler.ts       cscb_cron once-per-minute dispatch tick — `createCronScheduler({dispatcher, cronLog, cronTablePath, clock?})` returns a `start`/`stop`/`tick` handle whose single self-re-arming minute-aligned `setTimeout` chain (NOT `setInterval` — ticks are serialized so the hot-reload step mutates the table only between whole passes) is the ONLY code path that dispatches schedules (decision 8). `start()` runs the crontable bootstrap FIRST (this `start()` is the sole `ensureCrontableExists` caller), performs the initial read + parse through the same shared load path the tick's reload uses (parse errors → `parse-error` outcome lines, target `-`; each loaded line with no persona list → one undeliverable `warn` line, b.n4n), compiles each schedule's croner pattern once per load (queried, never started — no callback, so it schedules nothing itself), writes exactly ONE `scheduler started, N schedules loaded, M undeliverable (no persona list)` info line (PD-4 outage-window marker), then arms the tick; `start()` is failure-isolated and never throws out to the server. Each tick first re-loads the crontable if its `(mtimeMs, size)` differs from the last successful load — no watcher, no dirty flag — then stamps the current wall-clock minute and skips the whole pass unless it is strictly after the last-ticked minute (monotonic guard — a backwards clock jump must not re-fire fired minutes), matches every in-memory schedule against that minute in server-local time via croner (DST is the library's, D-Q3), and hands each match, in crontable line order, to the dispatcher. No catch-up: a tick fires only the minute observed at its start; an overrun minute is simply skipped, and a no-match minute does nothing and logs nothing. The at-most-once `Map<schedule instance, epoch minute>` is a LOGGED ASSERTION, not the mechanism (decision 8): keyed on the compiled-schedule instance (NOT raw line text), so two identical operator lines are distinct schedules that EACH fire (PD-6) — only the SAME loaded schedule reappearing twice in one pass is skipped and shouted as a `SCHEDULER BUG` info line (an info line kind, deliberately NOT an outcome class, so it never pollutes the `grep http-error` triage view). NO rate cap / backlog cap / busy-detection / queue-depth check of any kind (owner gate answers 1-2). `stop()` is idempotent and cancels the pending timer.
    ├── health-check.ts         Periodic liveness poller — checks every applied persona on a timer via client.status. The work list comes from `HealthCheckDeps.getPersonas()` (production: the pure `buildPersonaWorkList(config, include?)`, persona key → working directory, one entry per persona however many channels it lists, filtered by `include`; the server passes the relaunch gate, so a persona that is not up, whether its Slack connection is not serving or its bring-up is broken or retrying, is left out of the tick); streaks, guard calls and the `cwd-unreachable` flag are keyed by persona key (b.av2 SR-6.3), and log lines name it as `persona=<key>`. `HealthCheckDeps.isSessionAlive(key)` answers a liveness reading (`liveness-reading.ts`), not a boolean: `dead` schedules a restart at once, and `unknown` (a thrown probe included) skips the persona for the tick, clearing its streak and arming nothing (b.jg5 SRJ-314). It schedules recovery for dead sessions AND for sessions that are alive (`live` or `pending`) but not deliverable — either MCP-disconnected (b.9a7) OR connected-but-streamless (b.9cj — `connected === true` in the registry while the SDK has silently dropped the `_GET_stream` map entry, probed via `HealthCheckDeps.hasSessionStream`). Only `live` is ever counted healthy: a `pending` row connected with its stream takes the not-deliverable path too, with no not-connected notice (b.jg5 SRJ-314). Both non-deliverable cases require two consecutive failing ticks before acting, a shared false-positive guard for the freshly-launched window; routes all through `scheduleRestart` (restart.ts then reconnects vs. relaunches per case); skips personas at the failure cap via `HealthCheckDeps.isAtCap` (SR-25.3/25.4), including the reconnect path. A persona with a no-attempt reason (`noAttemptReason`: it is latched, through the optional `isLatched`, wired in production to the server's latch, b.jg5 SRJ-502; it is held on `ErrInvalidFlags`, through the optional `isHeld`, wired in production to the server's hold, b.jg5 SRJ-207; work in flight; or its `tmux-unavailable` outage raised; b.jg5 SRJ-315) is still read, but the tick never calls `scheduleRestart` or `notifyNotConnected` for it; `latched` is asked again right after the tick's own read, which can latch the persona (b.jg5 SRJ-512). b.f2b adds five optional dependencies, all wired in production: `isLaunchInFlight` (true while anything is in flight for the persona, such as a parked start launch, a running live-row sequence or a running dialog approver; production binds the server's "in flight for P" binding `isPersonaWorkInFlight`, which the lost-message routing's read gate shares and which is built from the retry timer's "blocks a retry" binding; a no-attempt reason), `hasPendingWorkingRowEvidence` (schedule on the first undeliverable tick while the reconnect adapter gathers idle evidence for a `working` row), `isAutoRestartDisabled` with `notifyNotConnected(key, cause)` (with `session_restart_delay` 0, report an alive persona it would reconnect through the not-connected notice, worded for a `disconnected` or a `streamless` session), and `endNotConnectedEpisode` (end the persona's episode on every tick that finds it deliverable). b.jg5 SRJ-310 adds a sixth, wired in production: `endTmuxUnresponsive(key)`, called on the same healthy branch, which ends the persona's `tmux-unresponsive` condition with the tick's `live` reading. That branch then clears the persona's `tmux-unavailable` outage itself (`clearOutageFlag` with the `live` reading, no new dep; b.jg5 SRJ-312). b.jg5 SRJ-308 adds two more, wired in production: `now()`, the clock the tick's start time is read from as its body starts (production: the notice episodes' clock; absent, `Date.now`), and `onTickEnd(tickStartedAt)`, called once when each tick body ends, after all of its per-persona work and however the body ends, bound to the condition's `onsetAtTick(tickStartedAt)` (a throw is logged and changes nothing else). b.jg5 SRJ-311 adds two more, wired in production: `isRetryArmed(key)` (the retry controller's `isArmed`) and `armRetryTimer(key)` (the controller's `arm` with the `environment` cause). For a persona held off on `tmux-unavailable` that the tick reads but does not find healthy (`dead`, `pending`, disconnected or streamless), the tick arms its retry timer when `isRetryArmed` answers exactly `false`, with one line, and still makes no attempt of its own (`armMissingRetryTimer`; see [Health-Check Poller](#health-check-poller) step 1); with either member absent it arms nothing. b.jg5 SRJ-610 adds one more, wired in production: `resetSlowRecoveryCount(key)` (the slow-recovery tracker's `noteHealthy`), called last on the healthy branch, which resets the persona's slow-recovery count and leaves an open episode open. `forgetDisconnectedStreak(key)` drops one persona's disconnected streak at once, for a persona teardown.
    ├── clear-latch.ts          b.jg5 SRJ-510 / SRJ-511 / SRJ-509 the `clear-latch` names, the `POST /clear-latch` request handler and the `server.port` record. Exports the one spelling of the command (`CLEAR_LATCH_COMMAND`), the route (`CLEAR_LATCH_ROUTE`) and the record's file name (`SERVER_PORT_FILE_NAME`, `serverPortFilePath(stateDir)`); the route and command are for the operator only, so no MCP tool, MCP instruction text, tool description or notice names them (SRJ-511). `handleClearLatch(req, remoteAddress, deps)` checks the method, the loopback rule (`isLocalAddress`, shared with `interject.ts`), the body cap (`INTERJECT_BODY_CAP_BYTES`), the JSON and the `persona` field, resolves the persona by name or key (`resolvePersonaTarget`), then makes exactly one call of the injected `clearByHand(key)` and answers with its result; it never throws. Injected dependencies (`ClearLatchDeps`): `getPersonaConfig` (the applied persona config, or null), `clearByHand` (production: `clearByHandOf(latchRecheck)`, `session-manager.ts`) and an optional `log`. The record (`ServerPortRecord`: `pid`, `port`): `writeServerPortRecord(path, record, write?)` writes `serverPortRecordText(record)` through `atomicWriteFileSync` and rethrows a failure (the caller logs `serverPortWriteFailedLine`); `readServerPortRecord(path, expectedPid, fs?)` never throws and answers the record or a fixed cause (`SERVER_PORT_CAUSE_*`: absent, unreadable, malformed, out of range, another PID), none carrying file content; `removeServerPortRecord(path, fs?)` is a best-effort unlink that never throws. The line builders: `clearLatchNotLatchedLine`, `clearLatchUnknownPersonaLine` (no argument), `clearLatchFailedLine`. The CLI's request (b.jg5 SRJ-510): `dialClearLatch(port, persona, requestFn?)`, the production `CliDeps.dialClearLatch`, makes one `POST` of `{ "persona": <persona> }` as JSON to the route on `CLEAR_LATCH_DIAL_HOST` (`127.0.0.1`) at `port` (`clearLatchUrl(port)` names the same place) and answers the status and the body text once the whole body is read (`ClearLatchDialAnswer`), a non-200 included. It goes through `node:http`'s `request` (the injectable seam `ClearLatchRequest`, `node:http`'s `request` by default) with the options of the pure `clearLatchRequestOptions(port, bodyBytes)`: `Content-Type: application/json`, `Content-Length` in bytes, and `agent: false`, a connection of its own so no pooled socket keeps the CLI alive. Unlike `fetch`, which sends a request to the proxy that `HTTP_PROXY` names unless `NO_PROXY` exempts `127.0.0.1`, it reads no proxy environment variable, so the persona argument (perhaps a token typed by mistake) never leaves the host. A synchronous throw of the request call, a request error (a failed connection) or a response error (a failed body read) rejects with that error unchanged, and a response aborted before its end rejects; a refused connection's cause, through `describeThrownValue`, reads like `Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:<port>`. It sets no timeout of its own (the CLI bounds the wait) and logs nothing. `parseClearLatchAnswer(text)` reads a 200's body as `{ persona, cleared }`, or null when it is malformed (not an object, `ok` not `true`, `persona` not a non-empty string or `cleared` not a boolean); it never throws. No import-time side effects: it reads no file, environment variable or config, binds nothing and logs nothing, and it loads no server-only module, since `cli.ts` and `pid.ts` import it. See [POST /clear-latch](#post-clear-latch) and [server.port](#serverport-state_dirserverport).

    ├── cozempic.ts             Optional cozempic CLI integration — path resolution helpers retained for downstream callers.
    ├── tokens.ts               Dry-run detection only — `isDryRun()` reads `SLACK_DRY_RUN` at call time. The server reads no Slack token from the environment; each persona's tokens come only from its credentials file (`persona-credentials.ts`).
    ├── ack-tracker.ts          b.av2 SR-4.5 / SR-6.5 (as amended by b.deo SRI-307) in-memory ack-reaction state. Entries are keyed by (persona key, conversation ID, message ts), encoded as a JSON array so no character inside a component can make two keys collide. `trackAck(personaKey, channelId, messageTs)` upserts an entry and prunes entries older than 30 days (`ACK_EXPIRY_MS`; there is no other bound or timer). `consumeAck(personaKey, channelId, messageTs)` deletes and reports only that persona's own entry, leaving another persona's entry for the same message alone. `forgetPersonaAcks(personaKey)` drops every entry of one persona (the persona teardown) and no other. Side-effect free at import; logs nothing.

Two entry points share one synchronous patch: the start pass `trustBootstrap(personaConfig)` (once per applied persona; failures go to `recordStartupError`, see startup step 4a-bis) and the per-launch `trustPatchPersona(persona)`, which `server.ts` installs into the session manager with `setPreLaunchTrustPatcher` so it runs before every spawn, resume and restart (failures are logged only). Idempotent (no rewrite when both flags set); atomic `.tmp` + `renameSync`; never auto-creates a missing file; never throws.
    ├── stop-hook-bootstrap.ts  SR-3 / b.av2 SR-9.4 patcher for `<claude_config_dir>/settings.json` — installs (or removes) the CSCB-managed Slack Reply Guard Stop-hook group, and runs the per-persona reply-guard steps before each launch. The managed command is the guard's absolute path followed by the record directory `<state dir>/reply-guard`, each single-quoted (`managedHookCommand(stateDir)`). Install rule, per directory (grouped by real path): the directory's personas are the applied personas whose effective `claude_config_dir` it is plus those whose running instance launched with it; the entry is ensured if any of them has an effective `stop_hook_bootstrap` of `true` or a record reading `true`, and removed otherwise. Two passes apply it: the start pass `stopHookBootstrap(personaConfig, stateDir)` over every applied persona (startup step 4a-ter) and the launch pass, which re-evaluates only a launching persona's new effective dir and its previous launched-with dir. `preLaunchReplyGuard(persona, personas, stateDir)` is the pre-launch step `server.ts` installs into the session manager: it writes the launching persona's record, updates its launched-with dir (kept in memory per persona key, empty at server start) and runs the launch pass, and returns an undo for a launch that turns out not to be one. It does nothing for a persona whose key is not in the applied set it reads at that moment (b.av2 SR-8.6 as amended by b.deo SRI-201, SRI-203, SRI-406, SRI-408, SRI-502, SRI-802, SRI-805), so a late launch of a persona a confirmed apply removed neither re-creates its record nor runs a launch pass. `teardownPersonaReplyGuard(stateDir, key)` deletes a persona's record and forgets its launched-with dir; the persona teardown calls it, then runs the launch pass (`stopHookLaunchPass`) over the removed persona's configured and launched-with dirs against the personas still applied. Never writes under the operator's `~/.claude`; no entry point throws.
    ├── reply-guard-record.ts   b.av2 SR-9.4 per-persona reply-guard record — the record directory `<state dir>/reply-guard` and the record `reply-guard/<key>` (see Configuration, reply-guard/<key>). Write (the exact text `true` or `false`, atomic, creating the directory), read (`true` only for `true` with at most one trailing newline; missing or unreadable is `absent`) and delete (a missing record is success). A key outside `PERSONA_KEY_RE` is refused before any filesystem call. Side-effect-free; every path comes from the caller's state directory.
    ├── atomic-write.ts         Atomic file writes. `atomicWriteFileSync(path, contents)` — write `<path>.tmp`, then rename it over `path`; on failure the `.tmp` file is removed and the error rethrown. Used by `stop-hook-bootstrap.ts`, `reply-guard-record.ts` and `clear-latch.ts` (the `server.port` record). `durableWriteFileSync(path, bytes, fs?)` (b.av2 SR-8.1 as amended by b.deo SRI-401) is the atomic and durable write of the reload files: it creates a temporary file beside `path` named `<name>.<pid>.<random hex>.tmp` (opened exclusively, so each write has its own), writes every byte as given, fsyncs and closes it, renames it over `path`, then fsyncs the directory so the rename survives a crash. A failure before the rename leaves `path` as it was, removes the temporary file (best effort) and rethrows the error as raised. A failure to open or fsync the directory, after the rename, throws `DurableWriteUnsyncedError` (`path`, `code`, `syncError`): the new bytes are at `path` but may not survive a crash. A failure to close the directory after a successful fsync is ignored. The `fs` seam (`DurableWriteFs`) lets tests observe the call order or fail one call. `durableUnlinkSync(path, fs?)` is the durable delete: unlink, then fsync the directory. It returns true when a file was removed and false when `path` was already absent (ENOENT or ENOTDIR, with no directory sync). Any other failure is rethrown: an unlink failure is thrown as raised and leaves `path` as it was; a failure to open or fsync the directory comes after the unlink and throws `DurableUnlinkUnsyncedError` (`path`, `code`, `syncError`): `path` is gone, but the removal may not survive a crash. A failure to close the directory after a successful fsync is ignored, as for the write. Both are used by `reload.ts`, the delete for `config.json.pending`, by `retired-keys.ts` for the retired-key record, and by `channel-delivery.ts` for the stored-choice file, whose delete only removes a file that a refused `set`'s unsynced write created. `cron-log.ts` uses the write alone, for the cron log's prune rewrite (see [Pruning](#pruning-cron_log_max_bytes)). Nothing here logs. Side-effect-free.
    ├── jsonl-persistence-check.ts  startup safeguard — detects JSONL transcript loss / non-persistent storage before the resume path; see startup step 4a-quater. Runs over the applied personas: `runJsonlPersistenceSafeguard(personaConfig, notify, deps?)`, with `resolveJsonlRoots(config, home?)` and `checkJsonlPersistence(config, readMountinfo?, home?)` for Layer 1. `runPersonaStorageCheck(persona, notify, deps?)` runs Layer 1 alone for one persona's effective root, for a persona a confirmed apply brings up (see Session Lifecycle, [Bring-up at apply](#bring-up-at-apply-bav2-sr-61)); it never throws. Also exports the b.av2 SR-7.4 archive-evidence helpers (as amended by b.deo SRI-704): `personaArchiveEvidenceScope(persona, mode?)` (in declarative mode, the default, the persona's `delivery: all` channel IDs and whether a zero count is attributable; in fungible mode no channel and a zero never attributable, since a persona serves every channel its app is a member of and the configuration cannot predict its traffic; b.deo SRI-704), `UNATTRIBUTABLE_ZERO_REASON`, `FUNGIBLE_MODE_ZERO_REASON`, `unattributableZeroReason(mode)` (the reason an inconclusive verdict names, per mode), `makeDefaultArchiveCount(config)`, which returns an `ArchiveCountSince` `(channelIds, sinceEpochSeconds, ref)` counting over several channels at once, and `rfc3339ToEpochSeconds`. `session-manager.ts`'s b.wrb/b.fwu `diagnoseJsonlMissing` reuses the scope helper and the count to classify lost / never-created / inconclusive inside the resume path. Layer 2 and `diagnoseJsonlMissing` read the mode with `channelModeOf(config)`; in fungible mode the archive evidence is never `lost`: a count gives inconclusive with `FUNGIBLE_MODE_ZERO_REASON`, and an unavailable count keeps its outcome. Layer 2 imports `compareRowToPersona` from `session-manager.ts` (a function-scope use, so the import cycle is safe). Layer 2 skips a persona whose `claude_config_dir` cannot be resolved (`resolveRealPathStrict`, seam `configDirFs`) with one quiet line, before any agent-director call: no lost-history notice, record or label-mismatch verdict (bug b.g57).
    ├── postinstall.ts          npm/bun postinstall scaffold — `runPostinstall()` resolves the state dir with the server's `resolveServerStateDir()` (`SLACK_STATE_DIR` made absolute, a relative value resolving as the server resolves it and an empty value counting as unset, else `~/.claude/channels/slack`), creates it and the MCP config parent, then writes skeleton `config.json` (the empty persona config `{"personas": []}`, which loads with zero personas; b.av2 SR-1.7) and `slack-mcp.json` only when absent — an existing `config.json` is never touched, whatever its shape, so a pre-persona one gets the conversion error when the server starts (safe to re-run; migrates legacy `routing.json` → `config.json`). It creates no `access.json`, and one already in the state dir is ignored and left in place (b.av2 SR-10.1). Skills (b.669): it manages the links in `~/.claude/skills/` only for an installed copy of the package, so postinstall never makes a user-wide link into a checkout that is later deleted. The module-internal `skillLinkSkipReason` (not exported; tests reach it through `runPostinstall`'s `packageDir` and `env` options) gives the reason to leave them alone, the first rule that applies winning: a `.git` entry (directory, worktree file or link) at the package root, which marks a repo checkout or git worktree; a root with no path segment named exactly `node_modules`, so not an installed package (a global install lives under `<global dir>/node_modules/`); or `CI` set to anything but empty, `0` or `false` (trimmed, case-insensitive). The test is path-based because Bun sets no `npm_config_global` for `bun add -g`. With a reason, postinstall creates no `~/.claude/skills/`, links and removes nothing and logs one `skipped: <home>/.claude/skills (skill links left alone: <reason>)` line; the `config.json` and `slack-mcp.json` steps run either way. A local `bun install` in a checkout or worktree skips, and so does a `scripts/install-local.sh` install: Bun runs that `file:` package's postinstall at the worktree's real path. While that `file:` install is in place, the global package path resolves into the worktree, so an existing link into it (one an install of the published package made) reads the worktree's copy; the skip leaves that link as it is. For an installed copy, it symlinks the bundled `debug-slack-channel-bots` skill from `<package root>/skills/` into `~/.claude/skills/` (idempotent: a link already pointing at the package's copy is kept and logged `skipped: … (already linked)`; a link elsewhere, dangling included, is replaced; a real directory or regular file at that name is the operator's and is left in place, logged `skipped: … (not a link; left in place — remove it to let postinstall link the skill)`), and removes the link earlier releases created for the retired `claude-slack-channels-config` skill. It decides the link is its own by `lstat` and `readlink`: only a symbolic link whose target, resolved against the link's directory, is this package's `skills/claude-slack-channels-config` path (whether that path exists or not) is removed; a real directory, a regular file or a link to any other path at that name is left and logged `skipped: … (not created by postinstall; left in place)`. Link and removal failures log one `warning:` line through `describeThrownValue` and never fail the install. `PostinstallOptions.homeDir` overrides the home directory behind every default (the state dir when `SLACK_STATE_DIR` is unset, `~/.claude/slack-mcp.json`, `~/.claude/skills/`); `packageDir` overrides the package root (default this copy's, the directory above `src/`), which the skills link from and `skillLinkSkipReason` judges; `linkSkills` overrides the decision (`true` links, `false` skips with the reason `the linkSkills option is false`; unset, `skillLinkSkipReason` decides); `env` is the environment the `CI` check reads (default `process.env`). Tests run it against a temp home. `runAgentDirectorPostinstallProbe(deps?)` runs the install check once (`deps.runInstallCheck`, default `runInstallCheck` from `install-check.ts`, loaded when the probe runs so a missing or unloadable agent-director package is one warning): it builds no agent-director client, opens no agent-director store and resolves the host binary only through the install check (b.jg5 SRJ-121). A pass logs `postinstall: agent-director <version> OK`, plus one `postinstall: note: <note>` line when the check carries the Phase 1 note; a failure logs one `postinstall warning:` line with the class label and the check's CSCB-built message, pointing at `bun run install-check`; a check that cannot load or throws logs one warning with the thrown value through `describeThrownValue`. The probe adds no install, upgrade or `bun add` advice of its own; a failure warning carries only the install check's message (for `ad-system-install-not-found`, the pointer to the block "The publishing host" in the README's switch-over runbook section, `PUBLISHING_HOST_BLOCK_POINTER`). It never throws and never fails the install; the SR-5.1 startup gate is the real enforcement.
    └── message-archive.ts      Optional SQLite archive of every inbound Slack message. Written through `persona-routing.ts`'s archive seam once per receiving persona, before any delivery decision, in both channel modes (a fungible-mode `app_mention`, which ends right after, included); `INSERT OR IGNORE` keeps one row per (channel, ts), so a message received by two personas, or delivered twice to one (the `message` / `app_mention` pair, a redelivery), is stored once. The archive write comes before the per-persona dedupe. Names are resolved through the receiving persona's own client: `createPersonaNameResolverSource(clientFor)` looks the persona's client up on every call and keeps one name resolver per persona over that client, rebuilt (with fresh caches) when `clientFor` returns a different client, so names always resolve through the persona's current client, and `createPersonaArchiveWriter(db, source, onError)` is the fire-and-forget writer behind the archive seam. A persona with no client (dry run, not serving) still gets its row, with IDs in place of names and no Slack call. A channel name comes from `conversations.info`, which needs the `channels:read` (public) or `groups:read` (private) bot scope; a user name comes from `users.info` (`users:read`). A failed lookup, such as `missing_scope` from an app installed without those scopes, is not logged: the ID stands in for the name and is cached like a found name (channel names for 24 hours, user names for the resolver's life), so a running server keeps storing it until the entry expires or a new resolver is built. A write failure is logged as `[slack] message-archive write failed: <describeThrownValue>`.

See [Slack Reply Guard](#slack-reply-guard-stop-hook). Bootstrapped into settings.json by `src/stop-hook-bootstrap.ts`.

└── write-credentials.sh        b.av2 SR-12 (as amended by b.deo SRI-1101 to SRI-1110) / SR-1.4 (part) the credentials script `claude-slack-channel-bots credentials` runs, shipped in the package (package.json `files`): `write-credentials.sh <credentials file path>` under bash or zsh. Turns off tracing and automatic export (`set +xa`), checks the path (absolute or `~/…`, a file; exit 2 otherwise) and that `curl` is installed before any prompt, asks for `yes` before replacing an existing file, reads the bot token then the app token without echo (an empty answer re-asks on a terminal), checks each locally (not empty, `xoxb-` / `xapp-`, letters, digits and dashes only), then validates `bot_token` with `auth.test` and `app_token` with `apps.connections.open` through `curl -q … --config -` (the token only in a header line on curl's stdin, never in argv or the environment; a check passes only when Slack's reply starts `"ok":true`), and only when both pass writes `{bot_token, app_token}` through an exclusive `mktemp` file beside the target (mode 0600 from creation, removed by a trap on any failure or interrupt) and one rename, refusing when the target changed meanwhile. Never prints a token.
```

CSCB has no tmux module, no Claude session-id store and no permission hook script of its own: agent-director owns the tmux integration and the Claude session-id state, the SR-2.1 poller carries permission requests, and AskUserQuestion is denied at the template level (SR-3.1). The permission trail has no CLI query wrapper: the trail file itself is the surface; see [Trail file location and query recipes](#trail-file-location-and-query-recipes--sr-v-5--sr-v-6).

## Data Flow

### Inbound (Slack → Claude Code)

Inbound delivery lives in `src/persona-routing.ts`. Each persona has its own Socket Mode connection (`src/persona-connections.ts`), and each connection's events reach the event router (`src/persona-event-router.ts`) tagged with that persona's key; `server.ts` only wires the router to the routing instance. The steps below run in code order, once per receiving persona P.

1. Slack message arrives on P's own connection (`message` or `app_mention` event). The event router logs `[slack] RAW <event> event persona=<P's key>: <first 300 chars of the event JSON>` and calls `receive(event, ack, <P's key>, <envelope flag>)`: P is the only receiver. The envelope flag is the Events API envelope's `is_ext_shared_channel`, passed exactly as received (`true`, `false`, another value, or absent), read from the envelope only, never from the event (b.deo SRI-301); the RAW line is the same in both modes. Two personas in one channel each receive the event on their own connection, and each runs its own pipeline.
2. **Intake.** `receive` acks the event first; an ack failure is logged and handling continues. Then, for the receiving persona P (the intake also accepts a key list, each run concurrently), the archive is written and P's pipeline runs. The archive write is unconditional and comes before dedupe and any decision; it is keyed by (channel, ts), so a message received by several personas, or received twice by one, is stored once (see `src/message-archive.ts`). Each persona's run is isolated: a throw is logged as `[slack] persona-routing: error handling event for persona <ref>` with a `describeSlackCallFailure` tail and never stops another persona's run. The archive write is the same in both channel modes.

   **The mode, and the `app_mention` rule** (b.av2 SR-4.1 as amended by b.deo SRI-302; b.deo SRI-201). After the archive write, the channel mode is read once for the event (`channelModeOf` over the configuration in effect as the event arrives; no copy is kept across events). In fungible mode an `app_mention`, a group-DM one included, ends here: no dedupe record, decision, line, dispatch, reaction or report. The `message` event that carries the same mention decides, so one @mention is delivered once, from its `message` event, whichever of the two arrives first. In declarative mode an `app_mention` carries on to dedupe.
3. **Dedupe** (b.av2 SR-4.1 as amended by b.deo SRI-302). P's own dedupe store (`src/inbound-dedupe.ts`) records the event's key: (channel, ts), or (channel, ts, edited.ts) for an event that carries a top-level `edited.ts`. A key P first saw less than 10 minutes ago (`INBOUND_DEDUPE_RETENTION_MS`) is a duplicate and stops here: no decision, dispatch, reaction, recovery, post or log line. This collapses any Slack redelivery (for example after a reconnect) and, in declarative mode, the `message` / `app_mention` pair Slack sends for a channel @mention. In fungible mode the pair never meets here, since the `app_mention` ended at step 2, and an edit that adds a mention (an `app_mention` plus a `message_changed`, with no plain `message`) delivers nothing. A record made under the mode in force before a switch change stands. An edit keeps the message's ts, so `edited.ts` tells an edited event apart from the original: in declarative mode an edit that adds P's mention arrives as an `app_mention` with the original ts and an `edited` object, gets its own key and reaches P once, with `via` `mention`, while a redelivery of that same edited event is a duplicate. A `message_changed` event is keyed like any other event but is then dropped by the decision (step 4.1, not a deliverable subtype), so an edit that adds `<!here>` / `<!channel>` wakes nobody. The window runs from the first sighting; a duplicate does not extend it. Expired keys are pruned lazily on each new record, with no timer. An event missing its channel or ts is not keyed and carries on as new. The routing instance keeps one store per persona key, created on first use, so it survives a reopen of P's connection; the stores are in memory only and are empty after a server restart.
4. **Decision** (`decideDelivery` in `src/delivery-decision.ts`, pure; see its Module Map entry). A key that is no applied persona first logs `[slack] persona-routing: no applied persona with key=<key> — event not delivered to it`. In declarative mode the decision gets P (its key, bot identity, channel entries and `dm.enabled`) and the applied personas, and nothing of the fungible section is read. In fungible mode it also gets `FungibleDecisionInputs`, built at the event (b.deo SRI-309): the mode, the envelope flag, `CHANNEL_ID_RE`, the stored choices through `getChannelDelivery()` (readability and lookup only: the routing never writes to the store or drops from it), and `fungibleDestinationsOf(config, config.personas)`, each applied persona's destination by the one destination rule. The decision runs against P in b.av2 SR-4.2 order (as amended by b.deo SRI-303 to SRI-309); steps 1 to 3 are the same in both modes:
   1. A subtype other than `file_share`, `bot_message`, `thread_broadcast` or `me_message`, or no channel, is dropped. An event with neither `user` nor `bot_id` is dropped as `no-author`.
   2. P's own messages (author `user` = P's bot user ID, or the event's `bot_id` = P's bot ID) are dropped. This self-exclusion is the only author filter: posts by people, bots, integrations, webhooks and other personas are delivered by the rules below, and nothing counts, throttles or arbitrates exchanges between personas.
   3. Conversation kind (b.av2 SR-4.3). A DM is an event with `channel_type` `im`; as a defensive fallback, an event without `channel_type` whose conversation ID starts with `D` is treated as a DM too (Slack does not send `app_mention` for 1:1 DMs, so a DM arrives as a `message` event with `channel_type` `im`). A DM that passed steps 1 and 2 depends only on P's `dm.enabled`: on, it is delivered with `via` `dm`, whatever the text mentions; off, it is dropped as `dm-disabled` and logs one `persona-dm-dropped` line naming P, the conversation, the ts and `dm.enabled`, with no Slack call. A DM is decided only against the persona whose connection received it, and nothing in this path is channel-specific, so a persona with zero channels and DMs on receives its DMs the same way. A group DM is recognised only by `channel_type` `mpim`. The app does not subscribe to `message.mpim` (the manifest has `message.im` but no `message.mpim`), so such events are rare; one that arrives is dropped as `group-dm` with the plain drop line, whatever `dm.enabled` says, and never logs `persona-dm-dropped`. Neither a DM nor an `mpim` event reaches the channel rules below, so neither logs `unclaimed-channel`; a group DM is never delivered, in either mode, and a DM is decided by `dm.enabled` alone in both. In declarative mode an `app_mention` in a group DM carries no `channel_type` and a `G…` or `C…` conversation ID, so it is decided by the channel rules below: it is not delivered unless a persona lists that ID, and it normally logs `unclaimed-channel`. In fungible mode such an `app_mention` ended at step 2 and is never decided.

   **Declarative mode**, steps 4 to 6 (the 0.11.1 rules):

   4. A channel P is not configured into is not delivered. When no applied persona lists the channel, one `unclaimed-channel` line names the channel and P; when another applied persona lists it, nothing is logged.
   5. A `delivery: all` channel delivers.
   6. A `delivery: mentions` channel delivers when the text contains P's user mention (`<@P>` or `<@P|label>`) or `<!here>` / `<!channel>` (with or without a label); `<!everyone>` and user-group mentions do not count.

   **Fungible mode**, steps 4 to 6 (`decideFungibleChannel`). No persona's `channels` is read, and whether any persona lists the channel plays no part.

   4. The fungible path's five conditions (`FUNGIBLE_REFUSALS`), checked in this order; the first one the event fails drops it with reason `fungible-refused` and that refusal, and a `message` event logs one `unclaimed-channel` line with the refusal's reason (`FUNGIBLE_REFUSAL_TEXTS`):
      1. `channel_type` is `channel` (public) or `group` (private); else `not-a-channel`, "the conversation is not a public or private channel".
      2. The channel ID matches `CHANNEL_ID_RE` (`C…` or `G…`); else `channel-id-malformed`, "the channel ID is malformed".
      3. The envelope flag `is_ext_shared_channel` is present; else `flag-missing`, "the event envelope carries no is_ext_shared_channel flag".
      4. The flag is a boolean; else `flag-not-boolean`, "the event envelope's is_ext_shared_channel flag is not a boolean".
      5. The flag is `false`; else `externally-shared`, "the channel is externally shared".
   5. P's channel delivery for the channel, from `channelDeliveryFor(P's key, channel, inputs)`: `mentions` when the channel is another applied persona's fungible destination (the loop guard, b.deo SRI-305: that persona's permission prompts and notices go there, so P never hears every message in it; a `dm` destination holds nothing, and P's own destination is never held); otherwise P's stored choice for the channel when the store is readable; otherwise `mentions`. An unreadable store (`readable` false, or no store loaded yet) applies no stored choice, so every channel is at `mentions`.
   6. P's user mention delivers with `via` `mention`, then `<!here>` / `<!channel>` with `via` `broadcast` (the same recognisers as declarative mode); otherwise a channel delivery of `all` delivers, and `mentions` drops the event as `not-mentioned`.

   Every outcome of an event that passed the five conditions carries the channel type (`public` or `private`) and P's channel delivery (`fungible`).

   **The audit line and the heard set** (b.deo SRI-307, SRI-902, SRI-304). The first event in P's persona life that took P's fungible path for a channel, delivered or not, adds the channel to P's heard set and logs one `persona-invited-channel` line, before any drop line or dispatch, so a `not-mentioned` drop and a lost message log it too; later events from that channel in the same life log none. Heard sets are kept per persona key, in memory only, beside the dedupe stores; every routing instance starts with empty heard sets, a switch change keeps them, and the persona teardown's `forget(key)` drops P's heard set (with its dedupe store) and no other key's. `set_channel_delivery` reads it through `heardChannels(key)`. Channel membership is never stored: nothing about it is written anywhere, and no Slack call is added to learn it.

   A delivered message carries `via`, how it reached P; the first match wins: `dm`, `mention`, `broadcast`, `receive_all_shared`, `receive_all`. In declarative mode `receive_all_shared` is a `delivery: all` channel that at least one other applied persona also receives with `delivery: all`; in fungible mode it is a channel where P's channel delivery is `all` and at least one other applied persona's channel delivery (`channelDeliveryFor`, its stored choice and the loop guard) is `all` too (b.av2 SR-4.4 as amended by b.deo SRI-306), whether or not that persona's app is a member of the channel at that time. Only a DM produces `dm`, and a DM never produces any other value.

   The classed lines are built by `formatPersonaDiagnostic`, e.g. `[slack] unclaimed-channel: personas[<i>] "<name>" (key=<key>): message in channel <C…> not delivered: no applied persona lists this channel` (declarative mode, `unclaimedChannelCause`), `[slack] unclaimed-channel: personas[<i>] "<name>" (key=<key>): message in channel <channel> not delivered in fungible mode: <reason>; to serve this channel, use declarative mode with the channel listed` (fungible mode, `fungibleUnclaimedChannelCause`), `[slack] persona-invited-channel: personas[<i>] "<name>" (key=<key>): hears <public|private> channel <C…|G…> in fungible mode, at channel delivery <mentions|all>` (`invitedChannelCause`) and `[slack] persona-dm-dropped: personas[<i>] "<name>" (key=<key>): direct message in conversation <D…> ts=<ts> dropped: dm.enabled is off for this persona` (the `ts=` part is left out when the event has no ts). The other drop reasons log `[slack] persona "<name>" (key=<key>) dropped message from channel=<C…> user=<U…>: <reason>`, with `bot_id=<B…>` in place of `user=` for an author without `user`. No drop line carries message text.

   For when a confirmed change takes effect here, see Session Lifecycle, [In-place update](#in-place-update-bav2-sr-86-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-802). A confirmed switch change applies from the next event (the mode is read per event), and a stored choice from the next event after the `set_channel_delivery` call that stored it.
5. **Author label and session lookup.** The author's name is resolved first, for the meta of a delivered message and for the notice of a lost one: through P's client, or for an author without `user` (a webhook or `bot_message`) from the event itself (`username`, else `bot_profile.name`, else its bot ID) with no Slack call. A failed user-name lookup falls back to the user ID and logs one line (`[slack] persona-routing: user-name lookup for persona <ref> failed, using the user ID: …`); the message is not lost. Then P's session is read with `getSessionByPersona(P's key)`, after that await, so a session replaced or dropped during the lookup is seen. With no registered, connected session the message is dropped (`[slack] No live session for persona <ref> chat_id=<C…> — dropping message`) and the b.kvq no-session branch runs (step 7).
6. **Stream check.** The dispatch line `[slack] Dispatching to persona <ref> chat_id=<C…> cwd="…" mcpSessionId=… hasGetStream=… connected=… text="<first 80 chars>"` is logged. If the session has lost its `_GET_stream` (`hasGetStreamKey` on the session's transport false), `notification()` would vanish silently, so it is not sent: `[slack] DROP: no _GET_stream for persona <ref> chat_id=<C…> …` is logged and the b.9cj streamless branch runs (step 7). Nothing is awaited from the session read to the send in step 8, so the probe and the send act on the same session (b.9cj).
7. **Lost message** (b.av2 SR-4.6, SR-7.3; b.jg5 SRJ-1011, SRJ-1501, SRJ-1509; b.kvq / b.9cj). Both branches are handled by `handleLostMessage` in `persona-routing.ts`. The message is not delivered, gets no ack reaction and no ack-tracker entry, and is never saved or replayed. `decideLostMessageState` (`lost-message.ts`) reports one of ten states, keyed by P, first match wins: P not up (the routing's injected `isPersonaUp` answers false: P is `retrying` or `broken`, or unknown to the controller) → `not-up`, and no restart is started, since P's own recovery launches it once it is up (a persona that is not up forwards no Slack event, so `not-up` is reached only when P stops being up between receiving the message and the session lookup, as with a Web API call refused for its bot token, or by a message the old half of a destructive modify receives after its bring-up state is cancelled and before its connection is stopped); P latched (the one conflict latch's `isLatched`, see [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502); an unusable recorded name and a launch start not recorded are such latches, which the one row read below can set itself, b.jg5 SRJ-512, SRJ-513) → `held-for-human`; P held on `ErrInvalidFlags` → `cannot-launch`; P's kill-failure episode open (the ordinary version of the kill-failure alert was raised at P's destination and P's row has not since read `ended` or `missing`, or been found gone or deleted by the collision ladder; see [The kill-failure alert](#the-kill-failure-alert-bjg5-srj-704-srj-1007)), or P waiting on an old-life hold whose old key's kill failed (b.jg5 SRJ-812) → `kill-failed`; P's `tmux-unresponsive` condition holding, or its `tmux-unavailable` or `ad-config-malformed` outage flag raised, with P below the restart cap and P's retry timer armed (`isRetryArmed`) → `not-answering` (an open unclassified-error episode alone is not this state; b.jg5 SRJ-1011 as amended: state 5 applies only while P's retry timer is armed, and its notice says CSCB is retrying, so a P at the cap reports the next state that applies, usually `restart-limit-reached`, whatever condition or flag is raised, and so does a P below the cap with no timer armed, which can reach `starting-now`; with `tmux-unavailable` raised below the cap, P's missing retry timer is armed before the decision, below); a live-row sequence or an old-life wait step running for P (`isSequenceOrWaitRunning`, production the session manager's `isSequenceOrOldLifeWaitRunning`: P's live-row sequence, `isLiveRowSequenceRunning`, b.jg5 SRJ-706, from the start's answer until the sequence settles, its step-6 launch included, or an old-life wait running on the instance id of a hold P waits on, `isOldLifeWaitRunningFor`, b.jg5 SRJ-811, SRJ-812, [The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809); either even while P's row reads `pending`) → `restarting`, asked here so it wins over the next state; a launch call for P in flight or P's dialog approver running (`isLaunchOrApproverRunning`, production `isLaunchInFlight(key) || isDialogApproverRunning(key)`; P's row reads `pending`), or the one row read below answering `pending` → `session-starting`, so a message lost while only the approver runs reports `session-starting` with no read and no human-triggered restart; a restart already pending or active → `restarting`; auto-restart disabled (`session_restart_delay: 0`) → `auto-restart-disabled`; P at the failure cap → `restart-limit-reached`; otherwise `starting-now`. The `kill-failed` input (`isKillFailed`) has two halves, both read at call time: P's open kill-failure episode (the kill-failure alerts' `isOpen`, through the holder `main()` sets), or P waiting on an old-life hold marked kill-failed (the session manager's `waitsOnKillFailedHold`, b.jg5 SRJ-812: the hold set's `waitsOnKillFailed` over the applied persona; [The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809), **The kill-failed mark**). A hold is marked once a persona teardown, start-sweep or old-life wait kill of the old row decided the ordinary version of the kill-failure alert with no stop ending its tries, or the wait's step 5 found the row still live; the mark lasts until the hold ends. A message lost while either holds reports `kill-failed` and starts no restart; one lost while P waits on a hold before any kill of its old key failed does not: with no wait step running and no earlier state applying it can reach `starting-now`, and the restart it fires answers `sequence-waiting` at the restart path's old-life gate (b.jg5 SRJ-810, SRJ-812; [Auto-Restart](#auto-restart), **The old-life gate**), so P comes up only once the hold ends. The alert's survivor version opens no episode and marks no hold, so a message lost after it never reports `kill-failed`, and neither does one lost after the episode or the hold ended. A CONFLICT latch that came with the alert (the kill's own CONFLICT after a survivor-naming failure) reports `held-for-human` first. The `cannot-launch` input is bound: `main()` passes `isHeldOnInvalidFlags`, read at call time from the server's `ErrInvalidFlags` hold (`isHeld`), so a message lost while P is held reports `cannot-launch` and fires no human-triggered restart ([The `ErrInvalidFlags` hold](#the-errinvalidflags-hold-bjg5-srj-207-srj-1008)). A message lost while a live-row sequence or an old-life wait step runs for P reports `restarting` with no row read (below) and fires no human-triggered restart. In the five states from `held-for-human` to `session-starting` no human-triggered restart fires (b.av2 SR-4.6 as amended by b.jg5 SRJ-1501; in `session-starting` it would be a launch over the `pending` row); only in `starting-now` (`firesHumanTriggeredRestart`) `scheduleRestart(key, cwd, undefined, { humanTrigger: true })` is called, with nothing awaited between the final decision and the call, so messages lost together schedule at most one restart (the restart it starts is Auto-Restart's, whose refused kill or launch counts nothing and posts no spawn-failure notice; for a retired key its reconnect starts the live-row sequence for an old life and its launch is a reuse spawn, never a `resume`, [Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-bjg5-srj-806-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-407)) (P's `working_directory` in the no-session branch, the session's `cwd` in the streamless branch). Before the decision (b.jg5 SRJ-311; `armStoppedRetryBeforeDecision`, asked before the read gate's check and again after the row read when one was awaited, since a retry may have stopped during it), when none of states 1 to 4 applies, state 5's condition holds, P's `tmux-unavailable` flag is raised and P is below the restart cap, the routing asks `armRetryTimerIfMissing(key)`, so the gated decision sees the timer and reports `not-answering`: production arms P's retry timer with the `environment` cause (`armEnvironmentRetryTimer`, the health tick's arm path) only when none is armed, P is not latched and nothing is in flight for it, logging `[slack] Lost message: persona=<key> has its tmux-unavailable outage raised with no retry timer — no restart scheduled; arming one (b.jg5 SRJ-311)`, and does nothing while the server is shutting down. A retry that stopped as not up, on a declined launch or on a failed run leaves the flag raised with no timer, so this lets a lost message start the retries again even with `health_check_interval` 0. The arm is the outage's own retry, never a restart; `ad-config-malformed` or the `tmux-unresponsive` condition alone arms nothing here, and at the cap nothing is armed (a timer armed there would stop at its first retry). When the check arms nothing (P latched, work in flight for P (a launch call, a running live-row sequence, an old-life wait step for a hold P waits on or a running dialog approver), no controller, shutting down), state 5 does not apply and the decision reports the next state: `held-for-human` in the first case, and `restarting` or `session-starting` in the second. Either branch then raises exactly one lost-message notice (`buildLostMessageNotice`) through the injected `notify`, the per-persona notifier's `notify`: it goes to P's destination in the mode in force when the notice is attempted (`permission_prompts` in declarative mode, `invited.permission_prompts` in fungible mode; the notifier resolves it, b.deo SRI-1002), names the sender and the recovery state, and carries no message text. It takes the notifier's path like every persona notice (see the `persona-notifier.ts` entry and Permission Relay, [Destination hold](#destination-hold-bav2-sr-71-failures-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-702-sri-703)). Nothing else is posted in the source conversation; when the destination is that conversation, the notice is the one post there. The notice is awaited; a failing `notify` logs one `persona-routing: lost-message notice … failed` line and is never thrown.

   **The one row read (b.jg5 SRJ-1011, SRJ-1501).** `handleLostMessage` reads P's row once (`readRowLiveness`, the liveness adapter of [Auto-Restart](#auto-restart) step 3, that is one `status` call) only when all of these hold, each asked at that time: the read is injected; none of states 1 to 5 applies (`decideEarlyLostMessageState`, the helper `decideLostMessageState` asks first); no launch call for P is in flight and no dialog approver for P runs (`isLaunchOrApproverRunning`); no live-row sequence or old-life wait step runs for P (`isSequenceOrWaitRunning`); and nothing is in flight for P (`isWorkInFlight`, the server's "in flight for P" binding `isPersonaWorkInFlight`: a launch call, a running live-row sequence, an old-life wait step for a hold P waits on or a running dialog approver). Otherwise no read is made. There is never more than one read per lost message: it is not retried, and no timer is armed by the routing for it.

   - **Its answers.** A `pending` reading is the `session-starting` input. A configured persona's own row that reads `pending` with no launch start never gives that reading: the adapter's own-row `status` step latches P with `launch-start-not-recorded` and the read answers `unknown` (b.jg5 SRJ-513), so the decision made after it reports `held-for-human` and no restart fires (see [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)). The same step clears a retired key's entry when the row reads live other than `pending` with the key's mark set, leaving the reading unchanged (b.jg5 SRJ-807; see [The shared own-row `status` read](#the-shared-own-row-status-read-bjg5-srj-115)). Any other reading (`live`, `dead`, `unknown`, or a value that is not a reading) leaves `session-starting` out, and so does a rejected read, which is caught, logged once as `[slack] persona-routing: lost-message row read for persona <ref> failed — session-starting left out: <describeAgentDirectorFailure>` (redacted) and never thrown. So a failed read never reports `session-starting`. Before `main()` has built the adapter the read answers `unknown` with no `status` call.
   - **Outside any attempt.** The read is made from the Slack event path, outside any launch or recovery attempt, and is not the human-triggered restart. What its answer raises or arms is the adapter's, as at the health tick's read (see [Auto-Restart](#auto-restart) step 3): a success clears `ad-unreachable` and `ad-config-malformed`; `ErrSpawnNotFound` reads `dead`; `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` raises `ad-unreachable`, reads `dead` (not `pending`) and arms nothing; `ErrTmuxNotAvailable` (ENVIRONMENT) raises `tmux-unavailable`, arms the retry timer and reads `unknown`; `ErrConfigMalformed` (CONFIG) raises `ad-config-malformed`, arms the retry timer and reads `unknown`; an UNAVAILABLE, UNCLASSIFIED or any other error reads `unknown`, arms no retry timer and opens no unclassified-error episode. `status` is not tmux-touching, so no answer starts `tmux-unresponsive`.
   - **Decided again after the read.** `decideLostMessageState` runs once, after the read, asking every query afresh, so a latch or an outage that began during the read, one the read itself raised included (an ENVIRONMENT or CONFIG answer), reports `held-for-human` or `not-answering` (the latter only while P's retry timer is armed and P is below the restart cap).
   - **A failed read and the restart.** When a failed read lets the state reach `starting-now`, the human-triggered restart still makes its own liveness read, and a `pending` row there is deferred, never launched over (see **`pending` rows** under [Auto-Restart](#auto-restart) step 3).

   **Invariant: lost-message reports go only to the persona's destination.** A server message in the conversation a message came from would give away, in a shared channel, a persona passing as a person. So no delivery failure is ever reported in the source conversation because the message came from there, for a channel or a DM source alike; when the source conversation is also the destination, the destination's one notice is the only post there. Future delivery or queueing work (b.4vj, guaranteed inbound delivery) is bound by the same rule and must report to the destination.
8. **Delivery.** P's session's MCP Server sends `notifications/claude/channel` (awaited) to its Claude Code client, with P's own mention token (`<@P>` or `<@P|label>`) stripped from the text; other mentions and broadcasts stay. Only P's session receives it. The meta, rendered by the harness as attributes of the `<channel>` tag, is `chat_id` (the source conversation), `message_id`, `user` (the author label from step 5), the author's `user_id` (or, for an author without `user`, its `bot_id`; never both), `ts`, `via` from step 4, `thread_ts` when present, and `attachment_count` / `attachments` when the message has files.
9. **Ack reaction** (b.av2 SR-4.5). Only after the send in step 8 has succeeded does P react, so only a dispatched message gets a reaction: a drop, a dedupe duplicate, a lost message (step 7) or a send that throws gets no reaction and no ack-tracker entry. If the server-wide `ack_reaction` is set (`deps.getReplySettings()`, the start-time value), `trackAck(P's key, channelId, messageTs)` records P's entry first, so P's first reply always finds it, and then the reaction is added through P's own client without being awaited (a failure is ignored; the entry stays and the message is still delivered). With `ack_reaction` absent, or no client for P (dry run, or P not serving), both are skipped. When one message is dispatched to several personas (each on its own connection), each runs this step for itself, so the message carries one reaction per dispatching persona, each under that persona's own identity, and each persona holds its own entry.

**The same in both modes** (b.deo SRI-1002). The archive write before any decision, dedupe's keys and retention, the decision's steps 1 to 3 (DMs by `dm.enabled`, group DMs never delivered), the lost-message states and their one notice (at the destination of the mode in force), delivery and the ack reaction are the same in both channel modes. Channel membership is never stored: fungible mode learns a channel only from the events that reach P, and keeps only the in-memory heard set.

Injected messages (`/interject` and cron, which posts through `/interject`) reach the persona's instance but do not come through this pipeline: they are not Slack messages, so they get no ack reaction. Their meta is unchanged, `user` and `ts` only, with no `via`; see [POST /interject](#post-interject).

### Outbound (Claude Code → Slack)

1. Claude Code calls MCP tools. Every session lists the same six tools in both channel modes: the five Slack tools (`reply`, `react`, `edit_message`, `fetch_messages`, `download_attachment`) and `set_channel_delivery`, whose path is below ([The `set_channel_delivery` path](#the-set_channel_delivery-path-bdeo-sri-501-to-sri-507)).
2. The tool handler resolves the calling persona at call time from the session's registered persona key (`SessionToolDeps.getPersona`). A session not yet matched to a persona gets `sessionNotMatchedRefusal` (`Tool "<tool>" refused: this session is not matched to a persona.`), and a key that is no applied persona gets `personaNotAppliedRefusal` (`Tool "<tool>" refused: persona key=<key> is not an applied persona.`), the two refusals all six tools share. The channel mode is read in the same step (`SessionToolDeps.getChannelMode`, `channelModeOf` over the configuration in effect; b.deo SRI-601), so the persona and the mode are both as applied at the call.
3. `checkPersonaTarget(persona, target, action, mode)` checks a Slack tool's target (`chat_id`, or `channel` for `fetch_messages`) against the persona and the mode as applied at the call, before the dry-run branch (b.av2 SR-5.1 as amended by b.deo SRI-601). `set_channel_delivery` has no Slack target and never reaches this step. There are three target kinds:
   - **Channel** — in declarative mode, the `id` of one of the persona's configured channels, whatever its `delivery` mode; in fungible mode, any value matching `CHANNEL_ID_RE` (`C…` or `G…`), whatever any persona lists: the persona's `channels` is not read, and Slack decides membership, refusing a channel the persona's app is not a member of (step 4). Each of the five Slack tools accepts it.
   - **DM conversation** (`D…`) — the same in both modes: allowed only while the persona's `dm.enabled` is on. Each of the five Slack tools accepts it. The ID is passed to Slack as is; Slack refuses a conversation the persona's app is not in, and that comes back as a tool failure (step 4).
   - **User ID** (`U…`/`W…`) — the same in both modes: allowed only for `reply` (its text and file uploads) and only while `dm.enabled` is on. `reply` calls `conversations.open` on the persona's own client, then posts the chunks, uploads the files and removes the ack reaction in the returned `D…` conversation, as the persona. The user ID itself never reaches a Slack write. The open runs on every such call; nothing is cached. The result names the opened conversation, so the session can use that `D…` ID for later edits, reactions, reads and thread replies. `conversations.open` needs the `im:write` bot scope. A failed open, or one that returns no conversation ID, is a tool error naming the persona and the user, and nothing is posted; when the failure is `missing_scope`, the error also names `im:write` and says to add it and re-install the app. `react`, `edit_message`, `fetch_messages` and `download_attachment` refuse a user ID whatever the switch, so no read, edit or reaction opens a DM.

   For when a confirmed change takes effect here, see Session Lifecycle, [In-place update](#in-place-update-bav2-sr-86-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-802).

   With `dm.enabled` off the persona has no DM target: every `D…`, `U…` or `W…` target on every tool is refused with the reason `DMs are off for this persona (dm.enabled is false).`, so no `conversations.open` is made and nothing is posted to, read from or reacted on in a DM. The "needs a conversation ID, not a user ID" reason applies only while DMs are on, to a user ID given to an act tool. Any other target is refused: in declarative mode (an unconfigured channel, a group DM, an empty value) as not a configured channel; in fungible mode (a value that is neither a channel ID nor an allowed DM target) with `FUNGIBLE_TARGET_REFUSAL`, `Persona <ref> may not target "<target>": it is neither a channel ID nor an allowed DM target.` Every refusal is a tool error naming the persona and the target, with no Slack call, dry run included.

   Nothing on this path assumes a configured channel, so a zero-channel persona with DMs on answers its DMs in place through the same check. The dry run of a `reply` to a user ID reports that it would open a DM and makes no `conversations.open` call. `reply` also runs `assertSendable()` on every file before any Slack call (so a refused file stops a user-ID reply before the open), and again on each file right before its upload so a file swapped in between is still caught; a refused file is a tool error.
4. The tool resolves the persona's own Web client at call time (`SessionToolDeps.clientFor`: the connection manager's long-lived client for that persona while it is serving; see `persona-start.ts`) and makes the Slack call with it, `reply` uploads (`filesUploadV2`) included, with no username or icon override. `download_attachment` authorises file fetches with that client's bot token, sent only to `https://files.slack.com` URLs. It refuses external (non-Slack-hosted) files and never follows a redirect off that origin with the header. A Slack call failure is logged token-safely and returned as a tool error naming the persona and, for a DM or user-ID target, that target. In fungible mode a failed call on a channel target is the tool error `slackRefusalToolErrorText(tool, persona, channel, code)` (b.deo SRI-602): `Tool "<tool>" failed for persona "<name>" (key=<key>) on channel "<channel>": Slack refused the call (<code>).`, the code being Slack's platform error (`slackPlatformReason`, such as `not_in_channel` or `channel_not_found`), or `…: the tool call failed.` when there is none; declarative-mode and DM-target failures keep their text. A failure after a user ID's DM was opened (a post or upload) also names the opened conversation: `Tool "reply" failed for persona <ref> on DM target "U…" (conversation D…): the tool call failed (<code>).`, with the same `(conversation D…)` part in the log line. A missing client or token is also a tool error.
5. `reply` splits its text with `chunkText(text, reply_chunk_limit, reply_chunk_mode)` (`lib.ts`), reading the server-wide settings through `SessionToolDeps.getReplySettings()` (start-time values; defaults 4000 and `newline`). After the first chunk posts (once per call, not per chunk), if `message_id` was provided, `SessionToolDeps.consumeAck(persona key, conversation, message_id)` finds the calling persona's own tracked entry and `ack_reaction` is set, that persona's reaction is removed via `reactions.remove` through its own client (a failure is ignored). The conversation is the one posted to (for a user-ID target, the opened `D…` conversation). Another persona's entry and reaction on the same message are left alone until that persona replies with the `message_id`; a persona that never reacted finds no entry and removes nothing.

#### The `set_channel_delivery` path (b.deo SRI-501 to SRI-507)

`set_channel_delivery(channel, delivery)` lets a persona's agent store its own channel delivery (`mentions` or `all`) for one channel in fungible mode. Its handler is `setChannelDelivery` in `createSessionServer` (`src/registry.ts`). It has no Slack target: it never calls `checkPersonaTarget`, reads no client, makes no Slack call and has no dry-run branch. It runs as one synchronous stretch, with no await between reading the session's persona key and the store's write, so no confirmed apply's step 1 comes between (b.deo SRI-502).

1. **Listed in every session**, in both modes, with the descriptions `SET_CHANNEL_DELIVERY_DESCRIPTION`, `SET_CHANNEL_DELIVERY_CHANNEL_DESCRIPTION` and `SET_CHANNEL_DELIVERY_DELIVERY_DESCRIPTION` (b.deo SRI-501).
2. **Resolution at call time** (b.av2 SR-5.1 as amended by b.deo SRI-502), each giving the other tools' refusal texts: no persona key on the session (`sessionNotMatchedRefusal`); a key that is not an applied persona's (`personaNotAppliedRefusal`); a key the stored-choice store marks retiring (`isRetiring`: a destructive modify's key from a confirmed apply's step 1 until its step 2 has settled), `personaNotAppliedRefusal`; and a session entry that is not the one the registry holds for its key (`getSessionByPersona(key) !== entry`: dropped, or replaced by a newer registration), `personaNotAppliedRefusal`.
3. **The refusals, in order** (`SET_CHANNEL_DELIVERY_REFUSALS`, b.deo SRI-503); the first rule broken gives the tool error, and a refusal stores, writes and logs nothing:
   1. `declarative-mode`: the mode read at the call (`getChannelMode`) is declarative, so in declarative mode every call is refused: `Tool "set_channel_delivery" refused for persona "<name>" (key=<key>): invited channels are off, and in declarative mode channel delivery is set by the operator in config.json.` (`channelDeliveryDeclarativeRefusal`).
   2. `store-unreadable`: no store is bound, or it is unreadable for the run: `…: the stored-choice file "<path>" is not readable, so no channel delivery can be stored. To fix: the operator moves the file aside, then restarts the server.` (`channelDeliveryUnreadableRefusal`; `<path>` is `CHANNEL_DELIVERY_FILE_NAME` when no store is bound).
   3. `delivery-invalid`: `delivery` is not `"mentions"` or `"all"`, a missing value included: `…: delivery "<value>" is not "mentions" or "all".` (`channelDeliveryValueRefusal`). The value is echoed only when it matches `ECHOABLE_KEY_NAME_RE`; otherwise the text reads `…: delivery is not "mentions" or "all" (the value given is not shown).`
