An instance the ladder leaves alone (`pending`, `check_permission`, `ask_user`, or a `working` wait that gave up with the session alive) is picked up by the health check's alive-but-not-connected path, which reconnects it through restart; an `ask_user` or `check_permission` row is never typed into, only once it moves on (Auto-Restart step 3). With `session_restart_delay` 0 nothing reconnects it, and the not-connected notice reports it (Health-Check Poller).
   - **Every server start.** Admission reads the same predicate at start, so an instance that survived the previous server process is refused until its persona's bring-up finishes, healthy personas included: `its bring-up has not run` before the controller has started that persona, `its Slack connection is not serving` while its bring-up is in progress. Once the persona is `up`, the instance registers through the same two routes: the start pass's launch reaches its row through the ladder, which reconnects a `waiting` or `working` row (a `working` one in the background, b.f2b: the pass parks that launch), and a `pending` row is reconnected by the health check, a `check_permission` or `ask_user` row only once its prompt is answered.
4. Session receives the messages its persona's pipeline (`persona-routing.ts`) delivers, by the channel mode in force: in declarative mode from the persona's configured channels, in fungible mode from every public or private channel its app is a member of that is not externally shared; in both modes, with `dm.enabled` on, its DMs. There is one session per persona however many channels it serves. `set_channel_delivery` resolves through the session entry itself, so a call through a session the registry does not hold for its key (a newer session replaced it, or a teardown dropped it) is refused with `personaNotAppliedRefusal`; the other tools resolve by key only
5. A keep-alive timer is started (`startSseKeepAlive`) that writes SSE comment frames (`:ping\n\n`) every ~30 s to prevent idle connection drops from proxies or load balancers

### Agent-director error classes (b.jg5 SRJ-104)

`src/ad-error-class.ts` is the one place an agent-director error gets its class. `classifyAdError(value)` maps any value thrown by an agent-director call to exactly one class and answers an `AdErrorClassification` (`errorClass`, and for some classes `reportedName` and `message`). It is pure (no I/O, clock, module state or agent-director call) and never throws: a throwing property read counts as an absent field, and an unexpected internal throw answers UNAVAILABLE.

| Class | Errors |
|---|---|
| `GONE` | `ErrTmuxSendKeys`, `ErrTmuxCaptureFailed` |
| `UNAVAILABLE` | `ErrTmuxUnresponsive`, `ErrTmuxKillFailed`, `ErrCallTimeout`; an `ErrUnknownErrorName` whose `unknownName` is none of `ErrInternal`, `ErrConfigMalformed`, `ErrSchemaMismatch`, `ErrSchemaMigrationRequired` and `ErrStoreOpen`; CSCB's own `UnknownError` wrapper; any value that is not an `AgentDirectorError` |
| `CONFLICT` | `ErrTmuxSessionConflict` |
| `UNUSABLE_NAME` | an `ErrInternal` whose description carries "the recorded tmux session name" (`UNUSABLE_RECORDED_NAME_PHRASE`, `ad-description-phrases.ts`) |
| `CONFIG` | `ErrConfigMalformed` |
| `ENVIRONMENT` | `ErrTmuxNotAvailable` |
| `LAUNCH_FAILURE` | `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` |
| `STATE` | `ErrSpawnNotFound`, `ErrInstanceIdCollision`, `ErrSpawnNotResumable`, `ErrSpawnNotInteractive`, `ErrSpawnNotPausable`, `ErrNoSessionId`, `ErrJsonlMissing`, `ErrJsonlNeverWritten`, `ErrInvalidFlags` |
| `DIRECTORY` | `ErrCwdNotFound`, `ErrCwdNotADirectory` |
| `UNCLASSIFIED` | every other `ErrInternal`; `ErrSchemaMismatch`, `ErrSchemaMigrationRequired` and `ErrStoreOpen` (a store agent-director cannot open); `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`; `ErrSendKeysWhileRelayed` (keys refused while the row sits on a relayed permission prompt, which CSCB gives no handling); and every other agent-director error, a base `AgentDirectorError` whose `errName` merely equals one of the class names above included |

The labels are the `AD_ERROR_CLASS_*` constants, listed in table order in `AD_ERROR_CLASSES` (type `AdErrorClass`).

- **Recognition by class.** Every error the client declares as a class is recognised by `instanceof` that class (through `isAdErrorInstance`), never by its `errName` or `name`; the classes come from `agent-director-errors.ts`, the three Phase-1-only ones through its bindings. A base `AgentDirectorError` whose `errName` merely equals a class's name is not that class: it is UNCLASSIFIED. CSCB's own `UnknownError` wrapper is recognised by its `errName` (`CSCB_UNKNOWN_ERROR_NAME`). `classifyAdError` decides in this order: a value that is not an `AgentDirectorError` is UNAVAILABLE; an `ErrUnknownErrorName` instance is decided by its `unknownName` and its envelope's `err_description` (below); an instance of a class the table names takes that class's answer, whatever its `errName`; only then is a value decided by an `errName` of `ErrInternal`, `ErrConfigMalformed` or a store-open name (A-13, below), then by CSCB's `UnknownError` (UNAVAILABLE); any other agent-director error is UNCLASSIFIED. So an `ErrSpawnNotFound` whose `errName` is `ErrInternal` or `UnknownError` is STATE, never UNUSABLE_NAME or UNAVAILABLE.
- **`unknownName` and description words.** `ErrInternal`, `ErrConfigMalformed`, `ErrSchemaMismatch`, `ErrSchemaMigrationRequired` and `ErrStoreOpen` have no class in any client and arrive as `ErrUnknownErrorName`; they are told apart by `unknownName`, matched exactly (a differently cased name is an unknown later name), and UNUSABLE_NAME from other `ErrInternal` by the phrase in the description. The three store-open names are UNCLASSIFIED, carrying the reported name and the redacted message. A value whose own `errName` is one of the five, and that is no instance of a class the table names, is classified the same way, reading `errDescription` (Assumption A-13).
- **The launch-timeout forms (b.jg5 SRJ-407).** `launchTimeoutFormOf(value, call)` and `isLaunchTimeoutError(value, call)` tell a launch timeout from the other UNAVAILABLE launch outcomes, by class plus phrase and only for a declared launch call (`spawn`, plain or reuse, or `resume`): an `ErrCallTimeout` instance, or an `ErrTmuxUnresponsive` instance whose description contains `LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_PHRASE` ("the session may have been created", `ad-description-phrases.ts`). An `ErrUnknownErrorName` whose `unknownName` is `ErrTmuxUnresponsive` is neither form. The class is unchanged: both forms stay UNAVAILABLE. Pure and never throws ([A launch's window and the read after a timeout](#a-launchs-window-and-the-read-after-a-timeout-bjg5-srj-407)).
- **UNAVAILABLE fallback.** An unknown later name (an `ErrUnknownErrorName` carrying a Phase-1-only name included, but not `ErrSchemaMismatch`, `ErrSchemaMigrationRequired` or `ErrStoreOpen`), CSCB's `UnknownError` wrapper and any value that is not an `AgentDirectorError` are UNAVAILABLE. An `ErrUnknownErrorName` carrying `ErrTmuxKillFailed` is so UNAVAILABLE and not a kill failure, and one carrying `ErrTmuxUnresponsive` is not a launch timeout.
- **`ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`** is UNCLASSIFIED; `withOutageDetection` (`outage-state.ts`) still raises `ad-unreachable` for it, and the liveness adapter, which tells it apart by class (`isAdErrorInstance`), reads it `dead` and raises `ad-unreachable` too (Auto-Restart step 3), and does not report it to the unclassified-error episode. At every launch and recovery site it is a refusal like any other UNCLASSIFIED outcome (below), never counted, except at the `working`-row wait's `status` reads, where it is transient: the wait goes on at the poll and ends `not-reconnected` at its timeout (b.jg5 SRJ-605), while the wrapper still raises `ad-unreachable` and arms P's retry timer.
- **STATE** has no fixed meaning; each call site gives it one.
- **UNUSABLE_NAME** latches the persona at every server site that meets it on the persona's own row (b.jg5 SRJ-512; the CLI precheck instead fails that persona's precheck and latches nothing): the case `unusable-recorded-name`, the refused operation `none`, and no further step (see **An unusable recorded name** under [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)). Every other `ErrInternal` is UNCLASSIFIED.
- **The CONFLICT case (b.jg5 SRJ-507).** A CONFLICT classification carries no case and no description. `src/conflict-latch.ts` tells the case from the description's words, which it reads through `conflictDescriptionOf`, checking the case phrases in `CONFLICT_CASE_ORDER` with the first match deciding and unrecognised text last; the order matters because one description can carry several case words ("the agent's pane was not found", "not this launch's session" and "never reported in" each come with "this row's own id"). The plain spawn's "its label names this instance id" and "its label does not name this instance id" are not case phrases.
- **Reported name and message.** An UNCLASSIFIED, UNUSABLE_NAME or CONFIG classification carries `reportedName` (`unknownName` for an `ErrUnknownErrorName`, else `errName`) only when `isSafeIdentifier` accepts it: an unsafe name is absent, never reported raw, with no placeholder. It carries `message` (the envelope's `err_description` for an `ErrUnknownErrorName`, else `errDescription`) rendered by `renderLogMessageText` (redacted, one line, capped at 300 characters), absent when that rendering is empty. `describeAdErrorClassification(c)` renders a classification for a log line from those fields only: `class=<class>[ name=<name>][ message="<message>"]`, the message JSON-quoted.

**The `ErrInvalidFlags` step.** `classifyWithInvalidFlagsRecheck(value, trigger?)` is the step for a site that gives `ErrInvalidFlags` no meaning. For an `ErrInvalidFlags` (`isInvalidFlagsError`, by class) it awaits exactly one immediate version re-check through `trigger` (default `triggerAdVersionRecheck`, `ad-version-gate.ts`, b.jg5 SRJ-204) and answers class UNCLASSIFIED (name `ErrInvalidFlags`, the rendered `errDescription`) with the re-check's answer (`pass`, `stop`, `could-not-run` or `not-running`). A trigger that throws or rejects counts as `could-not-run` with the fixed description `TRIGGER_FAILED_DESCRIPTION`. Any other value answers its pure class with no re-check. The step never rejects. A re-check that stops (a binary below the Phase 1 floor or too old) ends the server as the runtime re-check defines. The answer is an `AdErrorStepAnswer` (`classification`, and `recheck` present only for an `ErrInvalidFlags`); an overload types it as `AdInvalidFlagsStepAnswer`, whose `recheck` is not optional, when the argument is an `InvalidFlagsError` (the type `isInvalidFlagsError` narrows to), so a site that has narrowed the value reads the re-check's answer without a check.

The step is wired at seven sites:

- the shared read-pane (`readPersonaOwnPane`, **The shared read-pane** below);
- every plain spawn (the one plain-spawn handler `plainSpawnOutcomeAt`, then `plainSpawnFailedAt` and the private `invalidFlagsUnclassifiedAt` it shares with the `resume`, `session-manager.ts`, b.jg5 SRJ-111, SRJ-204): exactly one immediate re-check, then as at the `resume` below: a `stop` answers `failed` marked `stopping` with one line, and any other answer is the UNCLASSIFIED refusal and `retrying`. No further launch, no hold, no spawn-failure notice ([Plain spawn](#plain-spawn-bjg5-srj-111));
- the reconnect's `send-keys` (`reconnectMcpWithCause`, `session-manager.ts`, b.jg5 SRJ-118): the step is awaited, then one line (`reconnectInvalidFlagsLine`); the reconnect answers `transient` with nothing typed, marked `stopping` when the re-check answered `stop` (then nothing is reported); after any other answer `reportUnclassifiedAtSite` arms the persona's retry timer with the `unclassified` cause and reports the outcome to its unclassified-error episode (Server-Managed Startup step 5, the `waiting` branch);
- the `resume` at either `resume` site, `resumeOrFreshSpawn` and the live-row sequence's final launch, through the one `resume` handler (`resumeAtSite`, then `resumeFailedAt`, `session-manager.ts`, b.jg5 SRJ-113): the step is awaited, then one log line from the classification; when the re-check answers `stop`, nothing is posted and the `failed` action is marked `stopping`, which the restart path does not count; after any other answer it takes the UNCLASSIFIED refusal (b.jg5 SRJ-313): the outage state's site entry arms the persona's retry timer with the `unclassified` cause and reports the outcome to its unclassified-error episode, one refusal line is logged, no spawn-failure notice is posted, and the launch answers `retrying` (b.jg5 SRJ-1015), never counted. Nothing is deleted, killed or launched because of it (see [Server-Managed Startup](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1) step 5);
- the reuse spawn (`reuseSpawnForPersona`, `session-manager.ts`, b.jg5 SRJ-112): the step is awaited; when the re-check answers `stop`, one line, nothing posted, and the `failed` action is marked `stopping`, which is not counted; after any other answer (`pass`, `could-not-run` or `not-running`) the persona is held on `ErrInvalidFlags` (`decideInvalidFlagsHold`, `invalid-flags-hold.ts`, b.jg5 SRJ-207) and the reuse answers `held`, with one line: no spawn-failure notice, no `spawn-failed` entry, nothing counted, nothing armed and nothing reported to the unclassified-error episode ([The `ErrInvalidFlags` hold](#the-errinvalidflags-hold-bjg5-srj-207-srj-1008)). It never makes another launch: CSCB never falls back to a plain spawn or to any tmux-touching call ([Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)). Only the reuse holds: a `resume`'s `ErrInvalidFlags` keeps the re-check, then the UNCLASSIFIED refusal (above), and a plain spawn's is never held;
- the server's kills (`recheckKillOnInvalidFlags` in `killPersonaInstance` and in each try of the start sweep's kill, `sweepKillTry`, `session-manager.ts`, b.jg5 SRJ-110; the outcome is never UNAVAILABLE, so it is never tried again): the step is awaited and its answer kind kept as the kill outcome's `recheck`. When it answers `stop`, nothing is reported and the site does nothing more: the ladder answers `failed` marked `stopping`, the restart work answers `RESTART_OUTCOME_SHUTTING_DOWN`, the teardown's kill step fails with the row kept, and the start sweep records the kill as one a shutdown stopped (its `orphan-cleanup` entry with no alert text), kills no further row and skips its findMissing run. After any other answer the outcome is UNCLASSIFIED (**The checked kill** below);
- the click handler's `decide` (`permission-click-handler.ts`): after the trail event and log line, the step is started and not awaited, so the Slack interactive ack, which waits on the handler's return, is not held by a slow re-check (see [Click handler (SR-4)](#click-handler-sr-4)).

The other callers of the classifier are the UNAVAILABLE retry timer's arming predicate (`unavailableRetryCauseFor`, see the `unavailable-retry.ts` entry of the Module Map), which classifies every agent-director error reported inside a launch or recovery attempt, and an ENVIRONMENT or CONFIG error in any context (and whose `unavailable` answer for a tmux-touching call starts the `tmux-unresponsive` condition), the outage wrappers (`withOutageDetection`), which raise `tmux-unavailable` on an ENVIRONMENT error and `ad-config-malformed` on a CONFIG error and, on a GONE error from a tmux-touching call, clear `tmux-unavailable` and end that condition, the liveness adapter (`_buildIsSessionAliveAdapter`, Auto-Restart step 3), which reads an ENVIRONMENT or CONFIG `status` error `unknown` and raises the matching outage, a joiner of the shared `find-missing` sweep, which raises its own outage for either, the read-pane mapper (`paneReadFailureOf`, **The shared read-pane** below), the reconnect's `send-keys` (`reconnectMcpWithCause`), which decides every answer by class through the classifier and `isAdErrorInstance`, never by an error's name (Server-Managed Startup step 5, the `waiting` branch), and the CLI precheck's verdict (`precheckVerdictOf`, `cli-teardown.ts`), which raises no outage, latches nothing and makes no version re-check ([The CLI precheck](#the-cli-precheck-bjg5-srj-901)). The reporting point (`reportAgentDirectorError`) also classifies each error to send an UNCLASSIFIED one met in an attempt to the persona's unclassified-error episode ([The unclassified-error episode](#the-unclassified-error-episode-bjg5-srj-313-srj-1009)). The launch and recovery sites decide a refusal through the same arming predicate (below). The reuse spawn's `ErrInvalidFlags` takes the step and then, unless the re-check stops the server, the `ErrInvalidFlags` hold (above): no refusal, nothing armed and nothing counted.

**Refusals at the launch and recovery sites (b.jg5 SRJ-105).** Every launch and recovery call site decides whether an error is a refusal through the arming predicate, `unavailableRetryCauseFor(err, verb)` (`unavailable-retry.ts`), over this classifier, so it recognises errors by class (**Recognition by class** above). An error is a refusal in five cases:

- **UNAVAILABLE, from any verb:** `ErrTmuxUnresponsive`, `ErrTmuxKillFailed`, `ErrCallTimeout`, an unknown later name, CSCB's `UnknownError` wrapper and any value that is not an `AgentDirectorError`.
- **ENVIRONMENT, from any verb (b.jg5 SRJ-311):** `ErrTmuxNotAvailable`, `kill` included. Nothing is killed, deleted or relaunched because of it, it is never counted, and it never starts the `tmux-unresponsive` condition.
- **CONFIG, from any verb (b.jg5 SRJ-316):** `ErrConfigMalformed`, `kill` and the read verbs included. The wrapper (or the joiner of a shared sweep) has already raised the `ad-config-malformed` outage; the site only refuses and logs. Nothing is killed, deleted or relaunched because of it, it is never counted, never read as dead, and it never starts the `tmux-unresponsive` condition.
- **UNCLASSIFIED, from any verb (b.jg5 SRJ-313):** every other `ErrInternal`, the three store-open names, `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` (whose wrapper also raises `ad-unreachable`) and every name CSCB gives no handling (a STATE or GONE name a plain spawn gives no meaning included); and the `ErrInvalidFlags` of a `resume` or a plain spawn after its re-check (the `ErrInvalidFlags` step above; the reuse spawn's holds the persona instead). No step follows it: it never leads to a delete, a kill to recover or a launch, posts no spawn-failure notice, records no `spawn-failed` entry, is never counted and never starts `tmux-unresponsive`. Inside an attempt it arms the persona's timer and is reported to its unclassified-error episode.
- **A read error:** any other error from `status`, `get` or `list`, except `ErrSpawnNotFound` and an UNUSABLE_NAME answer. An UNCLASSIFIED read, a store agent-director cannot open included, is one, and keeps the `read-error` cause; it is reported to the unclassified-error episode too.

Because the predicate that arms the retry timer also decides the site's handling, the two decisions always agree. In the collision ladder (`session-manager.ts`) one private helper, `refusalAt`, handles a refusal. It logs one line and answers `failed`. It posts no spawn-failure notice and records no `spawn-failed` startup-errors entry. The site then calls nothing more, so a refusal never leads to a delete, a kill to recover, a launch or a reuse, and never gives `dead-session`; the one exception is a launch call's UNAVAILABLE refusal (a launch timeout included), which the launch site follows with exactly one `get` of the row and no launch ([A launch's window and the read after a timeout](#a-launchs-window-and-the-read-after-a-timeout-bjg5-srj-407)). The launch answers `retrying` in place of that `failed` when the refusal armed the timer (b.jg5 SRJ-1015), and `launchSession` answers that as `'refused'`, which is never counted (Auto-Restart step 5); the start pass counts it only in its `retrying` count (the start summary, Server-Managed Startup step 5). The helper covers these sites:

- every plain spawn and resume in the ladder: the first spawn, its retry-spawn after `ErrSpawnNotFound`, and the `resume` at either `resume` site (`resumeOrFreshSpawn`'s and the live-row sequence's final launch's) and the plain spawn after that `resume`'s `ErrSpawnNotFound`. At these sites one helper, `launchRefusalAt`, takes the CONFLICT row first (`conflictAt`, b.jg5 SRJ-105, SRJ-501): an `ErrTmuxSessionConflict`, by class through the classifier, latches the persona and answers `latched` ([Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)); then the UNUSABLE NAME row (`unusableNameAt`, b.jg5 SRJ-512), which latches the persona with the refused operation `none` and answers `latched`; only any other error goes on to `refusalAt`;
- the reuse spawn (`reuseSpawnForPersona`, its outcome table `reuseSpawnFailedAt`): the CONFLICT row first (`conflictAt`, refused operation "reuse spawn"), then the UNUSABLE NAME row (`unusableNameAt`), then `refusalAt` with the `spawn` verb, every line prefixed `reuseSpawnForPersona` ([Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708));
- the collision `get`;
- the `ErrJsonlMissing` diagnosis `get` (`diagnoseJsonlMissing`, which runs before the no-transcript reuse spawn). A refused one posts no inconclusive notice and records no `jsonl-diagnosis-inconclusive` entry, and the branch then makes no reuse spawn;
- the re-read after a `resume`'s `ErrSpawnNotResumable` and the re-read before a resume site's replacement (b.jg5 SRJ-710, SRJ-609; [Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)). A refused one ends the not-resumable step as the lost race, with nothing counted, and answers the refusal result before a replacement;
- a persona's `findMissing` sweep (`reconcileMissingSweep`, and the bypassing entry `bypassingFindMissingSweep`). Its shared, memoized core, `sharedFindMissingSweep`, calls `refusalAt` with the `find-missing` verb for the persona that started the run and for each persona that joined it alike, whatever the run's kind, and answers `FIND_MISSING_REFUSED`. `find-missing` is not a read verb, so only UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG and UNCLASSIFIED refuse a sweep; any other sweep error logs its `findMissing sweep failed … — proceeding` line (`bypassing findMissing sweep failed …` for a bypassing run), is never memoized, and the caller goes on. After a run succeeds, a failed post-run `get` of the calling persona's own row (any error but `ErrSpawnNotFound`; in the start sweep's run an UNUSABLE_NAME answer too, which latched nothing there and which `refusalAt` does not refuse) goes through `refusalAt` with the `get` verb for that caller, the starter or a joiner, and a refusal answers `FIND_MISSING_REFUSED` too, with a `post-sweep get refused for <ref>` line (`postRunGetRefusal`; see **One `get` after `unverified_ids`** under Server-Managed Startup step 5). The attempt stops with `failed`, which the launch answers as `retrying` when the timer was armed, at each launch site that sweeps: `resumeOrFreshSpawn`'s sweep before the resume (so no resume), the `working`-row wait's up-front sweep and its timeout sweep (no `status` read, reconnect or `dead-session`; a wait its teardown cancelled meanwhile still answers `cancelled`), and `launchOnPromptRow`'s sweep (no row read and no resume). The start sweep (`runStartSweepPostKillFindMissing`) acts for no persona and is never refused.

The reconnect's `send-keys` (`reconnectMcpWithCause`) is not a `refusalAt` site: it takes b.jg5 SRJ-118's reconnect row. An UNAVAILABLE (timeouts included), ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG or UNCLASSIFIED answer there (`ErrSendKeysWhileRelayed` and `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` included) is `transient`: the wrapper has raised the error's outage, armed the persona's retry timer inside an attempt and reported an UNCLASSIFIED answer to its unclassified-error episode, as at any call, and the reconnect types nothing, posts no spawn-failure notice, records no `spawn-failed` entry and counts nothing. The ladder answers `latched` for a latched persona and otherwise `retrying` (b.jg5 SRJ-1015, which `launchSession` answers `'refused'`); the restart adapter answers `'transient'` (Server-Managed Startup step 5, the `waiting` branch; Auto-Restart step 3).

**The checked kill (b.jg5 SRJ-110, SRJ-701, SRJ-703).** The server's five agent-director kill sites (listed below) take the checked kill (`checked-kill.ts`): one plain `kill` (`claude_instance_id` alone) whose outcome reaches its caller, `kill_sent` included, decided by class through the classifier; `checkedKill` never throws and never retries. Only a success lets the caller's next step (a launch, a reuse, a delete) run: a result with `kill_sent` true or false, a result with no `kill_sent` field (a binary older than Phase 1), `ErrSpawnNotFound` (the row is already gone) and a GONE answer (`ErrTmuxSendKeys`, `ErrTmuxCaptureFailed`: for `kill`, gone is success, SRJ-104). The CLI teardown is the one caller for which GONE is no success: it passes `goneIsFailure` (below).

A successful `kill_sent: false` on a live row means agent-director found no session of the row's current launch and the worker's process is gone, was not recorded, or could not be read at all: a normal dead-session recovery, or a session holding the name that belongs to another row, another agent-director store or no valid label, which is GONE for this row. It raises nothing by itself (SRJ-703).

Every other outcome is a non-success (`not-killed`) of class UNAVAILABLE (`ErrTmuxKillFailed`, with its description, included), CONFLICT, UNUSABLE_NAME, CONFIG, ENVIRONMENT or UNCLASSIFIED: the row is kept, no step follows, and the site's context decides the rest. A CONFLICT answer is never retried as a kill (SRJ-505). A class SRJ-110 has no row for (LAUNCH FAILURE, a STATE name other than `ErrSpawnNotFound`, DIRECTORY) is UNCLASSIFIED, its class kept as `unlistedClass`. An `ErrInvalidFlags` (STATE) first gets the `ErrInvalidFlags` step's immediate version re-check at each of these sites (`recheckKillOnInvalidFlags`); when the re-check decides that the server stops, the site does nothing more (SRJ-205). The sites:

- the restart path's kill (`_buildKillSessionAdapter`, `server.ts`, through `killPersonaInstance` in an attempt, as one try of the bounded retry): CONFLICT and UNUSABLE NAME latch the persona; UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG and UNCLASSIFIED (`ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` included) are refused, and the restart work launches nothing, records no success or failure and answers `RESTART_OUTCOME_REFUSED` (Auto-Restart step 4); an `ErrTmuxKillFailed` that stands also raises the kill-failure alert's ordinary version ([The kill-failure alert](#the-kill-failure-alert-bjg5-srj-704-srj-1007));
- the live-row sequence's two kills (steps 1 and 4, `killPersonaInstance` in the bounded retry, each declared a kill of a row read live): a CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME latches the persona, any other non-success ends the sequence without its launch, and the alert carries the request's context (`recovery` for a sequence the collision ladder starts; [The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717)). The collision ladder makes no kill of its own;
- the start sweep's kills (`sweepKill`, on the sweep's own client, in the bounded retry with the pass budget): the sweep deletes no row, and a non-success keeps the row, records one `orphan-cleanup` entry, latches nothing and arms nothing, and the kill-failure alert the tries call for is written as the sweep's entries, never posted (Server-Managed Startup step 4);
- the persona teardown's kill (`killPersonaInstanceForTeardown`: `killPersonaInstance` in teardown context, one call per try of the bounded retry, seeded as a live row it has not read, its between-try `status` read latching nothing): a non-success fails the kill step, nothing latches and nothing is armed, a CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME answer met is only answered in its `refusals`, the kill-failure alert the tries call for is raised with the context 'persona teardown', and the row is kept after any outcome, with no delete ([Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-307) step 8; b.jg5 SRJ-715);
- the abort of CSCB's own stuck launch (`abortKillOwnStuckLaunch`, site `STUCK_LAUNCH_ABORT_SITE`, `pendingRowRule stuck-launch abort`: `killPersonaInstance` in the bounded retry, seeded `pending`): a CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME latches the persona, the alert carries the context 'stuck-launch abort', and no delete or launch follows any outcome inside the kill; a success lets the live-row sequence start at its second step ([CSCB's own stuck launch and its one abort](#cscbs-own-stuck-launch-and-its-one-abort-bjg5-srj-412), b.jg5 SRJ-412).

Beside the server's sites, the CLI teardown's kill (`teardownKill`, `cli.ts`; b.jg5 SRJ-904) takes the same checked kill, one call per try of the bounded retry, with `TEARDOWN_KILL_OPTIONS`: only SRJ-110's success forms stop the persona, so a GONE answer is the GONE non-success, which fails the persona at once. Every other non-success fails it under the classifier's class, an unlisted class included, and nothing latches ([clean_restart](#clean_restart-sr-11-event-12) step 6, **The kill**).

**The bounded kill retry (b.jg5 SRJ-702).** `src/kill-retry.ts` (`runKillRetry`) wraps a site's single-try kill (the checked kill, or the site's binding of it). A kill of a row the path last read live is tried up to `KILL_RETRY_TRIES` (3) times, `KILL_RETRY_SPACING_MS` (2 s) apart, on the site's injected wait, before its outcome stands. The site's seed says what the path last read: a state other than `ended` and `missing` (`pending` and a state CSCB does not know included) or a row known live with no state read is live; a finished row, no row or nothing read gets one try, since on a finished row `kill` is a no-op success that proves nothing.

Only an UNAVAILABLE outcome is tried again: `ErrTmuxKillFailed`, `ErrTmuxUnresponsive`, `ErrCallTimeout`, an `ErrUnknownErrorName` of that class (one carrying `ErrTmuxKillFailed` included) or a wrapped unknown error, decided by the classifier (**Recognition by class** above). Every other outcome stands at once: a success, CONFLICT (never retried as a kill), UNUSABLE NAME, CONFIG, ENVIRONMENT (`ErrTmuxNotAvailable`, which ends the tries at once) and UNCLASSIFIED.

**The read between tries.** After each 2 s wait and before each further try, exactly one `status` read of the row, through the site's read:

- `ended`, `missing` or `ErrSpawnNotFound` ends the tries as the `row-finished` success with no further kill;
- a read that latched the persona (an UNUSABLE NAME answer, or its own row read `pending` with no launch start) ends them with no further kill, the last try's outcome standing: a failure end, since no call is made for a latched persona (b.jg5 SRJ-502);
- a CONFIG answer ends them (`read-config`), the last try's outcome standing, when the last state read (the seed, then each read) is `pending`, so no kill of a row last read `pending` is made while agent-director's config is unreadable; otherwise the try goes ahead, unless the caller sets `configReadEndsTries` (the CLI teardown only), which ends them on any CONFIG read, whatever state was last read, and keeps that read's error on the result (`configRead`). The read's site raises `ad-config-malformed` (**CONFIG (b.jg5 SRJ-316)** under [UNAVAILABLE retry](#unavailable-retry-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305));
- any other failed read lets the try go ahead. A live state read becomes the last state read.

The read's side effects (outage flags, the `ad-config-malformed` raise, a latch) are the read's own. A keep-going check, asked after each wait and again after each read, ends the tries with no further kill when it answers false or throws; the result then counts as stopped (`killRetryStopped`), as after a latching read.

The live-row sequence's two kills run through this retry (`retryPersonaKill`), seeded with the state the sequence last read and with the sequence's own keep-going check beside the server's (false once the sequence is stopped or the persona is latched). Before either kill the sequence applies the same rule itself: no kill at all of a row it last read `pending` while the persona's `ad-config-malformed` outage is raised ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717)).

**The start sweep's pass budget (AC 56).** The kills of one start-sweep pass share one budget (`createKillRetryPassBudget`). Once one kill has used all its tries with an UNAVAILABLE outcome standing, the budget is spent and every later kill in that pass makes one try, so a wedged tmux delays the start pass by at most one row's tries. A kill that ends in a success, in another class, by a read or by a stop does not spend it.

**Survivor tracking (b.jg5 SRJ-702, SRJ-110).** A try's `ErrTmuxKillFailed` whose description names a surviving pid is kept as the latest survivor-naming description. A description names one when `survivorPids` (`src/ad-description-phrases.ts`, the one module that holds that form) finds a pid in its survivor clause; no other detector exists. The worker's own pid is never a survivor: a description naming only the worker as outliving the kill exit wait, or the worker still running with no session or pane found, names none. A retried `kill` re-checks only the worker's process, so a survivor that a failed try named is checked by no later call. The result carries the alert decision for the outcome that stands (`KillRetryAlert`):

- `survivor`, quoting the latest survivor-naming description, on any success end after a survivor-naming failure: a read of `ended`, `missing` or `ErrSpawnNotFound`, or a later try's success (any `kill_sent`, `ErrSpawnNotFound` or `session-gone`);
- `ordinary` when the last outcome is `ErrTmuxKillFailed`, quoting its description, and on any failure end after a survivor-naming failure (a stop by a read or by the keep-going check included, and a later try's GONE non-success under `goneIsFailure`), quoting the latest survivor-naming description; both when the last outcome is an `ErrTmuxKillFailed` naming no survivor after a survivor-naming one;
- `none` otherwise: an `ErrTmuxKillFailed` naming no survivor followed by a final `ErrTmuxUnresponsive` calls for none.

The retry only decides which alert the tries call for and which descriptions it quotes; it decides by class and changes nothing else. The caller does the last outcome's own handling (latch, outage, retry timer), then raises the alert the decision calls for ([The kill-failure alert](#the-kill-failure-alert-bjg5-srj-704-srj-1007)).

**Only the outcome that stands is reported.** Inside an attempt (`retryPersonaKill`), each try passes the wrapper's `deferUnavailableReport`, so a try's UNAVAILABLE answer arms no retry timer, starts no `tmux-unresponsive` condition and is not the attempt's recorded error. When the tries end in a failure that no stop ended, and the caller's own keep-going check (`PersonaKillRetryOptions.keepGoing`, the live-row sequence's), when given, still answers true when asked once more after the tries (a throw counts as false), `reportDeferredUnavailable` reports the outcome that stands once: an UNAVAILABLE outcome arms the persona's timer once (the `kill-failed` cause for `ErrTmuxKillFailed`) and, for a kill of a row read live and an UNAVAILABLE other than `ErrTmuxKillFailed`, starts or continues the condition, whose first refusal time is then. A try's other answers are reported at once, as they stand at once; a success and a stop report nothing more, and neither does a failure whose caller's check answers false then (a live-row sequence stopped or its persona latched while the last try ran): no retry timer is armed and no `tmux-unresponsive` condition starts. A caller with no check of its own (the restart path) always gets the report of the outcome that stands. So a kill whose second try succeeds arms nothing and starts nothing, three failed tries arm the timer once, and a failed `status` read between tries is reported as any read is.

**A tmux server that is exiting (AD handoff rev 23).** After a kill ends the last session on its tmux server, a further try or the next call on that socket can briefly answer `ErrTmuxUnresponsive` or `ErrTmuxNotAvailable` while that server exits. Each is handled by its class, with no special case: `ErrTmuxUnresponsive` is UNAVAILABLE and tried again; `ErrTmuxNotAvailable` is ENVIRONMENT, ends the tries and raises `tmux-unavailable` with its one onset and, once tmux answers, its one all-clear (**ENVIRONMENT (b.jg5 SRJ-311)** under [UNAVAILABLE retry](#unavailable-retry-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305)). Nothing posts twice and nothing latches.

**Its lines (b.jg5 SRJ-1014).** One line per try (`killRetryTryLine`: try number, the outcome through `describeKillOutcome` with `kill_sent` and the redacted description, a mark when it names a surviving pid, and what follows), one per read (`killRetryReadLine`), one per stop (`killRetryStopLine`), and one end line (`killRetryEndLine`) when more than one call was made or an alert is called for, each with the site's prefix; every line is listed in docs/engineering-guide.md, Log Messages.

**Its sites.** The restart path's kill (Auto-Restart step 4), seeded with the run's `dead` reading, so one try. The live-row sequence's two kills ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717)), seeded with the state the sequence last read, up to `KILL_RETRY_TRIES` (3) tries on the sequence's injected clock. The start sweep's kills (Server-Managed Startup step 4), seeded with the state the sweep listed, with one pass budget per pass. The abort's kill of CSCB's own stuck launch ([CSCB's own stuck launch and its one abort](#cscbs-own-stuck-launch-and-its-one-abort-bjg5-srj-412)), seeded `pending`, so up to `KILL_RETRY_TRIES` (3) tries on the clock the pending-row rule's builder is given (`killRetryWait`), with none of `holdEnded`, `configReadEndsTries` or `goneIsFailure` and never the restart path's one-try seed. The restart path's, the sequence's and the abort's kills run through `retryPersonaKill` (`session-manager.ts`): each try is `killPersonaInstance` in an attempt, the read is the shared own-row `status` read ([The shared own-row `status` read](#the-shared-own-row-status-read-bjg5-srj-115)), and the keep-going check is false once the persona is latched or, through the query `main()` installs (`setPersonaKillKeepGoingQuery`), not up (torn down included) or the server is shutting down. The persona teardown's kill runs through the same bounded retry (`killPersonaInstanceForTeardown`, b.jg5 SRJ-715), seeded as a live row it has not read, with no keep-going check and its read between tries latching nothing, and reports nothing after its tries. The CLI teardown's kill (`teardownKill`, `cli.ts`) runs through it too, on `CliDeps.sleep`, seeded with the state the teardown last read, with no keep-going check, `configReadEndsTries` set (`TEARDOWN_KILL_RETRY_OPTIONS`), so a CONFIG read between tries ends the tries whatever state was last read, and its read latching nothing ([clean_restart](#clean_restart-sr-11-event-12) step 6).

The restart path's reconnect adapter (`_buildReconnectSessionAdapter`, `server.ts`) meets a refused sweep at two places. Its escalate-dead sweeps (after a `dead-session` reconnect, a `working` or `waiting` row whose `read-pane` answered GONE or found the row absent, and a prompt row whose one-line `read-pane` answered GONE or found the row absent) go through `sweepDeadTmuxChannelWithCause`, which reports `{ refused: true }`. A prompt row's deferral sweep (`checkPromptRowDeferral`) answers `'refused'` and reads nothing. The adapter answers `'transient'` for either, with no notice, so the restart run re-probes, kills and relaunches nothing (Auto-Restart step 3).

These errors keep their own handling:

- `ErrSpawnNotFound` keeps each site's meaning.
- The `working`-row wait's `status` reads, at its poll and at its timeout, are no refusal site (b.jg5 SRJ-605). `ErrSpawnNotFound` there gives `'dead-session'`. Any other error (UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG or UNCLASSIFIED, `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` included) is transient: the wait goes on at the poll and ends `'not-reconnected'` at the timeout, never `failed`, `refused` or `'dead-session'`, and is never counted. The wrapper still raises the error's outage (`ad-unreachable`, `tmux-unavailable` or `ad-config-malformed`), arms the persona's retry timer and reports an UNCLASSIFIED answer to the persona's unclassified-error episode, as at any read in a launch attempt (Server-Managed Startup step 5, **b.ecw terminal verdicts**).
- At the wait's poll and timeout reads, an UNUSABLE_NAME answer latches the persona and ends the wait `latched`.
- Every other class from a launch verb (LAUNCH_FAILURE, DIRECTORY, GONE, STATE) keeps the branch the ladder describes (Server-Managed Startup step 5), spawn-failure notice included. The reconnect's `send-keys` posts no spawn-failure or other failure notice of its own for any answer (an outage it meets is still reported through `withOutageDetection`, call `send-keys`, as for any wrapped call: ENVIRONMENT raises `tmux-unavailable` and CONFIG `ad-config-malformed`, each with its onset notice, and the CONFLICT and UNUSABLE NAME latches post their *Held:* notices): GONE, `ErrSpawnNotInteractive` and `ErrSpawnNotFound` give `dead-session`, and any other STATE, LAUNCH_FAILURE or DIRECTORY name gives `transient`.

A read error never starts the `tmux-unresponsive` condition, because `status`, `get` and `list` are not tmux-touching.

**Telling STATE classes apart.** A classification carries no name for STATE, whose errors mean different things at different sites. A site that must tell one agent-director error class from another reads it through `isAdErrorInstance(value, errorClass)`, against the classes from `agent-director-errors.ts` (for example `ErrSpawnNotFound`, or the binding `ErrTmuxKillFailed`), never through an `instanceof` ladder of its own. It never throws: a value that is not an instance, or an `instanceof` that throws, answers false. `isInvalidFlagsError`, `goneErrNameOf`, the arming predicate, the kill outcome, the liveness adapter (for `ErrSpawnNotFound` and `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`) and the read-pane mapper (for `ErrSpawnNotFound`) use it.

**The shared read-pane (b.jg5 SRJ-117).** Every `read-pane` of a persona's own row `cscb_<key>` in the server outside the dialog approver and the latch re-check goes through one reader, `readPersonaOwnPane(key, { nLines, lastRead, site, allowPending? })` in `src/session-manager.ts`, and its answer is one outcome from `src/pane-read.ts` (`PaneReadOutcome`).

What agent-director answers depends on the row's current launch, found by its label on the row's recorded socket. It answers the pane of that launch's worker; with no session of that launch there and exactly one leftover of the persona, it answers that leftover's pane, the one agent-director's own per-pane label marks with the leftover's token. With neither there it answers `ErrTmuxCaptureFailed`. It answers `ErrTmuxSessionConflict` when the worker's pane is not found, when the one leftover has no pane carrying its token, or when several leftovers run. So a pane does not prove on its own that the worker's own session is there (b.jg5 SRJ-613). CSCB never reads or sets that label.

The pure mapper `paneReadFailureOf(value)` gives a thrown value exactly one failure outcome, by class through `src/ad-error-class.ts` (`classifyAdError`, then `isAdErrorInstance` for `ErrSpawnNotFound`), never by an error's name. Each failure carries the class and the redacted one-line description (`describeAgentDirectorFailure`).

| Outcome (`kind`) | Answers | What it means to a caller |
|---|---|---|
| `pane` | a pane | Evidence about a screen only, never acted on alone (b.jg5 SRJ-613; below) |
| `gone` | GONE (`ErrTmuxCaptureFailed`) | The session is not there |
| `absent` | `ErrSpawnNotFound` | The row is absent |
| `conflict` | CONFLICT (`ErrTmuxSessionConflict`), the thrown value kept | The reader latches the persona and answers `latched` |
| `unusable-name` | UNUSABLE_NAME, the thrown value kept | The reader latches the persona and answers `latched` |
| `config` | CONFIG (`ErrConfigMalformed`) | The wrapper has raised `ad-config-malformed`; never evidence of death |
| `environment` | ENVIRONMENT (`ErrTmuxNotAvailable`) | The wrapper has raised `tmux-unavailable` |
| `unavailable` | UNAVAILABLE, timeouts included; an `ErrUnknownErrorName` of a later name | Agent-director or tmux could not answer; never evidence of death |
| `unclassified` | UNCLASSIFIED (`ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` included), every STATE name but `ErrSpawnNotFound`, LAUNCH_FAILURE, DIRECTORY | No handling at a pane read; never evidence of death |
| `latched` | — | The persona is latched: `cause` is the CONFLICT or UNUSABLE_NAME answer that latched it, absent when it was latched before the read |

The reader:

- asks the latch first (`personaLatchedNow`, b.jg5 SRJ-502): a latched persona gets no call, and the answer is `latched` with no cause (`PANE_READ_NOT_READ_LATCHED`);
- otherwise makes one `readPane` (`claude_instance_id` and `n_lines`, plus `allow_pending: true` only when the caller sets `allowPending`, which only the pending-row rule's lap does) through `withOutageDetection`, declaring the tmux-touching `read-pane` verb, so the wrapper raises the ENVIRONMENT and CONFIG outages and, inside an attempt, starts or ends `tmux-unresponsive` ([The tmux-unresponsive condition](#the-tmux-unresponsive-condition-bjg5-srj-307-srj-310));
- latches on a CONFLICT through the latch's CONFLICT entry (`setFromConflict`, refused operation "P's next check or recovery", `REFUSED_OPERATION_NEXT_CHECK_OR_RECOVERY`, b.jg5 SRJ-501) and on an UNUSABLE_NAME answer through the unusable-name entry (`latchOnUnusableName`, refused operation `none`, b.jg5 SRJ-512), each recording `lastRead`, the row state the calling path last read; it logs one line per latch it sets and answers `latched` with the answer as its cause. With no latch installed the answer is still `latched`, as at the ladder's CONFLICT row;
- answers an `ErrInvalidFlags`, to which `read-pane` gives no meaning, with exactly one immediate agent-director version re-check (`classifyWithInvalidFlagsRecheck`, b.jg5 SRJ-104, SRJ-204; a stop it decides ends the process as the re-check defines) and then the `unclassified` outcome, which carries the stop mark `stopping: true` when the re-check decided that the server stops (b.jg5 SRJ-205); unless the re-check decided the stop, it reports the persona's unclassified episode at the site `read-pane` (`reportUnclassifiedAtSite`, inside a launch or recovery attempt only), and it logs one line, `[slack] <site>: pane read for persona=<key> answered <classification> — UNCLASSIFIED after one immediate agent-director version re-check: <recheck> (b.jg5 SRJ-104, SRJ-204)` (`<recheck>` is the re-check's outcome: `pass`, `stop`, `could-not-run` or `not-running`);
- returns every other outcome unchanged for the site to handle. It posts nothing, counts nothing, and reports no dead evidence on its own.

Its callers are the working-pane read, `readWorkingPane(key, lastRead)` (site `readWorkingPane`, `FULL_PANE_READ_LINES` = 40 lines), which serves the launch wait's evidence read (Server-Managed Startup step 5) and `checkWaitingRowPane` (Auto-Restart step 3), and the `working`-row verdict, `workingReconnectVerdict` in `src/server.ts` (site `reconnectSession`, 40 lines), whose pane `checkWorkingRowPane` folds (Auto-Restart step 3), and b.jdc's two prompt-row paths, which read an `ask_user` or `check_permission` row with the one-line probe count `PROBE_PANE_READ_LINES` (1 line): the prompt-row verdict `promptRowReconnectVerdict` in `src/server.ts` (site `reconnectSession: prompt row`, Auto-Restart step 3, **Prompt rows**) and the collision ladder's `launchOnPromptRow` (site `spawnForPersona: prompt row`, Server-Managed Startup step 5), and the pending-row rule's lap, `readPendingRowLapPane` (site `pendingRowRule <ref> lap`, 40 lines, `allowPending`, the row last read `pending`; [The pending-row rule](#the-pending-row-rule-bjg5-srj-410)), each recording the row state it read. On `latched` the wait ends `latched`, the `working`-row verdict and the prompt-row verdict answer `'transient'` with no deferral noted, `checkWaitingRowPane` answers `defer` and the ladder answers `latched`, each with nothing typed. On an UNCLASSIFIED carrying the stop mark, every restart-path and ladder caller calls nothing more for the persona: `checkWaitingRowPane` answers `defer` with nothing typed, the `working`-row verdict answers `'transient'` with its evidence forgotten and no deferral noted, the prompt-row verdict answers `'transient'`, and the ladder answers a `failed` result marked `stopping`, each with its own line. Every other outcome takes the caller's handling, and the caller's line for a failure names its class (`read-pane class=<CLASS>`).

The dialog approver makes its own `read-pane` and keeps its own classification (Server-Managed Startup step 5, **Stops by class**); it shares only the CONFLICT latch helper (`latchOnConflict`) with the reader.

The CLI precheck of `stop --stop-bots` and `clean_restart` (b.jg5 SRJ-901, [The CLI precheck](#the-cli-precheck-bjg5-srj-901)) makes its own one-line `read-pane` (`CliDeps.directorReadPane`, `PROBE_PANE_READ_LINES` = 1 line) of a live row, outside the shared reader: the CLI is a short-lived process with no latch, so the read never latches (b.jg5 SRJ-114, SRJ-115), goes through no outage wrapper and raises no outage. It classifies the answer with the pure mapper `paneReadFailureOf`, by SRJ-117's CLI-precheck column: a pane, GONE or `ErrSpawnNotFound` passes; UNAVAILABLE is retried; CONFIG fails the persona at once; CONFLICT, UNUSABLE_NAME, ENVIRONMENT and UNCLASSIFIED (every other class included) fail it with no retry.

The latch re-check (b.jg5 SRJ-505, [The re-check](#the-re-check-bjg5-srj-505)) makes its own one-line `read-pane` of a latched persona's own row (`PROBE_PANE_READ_LINES`) outside the shared reader too, since that reader skips a latched persona and latches: the probe, and a "conflicting labels" latch's lap read of a `pending` row with `allow_pending`, which types nothing. It goes through the outage wrapper inside the re-check's no-information scope and classifies its answer with the pure mapper `paneReadFailureOf` by SRJ-117's latch-probe column, with no "no pane 0.0" case and no `ErrInvalidFlags` version re-check (that answer is UNCLASSIFIED there): its verdicts are `decideLatchRecheckProbe` and `decideLatchRecheckPendingReadPane` (`src/conflict-latch.ts`). It latches only through the round: an UNUSABLE NAME relatches, and at the lap read a CONFLICT with another case relatches.

**No site acts on a pane alone (b.jg5 SRJ-613).** The sites that read a pane are the `working`-row verdict (`workingReconnectVerdict`, whose pane `checkWorkingRowPane` folds), the `waiting`-row check (`checkWaitingRowPane`), the launch wait's evidence read (`staleWorkingRowIsIdle`), b.jdc's two prompt-row paths (`promptRowReconnectVerdict`, `launchOnPromptRow`), the dialog approver (`approverLap`), the pending-row rule's lap (`readPendingRowLapPane`), the latch re-check's probe and lap read (`latchRecheckReadPane`) and the CLI precheck (`precheckVerdictOf`). A pane any of them reads may be a single leftover's, so it leads at most to a deferral (the prompt-row verdict), a probe's finding handed off with the persona still latched or a lap read's clear of the latch, with nothing typed (the latch re-check), no action (the ladder's prompt-row action), a positive-idle fold that also needs the transcript (the `working`-row verdict and the launch wait), the reconnect (the `waiting`-row check), Enter (the approver and the pending-row rule's lap, each only on a recognised startup dialog, `paneShowsStartupDialog`) or a passed precheck, which proves nothing about whose session runs. On a prompt row nothing is typed on the pane; the reconnect comes only once a later read finds the row `waiting`, or a `working` row stale.

The backstop is the call that follows a pane read (a `send-keys`) or acts on the row (a kill), which agent-director answers by the row's current launch and which types or sends nothing when it refuses:

- the reconnect's one `send-keys` (`reconnectMcpWithCause`) on a live row that is not `pending` answers CONFLICT "not this launch's session" when a leftover holds the persona's session: P latches with its CONFLICT notice posted once, and the refused `send-keys` is never retried. The restart adapter answers `'transient'`; in the launch wait the ladder answers `latched`, which `launchSession` answers `'skipped'`. The reconnect's handling is the `waiting` branch of [Server-Managed Startup](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1) step 5; the hold is [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502);
- a kill that answers CONFLICT "not this launch's session" on a live row, `pending` included, means a leftover holds the persona's session and nothing was sent: P latches through the CONFLICT entry with the refused operation "P's next check or recovery", and the kill is never retried. Of the kill sites that exist, the live-row sequence's kills and the abort's kill of CSCB's own stuck launch (on a row read `pending`, recorded `pending`; [CSCB's own stuck launch and its one abort](#cscbs-own-stuck-launch-and-its-one-abort-bjg5-srj-412)) can meet a live row; the restart path's kill (made only after a `dead` reading) latches on a CONFLICT the same way; the start sweep and the persona teardown latch nothing (**The checked kill** above; [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502));
- the approver's Enter on a `pending` row answers `ErrSpawnNotInteractive`: the approver stops with nothing typed and no kill (**Pre-session dialog approval**, **Stops by class**, in the same step);
- the pending-row rule's lap Enter (`sendPendingRowLapEnter`, `allow_pending`) answers `ErrSpawnNotInteractive` the same way: nothing is typed, the not-interactive record is set so no further lap is made on that launch, and nothing is killed ([The pending-row rule](#the-pending-row-rule-bjg5-srj-410));
- after a passed CLI precheck, the CLI teardown's `pause` of the row (or the `kill` it escalates to), which agent-director answers by the row's current launch, so a leftover holding the persona's session is not the one it acts on. A `pause` that answers CONFLICT fails that persona's teardown at once, with no kill, and a `kill` that answers CONFLICT ("not this launch's session" included) fails it at once, with no further try; neither latches anything (b.jg5 SRJ-903, SRJ-904; [clean_restart](#clean_restart-sr-11-event-12) step 6).

Likewise a GONE (`ErrTmuxCaptureFailed`) says only that no session or pane of the row's current launch is there. It does not prove the worker gone after a kill failure whose description says no session or pane of this launch was found while the worker's process runs.

The kill-failure alert's ordinary version (*Kill failed*, [The kill-failure alert](#the-kill-failure-alert-bjg5-srj-704-srj-1007)) tells the human who checks the worker both `read-pane` caveats above (a GONE is no proof the worker is gone; a pane is no proof it is the worker's). For these it points to the "Operator actions" section of agent-director's README. The kill's CONFLICT "not this launch's session" is the same backstop as above: agent-director answers a kill by the row's current launch, so a kill made after a leftover's pane was read sends nothing to the leftover.

### Log-only routing (b.jg5 SRJ-1002)

Some notices have no Slack destination that is sure to be right, so they go to one server-log line and one `startup-errors.log` entry through `recordStartupError` (class per SRJ-1013, see [startup-errors.log](#startup-errorslog-claudechannelsslackstartup-errorslog)) and never reach Slack. The contexts, each with its own passage:

- every notice raised for a persona while its teardown's notice window is open ([Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-307), **The notice window**), including the all-clear of an outage whose onset was raised in it, whenever it comes;
- the start sweep's kill notices (Server-Managed Startup step 4; [Start sweep kill lines](#start-sweep-kill-lines-bjg5-srj-714-srj-702-srj-205));
- the CLI teardown's notices, which the CLI also prints ([stop command](#stop-command), [clean_restart](#clean_restart-sr-11-event-12));
- a kill-failure alert or an unclassified-error alert for a persona no longer in the applied configuration ([The kill-failure alert](#the-kill-failure-alert-bjg5-srj-704-srj-1007), [The unclassified-error episode](#the-unclassified-error-episode-bjg5-srj-313-srj-1009)), and a stopped kill retry of a persona removed during its tries (a `persona-kill-failed` entry with no alert text; a configured persona's stopped retry is its log line only);
- the old-life wait's kill-failure, unclassified-error, CONFLICT and UNUSABLE NAME notices ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809));
- the version gate's refusal, at start (Server-Managed Startup step 1) or at a runtime re-check ([Runtime version re-check lines](#runtime-version-re-check-lines-bjg5-srj-205-srj-206)).

A CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME answer a context's own calls meet (the teardown's kill, the start sweep, the CLI teardown, the old-life wait) is routed the same way and latches nothing. One met by a launch or recovery still in flight for a persona whose teardown window is open latches it, as for an applied persona, a removed persona included, and only its notice is written by the window (see below). One exception: an ENVIRONMENT or CONFIG answer at a start-sweep kill raises its outage for the row's persona when that persona is applied, and that onset posts as any onset does.

**A persona no longer in the applied configuration, elsewhere.** Whether a persona is still applied is decided only by the session manager's one installed configured-persona query (`setConfiguredPersonaQuery`; production: `main()`'s query over `getAppliedPersona`, read at each call). The four latch entries (`conflictAt`, `latchOnConflict`, `unusableNameAt`, `latchOnUnusableName`, through `latchEntryConfigured`) ask it too: for a key it does not count (for example, a launch or recovery that began before an apply removed the persona) whose persona teardown window is not open (`teardownWindowOpen`: none, or only `submitted`) a CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME makes no latch-time read, sets no latch, posts nothing and writes no `startup-errors.log` entry (SRJ-1013 has no class for it). The site's one line names the persona reference, the call and the redacted description, with `notConfiguredLatchOutcome(case, operation)` (`conflict-latch.ts`) as its outcome:

```text
the persona is not in the applied configuration (case=<case> refused=<operation>), so nothing is latched or posted (b.jg5 SRJ-1002)
```

`<case>` is `unusable-recorded-name` for an UNUSABLE NAME, whose `<operation>` is `none`.

**Inside an open teardown window (b.jg5 SRJ-1002, SRJ-1003).** An apply removes a persona from the configuration before its teardown runs, so a launch in flight that the teardown waits for (step 2) can meet a CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME for a key the query no longer counts. While that key's teardown window is `open` (`teardownWindowOpen`, read through the installed notice episodes, `setStuckLaunchEpisodes`, whose teardown query is the persona notifier's `teardownWindowState`; with none installed no window is open), the entry latches as for an applied persona: the latch is set, the site's line carries the set's outcome, and the latch's notice goes through the notice episodes to the notifier's open window, which writes it as one server-log line (`raised during its teardown`) and one `persona-teardown-notice` entry and posts nothing. The teardown's forget once the launch in flight has settled (step 3) drops the latch and stops its re-check timer, silently. In a window that is only `submitted`, or with none, the not-configured line above is written and nothing is latched.

**The query's defaults.** The configured-persona query's two readers take opposite defaults when none is installed (unit tests, the integration driver) or when it throws: the own-row read rule (`configuredReadingOf`: `readPersonaOwnRow`, `applyOwnRowStatusStep`) counts no key as configured, so no row read latches anyone by the note or launch-start rule; the CONFLICT and UNUSABLE NAME latch entries latch as for an applied persona. A query that throws at a latch entry logs one line (`latchEntryQueryFailedLine`), asked once per entry:

```text
[slack] configured-persona query for <ref> failed: <thrown value> — the latch entry latches as for a configured persona (b.jg5 SRJ-1002)
```

### Server-Managed Startup (SR-11 Event 1)

Called from `main()` in `server.ts`. Before step 1, `main()` creates the state and inbox directories (nothing is created at import) and installs the `unhandledRejection` handler (`createUnhandledRejectionHandler`, once, before any persona connects), so one persona's stray rejection is logged token-safely as `[slack] unhandled rejection (process keeps running): …` and never takes the process down.

In `main()` the steps run in this order: 1, 2, 2a, 2a-bis, 2a-ter, 2b, 2c, 3, then the message-archive setup, the per-persona notice episodes (`createPersonaEpisodes`, b.jg5 SRJ-1016, stored in the module-scope handle `shutdown` forgets through, and installed at once in the session manager for the stuck-launch episode's end at its own-row reads, `setStuckLaunchEpisodes`, b.jg5 SRJ-1017; see [The stuck-launch post](#the-stuck-launch-post-bjg5-srj-1017-srj-1016)), the per-persona latch (`createConflictLatch`, b.jg5 SRJ-501, in memory only and held in `main()` alone, with no module-scope handle) with its holds bound first (`bindConflictLatchHolds`, b.jg5 SRJ-502: the retry controller's `stop` with `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_LATCHED`, the `tmux-unresponsive` condition's silent end with `TMUX_UNRESPONSIVE_END_LATCHED`, the unclassified-error episodes' end with `UNCLASSIFIED_ERROR_END_LATCHED`, the slow-recovery tracker's `endForLatch`, and the stuck-launch episode's silent end over the notice episodes (`endStuckLaunchEpisodeForLatch`, `src/pending-row.ts`); the first four are built just below, and no latch can be set before the start pass), then its CONFLICT notice bound to those episodes (`bindConflictNotice`, b.jg5 SRJ-508), then its re-check timers (`buildLatchRecheck`, bound by `bindLatchRecheck`, b.jg5 SRJ-505; [The re-check](#the-re-check-bjg5-srj-505)), and the latch installed in the session manager (`setConflictLatch`), then the configured-persona query installed beside it (`setConfiguredPersonaQuery`, b.jg5 SRJ-114: a key counts as configured when `getAppliedPersona` finds it, read at each call and holding no state; see [Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)), then the one retired-key store, `retiredKeys`, installed for the session manager's row reads (`setRetiredKeyStore`, b.jg5 SRJ-807; the same binding the reload controller gets), so all three are in place before the start sweep and the start pass, then the kill retry's keep-going query (`setPersonaKillKeepGoingQuery`, b.jg5 SRJ-702: `isPersonaUp` and the shutting-down flag, read at each call and holding no state; see **The bounded kill retry** under [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)), the unclassified-error episodes, the kill-failure alerts (`createKillFailureAlerts` over the notice episodes, installed in the session manager with `setKillFailureAlerts` and kept for the persona routing's kill-failed query, b.jg5 SRJ-704; see [The kill-failure alert](#the-kill-failure-alert-bjg5-srj-704-srj-1007)), the slow-recovery tracker (`createSlowRecoveryTracker` over the notice episodes, b.jg5 SRJ-610, handed to `initRestart` as `slowRecovery` and, through its `noteHealthy`, to the health check as `resetSlowRecoveryCount`), the UNAVAILABLE retry controller, the live-row sequence registry (`createLiveRowSequenceRegistry`, b.jg5 SRJ-706, installed with `setLiveRowSequenceRegistry`, so it is in place before the start pass and any path that could start a sequence; the latch installed above gets its sequence-stop set observer then), the pending-row rule (`setPendingRowRule`, b.jg5 SRJ-410, over the notice episodes and the persona lifecycle serializer, likewise before the start pass), outage state and notifier installation, the connection manager, step 7, `Bun.serve` with the `server.port` record and then the PID file, and the cron scheduler, `initRestart`, then 4, 4a-bis, 4a-quater, 4a-ter, 5, 8 and 9. Step 6 is not a point in the sequence: it happens whenever a persona comes up. The UNAVAILABLE retry controller (b.jg5 SRJ-301, SRJ-303) is built on the system clock and installed as the outage state's trigger sink (`initOutageState`'s `triggerSink`) before the start pass, whose launches are the first attempts that can arm it. Its retry action uses the relaunch gate and the restart module, both set up later in `main()`, only when a retry falls due, 30 s after an arm at the earliest (see Auto-Restart, [UNAVAILABLE retry](#unavailable-retry-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305)). A runtime version re-check stop can begin a shutdown while `main()` is still starting up, so `main()` returns early once the `shuttingDown` flag is set, checked at eight points: after the step 2c await (before step 3), after the step 3 await (before the message-archive setup, step 7, `Bun.serve` and the cron scheduler), before step 4 (the start sweep), before step 4a-bis (`trustBootstrap`), before step 4a-quater (`runJsonlPersistenceSafeguard`), before step 4a-ter (`stopHookBootstrap`), before step 5, and before steps 8 and 9. So no sweep, bootstrap pass or bring-up starts once a shutdown has begun (b.jg5 SRJ-205), and the sweep itself reads the flag live through its shutdown query, so a shutdown begun during it makes no further agent-director call from it (step 4, **The stops**). The start pass's launch pool reads the flag live too, through the shutdown query `startBringUp` passes (`isShuttingDown: () => shuttingDown`), so a shutdown begun during the pass starts no queued launch (step 5). `main()` therefore restarts nothing `shutdown` stopped and opens no Slack connection after a shutdown has begun. The steps:

1. **SR-5.1 startup gate** — `runAgentDirectorStartupGate()` runs, in order: construct the Client, CSCB's Phase 1 floor check, install the Client, the SR-6.1 API surface probes, the same-user stat. The first failure stops the gate.
    - **Construct.** It awaits `createClient(opts)` (production injects `Client.create`), which runs AD's library-side discovery and the client's own too-old refusal at `min_binary_version` from `dist/version-floor.json`. The opts come from `buildAdClientOptions()` with no call timeout, so the gate's client, and its version probe, use the client's default call timeout (step 2c replaces it). They carry `logger: makeFilteredAdLogger(console)` (b.brv) so the Client's per-poll `SubprocessClient: <verb> ok` success dumps are dropped from `server.log` unless `CSCB_AD_VERBOSE` is set — see [Logging](#logging). The catch ladder `instanceof`-matches `ErrBunVersionTooOld` (→ `ad-bun-version-too-old`), `ErrSystemInstallNotFound` (→ `ad-system-install-not-found`, message pointing to the runbook section, `RUNBOOK_SECTION_POINTER`, and saying its step 1 checks agent-director's version as the workers' user in the bot server's launcher environment, which shows whether this launcher's HOME or PATH differs from the workers'; not to the block "The publishing host", since the gate runs on a bot host where the binary may only be missing from the launcher's HOME or PATH beside a live store and workers), `ErrSystemInstallTooOld` (→ `ad-system-install-too-old`, message from `buildSystemInstallTooOldMessage`: found version, the client's required minimum, that this CSCB release needs `PHASE1_FLOOR_VERSION` or later (release candidates included), binary path, that this CSCB release and agent-director Phase 1 are installed together, and the runbook section title; no upgrade instruction), and `ErrSystemInstallUnreachable` (→ `ad-system-install-unreachable`, message surfaces AD's `err.reason` verbatim, says to diagnose with the install-cscb skill and names the runbook section, `RUNBOOK_SECTION_POINTER`); anything else is `ad-client-construct`. The three `ad-system-install-*` branches append the `install-skill-pointer.ts` manual-skill-install instructions block to their message.
    - **Phase 1 floor (b.jg5 SRJ-203).** The gate reads the built client's `binaryVersion` (never its `version()` method, which reports the npm package's version) and checks it with `meetsPhase1Floor` (`src/ad-version-gate.ts`). The client's minimum sits below the floor and the client admits its `0.0.0-dev` sentinel, so this check refuses binaries the client accepts. A version below the floor or one that does not parse is refused before the Client is installed: the gate closes the refused client once, never calls `setClient`, and fails with phase `version`, class `ad-below-phase1-floor` (`AD_BELOW_PHASE1_FLOOR`, `src/install-check.ts`) and the message from `buildBelowPhase1FloorMessage` (found version, required floor with its release candidates, binary path, "found by the startup check", and `PHASE1_SWITCH_OVER_INSTRUCTION` with the runbook section title; no upgrade instruction, no install command, no install-skill block).
    - **Install.** Only after the floor passes or is left out (`skipPhase1Floor`, set only by `stop --stop-bots`'s CLI initialization, never by the server or `clean_restart`) does the gate call `setClient(client)`, so subsequent `getClient()` call sites resolve to it. The success-arm `adVersion` is the same `binaryVersion`.
    - **Probes and same-user stat.** Then the SR-6.1 API surface probes (`getPermission` presence, error-catalog class declarations in the dist, `--request-token` in the dist) and the stat of `~/.agent-director/state.db` against `geteuid()`; a failure here closes the client. A probe's message ends with `CLIENT_PACKAGE_REMEDY`; the `ad-same-user` message says to run the server as the user that owns the file, never to remove or recreate it, and names the runbook section.
    - **Failure.** Every failure outcome carries a `refusalKind`: `client-too-old` (`REFUSAL_KIND_CLIENT_TOO_OLD`, the `ErrSystemInstallTooOld` branch), `below-phase1-floor` (`REFUSAL_KIND_BELOW_PHASE1_FLOOR`) or `other` (`REFUSAL_KIND_OTHER`, every other branch). `runAgentDirectorStartupGate()` makes one `recordStartupError(classLabel, message)` call, which writes one line to stderr (captured in `server.log`) and one entry to `startup-errors.log`, then exits non-zero. It runs before the PID conflict check, so nothing else in `main()` runs. The server's start always runs the floor: `runAgentDirectorStartupGate()` offers no way to leave it out.
    - **Runtime version re-check (b.jg5 SRJ-204).** In the statement right after the gate passes, behind no branch and before the PID conflict check (step 2), `main()` calls `installAdVersionRecheck` with agent-director's `resolveSystemBinary`, the gate result's `adVersion` as the baseline, `recordStartupError`, a `stop` callback and the server log. Its first re-check runs 120 s later on its own timer, whatever `health_check_interval` is (`0` included), in dry run too. The `stop` callback first arms the shutdown deadline (`armShutdownDeadline`, `src/shutdown-deadline.ts`: 30 s, unref'd, exits with the same code), then sets `process.exitCode` to the same code (so a shutdown that hangs with no open handle, where the process exits on its own before the deadline can fire, still exits non-zero), then runs `shutdown('the runtime version re-check refused the agent-director binary (see startup-errors.log)', exitCode)`; if that shutdown rejects, the process still exits with the same code, and if it hangs, the deadline ends it. See `ad-version-gate.ts` in the Module Map and [Graceful Shutdown](#graceful-shutdown-sr-11-event-11).
2. **PID conflict check** — existing `checkPidConflict(PID_FILE)` invariant. CSCB enforces one instance per host. A stale PID file (its process not running) is removed with the `server.port` record beside it (b.jg5 SRJ-510; [server.port](#serverport-state_dirserverport)), and the start goes on.
    - **Retired-key record read (b.jg5 SRJ-801, SRJ-802).** In the statement right after the PID check, behind no branch (so in dry run too), `main()` calls `readRetiredKeysAtStart(STATE_DIR, { log: (line) => console.error(line) })` (`src/retired-keys.ts`) once, with production's reader, writer, clock and `recordStartupError`. It sits after the PID check, so a duplicate start reads nothing, and before step 2a's reload controller and its start resolution (which can write `config.json.last-applied`), the start sweep and every bring-up. A missing file is an empty record. A record that exists but cannot be read, parsed or validated records one `retired-keys-unreadable` entry naming the file, what is wrong with it and the move-aside remedy, and `main()` exits 1 in the next statement: no port, PID file, Slack connection, sweep, launch or last-applied write, and the start never guesses. Otherwise the loaded store is bound once, to the local `const retiredKeys`, the server's one store, which `main()` passes to the reload controller for apply step 1 (see [The apply pipeline](#the-apply-pipeline-sr-86-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-805)) and installs, after the configured-persona query and before the start sweep, for the session manager's own-row reads (`setRetiredKeyStore`, b.jg5 SRJ-807; see [Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)); nothing else in `src/` builds one (see Configuration, [retired-keys.json](#retired-keysjson-state_dirretired-keysjson)). In the next statement, behind no branch, `main()` builds the server's one old-life hold set (`createOldLifeHoldSet`, its lines to `console.error`; b.jg5 SRJ-809), bound to the local `const oldLifeHolds`, which it hands to the reload controller as `oldLifeHolds` and installs, right after the store and before the start sweep, for the session manager (`setOldLifeHolds`); nothing else in `src/` builds or installs one. It starts empty: holds live in memory, and the start sweep rebuilds the ones a restart dropped ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809)).
2a. **Start resolution: the last-applied record (b.av2 SR-1.7; b.av2 SR-8.7 as amended by b.deo SRI-403, SRI-407)** — `main()` builds the reload controller (`createReloadController`, `src/reload.ts`) over `reloadFilePaths(CONFIG_PATH)` and calls `resolveStart()`. Saving `config.json` does not change what runs: every start runs the last-applied record `config.json.last-applied` (see Configuration, Reload files) when it exists. Each file is read once, and the bytes validated are the bytes recorded or applied. The rules:

    - **Record present.** The record is validated in record mode (`parsePersonaConfigBytes` with `record: true`) and becomes the applied config; `config.json` is not read to decide what runs, so an edit that was never applied stays unapplied across restarts and reboots. Logs `[slack] Starting from the last-applied record "<record>"`. Credentials files are not read here: the bring-up (step 5) reads them as they stand, so a credentials change made while the server was down takes effect at this start.
    - **No record, valid `config.json`.** The file is validated in default mode, its exact bytes are written to the record with the durable write (`durableWriteFileSync`), and then it is applied. Logs `[slack] No last-applied record: recorded the configuration file "<config>" as "<record>"`. This is the path of a fresh install and of the first start after upgrading.
    - **No record, `config.json` missing or invalid.** Logs `[slack] Fatal: configuration error — <message>` (see Configuration, config.json, for the messages; a pre-persona file gets the SR-1.7 conversion error) and exits 1.
    - **No record, record unwritable.** Logs `[slack] reload-record-write-failed: cannot write the last-applied record "<record>" (<errno code>); the server does not start and nothing is applied` (the errno code only when the error carries one) and exits 1. When the rename succeeded but the directory sync failed (`DurableWriteUnsyncedError`), the line is instead `[slack] reload-record-write-failed: the last-applied record "<record>" was written but its directory could not be synced (<errno code>), so it may not survive a crash, and the next start will run it; the server does not start`, and the server exits 1 the same way.
    - **Record unreadable or invalid.** A record is absent only when reading it fails with ENOENT or ENOTDIR; any other read failure (`EISDIR` for a directory, `not a regular file` for a FIFO, socket or device, which is never read, or a record over the size cap; see Reload files, Size cap), and any validation failure, refuses the start without falling back to `config.json`. Logs one unclassed line, `[slack] Fatal: last-applied record error — <cause> Deleting the last-applied record "<record>" makes the next start apply the configuration file "<config>" as it stands.`, and exits 1.
    - **Real-path collision in the record (b.av2 SR-1.5, record-start part, as amended by b.deo SRI-104).** Record mode skips only the loader's shared-path rule, so a record whose personas share a `working_directory` or a `credentials_file` still starts. The collision is caught by each involved persona's bring-up checks (step 5), using the bring-up outcomes: a shared working directory is `persona-directory-unusable` (`retrying`, re-checked on its timer) and a shared credentials file is `persona-credentials-invalid` (`broken`), each naming the other persona. The other personas come up normally. A persona broken by the shared credentials file still holds the digest of its own path's bytes (hashed, never parsed), so a later re-save of that file is a pending credentials change for it (Reload Detection Tick). In dry run the credentials check does not run, so a shared credentials file is not caught there.
    - **Zero personas.** An empty `personas` array is a valid applied set: the start runs with no persona brought up.

    Every refusal is logged by the controller as one line and happens after the PID check, so a duplicate start never writes the record, and before any port is bound, the PID file is written, a Slack connection opens or anything is spawned. Nothing is applied on a refusal. On an applied start `main()` sets `personaConfig` to the applied config and keeps it as `appliedConfig`, the start-time server-wide values (such as `getRestartDelay`'s delay, `bind` and `port`), which never change until the next start. Step 2a-ter may then replace both with a copy whose `cron_table_path` alone differs, the crontable the start runs on.
