The only other assignment of `personaConfig` is a confirmed apply's step 1 (the reload controller's `onApplied`), which sets it to `configInEffect(appliedConfig, confirmed)`: `appliedConfig` with the confirmed persona set and the confirmed `allow_invited_channels` switch, the one server-wide setting applied in place (b.deo SRI-201; every consumer reads the mode through `channelModeOf(personaConfig)` at each use). `appliedConfig` is declared (`let appliedConfig!: PersonaConfig`) before `createReloadController`, so `onApplied`'s closure never depends on declaration order, and is assigned right after the start resolves; an `onApplied` that ran before that throws (`a confirmed apply ran before the start resolved its configuration`) and the controller logs it, rather than building a config without the start-time values. Detection is armed only after the start bring-up, so this is not expected. The start bring-up (step 5) also reads `appliedConfig`, launching over `configInEffect(appliedConfig, <the controller's applied config>)`, and its guard throws the same way while it is unset (`the start bring-up ran before the start resolved its configuration`). The Stop-hook start pass, the reply-guard getter, the bring-up controller's applied set and the launch after a bring-up retry all read `personaConfig` at call time, so they see the applied set as it stands. It then installs `trustPatchPersona` as the session manager's pre-launch trust patcher (`setPreLaunchTrustPatcher`) and `preLaunchReplyGuard` as its pre-launch reply guard (`setPreLaunchReplyGuard`, bound to `STATE_DIR` and the applied persona set), ahead of the Slack connections, `Bun.serve` and `initRestart`, so no launch path runs unpatched, and logs `[slack] Loaded persona config: <N> persona(s)`. `bind` and `port` come from the applied config. After a start from the record, the detection tick's first pass (step 9) compares `config.json` with the record per SR-8.3 (b.av2 SR-8.7 as amended by b.deo SRI-403, SRI-407), so an unconfirmed edit, destructive or not, stays pending and `config.json.pending` is written after the start; it is never applied at the start. A confirmation (`config.json.apply`) left while the server was down is processed by that first pass (see [Confirmation](#confirmation-sr-85)); the start itself never reads it.
2a-bis. **The stored-choice store (b.av2 SR-8.7 as amended by b.deo SRI-403, SRI-407)** — in the statement right after `appliedConfig` is set, behind no branch (so in both modes and in dry run too) and before the first await that follows, `main()` calls `loadChannelDeliveryAtStart(STATE_DIR, { applied, retiredKeys }, { log })` (`src/channel-delivery.ts`) once: `applied` is each applied persona's key with its declaration (`channelDeliveryDeclarationOf`), and `retiredKeys` is the retired-key store step 2 loaded, seen only through `ChannelDeliveryRetiredKeyView`. It reads `channel-delivery.json` once, uncapped, and runs the start rules right after the read, dropping the choices of keys that are not applied, whose declaration changed, or that the retired-key record holds without its mark; the writer, the durable delete and the clock are the store's defaults. A file that cannot be read, parsed or validated is the store's own unreadable state and its one `channel-delivery-unreadable` line, never a stop: the start goes on and runs every persona. The store is bound to the module-scope holder `channelDeliveryStore`, the server's one store, which the persona routing (`getChannelDelivery`, read at each event), the session tools (`SessionToolDeps.getChannelDelivery`, read at each call) and the reload controller (`ReloadControllerDeps.channelDelivery`, whose accessor throws `a confirmed apply ran before the start loaded the stored-choice store` while the holder is unset) all read at call time; nothing else in `src/` builds one (see Configuration, [channel-delivery.json](#channel-deliveryjson-state_dirchannel-deliveryjson)). Since it comes before the connection manager, `Bun.serve`, the PID file, the start sweep and the start bring-up pass, no event, tool call or apply runs before the store is in place.
2a-ter. **The crontable's default location (bug b.avm)** — in the statements right after step 2a-bis's stored-choice load, behind no branch (so in dry run too) and before the first await that follows, `main()` calls `prepareDefaultCronTable` (`src/cron-table-migration.ts`) once, over `inEffect` (the start-time configuration's `cron_table_path`), `defaulted` (its `cron_table_path_defaulted === true`, so a configuration without the flag is never prepared), `defaultPath` (`resolveDefaultCronTablePath(dirname(CONFIG_PATH))`) and `legacyPath` (`legacyCronTablePath(dirname(CONFIG_PATH))`), the resolvers the loader used, with the OS home and `process.env`, and only a log (`console.error`), so on the real file system. When the configuration left `cron_table_path` out and the default is not the old path, it creates the default's directory and moves a crontable left at the old path, leaving a symbolic link there (see [Location and the start's move](#location-and-the-starts-move-bug-bavm) under Scheduled Prompts). `cronTablePathForStart` over its outcome names the crontable the start runs on: the old path when a step failed before the file was at the new path, otherwise the configuration's. When that differs from `personaConfig.cron_table_path`, `main()` sets `personaConfig` to a copy with only `cron_table_path` replaced, and `appliedConfig` to the same, so the scheduler, the dispatcher and every launch's `CSCB_CRONTABLE_PATH` name it (the start bring-up's through `configInEffect(appliedConfig, <the controller's applied config>)`, step 5; every later launch's through `personaConfig`), and a confirmed apply keeps it (`configInEffect` keeps `appliedConfig`'s server-wide settings). The reload controller's applied configuration is left as resolved, still naming the default as `config.json` does, so detection sees no `cron_table_path` change and the fallback alone raises no pending change. So all of this comes before the start sweep, the start bring-up, whose launches take `CSCB_CRONTABLE_PATH` from the same path, and the scheduler's bootstrap in `cronScheduler.start()`. It never throws: each failure is one logged line, and the start goes on (a crontable the scheduler then cannot create or read is the scheduler's own line). `tests/cron-scheduler-wiring.test.ts` pins its place, its arguments and the override; `tests/reload-wiring.test.ts` and `tests/server-startup-wiring.test.ts` accept the override as the start's one other assignment of the applied and start-time configuration, located by `cronTableStartOverride` (`tests/test-helpers/source-audit.ts`).
2b. **agent-director's timing settings (b.jg5 SRJ-209)** — right after step 2a-ter's crontable preparation, behind no branch and before step 3, `main()` calls `installAdSettings()` (`src/ad-settings.ts`) once, in dry run too. So the startup read comes after the startup gate has passed and the start has resolved its configuration, and before the start pass. It reads `~/.agent-director/config.toml` under the server process's HOME, never a HOME from the configuration or a persona, applies agent-director's rule and registers the re-read on the runtime version re-check's tick hook, so the file is read again at each tick, `AD_VERSION_RECHECK_INTERVAL_MS` (120 s) apart, with no timer of its own (see [Health-Check Poller](#health-check-poller)). Its outcome never stops the start: an accepted read (a missing file included) logs the nine `[tmux]` values in effect, and a refused read writes one log line and leaves the defaults in effect (see [agent-director settings lines](#agent-director-settings-lines-bjg5-srj-209)). See `ad-settings.ts` in the Module Map and [agent-director config.toml](#agent-director-configtoml-agent-directorconfigtoml).
2c. **The call timeout (b.jg5 SRJ-213)** — right after step 2b, behind no branch (dry run too) and before step 3 and the start pass, `main()` awaits `_runCallTimeoutStartStep(appliedConfig)` once, with the start-time configuration. It takes `agent_director_call_timeout_ms` from it (`agentDirectorCallTimeoutMsOf`, the default when absent) and first runs the startup check (`checkAdCallTimeoutAtStartup`) against the values step 2b left in effect: at most one warning line, never a refusal. It then builds the persona client with that call timeout (`buildPersonaClientOrExit`, see `agent-director-startup.ts` in the Module Map): the gate's client is closed once and the new one installed as the singleton, before step 3's `makeTemplate`, so every later agent-director call the server makes carries the configured timeout. A later confirmed change to the setting takes effect at the next start. A construct failure or floor refusal of that client records one startup error and exits non-zero, as the gate does. `main()` then returns if a shutdown began during the await.
3. **SR-3.2 template refresh** — `installSlackChannelBotTemplate(personaConfig)` builds the SR-3.1 `MakeTemplateParams` and calls `client.makeTemplate({ ..., overwrite: true })`. Atomic replacement is the library's responsibility (sibling-tempfile + `rename(2)`). Fatal on rejection. It runs right after step 2c, over the loaded persona config, and keeps the params it installed for the apply-time refresh. That refresh (apply step 5, see [Template refresh](#template-refresh-bav2-sr-86-step-5-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-805)) rewrites only the memory-read rules and is not fatal.
4. **b.av2 SR-6.3 start sweep, as amended by b.jg5 SRJ-1506 (b.jg5 SRJ-714)** — `reconcileOrphans(personaConfig, KILL_RETRY_SYSTEM_CLOCK, () => shuttingDown)`, run before the trust patch and any spawn, and only while no shutdown has begun. It deletes no row: every row is read, live strays are killed with the result checked, a finished row is never killed, and pre-persona and absent-persona rows are kept and never resumed until agent-director's `expire` removes them. `client.list({ label: ['service=cscb'] })` is its one `list` (b.av2 SR-6.3, b.jg5 SRJ-116, SRJ-714): the service label only, so every CSCB row in every state is listed. The sweep then runs, in this order, with every latch and record decision made over the whole list before the first kill:

    - **4.1 The list failure.** A `list` that throws records one `orphan-cleanup-list-failed` entry (`ORPHAN_CLEANUP_LIST_FAILED_LABEL`) (`failed to list spawns for orphan reconciliation: <failure>`) and the sweep returns at once: nothing is latched, recorded, cleared or killed, no findMissing runs, no summary line is logged, and the start pass goes on.
    - **4.2 The latch pass (`latchFromListedRows`; b.jg5 SRJ-116, SRJ-501, SRJ-502, SRJ-504, SRJ-513).** Each listed row whose id is a key's own (`cscb_<key>`), whatever its `persona` label, goes through the shared own-row read's act step (`actOnOwnRowRead`, the same one `readPersonaOwnRow` applies to its `get` row; see [Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)) at the site `START_SWEEP_LIST_SITE` (`reconcileOrphans: start sweep list`). A configured persona whose own row reads `pending` with no launch start latches with `launch-start-not-recorded` (also when the row carries `provenance_conflict`), and one whose own row carries `provenance_conflict` otherwise latches with `conflicting-labels`, with the state the row was listed in; the notice is posted once per latch episode, so after a restart, which drops every latch, the start's list latches the persona again with one post (AC 45's list half). A row with any other id latches no one, a row labelled P with another id included. A configured persona already latched when the sweep runs (`latchGateReadingOf`) is held the same way. For each such persona its own row and every row labelled with it, in any state, are left as they are for the whole pass, ahead of `sweepDecision`, the pre-persona rule and the directory-broken deferral, a `cwd` or `config_dir` other than the persona's included (`startSweepLatchOf`; b.jg5 SRJ-502, AC 55); they are counted in `OrphanReconcileResult.leftForLatch`. One line per persona, after the act step's own lines: `[slack] reconcileOrphans: <ref> latched from its own listed row instanceId=<id> (case=<case>) — its own row and every row labelled with it are left unkilled (b.jg5 SRJ-116, SRJ-502, SRJ-714)`, or, for one already latched, `[slack] reconcileOrphans: <ref> is latched (case=<case>) — its own row and every row labelled with it are left unkilled (b.jg5 SRJ-502, SRJ-714)`.
    - **4.3 The clear at list rows (b.jg5 SRJ-807).** The same act step applies the row-read rule's clear decision, with `retiredMarked` read from the installed store: a key recorded with its mark set whose own row is listed live other than `pending` has its entry cleared ([The retired-key entry clear](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)). A key step 4.4 records is the exception (the act step's `clearRetiredEntry` passed false): its recording clears the mark instead, so the key gets one write.
    - **4.4 The recording (`recordAbsentPersonaKeys`; b.jg5 SRJ-714; b.jg5 SRJ-803 as amended by b.deo SRI-408).** After the latch pass and before the first kill, one `record` call through the installed store (`RetiredKeyStore.record`, `src/retired-keys.ts`, the only writer) records the `persona` label value of every listed row, in any state, that names no persona of the applied configuration (`absentPersonaKeysOf`; a pre-persona row gives no key), each with the cause `absent-at-start`; the keys are counted in `OrphanReconcileResult.recordedAsRetired`. The store's batch rules apply: a new key gets its entry, a marked key has its mark cleared, an unmarked recorded key writes nothing unless it is held only in memory. The store logs the write and its failure ([Retired-key record lines](#retired-key-record-lines-bjg5-srj-1013-srj-1014)); a failed write leaves the file as it was while the store holds those keys as retired in memory for the server's life (`isHeldInMemory`), so a persona re-added before the next start is never resumed (SRJ-805) and the apply that re-adds it writes the record first (SRJ-803 as amended by b.deo SRI-408); the sweep goes on to its kills, with no `orphan-cleanup` entry, and they still count as recorded (hatch A3). The next start records them again. No store installed records nothing and logs `[slack] reconcileOrphans: no retired-key store is installed, so the keys of absent personas' rows are not recorded as retired: <keys> (b.jg5 SRJ-714, SRJ-803)`; a `record` that throws logs `[slack] reconcileOrphans: recording the keys of absent personas' rows as retired failed: <error>; nothing is recorded (b.jg5 SRJ-714, SRJ-803)`; both count 0. No dialog approver needs stopping (SRJ-808): none runs before the bring-up.
    - **4.4a The listing's old-life holds (`beginStartSweepListingHolds`; b.jg5 SRJ-809, SRJ-714).** Right after the recording and before the first kill, every row listed live (`pending` included) whose `persona` label key the installed store answers as recorded without the "new life has begun" mark (a key 4.4 just recorded, or holds only in memory, included) begins an old-life hold on its `cwd`, cause `start-sweep-listing`, old key `oldLifeKeyOf` (the label, or the instance id when it is not the label's `cscb_<key>`), whatever 4.5 then does with the row: kill it, keep it or leave it for a latch. A finished row, an unlabelled row, and a row whose key is not recorded or is marked get none. This is how a restart rebuilds apply step 1's holds, a destructive modify's same-key old life the sweep keeps included. Right after these begins, and still before the first kill, each listed row is also a read for the holds, through the one read entry (`noteOldLifeRowRead` at `START_SWEEP_LIST_SITE`; b.jg5 SRJ-809, SRJ-811): a row listed `ended` or `missing` ends a hold on it, and a live row's `cwd` re-points one and its state seeds the hold's last read, so the hold's first wait is seeded with the state the row was listed in, a 4.4a hold's included ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809)). So a same-key row listed `pending` gets its first wait seeded `pending`, and while `ad-config-malformed` is raised for the old key or a waiting persona that wait makes no kill of it (SRJ-316) and its round ends `config-malformed-no-kill`.
    - **4.5 The kills (`sweepListedRow`, `killStartSweepRow`; b.jg5 SRJ-714, SRJ-1506).** Row by row in list order, of the rows step 4.2 left, each judged by its `persona` label against the applied personas, as below. A stray (a pre-persona row, or a labelled row `sweepDecision` sweeps) is killed only when it is listed live (`AGENT_DIRECTOR_LIVE_STATES`, `pending` included); a stray listed `ended` or `missing` gets no call and is kept, since a finished row is never killed. A swept `pending` row with no launch start is killed like any live stray, with no wait (b.jg5 SRJ-408): the kill ends no session for it, and step 4.6's run judges it by agent-director's ordinary rules. **No row is deleted, whatever its kill's outcome** (HO C2, C17; AC 77): a deleted row whose kill may have failed would leave a live session with nothing to find it by. Pre-persona rows and absent personas' rows are kept and never resumed, and agent-director's `expire` removes them later. **A kill that did not succeed holds the row's directory (`beginStartSweepKillHold`; b.jg5 SRJ-809, SRJ-714, SRJ-1506).** A row whose record is `SWEEP_ROW_KILL_FAILED` (every non-success class, CONFLICT and UNUSABLE NAME included) begins an old-life hold on its `cwd`, cause `start-sweep-kill-not-succeeded`, old key `oldLifeKeyOf`: an absent persona's row, a live pre-persona row, a row swept for its instance id and one swept for its `cwd` alike; a row 4.4a already holds keeps that one hold. When the kill's tries decided the ordinary kill-failure alert and were not stopped, the hold is marked kill-failed (SRJ-812). A kill that succeeded begins and marks nothing. These are SRJ-1506's two working-directory holds, with 4.4a's: until each ends, no persona in the held directory is launched, no MCP session from it is admitted and nothing is typed into the old life ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809), **What a hold refuses**). Once the sweep has stopped (`sweepStopped`: a shutdown or a re-check's stop) no hold begins or is marked, and a between-try read that settles after the stop ends none.
    - **4.6 The post-kill findMissing** (`runStartSweepPostKillFindMissing`; below). A row in its `ids` ends its old-life hold, unless the sweep stopped while the run was under way.
    - **4.7 The summary line** (`startSweepSummaryLine`; below).

    **Pre-persona rows (b.1ix).** A row with no `persona` label was spawned by a build that predates persona labels (instance IDs `cscb_<name>_<channel>`). No persona's `cscb_<key>` is ever such an ID, so no launch resumes or reuses it and keeping it is harmless; each persona's first launch spawns fresh (the old transcripts stay on disk, unresumed). A live one is a stray, killed with its result checked and kept (**Checked sweep kills**, below); an `ended` or `missing` one gets no call and no line.

    **Swept rows.** A labelled row is a stray when any of these holds, checked in this order (`sweepDecision`):
    - its `persona` label names a persona absent from the applied set (`absent persona`; its key was recorded in step 4.4);
    - its instance ID is not that persona's `cscb_<key>` (`wrong instance ID`);
    - its `cwd` differs from that persona's working directory by real path (`wrong cwd`, via `compareRowToPersona`).

    Every other row is kept for Server-Managed Startup step 5. **Unresolvable working directory (b.av2 SR-6.4).** When the persona's working directory has no real path (missing, not searchable, a dangling symlink) and the row's `cwd` has no real path either or equals the configured `working_directory` lexically (`compareRowToPersona`'s `cwdCheckDeferred`), the `cwd` condition cannot be evaluated and is deferred: the row is kept (the other conditions still apply), with one line per persona, `[slack] reconcileOrphans: persona "<name>" (key=<key>) working_directory="<path>" cannot be resolved to a real path — keeping its rows; the cwd check is deferred to its launch`. Such a persona is not up (`retrying`, or `broken` when its credentials also fail; Server-Managed Startup step 5), so its instance keeps running, unserved (Connection step 3, Permission Relay, `/interject`), and its row waits for the launch that follows the directory's return, where the ladder's `cwd` guard runs against the real path. A row whose `cwd` resolves to an existing directory elsewhere is swept as `wrong cwd` even while the working directory is missing, so a persona can't adopt another persona's directory; its launch then spawns fresh. A row whose `cwd` differs by real path from a resolvable working directory is swept as `wrong cwd` too. A `channel` label left on a row by an older spawn plays no part. Each swept row logs `[slack] reconcileOrphans: sweeping row (<reason>) persona=<persona> instanceId=<id> state=<state> — <what> (b.jg5 SRJ-714)`, with ` cwd=<row cwd>` before the dash for `wrong cwd`; `<persona>` is `"<name>" (key=<key>)` for an applied persona and the raw label value for an absent one, and `<what>` is `it is live, so it is killed; the row is kept` or `it is finished, so it is not killed (a finished row is never killed); the row is kept`.

    **Checked sweep kills (b.jg5 SRJ-110, SRJ-701, SRJ-714).** Each live stray, swept or pre-persona, gets one kill step (`killStartSweepRow`), which logs `[slack] reconcileOrphans: killing <row> state=<state> tmux_session=<session>; the row is kept whatever the outcome (b.jg5 SRJ-714)` and then makes the checked kill on the sweep's own client through the bounded retry (`sweepKill`, below). `<row>` is `orphan instanceId=<id> persona=<persona>` for a swept row and `pre-persona row instanceId=<id>` for a pre-persona row. The row is kept whatever the outcome:
    - **A success that stands** (any `kill_sent`, `ErrSpawnNotFound`, GONE, or a read between tries that found the row finished) logs `[slack] reconcileOrphans: kill succeeded for <row> (<outcome>) — row kept`, `<outcome>` being `describeKillOutcome`'s rendering, `kill_sent` included. The row counts as killed, a success after a survivor-naming failure included, which also writes the survivor entry (below).
    - **Any other outcome** counts the row as kept and kill-failed and records one `orphan-cleanup` entry (`startSweepKillFailedEntry`) naming the row, its listed state, its session and the outcome that stands with its class: `kill did not succeed for <row> state=<state> tmux_session=<session>: <outcome>; row kept, its session may still be running`, followed by the ordinary alert's tail when the retry decided it (below). Every class is recorded this way. A CONFLICT or an UNUSABLE NAME answer is routed so (b.jg5 SRJ-1002) and latches no one, a configured persona's own row included. An ENVIRONMENT answer raises `tmux-unavailable`, and a CONFIG answer `ad-config-malformed`, only for a row whose `persona` label names a persona in the applied configuration, and only when it is the outcome that stands (hatch A3); for an absent persona's row and a pre-persona row they are only logged and recorded.

    The start sweep is no launch or recovery attempt: no sweep kill latches anything, arms a retry timer, starts the `tmux-unresponsive` condition or feeds an unclassified-error episode. **The sweep's kill retries (b.jg5 SRJ-702, AC 56, AC 84).** Every sweep kill runs through the bounded retry ([Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104), **The bounded kill retry**) on the clock `reconcileOrphans` is handed, seeded with the live state the sweep listed the row in: up to `KILL_RETRY_TRIES` (3) tries `KILL_RETRY_SPACING_MS` (2 s) apart on UNAVAILABLE. Each pass builds one pass budget, so once one row's kill has used its `KILL_RETRY_TRIES` tries with UNAVAILABLE standing, every later kill in that pass (swept or pre-persona) is made once, and a wedged tmux delays the start pass by at most one row's tries; the try line then says the pass's retries are spent. The retry's keep-going check is the sweep's shutdown query (**The stops**, below). Before each further try the sweep makes one bare `status` read of the row on its own client (`sweepKillRead`), outside the outage wrappers. It latches nothing (the sweep latches only from its `list`; an UNUSABLE NAME answer is a failed read). Of the row-read rule it applies the retired-key entry clear alone (b.jg5 SRJ-807): when the row's id is a key's own (`cscb_<key>`, configured or not), a read live other than `pending` of a key recorded with its mark set clears that key's entry (`decideRetiredEntryClear` with the installed store's mark, then the store's `clear`), the clear line naming the site `START_SWEEP_KILL_STATUS_SITE` (`reconcileOrphans: status read between kill tries`), unless the sweep has stopped by the time the read returns. The read answers the same whatever the clear did. A CONFIG answer there raises `ad-config-malformed` for the row's configured persona through its raise entry, arming nothing, unless the sweep has stopped by then (**The stops**, below), and for any other row is only logged (`[slack] reconcileOrphans: the status read between kill tries for instanceId=<id> answered CONFIG; the row names no persona of the applied configuration, so no outage is raised — logged only (b.jg5 SRJ-110, SRJ-316)`); either way the tries end when the last state read (the listed state, or a later read's) is `pending`, and go ahead otherwise. Each try and read logs its line with the `[slack] reconcileOrphans` prefix. **The kill-failure alert's entries (b.jg5 SRJ-704, SRJ-714, SRJ-1007).** The retry's alert decision is written with the start sweep's context and its log-only closing sentence, for the row's own session and id (a pre-persona row's id as it is): after a kill that did not succeed, the ordinary version's text (decided for an `ErrTmuxKillFailed` that stands, or for any failure after a survivor-naming one) is appended to the kill's `orphan-cleanup` entry as `; kill-failure alert: instanceId=<id> (start sweep): <text>` (`sweepOrdinaryAlertTail`; the entry is unchanged when the decision is not `ordinary`); after a success that stands, the survivor version is one `persona-kill-survivor` entry, `instanceId=<id> (start sweep): <text>` (`recordSweepSurvivorAlert`). The sweep acts for no persona, so even a configured persona's row gets no post, no kill-failure episode, no retry timer and no latch ([The kill-failure alert](#the-kill-failure-alert-bjg5-srj-704-srj-1007)). A kill whose tries a stop ended writes neither (**The stops**, below).

    **4.6 The post-kill findMissing (b.jg5 SRJ-714, SRJ-120).** `kill` never changes a row's state, so a killed row would still read live at every later start and be killed again each time. After the last kill, when at least one kill was made and no stop came first, the sweep runs one findMissing over every row it gave a kill, swept and pre-persona alike, whatever each kill's outcome (a failed kill's session may be gone all the same, and only the run would tell) (`runStartSweepPostKillFindMissing`): a killed row whose session is gone then reads `missing`, and later starts leave it alone. It is an ordinary run of the memoized, single-flight core every `findMissing` caller shares (`sharedFindMissingSweep`, b.m4r, b.jg5 SRJ-120; see the b.m4r note under Server-Managed Startup step 5); the start sweep runs before any launch or health check, so the run is a fresh one, and the launches right after reuse it within its 10 s window. The call goes to the start sweep's client directly, like its list and kills, so the call raises or clears no persona's outage flag. As after any run the server makes, each configured persona's own row listed in `unverified_ids` is then read with one `get` through that persona's `withOutageDetection` (the shared own-row read), and a `provenance_conflict` note there, or the persona's own row reading `pending` with no launch start (b.jg5 SRJ-513), latches the persona. The run is the start sweep's (`startSweepRun`), so an UNUSABLE_NAME answer to one of those `get`s latches nothing (b.jg5 SRJ-512): it is routed to the server log (b.jg5 SRJ-1002) with `[slack] reconcileOrphans: post-sweep get for persona=<key>: <failure> — UNUSABLE NAME met in the start sweep: routed to the server log; nothing latches (b.jg5 SRJ-512, SRJ-1002)` and shows as `refused (<failure>)` in the `get`s' line (see the b.m4r note under Server-Managed Startup step 5). Those `get`s are made only while no shutdown has begun when the run returns (`postRunGetsGo`), and one that settles after a shutdown began is not acted on (**The stops**, below). No other row is read. After the run's own `[slack] reconcileOrphans: findMissing sweep for the rows the start sweep killed — count=<n> ids=[…] unverified=<n> unverified_ids=[…]` line (and the `get`s' line, when a row was read) comes `startSweepPostKillLine`: `[slack] reconcileOrphans: findMissing after the kills of <n> row(s): missing=<n> [<ids>] still-live=<n> [<ids>] not-judged=<n> [<ids>] — a row that still reads live is killed again by the next start's sweep when it sweeps it; a not-judged row was pending and not judged by this run (retry later)`. Each row given a kill is read with `readFindMissingRow` and the state the start sweep listed it with: `missing` holds the rows marked missing; `not-judged` the `pending` rows in neither list, which agent-director did not judge (retry later, never a reason to escalate, alert or kill); `still-live` the rest, judged and left live (in `unverified_ids`) or judged alive. The line is a log only: the start sweep's kill decisions do not depend on it. A failed run logs its failure line and `startSweepPostKillFailedLine`, `[slack] reconcileOrphans: findMissing after the kills of <n> row(s) failed — each reads as it did, and a live one is killed again by the next start's sweep when it sweeps it`; the sweep goes on to its summary.

    **4.7 The summary line (b.jg5 SRJ-714).** Every sweep that listed its rows ends with one line, a sweep a stop ended included: `[slack] reconcileOrphans: summary — listed=<n> killed=<n> kept=<n> (kill-failed=<n>) recorded-as-retired=<n> left-unkilled-for-latch=<n> (b.jg5 SRJ-714)` (`startSweepSummaryLine`). Each listed row is counted once, so `listed` is `killed` + `kept` + `left-unkilled-for-latch`. `killed` counts the kills whose success stands (`ErrSpawnNotFound` and a success after a survivor-naming failure included); `kept` the listed rows neither killed nor left for a latch (finished strays, rows that match their persona, directory-deferred rows, rows given a kill that did not succeed, and rows a stop left unreached), with `kill-failed` the rows given a kill that did not succeed, a kill a stop ended included; `recorded-as-retired` every key step 4.4's batch named (an already-recorded key, and keys held only in memory after a failed write, included; 0 with no store installed); `left-unkilled-for-latch` the rows step 4.2 left for a latch. `OrphanReconcileResult` (`listed`, `killed`, `kept`, `killFailed`, `recordedAsRetired`, `leftForLatch`) returns the same counts. The sweep keeps one record per listed row (`SweepRowRecord`: the row as listed, what it did with it, and its kill's result), from which the counts and step 4.6's rows are taken. A list failure (step 4.1) and dry run log no summary line.

    **The stops (b.jg5 SRJ-205, SRJ-702, SRJ-714).** *A shutdown.* `reconcileOrphans`' third argument is the server's shutdown query (`main()` passes `() => shuttingDown`; with none, nothing counts as shutting down, and a query that throws counts as shutting down). It is asked once the `list` returns, before each row, as the bounded retry's keep-going check (before each further try and read), when a between-try read returns (before its entry clear and its CONFIG answer's raise), when a kill's tries end (before its ENVIRONMENT or CONFIG answer's raise), before the findMissing run, before its post-run `get`s, as each of those `get`s settles (before its act step) and at the sweep's end, before its summary. Once it answers true the sweep makes no further agent-director call (`kill`, a `status` read, `find-missing`, `get`) and no further latch, record write, clear or outage raise, an answer that arrives after it included; what it has done stands, and the rows it has not reached count as kept. It logs one line, `START_SWEEP_SHUTDOWN_STOP_LINE`, once per sweep: `[slack] reconcileOrphans: the server began shutting down — the sweep stops: no further kill, status read, findMissing or get, and no further latch, record write or clear; what it did stands, and the rows it left unkilled count as kept (b.jg5 SRJ-714, SRJ-205)`, then its summary line. A shutdown begun during a findMissing run that then fails, or during its post-run `get`s, is logged the same way, the stop line before the summary (`endStartSweep`). *No answer is acted on after a stop.* Once the sweep has stopped (a shutdown begun, or a version re-check's stop; `sweepStopped`), an ENVIRONMENT or CONFIG answer to a kill, or a CONFIG answer to a between-try `status` read, for a configured persona's row raises no outage (`tmux-unavailable`, `ad-config-malformed`): one line instead, `[slack] reconcileOrphans: the <class> answer to the <call> for persona=<key> came after the sweep stopped — no outage is raised (b.jg5 SRJ-714)` (`<call>` is `kill` or `status read between kill tries`). A between-try read that returns after the stop makes no entry clear. A post-run `get` that settles after a shutdown began is not acted on (`OwnRowReadSite.actGoes`, the starter's `postRunGetsGo` asked as each `get` settles): no latch, no clear and no episode end, nothing posted, and one line, `[slack] reconcileOrphans: post-sweep get for persona=<key>: the get settled after its caller stopped — not acted on: no latch, clear or episode end (b.jg5 SRJ-714)`; the `get`s' line shows that persona as `persona=<key> not acted on (its caller stopped)`. A shutdown begun by the time the `list` returns means no latch pass, no record and no kill: every listed row counts as kept. A kill whose tries the shutdown stopped is recorded with the outcome that stands in its `orphan-cleanup` entry, with no alert text and no `persona-kill-survivor` entry: `kill did not succeed for <row> state=<state> tmux_session=<session>: <outcome>; its tries were stopped because the server is shutting down, so no kill-failure alert is raised; row kept, its session may still be running`. It also logs one line, `startSweepStoppedKillLine` with the cause `START_SWEEP_KILL_STOP_SHUTDOWN`, which quotes the retry decision's descriptions (`describeKillFailureDescriptions`), the latest survivor-naming one included when a try returned one: `[slack] reconcileOrphans: kill tries for <row> (start sweep) were stopped: the server is shutting down; its last outcome's class: <class>; no kill-failure alert is raised; <descriptions> (b.jg5 SRJ-702, SRJ-714)`. When the shutdown begins while the findMissing run is under way, its post-run `get`s are not made: the stop line, then `[slack] reconcileOrphans: after the findMissing sweep for the rows the start sweep killed — no post-sweep get is made: its caller stopped (b.jg5 SRJ-120, SRJ-714)`, then the post-kill line and the summary. A row that a stopped kill left live is killed and checked again by the next start's sweep, when that sweep sweeps it, and alerted on there as SRJ-704 says. *A version re-check stop.* A kill whose `ErrInvalidFlags` re-check decides that the server stops (`stop.stopping`) is recorded as a kill a shutdown stopped: the same one line, `startSweepStoppedKillLine` with the re-check's cause `START_SWEEP_KILL_STOP_RECHECK`, quoting the latest survivor-naming description the same way, `[slack] reconcileOrphans: kill tries for <row> (start sweep) were stopped: the version re-check decided that the server stops; row kept; the sweep makes no further call; its last outcome's class: <class>; no kill-failure alert is raised; <descriptions> (b.jg5 SRJ-702, SRJ-714, SRJ-205)`, and its `orphan-cleanup` entry with no alert text (the `recheck=stop` rendering shows in its `<outcome>`) and no `persona-kill-survivor` entry, counted kept and kill-failed. Nothing is posted. That line is its stop line: no `START_SWEEP_SHUTDOWN_STOP_LINE` is logged for it. No later row is killed (each counts as kept) and no findMissing follows; the summary line is still logged. Either way, once the latch pass has run, a latched persona's rows still count as left for its latch, and no stop blocks startup.

    A list failure records `orphan-cleanup-list-failed` (step 4.1). Dry run skips the sweep and logs `[slack] dry-run: skipping orphan reconciliation`.
4a-bis. **b.uhv / b.k54 trust-bootstrap** — `trustBootstrap(personaConfig)` (from `src/trust-bootstrap.ts`) runs over the applied personas: for each persona's working directory it patches the `.claude.json` in the persona's effective `claude_config_dir` (its own, else the top-level one) so the Claude Code trust-folder dialog never appears at launch. Each persona is patched once, however many channels it lists. It reads `<dir>/.claude.json` and ensures `projects[<working_directory>].hasTrustDialogAccepted` and `projects[<working_directory>].hasCompletedProjectOnboarding` are both `true`. Idempotent: when both flags are already `true` the file is not rewritten (verifiable via unchanged `mtime`). Writes are atomic (`.tmp` + `renameSync`), and the read-modify-write is fully synchronous, so two personas sharing one config dir cannot lose each other's update. Soft-skip behavior: a persona with no configured `claude_config_dir` logs `[slack] trust-bootstrap: "<name>" (key=<key>) has no claude_config_dir — skipping` and continues without recording an error (Claude uses its own default; there is nothing to patch). A missing or unreadable `.claude.json` logs an info line and calls `recordStartupError('trust-bootstrap-config-missing', '"<name>" (key=<key>): cannot read <path>')` — the file is never auto-created. Malformed JSON records `trust-bootstrap-config-parse`, and any unexpected per-persona failure records `trust-bootstrap` (`unexpected error for "<name>" (key=<key>) cwd=<dir>`). The function never throws to the caller, so one bad persona cannot block the rest. Runs in both real and dry-run modes — it's a config-file patch, not a session operation. The call site is in `main()` right after step 4 (`reconcileOrphans`), before any spawn fires; like steps 4a-quater and 4a-ter, it is not started once a shutdown has begun (b.jg5 SRJ-205).

    - **Per-launch patch (b.av2 SR-6.2).** The same patch also runs before every launch: `trustPatchPersona(persona)`, installed as the pre-launch trust patcher, runs at the top of every ladder run — fresh spawn, resume or restart (see step 5 and Auto-Restart step 5). At launch time a patch failure is logged only, as `[slack] trust-bootstrap: pre-launch patch failed [<class>] <detail> — <cause>` with the same class names, and never adds a `startup-errors.log` entry; a missing `.claude.json` therefore logs two lines (the info line and the failure line). The start pass records failures as described above.
4a-quater. **b.zak JSONL-persistence safeguard** — `runJsonlPersistenceSafeguard(personaConfig, notify)` (from `src/jsonl-persistence-check.ts`), run over the applied personas. Call site: `main()` in `server.ts`, immediately after step 4a-bis (`trustBootstrap`) and before step 4a-ter (`stopHookBootstrap`) — critically, **before** step 5's resume path, which brings a memory-less bot up fresh by a reuse spawn of the same id when `resume` throws `ErrJsonlMissing`. Detection/reporting only: it never changes resume behavior, never throws, and never blocks startup (wrapped in its own `try/catch` at the call site as well). Every warning is a persona notice: the server passes the per-persona notifier's `notify`, which posts to the affected persona's destination, names the persona, and only logs in dry run. Sibling scope: the lost / never-created / inconclusive classification inside the resume path itself is **b.wrb / b.fwu**, not this module. Two layers:

    - **Layer 1 — non-persistent storage.** `checkJsonlPersistence` resolves the deduped set of the personas' effective `<claude_config_dir>/projects` roots (a persona with no configured dir uses `<home>/.claude`; with no personas at all, the home default root is checked) and classifies each root's mount fstype by longest-prefix match over `/proc/self/mountinfo` (string-prefix, not a stat — a not-yet-created dir classifies by its parent mount). A root on `tmpfs`/`ramfs` → `recordStartupError('jsonl-non-persistent', …)` plus one notice through the notifier to each affected persona's destination — those whose effective JSONL root is the flagged root, not every persona (resume is structurally impossible for those personas on this host). An undeterminable fstype (unreadable/unparseable/unresolvable) → `recordStartupError('jsonl-persistence-check-warning', …)`, no notice.
    - **Layer 2 — per-persona transcript loss.** For each applied persona it fetches the persona's AD row (through `withOutageDetection`, the sanctioned CSCB→AD entry point). A row the collision ladder will replace instead of resuming — its `cwd` differs from the persona's working directory by real path, or its `config_dir` label is missing or mismatched (`compareRowToPersona`, the same check as step 5's guards) — is not checked: one log line naming the persona, the mismatch (the row's `cwd` against the working directory, or the missing or changed `config_dir` label) and that the transcript was not checked because the collision ladder will replace the row, with no record and no notice. Otherwise, when the row carries a `claude_session_id`, it stats the AD-recorded `jsonl_path` **and** a config-dir-aware fallback path composed the same way agent-director composes it (`resolveJsonlPath`, under the persona's effective config dir). Outcomes: persisted exists → healthy, silent. Persisted stale/missing but fallback exists → `recordStartupError('jsonl-transcript-stale-path', …)` + a notice through the notifier to that persona's destination (history is on disk but AD 0.8.0's resume only stats the persisted path, so it would throw `ErrJsonlMissing` and wipe the persona's memory). Both missing → the `message_archive_db` archive (when configured) is consulted for evidence under the b.av2 SR-7.4 rule (as amended by b.deo SRI-704; `personaArchiveEvidenceScope`): only messages in the persona's `delivery: all` channels since `started_at` count, in one query over all of them. A persona with no `delivery: all` channel counts 0 without the archive being opened (even when none is configured), and since every persona has a channel or DMs on, that persona always takes (once `started_at` parses) the unattributable-zero path below. A count ≥1 → `recordStartupError('jsonl-transcript-lost', …)` + a notice to that persona's destination saying its conversation memory has been lost (conversation provably happened, transcript is gone). A zero count for a persona with any `delivery: mentions` channel or DMs on is not evidence of idleness, because the archive cannot attribute messages from `mentions` channels or DMs to a persona: one quiet log line saying the archive evidence is inconclusive (`UNATTRIBUTABLE_ZERO_REASON`), no record and no notice. That `delivery: all` scope is declarative mode's. In fungible mode (the mode read with `channelModeOf(config)` from the configuration Layer 2 is given; b.deo SRI-704) the scope counts no channel and a zero is never attributable, since the configuration cannot predict which channels a persona serves: whatever count is given is taken as an unattributable zero, so a lost transcript is never reported, and the quiet inconclusive line gives `FUNGIBLE_MODE_ZERO_REASON` (through `unattributableZeroReason(mode)`) in place of `UNATTRIBUTABLE_ZERO_REASON`. With no count (an unparseable `started_at`, or an archive that gives no evidence because it is unconfigured or unreadable), the outcome is the one below. The archive check is read-only: a missing archive DB file yields no evidence (it is never created here). Both missing with no archive evidence → a single quiet log line only: a persona idle since spawn has no transcript yet because Claude creates the `.jsonl` lazily on first message — normal, not an error, and must not alarm every boot. Log lines name the persona as `"<name>" (key=<key>)`. Per-persona AD/get errors (including `ErrSpawnNotFound`) are logged and skipped; the sweep never aborts. A persona whose `claude_config_dir` cannot be resolved to a real path (bug b.g57) is skipped before its row is fetched, with one quiet line: its launch waits for the directory with the row kept, so there is no lost history to report.
4a-ter. **b.osj / b.av2 SR-9.4 stop-hook bootstrap** — `stopHookBootstrap(personaConfig, STATE_DIR)` (from `src/stop-hook-bootstrap.ts`) is the start pass: over every applied persona (b.av2 SR-6.2) it installs or removes the CSCB-managed Slack Reply Guard Stop hook in `<claude_config_dir>/settings.json`. Call site: `main()` in `server.ts`, immediately after step 4a-quater (`runJsonlPersistenceSafeguard`) and before step 5 (`startupSessionManager`) — before any spawn fires. Runs in both real and dry-run modes (config-file patch, not a session operation). Never throws to the caller; per-dir failures are caught and recorded via `recordStartupError`. The same install rule runs again before every launch, as the launch pass (step 5, "Reply-guard steps before every spawn and resume"). Behavior:

    - **Install rule, per directory (b.av2 SR-9.4).** Each applied persona counts toward its effective `claude_config_dir` (its own, else the top-level one) and toward the directory its running instance launched with (the launched-with dir, kept in memory per persona key: set at each launch, cleared by `teardownPersonaReplyGuard`, empty at server start). Directories are grouped by real path (`resolveRealPath`, lexical fallback), so two spellings of one directory are one group and its `settings.json` is patched once, at the first contributing persona's configured path. A persona is enabled when its effective `stop_hook_bootstrap` is `true` or its record (`reply-guard/<key>`, see Configuration) reads `true`. The entry is ensured when any persona counting toward the directory is enabled and removed otherwise (emptied groups pruned). Whether one persona is reminded is its own record's business, read by the guard at hook time, so personas sharing a directory each follow their own value. Diagnostics name the contributing personas as `personas="<name>" (key=<key>), …`.
    - **Managed-entry shape.** Own group `{"hooks":[{"type":"command","command":"<managed command>"}]}`, no `matcher` field (Stop is not tool-scoped). Recognition rule: any Stop-hook `command` string containing the substring `slack-reply-guard.sh` is CSCB-managed.
    - **Canonical command.** `managedHookCommand(stateDir)` is the guard's absolute path followed by the record directory `<state dir>/reply-guard`, each POSIX single-quoted (`shellSingleQuote`), because Claude Code runs a hook command through a shell; the guard reads the directory as its first argument. The script path resolves relative to the installed package (same idiom as `src/install-skill-pointer.ts`), correct under both published-package layout and repo checkout. Only the exact current command is canonical: a managed entry with a bare path, a stale install path or another record directory is rewritten to it (self-heal).
    - **Idempotent write decision.** `scanStopGroups` returns `hasSingleCanonicalGroup=true` only when there is exactly one Stop group whose sole hook entry has `type=='command'`, `command==canonicalCmd`, no `matcher`, and no extra keys. In that state the write is skipped entirely. Any drift — stale command, duplicates, extra keys, extra hooks in the managed group — triggers a strip-all-managed + append-canonical rewrite, written atomically (`atomicWriteFileSync`, `.tmp` + rename). Every read-modify-write is synchronous, so two personas launching at once cannot interleave on one `settings.json`.
    - **Create-missing.** ENOENT on the target `settings.json` for an enabled dir → the file is created with just the managed group.
    - **Malformed JSON soft-fail.** Non-ENOENT read errors, unparseable JSON, and non-object top levels all report a class label of `stop-hook-bootstrap-settings-read` / `stop-hook-bootstrap-settings-parse` / `stop-hook-bootstrap-settings-shape` and leave the file untouched — never a clobber.
    - **Personal-config-dir refusal (SR-3.11).** `isForbiddenHomeClaudeDir` resolves both the candidate dir and `homedir()/.claude` through `resolveRealPath` from `src/config.ts` (`realpathSync`, with a lexical `resolve()` fallback whenever realpath fails), so symlinked personal dirs cannot slip past a string compare. On a match the dir is skipped and never written, so a persona whose directory resolves there gets no reminder. The start pass records `stop-hook-bootstrap-refuse-home` once per server start (all spellings of `~/.claude` are one group); the launch pass logs the refusal to the server log only.
    - **Skip conditions.** A persona with no effective `claude_config_dir` gets a server-log line only (`[slack] stop-hook-bootstrap: "<name>" (key=<key>) has no claude_config_dir — skipping`), never a `startup-errors.log` record, and no reminder. Empty or whitespace-only dirs are treated as absent (guards against `resolve("")` landing in the process cwd). A dir that fails `statSync` (or is not a directory) is skipped; the ensure path reports `stop-hook-bootstrap-dir-missing` / `stop-hook-bootstrap-not-a-dir`, and a missing dir on the remove path is silent.
    - **jq presence check.** A one-time `command -v jq` probe per server start: if `jq` is absent the entry is **still installed** (the hook fails open at hook time when `jq` is missing) but a `stop-hook-bootstrap-jq-missing` startup error is recorded so operators see the warning. The launch pass does not probe.
    - **Duplicate collapse and removal (SR-3.7, SR-3.8).** When rewriting an enabled dir, every managed `{type, command}` object across every Stop group is stripped before the canonical group is appended, so pre-existing duplicates collapse to one. Removal for a dir with no enabled persona strips every managed object and prunes any group left with an empty `hooks` array.
    - **Never-throws contract.** A top-level `try/catch` around the whole entry point plus per-dir `try/catch` blocks record `stop-hook-bootstrap` / `stop-hook-bootstrap-dir` classes on unexpected failure. Other dirs continue processing. Timing note (SR-3.15): on-disk state is refreshed every boot and every launch, and Claude Code normally picks up hook edits in `settings.json` while running (its settings file watcher), so the managed hook's presence in a directory may change under a running instance, for example when a neighbour sharing the directory launches. A running instance still keeps the value it launched with, because the guard decides by that instance's own record (`reply-guard/<CSCB_PERSONA>`), which is written only at the instance's launch. A live session that survives a CSCB restart via reconnect is not relaunched, so its record, and its value, change only at its next spawn or resume.
5. **Per-persona bring-up and launch (b.av2 SR-6.1)** — `startupSessionManager(configInEffect(appliedConfig, applied), { bringUp: personaBringUps, isShuttingDown: () => shuttingDown })` over the applied set runs after the start-wide passes (step 4 sweep, 4a-bis trust patch, 4a-quater JSONL safeguard, 4a-ter Stop-hook bootstrap). It is the reload controller's `lifecycle.startBringUp`, and `main()` runs it through `reload.runStartBringUp()`, so it brings up exactly the persona set step 2a applied. The pass launches over the server's configuration in effect, as every later launch does: the controller's applied persona set and switch (`applied`) over the start-time server-wide values (`appliedConfig`), which carry the crontable step 2a-ter chose (`cronTablePathForStart`; the old path after a failed move), so its launches export that path as `CSCB_CRONTABLE_PATH` (bug b.avm). The controller's own configuration stays as resolved, naming the default as `config.json` does, so detection sees no `cron_table_path` change. A guard ahead of the call throws (`the start bring-up ran before the start resolved its configuration`) while `appliedConfig` is unset, and `main()` logs it as `[slack] Warning: session startup failed — continuing: …`. `personaBringUps` is the bring-up controller (`createPersonaBringUpController` in `src/persona-bringup-controller.ts`), built in `main()` right after the connection manager. It brings each persona up once, so a persona listed in several channels is brought up and spawned exactly once. Steps 1–3 run for every persona at once (the controller's `bringUp`), so no persona's Slack connection waits behind another persona's launch. Only step 4 goes through the launch pool: at most `concurrency` launches (default 3) run at a time, taken first in, first out in the order the personas become ready. A persona that is not `up` takes no launch slot. The pool asks the pass's shutdown query (`isShuttingDown`, which reads the `shuttingDown` flag live) right before it starts each launch, and once the query answers true (a throw counts as true) it starts no further launch (b.jg5 SRJ-205): each persona still queued makes no agent-director call, gets the per-persona outcome `not-launched-shutdown` (`NOT_LAUNCHED_FOR_SHUTDOWN`) and one line, `[slack] startupSessionManager: not launching <ref> — the server has begun shutting down; no agent-director call, counted in no summary count (b.jg5 SRJ-205)` (`startLaunchNotStartedForShutdownLine`), and is counted in no count and never failed. A launch already running is not interrupted, and the pass still resolves. Per persona, in order:
   - **`persona-start` line** — one line per applied persona as its bring-up starts, naming the persona, its entry and its key (see Logging, Persona bring-up lines).
   - **Steps 1 and 2: local credentials check** (`checkPersonaCredentials`) **and working-directory check** (`checkPersonaWorkingDirectory`), both evaluated before either stops the bring-up, so both causes are logged (`persona-credentials-*`, `persona-directory-*` lines). Dry run skips the credentials check and reads no credentials file.
   - **`claude_config_dir` check** — once steps 1 and 2 pass, the controller's `checkConfigDir` resolves the persona's effective `claude_config_dir`; an unresolvable one holds the persona (`persona-config-dir-unresolvable`, see Config-dir-unresolvable below) and step 3 does not run.
   - **Step 3: Slack validation and connection** — the connection manager's `bringUp(persona, tokens)`: `auth.test` on a short-lived validation client, then the long-lived Web API and Socket Mode clients (see the `persona-connections.ts` entry for the client options, the 10 s bounds on `auth.test` and `start()`, backoff and reopen). The manager logs every Slack outcome itself (`persona-slack-unreachable`, `persona-credentials-refused`). In dry run the persona is up at once with its placeholder identity.
   - **Step 4: launch** — only when the persona's outcome is `up`: `spawnForPersona` (SR-1.4 collision-then-act dispatcher), below. The connection is therefore up before the instance is launched. This is b.av2 SR-6.1's step 4 as amended by b.jg5 SRJ-1502: "(4) launch, which waits while an old life that may still be running holds the persona's working directory (b.jg5 SRJ-809, SRJ-810); the persona is retried on its UNAVAILABLE retry timer (b.jg5 SRJ-301) until that wait ends." `spawnForPersona`'s old-life gate makes that wait (below, and [The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809), **What a hold refuses**): a persona whose working directory a hold other than one on its own row holds (the start sweep's holds of step 4, rebuilt after a restart, included) makes no agent-director call, starts the hold's wait, has its retry timer armed with `held-for-old-life` and answers `sequence-waiting`, counted under "waiting on a live-row sequence" (b.jg5 SRJ-1015); its Slack connection stays up, and the hold's end retries it at once.

   **Outcomes (b.av2 SR-6.1, SR-6.4).** Every bring-up ends with one outcome, which the controller keeps per persona:

   | Cause | Class | Outcome |
   |---|---|---|
   | None: steps 1–3 passed | — | `up` |
   | Credentials file missing, unreadable or invalid (step 1) | `persona-credentials-missing` / `-unreadable` / `-invalid` | `broken` |
   | Slack refused a token (step 3, at bring-up or on a reopen), or refused the bot token in a Web API call of the running persona (bug b.ujn) | `persona-credentials-refused` | `broken` |
   | Slack unreachable (step 3) | `persona-slack-unreachable` | `retrying` |
   | Working directory missing or unusable (step 2) | `persona-directory-missing` / `-unusable` | `retrying` |
   | `claude_config_dir` cannot be resolved to a real path, found right before step 3 or by a later launch (bug b.g57) | `persona-config-dir-unresolvable` | `retrying` |

   A persona with both a credentials cause and a directory cause is `broken`. Its directory is still re-checked, and its start and cleared lines are logged, but it goes no further while the credentials cause holds; it comes up only once both clear. A credentials-broken persona is not retried. While the server runs, it recovers only through a confirmed change to its credentials file (b.av2 SR-6.4): apply step 6 brings it up afresh (see [The apply pipeline](#the-apply-pipeline-sr-86-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-805) and [Bring-up at apply](#bring-up-at-apply-bav2-sr-61)). A start, from the record or not, also reads every credentials file as it stands (b.av2 SR-8.7 as amended by b.deo SRI-403, SRI-407), so a fixed file brings it up at the next start too.

   A persona that isn't `up` is not launched by the start, records no startup error, raises no notice and is not counted as a failed spawn. The lines above say why. Its agent-director row and any instance still running from before are kept (b.av2 SR-6.4): nothing kills them for the persona being down, but the server does not serve the instance. Its MCP registration is refused (Connection step 3), the permission poller skips its rows (Permission Relay, Per-tick flow) and `/interject` answers 503 (Endpoint Inventory). When the persona comes up, its launch reaches the row through the collision ladder below, so the history is kept. Personas are brought up independently, so one persona's failure stops neither the others nor the server.

   **Retries run on per-persona timers, outside `startupSessionManager`.** The start pass returns once every persona has an outcome and every `up` persona's launch has settled or is parked waiting for a `working` row (see the `working` branch below, b.f2b); it never waits on a retry, and a retrying persona never delays another. Nor does it wait for a live-row sequence: a launch for a persona whose sequence runs answers `sequence-waiting` at once (b.jg5 SRJ-706), counted only under `waiting on a live-row sequence` (the start summary below), neither as failed nor as succeeded. Two kinds of retry exist, both on the SR-3.2 backoff (5 s doubling to a 300 s ceiling, no cap, `persona-retry-schedule.ts`), and neither touches the restart failure counter or cap (`backoff.ts`):

   - **Slack-unreachable** — the connection manager retries on its own per-persona timer with the tokens it was handed.
   - **Directory-broken** — the controller opens no Slack connection and re-checks the directory (`checkPersonaWorkingDirectory`) on the persona's own timer. Once the directory is usable the bring-up continues with no restart and no confirmation: Slack validation and connection, then the launch. If Slack is then unreachable, the persona becomes Slack-unreachable `retrying`.
   - **Config-dir-unresolvable (bug b.g57)** — the controller checks the persona's effective `claude_config_dir` (`checkLaunchConfigDir`) right before step 3, at start, at an apply bring-up and when a directory retry reaches Slack; an unresolvable directory holds the persona there, so it never connects. Every launch (start, retry, restart, apply) also resolves it first. When it can't be resolved, the launch makes no agent-director call and hands the persona to the controller (`holdForConfigDir`), which closes its Slack connection. Either way the persona is `retrying` with no connection and receives nothing: its MCP session is dropped if it was up, its notices are held (per persona, at most 20, oldest dropped), and its row and instance are kept (no kill, delete or spawn). The controller re-checks the directory on the persona's own timer (5 s doubling to 300 s). Once it resolves, the controller logs the cleared line, connects the persona with its held credentials and launches it, which resumes its row through the ladder with no confirmation. The restart path's kill is skipped too (`holdLaunchIfConfigDirUnresolvable`), and the relaunch is `'skipped'`, counting toward no failure or cap. A confirmed credentials change while held is taken as a retrying persona's is (see [Credentials change](#credentials-change-bav2-sr-86-step-4-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-805)).

   A retry keeps using the credentials content it holds, read at the persona's bring-up, until a confirmed change replaces it; the controller holds those tokens and never re-reads the file. An edit to the file made meanwhile is ignored by the retry. The detection tick notices it: the file's digest no longer matches the one the controller holds for the persona (`credentialsDigest`), so a credentials change is pending (see [Reload Detection Tick](#reload-detection-tick-bav2-sr-82-sr-83)). Once confirmed, apply step 4 hands a retrying persona the new content, and its later attempts use it (see [Credentials change](#credentials-change-bav2-sr-86-step-4-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-805)).

   **Launch after a retry.** A persona that reaches `up` through a retry is launched from its own retry path, not by the health check: when a directory retry's Slack step leaves the persona's outcome `up` (the manager's status is `up`, `lost` or `retrying` in the `reopen` phase, since a blip right after the connection came up does not undo it), or when the manager reports `up` right after `retrying` its bring-up (the controller's `onConnectionStatus`). The launch runs once per persona through `spawnForPersona(persona, personaConfig, false)` with the persona's current applied declaration, so it shares the one-launch-in-flight guard that restarts use and a launch failure takes the runtime spawn-failure path. An `up` after `lost` or a reopen launches nothing, since the instance is already running.

   **Applied-set guard (b.av2 SR-8.6 as amended by b.deo SRI-201, SRI-203, SRI-406, SRI-408, SRI-502, SRI-802, SRI-805).** From a confirmed apply's step 1 on, no launch or restart path acts for a key outside the applied set, even before that persona's teardown. The checks read the set live (`personaConfig`) and live in three places: the bring-up controller (`appliedPersonas` getter and `isApplied(key)`, `persona-bringup-controller.ts`), where a directory re-check for such a key stops (`[slack] persona "<name>" (key=<key>): no longer applied — its working-directory retry stops`) and a launch after a retry is skipped (`… up after its bring-up retry (<via>) but no longer applied — not launching`), and a re-check tests the directory against the current set; the shared up check (`isPersonaUpGiven` in `persona-start.ts`, over `PersonaUpQuery.isApplied`), behind the relaunch gate (restart, `launchSession`, the health-check work list, a latch re-check's launches) and `isPersonaUp` (MCP session admission, the permission poller's skip, `/interject`'s 503); and `preLaunchReplyGuard` (`stop-hook-bootstrap.ts`), which does nothing for such a key. This is the one full statement of the guard; Auto-Restart and the Health-Check Poller refer here. **Its one exception (b.jg5 SRJ-1512, beside SR-8.6 as amended by b.deo SRI-201, SRI-203, SRI-406, SRI-408, SRI-502, SRI-802, SRI-805)** is the old-life wait's kill and `find-missing` steps on a retired key's old row, and their retries ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809), **The wait's steps**): they run in the live-row sequence registry outside every launch or recovery attempt, never launch the key, and never arm a retry timer for it. Their calls arm nothing for the old key; only applied personas waiting on the hold are armed, and `armOldLifeWaiter` refuses a key the applied configuration does not have, logging `[slack] old-life-wait: persona=<key>: not in the applied configuration — no retry timer armed (b.jg5 SRJ-1512, b.av2 SR-8.6)`. The retry timer's full-mode action still stops for a key not applied, and a removed key's restart work beside the wait on its own row reaches the not-up check (the live-row sequence gate under [Auto-Restart](#auto-restart)). What the guard does not do is stop anything: the removed persona's Slack connection and instance stay until its teardown in apply step 2 of the same apply (see [Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-307)). For what else a removal changes at step 1, see [The apply pipeline](#the-apply-pipeline-sr-86-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-805).

   **Never posted to Slack (b.av2 SR-7.2, part).** Bring-up failures are logged to the server log only, at start and on every later retry, and never to `startup-errors.log`. No notice is posted or held for a later flush under any identity.

   Spawn-path log lines name the persona JSON-quoted with the key beside it, e.g. `spawnForPersona: spawned "Ops Bot" (key=ops_bot_5e2526f3) …`; under dry run each persona logs `dry-run: skipping spawn for "<name>" (key=<key>) cwd=<dir>` and nothing is spawned.
   - **Trust patch before every launch (b.av2 SR-6.2).** Each ladder run first calls the installed pre-launch trust patcher (`trustPatchPersona`, see step 4a-bis) for the persona's working directory in its effective config dir — once, before the first spawn or resume the ladder can make, so it covers fresh spawns, resumes and the replace step's reuse spawns below. It never runs under dry run and never for a call that joins an in-flight launch. A throw is logged as `[slack] spawnForPersona: pre-launch trust patch failed for "<name>" (key=<key>) — launching anyway: <error>` and the ladder continues.
   - **Pre-trust is only logged (b.jg5 SRJ-413).** The server never passes `no_pre_trust` on a spawn (plain or reuse) or a `resume`, so agent-director pre-accepts the persona's folder trust at every launch and reports the outcome as the result's `pre_trust`: `ok` (the trust entry was written), `skipped` (pre-trust was off for this launch) or `failed` (it could not be written). Every launch that returns success writes exactly one line about it, first in the after-launch step (`afterLaunchSucceeded`, before the approver starts; see the pre-session dialog approval bullet below), from `preTrustLogLine`: `[slack] spawnForPersona: "<name>" (key=<key>) <spawn|resume|reuse spawn> pre_trust=<value> (logged only, b.jg5 SRJ-413)`, the value shown as it arrived; a result without the field (an agent-director older than Phase 1) logs `[slack] spawnForPersona: "<name>" (key=<key>) <spawn|resume|reuse spawn> result carries no pre_trust: it came from an agent-director older than Phase 1 (logged only, b.jg5 SRJ-413)`. No value changes what the server does: the launch's result, notices, startup-errors entries, outage state and retry counts are the same for all four cases, and a folder-trust prompt that follows `skipped` or `failed` is answered by the startup-dialog approver like any other. The server's own trust patch above is unchanged and still runs before every launch.
   - **Reply-guard steps before every spawn and resume (b.av2 SR-9.4, SR-6.2).** Immediately before each actual `client.spawn` or `client.resume` the ladder makes — the fresh spawn, a resume, a dead-session or `ErrSpawnNotFound` recovery, the replace step's reuse spawns and the restart relaunch through the same ladder — it calls the installed pre-launch reply guard (`preLaunchReplyGuard`, `src/stop-hook-bootstrap.ts`). In order it (1) writes the launching persona's effective `stop_hook_bootstrap` to its record `reply-guard/<key>` (see Configuration), (2) sets the persona's launched-with dir to its effective `claude_config_dir` (or forgets it, with the no-configured-dir log line, when none is set), and (3) runs the launch pass of the step 4a-ter install rule over the new effective dir and the previous launched-with dir only. It writes only the launching persona's record, so a neighbour's launch in the same directory never rewrites another persona's record. The launch pass does no `jq` probe and never writes `startup-errors.log`: its failures, the `~/.claude` refusal included, are server-log lines (`[slack] stop-hook-bootstrap: pre-launch pass [<class>] …`). A failed record write removes any stale record (the guard then fails open to no reminder), logs one line naming the persona and the record path, and the launch proceeds; nothing in these steps blocks a launch. A path that only reconnects to a live instance or does nothing (`waiting`/`working` reconnect, the `pending`/`check_permission`/`ask_user` no-op) runs no reply-guard step. The optimistic first spawn runs the steps before it and, on `ErrInstanceIdCollision`, undoes them, so a later spawn or resume in that ladder runs them afresh. The undo restores the record (the previous text, or deleted when there was none) only if the step wrote it successfully, changed it, and the record still holds what the step wrote; it restores the launched-with dir only if the entry is still the one the step set; then it re-reads the applied persona set and re-runs the launch pass over the new and previous dirs. A teardown or another launch in between is never overwritten. Side effect: when the collision leads only to a reconnect and the running persona's record disagrees with its current config, the step may remove or add the managed hook, and the undo re-runs the install rule with the restored record: a hook the step removed comes back, and one it added stays when the config now enables it (correct under the install rule). When the step removed the hook and the undo re-adds it, that directory's `settings.json` is written twice and the managed group moves to the end of the Stop hooks. `server.ts` installs the step once a persona config is loaded; with none it does nothing (no record, no patch). It passes a getter, not a snapshot, so the step and its undo each read the live applied persona set. The effect: a running instance keeps the value it launched with, and a changed value takes effect at the persona's next launch; a confirmed change reaches that launch through step 1's swap of the applied set, with no call at apply. Dry run returns before the ladder, so it writes no record.
   - Attempt `client.spawn(SR-1.1 params)`, built from `persona-identity.ts` (b.av2 SR-2.2). This first spawn is plain: `buildSpawnParams` never adds the reuse flag (b.jg5 SRJ-711), so a key whose row is already there collides (`ErrInstanceIdCollision`) and goes on to the collision `get` and the ladder below, whose `resume` keeps the conversation. Only the reuse launch adds the flag ([Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)). A key recorded as retired gets no plain first spawn: its first launch is one reuse spawn of the same id, and its collision `get` decides by the retired-key rule ([Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-bjg5-srj-806-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-407)). A renamed persona's new key, which is not recorded and has no row, gets its plain first spawn only once the old key's row reads `ended` or `missing`: until then the old-life gate before the ladder holds it back, and the hold's end retries it at once (b.jg5 SRJ-711 bullet 2, SRJ-810; [The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809), **What a hold refuses**).
     - `template: 'slack-channel-bot'`, `relay_mode: 'on'`, `cwd` = the persona's working directory.
     - `claude_instance_id: cscb_<key>`, `tmux_session_name: slack_bot_<key>`.
     - `label: ['service=cscb', 'persona=<key>', 'config_dir=<12 hex>']`, and no other label. The `config_dir` value hashes the real path of the persona's effective `claude_config_dir` (no configured dir means `~/.claude`), taken from the launch's pre-launch check (`checkLaunchConfigDir`, `resolveRealPathStrict`). There is no lexical fallback (bug b.g57). A directory not created yet under a resolvable parent gets the label of the real path it will have: its nearest existing ancestor's real path plus the rest, which is the lexical path when no symlink is involved. Claude Code creates it at first launch. A directory that can't be resolved (a symlink on its path that points to nothing, `ENOTDIR`, or any error other than `ENOENT`) gets no label and is not launched (see the Config-dir-unresolvable retry above). Known limit: a dropped mount that leaves an empty mount point looks like a directory not created yet. The start sweep (step 4) and the ladder read the `persona`, `config_dir` and `cwd` fields; the permission poller reads the `persona` label. The CLI's teardown reads no label: it addresses `cscb_<key>` directly.
     - `extra_env`: `CSCB_PERSONA=<key>`, `CLAUDE_MANAGED_CHANNEL=<key>`, `CSCB_CRONTABLE_PATH` on every spawn (the resolved tilde-expanded `cron_table_path`: the default from `resolveDefaultCronTablePath`, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/cscb/crontab` with `SLACK_STATE_DIR` unset and `<config dir>/crontab` with it set, or the configured override), `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION=false` on every spawn (see Environment Variables), and `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` only when a `claude_config_dir` is configured (passed as configured, not real-pathed). Every plain spawn in the ladder sends these params unchanged (the first spawn, the retry spawn after the collision `get` found no row, and the spawn after `resume` found none); the reuse spawn (`reuseSpawnForPersona`) sends the same params with only `reuse_finished: true` added (b.jg5 SRJ-708; [Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)); a resume passes only the instance ID, and agent-director restores the env it stored with the row at spawn.
     - No `no_pre_trust`, on a plain spawn or a reuse (`buildSpawnParams`'s doc comment says so; see the pre-trust bullet above).
   - **Never two live instances (b.av2 SR-6.3).** The instance ID is fixed at `cscb_<key>`, so agent-director refuses a second spawn for a persona that already has a row (`ErrInstanceIdCollision`), and the ladder below decides what happens to that row. Within the process, `spawnForPersona` allows one in-flight launch per persona key: a second call for a key whose launch is still running — from the start pass, a restart or a human-triggered restart — logs `[slack] spawnForPersona: launch already in flight for "<name>" (key=<key>) — joining it` and returns that launch's result instead of starting a second ladder. The entry is cleared when the launch settles, whatever its outcome; different keys never wait on each other. Dry run returns before the check.
   - **A launch attempt (b.jg5 SRJ-301).** The ladder a `spawnForPersona` call starts runs as a launch attempt for the persona (`runInAttempt`, `src/unavailable-retry.ts`) until its result, the `working`-row wait included (the dialog approver that starts after a launch call returned success is not: it runs outside every attempt, see Pre-session dialog approval below); a joining call, the claude_config_dir deferral and dry run are no attempt. An UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT (`ErrTmuxNotAvailable`), CONFIG (`ErrConfigMalformed`) or UNCLASSIFIED outcome from any verb in it, or an error from `status`, `get` or `list` other than `ErrSpawnNotFound` and UNUSABLE_NAME, arms the persona's UNAVAILABLE retry timer through the installed trigger sink (a trigger while armed keeps the due time). An UNCLASSIFIED outcome in it, a read's included, is also reported to the persona's unclassified-error episode ([The unclassified-error episode](#the-unclassified-error-episode-bjg5-srj-313-srj-1009)). An UNAVAILABLE outcome other than `ErrTmuxKillFailed` from a tmux-touching call in it also starts or continues the persona's `tmux-unresponsive` condition ([The tmux-unresponsive condition](#the-tmux-unresponsive-condition-bjg5-srj-307-srj-310)). At every spawn, resume and collision `get` below, the same outcome is a refusal ([Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104), refusals at the launch and recovery sites). At the reconnect's `send-keys` it is the reconnect's `transient` answer (the `waiting` branch below), and at the `working`-row wait's `status` reads it is transient instead: the wait goes on, and at its timeout it ends `not-reconnected` (b.jg5 SRJ-605; the `working` branch below). A refusal logs one line, posts no spawn-failure notice, records no `spawn-failed` entry and ends the ladder with `failed`. Nothing is deleted, killed to recover or launched after it. An UNAVAILABLE refusal at a launch call (a launch timeout included) is then followed by exactly one `get` of the persona's row, which decides with no launch in the attempt ([A launch's window and the read after a timeout](#a-launchs-window-and-the-read-after-a-timeout-bjg5-srj-407)). Every other outcome takes the branch below as described, notices included. A `failed` result whose last agent-director error in the attempt armed the timer is answered as `retrying` (b.jg5 SRJ-1015), which the restart path does not count (Auto-Restart step 5) and the start pass counts only under `retrying` (the start summary below). The timer then retries the persona on its own (Auto-Restart, UNAVAILABLE retry). Dry run makes no agent-director call, so it arms nothing.
   - On `ErrInstanceIdCollision`, call `client.get({claude_instance_id})` through the shared own-row read (`readPersonaOwnRow`) and keep the whole row. **The row-read rule decides first (b.jg5 SRJ-114, SRJ-513):** a read that latched the persona (its own row reading `pending` with no launch start, or a `provenance_conflict` note on its own row, the persona configured, or an UNUSABLE_NAME answer to the `get`, b.jg5 SRJ-512; see [Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)) answers `latched` before the `cwd` and `config_dir` guards and the state branches, whatever the row's state: no wait, sweep, reconnect, sequence or launch, no notice, nothing counted. Any other note, or none, goes on below. **`cwd` guard (b.av2 SR-6.2 as amended, b.jg5 SRJ-1503)** first, before any state branch and so before any `findMissing` sweep or reconnect: a row whose `cwd` differs from the persona's working directory by real path (`compareRowToPersona`; a symlink to the directory matches, a row with no `cwd` never does) is never resumed, reconnected or waited on, whatever its state and `resume_enabled`. It is replaced on every ladder path with no row deleted: a live row goes through the live-row sequence, then a reuse spawn; a finished row gets a reuse spawn. It logs `[slack] spawnForPersona: "<name>" (key=<key>) row cwd=<row cwd> differs from working_directory=<dir> (state=<state>) — replacing the row by a reuse spawn of the same id; nothing is deleted`, then goes to the replace step (below) with the collision `get`'s state as the state last read.
