A row that also fails the `config_dir` check below is handled here. At start the sweep (step 4) has already killed such a row when it was listed live, and kept it, so at start this guard usually finds the row finished and replaces it by a reuse spawn. **Unresolvable working directory (b.av2 SR-6.4):** when the row's `cwd` does not match, the persona's working directory has no real path at that moment, and the row's `cwd` has no real path either (`cwdCheckDeferred`), the row cannot be shown to be elsewhere, so it is kept: no replacement. The ladder logs `[slack] spawnForPersona: "<name>" (key=<key>) working_directory=<dir> cannot be resolved to a real path — keeping its row (cwd=<row cwd>, state=<state>); the launch fails and is retried by the restart path`, raises `cwd-unreachable` for the persona and returns `failed`. A row whose `cwd` equals the missing path lexically matches and goes on to the state branches. A row whose `cwd` resolves to an existing directory elsewhere isn't deferred: it is replaced through the replace step like any other `cwd` mismatch. The deferral covers only this `cwd` guard; the `resume_enabled=false` and `config_dir` paths below replace the row, and the `ErrNoSessionId` and `ErrJsonl*` paths make their reuse spawn, whatever the directory's state. Otherwise branch on state per the [SR-11 substitution table](#sr-11-substitution-table):
     - **The replace step (b.jg5 SRJ-707, SRJ-709; `replacePersonaRow`).** Every row the ladder cannot keep (the `cwd` guard above, `resume_enabled=false`, the `config_dir` guard and the `pending` step's `cwd` and `config_dir` comparison, below) goes through one step that never deletes, never kills and never launches over a live row. It decides on the row state the path last read: the collision `get`'s state for the `cwd` guard and the `ended`/`missing` and `pending` branches; on a dead-session path (`reconcileMissingFirst`) the collision `get`'s `waiting` or the working-row wait's last read, a live row unless the route's cause is a row read (`deadSessionLastRead`: no row for `row-absent`, the state read for `row-read-finished`); on the prompt-row recovery the re-read after its sweep, which read it finished.
       - **A finished row** (`ended`, `missing` or no row) gets one reuse spawn of the same id (`reuseSpawnForPersona`, [Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708): `buildSpawnParams`'s params, the persona's `extra_env` included, with `reuse_finished: true`) through the finished-row branch (`reuseFinishedRow`), with no second trust patch. The step first logs `[slack] spawnForPersona: replacing the row of <ref> (<why>; last read <state>): a reuse spawn of the same id; nothing is deleted (b.jg5 SRJ-707)`, `<why>` being `resume_enabled is false`, `its cwd differs from the persona's working directory` or `its config_dir label is missing or differs`, and `<state>` the state read, `no-row` or `unreadable`. The reuse's outcomes are its own table's: a success answers `spawned` and keeps the old row as an earlier life; UNAVAILABLE and every other refusal answer `retrying` and post no onset at once; a CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME latches; `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` and a directory error are one counted launch failure; `ErrInvalidFlags` gets its version re-check and, unless that stops the server, holds the persona (`held`, launching nothing); an `ErrInternal` is never counted. A collision (`ErrInstanceIdCollision`: the row turned live) launched nothing. The first logs `[slack] spawnForPersona: the <what> of <ref> collided with a live row — nothing launched; re-running get-then-act once (b.jg5 SRJ-112)` and re-runs this step's get-then-act once (`ladderGetThenAct`, marked as the re-run): its collision `get` reads the row again and its branches decide again. A collision in that re-run makes no further call, arms the persona's retry timer with `collision` (`reportReuseCollisionAtSite`, `outage-state.ts`) and answers `retrying` (b.jg5 SRJ-1015): no spawn-failure notice, no entry, nothing counted, with `[slack] spawnForPersona: the <what> of <ref> collided with a live row again, in the re-run of get-then-act — nothing launched; answering retrying, no spawn-failure notice, nothing counted; the retry timer is armed (cause=collision; b.jg5 SRJ-112, SRJ-1015)` (`could not be armed` outside an attempt with a trigger sink). `<what>` is `reuse spawn`, or `reuse spawn after its resume's no-transcript answer` for the no-transcript step, which goes through the same branch.
       - **A live row** (any other state, `pending` and an unreadable state included) is never launched over: the step starts the live-row sequence through the session manager's start entry (`startLiveRowSequence`; [The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717)) with the state last read as its seed, entry at step 1, the conversation not kept, the retired-key flag set for a retired key (the reason `its key is retired and <mark words>`, [Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-bjg5-srj-806-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-407)), a launch at the end and the kill-failure alert context `recovery`. The sequence's checked kills and judged runs come first, and its step-6 launch is a reuse spawn of the same id. The step makes no other call and answers `sequence-waiting` (which `launchSession` maps to the uncounted `'refused'`) whatever the start entry answers, except `held`, which answers `held` (the persona is held on `ErrInvalidFlags`, `LIVE_ROW_START_HELD`), logging `[slack] spawnForPersona: replacing the row of <ref> (<why>; last read <state>): a live row goes through the live-row sequence first, which ends in a reuse spawn of the same id; start answered <answer> — answering <sequence-waiting|held>; no other call, nothing counted (b.jg5 SRJ-707, SRJ-705, SRJ-706)` (for a retired key the line reads `… goes through the live-row sequence first (its key is retired), which ends …` and its reference list ends `SRJ-706, SRJ-805)`), `<answer>` being `started`, `already-running`, `closed`, `not-installed` or `held`; the registry or the start entry logs its own line for each answer but `started`.
       - **A resume site's replacement with no dead evidence (b.jg5 SRJ-609, SRJ-611, SRJ-707; `replaceAtResumeSite`).** `resumeOrFreshSpawn`'s two replacements (`resume_enabled=false` and the `config_dir` guard) reach the step through `replaceAtResumeSite`. A row last read finished, or a path holding dead evidence ([Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611)), goes to the step as above. A row last read live on a path with no dead evidence (a dead-session route whose cause is `row-not-interactive`, or none carried) is not acted on from that earlier read, since the row may have finished since or be `pending` under another process's launch: the row is read again with one `get` through the shared own-row read (what `get before replacing`), and the fresh state decides. This never starts the live-row sequence itself. A read that latched the persona answers `latched`; a refused read answers the refusal result (`failed`; the `get` armed its read-error cause, so the launch answers `retrying`); `ended`, `missing` or no row goes to the step with the re-read state, so its reuse spawn of the same id; `pending` goes to the ladder's `pending` step (below: a covered row is left, a row that is not covered gets SRJ-411's sequence there); a known live state other than `pending`, or a state CSCB does not know (an unreadable one included, named `state=unreadable`), is the lost race of the not-resumable step (below): nothing killed, deleted or launched, `spawn-not-resumable-lost-race` armed, `retrying`. One line (`replaceRereadLine`): `[slack] spawnForPersona: replacing the row of <ref> (<why>; last read <state>; <evidence>) — the path holds no dead evidence, so the row is read again first: re-read: <re-read> — <outcome> (b.jg5 SRJ-609, SRJ-611, SRJ-707)`, `<outcome>` being `the persona is latched: answering latched; nothing more is called for it`, `the read was refused: answering the refusal result; nothing more is called`, `the row is finished: the replace step's reuse spawn of the same id`, `a launch in progress: no live-row sequence of its own; the ladder's pending step decides`, or the lost race's outcome (`a lost race: nothing killed, deleted or launched; …`).
     - **`config_dir` guard before any resume (b.av2 SR-6.2 as amended, b.jg5 SRJ-1504).** `resumeOrFreshSpawn` compares the row's `config_dir` label (from the collision `get` above) with `personaConfigDirLabelValue` of the persona's current effective `claude_config_dir`, through `compareRowToPersona`. It runs after the `resume_enabled=false` branch and after the `reconcileMissingFirst` sweep (b.4dk), immediately before `client.resume(...)`, so it covers both the `ended`/`missing` resume and the dead-session resume. When the directory stopped resolving since the pre-launch check (`configDirResolved: false`), there is no verdict: the row is kept, nothing is launched and the persona is held as above (`deferred`). On a mismatch or a missing label it does not resume, because agent-director's `ResumeParams` carries only the instance ID and a resume keeps the old `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`: a live row goes through the live-row sequence, then a reuse spawn of the same id (a new life); a finished row gets that reuse spawn directly; no row is deleted (the replace step above, through `replaceAtResumeSite`, so a row last read live on a path with no dead evidence is read again first). The old history stays in the old directory, archived to the earlier life; no transcript was lost, so neither `diagnoseJsonlMissing` nor an amnesia action runs. Log: `[slack] spawnForPersona: "<name>" (key=<key>) config_dir label missing (label absent, now=<hex> for claude_config_dir=<dir>) — not resuming; replacing its row by a reuse spawn of the same id`, or `config_dir label changed (was=<old hex>, now=<new hex> for claude_config_dir=<dir>)` with the same tail; `<dir>` is `<default>` when none is configured. The replace step's line follows.
     - `ended` / `missing` + `resume_enabled` → `config_dir` guard above, then `client.resume(...)`, logged `[slack] spawnForPersona: attempting resume for <ref>`. **`resume`'s outcomes (b.jg5 SRJ-113; `resumeAtSite`).** One handler decides them, by class, at every `resume` site: here, at the live-row sequence's final launch (its `resume` leg, [The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717), whose lines start `[slack] live-row-sequence:`) and at the latch re-check's retry of a latched `resume` (lines starting `[slack] latch-recheck:`; [The re-check](#the-re-check-bjg5-srj-505)), where a definite answer clears the latch before its row is handled, `ErrSpawnNotResumable` arms the lost-race cause and answers `retrying`, and the plain spawn after `ErrSpawnNotFound` has the re-check's collision row; and at the forced `resume` of the test seam `_forceResumeForPersona` (lines starting `[slack] forced-launch:`; the `session-manager.ts` entry), where `ErrSpawnNotResumable` is answered as at the re-check and a collision of the plain spawn after `ErrSpawnNotFound` or of the no-transcript reuse arms the collision cause and answers `retrying`. Only the no-transcript, not-resumable and collision rows differ between the sites. Nothing assumes a failed `resume` restored the row (HO rev 28): a later read of the row decides.
       - success → `[slack] spawnForPersona: resumed <ref>`, the after-launch step (Pre-session dialog approval below), action `resumed`;
       - `ErrNoSessionId` / `ErrJsonlMissing` / `ErrJsonlNeverWritten` (by class, `isNoTranscriptResumeError`) → the no-transcript step (below);
       - `ErrSpawnNotResumable` (by class) → the not-resumable step (below; b.jg5 SRJ-710);
       - `ErrSpawnNotFound` (by class; the row vanished between the dead-session verdict and the resume: expired, or a race) → one plain spawn of the same id (`plainSpawnAfterResumeNotFound`): `buildSpawnParams`'s params with no reuse flag, inside which agent-director makes its pre-spawn scan (b.jg5 SRJ-111). It logs `[slack] spawnForPersona: ErrSpawnNotFound on resume for <ref> — fresh-spawn: one plain spawn of the same id, which makes agent-director's pre-spawn scan; no spawn-failure notice for the ErrSpawnNotFound (b.jg5 SRJ-113, SRJ-111)` (`resumeNotFoundSpawnLine`), and posts no spawn-failure notice for the `ErrSpawnNotFound` itself. A success logs `[slack] spawnForPersona: fresh-spawned (after ErrSpawnNotFound on resume) for <ref>`, runs the after-launch step and answers `spawned`; every other outcome is the plain spawn's table ([Plain spawn](#plain-spawn-bjg5-srj-111), `<what>` `fresh spawn after ErrSpawnNotFound on resume`), its latch recording the state the path last read before the `resume`. Its collision re-runs get-then-act once here; at the live-row sequence's `resume` leg it ends the sequence without its launch (`spawn-collision`);
       - CONFLICT → the persona latches with the refused operation `resume`, whatever the case ("this row's own id", "left over from an earlier life", "no valid instance id", "a different instance id", "another agent-director store", or "conflicting labels", which a stray `@ad_owner` value or a duplicate label gives after "duplicate session" too), and the state the path last read; never a kill (the CONFLICT bullet below);
       - UNUSABLE_NAME → the persona latches with the refused operation `none` (the UNUSABLE_NAME bullet below);
       - `ErrInstanceIdCollision` (by class; agent-director's `resume` does not answer it, so this is a guard that keeps a collision from the spawn-failure notice, b.jg5 SRJ-713) → `resumeCollisionAt`, checked first in `resumeFailedAt`: as a reuse spawn's second collision (SRJ-112), no further call, the retry timer armed with the `collision` cause (`reportReuseCollisionAtSite`, so the attempt records it), one line (`resumeCollisionLine`), and `retrying`; nothing counted, posted or killed, and that retry's run of the restart path's decision is the get-then-act;
       - UNAVAILABLE (a launch timeout included), ENVIRONMENT (`ErrTmuxNotAvailable`), CONFIG and UNCLASSIFIED → a refusal (the launch attempt above); an UNAVAILABLE one, whatever its restore sentence says, is followed by one `get` whose row decides, with no launch in the attempt: after a launch timeout a covered `pending` row gets the approver ([A launch's window and the read after a timeout](#a-launchs-window-and-the-read-after-a-timeout-bjg5-srj-407));
       - `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` → one counted launch failure that kills nothing, makes no spawn in its place and arms the retry timer at once in pending-only mode (the `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` bullet below);
       - DIRECTORY (`ErrCwdNotFound`, `ErrCwdNotADirectory`) → `failed`, counted; the wrapper raised `cwd-unreachable`;
       - `ErrInvalidFlags` → the `ErrInvalidFlags` step, then UNCLASSIFIED (below).

       **The no-transcript step (b.jg5 SRJ-707, SRJ-712; `noTranscriptReuse`).** The row `resume` refused for these reasons is finished, so the persona is brought up fresh by one reuse spawn of the same id (`reuseSpawnForPersona`, [Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)) through the replace step's finished-row branch (`reuseFinishedRow`), and nothing is deleted, killed or plain-spawned. The ladder first logs `[slack] spawnForPersona: <failure> on resume for <ref> — a reuse spawn of the same id follows; nothing is deleted (b.jg5 SRJ-707)`. On `ErrJsonlMissing` specifically, `diagnoseJsonlMissing` runs **before** the reuse spawn, which resets the row it reads (see the b.wrb / b.fwu note below); a latched or refused diagnosis read ends the step with no reuse. The reuse is given the row state last read (the diagnosis `get`'s when it made one, else the caller's) and runs no second trust patch. A success after `ErrJsonlMissing` returns action `fresh-after-amnesia` (definite lost/never-created verdict) or `fresh-after-inconclusive-amnesia` (b.fwu — diagnosis inconclusive) rather than `spawned`, except for a recorded key: its reuse's `fresh-retired` (the key's new life has begun, its mark set; [Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)) is answered as it is, with no amnesia result, and the diagnosis's persona notice is not posted; when the diagnosis held a notice, one line says so, `[slack] spawnForPersona: <ref>'s key is retired, so its reuse spawn answered fresh-retired — answering it, not an amnesia result; the lost-transcript diagnosis's persona notice is not posted (b.jg5 SRJ-112, SRJ-806)`. The amnesia results keep the startup summary from counting a memory-loss recovery as an ordinary clean spawn. `ErrNoSessionId` and `ErrJsonlNeverWritten` skip the diagnosis entirely and return plain `spawned` (b.jgf — see the note below). Every other reuse answer is the reuse spawn's own ([Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)), a CONFLICT latching with the refused operation `reuse-spawn`. A reuse collision (`ErrInstanceIdCollision`: the row is live again) takes the finished-row branch's one re-run of get-then-act, and a second collision arms `collision` and answers `retrying` (the replace step above).

       **A `resume`'s `ErrInvalidFlags` (b.jg5 SRJ-104), at either `resume` site,** goes through the `ErrInvalidFlags` step (`classifyWithInvalidFlagsRecheck`, see [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)): one immediate agent-director version re-check, then class UNCLASSIFIED. Nothing is deleted, killed or launched because of it, and no spawn-failure notice is raised. A re-check that stops ends the server as the runtime re-check defines (`ad-version-gate.ts`): one line built from the classification only, `[slack] spawnForPersona: resume failed for <ref>: class=UNCLASSIFIED name=ErrInvalidFlags[ message="…"] (after one immediate agent-director version re-check: stop)`, and the `failed` action is marked `stopping`, which `launchSession` answers as `'skipped'` (not counted). After any other re-check answer it is an UNCLASSIFIED refusal (b.jg5 SRJ-313): `reportUnclassifiedAtSite` arms the persona's retry timer with the `unclassified` cause and reports the outcome to its unclassified-error episode, and the one line is the refusal line, `[slack] spawnForPersona: resume refused for <ref>: class=UNCLASSIFIED name=ErrInvalidFlags[ message="…"] (after one immediate agent-director version re-check: <pass|could-not-run|not-running>) — no spawn-failure notice; nothing more is called (b.jg5 SRJ-105)`; the launch answers `retrying` (b.jg5 SRJ-1015), never counted.
     - `ended` / `missing` + `resume_enabled=false` → not resumed (never reaches the `config_dir` guard): `[slack] spawnForPersona: resume_enabled=false for <ref> — not resuming; replacing its row by a reuse spawn of the same id`, then the replace step with the collision `get`'s finished state, so one reuse spawn of the same id. On a dead-session path the same branch decides on that path's last read and its evidence: a row last read live goes through the live-row sequence when the path holds dead evidence, and is read again first otherwise (`replaceAtResumeSite`, the replace step above).
     - **`ErrSpawnNotResumable` on a resume — the not-resumable step (b.jg5 SRJ-710, SRJ-611; `spawnNotResumableAtLadder`).** It is never by itself a reason to kill and replace, and it is no reuse site. The step reads the row once more with one `get` through the shared own-row read (`notResumableStep`, what `get after ErrSpawnNotResumable`; [Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)), so its note and launch-start latches apply, and decides on that re-read with the dead evidence the path holds ([Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611); `decideNotResumable`):
       - **The read latched the persona** (or found it latched) → `latched`, nothing more called.
       - **`pending`: a launch in progress, not a failure.** Nothing is counted or posted, and the `ErrSpawnNotResumable` starts no live-row sequence of its own, whatever evidence the path holds. The row goes to the ladder's `pending` step (`ladderPendingRowStep`, the `pending` branch below), whose answer is the ladder's: a covered row is left (`no-op`) with the persona's retry timer armed in pending-only mode, with no kill and no launch, and a row that is not covered (its `cwd` or `config_dir` label differing, or a retired key's old life) gets the replace step's live-row sequence (b.jg5 SRJ-409, SRJ-411; [Covered and uncovered rows](#covered-and-uncovered-rows-bjg5-srj-409-srj-411)). Nothing is armed beyond what that step arms.
       - **A known live state other than `pending` (`AGENT_DIRECTOR_LIVE_STATES`), on a path holding dead evidence** (GONE-based: the reconnect's `tmux-gone`, the prompt row's `prompt-row-ladder-gone`, or a GONE-based verdict the restart path carried in) that no read of the row as finished or gone has voided ([Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611), **Dead evidence covers one life**) → one live-row sequence through `startLiveRowSequence`, seeded with the re-read state, entry at step 1, the conversation kept, the retired-key flag unset (a `resume` was made, so the key was not recorded; the start entry sets the flag if it is recorded by then), a launch at the end and alert context `recovery`; its step 6 is a `resume` when the row has a session id and the persona may resume it ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717)). The ladder makes no other call, counts nothing and answers `sequence-waiting` whatever the start entry answers, except `held`, which answers `held`.
       - **Otherwise: a lost race** (a known live state with no dead evidence, or with dead evidence a finished read voided: the live re-read is a launch that evidence never saw, a state CSCB does not know or an unreadable one whatever evidence the path holds, `ended`, `missing`, no row, or a read refused by the shared read's own error rows, whose read-error cause it armed). Nothing is killed, deleted or launched, nothing is posted or counted, the persona's retry timer is armed with `spawn-not-resumable-lost-race` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_LOST_RACE`, through `reportLostRaceAtSite`, `outage-state.ts`) and the ladder answers `retrying` (b.jg5 SRJ-1015), so the persona is decided again at its next tick or retry.

       One line (`spawnNotResumableLine`): `[slack] spawnForPersona: <failure> on resume for <ref> — re-read: <re-read>; <evidence> — <outcome> (b.jg5 SRJ-710, SRJ-611)`, `<re-read>` being `state=<state>`, `state=no-row`, `the read failed` or `the read latched the persona`, `<evidence>` the dead evidence the path held (`describeDeadEvidence`), and `<outcome>` one of:
       - `the persona is latched: answering latched; nothing more is called for it` (`REREAD_LATCHED_OUTCOME`);
       - `a launch in progress, not a failure: nothing counted or posted, and no live-row sequence of its own; the ladder's pending step decides` (`NOT_RESUMABLE_PENDING_OUTCOME`), followed by the `pending` step's own line;
       - `the path holds dead evidence and the row is live: the live-row sequence, with the conversation kept (alert context recovery), ending in resume; start answered <answer> — answering <sequence-waiting|held>; no other call, nothing counted` (`notResumableSequenceOutcome`), `<answer>` being `started`, `already-running`, `closed`, `not-installed` or `held`, and the ladder answering `sequence-waiting` whatever the start entry answers, except `held`, which answers `held`;
       - `a lost race: nothing killed, deleted or launched; answering retrying, no spawn-failure notice, nothing counted; the retry timer is armed (cause=spawn-not-resumable-lost-race)` (`lostRaceOutcome`; `could not be armed` outside an attempt with a trigger sink).

       At the live-row sequence's own `resume` the same re-read runs with the sequence barred: it never starts a second sequence ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717), step 6).
     - `waiting` → the reconnect, `reconnectMcpWithCause(key, lastRead, ref)` with the collision `get`'s `waiting` as its last read, makes exactly one `send-keys` of `/mcp reconnect slack-channel-router` through `withOutageDetection` (the tmux-touching `send-keys` verb; the library appends Enter). It never retries, starts no tmux server and makes no tmux call of its own (b.jg5 SRJ-118, SRJ-609). It logs `reconnectStartLine` (`[slack] reconnecting MCP server "slack-channel-router": <ref>`), then, on a failure, one line from its builder, and decides its answer by class through the classifier:
       - a persona already latched (`personaLatchedNow`) → no `send-keys`; `transient`, latched (`reconnectLatchedLine`);
       - success → `ok`; the ladder answers `reconnected`;
       - GONE (`ErrTmuxSendKeys`) → `dead-session` with cause `tmux-gone`, at once (`reconnectGoneLine`);
       - `ErrSpawnNotInteractive` → `dead-session` with cause `row-not-interactive` (b.dup; `reconnectNotInteractiveLine`). The row finished after the `get` read it (a findMissing sweep, such as the one another persona's launch wait starts with, marked it `missing`), or it reads `pending` and the session holding the persona's name may be another launch's. A finished row is not proof that the worker is gone, so this is only a route into the recovery's decision, and the line claims nothing about the worker's process (b.jg5 SRJ-609);
       - `ErrSpawnNotFound` → `dead-session` with cause `row-absent`: a row read, not a GONE (`reconnectRowAbsentLine`);
       - CONFLICT → the persona latches through the latch's CONFLICT entry with the refused operation "P's next check or recovery" and the last read (b.jg5 SRJ-501); `transient`, latched. Its one line (`reconnectConflictLine`) names the case and, for "not this launch's session", adds `RECONNECT_NOT_THIS_LAUNCH_NOTE` (a leftover of an earlier launch may hold the persona's session, b.jg5 SRJ-613). Nothing was typed, and the refused `send-keys` is never retried;
       - UNUSABLE_NAME → the persona latches through the unusable-name entry (refused operation `none`, the last read, b.jg5 SRJ-512); `transient`, latched (`reconnectUnusableNameLine`);
       - `ErrInvalidFlags` → the `ErrInvalidFlags` step (one immediate version re-check), then UNCLASSIFIED: `transient`, marked `stopping` when the re-check stopped the server (`reconnectInvalidFlagsLine`);
       - UNAVAILABLE (timeouts included), ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG and UNCLASSIFIED (`ErrSendKeysWhileRelayed` and `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` included), and any STATE, LAUNCH_FAILURE or DIRECTORY name not named above → `transient` (`reconnectTransientLine`, naming the class); the wrapper has raised the error's outage, armed the persona's retry timer and reported an UNCLASSIFIED answer to its unclassified-error episode.

       No answer posts a spawn-failure notice, records a `spawn-failed` entry or counts anything, and nothing is typed on any path but success. The ladder maps the answer. A `dead-session`, whatever its cause, takes the dead-session route (`deadSessionRoute`, b.jg5 SRJ-611): one line, `deadSessionRouteLine`, `[slack] spawnForPersona: dead session for <ref> (state=<state>) — <evidence>[; the restart path carried in <carried evidence>]; the path <holds dead evidence|holds no dead evidence>; recovering via resume/fresh-spawn (b.jg5 SRJ-611)`, naming the route's own cause (`cause=tmux-gone: dead evidence (GONE-based)`, or `cause=row-not-interactive: not dead evidence`, `cause=row-absent: not dead evidence`) and any verdict the restart path carried into the launch, then `resumeOrFreshSpawn(..., { reconcileMissingFirst: true })` (see the note below) with the evidence the path holds ([Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611)), whose resume or spawn decides what holds the persona's name (agent-director classifies any leftover session, and a CONFLICT there latches the persona). A `transient` (`transientReconnectResult`, one `transientReconnectLine`) answers `failed` marked `stopping` after a re-check stop; `latched` when the reconnect latched or found the persona latched, or the latched query answers it latched; and otherwise `retrying` (b.jg5 SRJ-1015, which `launchSession` answers `'refused'`). Nothing more is called after a `transient` answer. The dialog approver's Enter `send-keys` is another site, with its own handling (**Pre-session dialog approval** below).
     - `working` → `waitForWaitingAndReconnect(...)` runs an up-front `findMissing({})` sweep via the shared `reconcileMissingSweep` helper (b.m4r — see note below), then polls `client.status(...)` until `waiting`, then sendKeys. While the row reads `working`, the wait also reads the persona's pane and, when it sits idle, the session's transcript, and a row that evidence shows stale is reconnected the same way (b.f2b, see note below). A `'dead-session'` verdict likewise takes the dead-session route, with the wait's cause (`waitForWaitingAndReconnectWithCause`, `WaitDeadSession`): the reconnect's own, `row-absent` for an absent row, or `row-read-finished` with the state read; only the reconnect's `tmux-gone` is dead evidence. Both `status` reads go through the shared own-row `status` read ([The shared own-row `status` read](#the-shared-own-row-status-read-bjg5-srj-115)): an UNUSABLE_NAME answer there, or the persona's own row reading `pending` with no launch start (b.jg5 SRJ-513), latches the persona and ends the wait `latched` (a latched wait, below), never `'dead-session'`. `ErrSpawnNotFound` there gives `'dead-session'`, and any other `status` error is transient: the wait goes on, and never answers `'transient'` for it (b.jg5 SRJ-605; **b.ecw terminal verdicts**, below). The wait's reconnect is the same one-`send-keys` reconnect, with the row state the wait read just before as its last read (`waiting`, or `working` for a stale row), and its answer is the wait's, unchanged. The wait answers `'transient'` for that reconnect's `transient`, for a refused findMissing sweep and for a stop its evidence read's version re-check decided; the ladder maps it as the `waiting` branch maps the reconnect's (`stopping`, `latched` or `retrying`), and a `'dead-session'` the same way too. No `working`-branch outcome records a `spawn-failed` entry. A `'not-reconnected'` verdict (the wait ended with the session alive and nothing typed) returns the action `not-reconnected`; `reconnected` means `/mcp reconnect` was typed. Right before the wait the ladder calls `hooks.onWorkingRowWait` (`LaunchHooks`, given only to the ladder a `spawnForPersona` call starts, never to a call that joins one), where the start pass parks the launch (b.f2b, see the parked-launch note below).
     - **b.4dk dead-session recovery — `reconcileMissingFirst`.** After a reboot/pod-resume a `waiting`/`working` row is frozen live-state but its tmux session is gone. AD's `resume` verb only accepts a terminal (`ended`/`missing`) row, so on such a row it throws `ErrSpawnNotResumable`, which takes the not-resumable step (above) and is never by itself a reason to kill. When `reconcileMissingFirst` is set (only the dead-session route of the `waiting` and `working` branches sets it, for every cause, dead evidence or not; b.jg5 SRJ-611 narrows only the evidence the route carries, never this run), `resumeOrFreshSpawn` runs a `findMissing({})` sweep via the shared `reconcileMissingSweep` helper before `resume`. AD's per-row, evidence-based sweep (requires agent-director ≥ 0.8.0, plan b.93m t1.93m.hp: degraded-mode guard removed) can move a row whose process is gone to `missing`, so the subsequent `resume` succeeds and restores the pre-reboot transcript (provided the row passes the `config_dir` guard, which runs after this sweep). Skipped when `resume_enabled=false`. A refused sweep (UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG or UNCLASSIFIED, b.jg5 SRJ-105) answers `failed`, which the launch answers as `retrying` when the timer was armed, before the `config_dir` guard and the resume: a resume of the still-live row would answer `ErrSpawnNotResumable`. Any other `findMissing` error (UNUSABLE_NAME, for example) → fall through to `resume` anyway (an `ErrSpawnNotResumable` then takes the not-resumable step). A persona latched once the sweep is done (`FIND_MISSING_LATCHED`: the run's `get` of its own row in `unverified_ids` read the `provenance_conflict` note, or the latch answers it latched, b.jg5 SRJ-120, SRJ-502) answers `latched` with one line, `[slack] spawnForPersona: <ref> is latched after the findMissing sweep before resume — not resuming; nothing more is called for it (b.jg5 SRJ-502)`, and gets no further call: no resume, sequence or spawn. The `ended`/`missing` collision branch above does NOT set the flag (row already terminal).
     - **b.m4r `working`-row stall — up-front `findMissing` sweep.** A bot killed mid-turn (its tmux session ended under it) leaves its AD row at `working`. Its `SessionEnd` does fire, but agent-director only soft-refreshes the row (`working` → `working`): it marks a row `ended` only for the `SessionEnd` reasons `logout`, `prompt_input_exit` and `exit`. The row stays `working` until a `findMissing` sweep reconciles it. Without a reconcile, `waitForWaitingAndReconnect`'s poll loop spins on `status` for the full `WAIT_FOR_WAITING_TIMEOUT_MS` window (10 min) before the timeout verdict finally returns `'dead-session'` — the channel stays down that whole time. `waitForWaitingAndReconnect` therefore runs AD's per-row, evidence-based `findMissing({})` sweep before entering the poll loop (requires agent-director ≥ 0.8.0, same b.93m t1.93m.hp capability as the `reconcileMissingFirst` path). A genuinely-dead row reconciles to `missing`, so the **first** status poll hits the ended/missing branch and returns `'dead-session'` in seconds; a genuinely-alive long-turn row is untouched by the evidence-based sweep and keeps the existing polling behavior (long-turn guard preserved). A refused sweep (UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG or UNCLASSIFIED, b.jg5 SRJ-105) ends the wait `'transient'`, before any `status` read. On any other `findMissing` error (UNUSABLE_NAME, for example), the sweep is logged and skipped and the poll loop proceeds unchanged. This prefers AD's `findMissing` verb over a CSCB-side tmux probe, mirroring `resumeOrFreshSpawn`'s `reconcileMissingFirst` branch (docs/engineering-guide.md, "Avoiding Duplicated Effort"). The sweep leaves a live session's row alone, so a `working` row that is stale while its session runs idle is handled by the b.f2b positive-idle rule below, not here.
     - **b.f2b stale `working` row — the positive-idle rule.** agent-director can leave a row `working` after the turn ended, with the session idle at its prompt, and nothing moves it back. The pane alone can't prove the session idle: Claude Code 2.1.280 can draw a live turn with no spinner (an API retry or stall shows static rows with no glyph and no timer). So while the row reads `working`, the wait reads its evidence every `WORKING_ROW_READ_INTERVAL_MS` (5 s; the first status poll reads at once, later polls in between read nothing, because every agent-director call goes through one queue shared by every persona) and folds it into the wait's run (`staleWorkingRowIsIdle`, `WorkingPaneWatch`):
       - **The pane.** `readPane` (last `FULL_PANE_READ_LINES` = 40 lines, `readWorkingPane`, through the shared read-pane `readPersonaOwnPane`; see [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104), **The shared read-pane**). A CONFLICT answer latches the persona with the refused operation "P's next check or recovery" (b.jg5 SRJ-501), and an UNUSABLE_NAME answer through the unusable-name entry (b.jg5 SRJ-512), each with the wait's last read (b.jg5 SRJ-117); a persona already latched is not read. Either way the wait ends `latched` at once, with no further call and nothing typed (b.jg5 SRJ-608; a latched wait, below). An UNCLASSIFIED answer carrying the reader's stop mark (its `ErrInvalidFlags` version re-check decided that the server stops, b.jg5 SRJ-205) logs one line and ends the wait `'transient'` with the stop noted, no further call and nothing typed; the ladder answers a `failed` result marked `stopping`, with no spawn-failure notice and no `spawn-failed` entry, and `launchSession` answers `'skipped'`. Every other failed read (GONE, an absent row, UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG, any other UNCLASSIFIED) is no evidence, and the wait goes on. `classifyWorkingPane` reads it as `prompt` when its bottom 12 lines show a dialog, anchored to Claude Code's layout (`paneShowsDialog`): a numbered option list (an option `1.` and, below it, an option `2.`) with the `❯` cursor on one of its options, plus a question line ending in `?` above it, a dialog option or footer (`DIALOG_NEEDLES`: a permission dialog's deny option, the select-menu footers, the pre-session dialogs' options) on or below it, or its options inside the dialog's box (`│`). Otherwise it is `busy` for Claude Code's spinner line anywhere (`BUSY_SPINNER_LINE_RE`, in the spinner's own shape: at column 0 a spinner glyph, a space, a short message with no ellipsis, which can be several words (a custom `spinnerVerbs` verb or a task's `activeForm`), then an ellipsis ending the line or followed by ` (` and the turn's status; a line that starts with `●`, which Linux also draws before every reply and tool call, counts only as a single word and an ellipsis ending the line, or with a status that starts with an elapsed time, a token arrow or `thinking`), for `to interrupt` or `esc to cancel` in the bottom lines (`BUSY_PANE_NEEDLES`), or for an API retry row there (`BUSY_API_RETRY_ROWS`: `No response from the API after … · retrying` with its `A proxy or gateway that buffers…` line, `Rate limit reached · Retrying in`, `Waiting for API response · will retry in`, `· attempt n/m`); `blank` with no text; else `idle`. A prompt outranks a busy sign. The patterns are verified against Claude Code 2.1.280.
       - **The transcript**, read only when the pane is `idle` (`readPersonaTranscript`): the row is fetched through the shared own-row read (`readPersonaOwnRow`, one `get` through `withOutageDetection`), its transcript located with the persona's effective `claude_config_dir` (`locateTranscript`: the row's `jsonl_path` when it names the row's `claude_session_id`, else `<claude_config_dir>/projects/<cwd slug>/<claude_session_id>.jsonl`), and its last 256 KiB read (`readTranscriptTurnState`, `src/session-transcript.ts`). It is `ended` when its last conversation entry is a completed turn (Claude's final reply, or the user's interrupt marker), else `open` (a Stop hook's context or blocking error after the reply keeps the turn open); an absent row (`ErrSpawnNotFound`, reason `its agent-director row is absent (ErrSpawnNotFound)`), a failed `get`, a row that names no transcript or a file that can't be read is `unreadable`. A `get` that latched the persona (its own row reading `pending` with no launch start, b.jg5 SRJ-513, a `provenance_conflict` note, b.jg5 SRJ-114, or an UNUSABLE_NAME answer, b.jg5 SRJ-512) gives no evidence and nothing more is read; the wait then ends (a latched wait, below). The state the `get` read (the row's state, no row, or `unreadable` for an UNUSABLE_NAME answer) becomes the wait's last read (b.jg5 SRJ-501).
       - **The run** (`foldWorkingPaneRun`, the positive-idle rule). An `idle` pane read with an `ended` transcript continues an idle run only while the screen and the transcript's snapshot (path, device, inode, size, mtime) are both unchanged, and otherwise starts one. A `prompt` pane continues or starts a prompt run. A `busy` or `blank` pane, a failed pane read, or an idle pane whose transcript is `open` or `unreadable` ends the run: no evidence.
       - An idle run spanning `STALE_WORKING_WINDOW_MS` (60 s) means the row is stale: the reconnect, as the `waiting` branch makes it (with `working` as its last read), whatever `session_restart_delay` is (the reconnect is part of the launch, not an auto-restart). A live turn, an API retry included, never ends its transcript with a completed turn, so it is never taken for idle and never typed into (the b.rmy invariant).
       - A prompt run spanning the window is logged and reported through the `blocked-on-prompt` not-connected notice (saying whether auto-restart is disabled), once per wait; nothing is typed and the wait goes on.
       - A failed pane read is no evidence: the wait's first failure is logged and the wait goes on. An idle pane whose transcript gives no evidence is logged, again only when the reason changes, and the wait goes on.
       - Each poll that reads the row `working` without reconnecting it is one more deferral in the persona's run on the row (`noteWorkingRowDeferral`, the run kept per persona in `workingRowDeferredSince` and shared with the restart path); any other state ends the run. Once the run has lasted `UNPROVEN_IDLE_NOTICE_AFTER_MS` (10 min) from its first deferral, the `unproven-idle` not-connected notice is raised (*Not connected*: its session reads working but CSCB can't prove it's idle, so it won't type into it), whatever `session_restart_delay` is, once per episode; the wait goes on.
     - **b.f2b a cancelled wait.** The persona's teardown cancels the wait (`cancelWorkingRowWait`, see [Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-307)). Each wait registers itself per persona (`workingRowWaits`); a cancel sets its flag and wakes it from its poll sleep (`sleepUnlessCancelled`). The wait checks the flag after each agent-director call, types nothing once it is set, logs that it was cancelled and returns `'cancelled'`, which the ladder reports as `not-reconnected`. A cancel that finds a launch in flight that hasn't started its wait yet records the key (`cancelledLaunchWaits`, forgotten when that launch settles), so a wait it starts is cancelled from its first check.
     - **b.jg5 SRJ-502 a latched wait.** At the same points as the cancel check, after each agent-director call the wait makes (its `find-missing` sweeps, `status` reads, pane reads and transcript `get`s), it asks whether its persona is latched (`personaLatchedNow`: the launch gate's reading of the installed latch, where a query that throws or a record that can't be read counts as latched; false with no latch installed). A latch its own transcript `get`, pane read or poll or timeout `status` read set (a `pending` row with no launch start, b.jg5 SRJ-513, a note, an UNUSABLE_NAME answer, b.jg5 SRJ-512, or the pane read's CONFLICT answer, b.jg5 SRJ-501), one the `get` after a `find-missing` run's `unverified_ids` set (b.jg5 SRJ-120; its sweep then answers `FIND_MISSING_LATCHED`), or one set elsewhere ends the wait with `latched` (`WAIT_OUTCOME_LATCHED`) and one line, `[slack] waitForWaitingAndReconnect: <ref> is latched — the wait ends; nothing more is called and nothing is typed (b.jg5 SRJ-502)`: no further call, nothing typed and no not-connected notice. The ladder answers `latched`. A cancelled wait still answers `cancelled`.
     - **b.f2b a wait that ends without a reconnect.** Every path that ends the wait with the session alive and nothing typed returns `'not-reconnected'` (`'ok'` always means `/mcp reconnect` was typed): a transition to `pending`, `ask_user` or `check_permission`; the timeout, when the row is live but not `waiting`; and the timeout, when its `status` read fails with any error but `ErrSpawnNotFound` (b.jg5 SRJ-605). A row that reads `waiting` at the timeout is reconnected. Each of these give-up lines ends with what actually happens next for the restart delay in effect (`reportWaitEndedDisconnected`, its line built by the exported `waitEndedDisconnectedLine` from a `WaitEndedReport`: `waitEndedOnStateReport`, `waitTimedOutLiveReport` or `waitTimedOutUnreadReport`): with auto-restart on, the health check's recovery; with `session_restart_delay` 0, that nothing will reconnect the persona, and the not-connected notice is raised (once per episode; see Health-Check Poller): `blocked-on-prompt` when the row ended at `ask_user` or `check_permission`, `unproven-idle` when the timeout finds it `working`, otherwise `auto-restart-disabled` with a fixed, token-free cause (for a row read in a state, `waitEndedOnStateReport` and `waitTimedOutLiveReport` pick the prompt or the `auto-restart-disabled` notice through the module-private `waitEndedNotice`, which is not exported; for a failed timeout read, `waitTimedOutUnreadReport` gives the cause itself: that agent-director could not report the persona's state when CSCB stopped waiting for it). At any delay the timeout on a `working` row is one more deferral, so a run that has lasted `UNPROVEN_IDLE_NOTICE_AFTER_MS` raises the `unproven-idle` notice there too. The lines are listed in docs/engineering-guide.md, Log Messages.
     - **b.ecw terminal verdicts key on agent-director's row, never on the tmux session (b.jg5 SRJ-605).** Every terminal branch of `waitForWaitingAndReconnect` decides off agent-director's row for the claude process (AD ≥ 0.8.0: `findMissing` verdicts per-row and evidence-based); the wait makes no tmux probe. Where it answers `'dead-session'`, the recovery's resume or spawn (`resumeOrFreshSpawn`) decides what holds the persona's name: agent-director classifies any leftover session, and a CONFLICT there latches the persona (b.jg5 SRJ-501). Each `'dead-session'` end carries one cause (`WaitDeadSession`, b.jg5 SRJ-611): a row read (`row-read-finished`, `row-absent`) is not dead evidence ([Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611)).
       - **ended/missing branch (in-loop):** keys on the process. `ended` means the process exited with a `SessionEnd` reason agent-director marks ended (see the b.m4r note above); `missing`, after the up-front sweep, is agent-director's sweep verdict on the row. One line, `waitRowFinishedLine` (`[slack] waitForWaitingAndReconnect: <ref>'s row reads state=<state> — dead session (cause=row-read-finished: not dead evidence); the recovery's resume or spawn decides what holds its name (b.ecw, b.jg5 SRJ-605, SRJ-611)`), then `'dead-session'` directly with the cause `row-read-finished` and the state read — **no tmux probe**. A finished row is not proof that the worker is gone, so the verdict routes it to `resumeOrFreshSpawn`, whose resume or spawn decides; a `resume` there that answers `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` because the name is still taken is one counted launch failure, and nothing is killed because of it (the `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` bullet below).
       - **timeout branch:** keys on the process via a **fresh** `reconcileMissingSweep` (the 10s memo has long expired at the 10-minute deadline) + one `status` call. A refused sweep (b.jg5 SRJ-105) answers `'transient'`, and no `status` call follows. `ended`/`missing` → `'dead-session'`, cause `row-read-finished` (`waitRowFinishedLine`, its timeout form `[slack] waitForWaitingAndReconnect: timed out for <ref> after <ms>ms — its row reads state=<state> — dead session (cause=row-read-finished: not dead evidence); …`); `waiting` → reconnect (b.f2b: the turn ended at the deadline); any other live state (working/ask_user/check_permission/pending) → `'not-reconnected'` (b.f2b), the process left alive (a process mid-long-turn is not an error — the b.rmy/b.3ce long-turn guard, keyed on the process). `ErrSpawnNotFound` → `'dead-session'`, as at the poll (below). An UNUSABLE_NAME answer, or the row reading `pending` with no launch start, latches the persona and ends the wait `latched` (b.jg5 SRJ-512, SRJ-513). Any other `status` error (UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG, UNCLASSIFIED, `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` included) → `'not-reconnected'` through `reportWaitEndedDisconnected` (`waitTimedOutUnreadReport`: the line names the error's class and no tmux session), never `'dead-session'` or `'transient'`, so an agent-director outage can't manufacture a `'dead-session'` (the b.rmy invariant) or a counted failure.
       - **ErrSpawnNotFound branch (in-loop and at the timeout):** the row is absent. One line (`waitRowAbsentLine`, naming `cause=row-absent: not dead evidence`), then `'dead-session'` directly, cause `row-absent`, with no tmux probe: the recovery's spawn classifies any leftover session.
       - **Any other `status` error (in-loop):** transient (b.jg5 SRJ-605): UNAVAILABLE, a timeout, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG and UNCLASSIFIED, `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` included. The wait sleeps its poll interval and polls again, with no post, no result of its own, no `failed` and nothing counted toward `recordFailure`. It logs its first failed read (`waitPollStatusErrorLine`, naming the error's class) and again only when the class changes. The wrapper (`withOutageDetection`) has raised the error's outage (`ad-unreachable`, also for `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`; `tmux-unavailable`; `ad-config-malformed`), armed the persona's retry timer and reported an UNCLASSIFIED answer to its unclassified-error episode, as at any row read in a launch attempt (b.jg5 SRJ-105, SRJ-301), so the launch's result follows the wait's outcome, never `refused`. A refused sweep, up front or at the timeout, is still a refusal (above).
     - **b.m4r shared memoized sweep — `sharedFindMissingSweep` (b.jg5 SRJ-120).** Every `findMissing({})` call goes through one memoized, single-flight core, `sharedFindMissingSweep` in `src/session-manager.ts`, never `client.findMissing({})` inline. A persona's runs go through the module-private `reconcileMissingSweep`, one call through `withOutageDetection` for that persona; the start sweep's post-kill run (`runStartSweepPostKillFindMissing`, step 4.6, over every row the sweep gave a kill, whatever its outcome) calls the start sweep's client directly and acts for no persona. The callers are this `working`-row wait's up-front and timeout sweeps, `resumeOrFreshSpawn`'s `reconcileMissingFirst`, the tick/restart escalate-dead path (the exported `sweepDeadTmuxChannelWithCause`, which the reconnect adapter calls, and `sweepDeadTmuxChannel`, the same without its answer; both log their unconditional operator line first), the two b.jdc prompt-row callers through `reconcileAndReadRowState` (the sweep, then one `status` read of the row: the ladder's prompt row whose one-line `read-pane` answered GONE or found the row absent, and the restart path's deferrals on a prompt row once they have run for 10 min), and the start sweep's post-kill run. Every one of them makes an ordinary run.
       - **Ordinary runs** (`FIND_MISSING_RUN_ORDINARY`, module-private). An ordinary caller joins the run in flight, if there is one, a bypassing run included. Otherwise it reuses the memoized result when that run's call resolved less than `FIND_MISSING_MEMO_TTL_MS` (10 s) ago, measured on the session manager's clock (`_now`), with no call and no `get`. Otherwise it starts a run. This only sheds load: on a fleet restart (`startupSessionManager` at `concurrency=3`) every `working`-row collision and each `reconcileMissingFirst` would otherwise fire its own whole-store sweep, and after a reboot that wipes `/tmp` (b.nk5) every persona escalates dead-tmux at once; one shared run reconciles the whole store for all of them.
       - **Bypassing runs** (`FIND_MISSING_RUN_BYPASSING`, module-private). The exported entry `bypassingFindMissingSweep(key, logPrefix, nextStepGetKey?, call?)` always starts a new run through `withOutageDetection` for `key`, whatever is memoized or in flight, for a caller that must see a run made after its own step (a memo can predate that step). The new run becomes the run in flight, so ordinary callers arriving meanwhile join it, and its result is memoized for later ordinary callers like any other run's. Its callers are the live-row sequence, the old-life wait, the pending-row rule ([The pending-row rule](#the-pending-row-rule-bjg5-srj-410)) and the latch's two (b.jg5 SRJ-506): the run after a re-check's probe found the condition cleared (log prefix `latch-recheck`) and the run after a clear by step 1 (log prefix `latch-clear`), both with no `nextStepGetKey` ([How a latch clears and relatches](#how-a-latch-clears-and-relatches-bjg5-srj-506-srj-1005)). For the first, P is still latched, so the run answers it `FIND_MISSING_LATCHED`, which that caller reads as no refusal; the second runs inside a recovery attempt of the now unlatched P, so its refusal arms P's retry timer. Each of the sequence's runs is a bypassing run with the persona's key as `nextStepGetKey`, since the sequence's next step is its own `get` of that row ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717), started from the collision ladder's replacement sites). The wait's runs (b.jg5 SRJ-811, log prefix `old-life-wait`) are made for the old key, with the old key as `nextStepGetKey` only when the old row is a configured persona's own `cscb_<key>`, and pass the entry's fourth argument (`FindMissingCallOptions`): the wrapper options that arm nothing for the old key, and a failure sink that records the run's class for the wait's end handler ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809), **The wait's steps**). Its run line reads `bypassing findMissing sweep` where an ordinary run's reads `findMissing sweep`, and so do its failure and refusal lines. It answers as an ordinary run does (the result, `FIND_MISSING_REFUSED`, `FIND_MISSING_LATCHED` or `undefined`, below); a persona already latched before the run gets `FIND_MISSING_LATCHED` too, whatever the run found, while a refusal still answers `FIND_MISSING_REFUSED`. It never throws.
       - **Which result the memo keeps.** Runs are numbered as they start. A run that succeeds is memoized only when no run that started after it has been memoized already, so an older run resolving later never overwrites a newer result, and it clears the in-flight slot only while it is still the run there. Each run logs its line once, with its starter's prefix and reference: `[slack] <prefix>: findMissing sweep for <ref> — count=<n> ids=[…] unverified=<n> unverified_ids=[…]`.
       - **Failures are never memoized.** A failed run, of either kind, clears only its own in-flight slot, leaves any earlier memoized result in place and makes no `get`; the next ordinary caller starts a new run. A refused run (UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG or UNCLASSIFIED, b.jg5 SRJ-105) answers `FIND_MISSING_REFUSED` to its starter and to each joiner alike, a bypassing run's included, each logging its own refusal line, and each caller stops its attempt (see the `refusalAt` sites above). Any other failure logs `[slack] <prefix>: findMissing sweep failed for <ref>: <failure> — proceeding` (`bypassing findMissing sweep failed` for a bypassing run), and the caller goes on. Sharing a run never changes whose retry timer arms (b.jg5 SRJ-301): the persona that starts a run reports its failure through its own `withOutageDetection`, and a persona that joins a run someone else started (another persona's, or the start sweep's direct call) reports the failure under its own key (`reportAgentDirectorError(key, err, 'find-missing')`), which arms only when the joiner runs inside its own launch or recovery attempt; when the run failed with ENVIRONMENT (`ErrTmuxNotAvailable`), the joiner first raises its own `tmux-unavailable` (b.jg5 SRJ-311) through `raiseTmuxUnavailable(key, err)`, which picks the onset from the error, as the starter's wrapper does for the starter, and with CONFIG (`ErrConfigMalformed`) its own `ad-config-malformed` the same way (b.jg5 SRJ-316). The start sweep acts for no persona, so its own failure is reported for none and is never a refusal.
       - **The not-judged reading.** `readFindMissingRow(result, id, stateBefore)` (pure) reads one row of a result: in `ids`, marked `missing` (`marked-missing`); in `unverified_ids`, judged and left live (`judged-left-live`); in neither, `not-judged` when its state before the run was `pending` (the row is inside agent-director's grace period, or its launch's worker process is alive), else `judged-alive`. A not-judged row means retry later, whatever time has passed, and is never a reason to escalate, alert or kill. The start sweep's post-kill line reads its killed rows this way (step 4).
       - **One `get` after `unverified_ids`.** When a run the server makes resolves (never at a memo reuse), and before its starter or any joiner goes on, each configured persona's own row listed in `unverified_ids` (`cscb_<key>`, with `<key>` a persona of the applied configuration now, by the installed configured-persona query) is read with one `get` through the shared own-row read (`readPersonaOwnRow`, through `withOutageDetection` for that persona, whatever persona the run was made for): each persona once, all at once, and the run waits for every read to settle before any caller goes on. Two rows are skipped. One is the row of the starter's next-step key (`nextStepGetKey`, which only the bypassing entry passes; a joiner's is not considered): that path's next step is itself a `get` of the row. The other is the row of a persona already latched when the run resolves (`personaLatchedNow`; a latched query that throws counts as latched): it gets no `get` and no latch call, so the persona is not relatched and nothing is posted for it, and its own caller still gets `FIND_MISSING_LATCHED`. A `provenance_conflict` note on a row read this way latches its persona, as at any shared read (see [Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)); an absent `get` changes nothing. A `get` that fails with any other error never fails the run, is never memoized as a failure and never stops the other `get`s; the run carries it to its callers (`refusedReads`), and only the caller whose persona's own row it was acts on it: a refusal answers that caller `FIND_MISSING_REFUSED` with its `post-sweep get refused` line, while an UNUSABLE_NAME answer latches that persona, as the note does, and its caller gets `FIND_MISSING_LATCHED`, except in the start sweep's run (below) (see **Errors** under [Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)); for every other caller it only shows in the line below. A refusal answers `FIND_MISSING_REFUSED` whether or not the persona is latched. Any other row in `unverified_ids` (another caller's, a pre-persona row, the `cscb_<key>` row of a key outside the applied configuration) gets no `get`, and a note on it is not acted on: it is not CSCB's to act on or post about. With no query installed, no row is read. When at least one listed persona was read or skipped, one line lists every one of them, in `unverified_ids` order, with what its read answered or that it was skipped as already latched: `[slack] <prefix>: after the findMissing sweep for <ref> — one get of each configured persona's own row in unverified_ids: persona=<key> <read|latched|absent|refused (<failure>)|skipped (latched)>, … (b.jg5 SRJ-120)`. With no configured persona listed, no line is logged. **The start sweep's run** (`FindMissingSweepOptions.startSweepRun`, which only `runStartSweepPostKillFindMissing` passes; a run another caller started keeps that caller's reads) makes its post-run `get`s with `unusableNameRoutedIn` set (`'the start sweep'`), so an UNUSABLE_NAME answer there latches nothing (b.jg5 SRJ-512, SRJ-1002): `readPersonaOwnRow` logs `[slack] reconcileOrphans: post-sweep get for persona=<key>: <failure> — UNUSABLE NAME met in the start sweep: routed to the server log; nothing latches (b.jg5 SRJ-512, SRJ-1002)` (`<failure>` through `describeAgentDirectorFailure`) and answers `refused` carrying the error, so the persona shows as `refused (<failure>)` in the line above; carried to a caller, it is no refusal (`postRunGetRefusal` answers false) and that caller goes on as after any read. The note and launch-start decisions still latch in that run. The start sweep also passes `postRunGetsGo` (`FindMissingSweepOptions.postRunGetsGo`, the negation of its shutdown stop), asked once when the run it started returns: an answer other than true, or a throw, makes none of the post-run `get`s, and the run logs `[slack] <prefix>: after the <run> — no post-sweep get is made: its caller stopped (b.jg5 SRJ-120, SRJ-714)` instead; nothing is latched or refused. With the option absent, as for every other caller, the `get`s are made.
       - **A latched persona stops its path (b.jg5 SRJ-502).** A persona's caller gets `FIND_MISSING_LATCHED` instead of the result when its persona is latched once the sweep is done: the run's `get` latched it, or the latch answers it latched (`personaLatchedNow`), asked after a memo reuse, a run, a join or a failure that is no refusal. It then calls nothing more for the persona: `reconcileMissingFirst` answers `latched` with no resume (see the b.4dk note above), `reconcileAndReadRowState` reads no row and logs `[slack] <prefix>: <ref> is latched after the findMissing sweep — its row is not read; nothing more is called for it (b.jg5 SRJ-502)` (its own row read after the sweep goes through the shared own-row `status` read, and one that latches the persona answers `FIND_MISSING_LATCHED` too, after its own latch line; so does a persona latched elsewhere while that read was awaited, whatever it gave, through `latchedAfterOwnRowRead`, which logs `[slack] <prefix>: <ref> is latched after its status read after the findMissing sweep — nothing more is called for it (b.jg5 SRJ-502)`), after which the ladder's prompt row answers `latched` and the restart path's prompt-row deferral answers `latched` (Auto-Restart step 3, **Prompt rows**), and the `working`-row wait ends with its latched line (a latched wait, above). The escalate-dead sweep reports a latched persona as an unrefused sweep, and the restart run's latch check after the reconnect stops it (Auto-Restart step 3).
       - **Against the health-check tick.** The 10 s window is far shorter than the ~120 s tick cadence, so the following tick's escalate-dead sweeps run again. A swept row is not sure to read dead afterwards, though: agent-director may leave it live (in `unverified_ids`, or, when `pending`, not judged), and it then stays live for further ticks, each of which tries again. The `reconcileMissingFirst` and `working`-row callers are clustered within one start rather than spaced by ticks, so they benefit from the memo directly.
     - `check_permission` / `ask_user` → never typed into (b.rmy). **b.jdc:** a session that dies under a prompt keeps its row in that state (agent-director only refreshes a row at SessionEnd and leaves reaping to its findMissing sweep), so the ladder (`launchOnPromptRow`, b.jg5 SRJ-607) first makes one `read-pane` of the persona's own row through the shared read-pane (`readPersonaOwnPane`, site `spawnForPersona: prompt row`, `PROBE_PANE_READ_LINES` = 1 line, the collision `get`'s state as the recorded state; see [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104), **The shared read-pane**), with no tmux call. Its outcome decides (b.jg5 SRJ-117's b.jdc ladder-action column):
       - **A pane** → no-op, as before (the poller relays the prompt; if the persona stays disconnected, the restart path reports it).
       - **UNAVAILABLE** (timeouts included), **CONFIG** (the wrapper has raised `ad-config-malformed`, b.jg5 SRJ-316) **or UNCLASSIFIED** (b.jg5 SRJ-105) → taken as alive: no-op, with one line naming the class (`promptRowLadderNoActionLine`).
       - **ENVIRONMENT** (the wrapper has raised `tmux-unavailable`, b.jg5 SRJ-311) → no-op, with one line naming the class (the same builder).
       - **UNCLASSIFIED carrying the stop mark** (`stopping`: the reader's `ErrInvalidFlags` version re-check decided that the server stops, b.jg5 SRJ-204, SRJ-205) → a `failed` result marked `stopping`, with its own line (`promptRowLadderStoppingLine`): no post, no `spawn-failed` entry, nothing counted.
       - **CONFLICT or UNUSABLE_NAME** (the reader has latched the persona with the collision `get`'s state: CONFLICT with the refused operation "P's next check or recovery", b.jg5 SRJ-501; UNUSABLE_NAME with `none`, b.jg5 SRJ-512), **or a persona already latched**, which the reader does not read → `latched` (`promptRowLadderLatchedLine`), nothing typed.
       - **GONE** (`ErrTmuxCaptureFailed`: agent-director found no pane of the row's launch) **or the row absent** (`ErrSpawnNotFound`, which takes the GONE column without being a GONE, b.jg5 SRJ-117) → one line (`promptRowLadderNoPaneLine`), then the latch is asked (`personaLatchedNow`, b.jg5 SRJ-502): a persona latched while the read was awaited answers `latched` with no sweep. Otherwise the memoized `reconcileMissingSweep` runs, then the row is read again: `ended` or `missing` is a dead session, recovered through `resumeOrFreshSpawn` (for a retired key a reuse spawn, never a `resume`, b.jg5 SRJ-805, SRJ-607; [Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-bjg5-srj-806-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-407)) after one `deadSessionRouteLine` naming its cause: `prompt-row-ladder-gone` after a GONE, dead evidence, and `row-absent` after an absent row, not dead evidence ([Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611)), handed on with any verdict the restart path carried in; any other state, or a failed read, is a no-op left to the restart path (`promptRowLadderAfterSweepLine`). A refused sweep (b.jg5 SRJ-105) reads nothing and answers `failed`, which the launch answers as `retrying` when the timer was armed: no resume and no launch. A persona latched once the sweep is done (b.jg5 SRJ-120, SRJ-502) gets no row read and its latched line (`reconcileAndReadRowState`, see the b.m4r note above), and the ladder answers `latched`: no further call, no resume, sequence or launch.
     - `pending` → the ladder's `pending` step (`ladderPendingRowStep`; b.jg5 SRJ-409, SRJ-411, SRJ-1504), which the not-resumable step and a resume site's replacement also hand a row they re-read `pending` (above). It runs the one pending-row step (`pendingRowStep`, with `statusOnlySite` false; [Covered and uncovered rows](#covered-and-uncovered-rows-bjg5-srj-409-srj-411)): the row compared with the persona (`compareRowToPersona`), then decided by `decidePendingRowCover`. A row that is not covered (its `cwd` differs from the persona's working directory by real path, its `config_dir` label is missing or differs, or it is a retired key's old life with no "new life has begun" mark) logs `uncoveredPendingRowLine` and goes to the replace step (`replacePersonaRow`, with the retired-key flag for an old life), which starts the live-row sequence (a `pending` row is live; the sequence waits until G past its launch start), and the ladder answers `sequence-waiting`. An undecided row arms the persona's retry timer in pending-only mode with one `undecidedPendingRowLine`: a `claude_config_dir` that cannot be resolved also keeps its deferral (`deferForUnresolvedConfigDir`, the launch answers `deferred`, bug b.g57), and a `cwd` that cannot be compared answers `no-op`. A covered row is left as it is (`no-op`, `[slack] spawnForPersona: no action — state=pending for <ref>`), with no kill and no launch, and the persona's retry timer armed in pending-only mode (b.jg5 SRJ-409). At the collision `get` the `cwd` guard above has already compared the `cwd`, and a persona working directory with no real path fails the launch there (`failed`, the `cwd-unreachable` outage, b.av2 SR-6.4) before this step. A configured persona's own `pending` row with no launch start never reaches here: the read latched it (the step would answer `latched`).
     - **b.wrb `ErrJsonlMissing` diagnostic — legible amnesia (b.jg5 SRJ-712).** When resume throws `ErrJsonlMissing`, `diagnoseJsonlMissing` runs before the no-transcript reuse spawn, while the row it reads is still the old life's (`jsonl_path` / `claude_session_id` / `cwd` / `started_at`; the reuse resets them), to make the loss legible. It is a sibling of the b.zak safeguard (step 4a-quater), which runs *before* the resume path; this one runs *inside* it, on the row resume actually failed to open. Its row fetch is the shared own-row read (`readPersonaOwnRow`, b.jg5 SRJ-114). Never throws. Its texts are built from exported constants: the entry classes `JSONL_TRANSCRIPT_LOST_ENTRY_CLASS` (`jsonl-transcript-lost-on-resume`) and `JSONL_DIAGNOSIS_INCONCLUSIVE_ENTRY_CLASS` (`jsonl-diagnosis-inconclusive`), and the wording `JSONL_DIAGNOSIS_REUSE_WORDING`, "brought up fresh by a reuse spawn of the same instance, and its row is kept (its history archived to the earlier life)": the log lines and entry details say "the persona is " + that wording, the notices "I was " + it. The log line and, at start, the entry are written when the verdict is reached; a verdict's notice is held back and posted by the no-transcript step only when the reuse spawn answers `spawned`, and dropped otherwise (the entry stays; a later attempt makes its own diagnosis). Two things happen:
       - **Path + provenance logging.** AD's `ErrJsonlMissing` description enumerates every transcript candidate it stat'd as `<source> <path> (<stat error>)`, joined by `"; "` — a capability AD's bug `b.1ba` delivered, introduced in agent-director v0.10.0. When the description carries that enumeration, `parseJsonlMissingCandidates` parses it and logs the candidates verbatim, labelled *paths+sources reported by agent-director*. The parsed source tokens are `persisted` (AD's recorded `jsonl_path`), `fallback` (its `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`-aware recomputed path), and `history` (an archived `session_history` entry). When the description does **not** match that shape — a pre-0.10.0 AD, or any AD whose message wording differs — the parse yields nothing and CSCB reconstructs the candidates locally instead: the persisted `jsonl_path` column plus a `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`-aware fallback via `resolveJsonlPath` and the persona's effective `claude_config_dir` (its own, else the top-level one), labelled explicitly *locally computed* so a reader never mistakes a CSCB-side reconstruction for what AD actually stat'd. The parse keys off those literal source tokens, not any version string, so it degrades cleanly in both directions. Every candidate field (source, path, note) can carry agent-director's text, so the candidate list every text of the diagnosis quotes is built once by `jsonlCandidatesText(candidates)` (b.jg5 SRJ-712, SRJ-1001): each field rendered by `renderLogMessageText` (redacted, on one line, capped), each candidate as `<source> <path> (<note>)`, joined by `"; "`, or `JSONL_NO_CANDIDATES_TEXT` (`(no transcript path could be determined)`) when there is none; the absent-row path's agent-director detail uses it too. A row's `started_at` is quoted the same way (rendered, or `(none)` when absent or empty). The log line and the startup-errors entry quote that rendered text unescaped; the notices (`jsonlTranscriptLostNoticeText(archivedSinceSpawn, pathsTried)`, `jsonlCandidatesInconclusiveNoticeText(reason, detailProvenance, candidates)`, `jsonlRowAbsentInconclusiveNoticeText(adReported)`) quote it through `renderLogMessageText` once more, so the quote as a whole is capped at `MAX_LOGGED_MESSAGE_LENGTH`, and escape it once for Slack (`escapeSlackControlCharacters`), so a path or note cannot mention `@channel` or a user.
       - **lost / never-created / inconclusive classification (b.fwu).** Using b.zak's read-only `makeDefaultArchiveCount` / `rfc3339ToEpochSeconds` helpers over `message_archive_db`, bounded by `started_at`, and the b.av2 SR-7.4 scope (as amended by b.deo SRI-704) from `personaArchiveEvidenceScope` (the same helper step 4a-quater's Layer 2 uses), `diagnoseJsonlMissing` counts archived messages only in the persona's `delivery: all` channels since `started_at` and returns one of `'lost' | 'never-created' | 'inconclusive'`. That scope and the `delivery:` wording below are declarative mode's: in fungible mode (read with `channelModeOf(config)` at the diagnosis; b.deo SRI-704) no channel is counted and a zero is never attributable, so a count always gives **inconclusive** with `FUNGIBLE_MODE_ZERO_REASON` (`unattributableZeroReason(mode)`), never **lost** or **never-created**, and no count keeps the outcome below:
         - **lost** — archive shows ≥1 message since spawn in the persona's `delivery: all` channels, real conversation history destroyed. Made operator-visible via `recordStartupError('jsonl-transcript-lost-on-resume', …)` (startup only), the log line `[slack] ErrJsonlMissing diagnostic: <ref> instance=cscb_<key>: resume threw ErrJsonlMissing and the persona is brought up fresh by a reuse spawn of the same instance, and its row is kept (its history archived to the earlier life), but the message archive holds <n> message(s) since spawn (started_at=<t>). Conversation history was LOST. Transcript candidates tried (<provenance>): <candidates>.`, **and**, once the reuse is up, a notice through the notifier to the persona's destination ("my conversation memory has been lost and I was brought up fresh by a reuse spawn of the same instance, and its row is kept (its history archived to the earlier life)").
         - **never-created** — strictly evidence-based: the archive was actually consulted and returned 0 messages since spawn, and that zero is attributable — the persona has no `delivery: mentions` channel and DMs off, so its `delivery: all` channels carry all of its traffic. The transcript was never written (Claude creates the `.jsonl` lazily on first message; expected and lossless). One quiet log line only, `[slack] ErrJsonlMissing diagnostic: <ref> instance=cscb_<key> — transcript never created (archive consulted: 0 archived messages since spawn). Nothing to lose; the persona is brought up fresh by a reuse spawn of the same instance, and its row is kept (its history archived to the earlier life). Transcript candidates tried (<provenance>): <candidates>.`
         - **inconclusive (b.fwu)** — "no evidence either way": the AD row fetch answered `ErrSpawnNotFound` (a CONFIG answer is a refusal at that `get`: no verdict, no notice, no entry), `started_at` was absent or unparseable, the count was 0 but the persona has a `delivery: mentions` channel or DMs on (b.av2 SR-7.4 as amended by b.deo SRI-704: the archive cannot attribute messages from `mentions` channels or DMs to a persona, so the zero proves nothing — `UNATTRIBUTABLE_ZERO_REASON`; a persona with no `delivery: all` channel counts 0 without the archive being consulted, so once `started_at` parses it always gets this reason, even when `message_archive_db` is not configured), `message_archive_db` is not configured, or the archive read failed. Each emits `recordStartupError('jsonl-diagnosis-inconclusive', …)` carrying the reason (`the agent-director row is absent (ErrSpawnNotFound)` / started_at absent or unparseable / zero count not attributable / archive unconfigured / archive read failed) with the log line `[slack] ErrJsonlMissing diagnostic: <ref> instance=cscb_<key>: resume threw ErrJsonlMissing and the persona is brought up fresh by a reuse spawn of the same instance, and its row is kept (its history archived to the earlier life), but diagnosis was INCONCLUSIVE — could not determine whether conversation history was lost because <reason>.` **and**, once the reuse is up, a notice through the notifier to the persona's destination, worded as *uncertainty* ("on restart I was brought up fresh by a reuse spawn of the same instance, and its row is kept (its history archived to the earlier life); I could not determine whether my prior conversation history was preserved") — deliberately distinct from the `lost` wording, since a false "your history was destroyed" is its own harm. When `message_archive_db` is unconfigured the operator message states diagnosis is impossible because no message archive is configured, with a hint to enable it.

         Any other error from the row fetch is a read error (b.jg5 SRJ-105), not an inconclusive diagnosis: `refusalAt` logs `spawnForPersona: ErrJsonlMissing diagnosis get refused for <ref>: …` and the diagnosis answers `failed`, which the launch answers as `retrying` when the timer was armed. No inconclusive notice is posted, no `jsonl-diagnosis-inconclusive` entry is recorded, and the branch makes no reuse spawn (see the `refusalAt` sites above). An error `refusalAt` does not refuse (not reached: every `get` error but `ErrSpawnNotFound` and UNUSABLE_NAME is a refusal) logs `[slack] spawnForPersona: ErrJsonlMissing diagnosis get failed for <ref>: <failure> — nothing more is called` and answers an unmarked `failed` the same way: no diagnosis, no reuse spawn, no spawn-failure notice. Only `ErrSpawnNotFound` gives an inconclusive verdict.

         A row fetch that latched the persona (a `provenance_conflict` note on its own row, b.jg5 SRJ-114, SRJ-502, or an UNUSABLE_NAME answer, b.jg5 SRJ-512, which records the state `unreadable`) reports no diagnosis either, since its texts say the persona is brought up fresh: no `lost`, `never-created` or inconclusive verdict, no startup-errors entry, no notice and no amnesia count. The diagnosis answers `latched`, the branch makes no reuse spawn, and the ladder answers `latched` (see [Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)). The same holds when the persona latched elsewhere while the fetch was awaited (the health tick's liveness read, b.jg5 SRJ-315), whatever the fetch gave: `latchedAfterOwnRowRead` (asked right after the fetch, unless it answered `latched`, and before any other answer is handled) logs `[slack] spawnForPersona: <ref> is latched after its ErrJsonlMissing diagnosis get — nothing more is called for it (b.jg5 SRJ-502)`. It asks the latch, not the fetch, so a row the fetch latched itself (its note or launch-start line comes first) logs this line too.

         All three verdicts go on to the same reuse spawn of the same id. On its success `lost` and `never-created` surface as the `fresh-after-amnesia` action; **inconclusive** surfaces as the `'fresh-after-inconclusive-amnesia'` action (see the honest-summary note below). For a recorded retired key the reuse's `fresh-retired` passes through instead: no amnesia result, and the diagnosis's persona notice is not posted (the no-transcript step above). This is distinct from b.zak's `jsonl-transcript-lost` class (which fires *pre-resume* to warn of an impending wipe); `jsonl-transcript-lost-on-resume` records a loss found on the row resume tried and failed.
     - **b.jgf `ErrJsonlNeverWritten` — the ceremony-free branch.** agent-director 0.10.0 split the old "resume cannot open a transcript" condition into two typed errors, and CSCB branches on both. `ErrJsonlMissing` means a transcript path was recorded but is not there now: history *may* have existed and been destroyed, and that ambiguity is exactly what the b.wrb / b.fwu diagnosis above exists to resolve. `ErrJsonlNeverWritten` asserts the opposite — the session produced no transcript at all — which proves there is nothing to lose, so bringing the persona up fresh is lossless by construction. It therefore shares the no-transcript reuse spawn but none of the ceremony: `diagnoseJsonlMissing` and the `fresh-after-*` actions are gated on the name `ErrJsonlMissing`, so this branch emits one informational log line, raises **no** persona notice, records no startup-error class, and returns plain `spawned` — the same shape as the `ErrSpawnNotFound` branch. Returning a successful action is the load-bearing part: `restart.ts` treats `failed` as retryable, so before b.jgf this error fell to the generic failure tail and the channel retried the one operation that could never succeed, on a doubling backoff, posting a spawn-failure message each pass.
