     - from a GONE answer: `dead-session` when the reconnect's one `send-keys` answered `ErrTmuxSendKeys` (cause `tmux-gone`); `working-tmux-gone` when the `working` defer's `read-pane` answered GONE (`ErrTmuxCaptureFailed`); `waiting-row-pane-gone` (`ESCALATE_DEAD_WAITING_ROW_PANE_GONE`) when the `waiting`-row check's `read-pane` answered GONE; `prompt-row-tmux-gone` when the prompt-row verdict's one-line `read-pane` of an `ask_user` or `check_permission` row answered GONE (b.jdc, b.jg5 SRJ-606). These are dead evidence;
     - from a refusal: `row-not-interactive` when agent-director refused the reconnect's keystrokes as not interactive (`ErrSpawnNotInteractive`, cause `row-not-interactive`, b.dup): the row finished after it was read, or it reads `pending` and its session may be another launch's. It does not prove the worker gone and is not dead evidence, so it is only a route into the restart run's decision, and the run kills nothing because of it (step 4, b.jg5 SRJ-609, SRJ-611);
     - from a row read: `row-absent-at-pane-read` (`ESCALATE_DEAD_ROW_ABSENT_AT_PANE_READ`) when the row was absent (`ErrSpawnNotFound`) at the `read-pane` of the `working` defer, the `waiting`-row check or the prompt-row verdict, which takes the GONE handling without being a GONE (b.jg5 SRJ-117), or at the reconnect's `send-keys` (cause `row-absent`, never swept as a GONE, b.jg5 SRJ-118). Not dead evidence.

     The adapter's answer carries the verdict it swept with ([Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611)). The prompt row's 10-minute deferral sweep, which runs no escalate-dead sweep of its own, carries the cause `row-read-finished` (see **Prompt rows** below), not dead evidence either.

     A GONE says that agent-director found no session or pane of the row's launch; it does not prove the worker's process gone (b.jg5 SRJ-613). The wrapper emits an operator-visible log line worded by the verdict, `[slack] escalate-dead: persona=<key> verdict=<verdict> — <evidence>, triggering internal findMissing reconciliation (the row may stay live for further ticks, each escalate-dead tick sweeping again; ~/startup/find-missing-loop.sh is belt-and-braces)`, built by the exported `escalateDeadSweepLine`, whose `<evidence>` is exactly one text per verdict, from the exported `ESCALATE_DEAD_EVIDENCE` (`src/session-manager.ts`). Every text says only what was observed and claims no tmux session or worker is gone; `row-not-interactive`'s says that the refusal does not prove the worker gone:

     | Verdict | `<evidence>` |
     |---|---|
     | `dead-session` | `agent-director's send-keys answered GONE (ErrTmuxSendKeys) at the /mcp reconnect: no session of the row's launch was found` |
     | `row-not-interactive` | `row not interactive (agent-director refused the /mcp reconnect keystrokes as not interactive: the row finished, or a pending row's session may be another launch's; this does not prove the worker gone)` |
     | `working-tmux-gone` | `agent-director's read-pane found no pane of the row's launch (GONE) on its working row` |
     | `waiting-row-pane-gone` | `agent-director's read-pane found no pane of the row's launch (GONE) on its waiting row` |
     | `row-absent-at-pane-read` | `its agent-director row was absent (ErrSpawnNotFound) at the pane read or the /mcp reconnect's send-keys: a row read, not a GONE` |
     | `prompt-row-tmux-gone` | `agent-director's read-pane found no pane of the row's launch (GONE) on its ask_user or check_permission row` |

     The sweep then runs the memoized `reconcileMissingSweep` (b.m4r), an ordinary run: it joins a run in flight or reuses a result memoized within 10 s, and otherwise starts a run. The run may reconcile the frozen row to `missing`; agent-director may also leave it live (in `unverified_ids`, or, when `pending`, not judged, b.jg5 SRJ-120). After a run the server makes (not a memo reuse), each configured persona's own row in `unverified_ids` is read with one `get` through the shared own-row read, and a `provenance_conflict` note there latches its persona (see the b.m4r note under Server-Managed Startup step 5). A refused sweep (UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG or UNCLASSIFIED, b.jg5 SRJ-105) logs its refusal line and answers `{ refused: true }`; the adapter then answers `'transient'` instead of an escalate-dead answer, so the run re-probes, kills and relaunches nothing, and the persona is left to the retry timer the refusal arms. A persona latched once the sweep is done answers as an unrefused sweep, and the latch check below stops the run. The one escalation that runs no such sweep is a prompt row's deferral that has already swept and read the row dead (see **Prompt rows** below).
   - **Latch check (b.jg5 SRJ-502).** Right after the reconnect gives an escalate-dead answer, before the re-probe, `restart.ts` asks the latch (`RestartDeps.isLatched`) again, since the sweep's `get` may have latched the persona: a latched persona answers `latched` (`RESTART_OUTCOME_LATCHED`) with `[slack] Skipping restart for persona=<key> — the persona is latched; no agent-director call, nothing recorded (b.jg5 SRJ-502)`, and gets no re-probe, kill or launch. It is asked once more right before the kill (step 4).
   - **Re-probe.** `restart.ts` then calls `isSessionAlive(key)` again (`reprobeDeadAfterEscalate`), and reads its answer as the first probe's is read: a thrown probe reads `unknown`. The shutdown check and the up check (step 1) are asked again after it, then the latch, since the re-probe's own read may have latched the persona (b.jg5 SRJ-512): a latched persona answers `latched`, with no arm hook, deferral, kill or launch. Only `dead` goes on to the relaunch:
     - **`dead`** → the run goes on to the relaunch (step 5) at once, with the same accounting as any dead-session relaunch. The kill decision (step 4, `killBeforeRelaunch`) says whether the checked kill comes first and which verdict the relaunch carries into the ladder (b.jg5 SRJ-110, SRJ-314, SRJ-611):
       - After a verdict that is not dead evidence (`row-not-interactive`, `row-absent-at-pane-read`, `row-read-finished`, or a bare `'escalate-dead'` that carries none) there is no kill, whatever the re-probe read: the work asks the latch, logs `relaunchWithoutKillLine` (`[slack] No kill before the relaunch for persona=<key> — its escalate-dead verdict (<verdict>) is not dead evidence, which never by itself leads to a kill; the relaunch's own row read decides (b.jg5 SRJ-609, SRJ-611)`, `<verdict>` being `verdict=<source>` or `none carried`; reason `RELAUNCH_NO_KILL_NOT_DEAD_EVIDENCE`) and relaunches carrying the verdict, the ladder's collision `get` reading the row itself (b.jg5 SRJ-609, SRJ-611).
       - After a GONE-based verdict (dead evidence, [Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611)) whose re-probe read the row (`ended`, `missing` or `ErrSpawnNotFound`), that read voids the verdict, since dead evidence covers one life: no kill, `[slack] No kill before the relaunch for persona=<key> — its escalate-dead verdict (verdict=<source>) is dead evidence, but the re-probe found <the row ended | the row missing | no row (ErrSpawnNotFound) | no row state>, which voids it (dead evidence covers one life): the relaunch carries no verdict (b.jg5 SRJ-110, SRJ-314, SRJ-611)` (reason `RELAUNCH_NO_KILL_VERDICT_VOIDED`), and a relaunch carrying none. A launch that lands after the re-probe, `pending` included, is never killed: the relaunch's collision `get` reads it.
       - After a GONE-based verdict whose re-probe is the `dead` reading of `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`, which reads no row and voids nothing, the checked kill (step 4) comes first, and the relaunch carries the verdict unless that kill read the row finished.

       Waiting for the next tick instead would add a full `health_check_interval` plus another backoff delay.
     - **`live`** (the sweep failed, agent-director left the row live, or a memoized sweep result predates the kill) → it returns `reconnect-deferred`, as for `'transient'`, with no kill, launch or accounting. Nothing promises that a later tick reads the row dead: agent-director may take several ticks to mark it (b.jg5 SRJ-610). Each later tick whose reconnect escalates dead runs the ordinary sweep again and nothing more: no kill, no counted failure, no other destructive step, and no timer of its own. The re-probe also tells the slow-recovery count (see **Slow recovery** below).
     - **`pending`** → its session has not started (agent-director may not have judged the row); after its line it hands the reading to the `pending` deferral, awaited, as the first probe's is (b.jg5 SRJ-409, SRJ-411; **`pending` rows** below), and returns `pending-deferred` with no relaunch, so the UNAVAILABLE retry timer records the row read `pending`; at a retry of the persona's timer a deferral that answers the row gone returns that dead reading instead (**`pending` rows** below). It resets the slow-recovery count and is not counted: a `pending` row is not the slow recovery this count is for, and its only notice is the stuck-launch post the pending-row rule makes at B ([The pending-row rule](#the-pending-row-rule-bjg5-srj-410); b.jg5 SRJ-1010).
     - **`unknown`** → it returns `liveness-unknown` with no relaunch and nothing counted, and calls the arm hook, as the first probe's `unknown` does. It neither adds to nor resets the slow-recovery count.

     Before the kill that follows `dead`, the run asks the latch again (step 4), so a persona that latched during the re-probe is never killed.

     The re-probe's lines are built by exported builders in `restart.ts`: one per reading (`reprobeDeadLine`, `reprobeLiveLine`, `reprobePendingLine`, `reprobeUnknownLine`), and `reprobeUnhandledLine` for the fallback on a reading kind none of the cases names (a kind the typecheck rules out), which relaunches nothing, tells the slow-recovery observer nothing and returns `reconnect-deferred`; the `live` one is `[slack] Session still reads live after escalate-dead — no relaunch in this restart run for persona=<key>; the row may stay live for further ticks, each escalate-dead tick sweeping again`.
   - **Slow recovery (b.jg5 SRJ-610, SRJ-1010, SRJ-1016).** The optional `RestartDeps.slowRecovery` observer (`RestartSlowRecoveryObserver`; production: the tracker `createSlowRecoveryTracker` builds in `src/slow-recovery.ts`, one per server, built in `main()` over the notice episodes and handed to `initRestart`) is told what each run read, only once the shutdown, up and latch gates after each probe have passed, and the health check resets the count on its own (below):
     - an escalate-dead answer (carrying its verdict or bare) whose re-probe reads `live` → `noteLive`: the persona's count goes up by one;
     - a row read of `ended` or `missing`, or no row (`ErrSpawnNotFound`), at the run's first probe or at the re-probe → `noteDead`: the count resets and the persona's slow-recovery episode ends silently;
     - the `dead` reading from `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`, which reads no row (`LIVENESS_READING_DEAD_INSTALL_GONE`, `isInstallGoneDeadReading` in `src/liveness-reading.ts`) → `noteInstallGone`: the count resets and an open episode stays open (hatch A2);
     - a reconnect ending with any verdict other than an escalate-dead one (a success, `'transient'`, `'pending'`, no answer or a throw), and a run that finds the session already connected with its stream → `noteOther` with `RESTART_SLOW_RECOVERY_OTHER_VERDICT`; a `pending` first probe → `noteOther` with `RESTART_SLOW_RECOVERY_OTHER_PENDING_PROBE`; a `pending` re-probe → `noteOther` with `RESTART_SLOW_RECOVERY_OTHER_PENDING_REPROBE`: the count resets, an open episode stays open; a deferral that then answers the row gone at a retry (**`pending` rows** below) adds `noteDead`;
     - an `unknown` or thrown re-probe, and a run that stops before the reconnect for any other reason (an `unknown` first probe, a latch, a launch in flight, shutdown, not up) → nothing.

     The health check resets the count too ([Health-Check Poller](#health-check-poller) step 4, **Healthy: the slow-recovery count resets**): each tick that finds the persona `live` (never `pending`), connected and with its stream calls `HealthCheckDeps.resetSlowRecoveryCount(key)`, bound in `main()` to the tracker's `noteHealthy`, after the tick's other healthy-branch calls; the count resets and an open episode stays open, and a throw is the persona's error for the tick. So a persona that heals on its own starts a later count from 0, and the post needs three consecutive escalate-dead ticks whose re-probe reads `live` with no healthy tick between them. Each reset logs `[slack] slow-recovery: persona=<key> count reset from <n> — <reason>` only when the count was above 0.

     When `noteLive` brings the count to `SLOW_RECOVERY_POST_THRESHOLD` (3) and no episode is open, the tracker begins P's `slow-dead-session-recovery` episode (`PERSONA_EPISODE_KIND_SLOW_DEAD_SESSION_RECOVERY`) and posts `slowRecoveryText(key)` once through the episodes' sink, the persona notifier: `:hourglass_flowing_sand: *Slow recovery* — agent-director has not yet marked the worker row of this persona's session "slack_bot_<key>" ended or missing. CSCB keeps retrying; no action is needed unless this persists.` While the episode is open, further live re-probes count and post nothing. A count reset alone never ends an open episode; only a row read of `ended`, `missing` or no row, P's latch (the hold observer, see [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)) or P's teardown ends it, so a second post needs a new episode and three more such ticks. After a latch clears (b.jg5 SRJ-506), the latch's set having reset the count and ended the episode, P's count starts from zero and a third such tick posts in a new episode ([How a latch clears and relatches](#how-a-latch-clears-and-relatches-bjg5-srj-506-srj-1005)). Once the episodes are closed at shutdown, the third logs `notice not posted — the server is shutting down` and posts nothing. Between P's teardown submit and its window (b.jg5 SRJ-1003) the post is muted: nothing reaches Slack, it counts as posted in its episode, and the line reads `[slack] slow-recovery: persona=<key> notice not posted — muted, its persona teardown was submitted; it counts as posted in its episode; <n> consecutive escalate-dead verdicts whose re-probe still reads the row live` (`slowRecoveryNoticeMutedLine`). The count is the kind's count in the episodes instance (`addCount`, `resetCount`), kept apart from the episode, so a teardown's `forget` and shutdown's `close` clear it with the episode. The tracker makes no agent-director call, adds no timer and never throws; a note that throws inside logs `[slack] slow-recovery: persona=<key> failed: <error>`, and one that throws at the restart side logs `[slack] restart: the slow-recovery <note> failed for persona=<key>: <error>`; neither changes the run.

   Recovery of such a persona waits on agent-director marking its row `ended` or `missing`; until then the operator sees the persona silent and, after the third consecutive escalate-dead tick whose re-probe still reads the row live, one *Slow recovery* notice at its destination (README, Troubleshooting). The external `~/startup/find-missing-loop.sh` is belt-and-braces only — recovery does not depend on it, and removing it stays a separate operator decision. Not counting at the reconnect keeps the failure count tied to actual launch attempts (the single counting site, SR-25.1) rather than a non-launch reconnect site — the sweep and the re-probe record neither success nor failure. Each outcome logs one line; they are listed in docs/engineering-guide.md, Log Messages.

   **`working` defer (b.9a7, b.rmy, b.d61, b.f2b, b.jg5 SRJ-603).** A `working` row means the persona may be mid-turn, and typing `/mcp reconnect` into its pane would corrupt the turn (b.9a7 hazard 2). The row alone is no proof of a live turn, though: when the persona's session is killed mid-turn, its `SessionEnd` only soft-refreshes the row (see the b.m4r note under Server-Managed Startup), so agent-director keeps it `working` until a `findMissing` sweep reconciles it to `missing`. Deferring on the row alone would repeat every tick, and the persona would never relaunch (b.d61). So `workingReconnectVerdict` (`src/server.ts`) checks, in order:
   - **Launch in flight** (`isLaunchInFlight(key)`) → `'transient'`, first and with no agent-director call. The launch owns the session's lifecycle.
   - Otherwise it makes one `read-pane` of the persona's own row through the shared read-pane (`readPersonaOwnPane`, site `reconnectSession`, `FULL_PANE_READ_LINES` = 40 lines, the row state `working`; see [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104), **The shared read-pane**), and probes no tmux session. Its outcome decides (b.jg5 SRJ-117's working-row column):
   - **A pane** → the positive-idle rule decides (b.f2b). A `working` row can be stale: agent-director may leave it `working` after the turn ended, and deferring on it forever would strand the persona. The pane may be a single leftover's (b.jg5 SRJ-613), so it is never proof on its own. `checkWorkingRowPane(key, pane, { persona, latchedNow })` works on that pane and makes no `read-pane` of its own; only when the pane shows an idle screen does it read the transcript (one `get` of the row), located with the persona's effective `claude_config_dir` (the adapter gets the persona from `getAppliedPersona`; without it only the row's persisted `jsonl_path` is read). It folds the evidence into a run kept per persona across attempts (`workingRowPaneRuns`), with the same `classifyWorkingPane` / `foldWorkingPaneRun` rules as the launch wait (Server-Managed Startup step 5):
     - the same idle screen and the same transcript, ended with a completed turn, unchanged at every read across reads spanning `STALE_WORKING_WINDOW_MS` → `'reconnect'`: the run is forgotten and the adapter goes on to the reconnect below, as for any other alive row;
     - a running turn (the b.9a7 deferral line), a blank pane, an idle pane whose transcript doesn't end with a completed turn or can't be located or read, or idle evidence not yet held for the window → `'transient'`, nothing typed; every case but the last ends the run, and a pending idle run makes the health check schedule the next attempt on its first undeliverable tick (Health-Check Poller step 4);
     - a prompt or dialog → `'transient'`, nothing typed; once shown across reads spanning the window, the `blocked-on-prompt` not-connected notice is raised (once per episode).

     The run is forgotten when an attempt reads the row in another state or its status call fails, when the read gives anything but a pane (`forgetWorkingRowEvidence`), when any launch for the persona starts (`spawnForPersona`), and with the persona's not-connected episode (`forgetNotConnectedEpisode`: its MCP session registered again, the health check found it deliverable, or it was torn down).

     **Bounded deferral (b.f2b).** Every `'defer'` of the check is also one more deferral in the persona's run on the row (`noteWorkingRowDeferral`, shared with the launch wait), and so is an UNAVAILABLE or CONFIG read below. Once the run has lasted `UNPROVEN_IDLE_NOTICE_AFTER_MS` (10 min) from its first deferral, the `unproven-idle` not-connected notice is raised, once per episode: its session reads working but CSCB can't prove it's idle, so it won't type into it; the notice says CSCB keeps checking. Without it, a row whose idleness can never be proven (an unreadable transcript, a compaction summary, a screen that keeps changing) would be held back from for good with nothing reported, since nothing else escalates it at a non-zero delay. The run ends (`endWorkingRowDeferral`) when an attempt reads another state (a failed status call leaves it as it is), when `'reconnect'` is returned, when a launch for the persona starts and with the episode. A read that meets ENVIRONMENT, UNCLASSIFIED or a latch neither extends nor ends it.

     The check asks the adapter's latched gate (`latchedNow`, b.jg5 SRJ-502) right before it notes a deferral, which can raise `unproven-idle`, and right before the `blocked-on-prompt` notice: a persona latched meanwhile gets `'transient'` with its run forgotten, no deferral noted and no notice. A persona latched by its transcript `get` is answered the same way (see [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)).
   - **GONE** (`ErrTmuxCaptureFailed`: agent-director found no pane of the row's launch) → `escalateRowWithNoPane(key, 'working-tmux-gone', latchedNow)`: the evidence is forgotten, then `sweepDeadTmuxChannelWithCause(key, 'working-tmux-gone')` runs once and the answer is escalate-dead carrying `working-tmux-gone`, dead evidence ([Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611)) (`'transient'` when the sweep was refused, or when the persona is found latched before it, with no sweep). Nothing is typed. When the sweep reconciles the row to `missing`, the re-probe above relaunches the persona in the same run; a row agent-director leaves live waits for a later tick.
   - **The row absent** (`ErrSpawnNotFound`) → the same, with the verdict `row-absent-at-pane-read`: a row read that takes the GONE handling without being a GONE (b.jg5 SRJ-117), and not dead evidence, so a `dead` re-probe after it relaunches with no kill.
   - **UNAVAILABLE** (timeouts included) **or CONFIG** (the wrapper has raised `ad-config-malformed`, b.jg5 SRJ-316) → `'transient'`, with the evidence forgotten and one deferral noted on the row: a read that could not run is never proof the session is dead (b.rmy), nor evidence that it is idle.
   - **ENVIRONMENT** (the wrapper has raised `tmux-unavailable`, b.jg5 SRJ-311) **or UNCLASSIFIED** (the wrapper reported the persona's unclassified-error episode, or the reader did after an `ErrInvalidFlags` re-check; b.jg5 SRJ-105) → `'transient'`, with the evidence forgotten and no deferral noted. An UNCLASSIFIED carrying the stop mark (`stopping`: the reader's `ErrInvalidFlags` version re-check decided that the server stops, b.jg5 SRJ-204, SRJ-205) gets the same answer with its own line, and nothing more is called for the persona.
   - **CONFLICT or UNUSABLE_NAME** (the reader has latched the persona with the row state `working`: CONFLICT through the latch's CONFLICT entry with the refused operation "P's next check or recovery", b.jg5 SRJ-501; UNUSABLE_NAME through the unusable-name entry, b.jg5 SRJ-512), **or a persona already latched**, which the reader does not read → `'transient'`, with the evidence forgotten, no deferral noted, no notice and nothing typed (b.jg5 SRJ-502). So does a persona the latch holds by the time the read answers.

   The deferral lasts only while a launch is in flight, or agent-director reads the persona's pane, or cannot answer, and the positive-idle rule has not shown the row stale. Each branch logs one line; they are listed in docs/engineering-guide.md, Log Messages.

   **Prompt rows (b.f2b, b.jdc).** `/mcp reconnect` and Enter typed into a session that waits on a question (`ask_user`) or a permission dialog (`check_permission`) could confirm the dialog's default, so the adapter never types into those states. The row alone is no proof anyone is waiting on the prompt, though: a session that dies under a prompt keeps its row in that state until a `findMissing` sweep reaps it, and deferring on the row alone kept such a persona "blocked on a prompt" for good, never relaunched, with a *Waiting on a prompt* notice about a session that no longer existed (b.jdc, `/ci-live` run 6). So `promptRowReconnectVerdict` (b.jg5 SRJ-606) checks, in order, reading before it notifies:
   - **Launch in flight** (`isLaunchInFlight(key)`) → `'transient'`, first and with no agent-director call and no notice: the launch owns the session.
   - Otherwise it makes one `read-pane` of the persona's own row through the shared read-pane (`readPersonaOwnPane`, site `reconnectSession: prompt row`, `PROBE_PANE_READ_LINES` = 1 line, the row state the adapter read; see [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104), **The shared read-pane**), and makes no tmux call. Its outcome decides (b.jg5 SRJ-117's b.jdc reconnect-verdict column):
   - **CONFLICT or UNUSABLE_NAME** (the reader has latched the persona with that row state: CONFLICT through the latch's CONFLICT entry with the refused operation "P's next check or recovery", b.jg5 SRJ-501; UNUSABLE_NAME through the unusable-name entry, refused operation `none`, b.jg5 SRJ-512), **or a persona already latched**, which the reader does not read → `'transient'`, with one line (`promptRowLatchedLine`), no deferral noted, no notice and nothing typed (b.jg5 SRJ-502).
   - **UNCLASSIFIED carrying the stop mark** (`stopping`: the reader's `ErrInvalidFlags` version re-check decided that the server stops, b.jg5 SRJ-204, SRJ-205) → `'transient'`, with its own line (`promptRowPaneReadStoppingLine`), and nothing more is called for the persona.
   - **Latched by the time the read answers** (the adapter's latched gate, `latchedNow`, b.jg5 SRJ-502) → `'transient'`, with the gate's line, no sweep, no deferral noted and no notice.
   - **A pane** → the deferral below.
   - **GONE** (`ErrTmuxCaptureFailed`: agent-director found no pane of the row's launch) → the run of deferrals on the row ends, one line (`promptRowPaneGoneLine`), then `escalateRowWithNoPane(key, 'prompt-row-tmux-gone', latchedNow)`: `sweepDeadTmuxChannelWithCause(key, 'prompt-row-tmux-gone')` runs once and the answer is escalate-dead carrying `prompt-row-tmux-gone`, dead evidence ([Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611)) (`'transient'` when the sweep was refused, or when the persona is found latched before it, with no sweep), with no notice. Once the row reads dead, the re-probe above relaunches the persona in the same run; a row the sweep leaves live may stay live for further ticks.
   - **The row absent** (`ErrSpawnNotFound`) → the same, with its own line (`promptRowAbsentAtPaneReadLine`) and the verdict `row-absent-at-pane-read`: a row read that takes the GONE handling without being a GONE (b.jg5 SRJ-117), and not dead evidence.
   - **UNAVAILABLE** (timeouts included), **CONFIG** (the wrapper has raised `ad-config-malformed`, b.jg5 SRJ-316) **or UNCLASSIFIED** (the wrapper reported the persona's unclassified-error episode, or the reader did after an `ErrInvalidFlags` re-check; b.jg5 SRJ-105) → taken as alive, with one line naming the class (`promptRowTakenAsAliveLine`), then the deferral below: a read that could not run is never proof the session is dead (b.rmy).
   - **ENVIRONMENT** (the wrapper has raised `tmux-unavailable`, b.jg5 SRJ-311) → `'transient'`, with one line (`promptRowPaneReadEnvironmentLine`), no deferral noted and no notice.

   **The deferral** (for a pane or a read taken as alive) is one more deferral in the persona's run on the row (`checkPromptRowDeferral`, the run kept per persona in `promptRowDeferredSince`). Once the run has lasted `PROMPT_ROW_SWEEP_AFTER_MS` (10 min) from its first deferral, each deferral first runs the memoized `reconcileMissingSweep` and reads the row again: on `ended` or `missing` the run ends, the check logs what it read (`promptRowSweepFinishedLine`: `[slack] reconnectSession: persona=<key> has read <state> for <N> min of deferrals, and after a findMissing sweep its row reads <ended|missing> — not deferring; escalating (escalate-dead), the restart path's re-probe decides (cause=row-read-finished: not dead evidence; b.jdc, b.jg5 SRJ-611)`) and the adapter answers escalate-dead carrying the cause `row-read-finished`. A finished row is a row read, not dead evidence ([Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611)): the re-probe decides, and a `dead` re-probe relaunches the persona with no kill. A refused sweep (b.jg5 SRJ-105) makes `checkPromptRowDeferral` answer `'refused'` without reading the row, and the adapter answers `'transient'` with no notice. A persona latched once the sweep is done (the run's `get` of its own row in `unverified_ids` read the `provenance_conflict` note, or the latch answers it latched, b.jg5 SRJ-120, SRJ-502) gets no row read and one line, `[slack] reconnectSession: prompt row: persona=<key> is latched after the findMissing sweep — its row is not read; nothing more is called for it (b.jg5 SRJ-502)`; `checkPromptRowDeferral` answers `'latched'`, and the adapter answers `'transient'` with no `blocked-on-prompt` notice and no escalation, since the persona is held (b.jg5 SRJ-502) and its latch's own notice already tells the human (SRJ-508). A row read after the sweep that latches the persona (an UNUSABLE_NAME answer, or its own row reading `pending` with no launch start, through the shared own-row `status` read) answers `'latched'` the same way, after its own line. Otherwise the adapter asks its latched gate once more (`latchedNow`): a persona latched meanwhile (for example by a launch outside the restart serializer while the `read-pane` was awaited) gets `'transient'` with no notice. Otherwise it defers (`deferPromptRow`, `'transient'`): it logs the deferral, raises the persona's `blocked-on-prompt` not-connected notice (once per episode) and types nothing. The run ends when an attempt reads another state, or its `read-pane` answers GONE or finds no row (a failed status call, a latched persona and an ENVIRONMENT read leave it as it is), when it escalates, when a launch for the persona starts and with the not-connected episode (`forgetNotConnectedEpisode`).

   Once the prompt is answered, a later tick reconnects the persona when it can tell the session is idle again: its row reads `waiting`, or the positive-idle rule shows a `working` row stale. The restart path runs only with auto-restart on, so the notice says exactly that, and to type `/mcp reconnect` if the persona stays disconnected (a row left `working` whose idleness can't be proven is never reconnected on its own).

   **`waiting` rows (b.f2b, b.jg5 SRJ-604).** Before typing into a `waiting` row, the adapter reads its pane once (`checkWaitingRowPane(key, latchedNow)`: one `read-pane` of the row through the shared read-pane, `readWorkingPane`, 40 lines, the row state `waiting`), and probes no tmux session. Its answer is `reconnect`, `defer`, `gone` (`WAITING_ROW_PANE_GONE`) or `absent` (`WAITING_ROW_PANE_ABSENT`), by b.jg5 SRJ-117's waiting-row column:
   - **A pane** → judged with the same `classifyWorkingPane`: a running turn defers (`'transient'`); a prompt or dialog defers too and raises the `blocked-on-prompt` notice (once per episode), unless the adapter's latched gate, asked right before the notice, finds the persona latched (no notice); anything else goes on to the reconnect. The pane may be a single leftover's (b.jg5 SRJ-613), so it is no proof the worker's own session is there.
   - **GONE** (`ErrTmuxCaptureFailed`) → `gone`: nothing is typed; the adapter calls `escalateRowWithNoPane(key, 'waiting-row-pane-gone', latchedNow)`, which runs the dead-tmux sweep once and answers escalate-dead carrying `waiting-row-pane-gone`, dead evidence ([Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611)) (`'transient'` when the sweep was refused, or when the persona is found latched before it, with no sweep), as the `working` row's GONE above.
   - **The row absent** (`ErrSpawnNotFound`) → `absent`: the same, with the verdict `row-absent-at-pane-read`, not dead evidence.
   - **CONFLICT or UNUSABLE_NAME** (the reader has latched the persona with the row state `waiting`, b.jg5 SRJ-501, SRJ-512), **or a persona already latched**, which the reader does not read → `defer`, with no notice and nothing typed (b.jg5 SRJ-502).
   - **ENVIRONMENT** (the wrapper has raised `tmux-unavailable`, b.jg5 SRJ-311) → `defer`, nothing typed.
   - **UNCLASSIFIED carrying the stop mark** (`stopping`: the reader's `ErrInvalidFlags` version re-check decided that the server stops, b.jg5 SRJ-204, SRJ-205) → `defer`, nothing typed, and nothing more is called for the persona.
   - **UNAVAILABLE** (timeouts included), **CONFIG** (the wrapper has raised `ad-config-malformed`, b.jg5 SRJ-316) **or any other UNCLASSIFIED** → `reconnect`, on the `waiting` row alone, agent-director's own idle signal, with one line naming the class.

   The check logs one line for each answer but a plain `reconnect`. A findMissing sweep can still mark the row `missing` before the keystrokes land (b.dup): agent-director refuses them as not interactive (`ErrSpawnNotInteractive`), and the reconnect answers `'dead-session'` with cause `row-not-interactive`. That refusal does not prove the worker gone (a finished row is not proof of death, and the row may read `pending` under another process's launch, b.jg5 SRJ-609), so it is not dead evidence and only a route into the restart run's decision: the adapter sweeps with the `row-not-interactive` verdict and answers escalate-dead carrying it, and a `dead` re-probe relaunches the persona in the same run with no kill, carrying the verdict into the ladder, with no spawn-failure notice (b.jg5 SRJ-609, SRJ-611).

   **`pending` rows (b.dup, b.jg5 SRJ-314, SRJ-409, SRJ-411).** A `pending` row's session has not started (SessionStart has not fired). agent-director refuses send-keys to it (`ErrSpawnNotInteractive`), which the reconnect would answer as `'dead-session'` with cause `row-not-interactive`, a route into the restart run's decision only and no proof the worker is gone (b.jg5 SRJ-609), and the session connects its MCP servers on its own once it starts. Three reads reach the one deferral, `deferPendingRow(key, launchStartedAt?, appliedPersona?)` in `src/server.ts`, async, awaited inside the restart work's recovery attempt:
   - **The liveness probe reads `pending`.** `runRestartWork` calls `RestartDeps.deferPendingRow(key, reading)` (wired in `main()`) once, awaited, before it looks at the session's connection, so a `pending` row that is connected with its stream, connected but streamless, or disconnected is deferred alike. The reconnect adapter is not called.
   - **b.d61's re-probe after an 'escalate-dead' reconnect reads `pending`.** After its own line (`reprobePendingLine`) the work calls `RestartDeps.deferPendingRow` the same way, awaited, and answers `pending-deferred`.
   - **The probe read `live`, and the reconnect adapter's own `status` read finds `pending`.** The adapter answers `deferPendingRow`'s `'pending'`; `restart.ts` treats it as it treats `'transient'`, but answers `pending-deferred` instead of `reconnect-deferred`.

   Every way, the deferral logs one line (naming the launch start when one was read), types nothing, counts nothing and raises no notice, then decides the row (b.jg5 SRJ-409, SRJ-411): for the applied persona with the key (`appliedPersona`, default `getAppliedPersona`; a key that is not applied is read no further) it runs the session manager's read-and-step entry, `readAndStepPendingRow`: one `get` of the persona's own row through the shared own-row read (`PENDING_ROW_STEP_GET_SITE`), whose row supersedes the `status` read's, launch start included, then the one pending-row step at a status-only site ([Covered and uncovered rows](#covered-and-uncovered-rows-bjg5-srj-409-srj-411)). A covered or undecided row arms the persona's retry timer in pending-only mode and is never killed, reused or launched over; a row that is not covered goes through the live-row sequence (one start, the conversation not kept, alert context `recovery`), with nothing typed and no approver; a read that latched the persona does nothing more. A row the `get` reads in another state, no row, or a refused `get` gets one line of its own and nothing more in this run; a step that throws is logged. Outside a retry of the persona's retry timer, whatever the step did, the deferral answers `'pending'` and the run answers `pending-deferred`, so the UNAVAILABLE retry timer records the row read `pending`.

   **At a retry of the persona's timer (b.jg5 SRJ-410).** Inside a full-mode retry (`isInsideTimerRetry(key)`, [The pending-row rule](#the-pending-row-rule-bjg5-srj-410)), the restart work's deferral at its first probe and at its re-probe does more: a covered row gets the pending-row rule's one run of that retry (`runPendingRowRuleAtRetry`) on the row the step's `get` read, and a rule answer of gone (`ended`, `missing` or no row), or the step's own `get` reading `ended`, `missing` or no row, makes the deferral answer that `DeadRowRead` with one line (`deferringPendingRowGoneLine`) in place of `'pending'` (`DeferPendingRowAnswer`; `RestartDeps.deferPendingRow` answers `RestartPendingDeferralAnswer`). `runRestartWork` then logs `pendingDeferralGoneLine`, tells the slow-recovery observer `noteDead` and goes on to its dead branch in the same run: at the first probe as a `dead` reading that read the row, so no kill (`RELAUNCH_NO_KILL_ROW_READ`); at the re-probe the reading is returned, and an escalate-dead verdict is voided (`RELAUNCH_NO_KILL_VERDICT_VOIDED`). So the launch never goes over a row last read `pending`. Any other answer (`'pending'`, none, or a value that is not a gone read) keeps `pending-deferred`. The reconnect adapter's deferral passes `mayRunRule: false`: its `'pending'` cannot carry a gone answer to the dead branch, so it makes no rule run and no gone answer, and the next retry's first probe runs the rule. The launch start is carried raw from the `status` result (the liveness reading's `launchStartedAt`, or `pendingLaunchStartOf` in the reconnect adapter) and only named in the line: the deferral neither parses nor ages it; the rule ages the row from the `get`'s launch start. Before b.dup the adapter typed into a `pending` row and the refusal raised a spawn-failure notice on every attempt.

   A configured persona's own `pending` row with no launch start reaches neither path (b.jg5 SRJ-513). The `status` read that found it, the liveness adapter's or the reconnect adapter's, applied the own-row `status` step first, which latched the persona with `launch-start-not-recorded` ([The shared own-row `status` read](#the-shared-own-row-status-read-bjg5-srj-115)): the probe reads `unknown` and the run stops at its latch check, and the reconnect adapter answers `'transient'` with nothing typed and no `deferPendingRow` hand-off. No automated path sends keys to such a row or kills it. A `pending` row under a key no configured persona uses latches nothing and is deferred as above.

   **A retired key's old life (b.jg5 SRJ-805).** Right after its state read and latched gate, the reconnect adapter asks the session manager's `retiredKeyReadingOf(key)`. A key recorded as retired with no "new life has begun" mark (a mark held in memory after a failed write counts as set) whose row reads live other than `pending` (`waiting`, `working`, a prompt state, or a state CSCB does not know) is the old life (`ownRowOldLifeOf` answers `retired`): no pane is read and `/mcp reconnect` is never typed into it; the adapter ends the row's `working` evidence and deferral runs, starts the live-row sequence through `startLiveRowSequence` (seeded with the state read, entry at step 1, the conversation not kept, the retired-key flag, a launch at the end, alert context `recovery`), logs one line naming the start's answer, and answers `'transient'`, never counted (`replaceOwnRowOldLife`). The pane reads of the `working` and `waiting` branches are awaited, so the adapter asks again right before typing `/mcp reconnect`, after its last latched gate: a key recorded meanwhile gets the same live-row sequence and `'transient'`, with nothing typed. With the mark set the live row is the new life and is reconnected as above; a `pending` row keeps the deferral ([Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-bjg5-srj-806-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-407)).

   **A held own row (b.jg5 SRJ-810, SRJ-805).** A key that is not recorded whose own row `cscb_<key>` is held for an old life (`isOwnRowOldLifeHeld`: a row the start sweep swept for its `cwd` whose kill did not succeed) and reads live other than `pending` takes the same path (`ownRowOldLifeOf` answers `held`), at the state read and at the second ask right before typing: nothing is typed and no pane is read, the live-row sequence is started with no retired-key flag, and the adapter answers `'transient'` with `[slack] reconnectSession: persona=<key> is <state> and its own row is held for an old life — not typing /mcp reconnect into it; the live-row sequence replaces it (start answered <answer>); deferring (b.jg5 SRJ-810, SRJ-805)` (`reconnectHeldOwnRowLine`). While the old-life wait runs on that row the start answers `already-running`, and the start entry arms the persona's timer with `held-for-old-life` (b.jg5 SRJ-811), so no sequence starts beside the wait. Any other key is reconnected as above. Every other caller of the reconnect meets the reconnect's own guard ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809), **What a hold refuses**).
4. **Kill zombie** — right before it the work asks the latch once more (b.jg5 SRJ-502): a persona latched meanwhile (a launch outside the serializer can latch it during the work's awaits, the re-probe's included) answers `latched` with the `Skipping restart` line and is never killed (see [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)). One function decides whether the kill is made, `killBeforeRelaunch` (`src/restart.ts`), from the run's last `dead` reading (the first probe's, or the re-probe's after an escalate-dead answer) and the escalate-dead answer, if any (b.jg5 SRJ-110, SRJ-314, SRJ-611). No automated path sends `kill` for a row it has just read `ended` or `missing`, or found gone: on a finished row the kill is a no-op success (`kill_sent: false`) that proves nothing about a worker, and a launch that started since that read, `pending` included, is not the one the read saw. Only a `dead` reading of `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`, which read no row, keeps the checked kill:

   | Escalate-dead answer | `dead` reading | Kill | The launch carries |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | none (the first probe) | `ended`, `missing`, `ErrSpawnNotFound`, or a reading with no row state | none | nothing |
   | none (the first probe) | `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` | the checked kill | nothing |
   | a verdict that is not dead evidence, or a bare `'escalate-dead'` | any | none | the verdict (none if bare) |
   | a GONE-based verdict (dead evidence) | `ended`, `missing`, `ErrSpawnNotFound` | none: the re-probe's read voids the verdict | nothing |
   | a GONE-based verdict (dead evidence) | `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` | the checked kill | the verdict, or nothing when the kill read the row finished |

   Each launch with no kill logs `relaunchWithoutKillLine` with its reason (the two escalate-dead forms are in step 3, **Re-probe**; after a first liveness read that read the row, `[slack] No kill before the launch for persona=<key> — its liveness read found <the row ended | the row missing | no row (ErrSpawnNotFound) | no row state>: no kill is sent for a row just read finished or gone, which proves nothing about a worker, and a launch that started since that read is not the one it saw; the launch carries no verdict (b.jg5 SRJ-110, SRJ-314)`, reason `RELAUNCH_NO_KILL_ROW_READ`), then `[slack] Relaunching session for persona=<key> cwd="<path>" — kill: none (b.jg5 SRJ-611)`, and goes on to step 5. A verdict derived from `ErrSpawnNotInteractive` never leads to a kill. The checked kill calls `RestartDeps.killSession(key, lastRead)`, with `lastRead` the `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` reading, which carries no row state.

   **The guards stay.** The kill adapter (`_buildKillSessionAdapter` in `src/server.ts`) first asks `isLaunchInFlight(key)`: when a launch for the persona is already running, it logs `[slack] killSession (restart adapter): launch already in flight for persona=<key> — not killing` and answers `KILL_SESSION_NOT_KILLED_GUARD` with no call. Mid-ladder the row can read dead, so a kill here would take down the process the running launch is bringing up; the relaunch in step 5 joins that launch instead (b.av2 SR-6.6). A persona whose `claude_config_dir` cannot be resolved to a real path gets no call either (`holdLaunchIfConfigDirUnresolvable`, `[slack] killSession (restart adapter): persona=<key> claude_config_dir cannot be resolved to a real path — not killing; its row is kept`), and the relaunch gate then answers the launch `'skipped'`. After either guard the work logs `[slack] Relaunching session for persona=<key> cwd="<path>" — kill: not killed (a guard made no call)` and goes on as it always has.

   **The checked kill (b.jg5 SRJ-110, SRJ-701, SRJ-702).** Otherwise the adapter's kill runs through the bounded retry (`retryPersonaKill`, inside the restart work's recovery attempt, on the clock the adapter was built with; [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104), **The bounded kill retry**), each try one checked kill, `killPersonaInstance(key, { context: KILL_CONTEXT_ATTEMPT })`. The retry is seeded with the run's `dead` reading: only a live row's kill is retried, so this kill is one try, its outcome standing at once, with no `status` read and no wait. It logs its one try line (`[slack] killSession (restart adapter): kill try 1 of 1 for cscb_<key>: <outcome> — <what follows> (b.jg5 SRJ-702)`, and, for an `ErrTmuxKillFailed`, the end line naming the ordinary alert decision), then `[slack] killSession (restart adapter): kill for persona=<key>: <outcome>` (`describeKillOutcome`, `kill_sent` included), does the outcome's own handling (below), raises the retry's alert decision (`raisePersonaKillFailureAlert`, context `recovery`; [The kill-failure alert](#the-kill-failure-alert-bjg5-srj-704-srj-1007)) and answers the outcome, so any alert comes before the launch: an `ErrTmuxKillFailed` that stands raises the ordinary version. This kill follows only the `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` `dead` reading, so it is not a kill of a row read live: it is not tmux-touching and starts no `tmux-unresponsive` condition. The work launches only after a success: a result with `kill_sent` true or false, a result with no `kill_sent` field, `ErrSpawnNotFound`, GONE, or a `status` read between tries that found the row finished (`row-finished`). It then logs `[slack] Relaunching session for persona=<key> cwd="<path>" — kill: <outcome>` (`relaunchAfterKillLine`) and goes on to step 5. After a GONE-based verdict, a kill that read the row finished voids the verdict too (dead evidence covers one life), and the relaunch carries none, with one line after the relaunch line (`killVoidsVerdictLine`): `[slack] The kill before the relaunch for persona=<key> answered ErrSpawnNotFound (the row is gone), which voids its escalate-dead verdict (verdict=<source>; dead evidence covers one life): the relaunch carries no verdict (b.jg5 SRJ-611)` for `row-gone`, or `[slack] The kill before the relaunch for persona=<key> ended its tries at a status read that found <the row ended | the row missing | no row (ErrSpawnNotFound)>, which voids its escalate-dead verdict (verdict=<source>; dead evidence covers one life): the relaunch carries no verdict (b.jg5 SRJ-611, SRJ-702)` for `row-finished` (`KillVoidingFinishedRead`). An old-life wait's hold end (`row-finished` read `hold-ended`) is no read of the row and voids nothing. Every other answer launches nothing, records no success or failure and leaves the counter, backoff and cap latch as they were (SRJ-302), and the kill is never repeated:
   - **CONFLICT:** the adapter latches P through the latch's CONFLICT entry (`latchOnRestartKillOutcome`; b.jg5 SRJ-501, SRJ-505) with the refused operation "P's next check or recovery" (`next-check-or-recovery`) and logs `[slack] killSession (restart adapter): kill refused for persona=<key>: <failure> — CONFLICT: <latch outcome>; no spawn-failure notice; nothing more is called (b.jg5 SRJ-105, SRJ-501)`. A "not this launch's session" answer is the kill backstop of [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104) (**No site acts on a pane alone**). The work logs `[slack] Session kill for persona=<key> did not succeed (<outcome>) — the persona is latched; no relaunch; not counted` and answers `latched` (`RESTART_OUTCOME_LATCHED`); the latched persona's kill is never sent again.
   - **UNUSABLE NAME:** the adapter latches P through the unusable-name entry (b.jg5 SRJ-512) and logs `[slack] killSession (restart adapter): kill refused for persona=<key>: <failure> — UNUSABLE NAME: <latch outcome>; no spawn-failure notice; nothing more is called (b.jg5 SRJ-105, SRJ-512)`; the work logs the same latched line and answers `latched`.
   - Either latch records the row state the run last read (`lastRead`). The kill follows only the `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` reading, which carries none, so the latch makes one latch-time `status` read, its lines prefixed `killSession (restart adapter)`.
   - **UNAVAILABLE** (`ErrTmuxKillFailed` included), **ENVIRONMENT** (the wrapper raises `tmux-unavailable`, b.jg5 SRJ-311), **CONFIG** (the wrapper raises `ad-config-malformed`, b.jg5 SRJ-316) and **UNCLASSIFIED** (`ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` included, whose wrapper still raises `ad-unreachable`; and a class the kill has no row for, which `killPersonaInstance` reports as UNCLASSIFIED): the persona's retry timer is armed inside the attempt (an UNAVAILABLE one once, by the outcome that stands, `reportDeferredUnavailable`), an UNCLASSIFIED outcome feeds its unclassified-error episode (b.jg5 SRJ-313), and the work logs `[slack] Session kill for persona=<key> did not succeed (<outcome>) — no relaunch; not counted` and answers `refused` (`RESTART_OUTCOME_REFUSED`).
   - **Latched meanwhile (b.jg5 SRJ-702, SRJ-502):** after any non-success but a version re-check's stop, the work asks the latched query once more; a persona latched while the kill ran (a latch set elsewhere; a query that throws counts as latched) gets the latched line above and `latched`, with no relaunch and nothing counted.
   - **Under the latch re-check's permit (b.jg5 SRJ-505, SRJ-506):** in the re-check's own run of this work ([The re-check](#the-re-check-bjg5-srj-505)) the latched checks read the latch as the permit does (`readLatchedForCall`): only a latch that revoked the permit, by the kill's own CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME or any other set during the run, counts, so a kill that fails otherwise (UNAVAILABLE included) answers `refused`, never `latched`. Inside the re-check nothing is armed or fed for the persona while it is still latched, and the run ends with it latched and is not cleared after it.
   - **`ErrInvalidFlags`:** one immediate version re-check (b.jg5 SRJ-104, SRJ-204); after a re-check that does not stop, the outcome is UNCLASSIFIED, as above. When the re-check decides that the server stops, the adapter latches nothing, and the work logs `[slack] Session kill for persona=<key> did not succeed (<outcome>) — the version re-check decided that the server stops; no relaunch; not counted; nothing more is called` (`killStopsServerLine`) and answers `shutting-down` (`RESTART_OUTCOME_SHUTTING_DOWN`), recording nothing (b.jg5 SRJ-205).
   - A `killSession` that throws, or answers something that is not a kill outcome, shows no success: the work logs the same not-succeeded line with `killSession threw: <error>` or `killSession answered no kill outcome` in the parentheses and answers `refused`.
5. **Relaunch** — `launchSession(key, personaConfig, { canLaunch: canRelaunch, deadEvidence })` asks the relaunch gate (`createPersonaRelaunchGate` in `src/persona-start.ts`) first, then looks up the persona with that key (`false` when there is none; asking the gate first keeps a key a confirmed apply removed from counting as a failure), and otherwise collapses `spawnForPersona`'s richer outcome to `true`, `false`, `'skipped'` or `'refused'` — the single counting site (SR-25.1). The b.f2b action `not-reconnected` (a `working`-row wait that ended with the session alive and nothing typed, or that its teardown cancelled) maps to `true`: the session runs, so it is not a failure. Resume vs fresh is decided by the SR-1.4 collision-then-act dispatch (no separate `sessionId` arg from CSCB — agent-director owns resume state), the same persona-keyed ladder as startup, so the b.av2 SR-6.2 `cwd` and `config_dir` guards apply to runtime relaunches too. A relaunch runs only the launch: it never repeats the start bring-up's credentials, working-directory or Slack steps (Server-Managed Startup step 5): a row in another directory, and a row whose `config_dir` label is missing or differs, is replaced rather than resumed, with no row deleted: a finished row by a reuse spawn of the same id, a live row through the live-row sequence first (the relaunch then answers `'refused'` and the work `sequence-waiting`). For a key recorded as retired the relaunch is a reuse spawn, never a `resume`, and its success (`fresh-retired`) maps to `true` ([Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-bjg5-srj-806-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-407)). Like every launch, the relaunch is preceded by the trust patch for the persona's working directory in its effective config dir (the pre-launch patcher at the top of the ladder; see startup step 4a-bis), and a patch failure there is logged only. Its spawn or resume is likewise immediately preceded by the reply-guard steps (startup step 5), so the persona's record is rewritten with its current effective `stop_hook_bootstrap`; a relaunch that only reconnects writes nothing. The relaunch goes through `spawnForPersona`'s one-in-flight-launch-per-persona rule (b.av2 SR-6.3), so a relaunch that overlaps a still-running launch for the same persona (the start pass or another trigger) joins it and receives its outcome. `restart.ts` counts each `launchSession` result it receives, so overlapping restarts that join one failed launch count that failure once per caller. A joined launch's failure record and notice follow the mode (startup or runtime) of the launch that actually ran, not of the caller that joined it. On a `true` outcome, `recordSuccess` resets the counter and cap latch; on `false`, `recordFailure` increments it. The live-row sequence's final launch does not come back through `launchSession`: the sequence-launch entry counts its result once, by class (only a LAUNCH FAILURE or DIRECTORY failure, the result carrying `countedClass`), through `recordLaunchResultOutsideRestartWork` (`restart.ts`), and a call that joins that launch gets any failure not marked stopping as `retrying`, which it answers `'refused'` ([Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)).

   **The carried verdict (b.jg5 SRJ-611).** A relaunch that follows an escalate-dead answer passes the verdict the kill decision kept (step 4: the verdict that answer carried, unchanged, unless the re-probe or the kill read the row finished or gone, which voids a GONE-based one) as `RestartDeps.launchSession`'s fourth argument, `deadEvidence`, through `main()`'s binding to `launchSession` and on to `spawnForPersona`, which decides it again from its cause or verdict (`carriedDeadEvidenceOf`) and keeps it for the ladder's run; every other launch passes none. A relaunch that joins a launch already in flight gets that launch's result, and its verdict is dropped with one line (`joinedLaunchDropsDeadEvidenceLine`). In the ladder the verdict goes with each path to `resumeOrFreshSpawn`: the `ended`/`missing` branch names it in one `deadSessionRouteLine`, its collision `get`'s finished read voiding it, and a dead-session route holds dead evidence when its own cause or the carried verdict is dead evidence and no read of the row as finished or gone, nor a reconnect's `row-not-interactive` for the carried verdict, has voided it ([Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611), **Dead evidence covers one life**). In the ladder the evidence reaches `resumeOrFreshSpawn`, where two steps decide on it: the not-resumable step starts the live-row sequence only when the path holds dead evidence, and a resume site's replacement of a row last read live re-reads the row first when it holds none (Server-Managed Startup step 5; b.jg5 SRJ-710, SRJ-609). Their lines name it.

   **Retrying, sequence-waiting, latched, held and stopping launches are not counted (b.jg5 SRJ-301, SRJ-302, SRJ-1015).** A launch whose attempt's last agent-director error armed the persona's UNAVAILABLE retry timer answers `retrying` (`SPAWN_ACTION_RETRYING`) and comes back as `'refused'` (armed means the trigger sink answered that the persona has a timer after the call; when nothing is armed, after the controller is closed or when its first timer could not be set, the failure is an ordinary `false`): `restart.ts` records neither success nor failure, leaves the counter, backoff and cap latch as they were and logs `[slack] Session relaunch refused for persona=<key> — not counted; its UNAVAILABLE retry timer owns the persona`. A persona is never given up on for UNAVAILABLE or UNCLASSIFIED alone; only a counted launch failure (`false`) moves toward `RESTART_FAILURE_CAP`. The refusal itself posts no spawn-failure notice and records no `spawn-failed` entry: the ladder handles it at the site where it met it (Server-Managed Startup step 5). A resume whose `ErrInvalidFlags` re-check decided the stop comes back as `'skipped'` and is not counted either, and so does a launch whose reconnect's re-check decided it. A launch whose reconnect was `transient` for a persona that is not latched, a reuse's second `ErrInstanceIdCollision` and SRJ-710's lost race answer `retrying` too and come back `'refused'` (b.jg5 SRJ-118, SRJ-112, SRJ-710). `launchSession` answers `'refused'` for `retrying`, never `'skipped'`: `'skipped'` makes the restart work answer launch-skipped, which stops the retry timer, and a persona is never given up on for UNAVAILABLE alone (SRJ-302), so a retry whose relaunch answers `retrying` re-arms the timer at the doubled wait and records nothing. A `latched` launch (b.jg5 SRJ-502, SRJ-1015) comes back `'skipped'`: the persona was already latched, or latched at a CONFLICT in this launch; the restart work then asks the latched query again and, finding it latched, logs `[slack] Session relaunch for persona=<key> ended latched — not counted; nothing more is done for it` and answers `latched`, recording nothing. A latched query that throws there is taken as latched too: the line then reads `ended latched (the latched query failed: <error> — taken as latched) — not counted; …`. A `held` launch (b.jg5 SRJ-207, SRJ-1015) comes back `'skipped'` too, and the restart work, finding the persona held, answers `held` and records nothing; the latch or the hold stops the retry timer (SRJ-305). A launch held for the persona's running live-row sequence, for an old-life wait running on its own row, or by the old-life gate for a hold on its working directory (`sequence-waiting`, b.jg5 SRJ-706, SRJ-811, SRJ-810, SRJ-1015), comes back `'refused'`, as `retrying` does: it made no call and records nothing. For the wait and the gate the result carries `sequenceWaitingCause: 'old-life-hold'` (`SEQUENCE_WAITING_CAUSE_OLD_LIFE_HOLD`), and the persona's retry timer was armed at the refusal with the `held-for-old-life` cause, since the wait launches no one ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809), **The wait's steps** and **What a hold refuses**).

   **Relaunch gate.** The gate (`createPersonaRelaunchGate`, over the connection manager and the bring-up controller) answers true only while the persona's Slack connection is serving, its bring-up outcome is `up` and its key is in the applied set (see the applied-set guard under Server-Managed Startup step 5). A key outside the applied set is refused first, whatever its status, with `[slack] persona=<key>: not relaunched — it is no longer in the applied configuration`, and restart.ts then logs its usual `Not scheduling restart` line. Besides step 1's up check, `launchSession` asks it, which covers a change during the kill. A latch re-check asks it too, before each of its own launches, which makes no call for a persona not up ([The re-check](#the-re-check-bjg5-srj-505), **The retries**). When that check answers false, `launchSession` returns `'skipped'` without spawning or running the trust patch or the reply-guard steps, and `restart.ts` records neither success nor failure, so the counter, backoff and cap latch stay as they were and no cap notice is raised. The gate's own log lines are in the `persona-start.ts` entry of the Module Map. Once the persona is up again it is eligible, and its next restart counts normally.
6. **Cap latch** — after the 5th consecutive failure (`RESTART_FAILURE_CAP = 5`, exported from `src/restart.ts`), `shouldNotifyCap(key, …)` fires once per episode and `onCapReached(key)` calls the session manager's `notifyRestartCapReached(key)`, which raises a synthetic `ErrSpawnCapReached` spawn-failure notice through the per-persona notifier to the persona's destination, with the remediation "restart the server to retry — automatic restarts are suspended for this persona"; **no** further timer is scheduled. `main()`'s `onCapReached` also ends the persona's unclassified-error episode silently (`UNCLASSIFIED_ERROR_END_CAPPED`), each step isolated. A capped persona has no registered session; an inbound Slack message hits the no-session branch in `src/persona-routing.ts`, whose `decideLostMessageState` detects the cap (`isAtCap(key, RESTART_FAILURE_CAP)`) and does **not** fire a restart — firing one would only burn a spawn attempt against a persona that cannot come up. The persona's destination gets a lost-message notice in the `restart-limit-reached` state, saying automatic restarts are suspended and the server must be restarted. A **server restart** clears the in-process counter (lost on restart by design) and gives every persona a fresh attempt; besides it, only the persona's teardown and a clear by hand of its latch reset its count (`forgetFailures`). A latched persona at the cap gets no launch and no run of the restart path's decision from its latch re-check, only its reads. A clear of its latch by the re-check leaves the count as it is, so the retry at once after the clear launches nothing (`capped`, unless an earlier check of the retry entry answers first); a clear by hand resets the count first, so its retry at once is not refused by the cap ([The re-check](#the-re-check-bjg5-srj-505), **The restart cap**).

#### Dead evidence (b.jg5 SRJ-611)

Every `dead-session` and escalate-dead verdict carries what proved it, and one pure decision, `isDeadEvidence` (`src/session-manager.ts`), says whether that is dead evidence. It is decided by value alone, with an exhaustive switch over `DEAD_SESSION_CAUSES` and `ESCALATE_DEAD_VERDICTS`, so a new cause or verdict fails the typecheck until it is decided; an unknown value, `undefined` and `DEAD_EVIDENCE_NONE` are not dead evidence (fail safe).

| Cause or verdict | Where it comes from | Dead evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `tmux-gone` (cause) | the reconnect's `send-keys` answered GONE (`ErrTmuxSendKeys`) | yes |
| `dead-session` (verdict) | the restart adapter's verdict for `tmux-gone` | yes |
| `working-tmux-gone` (verdict) | the `working` defer's `read-pane` answered GONE (`ErrTmuxCaptureFailed`) | yes |
| `waiting-row-pane-gone` (verdict) | the `waiting`-row check's `read-pane` answered GONE | yes |
| `prompt-row-tmux-gone` (verdict) | the prompt-row verdict's `read-pane` answered GONE | yes |
| `prompt-row-ladder-gone` (cause) | the collision ladder's prompt-row `read-pane` answered GONE (`launchOnPromptRow`) | yes |
| `row-not-interactive` (cause and verdict) | the reconnect's keystrokes refused as not interactive (`ErrSpawnNotInteractive`) | no |
| `row-absent` (cause) | no row (`ErrSpawnNotFound`) at the reconnect, the launch wait's `status` read or the ladder's prompt-row `read-pane` | no |
| `row-absent-at-pane-read` (verdict) | no row at a restart-path `read-pane` or the reconnect | no |
| `row-read-finished` (cause) | the launch wait's `status` read, or the prompt row's 10-minute sweep, read the row `ended` or `missing` | no |

A refused `send-keys`, a finished row or an absent row proves nothing about the worker's process: the row may be `pending` under another process's launch (b.jg5 SRJ-613). A path carries its verdict as a `CarriedDeadEvidence` (`{ source, evidence }`, branded so that only `carriedDeadEvidenceOf` and `CARRIED_DEAD_EVIDENCE_NONE` make one and a value built by hand fails the typecheck; the restart module imports the type only and decides the kill only from its `evidence` flag); its lines render it with `describeDeadEvidence` as `cause=<source>: dead evidence (GONE-based)`, `cause=<source>: not dead evidence` or `no cause carried: not dead evidence`. Where it travels:

- **The launch wait** (`waitForWaitingAndReconnectWithCause`): each `dead-session` end carries one cause (`WaitDeadSession`): the reconnect's own, `row-absent` for an absent row, or `row-read-finished` with the state read.
- **The collision ladder:** each dead-session route of the `waiting` and `working` branches (`deadSessionRoute`) logs `deadSessionRouteLine` and hands `resumeOrFreshSpawn` the evidence the path holds: its own cause, or the verdict the restart path carried in, whichever is dead evidence (`heldDeadEvidence`), unless a read of the row as finished or gone, or the reconnect's `row-not-interactive` for a carried verdict, has voided it (below). The `find-missing` run before the `resume` (`reconcileMissingFirst`) runs on every such route, for every cause; only the evidence differs. The prompt-row recovery hands on `prompt-row-ladder-gone` after a GONE and `row-absent` after an absent row.
- **The restart path:** every escalate-dead answer of the reconnect adapter carries the verdict it swept with (`ReconnectEscalateDead`); after a `dead` re-probe, only dead evidence with a re-probe of `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`, which reads no row, leads to the checked kill before the relaunch, and a re-probe that read the row voids it (Auto-Restart steps 3 and 4); the relaunch carries the verdict the kill decision kept into the ladder (step 5).

Two ladder steps decide on the evidence a path holds (Server-Managed Startup step 5):

- **The not-resumable step** (`decideNotResumable`, b.jg5 SRJ-710): a `resume` that answered `ErrSpawnNotResumable`, whose re-read finds the row in a known live state other than `pending` (`AGENT_DIRECTOR_LIVE_STATES`), starts the live-row sequence (conversation kept, ending in `resume`) only with dead evidence; without it the answer is the lost race. A `pending` re-read starts no sequence of its own, whatever the evidence, and a re-read in a state CSCB does not know (an unreadable one included) is the lost race whatever the evidence: an unknown state never leads to a kill.
- **A resume site's replacement** (`replaceAtResumeSite`, b.jg5 SRJ-609): a row last read live on a path with no dead evidence is read again before the replace step, so its earlier live read never starts the sequence.

A verdict derived from `ErrSpawnNotInteractive` never leads to a kill (b.jg5 SRJ-609, SRJ-611), nor does any other verdict that is not dead evidence, nor dead evidence a later read voided, nor does `ErrSpawnNotResumable` by itself.

**Dead evidence covers one life (b.jg5 SRJ-611, SRJ-710).** Once a recovery path has read P's row `ended`, `missing` or gone (`ErrSpawnNotFound`), every piece of dead evidence it holds at that read, its own or carried in, is void for the rest of that attempt. A later live reading of the row is a launch that evidence never saw: a new launch (a `resume`, a reuse spawn, or a spawn after a delete, made by a human or another orchestrator), or the row's own worker's late hook after `find-missing` could not judge its process and marked the row `missing`. It is handled as on a path with no dead evidence: a live re-read after `ErrSpawnNotResumable` is the lost race, and a resume site's replacement reads the row again first. A GONE the path meets after that read, on the life it then reads live (a re-run's `waiting` row whose `send-keys` answers `ErrTmuxSendKeys`, for example), is new dead evidence for that life. The reads and answers that void:

- the collision `get` reading `ended` or `missing`, or answering `ErrSpawnNotFound` (`ladderGetThenAct`, right at the read, so every branch after it and any re-run it gives, the retry spawn's included, carry none);
- the read behind a dead-session route's `row-absent` or `row-read-finished` cause (the reconnect's `send-keys` answering `ErrSpawnNotFound`, the `working`-row wait's `status` reading `ended`, `missing` or no row), which `deadSessionRoute` hands `resumeOrFreshSpawn` as the path's last read;
- b.jdc's ladder action's re-read after its `find-missing` run (`launchOnPromptRow`) reading the row `ended` or `missing`: its own `prompt-row-ladder-gone` and a carried verdict are both voided;
- the `get` b.jg5 SRJ-120 makes of P's own row after the path's own `find-missing` run, before its `resume` (only for a row the run lists in `unverified_ids`, and only when the run was made, not on a memo hit), reading the row finished or no row; that read also becomes the path's last read, so the steps after it (the `resume_enabled` false and retired-key steps, the `config_dir` replacement, the `resume`'s latch state and the no-transcript reuse) act on it;
- `resume` answering `ErrSpawnNotFound` (the line logged at the answer, before the plain spawn, whose collision re-run carries none);
- the restart path's re-probe reading the row, and its kill answering `ErrSpawnNotFound` or ending its tries at a read that found the row finished (Auto-Restart steps 3 and 4).

Two re-runs of get-then-act carry no dead evidence whatever the path read: the one re-run a reuse collision gives (`reuseFinishedRow`, every caller; b.jg5 SRJ-112), and the get-then-act a retired key's first launch enters when its reuse collides (`retiredKeyFirstLaunch`), whose new life the evidence never saw. A reconnect's `send-keys` answering `ErrSpawnNotInteractive` (`row-not-interactive`) voids a verdict the path carries in, whatever route carried it, an `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` re-probe's included: that answer means the row is finished, or `pending` under a launch the verdict never saw (the route's own `row-not-interactive` cause stays, as no dead evidence). Three reads void nothing: an `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` re-probe, which reads no row; a `find-missing` result or listing; and the live-row sequence's own reads after its kill.

The session manager voids through one helper (`voidDeadEvidence`), at the top of `resumeOrFreshSpawn` for a finished last read and at each site above. It hands on no evidence and logs one line per voided piece (the path's own, then a carried verdict when that is another source); evidence that is not dead evidence passes through with no line. The line (`deadEvidenceVoidedLine`):

`[slack] spawnForPersona: <ref>'s dead evidence (<evidence>) is void for the rest of this attempt — <voided by>; a later live reading of the row is a launch that evidence never saw, handled as on a path with no dead evidence (b.jg5 SRJ-611)`

`<evidence>` is rendered by `describeDeadEvidence`. `<voided by>` is a read, `<by> read the row <state>` or `<by> found no row (ErrSpawnNotFound)` (`deadEvidenceVoidingRead`), `<by>` being `the collision get`, `the prompt-row ladder action's re-read after its find-missing run`, `the get of its own row after the path's find-missing run`, `the read behind its dead-session cause (cause=<cause>)` (`deadEvidenceReadByCause`) or `the path's last read` (the fallback, `DEAD_EVIDENCE_READ_BY_PATH`); or an answer: `resume answered ErrSpawnNotFound: the row is gone`, `the reconnect's send-keys answered ErrSpawnNotInteractive (row-not-interactive): the row is finished, or pending under a launch the verdict never saw`, `the reuse spawn collided, and the re-run of get-then-act it gives carries no dead evidence` or `the retired key's first launch is a reuse spawn that starts a new life, which the evidence never saw, so the get-then-act its collision enters carries no dead evidence` (`DEAD_EVIDENCE_VOIDED_BY_*`). A dead-session route whose evidence a read voided logs `deadSessionRouteLine` with `the path holds no dead evidence: <voided by>, which voids it` in place of `the path holds dead evidence`. The restart path logs its own lines for a voided verdict (Auto-Restart steps 3 and 4).

No truly dead session is left unrecovered by the rule: a finished row needs no evidence (`resume` or a reuse acts on it), and a live one is judged afresh at the persona's next attempt, at most one retry cycle later.

#### UNAVAILABLE retry (b.jg5 SRJ-303, SRJ-305)

A persona that agent-director refused is brought back by the restart path's own decision, run by its retry timer instead of a restart timer. `main()` builds one controller (`createUnavailableRetryController`) whose retry action is `createFullModeRetryAction` over the restart module's retry entry, `runRestartRetry(key, cwd, isInFlight, blockCause?)`, and the session manager's row read, `readPersonaRowState`. Each timer runs in one of two modes: in full mode a retry reruns the restart path's decision (below); in pending-only mode it only reads the persona's row (see [Pending-only mode](#pending-only-mode-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305-srj-306)). A full-mode retry runs the steps above with two left out: step 1's delay check and step 2's backoff timer. `getRestartDelay` is never read, no restart timer is armed, cleared or needed, and it runs with `session_restart_delay` 0 too. Each full-mode retry:

1. **Pre-call checks** — before any call, the action stops the timer, in this order, when the server is shutting down, the persona is not in the applied configuration (`getAppliedPersona`), it is latched (`FullModeRetryDeps.isLatched`, `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_LATCHED`; see [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)), it is held on `ErrInvalidFlags` (`FullModeRetryDeps.isHeld`, `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_HELD`; see [The `ErrInvalidFlags` hold](#the-errinvalidflags-hold-bjg5-srj-207-srj-1008)), it is not up (the relaunch gate), or it is at the restart cap (`isAtCap(key, RESTART_FAILURE_CAP)`). These run outside the serializer. They are one exported gate, `retryRunGateStop(deps, key)` over `RetryRunGateDeps` (the six members of `FullModeRetryDeps` it reads), which answers the first stop reason that holds; `main()` keeps the six bindings in one `retryRunGate` object, spread into `createFullModeRetryAction` and given to the pending-row rule's install as its `gate`, so the rule's run at a dialog approver's stop is gated the same way ([The pending-row rule](#the-pending-row-rule-bjg5-srj-410), **The approver-stop run**).
2. **Through the serializer** — `runRestartRetry` marks the key active (`isRestartPendingOrActive`, so the health tick skips the persona meanwhile) and submits its work through the same `RestartDeps.serialize` as a fired restart timer. Before `initRestart` has run it does nothing and answers `not-initialised`.
3. **In-flight check first** — inside that serialized work, after the latched gate (`RestartDeps.isLatched`: a persona that latched while the retry waited answers `latched` with no agent-director call) and the held gate (`RestartDeps.isHeld`: a persona held while it waited answers `held` the same way), the first step is the "blocks a retry" binding (`isPersonaRetryBlocked` in `main()`, the controller's `isInFlight`; a check that throws counts as in flight). It is true exactly when the session manager's `personaRetryBlockCause(key)` names a cause, the first that holds: a launch call in flight (`isLaunchInFlight`, cause `launch`), an old-life wait running on the persona's own `cscb_<key>` (`old-life-wait`), its live-row sequence (`isLiveRowSequenceRunning`, b.jg5 SRJ-706, `live-row-sequence`), or an old-life wait step running for a hold it waits on (`isOldLifeWaitRunningFor`, b.jg5 SRJ-811, `old-life-wait`). While one holds, the retry makes no agent-director call and answers `in-flight`, with the line `[slack] Restart retry skipped for persona=<key> — <what>; no agent-director call` (`restartRetrySkippedLine`, `src/restart.ts`), `<what>` being `a launch is in flight`, `its live-row sequence runs` or `an old-life wait step it waits on runs` (`retryBlockSkipText`; the first when the cause cannot be read). The controller gets the same query (`retryBlockCause`) and names the cause in its again-reason (`retryBlockAgainReason`): `launch-in-flight`, `live-row-sequence-in-flight` or `old-life-wait-in-flight`. The ErrInvalidFlags hold's retry at once after a version change passes the query too. A running dialog approver is not in this binding and never skips a retry (b.jg5 SRJ-303, SRJ-401): it runs after its launch call returned. The health tick, the session-disconnect handler and the lost-message routing's read gate (`isWorkInFlight`, Inbound step 7) take the broader "in flight for P" binding, `isPersonaWorkInFlight`, built from this one (`isPersonaRetryBlocked(key) || isDialogApproverRunning(key)`), so the tick never attempts over work that holds back a retry. The skip is a refusal: the timer re-arms at the doubled wait.
4. **Cap check second** — next, still inside the serialized work, the restart cap (`isAtCap(key, RESTART_FAILURE_CAP)`). A retry queued behind other restart work for the persona can find the cap reached while it waited: a counted failure in that work reached it after the pre-call check. It then logs `[slack] Restart retry skipped for persona=<key> — the persona is at the restart cap; nothing killed or launched` and answers `capped`, with no agent-director call, nothing counted and no notice (the cap notice went out with the failure that reached the cap). Failures are counted only inside restart work, which the serializer runs one at a time per persona, so the cap cannot be reached while the retry's own work runs. The restart timer's own work does not ask the cap.
5. **The restart path's decision** — otherwise it runs `runRestartWork`: its latched gate, held gate, and live-row sequence gate (a sequence that started after the in-flight check answers `sequence-waiting` here), then, as one recovery attempt, step 1's shutdown and up checks, the old-life gate (a held persona answers `sequence-waiting` with no call, its hold's wait started; a persona not up or a server shutting down never reaches it; [Auto-Restart](#auto-restart), **The old-life gate**), the liveness read (step 3), then a return with nothing done on `unknown`, the `pending` deferral on `pending` (whatever the session's connection shows), a reconnect of a `live` row (for a retired key's old life, the live-row sequence instead, [Auto-Restart](#auto-restart) step 3), or, on `dead` only, the checked kill (step 4) and the launch (step 5; for a retired key a reuse spawn, never a `resume`, [Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-bjg5-srj-806-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-407)), with the same success and failure accounting. It never launches over a live or `pending` row. A `live` persona already connected with its stream gets no launch. An `unknown` reading's arm hook lands while the timer is running its retry, so it keeps the due time; the answer below re-arms the timer.

`runRestartWork` answers what it did (`RESTART_OUTCOME_*`; the restart timer ignores it), and the action maps the outcome:

| Outcome | The retry timer |
|---|---|
