| `already-connected` (the row reads live, connected with its stream), `reconnected` | Stops: nothing left to recover. `already-connected` also ends a holding `tmux-unresponsive` condition and clears `tmux-unavailable` through `FullModeRetryDeps.endTmuxUnresponsive` (reason `retry`, reading `live`); `reconnected` has no end hook of its own: its tmux-touching calls (the reconnect's `send-keys`) end the condition and clear the flag at the wrapper when they succeed |
| `capped` (a counted launch failure reached the cap, or the persona was already at it when the retry's serialized work started: the cap check) | Stops: at the restart cap |
| `not-up` | Stops: the persona is not up; its bring-up owns it |
| `launch-skipped` (the launch's own gate declined it) | Stops |
| `shutting-down` | Stops |
| `latched` (the work's latched gate found the persona latched, or its launch latched it) | Stops: the persona is latched (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_LATCHED`) |
| `held` (the work's held gate found the persona held on `ErrInvalidFlags`, or its launch's reuse spawn held it) | Stops: the persona is held on `ErrInvalidFlags` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_HELD`) |
| `in-flight` (a launch call in flight, a live-row sequence running, or an old-life wait step running for a hold the persona waits on, at the retry entry's in-flight check) | Re-arms at the next wait (a refusal; again-reason `launch-in-flight`, `live-row-sequence-in-flight` or `old-life-wait-in-flight`, by the cause) |
| `sequence-waiting` (the work's live-row sequence gate found a sequence running, or its old-life gate held the persona) | Re-arms at the next wait, a refusal; never stops the timer. The again-reason is `old-life-wait-in-flight` when what blocks a retry once the run is over is an old-life wait step the persona waits on (`sequenceWaitingAgainReason` over `retryBlockCause`, b.jg5 SRJ-810, SRJ-302), else `live-row-sequence-waiting` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_AGAIN_SEQUENCE_WAITING`) |
| `refused` (the launch was refused, and its UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG or UNCLASSIFIED outcome armed the timer during the run; or the kill before it did not succeed and latched nothing, step 4) | Re-arms; the re-armed line names that cause |
| `counted-failure` (a launch failure counted below the cap) | Re-arms, until the cap stops it |
| `reconnect-deferred` (the reconnect did not succeed or was deferred, on a row other than `pending`) | Re-arms |
| `pending-deferred` (the run found the row `pending` and deferred it: the liveness probe read it `pending`, whatever the session's connection showed, or the reconnect adapter's read or b.d61's re-probe did; the deferral's own `get` and step armed a covered row pending-only or started the live-row sequence for an uncovered one) | Re-arms (a refusal, never "nothing left to recover", even for a session connected with its stream), recording `pending` as the last row read; stays in full mode |
| `launched` | Re-arms, recording `pending` (the launch's row) as the last row read, in pending-only mode: the timer keeps running after a successful launch. The switch is not taken, and the timer stays in full mode, when `arm` recorded another cause during that retry or a `kill-failed` cause is recorded |
| `not-initialised` | Re-arms |
| `liveness-unknown` (the liveness read or the re-probe read `unknown`, or threw) | Re-arms at the next wait (again-reason `liveness-unknown`, a refusal); never stops the timer. It read no row, so the last row read is kept as it is (`keepsLastRow`) |

Every re-arm takes the next wait of the one sequence (30, 60, 120, 240, 300, 300 … s), measured from the end of the retry, so, when retries take no time, they fall 30, 90, 210, 450 and 750 s after the arm, then every 300 s; nothing resets the wait count while the timer runs, a switch of mode included. A retry that throws, rejects or gives no answer re-arms too. A trigger while armed, waiting or running, keeps the due time and the wait count and records its cause kind. Two retries for one persona never overlap. Every retry, in either mode and a retry skipped for a launch in flight included, first calls the optional observer `UnavailableRetryDeps.onRetryFire(key, firedAt)` after its retry line and before its action; production binds the `tmux-unresponsive` condition's onset check at a retry, which posts the onset with the health check off ([Its three posts](#its-three-posts-bjg5-srj-308-srj-309-srj-1006)). The observer changes nothing here and a throw from it is swallowed.

**ENVIRONMENT (b.jg5 SRJ-311).** An `ErrTmuxNotAvailable` answer from any verb for the persona, `kill` included, raises `tmux-unavailable` and arms the persona's timer with the `environment` cause, in or out of an attempt (the `unavailable-retry.ts` entry of the Module Map); repeated answers raise one onset and keep the due time. Two kills are the exception (b.jg5 SRJ-110; hatch A3): a persona teardown's kill and a start-sweep kill arm nothing, and raise `tmux-unavailable` only for a persona in the applied configuration (for a teardown, the persona torn down; for the sweep, the persona the swept row's label names); otherwise the answer is only logged and recorded. The onset is *tmux server changed* when the first raising answer is the re-bound-socket form (`isDifferentTmuxServerError`), else *tmux unavailable* (b.jg5 SRJ-1021; the `outage-state.ts` entry); everything below holds for both forms. It is a refusal at every launch and recovery site: the collision ladder, the reconnect keystrokes, the `working`-row wait's sweeps and the restart path's kill. At the `working`-row wait's `status` reads it is transient instead: the wait goes on, and at its timeout it ends `not-reconnected` (b.jg5 SRJ-605). The startup-dialog approver, which runs outside every attempt, is a raising site too: the wrapper raises the outage and arms the timer as from any verb, and the approver stops (`tmux-unavailable`) with nothing typed and nothing counted (Server-Managed Startup step 5, Pre-session dialog approval). It never leads to a kill, delete or launch, never gives `dead-session`, posts no spawn-failure notice and records no `spawn-failed` entry. While it is raised the pending-row rule makes no stuck-launch post and no abort of CSCB's own stuck launch, and an abort kill it answers is tried again only once it clears, with no second relaunching post ([CSCB's own stuck launch and its one abort](#cscbs-own-stuck-launch-and-its-one-abort-bjg5-srj-412)). A launch it ends answers `retrying`, so it is never counted, and it never starts `tmux-unresponsive`. It is retried only on this timer's backoff, with `session_restart_delay` 0 and `health_check_interval` 0 alike: while `tmux-unavailable` is raised, the health tick reads the persona but makes no attempt for it ([Health-Check Poller](#health-check-poller) step 1), and the timer retries on its backoff; a tick that finds such a persona not healthy with no timer armed (a retry that stopped as not up, on a declined launch or on a failed run leaves the flag raised) arms one with the `environment` cause. A message lost while `tmux-unavailable` is raised schedules no restart; below the restart cap it arms a missing timer first (not while P is latched or a launch is in flight) and reports `not-answering`, and at the cap it arms nothing and reports the next state that applies, usually `restart-limit-reached` ([Inbound step 7](#inbound-slack--claude-code)). A session disconnect (`restartDisconnectedPersona` in `server.ts`, reached from `onsessionclosed` and the SSE abort) while the flag is raised never schedules a restart and logs one line ([Disconnection](#disconnection) step 3): with the timer armed (`isArmed`) it does nothing more, since the timer recovers it; with none armed it arms one with the `environment` cause (`armEnvironmentRetryTimer`, the tick's arm path), unless the persona is latched or work is in flight for it, which arm nothing. A timer so armed for a persona held on `ErrInvalidFlags` stops at its first retry on the pre-call held check, with no agent-director call. The outage ends, and the timer stops through the condition-end entry (Condition ends, below), only when tmux answers: a tmux-touching success or GONE error, or a health tick or retry that finds the row live other than `pending`, connected and with its stream. A successful read (`status`, `get`, `list`, `find-missing`) or `delete` ends neither.

**CONFIG (b.jg5 SRJ-316).** An `ErrConfigMalformed` answer (agent-director refuses its config file) from any verb for the persona, `kill` and the reads included, raises `ad-config-malformed` (the `outage-state.ts` entry of the Module Map) and arms the persona's timer with the `config` cause (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_CONFIG`), in or out of an attempt, so the persona is retried on this timer's backoff whatever `session_restart_delay` and `health_check_interval` are; repeated answers raise one onset and keep the due time. A persona teardown's kill and a start-sweep kill are the exception, as for ENVIRONMENT: they arm nothing and raise `ad-config-malformed` only for a configured persona (b.jg5 SRJ-110; hatch A3). An onset raised while the persona's teardown window is open (the teardown's kill, its read between tries, or the launch in flight it waits for), and that outage's all-clear whenever it comes, are written to the server log and a `persona-teardown-notice` entry, never posted (b.jg5 SRJ-1002, SRJ-1003; [Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-307)). The outage is a notice-episode kind of its own (b.jg5 SRJ-1016), so between the persona's teardown submit and its window its onset is muted as the episodes' posts are: the notifier logs `onset for <ref> of ad-config-malformed not posted — muted, its persona teardown was submitted; its all-clear is written, never posted: <first line>`, posts nothing and writes no entry, and that outage's all-clear is written the same way, never posted (`PERSONA_NOTICE_SUBMIT_MUTED_OUTAGE_CLASSES`). It is a refusal at every launch and recovery site: the collision ladder's spawns (plain and reuse) and resumes, the live-row sequence's kills, the collision `get` and the `ErrJsonlMissing` diagnosis `get`, the reconnect keystrokes, a persona's `find-missing` sweep, and the restart path's kill. At the `working`-row wait's poll and timeout `status` reads it is transient instead: the wait goes on, and at its timeout it ends `not-reconnected` (b.jg5 SRJ-605). The startup-dialog approver, which runs outside every attempt, is a raising site too: the wrapper raises the outage and arms the timer as from any verb, nothing is counted, and the approver keeps polling within its bound B, its next lap at the slow 5 s pace (Server-Managed Startup step 5, Pre-session dialog approval). The live-row sequence makes no kill of a row it last read `pending` while the outage is raised, at step 1 or step 4: it ends without its launch, arming the persona's timer with its other-end cause, and a kill's tries end at a CONFIG read between them on a row last read `pending` ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717)). Nor does the pending-row rule abort CSCB's own stuck launch while it is raised: step 3 makes neither stuck-launch text and no abort until it clears, and the abort asks again after its approver stop, before its kill ([CSCB's own stuck launch and its one abort](#cscbs-own-stuck-launch-and-its-one-abort-bjg5-srj-412)). No step follows it: it never leads to a kill, delete or launch, the liveness reading stays `unknown` (never `dead`), it posts no spawn-failure notice, records no `spawn-failed` entry, is never counted toward the failure cap and never starts or continues `tmux-unresponsive`. A launch it ends answers `retrying`. The outage's clear (a successful wrapped call, or a liveness `status` success or `ErrSpawnNotFound`) posts the all-clear but stops no timer: SRJ-305 gives this outage no stop, and `main()` passes only `tmux-unavailable` clears to the condition-end entry, so the timer stops by the rules below. A message lost while the flag is raised reports `not-answering` only while P's retry timer is armed and P is below the restart cap; otherwise it reports the next state that applies, `restart-limit-reached` at the cap, and can reach `starting-now` below it ([Inbound step 7](#inbound-slack--claude-code)).

**UNCLASSIFIED (b.jg5 SRJ-313).** An UNCLASSIFIED answer (see [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)) from any verb inside a launch or recovery attempt for the persona arms its timer: with the `unclassified` cause (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_UNCLASSIFIED`) from a non-read verb, with the `read-error` cause from `status`, `get` or `list`. The resume path's `ErrInvalidFlags` and the reconnect's `send-keys` answering `ErrInvalidFlags` (not the reuse spawn's, which holds the persona and arms nothing) arm the `unclassified` cause through the outage state's site entry after the re-check. Outside an attempt it arms nothing and starts no episode. It is a refusal at every launch and recovery site, so it is never counted, never destructive, posts no spawn-failure notice and no condition, and never starts or continues `tmux-unresponsive`. At the `working`-row wait's poll and timeout `status` reads it is transient instead: the wait goes on, and at its timeout it ends `not-reconnected` (b.jg5 SRJ-605). The persona is retried on this timer's backoff, and a human hears of it once, through the unclassified-error alert ([The unclassified-error episode](#the-unclassified-error-episode-bjg5-srj-313-srj-1009)).

**Inside a latch re-check (b.jg5 SRJ-505).** A latched persona has no retry timer, and its re-check's answers arm none: inside the re-check's scope, while the persona is still latched, no cause arms (UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG and UNCLASSIFIED alike), `tmux-unavailable` is not raised (a `find-missing` run's ENVIRONMENT answer excepted, b.jg5 SRJ-506) and no unclassified-error episode is fed; CONFIG still raises `ad-config-malformed`. The persona stays latched, and its next re-check comes on the re-check's own 120 s timer ([The re-check](#the-re-check-bjg5-srj-505)).

**Counting.** Refusals are never counted toward `RESTART_FAILURE_CAP`: a refused launch records nothing (Auto-Restart step 5), and an in-flight skip, a cap skip, a latched skip, a held skip or a `sequence-waiting` skip makes no call. A CONFLICT is never counted either: the launch it ends answers `latched`, which records nothing. Nor is a hold: a launch whose reuse spawn met `ErrInvalidFlags` answers `held`, which records nothing. A retry's own launch failure is counted at Auto-Restart step 5's single counting site like any other, so it moves the persona toward the cap, and at the cap the timer stops. A successful launch records a success, as in Auto-Restart step 5, and leaves the timer running, in pending-only mode unless the switch is blocked (the `launched` row above): the next retry reads the new row and stops the timer once it is out of `pending`. Every successful launch, a retry's or any other, also arms the persona's timer pending-only through its after-launch step (b.jg5 SRJ-301, SRJ-409), so a launch's row is watched whether or not a timer ran before it. The live-row sequence's final launch is counted once by its own entry (`launchForLiveRowSequence`), by class: only a LAUNCH FAILURE (`ErrTmuxSessionCreate`) or DIRECTORY (`ErrCwdNotFound`, `ErrCwdNotADirectory`) failure from the `resume` or the reuse spawn counts, the result carrying `countedClass`; a `resume`'s `ErrSpawnNotFound`, a reuse collision, and every retrying, latched, held, stopping or deferred result count nothing, and a call joining that launch gets `retrying`, which `launchSession` answers as the uncounted `'refused'` ([Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)).

**The live-row sequence's causes (b.jg5 SRJ-301, SRJ-717).** A live-row sequence that ends without its launch arms the persona's timer through the trigger sink, with `sequence-not-judged` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_SEQUENCE_NOT_JUDGED`) after a run did not judge its `pending` row, and with `sequence-ended-without-launch` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_SEQUENCE_ENDED`) after any other end without the launch; a trigger while armed keeps the due time, as any trigger does. Neither cause is ever counted toward `RESTART_FAILURE_CAP`, and the sequence itself never calls the failure counter (its final launch's result is counted once by the session manager's sequence-launch entry). A collision at the final launch (the reuse spawn's, or the plain spawn's after the `resume`'s `ErrSpawnNotFound`) arms `collision` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_COLLISION`) instead, and a final `resume`'s `ErrSpawnNotResumable` whose re-read found a lost race arms `spawn-not-resumable-lost-race` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_LOST_RACE`, b.jg5 SRJ-710; one whose re-read found the row `pending` arms `sequence-ended-without-launch`), neither counted. A final launch whose `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` armed the timer at once in pending-only mode gets no cause from the sequence. A final launch call that succeeds (`LIVE_ROW_LAUNCH_CALL_SUCCESS_ACTIONS`: `spawned`, `fresh-retired`, `resumed`, `fresh-after-amnesia`, `fresh-after-inconclusive-amnesia`) gets none either: its after-launch step arms the timer pending-only with the `pending-row` cause (a latched persona excepted), and the end line says so (`liveRowSequenceEndArmText`). A stop for a latch, a teardown or shutdown, an abort that latched the persona, a final launch that answered `held` (b.jg5 SRJ-207) and the no-launch form arm nothing. See [The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717) for every end and its arm.

**The old-life wait's cause (b.jg5 SRJ-811, SRJ-1512).** A persona waiting on an old-life hold is armed with `held-for-old-life` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_OLD_LIFE_HOLD`) when a wait round ends with the hold going on, when its launch is refused because a wait runs on its own row (`sequence-waiting`), at the hold step of every launch path and of the restart path's old-life gate, and at the reconnect's guard for a held own row (b.jg5 SRJ-810); never while it is latched, held on `ErrInvalidFlags` or not up (SRJ-305; `armOldLifeWaiter`), and a persona so skipped is not retried at the hold's end either. It is armed outside any attempt, never counted, never starts or continues the `tmux-unresponsive` condition, and is never armed for the old key itself ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809), **The wait's steps**). A retry skipped because a wait step runs for a hold the persona waits on is a refusal with again-reason `old-life-wait-in-flight`. The wait never clears a waiting persona's `tmux-unavailable` (only its `ad-config-malformed`): that clear would reach `conditionEnded` and stop this timer, so the outage lasts until the persona's own calls clear it after the hold ends.

**Run now (b.jg5 SRJ-810).** `runNow(key, cause, why)` runs the persona's retry at once, `why` (a short CSCB-written label) named in its one line; the old-life hold's end-retry observer calls it with `held-for-old-life` and `old-life-hold-ended` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_RUN_NOW_HOLD_ENDED`) for each persona that waited on the hold that ended ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809), **What a hold refuses**). A timer waiting for its due time is cleared and its retry runs now, in its current mode, its wait count carried on, so a later refusal re-arms at the next wait of the one sequence (`ran`: `[slack] unavailable-retry: persona=<key> retrying now[ (pending-only)] (<why>) — its pending retry is run at once, its wait count carried on`); a retry already running is left alone, since its answer re-arms or stops the timer (`running`: `… not retried now (<why>) — its retry is running; that run's answer re-arms it`); a persona not armed is armed with `cause` in full mode, wait count 0, and run at once (`armed`: `… retrying now (<why>) — armed (<cause>) and run at once`); after `close` nothing runs (`closed`: `… not retried now (<why>) — <close reason>`). Two runs never overlap for one persona, and the run goes through the same action, pre-call checks included, as a timer's fire. Never throws.

**Stop rules and where each is checked.**

| Stop | Checked at |
|---|---|
| Nothing left to recover | The `already-connected` or `reconnected` outcome |
| The restart cap, reached through counted launch failures | `onCapReached`, bound in `main()`, which stops the timer at once in either mode with `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_CAPPED` (b.jg5 SRJ-305), so the pending-only arm of the counted `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` that reached the cap is not left until its first retry (`onCapReached` runs once per cap episode: an arm left by a later counted failure at the cap stops at the pre-call check); the pre-call `isAtCap` check; the retry entry's cap check inside its serialized work (the cap check above); the `capped` outcome |
| The persona is not up | The pre-call relaunch gate; the `not-up` and `launch-skipped` outcomes |
| The persona is not in the applied configuration | The pre-call `getAppliedPersona` lookup (the relaunch gate refuses it too) |
| The persona latches, whatever the case and whatever the timer's causes or last row read | The latch's hold, which calls `stop(key, UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_LATCHED)` on every set, never `conditionEnded`, so neither exception below keeps the timer; the pre-call latched check, for a timer armed after the latch; the `latched` outcome |
| The persona is held on `ErrInvalidFlags`, whatever the timer's causes or last row read (b.jg5 SRJ-207) | The hold's set reaction, which calls `stop(key, UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_HELD)` at each new hold, never `conditionEnded`, so neither exception below keeps the timer; the pre-call held check, right after the latched one, for a timer armed while the persona is held; the `held` outcome. Not terminal: once the hold ends a later refusal can arm the timer again |
| The persona is torn down | [Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-307) step 1 (`stopRetryTimer`), again in step 3 once its launch in flight settled (a timer that launch armed), once more in step 8 after its kill (which arms none), and at submit for a destructive modify's old half |
| The server shuts down | The pre-call shutdown check; the `shutting-down` outcome; `shutdown()` closes the controller ([Graceful Shutdown](#graceful-shutdown-sr-11-event-11)), which also refuses every later arm |
| In pending-only mode, the row is out of `pending` (live, `ended`, `missing` or gone), unless a full-mode cause armed the timer during that retry | The pending-only row read ([Pending-only mode](#pending-only-mode-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305-srj-306)) |
| A condition ends (`tmux-unresponsive`, `tmux-unavailable`), except while the last row read is `pending` or a `kill-failed` cause is recorded | `conditionEnded`: called by every end of the `tmux-unresponsive` condition ([The tmux-unresponsive condition](#the-tmux-unresponsive-condition-bjg5-srj-307-srj-310)) and every real clear of `tmux-unavailable` (the outage state's cleared-flag observer) |

The pre-call checks run in both modes, and no other stop is overridden: only the pending-only row read's stops yield to a full-mode cause. A stop forgets the persona, so a later trigger starts again at the first wait. A retry already running when its timer is stopped finishes, but its answer is dropped.

**The stop observer (b.jg5 SRJ-305, SRJ-308, SRJ-309).** Every real stop of a persona's timer calls the controller's optional `onStopped(key, reason)` once, after its stopped line and before the stop's hand-off: every stop in the table above, `stop`, `stopAll` and `close`, and a timer dropped because its re-arm failed (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_RUN_FAILED`, `its retry run failed`). A call that finds nothing armed, a first arm that failed (no timer ever ran) and a pending-only stop that yielded to a full-mode cause are not stops and call nothing. A throwing observer is swallowed and changes nothing about the stop. `main()` binds it to two consumers, each isolated so a throw in one does not skip the other: the `tmux-unresponsive` condition's `cancelAlert(key, reason)`, so any stop while the condition holds holds its onset back until a later refusal and cancels an alert check that has not posted ([Its three posts](#its-three-posts-bjg5-srj-308-srj-309-srj-1006)), then the unclassified-error episodes' `retryStopped(key, reason)`, which ends the persona's unclassified-error episode only for the stops `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_RECOVERED` (nothing left to recover), `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_ROW_LIVE` (a pending-only retry read the row live out of `pending`), `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_TMUX_UNAVAILABLE_CLEARED` and `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_TMUX_UNRESPONSIVE_ENDED` (the timer's tmux condition ended) and `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_ROW_GONE` (a pending-only retry read the row `ended` or `missing`, or found none) ([The unclassified-error episode](#the-unclassified-error-episode-bjg5-srj-313-srj-1009)). The terminal stop reasons, `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_TERMINAL_STOPS` (torn down, not in the applied configuration, shutdown), are the ones after which a later refusal never arms that alert check again and never lets the onset post again in that episode; a terminal stop also withdraws a re-arm that an earlier non-terminal stop in the episode left pending. The timer's lines and the retry entry's are listed in docs/engineering-guide.md, Log Messages.

#### Pending-only mode (b.jg5 SRJ-303, SRJ-305, SRJ-306)

A pending-only timer watches a row left `pending` without typing into it or launching over it.

**Entering and leaving.** A timer enters pending-only mode in two ways: the direct entry `armPendingOnly(key)`, for a covered `pending` row, and the switch after a full-mode retry whose launch succeeded (`launched`). The switch is taken only when no other cause armed the timer (`arm`) during that retry and no `kill-failed` cause is recorded; otherwise the timer stays in full mode. The wait count carries on through the switch. `armPendingOnly` has two production callers in the outage state, both through the trigger sink. The launch-failure arm (`armPendingOnlyAfterLaunchFailure`): a launch's `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` (a plain spawn's or a `resume`'s in the collision ladder, or the reuse spawn's or the `resume`'s at the live-row sequence's final launch) arms the persona's timer at once in pending-only mode, inside the launch attempt and with no `get` first, so the retry's read of the row decides what the failure left (b.jg5 SRJ-111, SRJ-112, SRJ-113, SRJ-409). The pending-row arm (`armPendingOnlyForPendingRow`, through the session manager's `armPendingRowWatch`, which never arms a latched persona), in or outside an attempt, for a covered or undecided `pending` row (b.jg5 SRJ-301, SRJ-409; [Covered and uncovered rows](#covered-and-uncovered-rows-bjg5-srj-409-srj-411)): the after-launch step of every launch that returned success (the ladder's, the restart path's, a full-mode retry's, the hand-off run's after a pending-only stop, the live-row sequence's final launch and every reuse spawn), the collision ladder's `pending` step (the `pending` branch, the not-resumable step's re-read and a resume site's re-read), a dialog approver's stop with its row still `pending` (Server-Managed Startup step 5, **The arm at its stop**), the restart path's `pending` deferral (its first probe, its re-probe and the reconnect adapter's `pending`), and a pending-only retry's own pending-row step (below). On a timer already armed, `armPendingOnly` keeps the due time, the wait count and the mode, and records its cause and `pending` as the last row read, so a full-mode timer stays in full mode. Any other cause that arms a pending-only timer (`arm`) promotes it to full mode and keeps its due time; nothing else leaves pending-only mode.

**The last row read.** After each retry it is the `row` of that retry's answer (`pending` for `pending-deferred`, `launched`, and a pending-only `row-pending` or `launch-in-flight`; the row read for a stop that yielded, below), else `pending` when `armPendingOnly` landed during that retry, else kept as it is when the answer read no row (`keepsLastRow`: the `liveness-unknown` outcome), else cleared. A retry that fails (throws or rejects) keeps it. `view` shows it as `lastRow`, with the `mode`.

**Each pending-only retry.** The same pre-call checks as full mode run first (shutdown, not applied, not up, at the cap), then the same "blocks a retry" check as in full mode (a running dialog approver does not skip it). Unless work in flight blocks it, it makes one `status` call (`readPersonaRowState`) inside a recovery attempt for the persona, and the state decides (the read also carries a `pending` row's raw launch start, superseded by the pending-row step's `get` below; the pending-row rule ages the row from that `get`'s launch start):

| Row read | The retry timer |
|---|---|
| None: work in flight blocks the retry (the predicate answers true or throws) | Re-arms at the next wait (`launch-in-flight`, `live-row-sequence-in-flight` or `old-life-wait-in-flight` by the cause, `launch-in-flight` when it cannot be read; a refusal), with no agent-director call; the last row read stays `pending` |
| `pending` with no launch start (b.jg5 SRJ-513) | The read latches the persona with `launch-start-not-recorded` (the shared own-row `status` read): the latch's hold stops the timer, and the retry, asking the latched query right after its read, stops with `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_LATCHED` and hands nothing on. The row never reaches the `pending` row below |
| `pending` | The pending-row step (`FullModeRetryDeps.stepPendingRow`, bound in `main()` to `retryPendingRowStep(key, getAppliedPersona(key))`; b.jg5 SRJ-409, SRJ-411), inside a recovery attempt: one `get` through the shared own-row read, whose row supersedes the `status` read's, then the one pending-row step at a status-only site (`readAndStepPendingRow`). A covered or undecided row is armed pending-only (keeping the due time); an undecided row gets nothing more, and a covered one gets the pending-row rule's one run of this retry on the row the `get` read (`runPendingRowRuleAtRetry`, [The pending-row rule](#the-pending-row-rule-bjg5-srj-410)), its answer mapped by `pendingStepOfRuleAnswer`: a refusal (younger than G among them), the held post or a refused `get` is `kept`, and the retry re-arms at the next wait (`row-pending`, a refusal), as does a refused step `get`; a row the rule read gone (`ended`, `missing`, no row) or live is answered as that row below (the gone hand-off, or the live stop), and a latch as latched; a row that is not covered starts one live-row sequence (the conversation not kept, alert context `recovery`), as does the rule's abort of CSCB's own stuck launch (entry at step 2, the conversation kept, alert context `stuck-launch abort`; [CSCB's own stuck launch and its one abort](#cscbs-own-stuck-launch-and-its-one-abort-bjg5-srj-412)), and the retry re-arms at the next wait naming it (`live-row-sequence-started`, `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_AGAIN_SEQUENCE_STARTED`, a refusal; the last row read stays `pending`), with no launch, resume, approver or keystroke of its own; the sequence then blocks the next retry (`live-row-sequence-in-flight`) until it ends. A `get` that latched the persona stops as latched; a `get` that reads another state or no row is answered as that row below. With no step given, the `pending` read re-arms at the next wait (`row-pending`) with no other call. A step that throws or rejects fails the retry, which re-arms |
| Live, other than `pending` (`waiting`, `working`, `ask_user`, `check_permission` …) | Stops, with no call beyond the read (unless a full-mode cause armed during the retry, below). When the optional probes `isSessionConnected` and `hasSessionStream` both answer true, the retry first ends a holding `tmux-unresponsive` condition and clears `tmux-unavailable` through `endTmuxUnresponsive` (reason `retry`, the row's state as its reading); a probe that is absent, throws or answers false ends and clears nothing |
| `ended`, `missing`, or no row (`ErrSpawnNotFound`, logged as `absent`) | Stops, then hands the persona to one run of `runRestartRetry`, the restart path's decision. The stop comes first, so a refused launch in that run arms a fresh timer, in full mode, through the trigger sink (unless a full-mode cause armed during the retry, below) |
| A read error | A `status` error inside the attempt: its cause arms the timer and promotes it to full mode, and the retry re-arms. A CONFIG error arms its `config` cause and promotes it the same way. An UNUSABLE_NAME answer latches the persona (the shared own-row `status` read, b.jg5 SRJ-512): the latch's hold stops the timer, and the retry, asking the latched query right after its read, stops with `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_LATCHED` and hands nothing on |

**A full-mode cause overrides a row-based stop.** Both stops above rest on the row read alone. When a full-mode cause armed the timer during that retry (`arm`: another launch or recovery attempt for the persona met UNAVAILABLE while the read ran), the stop is not taken: the answer counts as `again`, the timer re-arms at the next wait in full mode, the row read becomes the last row read, and the re-armed line names that cause (`retry <n> (pending-only): <cause> — re-armed in full mode, next retry in <s> s`). The gone-row hand-off is held back, since the next full-mode retry runs the restart path's decision itself. The early stops (shutdown, not applied, not up, at the cap) come before the read and are never overridden.

**What a pending-only retry does from G (b.jg5 SRJ-410).** The retry action runs inside the retry marker (`runInTimerRetry`, `src/unavailable-retry.ts`), in both modes, so the pending-row rule knows it runs at a retry. Before G past the row's launch start the rule makes no call and no line, so the retry's calls are its `status` and the step's `get`. From G the rule adds, at most once per retry (`claimTimerRetryRuleRun`): one lap when no dialog approver runs and the launch has not met a `send-keys` `ErrSpawnNotInteractive` (a `read-pane` and, on a startup dialog, Enter), then one bypassing `find-missing` run and one more `get`. At B a row still `pending` gets the held post ([The pending-row rule](#the-pending-row-rule-bjg5-srj-410)). The rule never kills, launches or reuses the row; a row it reads gone is handed off as above. The marker closes when the action settles, and `runOutsideAttempts` leaves it, so the hand-off run, an approver and a live-row sequence run outside it.

**Condition ends (SRJ-306).** `conditionEnded(key, condition, reading?)` is the stop called when a condition ends. It has two callers, both bound in `main()`. One is the `tmux-unresponsive` condition's end, once per end of a holding condition, whichever rule ended it (a tmux-touching call, a health tick or a retry; see [The tmux-unresponsive condition](#the-tmux-unresponsive-condition-bjg5-srj-307-srj-310)). The other is the outage state's cleared-flag observer (`OutageStateDeps.onFlagCleared`), once per real clear of the persona's `tmux-unavailable` flag, with the condition `tmux-unavailable` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CONDITION_TMUX_UNAVAILABLE`): a tmux-touching success or GONE error at the wrappers, the health tick's healthy branch, or a retry that finds the persona healthy (b.jg5 SRJ-311, SRJ-312). The silent boot and teardown reset (`resetAllToHealthy`) reaches neither caller. A `reading` the end or clear brings (a tick's `live`, the live row state a retry read, or a successful launch call's `pending`) becomes the last row read before the rule below is applied, so a stale `pending` read does not keep the timer and a launch's `pending` row does; an end with no reading (any other tmux-touching success, or GONE) leaves the last row read as it is. It stops the timer with the condition's reason, except in two cases, where it keeps the timer with its due time and logs a `kept` line naming why:

- the last row read was `pending` (from `armPendingOnly`, a `pending-deferred` or `launched` outcome, or a pending-only retry: a `pending` read or a `launch-in-flight` skip), or
- a `kill-failed` cause is recorded (an `ErrTmuxKillFailed`, which starts no condition).

The exceptions hold against this entry only. Every other stop rule above still stops the timer in both cases. A successful launch leaves `pending` as the last row read: a launch call that ends a holding `tmux-unresponsive` condition brings the `pending` reading, so the timer is kept, and a retry whose own launch succeeds ends it that way and keeps running in pending-only mode.

While the persona's retry is running, `conditionEnded` records the condition and its reading, logs nothing and answers `deferred`. Once the retry has answered, the recorded reading replaces the last row read only when the answer carries no row of its own (a failed retry, the liveness-unknown `again`, an `again` without a row); otherwise the answer's row (such as a successful launch's `pending`, or a yielded pending-only stop's row) is the later read and stays. A deferred `pending` reading (only a successful launch call brings one) replaces the answer's row all the same, since the run cannot order its own read against that launch; keeping the timer costs one more retry, while dropping it would lose the pending-only watch on that row (`deferredReadingApplies`, `src/unavailable-retry.ts`). Once that retry's `again` answer (or a failed retry) has set the last row read and the mode, the rule is applied once, for the latest condition recorded: kept (one `kept` line, then the re-armed line) or stopped with the condition's reason, with no re-arm. A `stop` answer makes it moot: only the answer's stopped line is logged. A row-based stop that yielded to a full-mode cause (above) counts as `again` here: the rule is applied with the stop's row as the last row read. If it stops the timer, the held hand-off (a gone row's run of `runRestartRetry`) runs after that stop; if it keeps the timer, the timer re-arms in full mode. An `arm` (full mode) that lands later in the same run, a refusal that started the condition again, cancels the recorded end and its reading, so nothing is applied for it and the timer is not stopped while the condition holds (it re-arms at its doubled wait); an end that lands after that arm is recorded again and applied at the run's end as above. An `armPendingOnly` in the run is no refusal and cancels nothing (b.jg5 SRJ-301, SRJ-306): the end is still applied at the run's end, and the `pending` row the arm marked as the last row read keeps the timer with its `kept` line, so a full-mode retry whose own launch succeeds keeps watching that launch's row.

`conditionEnded` answers `stopped`, `kept`, `deferred`, or `not-armed` (no timer, no line).

#### The tmux-unresponsive condition (b.jg5 SRJ-307, SRJ-310)

`tmux-unresponsive` is a per-persona condition: agent-director refused a call that touches the persona's tmux session. It is held in the notice episodes (`createTmuxUnresponsiveCondition`, `src/persona-episodes.ts`): it holds while the persona's `tmux-unresponsive` episode is open. Its only posts are its onset, alert and recovery notices ([Its three posts](#its-three-posts-bjg5-srj-308-srj-309-srj-1006) below); a refusal that clears before the next onset check posts nothing. A message lost while it holds reports `not-answering` only while P's retry timer is armed and P is below the restart cap; otherwise it reports the next state that applies, `restart-limit-reached` at the cap, and can reach `starting-now` below it ([Inbound step 7](#inbound-slack--claude-code)).

**Declared verbs.** Every call through `withOutageDetection` / `withSpawnDetection` declares its verb (`AdCall`, `src/ad-error-class.ts`). The tmux-touching calls (`isTmuxTouchingCall`) are `spawn` (plain or reuse), `resume`, `read-pane`, `send-keys`, `pause`, and a `kill` declared as a kill of a row the site read live. The live-row sequence's two kills declare it (`rowReadLive` true); the collision ladder makes no kill. The restart path's kill follows a `dead` reading and the persona teardown's kill reads no row, so both declare a kill of a row not read live, which is not tmux-touching. No wrapped call uses `pause` today.

**What starts it.** Only the reporting step, `reportAgentDirectorError` (`src/outage-state.ts`), and only when all of these hold:

- the call ran inside a launch or recovery attempt for the persona (`isInsideAttempt`);
- the declared call is tmux-touching;
- the arming predicate (`unavailableRetryCauseFor`) answers the `unavailable` cause for the error, so it is an UNAVAILABLE outcome other than `ErrTmuxKillFailed`.

The reuse spawn's call is a `spawn` made inside its caller's attempt, so its UNAVAILABLE answer starts or continues the condition as a plain spawn's does, and its success ends it with the reading `pending` ([Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)).

The first such refusal starts the condition: its episode opens with the clock's time, the first refusal's time (`firstRefusalAt`), and one started line is logged. A later refusal while it holds continues it: the time is kept and nothing is logged. Whether the retry timer armed does not matter; the two sinks are told apart.

**What never starts it.** An error from `status`, `get`, `list` or `find-missing` (never tmux-touching), whatever its class. `ErrTmuxKillFailed`, which the arming predicate answers with the `kill-failed` cause. A kill of a row not read live (the restart path's kill, a teardown's kill). A try of a bounded kill retry (b.jg5 SRJ-702): its UNAVAILABLE answer is held back (`deferUnavailableReport`), and only the outcome that stands, after the tries, is reported (`reportDeferredUnavailable`), so a live row's kill that fails and then succeeds starts nothing, and one whose UNAVAILABLE stands starts the condition once, then. Any call outside every attempt for the persona: a persona teardown's or the CLI's bot teardown's kill, the start sweep, the health tick, the permission poller and click handler, the JSONL safeguard, and the startup-dialog approver's `read-pane` and `send-keys` (it runs outside every attempt, b.jg5 SRJ-401). Any call inside a latch re-check of a persona that is still latched (`isInsideLatchRecheck`, b.jg5 SRJ-307, SRJ-505): its probe, retries and run of the restart path's decision start and continue nothing ([The re-check](#the-re-check-bjg5-srj-505)).

**What ends it.** One of three rules, in any context:

1. A tmux-touching call for the persona succeeds, or throws a GONE error (`ErrTmuxSendKeys`, `ErrTmuxCaptureFailed`): the wrapper ends it with reason `tmux-verb`. A successful launch call (`spawn` or `resume`, `AD_LAUNCH_VERBS` / `isLaunchCall` in `src/ad-error-class.ts`) brings the reading `pending`, since the row it launched is `pending`, so the retry timer is kept (SRJ-305, SRJ-306). Any other tmux-touching success, and a GONE error, brings no reading.
2. A health tick or a retry finds the persona's row live other than `pending`, with its session connected and its stream present: the tick's healthy branch (reason `tick`, reading `live`; [Health-Check Poller](#health-check-poller) step 4), a full-mode retry's `already-connected` outcome (reason `retry`, reading `live`) or a pending-only retry's read of a live row out of `pending` with both probes true (reason `retry`, the row's state as reading; [UNAVAILABLE retry](#unavailable-retry-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305) and [Pending-only mode](#pending-only-mode-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305-srj-306)).
3. After a launch timeout, this launch's row reaches a live state other than `pending` (b.jg5 SRJ-407; reason `launch-row-live`, `TMUX_UNRESPONSIVE_END_LAUNCH_ROW_LIVE`, ended line `after a launch timeout, this launch's row left pending for a live state`, the row's state as reading). It applies only once a `pending` read established this launch's row: the one `get` after the timeout read the row `pending` with a launch start inside the call's window, which set the persona's "this launch's row" record ([A launch's window and the read after a timeout](#a-launchs-window-and-the-read-after-a-timeout-bjg5-srj-407)). A first `get` already live other than `pending` sets no record and leaves the condition to rules 1 and 2. Every shared own-row read checks the record (`checkThisLaunchRowOnRead`): `readPersonaOwnRow`'s `get` and the own-row `status` step (`applyOwnRowStatusStep`), so an approver's lap, a retry's row read and a health tick's liveness read all can. The first read that finds the row in a live state other than `pending` forgets the record, then ends the condition through the outage state's end entry (`endTmuxUnresponsiveForLaunchRow(key, reading)`, `src/outage-state.ts`, through the installed condition sink) with one line (`thisLaunchRowLiveLine`); a read that latched the persona forgets the record with no end of its own (the latch's silent end applies), and no later read ends it again. `ended`, `missing`, no row, or `pending` with another launch start forget the record with no end; `pending` with the same launch start, or a state CSCB does not know, keep it. A new launch call and the persona's teardown forget it too.

Rule 1 usually comes first after a launch timeout at a startup dialog: the approver's first successful `read-pane` is a tmux-touching success, so it ends the condition with `tmux-verb` while the row still reads `pending`; rule 3 ends it when no pane read succeeds before a read sees the row live. Whichever rule ends it, the end reaches the retry controller once (below), and a timer that still holds the `pending-row` cause is kept.

A successful `status`, `get`, `list` or `find-missing` alone never ends it, except by rule 3, and neither does a live row whose session is not connected or has no stream.

**A latch ends it silently (b.jg5 SRJ-310, SRJ-502).** When the persona latches, the latch's hold ends a holding condition with reason `latched` (`TMUX_UNRESPONSIVE_END_LATCHED`, ended line `the persona latched`), no reading and the silent option, after the hold has stopped the retry timer and before the CONFLICT notice is posted ([Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)).

**Each end reaches the retry timer.** An end of a holding condition ends its episode, logs one ended line naming the reason, and calls the retry controller's condition-end entry once, `conditionEnded(key, 'tmux-unresponsive', reading)`, so SRJ-306's exceptions apply ([Pending-only mode](#pending-only-mode-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305-srj-306), Condition ends). An end on a persona that holds no condition does nothing. A persona teardown's forget and `shutdown()`'s close of the notice episodes drop a holding condition silently, with no post, no line and no call to the retry timer.

##### Its three posts (b.jg5 SRJ-308, SRJ-309, SRJ-1006)

The condition posts up to three notices, each at most once per episode (one mark each in the episode's latch), through the episodes' sink, the per-persona notifier, which adds the persona prefix. The texts are built by `tmuxUnresponsiveOnsetText(key)`, `tmuxUnresponsiveAlertText(key, thresholdMs)` and `tmuxUnresponsiveRecoveryText(key)` in `src/persona-episodes.ts`; each names the persona's session quoted, `"slack_bot_<key>"` (`personaTmuxSessionName`, SRJ-1001). No post is counted toward `RESTART_FAILURE_CAP`, none stops, re-arms or delays the retry timer, and none is an outage onset or all-clear. `main()` passes the condition two accessors: `healthCheckOn` (`health_check_interval` is not 0 in the configuration in effect, read at each onset check; absent, on) and `alertThresholdMs` (`adAlertThresholdMsInEffect`; absent, no alert check is armed).

- **Onset (SRJ-308).** Never at the first refusal. With the health check on, each health tick body checks it once, after all of the tick's per-persona work (`onsetAtTick(tickStartedAt)`; see [Health-Check Poller](#health-check-poller) step 5): for every condition still holding whose first refusal is strictly before the tick's start, including a persona the tick skipped (a restart pending or active, at the cap), read without an attempt (work in flight, `tmux-unavailable` raised) or left out, it posts the onset unless already posted. A condition that the same tick ended (the healthy branch) is no longer open, so a single refusal that clears by the next tick posts nothing. With the health check off, each fire of the persona's retry timer checks it (`onsetAtRetry(key, firedAt)`, the retry controller's `onRetryFire` observer, called after the retry line and before the action, so a retry skipped for a launch in flight counts too), and the onset is posted at the first fire at least `TMUX_UNRESPONSIVE_ONSET_FLOOR_MS` (120 s) after the first refusal while the condition holds. Once the episode's alert has posted, no onset posts in that episode, at a tick or at a retry: the alert already said more, and the first check that would have posted it logs `onset not posted — its alert already posted`, once per episode. So with the health check off and an alert threshold of 180 s, the alert posts just after 180 s, before the first retry at least 120 s after the first refusal (210 s when retries take no time), and the order is the alert, then the recovery, with no onset. Since the onset's text says CSCB keeps retrying, no onset posts either while the persona's retry timer is stopped (SRJ-305): every stop the retry controller's stop observer reports to `cancelAlert(key, reason)` while the condition holds (and the teardown's direct `cancelAlert` call), whatever its reason and whether or not an alert check is pending, marks the episode stopped, and the first check that would have posted the onset then logs `onset not posted — its retry timer stopped and no refusal has re-armed it`, once per episode. The alert-held line takes precedence once the alert has posted. A later refusal in the same episode (`start` answering `continued`, after its reporting point has armed the retry timer again) clears a non-terminal mark, so the onset may post again at a later check on the usual terms. A terminal stop's mark (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_TERMINAL_STOPS`: torn down, not in the applied configuration, shutdown) is never cleared in its episode, and a later non-terminal stop never weakens it, so no onset posts in that episode after such a stop. Only a refusal clears the mark: the health tick's own arm of a missing timer (`armMissingRetryTimer`, [Health-Check Poller](#health-check-poller)) clears nothing, and the condition never reads whether the timer is armed. The mark is dropped when the episode closes, so a new episode starts with none. The check makes no agent-director call and never throws; its line is `onset posted — still not answering at <a health tick|a retry>, <s> s after its first refusal`.
- **Alert (SRJ-309).** One check per episode, armed when the condition starts, on the episodes' clock from the first refusal, with the never-early wait (`armNeverEarlyWait`) over the threshold in effect plus 1 ms, read at the arm and at every fire. So it posts only once the condition has lasted strictly longer than the threshold in effect then (360 s at agent-director's defaults, "over 6 minutes"; 180 s, "over 3 minutes", with `stopping_window_seconds` 30 and `starting_session_seconds` 120), and waits again when a raised threshold has not yet passed. It posts only while the episode it was armed for is still open (the `view().episode` number guards a later episode), needs no onset, never caps and never touches the retry timer: retries continue. The minutes come from `wholeMinutes` of the threshold in effect at the post. The episode's end, a new episode, `forget`, `forgetAll` and `close` cancel it (through the episodes' `whenClosed`). Since the alert's text says CSCB keeps retrying, any stop of the persona's retry timer while the condition holds cancels a check that has not posted: the retry controller's stop observer, `onStopped(key, reason)`, is bound to `cancelAlert(key, reason)` ([UNAVAILABLE retry](#unavailable-retry-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305), The stop observer), and the teardown's `stopRetryTimer` binding, at a destructive modify's submit too, also calls `cancelAlert(key, UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_TORN_DOWN)` itself after its stop, so a persona with no armed timer has its check cancelled too. `cancelAlert` first records the stop for the onset (above), then cancels only the check armed for the episode open now, keeps the condition and the episode (a teardown's forget ends it), and logs `alert check cancelled — its retry timer stopped: <reason>`; the direct call after a stop that already cancelled finds nothing and logs nothing. An alert already posted stays posted. When the stop's reason is not terminal (not in `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_TERMINAL_STOPS`: torn down, not in the applied configuration, shutdown), the episode is marked re-armable: the next refusal in the same episode (`start` answering `continued`, after its reporting point has armed the retry timer again) arms the check again against the episode's first refusal time, logging `alert check armed again — a new refusal armed its retry timer again`; so a condition already past its threshold posts the alert at the check's first fire, with no further wait. After a terminal stop, no later refusal brings the check back, even when an earlier non-terminal stop had already cancelled it and marked the episode re-armable: the terminal stop withdraws that pending re-arm, so no *Still not answering* posts after a teardown, a removal from the configuration or a shutdown. The marks are dropped when the episode closes. A failed arm leaves the condition holding with no alert check (`alert check not armed: <error>`). Its line is `alert posted — not answering for <s> s, over its alert threshold of <s> s`.
- **Recovery (SRJ-310).** At an end of a holding condition, by any end rule above, the recovery is posted before the episode ends, only when the episode's onset or its alert was posted (`hasPosted`, answered as `ended-after-notice`); an episode ended before either posts nothing, and it is never the generic all-clear. `end(key, reason, reading?, { silent: true })` posts no recovery even after a notice and logs `recovery not posted — a silent end (a CONFLICT answer ended it)`; its one caller is the latch's hold, whose CONFLICT notice follows. After the ended line, a posted recovery logs `recovery posted`. A teardown's forget and shutdown's close post nothing.

**During a persona teardown (b.jg5 SRJ-1003).** From the teardown's submit until its window opens (`teardownWindowState(key)` answers `submitted`), each of the three posts reaches no sink but still counts as posted in its episode, so an old half's onset, alert or recovery never reaches the new half's destination; the lines read `onset not posted — muted, its persona teardown was submitted; it counts as posted in its episode; still not answering at …`, `alert not posted — muted, its persona teardown was submitted; it counts as posted in its episode; not answering for …` and `recovery not posted — muted, its persona teardown was submitted`. While the window is open a post goes to the sink as usual, and the notifier's window writes it as a `persona-teardown-notice` entry, never posted.

A new episode after an end posts each notice again. Shutdown calls the episodes' `close()`: every episode ends silently, which cancels every alert check, and a later `start` (a launch still in flight that meets UNAVAILABLE) answers `closed`: no episode, no line, no alert check and no post. Each line is prefixed `[slack] persona-episodes: persona=<key> tmux-unresponsive`; every line, the failure-only ones included, is listed in docs/engineering-guide.md, Log Messages.

**Held apart from the outages.** It is a condition, not an `OutageClass`, and `outage-state.ts` keeps it apart in four ways: starting or ending it raises or clears no outage flag (no `setOutageFlag` / `clearOutageFlag`); it posts no `ONSET_TEMPLATES` onset and no `ALL_CLEAR_TEMPLATE` all-clear; it records no bad-stretch history; and it never holds back or joins an outage's all-clear. The wrappers only tell the condition sink when it starts or ends, and a sink that throws changes nothing about the call's own outcome.

#### The unclassified-error episode (b.jg5 SRJ-313, SRJ-1009)

agent-director returned an error CSCB cannot classify (UNCLASSIFIED: see [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)) in a launch or recovery attempt for the persona. The persona is retried on its UNAVAILABLE retry timer, nothing is counted or destroyed, and a human hears of it once per episode, only when it outlasts the alert threshold. It is held in the notice episodes as the persona's `unclassified-error` episode (`createUnclassifiedErrorEpisodes`, `src/persona-episodes.ts`), which `main()` builds after the episodes instance and installs as the outage state's unclassified sink.

**What feeds it.** The outage state's reporting point (`reportAgentDirectorError`, `src/outage-state.ts`) reports each UNCLASSIFIED outcome met inside a launch or recovery attempt for the persona, from any declared verb, a row read's included, once to `report(key, error)`. These sites reach it:

- every spawn and resume of the collision ladder, the collision `get`, the `ErrJsonlMissing` diagnosis `get` and a persona's `find-missing` sweep (all refusals through `refusalAt`);
- the reconnect's `send-keys` (`reconnectMcpWithCause`), whose UNCLASSIFIED answer, `ErrSendKeysWhileRelayed` included, is `transient` (b.jg5 SRJ-118);
- the `working`-row wait's `status` reads, where the answer is transient and the wait goes on (b.jg5 SRJ-605);
- the restart path's liveness read and re-probe, the reconnect adapter's reads, its sweeps, and the restart kill (`killPersonaInstance` in an attempt, Auto-Restart step 4);
- a retry's own row read (`readPersonaRowState`), so a store agent-director cannot open (`ErrSchemaMismatch`, `ErrSchemaMigrationRequired`, `ErrStoreOpen`) reaches it through every retry's read;
- the resume path's `ErrInvalidFlags` and the reconnect's `send-keys` answering `ErrInvalidFlags`, through the site entry `reportUnclassifiedAtSite`, with the classification its re-check step gave (nothing when the re-check stopped the server);
- the reuse spawn (`reuseSpawnForPersona`): an UNCLASSIFIED answer, a refusal through `refusalAt`; a name it gives no meaning (GONE, a STATE name other than `ErrInstanceIdCollision`), through `reportUnclassifiedAtSite` (its `ErrInvalidFlags` holds the persona instead and reports nothing here) ([Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708));
- a kill in an attempt (the live-row sequence's kills, the restart kill) whose outcome is of a class the kill has no row for (a STATE name other than `ErrSpawnNotFound`, `ErrInvalidFlags` after a re-check that did not stop included, LAUNCH FAILURE, DIRECTORY; b.jg5 SRJ-110), through the same site entry with `unclassifiedClassificationOf`'s classification. The persona teardown's kill and the start sweep's kills feed nothing.

The liveness adapter's `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` is not reported (it keeps its `dead` reading), and an `ErrInternal` carrying the unusable recorded name is UNUSABLE_NAME, not UNCLASSIFIED. Outside an attempt nothing is reported: the startup-dialog approver's `status`, `read-pane` and `send-keys` calls run outside every attempt (`runOutsideAttempts`, b.jg5 SRJ-401), so their UNCLASSIFIED answers open no episode and arm no retry timer. Nor is anything reported inside a latch re-check of a persona that is still latched (`isInsideLatchRecheck`, b.jg5 SRJ-313, SRJ-505): its answers give no information ([The re-check](#the-re-check-bjg5-srj-505)).

**Start.** With no open episode, an outcome begins one on the episodes' clock, logging one started line. The episode's start time is its first outcome's time.

**The alert.** In an open episode whose alert has not been posted, an outcome met strictly more than the alert threshold in effect at that moment (`adAlertThresholdMsInEffect`, read at each check; b.jg5 SRJ-210) after the episode's first outcome posts the one alert, quoting that outcome. No timer is armed: unlike the `tmux-unresponsive` alert check ([Its three posts](#its-three-posts-bjg5-srj-308-srj-309-srj-1006)), only an outcome met past the threshold posts it, so with retries at 30, 90, 210, 450 s after the first outcome the alert comes at the 450 s retry at agent-director's defaults (360 s) and at the 210 s retry with a 180 s threshold. No second alert follows in the episode. The text is `unclassifiedErrorAlertText`: *Unclassified agent-director error*, naming the classifier's reported name when it is a safe identifier (left out otherwise, with no placeholder) and quoting its rendered message (redacted, one line, capped at `MAX_LOGGED_MESSAGE_LENGTH`), escaped for Slack after the cap; it says CSCB keeps retrying and takes no destructive action, and that a human should check the host's agent-director.

**Routing**, decided when the alert is posted:

- the persona's teardown window is open (b.jg5 SRJ-1003; the episodes' `teardownWindowState(key)`): the alert, unescaped, goes through the episodes' sink, whose window writes it as one server-log line and one `persona-teardown-notice` entry and posts nothing, whether the persona is configured or not (so no `persona-unclassified-error` entry); its line is `alert written to the server log and startup-errors.log (persona-teardown-notice) — raised during its persona teardown; <met>`. This is the launch in flight a teardown waits for meeting UNCLASSIFIED outcomes past the threshold;
- the persona is in the applied configuration (`getAppliedPersona`): the alert goes through the episodes' sink, the per-persona notifier, to the persona's destination; between the persona's teardown submit and its window the post is muted (it counts as posted, and its line reads `alert not posted to its destination — muted, its persona teardown was submitted; it counts as posted in its episode; <met>`);
- it is not (an attempt still in flight when the persona left the applied configuration), or the lookup throws: one `recordStartupError(PERSONA_UNCLASSIFIED_ERROR_LABEL, 'persona=<key>: <text>')` call, with the text unescaped, which writes one server-log line and one `persona-unclassified-error` entry in `startup-errors.log`. Nothing reaches Slack.

Either way the alert counts as posted for the episode.

**End.** The episode ends silently, with one ended line naming the reason, when:

- a full-mode retry finds nothing left to recover (the retry timer's stop `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_RECOVERED`, through the stop observer: `UNCLASSIFIED_ERROR_END_RECOVERED`);
- a pending-only retry reads the row live out of `pending` (the stop `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_ROW_LIVE`: `UNCLASSIFIED_ERROR_END_ROW_LIVE`); a pending-only stop that yielded to a full-mode cause is no stop, so the episode stays open;
- the retry timer stops because the persona's tmux condition ended: its `tmux-unavailable` condition cleared or its `tmux-unresponsive` condition ended (the stops `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_TMUX_UNAVAILABLE_CLEARED` and `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_TMUX_UNRESPONSIVE_ENDED`: `UNCLASSIFIED_ERROR_END_CONDITION_ENDED`);
- a pending-only retry reads the row `ended` or `missing`, or finds none, and hands the persona to the restart path's decision (the stop `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_ROW_GONE`: `UNCLASSIFIED_ERROR_END_ROW_GONE`);
- the persona reaches the restart cap (`onCapReached`: `UNCLASSIFIED_ERROR_END_CAPPED`);
- the persona latches, whatever the case (the latch's hold, after it stopped the retry timer and before the CONFLICT notice: `UNCLASSIFIED_ERROR_END_LATCHED`; [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)); the timer's latch stop itself, `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_LATCHED`, is not one of the stops above;
- the persona is torn down (the episodes' `forget(key)`) or the server shuts down (`close()`), with no line.

These timer stops all mean the retries are over because the persona's state got better, and no retry follows any of them. Every other stop of the retry timer leaves it open: not up, not in the applied configuration, a declined launch, a failed run and the rest.

The ended line is `[slack] persona-episodes: persona=<key> unclassified-error ended — <reason>`, with `<reason>` one of `a retry found nothing left to recover`, `a retry read its row live out of pending`, `its retry timer stopped when its tmux condition ended`, `a retry read its row ended or gone`, `the persona reached the restart cap` and `the persona latched`. A later outcome after an end begins a new episode, whose alert is posted again.

**Held apart.** It touches no outage flag, retry timer or restart counter, posts no condition and is not a `tmux-unresponsive` episode. Each line is prefixed `[slack] persona-episodes: persona=<key> unclassified-error`; every line is listed in docs/engineering-guide.md, Log Messages.

#### Session conflict latch (b.jg5 SRJ-501, SRJ-502)

A persona whose tmux session agent-director refuses to act on (`ErrTmuxSessionConflict`, class CONFLICT), or whose own row agent-director has noted conflicting labels on (`provenance_conflict`), or whose own row reads `pending` with no launch start, latches: from then on no automated path kills, reuses, launches or recovers it but its own re-check, which makes at most one read and one named call per 120 s ([The re-check](#the-re-check-bjg5-srj-505)), and a human decides. The latch is the server's one instance (`createConflictLatch`, `src/conflict-latch.ts`), built in `main()` and held in memory only.

**A human-initiated teardown (b.jg5 SRJ-503, SRJ-513).** The latch holds only the server's automated paths. A CLI `stop --stop-bots` or `clean_restart` is a human's deliberate action, and the CLI has no latch: it tears a persona the server holds down as any other, its kill the ordinary checked kill (a plain `kill`, never with agent-director's finished-row option). A finished row is skipped at the teardown's state read; a `pending` row with no launch start gets the pause, `ErrSpawnNotPausable`, then that kill, which ends no session ([clean_restart](#clean_restart-sr-11-event-12) step 6).

**What latches today.** A CONFLICT at a spawn or `resume` the collision ladder makes (Server-Managed Startup step 5): the first spawn, its retry-spawn after the collision `get` found no row, the spawn after `resume` answered `ErrSpawnNotFound`, and the resume. The live-row sequence's final `resume` and the plain spawn after its `ErrSpawnNotFound` latch the same way, through the same `resume` handler (`resumeAtSite`, b.jg5 SRJ-113). Every plain spawn's CONFLICT comes through the one plain-spawn handler, and what it leaves of the row (none after the pre-spawn scan's refusal, `ended` after "duplicate session") is in [Plain spawn](#plain-spawn-bjg5-srj-111). A `resume`'s CONFLICT latches with the refused operation `resume` whatever its case: "this row's own id", "left over from an earlier life", "no valid instance id", "a different instance id", "another agent-director store", or "conflicting labels", which a stray `@ad_owner` value or a duplicate label gives after "duplicate session" too ([Server-Managed Startup](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1) step 5, `resume`'s outcomes); never a kill. The reuse spawn latches the same way on a CONFLICT (`conflictAt`, refused operation "reuse spawn", its line prefixed `reuseSpawnForPersona` and naming the `reuse spawn`), at the live-row sequence's final launch, at the replace step's finished-row branch and at the no-transcript step after the ladder's `resume`, with the case its description gives ("another agent-director store" and "conflicting labels" included) and never a kill ([Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)). The only other agent-director error that latches is an UNUSABLE_NAME answer (**An unusable recorded name**, below). Two row reads latch too: a conflicting-labels note and a `pending` row with no launch start (both below), the start sweep's `list` rows included ([Server-Managed Startup](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1) step 4). The site's helper, `launchRefusalAt`, takes the CONFLICT row (`conflictAt`) before the refusal rows: the class comes from `classifyAdError`. It latches the persona through `setFromConflict` (the set observers, holds before the notice, run inside the set), then logs one line, `[slack] spawnForPersona: <what> refused for <ref>: <failure> — CONFLICT: the persona latched; no spawn-failure notice; nothing more is called (b.jg5 SRJ-105, SRJ-501)`, and answers `latched`. The ladder then takes no further step: no sequence or spawn, no spawn-failure notice, no `spawn-failed` entry and nothing counted. A `setFromConflict` that throws changes only the middle of that one line, `— CONFLICT: latching the persona failed: <error>; …`, and the answer is the same. The dialog approver is the other CONFLICT site: a CONFLICT answer to its `status`, `read-pane` or `send-keys` latches the persona through `setFromConflict` with the refused operation "P's next check or recovery" (`REFUSED_OPERATION_NEXT_CHECK_OR_RECOVERY`) and the recorded state `pending` (unreadable for a `status` answer, which read no state); it logs one `CONFLICT` line (`approverConflictMessage`) and stops with nothing typed (`latched`; Server-Managed Startup step 5, Pre-session dialog approval). The shared read-pane (`readPersonaOwnPane`, the reader of the working-pane read, the `working`-row verdict and both b.jdc prompt-row paths) is the third: a CONFLICT answer latches the persona through the same entry and refused operation, recording the row state its caller last read, with one `CONFLICT` line, and its caller ends with nothing typed ([Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104), **The shared read-pane**). The reconnect's `send-keys` (`reconnectMcpWithCause`, b.jg5 SRJ-118) is the fourth: a CONFLICT answer latches the persona through the same entry and refused operation, recording the row state the reconnect's caller last read (`waiting`, or `working` for a stale row), logs one `reconnectConflictLine` and answers `transient` with nothing typed; the refused `send-keys` is never retried, and every later path finds the persona latched (its re-check reads the row with `status` only, and a "not this launch's session" latch is never cleared by a live reading: [The re-check](#the-re-check-bjg5-srj-505), row 6) (Server-Managed Startup step 5, the `waiting` branch). All three share one helper, `latchOnConflict`. The kills are the fifth (b.jg5 SRJ-110, SRJ-501, SRJ-505): a CONFLICT at a live-row sequence's kill or at the abort's kill of CSCB's own stuck launch (both through `latchOnKillOutcomeAt`; the abort's records `pending` and logs with the prefix `pendingRowRule stuck-launch abort`, [CSCB's own stuck launch and its one abort](#cscbs-own-stuck-launch-and-its-one-abort-bjg5-srj-412)) or the restart path's kill (`_buildKillSessionAdapter`, through `latchOnRestartKillOutcome`) latches the persona through `conflictAt` with the refused operation "P's next check or recovery" and the row state the path last read, logs one `CONFLICT` line prefixed `live-row-sequence` or `killSession (restart adapter)`, and nothing is deleted or launched after it; the refused kill is never sent again, its re-check included ([The re-check](#the-re-check-bjg5-srj-505)). On a live row such an answer, "not this launch's session", is the kill backstop of [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104). The start sweep's kills and the persona teardown's kill latch nothing.

**A conflicting-labels note (b.jg5 SRJ-114, SRJ-501).** A read of a configured persona's own row at the collision `get`, the `ErrJsonlMissing` diagnosis `get`, the transcript `get` or the `get` after a `find-missing` run lists the row in `unverified_ids` (b.jg5 SRJ-120), or the persona's own row as the start sweep's `list` gives it (b.jg5 SRJ-116; [Server-Managed Startup](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1) step 4, which then leaves every row of the persona unkilled), whose `liveness_note` is `provenance_conflict`, latches the persona too: the shared own-row read calls the latch's `set` with case `conflicting-labels`, refused operation `bring-up` (the persona's bring-up by the restart path's decision), the state that `get` read (or the row was listed in) as the recorded state (a `waiting` row counts as live), the session `slack_bot_<key>` and no description, since a note carries none. Its CONFLICT notice is the "conflicting labels" notice without the `agent-director said` description line. The site then calls nothing more for the persona. The `get` after a `find-missing` run is never made for a persona already latched, so that read never relatches one. Which reads count, and what each site does next, is in [Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114).

**An unusable recorded name (b.jg5 SRJ-501, SRJ-512).** An UNUSABLE_NAME answer (an `ErrInternal` whose description carries "the recorded tmux session name", an `ErrUnknownErrorName` told apart by its `unknownName` and that phrase through the classifier, `isUnusableNameError`) to a call on a persona's own row latches the persona with the case `unusable-recorded-name` and the refused operation `none`, through `unusableNameSetInput` (the latch's `setFromUnusableName` builds the same input): the classification's message as the description (redacted, on one line and capped by the classifier) and the session that message quotes, else `slack_bot_<key>`. The sites that set it, each logging one `UNUSABLE NAME` line (the engineering guide's Auto-Restart, Log Messages):

- the collision ladder's plain spawns and resume (`launchRefusalAt`, after the CONFLICT row), through `unusableNameAt`, with the row state the path last read, or one latch-time `status` read when it read none;
- the reuse spawn (`reuseSpawnForPersona`, through `unusableNameAt` after its CONFLICT row), with the row state its caller last read, no row included;
- the live-row sequence's kills (through `latchOnKillOutcomeAt` and `unusableNameAt`), with the state the sequence last read; the sequence then ends without its launch ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717));
- the abort's kill of CSCB's own stuck launch (through `latchOnKillOutcomeAt` and `unusableNameAt`), recording `pending`; no sequence follows ([CSCB's own stuck launch and its one abort](#cscbs-own-stuck-launch-and-its-one-abort-bjg5-srj-412));
- the restart path's kill (`_buildKillSessionAdapter`, through `latchOnRestartKillOutcome` and `unusableNameAt`, b.jg5 SRJ-110), with the row state the restart run last read (its `dead` reading: `ended`, `missing` or no row), or one latch-time `status` read when that reading carries none (`ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`); the restart work answers `latched` and launches nothing;
- the shared own-row `get` ([Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114); not the start sweep's post-run `get`s, which route the answer to the server log and latch nothing, b.jg5 SRJ-1002) and the shared own-row `status` read ([The shared own-row `status` read](#the-shared-own-row-status-read-bjg5-srj-115): the launch wait's poll and timeout reads, the prompt rows' re-read after a sweep, the retry timer's row read, the latch-time read, the dialog approver's readiness read and a persona's kill retry's read between tries), each recording `unreadable` and making no further read;
- the liveness and reconnect adapters (`src/server.ts`), which apply the own-row `status` step after their own `status` call (the health tick's read, the restart path's probe and re-probe, the lost-message read, the reconnect's state read), recording `unreadable`;
- the persona's own pane reads (the launch wait's evidence read and `checkWaitingRowPane`, through `readWorkingPane`, the `working`-row verdict `workingReconnectVerdict`, and b.jdc's prompt-row verdict `promptRowReconnectVerdict` and the ladder's `launchOnPromptRow`, and the pending-row rule's lap `readPendingRowLapPane`), through the shared read-pane (`readPersonaOwnPane`) and `latchOnUnusableName`, with the row state its caller last read (`working` or `waiting` for the two restart-path checks, `ask_user` or `check_permission` for the prompt-row paths, `pending` for the lap); the lap's Enter (`sendPendingRowLapEnter`) latches the same way on its own CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME, recorded `pending`;
- the dialog approver's `read-pane` and `send-keys`, through `latchOnUnusableName`, recording `pending` (the state the lap's `status` read); the approver types nothing and stops (`latched`);
- the reconnect's `send-keys` (`reconnectMcpWithCause`, b.jg5 SRJ-118), through `latchOnUnusableName`, recording the row state its caller last read; nothing is typed, the `send-keys` is not retried, and the reconnect answers `transient` (`reconnectUnusableNameLine`).
- the latch re-check's probe and lap read (`latchRecheckReadPane`, through `latchOnUnusableName`) and its launches (through their handlers' `unusableNameAt`), recording the state the re-check last read, with no latch-time read; the persona relatches with this case ([The re-check](#the-re-check-bjg5-srj-505)).

No other site latches on it: the persona teardown's kill and the start sweep's kills keep their own handling, and a teardown latches nothing. Nor does the CLI: an UNUSABLE_NAME at the CLI teardown's kill fails that persona at once, and one at its read between tries is a failed read after which the next try goes ahead (b.jg5 SRJ-904, SRJ-1002). An UNUSABLE NAME the teardown's kill meets, at a try or at the read between its tries, is raised as one notice that the teardown's window writes to the server log and a `persona-teardown-notice` entry (b.jg5 SRJ-1002, SRJ-1003; [Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-307) step 8). Every other `ErrInternal` stays UNCLASSIFIED.

**A launch start not recorded (b.jg5 SRJ-501, SRJ-513).** A configured persona's own row that reads `pending` with no launch start latches the persona with the case `launch-start-not-recorded`, the refused operation `none`, the recorded state `pending`, the session `slack_bot_<key>` and no description (`launchStartNotRecordedSetInput`; the latch's `setLaunchStartNotRecorded` builds the same input). Only an agent-director process older than the install, or a hand edit, writes such a row, and agent-director acts on no session for it. The trigger is the row-read rule's first decision ([Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)), so it latches wherever that rule is applied: every `get` through the shared own-row `get` read, every `status` through the own-row `status` step ([The shared own-row `status` read](#the-shared-own-row-status-read-bjg5-srj-115)) and each own row of the start sweep's `list` through the same act step ([Server-Managed Startup](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1) step 4, which then leaves every row of the persona unkilled), whether or not the row is the persona's current life. A persona already latched with another case relatches with this one (one new notice, below); a persona already latched with it keeps its record. A row under a key no configured persona uses latches nothing. While it holds, no automated path sends keys to the row's session or kills it: `deferPendingRow` gets no hand-off (Auto-Restart step 3, **`pending` rows**) and the pending-only retry stops ([Pending-only mode](#pending-only-mode-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305-srj-306)).

**What the record holds.** For a CONFLICT, the case and the quoted session come from agent-director's description (see the `conflict-latch.ts` entry of the Module Map).
