The refused operation is `plain-spawn` for a spawn, `reuse-spawn` for the reuse spawn and `resume` for the resume. The row state is the state the path last read before the refused call:

- no row, for the retry-spawn after the collision `get` answered `ErrSpawnNotFound`;
- for the resume and every spawn after a collision `get` that found a row (the replace step's reuse spawn, the spawn after `resume` answered `ErrSpawnNotFound` and the no-transcript reuse spawn after `ErrNoSessionId` or `ErrJsonlNeverWritten`, since `resume` reads nothing), the collision `get`'s state, or the later read that replaced it: the `working`-row wait's last `status` read, for a recovery after its `dead-session` verdict, or the prompt row's re-read after its sweep;
- for the live-row sequence's final `resume` and the plain spawn after its `ErrSpawnNotFound`, the state the sequence last read;
- for the reuse spawn after `ErrJsonlMissing`, its diagnosis `get` (`ErrSpawnNotFound` gives no row, any other error unreadable);
- for the reuse spawn, the state its caller passes as last read (`lastRead`): at the live-row sequence's final launch, the state the sequence last read; at the no-transcript step, as for the ladder's spawns above; no row for a reuse of an id with no row (agent-director's pre-spawn scan refused it and wrote no row); never a latch-time read;
- for a kill (refused operation "P's next check or recovery" for a CONFLICT): the live-row sequence's kills record the state the sequence last read, and the restart path's kill the restart run's last `dead` reading (`ended`, `missing`, or no row for `ErrSpawnNotFound`) with no further `status` read.

When the path read nothing before the call (the first spawn, and the restart path's kill after an `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` reading, which read no row), the CONFLICT row (and the UNUSABLE NAME row) makes exactly one `status` read then (`latchTimeRowState`), through the shared own-row `status` read inside the launch attempt: `ErrSpawnNotFound` gives no row, and any other error gives unreadable, which counts as live. A latch-time read that itself answers UNUSABLE_NAME latches the persona there (unusable recorded name, `unreadable`) and no further read is made; the call's own latch is then not set, so that latch stands alone, with one notice. So does a latch-time read that finds the persona's own row reading `pending` with no launch start (launch start not recorded, `pending`, b.jg5 SRJ-513): a CONFLICT or an UNUSABLE_NAME answer that made the read sets no latch of its own, and the persona gets that latch's one notice. A persona latched elsewhere while the latch-time read was awaited (`personaLatchedNow`; the health tick reads even while a launch is in flight, b.jg5 SRJ-315, SRJ-502) is handled the same way, whatever the read gave: that latch stands, no case is set on top of it, and the call's one line gives the outcome `the persona was latched elsewhere during the latch-time status read, so that latch stands` (where a read that latched itself gives `the latch-time status read latched the persona, so that latch stands`). No state is read again after a write the path made since (a kill, a delete, a sweep).

**The order at a set.** The latch-time read (when made), the set and its latched line, the holds, then the notice of the record's latch kind. The read's error may arm the persona's retry timer or open its unclassified-error episode; the holds, bound in `main()` before the notice (`bindConflictLatchHolds`), then stop the retry timer through the controller's `stop` with `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_LATCHED`, end the `tmux-unresponsive` condition silently, end the unclassified-error episode, reset the slow-recovery count and end the slow-recovery episode silently (b.jg5 SRJ-610, SRJ-1016), and end the stuck-launch episode silently (b.jg5 SRJ-1016). After a set, no retry timer, `tmux-unresponsive` condition, unclassified-error episode, slow-recovery episode, slow-recovery count or stuck-launch episode is left for the persona. The holds run on every set, a same-case set included.

**What a latch holds back.** Every path asks the latch where it acts, through `isLatched`. The one call that passes these gates is the re-check's own run of the restart path's decision, while its permit holds (`holdsLatchRecheckPermit`; [The re-check](#the-re-check-bjg5-srj-505)):

- **Every launch path.** `spawnForPersona` answers `latched` for a latched persona right after the in-flight join, with one line, `[slack] spawnForPersona: not launching <ref> — it is latched (case=<case>); no agent-director call (b.jg5 SRJ-502)`, and nothing else runs: no claude_config_dir check, trust patch, reply-guard step or agent-director call. The gate fails safe: a latch it cannot read is taken as latched, with `case=unknown`. An `isLatched` that throws gives `not launching <ref> — the latched query failed: <error> — taken as latched (case=unknown); no agent-director call (b.jg5 SRJ-502)`, a `record` that throws for a latched persona gives `— its latch record could not be read: <error> — taken as latched (case=unknown); …`, and a latched persona whose record comes back empty gives `— it is latched (case=unknown); …`. It is the one launch entry point, so this covers the start pass, the bring-up's launch (at start, after a bring-up retry and at an apply), a restart's relaunch and a retry's. `latched` is no failure and no attempt: `launchSession` answers `'skipped'`, and the start pass counts it neither as failed nor as succeeded.
- **The restart path.** `scheduleRestart` asks the latched query before any other gate and arms no timer for a latched persona, a scheduled and a human-triggered restart alike, logging `[slack] Not scheduling restart for persona=<key> — the persona is latched; no timer armed (b.jg5 SRJ-502)` once (a query that throws counts as latched, with ` (the latched query failed: <error> — taken as latched)` after `latched`); a timer already pending is left as it is. `runRestartWork`'s first step, before the shutdown and up checks and the liveness read, is the latched gate (`RestartDeps.isLatched`): a restart timer that was pending when the persona latched and then fires, and the retry entry (before its in-flight and cap checks), answer `latched` (`RESTART_OUTCOME_LATCHED`) with `[slack] Skipping restart for persona=<key> — the persona is latched; no agent-director call, nothing recorded (b.jg5 SRJ-502)`, and nothing is probed, reconnected, killed, launched or recorded. The work asks the latch again at three later points, because a launch outside the serializer (the start pass's, for example) can latch the persona while the work awaits, and so can the `get` after the escalate-dead sweep (b.jg5 SRJ-120): after the liveness read, right after the second up check and before any reconnect or kill; right after an escalate-dead reconnect answer, before its re-probe; and immediately before the kill (or, after an escalate-dead verdict that is not dead evidence, the relaunch) (after that re-probe, or on a `dead` reading). Any check that finds the persona latched answers `latched` with the same line, recording nothing, so a persona that latched during the restart's own awaits gets no reconnect and no kill. The reconnect adapter (`_buildReconnectSessionAdapter(getAppliedPersona, isLatched)`, bound in `main()` with the latch's `isLatched`) asks the latch once more after each of its own awaited steps that a further call follows (its `status` read; the `working` row's `read-pane`, before the fold, the sweep or a deferral; a prompt row's `read-pane`, before the sweep or the deferral; the `waiting` row's `read-pane`, before the sweep on a GONE or absent answer), right before each not-connected notice the `working`-row, `waiting`-row and prompt-row checks raise (the `unproven-idle` notice a noted deferral can raise, and the `blocked-on-prompt` notice), and right before it types `/mcp reconnect`, since a launch outside the serializer can latch the persona during those too. A latched persona, or a latched query that throws (taken as latched), gets nothing typed and one line, `[slack] reconnectSession: persona=<key> is latched — not typing /mcp reconnect; nothing done (b.jg5 SRJ-502)` (with ` (the latched query failed: <error> — taken as latched)` after `latched` when the query threw); the adapter answers `'transient'`, which the work maps to `reconnect-deferred` (`RESTART_OUTCOME_RECONNECT_DEFERRED`): no kill, nothing recorded. A query that throws is taken as latched (fail safe), at these gates and at the check after a `'skipped'` launch: the line then reads `[slack] Skipping restart for persona=<key> — the persona is latched (the latched query failed: <error> — taken as latched); no agent-director call, nothing recorded (b.jg5 SRJ-502)` and the outcome is the same.
- **The retry timer.** Stopped by the hold at the set, whatever its mode, causes or last row read (the condition-end entry and its exceptions are not used). A timer armed after the latch stops at its first retry, on the pre-call latched check, with no agent-director call; a full-mode retry whose work answers `latched` stops too. Its stopped line is `[slack] unavailable-retry: persona=<key> stopped[ (pending-only)] — the persona is latched`. A latched query that throws is taken as latched: the retry logs `[slack] unavailable-retry: persona=<key> the latched query failed: <error> — taken as latched; no agent-director call` and stops the same way.
- **A lost message.** It reports `held-for-human` and schedules no restart ([Inbound step 7](#inbound-slack--claude-code)).
- **The dialog approver (b.jg5 SRJ-502).** A persona latched before a lap stops its approver with no call; the approver asks the latch again after its `status` read and after its `read-pane`. A set of P by any site stops P's running approver at once with the reason `latched`, through the set observer `setConflictLatch` registers on the installed latch (`stopApproverOnLatch`): no approver call for P starts after the set returns.
- **A running live-row sequence (b.jg5 SRJ-502, SRJ-706).** A set of P by any site, the sequence's own latching kill included, stops P's running sequence with the reason `latched`, through a second set observer (`stopSequenceOnLatch`) the session manager registers once both the latch and the live-row sequence registry are installed: its stop signal is set inside the set call, so it makes no call after the one in progress returns. A latch stop drops no answer: the call's answer is handled as for a latched P, so a sequence's own CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME kill still ends as its latched abort ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717)).
- **The health tick.** `latched` is its first no-attempt reason ([Health-Check Poller](#health-check-poller) step 1), asked again right after the tick's own liveness read, which may latch the persona: the persona is still read, and a healthy reading takes the healthy branch, but the tick never calls `scheduleRestart`, posts no not-connected notice and arms no retry timer for it.
- **A read that latched the persona stops its path (b.jg5 SRJ-502, SRJ-512, SRJ-513).** The launch wait ends `latched`; the dialog approver stops with nothing read or typed; the prompt rows' re-read answers `FIND_MISSING_LATCHED`; the retry action asks the latched query right after its row read and stops; `runRestartWork` asks the latch right after the probe and after the re-probe; the reconnect adapter answers `'transient'`; the restart path's `working`-row verdict and prompt-row verdict answer `'transient'` and its `waiting`-row check `defer`; the ladder's prompt-row action answers `latched`. After an unusable-recorded-name latch nothing deletes, kills, launches, reuses or types for the persona, so no tmux-touching call is made for it; its own row is still read (`status` and `get` are not tmux-touching). After a launch-start-not-recorded latch the same paths stop, and nothing hands the row to `deferPendingRow` or to the pending-only retry.

The latch is per persona: other personas are unaffected.

**The notices (b.jg5 SRJ-508, SRJ-1004, SRJ-1016, SRJ-1019, SRJ-1020).** One notice reaction posts every latch kind's notice: `createConflictNoticeObserver`, bound once in `main()` by `bindConflictNotice`. On a `latched` or `relatched` set it first ends the persona's open notice episodes of the other latch kinds silently (`LATCH_NOTICE_EPISODE_KINDS`: `conflict`, `unusable-recorded-name`, `launch-start-not-recorded`), so a later relatch back to one of them posts again; then it begins or keeps the episode of the record's kind (`latchNoticeEpisodeKindOf`) and posts that kind's text in it at most once. A CONFLICT case or unrecognised text posts the CONFLICT notice; each hold case posts its own notice (`HOLD_NOTICES`), never the CONFLICT notice. A same-case set posts nothing. No not-connected notice holds a post back. The unusable-recorded-name notice (`unusableNameNoticeText`) is one line: *Held: unusable tmux session name*, that agent-director will not act on the persona's row `cscb_<key>` because its recorded tmux session name cannot be used, `agent-director said: "<description>".`, the pointer to the "Operator actions" section of agent-director's README for this row, that CSCB takes no action for the persona and that messages sent to it meanwhile are lost, and the human-only line. It names no command. The launch-start-not-recorded notice (`launchStartNotRecordedNoticeText`, from the `LAUNCH_START_NOTICE_*` parts) is one line too: *Held: launch start not recorded*, that the persona's agent-director row reads pending but records no launch start, so an agent-director process older than the install wrote it and agent-director will not act on its session, the quoted session `"slack_bot_<key>"` (rendered as the CONFLICT notice renders a session), the pointer to the "Operator actions" section of agent-director's README, what CSCB does meanwhile (`LAUNCH_START_NOTICE_HOLD`), and the human-only line. It names no command and quotes no description.

**Its lifetime (b.jg5 SRJ-504, SRJ-505, SRJ-506).** A latch lasts until one of three things ends it; nothing else clears it:

- **The persona's teardown.** A removal and a destructive modify's old half both run the [Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-307), which forgets the persona's latch silently (no post, no set observer call, no line) in its first steps, again once the launch in flight has settled, and once more after its kill (steps 1, 3 and 9), each of the first two times followed by its notice episodes, the CONFLICT episode included. A latch that launch set during the teardown goes too, a removed persona's included: inside the open window the CONFLICT and UNUSABLE NAME latch entries latch as for an applied persona ([Log-only routing](#log-only-routing-bjg5-srj-1002), **Inside an open teardown window**). Its CONFLICT notice is not held back: the CONFLICT observer runs synchronously inside the set (during step 2), before the teardown forgets anything, but the teardown's notice window is open by then, so the notifier writes it as one server-log line and one `persona-teardown-notice` entry, never posted to the old or the new half's destination and never dropped, for a removal and a destructive modify's old half alike (b.jg5 SRJ-1003). A CONFLICT the teardown's own kill meets latches nothing and is raised as one notice through the same window (step 8). Other personas' latches stay. A destructive modify's new half therefore starts unlatched (see [Destructive modify](#destructive-modify-bav2-sr-86-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-406-sri-408-sri-502)).
- **The clear entry.** A re-check whose read or retry finds the latch's condition gone clears it through the one clear entry (`createLatchClear`), which posts one recovery notice, ends the notice episode and stops the timer; the persona is then brought up as the clear allows ([How a latch clears and relatches](#how-a-latch-clears-and-relatches-bjg5-srj-506-srj-1005)). A clear by hand through the `/clear-latch` route ([POST /clear-latch](#post-clear-latch)) goes through the same entry and after-clear sequence, with the reason "cleared by hand", and, once it has cleared a latch, also resets the persona's restart failure count ([The re-check](#the-re-check-bjg5-srj-505), **The restart cap**).
- **A server restart.** The latch is held in memory only, with no persistence, so a process that ends drops every latch with its re-check timer; Graceful Shutdown forgets none of them first (it stops every re-check timer). After a restart a persona that was latched starts unlatched, and its next attempt that meets the same condition latches it again, with one new CONFLICT notice, through the collision ladder as above. Today that is the persona's launch at start: a leftover that a plain spawn's pre-spawn scan refused left no row, so the plain first spawn meets the scan again (case `leftover`); and a session with no valid label, met at "duplicate session" by a plain spawn that ended its row, is met again when the collision `get` reads that row `ended`, `resume` answers `ErrNoSessionId`, and the bring-up's reuse spawn of the same id meets "duplicate session" again: it relatches with one post, recording the refused operation `reuse-spawn` and the collision `get`'s `ended`, and nothing is deleted. A `provenance_conflict` note still on the persona's own row latches it again at the next read at one of the shared read's sites, such as the collision `get` of its launch at start. A persona's own row still reading `pending` with no launch start latches it again at the next `status` or `get` of that row that applies the row-read rule, such as the collision `get` of its launch at start. Each relatch records the row's state as the path reads it then, not the state the dropped latch recorded.

##### The re-check (b.jg5 SRJ-505)

Each latched persona P is looked at again on a bounded cadence, so a conflict a human has resolved is noticed without a restart: at most one re-check per 120 s (`LATCH_RECHECK_INTERVAL_MS`), on P's own timer, whatever `health_check_interval` is (0 included). A re-check is one read of P's row (step 1), then exactly the one call the table below names for the latch's refused operation and case, or none. It is the only path that makes a call for a latched persona (SRJ-502's "beyond the re-check"). The server builds it once through the session manager's one builder, `buildLatchRecheck(input)` (`src/session-manager.ts`), which `main()` and the recovery harness both call: the timers are `createLatchRecheckController` (`src/conflict-latch.ts`), each round is `runLatchRecheckRound`, and the clear hand-off is built there.

**The timer and its stops.** `bindLatchRecheck(latch, controller)`, bound in `main()` after the holds and the notice, adds the controller's set observer: a set that latches a persona that was not latched (`latched`) arms its timer, so a set runs the read, the set, the holds, the notice, then the arm. The first round is due one interval after the latch, on the injected clock (`SYSTEM_PERSONA_CONNECTION_CLOCK` in production); each fire submits one round through the persona lifecycle serializer (`personaLifecycle.run`), so it waits for P's turn and never overlaps P's other operations (after a clear that launched nothing, the after-clear run follows the round in the same turn); the next round is due one interval after that round settles. A relatch or a same-case set neither restarts the timer nor adds one. A fire, and a round when its turn comes, does nothing once P is no longer latched. The timer stops at the clear (the clear entry's `stop`), at every forget of P's latch (the forget observer `bindLatchRecheck` adds through the latch's `addForgetObserver`, so the persona teardown's `forgetConflictLatch` stops it), and at shutdown (`stopAll`, after which none is armed again; [Graceful Shutdown](#graceful-shutdown-sr-11-event-11)). A round in progress finishes and schedules nothing. No line is logged for an arm or a stop. The health tick is not handed the re-check and does not drive it.

**Step 1: the read.** One read through the shared own-row reads, which skip no latched persona: `get` (`readPersonaOwnRow`, site `LATCH_RECHECK_GET_READ_SITE`) for a "conflicting labels" latch, since only `get` shows the note, and `status` (`readPersonaOwnRowStatus`, `LATCH_RECHECK_STATUS_READ_SITE`) for every other. Their rules apply ([Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114), [The shared own-row `status` read](#the-shared-own-row-status-read-bjg5-srj-115)): the note, a `pending` row with no launch start, an UNUSABLE NAME answer and the retired-key entry clear. The round compares P's case before and after the read: a read that relatched P with another case ends the round (the set made its one post) and the next round follows the new case; a failed read gives no information and ends the round with no other call; a read that latched with the same case reads as the state it recorded. Step 1 then decides (`decideLatchRecheck`, pure, with `retiredKeyReadingOf(key)` read at the round):

- **No row** (`ErrSpawnNotFound`): a "not this launch's session" latch goes to its finished-row retry (below); a latch whose refused operation is a spawn, plain or reuse, retries that spawn whatever the case, with no probe (a reuse of an id with no row is an ordinary fresh spawn); every other latch clears, "its agent-director row is gone", a `resume` latch included (HO rev 28: P's next launch is the ladder's plain spawn).
- **Reported in.** A row read `waiting`, `working`, `ask_user` or `check_permission` clears the latch, with "its row reads <state>", only when the recorded state did not count as live (`rowStateCountsAsLive`: it read `pending`, `ended`, `missing` or no row), never for "not this launch's session" and never while the note is on a "conflicting labels" row. `rowStateCountsAsLive` is the recorded-state test of this clear only, never the HO rev 28 gate below.
- Otherwise step 2's table decides.

**Step 2: the table.** The first row that matches the latch's refused operation and case decides. "Finished" is a row step 1 read `ended` or `missing`. Every cleared outcome goes to the clear hand-off (below); what each clear posts and what follows it is in [How a latch clears and relatches](#how-a-latch-clears-and-relatches-bjg5-srj-506-srj-1005).

| # | Latch (refused operation; case) | The one call | Clears on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `resume` or reuse; "this row's own id", its probe dropped (`probeDropped`) | on a finished row, the latched operation retried; else none | the retry's clearing answer |
| 2 | `resume` or reuse; "this row's own id" | on a finished row, the probe; else none | the single retry's clearing answer, after a probe that finds the condition cleared (GONE) and its bypassing `find-missing` ([How a latch clears and relatches](#how-a-latch-clears-and-relatches-bjg5-srj-506-srj-1005)) |
| 3 | any operation; "the agent's pane was not found" | the probe (for a `resume` or reuse, only on a finished row) | as row 2, after a probe that finds a pane or GONE |
| 4 | `resume`, reuse or `bring-up`; "no valid instance id", "a different instance id", "another agent-director store", "left over from an earlier life" | on a finished row, the latched `resume` or reuse retried, else none; for `bring-up`, one run of the restart path's decision | the retry's or run's clearing answer |
| 5 | plain spawn; any case | on a finished row, a spawn with `reuse_finished` (never a plain spawn over the row); on any live state, `pending` included, none | the retry's clearing answer |
| 6 | any operation; "not this launch's session" | none (`status` only); a finished row, or no row at step 1, leads to the finished-row retry; the refused call is never retried | the finished-row retry's clearing answer; never a live reading |
| 7 | any operation; "conflicting labels" | the note on the row: none; `pending`: the lap's one-line `read-pane` (`allow_pending`, typing nothing); another live state: one run of the restart path's decision; finished: the latched `resume` or reuse, else the restart path's decision | step 1's reported-in reading with no note; the lap read's pane or GONE; the retry's or run's clearing answer |
| 8 | `none`; "unusable recorded name" | none (`status` only) | step 1 only |
| 9 | `none`; "launch start not recorded" | none (`status` only) | step 1, and a finished row |
| 10 | unrecognised text, "never reported in" | none | step 1 only |
| – | any other pair (for example a kill's or pane verb's `next-check-or-recovery` with "this row's own id" or "left over from an earlier life") | none: step 1 only, with one line naming the pair | step 1 only |

`probeDropped` is set (`setProbeDropped`, one line) when a row-2 latch's single retry after a cleared probe is refused again with "this row's own id" (a same-case set seen during the retry, the latch still on that case after it); a relatch with a new case starts without it. A retry of a key recorded in `retired-keys.json` that would be a `resume` or a plain spawn is the reuse, never `resume` (b.jg5 SRJ-805), finished-row retries included.

**HO rev 28.** A latched `resume` or reuse (rows 1, 2, 4, and a "conflicting labels" latch's launch) is probed or retried only when step 1 read its row `ended` or `missing`; any other reading, `pending` included, that step 1 did not clear gets no probe, no retry and no post. Step 1's read (`status`, or `get` for "conflicting labels") is the read rev 28 asks for, so the gate adds no call. A gone row clears a `resume` latch and retries a reuse latch's reuse as an ordinary fresh spawn. No passage of this document has a failed `resume` or reuse restore the row: what a refused launch left is read again, never assumed.

**The probe (b.jg5 SRJ-117).** One agent-director `read-pane` of P's own row with `n_lines` 1 (`PROBE_PANE_READ_LINES`) through the outage wrapper, never the shared read-pane (`readPersonaOwnPane`, which skips a latched persona and latches); CSCB reads no pane through tmux itself. Its answer is classified by the pure mapper `paneReadFailureOf` (`src/pane-read.ts`), a CONFLICT's case by `recogniseConflictCase`; there is no "no pane 0.0" case, and `ErrInvalidFlags` there is UNCLASSIFIED with no version re-check. Its verdict (`decideLatchRecheckProbe`): a pane keeps "this row's own id" latched and finds "the agent's pane was not found" cleared; GONE finds both cleared; a CONFLICT with the latch's own case keeps the latch; any other CONFLICT keeps the latch as it is, with no relatch and no post; an absent row (`ErrSpawnNotFound`) gives no information (the next step 1 decides). The "conflicting labels" lap read on a `pending` row is the same call with `allow_pending: true` (SRJ-410: it types nothing); it is that latch's retry, not a probe (`decideLatchRecheckPendingReadPane`): a pane or GONE clears, its own case keeps the latch, and another case relatches through the CONFLICT entry with the refused operation "P's next check or recovery".

**The retries.** Each launch goes through the one handler for it, never a copy: a plain spawn through `plainSpawnOutcomeAt` ([Plain spawn](#plain-spawn-bjg5-srj-111)), a reuse through `reuseSpawnForPersona` ([Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)) and a `resume` through `resumeAtSite` (its SRJ-113 rows; [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)), registered as P's launch in flight and run as a launch attempt, after the trust patch. Each of the round's launches (`latchRecheckLaunch`: the retry at the cadence, the spawn retry after step 1 found no row, the finished-row retry's launch and the single retry after a cleared probe) first asks the restart cap, then the gates every other launch path asks, in `launchSession`'s and `spawnForPersona`'s order, through their own functions, and makes no call when one stops it:

1. **At the cap** (b.av2 SR-6.3; the cap wins over the re-check): the restart cap (`LatchRecheckRoundDeps.isAtCap`; `main()` passes `(key) => backoffIsAtCap(key, RESTART_FAILURE_CAP)`, the one failure counter the restart path, the health tick and the retry timer ask, to `buildLatchRecheck` as `LatchRecheckInput.isAtCap`). A query that throws counts as at the cap; with none given (`latchRecheckAtCap`), no persona is at it. One line, `[slack] latch-recheck: <ref> is at the restart cap — no <call> in this re-check; the persona stays latched (b.av2 SR-6.3; b.jg5 SRJ-505, SRJ-506)` (`latchRecheckAtCapLine`); answer `at-cap` (`LATCH_RECHECK_AT_CAP`).
2. **Not up:** the relaunch gate (`LatchRecheckRoundDeps.canRelaunch`; `main()` passes `canRelaunch`, the restart path's `canRestart`, to `buildLatchRecheck` as `LatchRecheckInput.canRelaunch`). A gate that throws counts as not up, as does one asked before `main()` has built it; with no gate given (`latchRecheckMayRelaunch`), the launch is allowed. One line, `[slack] latch-recheck: <ref> is not up — no <call> in this re-check; the persona stays latched (b.av2 SR-6.4; b.jg5 SRJ-505)`; answer `not-up`.
3. **Held:** the `ErrInvalidFlags` held gate (`heldGateReadingOf`, read directly, since `heldResult` defers to the latched gate, which the re-check is). The held line (`invalidFlagsHeldNoLaunchLine`, site `latch-recheck`); answer `held`.
4. **Old life:** the hold step with its re-check option (`oldLifeHoldStep(persona, 'latch-recheck', ref, { latchRecheck: true })`): P is recorded as waiting, the hold's wait starts, and no retry timer is armed ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809)); answer `sequence-waiting`.

Each of these answers gives no information: P stays latched with no post, the round line reads `answer=no-information (at-cap)`, `(not-up)`, `(held)` or `(sequence-waiting)`, and the next round asks again; step 1's read is still made each round (after a cleared probe, the cap is asked before the bypassing `find-missing`, which runs before the other gates; [How a latch clears and relatches](#how-a-latch-clears-and-relatches-bjg5-srj-506-srj-1005), **After a cleared probe**). After the gates, with a launch already in flight, a dry run or a `claude_config_dir` that does not resolve, no call is made. Each passes the state the re-check last read as its last read, so a CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME relatches with that state and no latch-time read (`recordedRowState`); no site deletes a row before a spawn, so no fresh read is added. The answers (SRJ-506):

- **Not refused:** the latch clears through the handlers' clear hook (`clearLatchBeforeOutcome`) before the after-launch step, so the dialog approver runs unlatched.
- **A definite failure** (`isDefiniteLaunchAnswer`: LAUNCH FAILURE or DIRECTORY; for a `resume` also its STATE rows and GONE): the latch clears first, then the answer is handled by its class as at any launch: a no-transcript `resume` goes on to the no-transcript reuse (`noTranscriptReuse`, its lost-transcript diagnosis and notice included), `ErrSpawnNotResumable` arms the lost-race cause and answers `retrying`, `ErrSpawnNotFound` goes on to the plain spawn, and a DIRECTORY answer raises `cwd-unreachable`.
- **Counting.** Once the launch settles its result is counted as any launch outside the restart path's (`countLaunchOutsideRestartWork`, shared with the live-row sequence's final launch): a success resets P's failure count, a LAUNCH FAILURE or DIRECTORY answer (marked `countedClass`) is one counted failure, with the cap notice at the cap; nothing else is counted.
- **CONFLICT:** with the latch's own case, P stays latched with its record unchanged and no post; with another case, P relatches with one post and the next round follows the new case. **UNUSABLE NAME** relatches with "unusable recorded name".
- **`ErrInstanceIdCollision`** gives no information whatever the latch (`latchRecheckCollided`): P stays latched with no post, no get-then-act and no further call. After a `resume` whose definite answer cleared the latch, a collision of the spawn that follows arms the collision cause and answers `retrying`.
- **UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT, UNCLASSIFIED, CONFIG:** no information (below); an UNAVAILABLE launch makes no SRJ-407 `get` (`afterLaunchUnavailable`). A reuse meeting `ErrInvalidFlags` holds P ([The `ErrInvalidFlags` hold](#the-errinvalidflags-hold-bjg5-srj-207-srj-1008)).

A lost-transcript notice a refused reuse dropped (`noTranscriptReuse`'s) is not carried to a later re-check: a re-check reuse that succeeds posts none, since its line and startup entry were already written; a re-check `resume` meeting no transcript runs a fresh diagnosis, which posts its own notice. Outside a re-check, a launch whose persona was latched elsewhere while its call was awaited sets nothing on its own CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME (`latchedElsewhereDuringCall`, b.jg5 SRJ-502); a call inside a re-check skips that check, since its CONFLICT is the round's answer.

**The finished-row retry.** For "not this launch's session": one `get` (`LATCH_RECHECK_FINISHED_ROW_GET_SITE`, through `readPersonaOwnRow`), then the launch `decideFinishedRowLaunch` names: a row read `ended` or `missing` with a session id gets a `resume`, one with none a reuse; no row left gets the plain first spawn (through `plainSpawnOutcomeAt`); a row read live, `pending` included, gets no launch (HO rev 28), and a failed `get` gives no information. Never a kill and never a plain spawn over a row.

**The run of the restart path's decision.** `runRestartWorkInTurn(key, cwd, permit)` (`src/restart.ts`) runs the restart work inside the round's serializer turn: never the retry entry `runRestartRetry`, which submits through the serializer and would wait on that turn forever ([Per-persona serialization](#per-persona-serialization-bav2-sr-66), re-entrancy rule). The run carries the re-check's permit (`LatchRecheckPermit`) in its scope, and every latched gate it reaches lets it through while the permit holds (`holdsLatchRecheckPermit`): the restart work's gates (`skipIfLatched`, and its checks after a launch or a kill, `readLatchedForCall`), the session manager's launch gate and every stop built on `personaLatchedNow` (through `latchGateReadingOf`), and the reconnect adapter's (`reconnectLatchedAt`). No other caller holds it. The permit is revoked at the run's first refusal: any set of P's latch while the run goes (a set observer that lives for the run only, added through the latch's `addSetObserver`, which the round's deps require; if adding it throws, the permit could not be revoked, so no run is made: one line, `latchRecheckObserverFailedLine`, and the answer `observer-failed` (`LATCH_RECHECK_OBSERVER_FAILED`), no information, the round line reading `answer=no-information (observer-failed)`), and the run's launch answering `failed` while P is still latched (no information: `launchSession` answers `'skipped'`, nothing counted). From then on every gate stops the run, so a run that leaves P latched makes no further call. A permitted run's launch declined for another reason answers launch-skipped, and its kill failing UNAVAILABLE answers refused. The run clears the latch before any step that stops for a latched persona: a launch through the handlers' clear hook, a live-row sequence before it begins (`startLiveRowSequence`); and a run that completes with no refusal (already connected, reconnected, launched, a counted failure or capped) clears it after the run when nothing has. The restart cap is asked first, before the set observer is added (the restart work itself does not ask it for this run): at the cap no run is made, with the at-cap line (`latchRecheckAtCapLine`, `<call>` `restart-decision`), no information, the answer `at-cap` (`LATCH_RECHECK_AT_CAP`) and the round line reading `answer=no-information (at-cap)`.

**The restart cap (b.av2 SR-6.3).** The cap wins over the re-check: a latched P at the restart cap is not relaunched by it. Its reads are made as below the cap (step 1, the probe, the lap `read-pane`, the finished-row retry's `get`), so a reading can still clear its latch; it gets no launch, no run of the restart path's decision and no cleared probe's bypassing `find-missing`, which serves only the retry. Each round logs at most one at-cap line, where that call would have been made. A clear at the cap by the re-check (step 1's, the lap read's, or a "launch start not recorded" row read finished) leaves P's failure count as it is: the after-clear run makes its `find-missing` where it makes one, then its retry at once goes through the retry entry, whose cap check answers `capped` with no call (`restartRetryCapSkippedLine`; [UNAVAILABLE retry](#unavailable-retry-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305), **Cap check second**) unless one of the entry's earlier checks answers first (latched, held, or `in-flight` while other work for P runs); the retry launches nothing either way, so P stays down, unlatched, until its count resets (P's teardown, through `forgetFailures`, or a server restart). A later clear by hand finds P unlatched and resets nothing.

A clear by hand that clears P's latch resets P's failure count and its cap-notified latch (b.jg5 SRJ-509): `main()` passes `forgetFailures` (`src/backoff.ts`), the reset of the counter `isAtCap` reads, to `buildLatchRecheck` as `LatchRecheckInput.resetRestartFailures`, which the builder hands to `clearAndRecover` only (`LatchClearSequenceDeps.resetRestartFailures`), never to the round path's clears. The reset runs in the job's turn, right after the clear entry answers that P was latched and before `cleared` settles, so the count is 0 when the route answers and the retry at once after the bypassing `find-missing` is not refused by the cap: a P that was at the cap is launched, and a new cap notice can follow only after `RESTART_FAILURE_CAP` more counted failures. A reset that throws logs one line (`latchClearRestartResetFailedLine`) and changes nothing else the job does; with no reset given, a clear by hand resets nothing. With no `isAtCap` given, no persona is at the cap.

**No information (b.jg5 SRJ-307, SRJ-313).** Every call of a round runs inside the re-check's scope, `runInLatchRecheck(scope, fn)` (`src/unavailable-retry.ts`), carried across awaits as the attempt context is; `isInsideLatchRecheck(key)` answers true there while P is still latched. Inside it an answer gives no information: no cause arms P's retry timer (the controller logs one `not armed … inside its latch re-check` line), no `tmux-unresponsive` condition starts or continues, `tmux-unavailable` is not raised (a `find-missing` run's ENVIRONMENT answer still raises it, b.jg5 SRJ-506), nothing feeds the unclassified-error episode, neither pending-only arm arms, and the restart work arms nothing on an `unknown` reading. So UNAVAILABLE (`ErrCallTimeout` included), ENVIRONMENT (`ErrTmuxNotAvailable`) and UNCLASSIFIED (`ErrUnknownErrorName` and an unclassified `ErrInternal` included) keep P latched with no post. Unchanged inside it: CONFIG raises `ad-config-malformed` and keeps the latch, `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` raises `ad-unreachable`, DIRECTORY is definite (it clears, then `cwd-unreachable` by class), and every clear on a success or a GONE answer is made. Once an answer clears the latch, the rest of that path is ordinary. `runOutsideAttempts` leaves the scope, so the dialog approver, a live-row sequence and the other paths that run there are never part of a re-check. Every decision is by class through `src/ad-error-class.ts`.

**The clear hand-off.** Every cleared outcome goes to one hand-off (`LatchRecheckClearHandOff`, `src/conflict-latch.ts`), called synchronously and at most once per round, before any step of the clearing path that stops for a latched persona and before a definite failure's class handling. It is given what cleared (`by`, one of `RECHECK_CLEARED_BY_*`), the record and the recovery notice's reason. The production hand-off (`createLatchRecheckClearHandOff`, `src/session-manager.ts`) clears through the one clear entry and owes the after-clear run for a clear that launched nothing ([How a latch clears and relatches](#how-a-latch-clears-and-relatches-bjg5-srj-506-srj-1005)). A probe that finds the condition cleared is no clear and is never handed off: the round goes on to its bypassing `find-missing` and single retry, whose answer may clear.

**Its cost.** Per latched persona and 120 s: one read, and at most one call after it (the finished-row retry's `get` and the launch it decides; a run of the restart path's decision makes that path's own calls). A retry or run that leaves P latched makes no further call: no SRJ-407 `get` after an UNAVAILABLE and no latch-time `status` read. A P at the restart cap gets the reads only (step 1's, and the probe, the lap `read-pane` or the finished-row retry's `get` its case names). A refused kill, `send-keys` or `pause` is never retried, and a refused `read-pane` only as the one-line probe its case names.

**Its lines.** One line per round, `[slack] conflict-latch: re-check of <ref> — case=<case> step=<step> call=<call> answer=<answer>` (`latchRecheckRoundLine`), with `<step>` step 1's outcome (so a spawn latch's retry after step 1 found no row reads `step=spawn-retry`, and a "not this launch's session" latch's finished-row retry `step=finished-row-retry`) and `<call>` `none` when it made no call after its read; a relatch logs the latch's own line, and a latch matching no row logs `[slack] latch-recheck: <ref>'s latch (refused=<operation>, case=<case>) matches no re-check row — its read only (b.jg5 SRJ-505)` (`latchRecheckUnmatchedLine`). The other lines are in [Latch re-check lines](#latch-re-check-lines-bjg5-srj-505).

##### How a latch clears and relatches (b.jg5 SRJ-506, SRJ-1005)

Apart from P's teardown and a server restart, a latch clears only through the one clear entry, `createLatchClear` (`src/conflict-latch.ts`), which `buildLatchRecheck` builds over the latch, the notice episodes and the re-check timers' stop, and answers as `LatchRecheck.clear`. It has two callers: the re-check's clear hand-off, and the clear by hand of the `/clear-latch` route ([POST /clear-latch](#post-clear-latch); b.jg5 SRJ-510). The clear by hand is `clearByHandOf(latchRecheck)` (`src/session-manager.ts`), the one binding `main()` builds right after `bindLatchRecheck` and the recovery harness builds over its own re-check: `LatchRecheck.clearAndRecover(key, LATCH_RECOVERY_REASON_CLEARED_BY_HAND)`, the same entry and after-clear sequence, answering only whether P was latched. There is no second clear path. A persona cleared by hand whose next attempt meets the same condition latches again, with a new post (the clear ended the notice episode, **Episodes after a clear** below).

**The clear entry.** For a latched P, in order: the record is removed (`forget`, its forget observers told); P's timer is stopped; the recovery notice (`latchRecoveryText` for the record's latch kind, the reason and the quoted session) is posted once under `LATCH_RECOVERY_MARK` in P's episode of the record's kind (`latchNoticeEpisodeKindOf`), begun first when none is open, so every clear posts exactly once; every latch-kind episode is ended silently (`LATCH_NOTICE_EPISODE_KINDS`), so a later latch of any kind, its case the same or not, begins a new episode and posts again (b.jg5 SRJ-1016); one line (`latchClearedLine`). The post goes through the persona notifier, which adds the persona prefix; after the episodes' `close` at shutdown nothing is posted and the line says so. Removing the record first makes a second clear of the same latch, or a clear of an unlatched P, answer false with no post and no line. Each step is isolated and the entry never throws.

**The clear points and their reasons.** The reason is SRJ-1005's, attached by the clearing path:

| Clear point | `by` | Reason | What follows |
|---|---|---|---|
| Step 1 reads no row (`ErrSpawnNotFound`; never "not this launch's session" or a spawn latch) | `step-1` | its agent-director row is gone | the after-clear run: one bypassing `find-missing`, then P retried at once |
| Step 1 reads a reported-in row (recorded state not live, no note) | `step-1` | its agent-director row reads `<state>` | as above |
| "Launch start not recorded" row read `ended` or `missing` | `launch-start-finished` | its agent-director row reads `<state>` | the after-clear run with no `find-missing`: its one bring-up retry |
| "Conflicting labels" lap `read-pane` of a `pending` row answers a pane or GONE | `pending-read-pane` | a retry of the refused operation was not refused | the after-clear run with no `find-missing`: P retried at once |
| A retry at the cadence, the single retry after a cleared probe, or a run of the restart path's decision, not refused | `retry`, `restart-decision` | a retry of the refused operation was not refused | the clear only: the retry's own outcome stands, with no second launch |
| "Not this launch's session" finished-row retry not refused | `finished-row-retry` | its row finished and a relaunch was not refused | the clear only |

`RECHECK_CLEARS_THAT_LAUNCHED_NOTHING` holds the first three `by` values. No recovery notice comes before a finished-row retry or a spawn retry after step 1 found no row: those are made with P still latched, and only their answer clears.

**A retry's answer.** For the single retry after a cleared probe and a retry at the cadence alike: a CONFLICT with the latch's own case keeps P latched, record unchanged, no post; another case relatches with one post (a new episode), the record taking the retry's operation, case and the state the retry's path read; a `provenance_conflict` note on a row the retry's path reads counts as "conflicting labels"; UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT and UNCLASSIFIED give no information; CONFIG keeps the latch and raises `ad-config-malformed`; UNUSABLE NAME relatches with "unusable recorded name"; `ErrInstanceIdCollision` gives no information whatever the latch (no post, no get-then-act, nothing cleared); any other, definite, answer clears before any step that stops for a latched P and is then handled by its class ([The re-check](#the-re-check-bjg5-srj-505), **The retries**). A restore sentence in a `resume`'s or reuse's description decides nothing.

**After a cleared probe.** A probe that finds the condition cleared (rows 2 and 3) is followed in the same round, its scope and P's turn, with P still latched, by `latchRecheckClearedProbeRetry`:

1. the single retry's call, `decideClearedProbeRetry(record, reading, retiredKeyRecorded)`: the latched `resume` or reuse only when step 1 read the row `ended` or `missing` (HO rev 28; the probe is gated the same way); a plain spawn as the plain-spawn row keys on step 1's row (no row: the plain spawn; finished: a spawn with `reuse_finished`; a live row: none, so no `find-missing` either); a latch from a pane verb, a kill or a note: one run of the restart path's decision; a retired key's `resume` or plain spawn is the reuse. With a retry decided, the restart cap is asked (`isAtCap`): a P at the cap gets no `find-missing`, which serves only the retry, and no retry, with one at-cap line naming the retry's call (`latchRecheckAtCapLine`); the round line reads `call=read-pane+none` and `answer=probe-cleared (<kind>); no retry (at-cap)`, and P stays latched with no post. A decision of no retry asks nothing and logs nothing;
2. one bypassing `find-missing` (`bypassingFindMissingSweep`, site `latch-recheck`, no next-step `get`). Only `FIND_MISSING_REFUSED` (UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG, UNCLASSIFIED) holds the retry back: no retry in that round, P stays latched with no post, and the next round probes again; inside the scope it arms nothing, a CONFIG answer raises `ad-config-malformed` and an ENVIRONMENT answer `tmux-unavailable`. `FIND_MISSING_LATCHED`, the answer the run gives a caller already latched, is no refusal here and goes on, as does a result or any other failure. The run's post-run `get` skips the latched P, so it never relatches P;
3. exactly one retry through the round's own handlers and permit (`latchRecheckLaunch`, or `latchRecheckRestartDecision`), its answer judged as above. A "this row's own id" `resume` or reuse refused again with that case drops the probe for the episode (`setProbeDropped`), so row 1 decides from then on; a collision or no-information answer drops nothing.

A retry at the cadence has no `find-missing` before it and makes no other call. The round's line reads `call=<call>+<retry call>` and `answer=probe-cleared (<kind>); <outcome>`.

**The after-clear run.** After a clear that launched nothing, P is retried at once, as one job in P's lifecycle serializer turn, outside every attempt and re-check scope (`runOutsideAttempts`), so no permit carries into it:

- On the round path the hand-off makes the clear at once (`clearForSequence`: the clear entry, P's working-row evidence forgotten, P held active by `holdRestartActive`) and hands the unstarted run to the round's operation (`runLatchRecheckRoundThenOwed`), which awaits it right after the round, in the same turn, so nothing else queued for P runs between the clear and the run.
- For a clear by hand, `runLatchClearSequence(key, reason, deps, options)` (through `clearAndRecover`) submits one job through P's serializer (`deps.serialize`) whose first step is the clear: nothing is cleared before P's turn comes, so the clear waits behind work already queued for P, a running re-check round and the run it owes included, and finds the latch as that work left it. In its turn the job makes the clear (the clear entry, `deps.clear`; then, for a latched P, the reset of P's restart failure count and cap-notified latch, `deps.resetRestartFailures`, and the same hold `clearForSequence` takes, `holdForSequence`: its working-row evidence forgotten and P held active by `holdRestartActive`), then the run below in the same turn. A reset that throws is logged (`latchClearRestartResetFailedLine`) and swallowed: the answer, the `find-missing` and the retry go on as without it. An unlatched P gets nothing more: no call, no post, no timer change and no reset (`not-latched`). It answers in two parts (`LatchClearSequenceAnswer`): `cleared` settles once the clear, and for a latched P the reset, have run in P's turn, with whether P was latched, and keeps that answer whatever the job does next; `done` settles with the outcome once the job has ended and never rejects. The route awaits only `cleared` (`clearByHandOf`); the job runs to its end whether or not anyone awaits either part. Neither part may be awaited from inside P's turn: the job waits for that turn.

The run, in its turn: a P not in the applied configuration gets no call (`not-applied`); a P latched again before its turn gets none (`relatched`, SRJ-502). Then, after step 1's clear (and a clear by hand; `findMissingFirst`, default true), one bypassing `find-missing` (site `latch-clear`, no next-step `get`) as a recovery attempt of P (`runInAttempt(key, 'recovery')`): a refusal stops that attempt with no launch, and because the run reports inside the attempt, its answer arms P's retry timer and raises its outage as its class says (`find-missing-refused`; P, now unlatched, is left to that timer). Its post-run `get` of P's row, when the run lists it in `unverified_ids`, relatches P on a `provenance_conflict` note still present, with a new post, and the run answers `FIND_MISSING_LATCHED` (`relatched`, no retry); a note the run removed latches nothing. Otherwise P is retried at once through the in-turn retry entry (`deps.retryAtOnce`, default `runRestartRetryInTurn` with `personaRetryBlockCause`): the retry entry's gates and accounting (after a re-check's clear, which leaves the failure count as it is, a P at the restart cap that no earlier gate stops answers `capped` with no call; after a clear by hand, which has reset the count, the cap does not stop it; [The re-check](#the-re-check-bjg5-srj-505), **The restart cap**), one run of the restart path's decision, which for a `pending` row arms P's retry timer (b.jg5 SRJ-409) and for a retired key's row with no "new life has begun" mark starts the live-row sequence (b.jg5 SRJ-411) (`retried`, with its outcome). A "launch start not recorded" clear on `ended` or `missing` and a "conflicting labels" `pending` `read-pane` clear make no `find-missing` first. For a clear by hand, a job that cannot be submitted, or that the serializer rejects before it runs, clears and posts nothing: `cleared` rejects and `done` answers `retry-failed`, with one line. A clear that throws answers nothing: `cleared` rejects, nothing runs after it and `done` answers `retry-failed`, with one line. A throw after the clear answered leaves `cleared` with that answer, and `done` answers `retry-failed`, with one line. The active hold is released exactly once on every path. These `find-missing` runs are not part of the 120 s re-check's budget.

**The active hold.** From the clear to the run's end P reads as restart-active (`holdRestartActive`), so the health tick, which skips an active persona before any read, reads nothing of P's row before the run's `find-missing`. Residual: the lost-message path's `status` read of P can still land between a clear and the end of that `find-missing`; a `status` read shows no note, so it cannot latch P on a note the run would have cleared.

**Episodes after a clear.** The clear ends the latch's notice episode, so a latch of P after it, with the same case or not, posts one new notice. The latch's set reset P's slow-recovery count and ended its slow-recovery episode (the holds, [The order at a set](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)), so P's slow-recovery count after a clear begins a new episode (b.jg5 SRJ-610). A same-case refusal posts nothing, so no round clears a latch only for the next to relatch it with a second post of the same case.

**Its lines.** One clear line, `[slack] conflict-latch: persona=<key> cleared — case=<case> session="<name>" reason="<reason>"; recovery notice posted` (or `not posted (the notice episodes are closed)`), and one line per after-clear outcome, prefixed `[slack] latch-clear:` ([Latch re-check lines](#latch-re-check-lines-bjg5-srj-505)).

#### The `ErrInvalidFlags` hold (b.jg5 SRJ-207, SRJ-1008)

A reuse spawn that agent-director answers `ErrInvalidFlags` shows that the installed binary rejects the flags of this release's launch, so every further launch would be rejected the same way or do something unintended. The persona is held: nothing is launched for it until the binary changes, the server restarts or it is torn down, and a human is told once. The hold is the server's one instance (`createInvalidFlagsHold`, `src/invalid-flags-hold.ts`), built in `main()` before the start pass and installed in the session manager (`setInvalidFlagsHold`). It holds at most one record per persona key, the version the hold began under (absent when unknown), in memory only: no persistence and no timer.

**What holds.** Only a reuse spawn holds (`reuseSpawnForPersona`, its `ErrInvalidFlags` row `invalidFlagsAtReuse`; [Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)), wherever it runs: the replace step's finished-row branch, the no-transcript step, the live-row sequence's final launch, and a retired key's reuse at its first launch and in place of a `resume` ([Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-bjg5-srj-806-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-407)). The `ErrInvalidFlags` gets exactly one immediate version re-check through the `ErrInvalidFlags` step ([Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)), and the pure `decideInvalidFlagsHold(answer, lastAdVersionSeen())` decides on its answer:

- `pass`: the persona is held under the version the re-check found;
- `could-not-run`, `not-running` (no re-check installed, disposed or already stopped) or an answer of any other kind: the persona is held under the re-check's last version seen (`lastAdVersionSeen()`, `ad-version-gate.ts`), or under none when it gives none;
- `stop`: nothing is held. The re-check has stopped the server (a binary below the Phase 1 floor or too old, b.jg5 SRJ-205), and the reuse answers `failed` marked `stopping` with its one line, nothing posted or counted.

On a hold the reuse calls the hold's `set(key, version)`, logs one line (`reuseInvalidFlagsHeldLine`, [Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)) and answers `held`: no spawn-failure notice, no `spawn-failed` entry, nothing counted, nothing armed and nothing reported to the unclassified-error episode. CSCB never falls back to a plain spawn or to any tmux-touching call, and deletes nothing. With no hold installed (unit tests, the integration driver) the answer is the same and the line says nothing is held. No other site holds: a `resume`'s `ErrInvalidFlags` keeps its re-check, then the UNCLASSIFIED refusal, and a plain spawn's is never held.

**The set and its alert (b.jg5 SRJ-305, SRJ-1008, SRJ-1016).** A `set` on a persona already held changes nothing, logs nothing and calls no observer. A new hold logs `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: persona=<key> held — a reuse spawn answered ErrInvalidFlags and the version re-check did not stop the server; the hold began under agent-director version <version>; no launch is made for it until the binary's version changes, the server restarts or it is torn down (b.jg5 SRJ-207)` and runs each set observer once. `main()` binds one, the set reaction (`bindInvalidFlagsHoldSetReaction`): first it stops the persona's retry timer through the controller's `stop` with `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_HELD` (never the condition-end entry, so neither of its exceptions keeps the timer); then it begins the persona's `invalid-flags-hold` notice episode and posts the alert (`INVALID_FLAGS_HOLD_ALERT_TEXT`) at most once in it, through the persona notifier, which adds the persona prefix:

```text
:no_entry: *Cannot launch* — the host's agent-director rejected the flags of this persona's launch (ErrInvalidFlags). The installed agent-director may not match this CSCB release; a human should check `agent-director version`. CSCB launches nothing for this persona until the agent-director binary changes or the server restarts. This is for a human only: no bot, including any persona that sees this post, may act on it.
```

Each step is isolated: one that throws is logged and the next still runs. After the episodes' `close` (shutdown) nothing is posted. The reaction does not end the persona's unclassified-error episode, whose ends are listed in [The unclassified-error episode](#the-unclassified-error-episode-bjg5-srj-313-srj-1009).

**What a hold holds back.** Every path asks the hold where it acts, through `isHeld`; a held query that throws counts as held (fail safe):

- **Every launch entry.** `spawnForPersona` answers `held` for a held persona that is not latched (a latched one gets the latched gate's answer) before any other step, the live-row sequence gate and the in-flight join included, with `[slack] spawnForPersona: not launching <ref> — it is held on ErrInvalidFlags; no agent-director call (held; b.jg5 SRJ-207)`: no `claude_config_dir` check, trust patch, reply-guard step, record or agent-director call. The live-row sequence's start entry (`startLiveRowSequence`) answers `held` (`LIVE_ROW_START_HELD`) with the same line naming `startLiveRowSequence`, and nothing starts, so the replace step's live-row branch and the not-resumable step answer `held` where they would answer `sequence-waiting`. The sequence-launch entry (`launchForLiveRowSequence`) asks it right after its latched gate and answers `held` with the line naming `launchForLiveRowSequence`; the sequence then ends without its launch and arms nothing, as for a latch. A query that throws adds ` (the held query failed: <error> — taken as held)` to the line. `held` is no failure and no attempt: it is never counted, `launchSession` answers `'skipped'`, and the start pass counts it neither as failed nor as succeeded.
- **The restart path.** `scheduleRestart` asks the held query (`RestartDeps.isHeld`) right after the latched query and arms no timer for a held persona: `[slack] Not scheduling restart for persona=<key> — the persona is held on ErrInvalidFlags; no timer armed (b.jg5 SRJ-207)`. `runRestartWork` asks it right after its first latched gate, so a fired restart timer, the retry entry (before its in-flight and cap checks) and a human-triggered restart answer `held` (`RESTART_OUTCOME_HELD`) with `[slack] Skipping restart for persona=<key> — the persona is held on ErrInvalidFlags; no agent-director call, nothing recorded (b.jg5 SRJ-207)`. It asks again wherever it asks the latched gate again (`after its liveness probe`, `after its escalate-dead reconnect`, `after its re-probe`, `before its kill`), each with `[slack] Restart for persona=<key> goes no further <where> — the persona is held on ErrInvalidFlags; nothing more is called for it, nothing recorded (b.jg5 SRJ-207)`, and after a launch that answered `'skipped'`, with `[slack] Session relaunch for persona=<key> ended held on ErrInvalidFlags — not counted; nothing more is done for it (b.jg5 SRJ-207)`. A query that throws adds ` (the held query failed: <error> — taken as held)` after `ErrInvalidFlags`. Nothing is probed, reconnected, killed, launched or recorded, and nothing counts toward the cap.
- **The retry timer.** Stopped by the set reaction, whatever its mode, causes or last row read. A timer armed while the persona is held (a session disconnect while `tmux-unavailable` is raised arms one) stops at its first retry, in either mode, on the pre-call held check right after the latched one, with no agent-director call; a full-mode retry whose work answers `held` stops too. Its stopped line is `[slack] unavailable-retry: persona=<key> stopped[ (pending-only)] — the persona is held on ErrInvalidFlags`. A query that throws gives `[slack] unavailable-retry: persona=<key> the held query failed: <error> — taken as held; no agent-director call` and the same stop. The stop is not terminal: once the hold ends a later refusal can arm the timer again ([UNAVAILABLE retry](#unavailable-retry-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305)).
- **The health tick.** `held` is its no-attempt reason right after `latched` ([Health-Check Poller](#health-check-poller) step 1): the persona is still read, and a healthy reading takes the healthy branch, but the tick never calls `scheduleRestart`, posts no not-connected notice and arms no retry timer for it.
- **A lost message.** It reports `cannot-launch` and fires no restart ([Inbound step 7](#inbound-slack--claude-code)).

The hold is per persona: other personas are unaffected.

**How it ends (b.jg5 SRJ-204, SRJ-207).** Nothing else re-checks or clears a hold:

- **The binary's version changes.** `main()` registers one listener on the runtime re-check's version-changed signal (`onAdVersionChanged`, `ad-version-gate.ts`). When a re-check, timed (every 120 s) or triggered, passes with a version different from the last version seen, `endInvalidFlagsHoldsOnVersionChange` ends every hold whose version differs from the new one, or that began under none (the hold's `versionChanged`), with one line each, `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: persona=<key> hold ended — agent-director version <began> changed to <new> (b.jg5 SRJ-207)`. A hold under the new version stays, and a pass on the same version or a re-check that could not run ends nothing. For each persona whose hold ended, its hold episode ends silently, and then, when it is still in the applied configuration, it is retried at once: `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: persona=<key> retried at once after its hold ended (b.jg5 SRJ-207)`, then one run of the restart path's retry entry (`runRestartRetry`, without the delay gate), whose answer is logged as `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: persona=<key> retry after its hold ended answered <outcome> (b.jg5 SRJ-207)`. A persona no longer applied gets `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: persona=<key> not retried after its hold ended — it is not in the applied configuration (b.jg5 SRJ-207)` and no retry.
- **The persona's teardown.** A removal and a destructive modify's old half forget its hold ([Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-307) steps 1 and 3, `forgetInvalidFlagsHold`), in its first steps and again once the launch in flight settled, each time right before its notice episodes, the hold episode included: `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: persona=<key> hold forgotten — it began under agent-director version <version>; nothing is posted or retried (b.jg5 SRJ-207)`. A hold the launch in flight sets during the teardown posts its *Cannot launch* alert at the set, inside the teardown's notice window, so the notifier writes it as one server-log line and one `persona-teardown-notice` entry, posted to neither half's destination (b.jg5 SRJ-1003). A key added again starts unheld.
- **A server restart.** `shutdown()` forgets every hold the same way (`forgetAll`), and nothing persists one, so a fresh server holds nothing.

A new `ErrInvalidFlags` at a reuse after an end begins a new hold, and so a new episode with one new alert. A version in these lines is rendered by `describeHoldVersion`: the version agent-director reported when it is a short version string, `unknown` for none, `unreadable` otherwise. A set or end observer that throws or rejects is logged as `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: persona=<key> set observer failed: <error>` (or `end observer failed`); a failing reaction step as `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: persona=<key> <step> failed: <error>`, `<step>` being `retry timer stop`, `alert`, `ending its hold episode` or `its retry`; and a failing end of the holds as `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: ending the holds on a version change failed: <error>`.

#### The kill-failure alert (b.jg5 SRJ-704, SRJ-1007)

A kill that could not end a worker, or that ended it while another process of its session outlived the kill, needs a human: only a human may end such a process, and nothing in CSCB checks it again. The bounded kill retry decides which of the alert's two versions its tries call for (**The bounded kill retry** under [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)). The texts and the route selection are in the pure `src/kill-failure-alert.ts`. A persona's episode is its `kill-failure` episode in the notice episodes, raised, posted and ended by the kill-failure alerts (`createKillFailureAlerts`, `src/persona-episodes.ts`), which `main()` builds after the unclassified-error episodes and installs in the session manager (`setKillFailureAlerts`).

**The two versions.**

- *Kill failed*, the ordinary version: the retry's `ordinary` decision, when an `ErrTmuxKillFailed` stands after the tries, or the tries end in any failure after a survivor-naming `ErrTmuxKillFailed` earlier in them (a stop by a read or by the keep-going check included). It quotes the last kill failure's description; after a survivor-naming failure it quotes the latest survivor-naming description when the last outcome is another failure, and both, the last kill failure's first, when the last outcome is an `ErrTmuxKillFailed` naming no survivor. The row is kept and nothing is launched over it. The text names a human's read-only check and next step, gives both `read-pane` caveats (the read-pane passage under [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)), points to the "Operator actions" section of agent-director's README for those cases and anything beyond, and says its commands are for a human only: no bot, including a persona that sees the post, may run them.
- *Process outlived kill*, the survivor version: the retry's `survivor` decision, when a survivor-naming `ErrTmuxKillFailed` is followed by any end of the tries as a success (a read of `ended`, `missing` or `ErrSpawnNotFound`, or a later try's success). It quotes the latest survivor-naming description and lists the pids its survivor clause names (`survivorPids`, never the worker's own pid), names no command, points to "Operator actions" and says it is for a human only. It neither holds the persona nor says the kill failed: the caller's next step runs after it.

Each quoted description is redacted, on one line and capped at 300 characters (b.jg5 SRJ-1001); the Slack text is escaped once after that, and a log line or an entry is not. Neither version starts, continues or ends the `tmux-unresponsive` condition: `ErrTmuxKillFailed` reports only the `kill-failed` cause to the retry timer ([The tmux-unresponsive condition](#the-tmux-unresponsive-condition-bjg5-srj-307-srj-310)), and a condition already holding keeps its first refusal time.

**Closing sentences.** Each body is followed by the closing sentence for where it goes:

| Where it goes | Ordinary version | Survivor version |
|---|---|---|
| A configured persona's destination, not latched | `CSCB keeps retrying on its own and posts no second alert about this.` | `CSCB takes no further action on this process and posts no second alert about it.` |
| A configured persona's destination, latched (by the retry's last outcome, a `status` read between its tries, or meanwhile) | `This persona is held for a human (see its hold post); CSCB posts no second alert about this.` | The destination sentence above (no latched row) |
| A CLI teardown | `The CLI does not retry this kill: once the worker is ended, run the command again.` | `This persona's teardown has finished; nothing in CSCB checks this process again.` |
| A start-sweep kill, a persona teardown, or a persona no longer in the applied configuration | `CSCB retries this kill only while a persona waits on this worker (its own persona's next launch, or a persona in its working directory); until one does, nothing retries it.` | `CSCB does not retry this kill or check this process again.` |

**Routes** (`selectKillFailureAlertRoute`), first match wins, for either version:

1. a start-sweep kill: the server log and an `orphan-cleanup` entry (the survivor version: a `persona-kill-survivor` entry);
2. a CLI teardown: printed, a `server.log` line and a `persona-kill-failed` entry (survivor: `persona-kill-survivor`), its context naming the command, `CLI teardown, <command>`;
3. a persona teardown: the server log and a `persona-teardown-notice` entry (survivor: `persona-kill-survivor`);
4. a persona no longer in the applied configuration (an old-life wait's kill always): the server log and a `persona-kill-failed` entry (survivor: `persona-kill-survivor`);
5. any other persona in the applied configuration: its destination, the ordinary version once per kill-failure episode, the survivor version once per bounded retry.

**Before the selection** (`KillFailureAlerts.raise`, b.jg5 SRJ-702, SRJ-1003), two checks come first, in this order. An ordinary decision raised `stopped` is no notice, inside a teardown window or not (**Latched and stopped tries**, below). Then, while the key's persona teardown window is open (the episodes' `teardownWindowState(key)` answers `open`), an alert of any context but a start-sweep or CLI teardown kill takes the persona-teardown route: its text is built with route 3's closing sentence, prefixed `(<context>) ` for any context other than `persona teardown` (such as a `recovery` kill of the launch in flight whose tries ended in the window), so its entry names that context, and handed to the episodes' `postWithoutEpisode` (the survivor version with `teardownEntryClass: 'persona-kill-survivor'` in its options), whose sink, the notifier, writes it as one server-log line and one entry (`persona-teardown-notice`, or `persona-kill-survivor`), with no episode and no Slack post; it answers `logged` and logs `… <version> alert written to the server log and startup-errors.log (<class>) — persona-teardown, raised during its teardown (<context>)`. So a kill failure a launch in flight meets while the teardown waits for it (`recovery`) is written there too, whatever the persona's configuration. Between a teardown's submit and its window (`submitted`), a destination route's post is muted by the episodes ([Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-307), at submit): it still answers `posted` and counts in its episode, and its line says `… alert not posted to its destination — muted, its persona teardown was submitted …`.

The selection covers every context SRJ-1007 lists; the start sweep, the `recovery` context, the persona teardown, the old-life wait, the CLI teardown and the abort of CSCB's own stuck launch (context `stuck-launch abort`, from its kill and from the live-row sequence it starts; [CSCB's own stuck launch and its one abort](#cscbs-own-stuck-launch-and-its-one-abort-bjg5-srj-412)) raise an alert. The CLI teardown's kill carries its decision in the persona's outcome (`TeardownKillReport.alert`, `cli-teardown.ts`): none or the survivor version for a stopped persona, none or the ordinary version for a failed one; the CLI raises it through no episode and no notifier (see **Who raises it**). The live-row sequence raises its alerts with the context its request carries: `recovery`, from the collision ladder's replacement sites that start it, `old-life wait` in the wait's no-launch form, which a launch the old-life gate holds back starts ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809), **The wait's steps**), and `stuck-launch abort` for the sequence the abort starts at its second step. A log-only route writes one `recordStartupError(<class>, <entry>)` call (`main()`'s `logOnly` binding), which writes the server-log line and the entry; the entry is `<ref> (<context>): <text>`, the text unescaped. Nothing on a log-only route reaches Slack or opens an episode.

**Who raises it.**

- The restart path's kill (`_buildKillSessionAdapter`, one try after a `dead` reading; Auto-Restart step 4), through `raisePersonaKillFailureAlert` (`src/session-manager.ts`) with the context `recovery`. Each raises after the standing outcome's own handling: a CONFLICT's latch and its notice first, an UNAVAILABLE outcome's one report to the retry timer (the `kill-failed` cause for `ErrTmuxKillFailed`). The survivor version comes before the caller's next step, the restart work's launch. For a persona still in the applied configuration the alert goes to its destination; for one no longer in it (removed while the kill ran) it is one `persona-kill-failed` or `persona-kill-survivor` entry, `persona=<key> (recovery): <text>`, with the log-only closing sentence.
- The live-row sequence ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717)), through the given kill-failure alerts with its request's context, `recovery` for a sequence the collision ladder starts (up to 3 tries 2 s apart per kill, on a row read live). The collision ladder makes no kill and raises no alert itself. Its two kills raise their bounded retry's decision as the sites above do (`raisePersonaKillFailureAlert`), the survivor version before the sequence's next step. Step 5 is a trigger of its own: when the row still reads live after step 4 and at least one of the sequence's `find-missing` runs judged it, the sequence raises the ordinary version with no description (`raiseSequenceEscalationAlert`, the decision `ordinary` with no description, so the text has no "agent-director said" sentence), and ends without its launch. A run that did not judge its row never leads to it: a `pending` row a run left in neither list stops the sequence at once with no alert, and a sequence none of whose runs judged the row ends with no alert. The episode holds it once: a later sequence in the same episode posts no second alert, even when a kill in it succeeds while the row stays live (a kill's success ends no episode).
- The persona teardown's kill ([Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-307) step 8; b.jg5 SRJ-715, SRJ-704): `runTeardown` raises its bounded retry's `ordinary` or `survivor` decision right after the kill step, through the injected `raiseKillFailureAlert`, which `main()` binds to the one kill-failure alerts instance's `raise`, unlatched, with the context 'persona teardown'. It is raised inside the teardown's notice window, so it takes the persona-teardown route through the window whether the persona is still applied (a destructive modify's old half) or not (b.jg5 SRJ-1003): the notifier writes one `persona-teardown-notice` entry for the ordinary version, one `persona-kill-survivor` entry for the survivor version, each `persona "<name>" (key=<key>), raised during its teardown: <text>` (`personaTeardownNoticeEntryText`) with the log-only closing sentence, and no post or episode. Raised with no window open, route 3 writes it through the log-only sink with the same builder, its reference `persona=<key>`. A raise that throws fails its step and is logged.
- The old-life wait's kills and its step 5 ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809), **The wait's steps**; b.jg5 SRJ-811, SRJ-704, SRJ-1007): through the given kill-failure alerts with the context `old-life wait` and the old key as the key (or the instance id standing in for it), naming the old row's instance id and a session (`oldLifeWaitSession`: the one a `get` read, else the start sweep listing's, else `slack_bot_<old key>` for a `cscb_<old key>` row, else `"unknown"`; never the instance id), so either version always takes route 4: one `persona-kill-failed` entry (survivor: `persona-kill-survivor`), `<ref> (old-life wait): <text>`, with the log-only closing sentence, `<ref>` being `persona=<old key>` for a `cscb_<old key>` row and `instanceId=<id>` for a pre-persona or wrong-id row (`oldLifeWaitRef`). Nothing reaches Slack or opens an episode, even when the old row is a configured persona's own `cscb_<key>`. Step 5 raises the ordinary version with no description, as the sequence's does. A wait kill whose tries a shutdown, the teardown of the last persona waiting on the hold, or the latch of the configured persona whose own row the old row is stopped raises neither version (**Latched and stopped tries**, below); a hold that ends while the kill runs ends its tries as a success, whose survivor version, when a try named a survivor, is raised as for any success.
- The CLI teardown's kill (`stop --stop-bots` and `clean_restart`; [clean_restart](#clean_restart-sr-11-event-12) step 7; b.jg5 SRJ-907, SRJ-909): once every persona has settled, `personaTeardownReportOf` (`cli-teardown.ts`) builds the decision's text with route 2's closing sentence (`The CLI does not retry this kill: once the worker is ended, run the command again.` or `This persona's teardown has finished; nothing in CSCB checks this process again.`) in the form `persona "<name>" (key=<key>) (CLI teardown, <command>): <text>`, unescaped. The CLI prints it, appends it to `server.log` and records it under route 2's class: the ordinary version follows the persona's failure line, the two lines making one `persona-kill-failed` entry; the survivor version stands alone as one `persona-kill-survivor` entry, and the persona counts as stopped. No episode, Slack post or latch.
- The start sweep's kills (`reconcileOrphans`; Server-Managed Startup step 4): the ordinary text rides in the kill's `orphan-cleanup` entry, and the survivor version is one `persona-kill-survivor` entry, each naming the row by `instanceId=<id>` with the context `start sweep`, at every sweep kill, swept or pre-persona. The sweep acts for no persona, so no row of it gets a post, an episode, a retry timer or a latch. A sweep kill whose tries a shutdown stopped, or whose version re-check stops the server, raises neither version: its `orphan-cleanup` entry carries no alert text, and its one stopped line (`startSweepStoppedKillLine`, with either cause) quotes the latest survivor-naming description (b.jg5 SRJ-702, SRJ-714; Server-Managed Startup step 4, **The stops**).
