**Latched and stopped tries.** The ordinary version at a destination ends with the latched closing sentence when the persona is latched as it is raised: by the retry's last outcome (a CONFLICT or an UNUSABLE NAME answer), by a `status` read between its tries, or by another path meanwhile. The latch's hold has stopped its retry timer, so none runs for it. An ordinary decision whose tries the keep-going check stopped while the persona is not latched (it is torn down or not up, or the server is shutting down), or whose last outcome's version re-check decided that the server stops, is raised `stopped`, with the last outcome's class (`lastOutcomeClass`: its failure class, or its outcome kind) and the stop's cause (`stopCause`), both given by `raisePersonaKillFailureAlert`. The cause is `the last outcome's version re-check stops the server` for a re-check's stop; for tries the live-row sequence's own stop ended, the sequence passes it (`liveRowStopCauseText`: `its live-row sequence was stopped: the persona's teardown began`, `… the server is shutting down`, `… the persona is not up` or `… the persona latched`); otherwise it is what the server's keep-going query tells right after the tries, `its keep-going check answered false: the server is shutting down` or `its keep-going check answered false: the persona is torn down or not up`, with the generic `PERSONA_KILL_STOP_CAUSE_GENERIC` (`its keep-going check answered false: the persona is torn down or not up, or the server is shutting down`) when no query is installed, it throws, or it tells neither (the caller's own keep-going check stopped the tries). A stopped retry is no notice (b.jg5 SRJ-702, SRJ-1003, SRJ-1013) and is decided before every route, the teardown window's included, whatever its alert decision: `ordinary`, or `none` (an `ErrTmuxUnresponsive` stop with no `ErrTmuxKillFailed` standing and no survivor-naming failure) recorded the same way; neither version is raised, nothing is posted and no episode is read or changed. For a configured persona the record is the line below only; for a persona no longer in the applied configuration it is that line and one `persona-kill-failed` entry carrying it, with no alert text (never a `persona-teardown-notice` entry). One line names the persona, the stop's cause, the last outcome's class, the redacted descriptions (the latest survivor-naming one included) and the context: `… ordinary alert not raised — its tries were stopped (<cause>)[; its last outcome's class: <class>], so nothing retries this kill; <descriptions> (<context>)`. An old-life wait's kill is stopped only by a shutdown, by the teardown of the last persona waiting on its hold, or by the latch of the configured persona whose own row the old row is; never by another persona's latch or a persona not being up. Each stop names its own cause (`oldLifeWaitStopCause`, mapping the sequence's `liveRowStopCauseText`), whatever the decision (an ordinary decision with no description when the tries decided none): `its old-life wait was stopped: the server is shutting down` (`OLD_LIFE_WAIT_STOP_CAUSE_SHUTDOWN`), `its old-life wait was stopped: the last persona waiting on its hold was torn down` (`OLD_LIFE_WAIT_STOP_CAUSE_TEARDOWN`; the teardown stop comes from `forgetOldLifeWaits`) or `its old-life wait was stopped: the persona whose own row it is latched` (`OLD_LIFE_WAIT_STOP_CAUSE_LATCHED`: the keep-going check's latch stop, or a between-try read that latched that persona, which the sequence passes as `its live-row sequence was stopped: the persona latched`); a cause it does not know, or none, renders the neutral `its old-life wait was stopped` (`OLD_LIFE_WAIT_STOP_CAUSE_UNKNOWN`), never the shutdown's. For a persona with no destination route (one no longer in the applied configuration, so a persona removed during the tries, and always an old-life wait's old key, whose entry names the wait's reference) that line's content is also written through the log-only sink as one `persona-kill-failed` entry, `<ref> (<context>): the kill-failure ordinary alert not raised — …` (`<ref>` `persona=<key>`, or the wait's `persona=<old key>` or `instanceId=<id>`), with no alert text, logged `… stopped retry's log line (no alert text) written to the server log and startup-errors.log (persona-kill-failed) — stopped`; never a `persona-teardown-notice` entry. A configured persona's stop writes the line only, and so does a stop raised with `lineOnly` (`KillFailureRaiseInput.lineOnly`): an old-life wait's kill on a configured persona's own row that this persona's latch stopped is that persona's stop, so it writes its one line, with `OLD_LIFE_WAIT_STOP_CAUSE_LATCHED`, and no `persona-kill-failed` entry; a shutdown or last-waiter-teardown stop of the same wait still writes the old key's entry. It answers `stopped`.

**The episode (b.jg5 SRJ-1016).** The ordinary version at a destination begins the persona's `kill-failure` episode and posts once in it; a later ordinary alert in the same episode posts nothing. It ends silently, with one ended line, when a read of the persona's own row reads `ended` or `missing`, or answers `ErrSpawnNotFound` (`endKillFailureEpisodeOnRead`): the shared own-row `get` (`readPersonaOwnRow`) and the own-row `status` step (`applyOwnRowStatusStep`), so the shared `status` read, the kill retry's read between tries and the liveness and reconnect adapters' step all end it. On the replacing path these are the collision ladder's `get` and the live-row sequence's `get`s and between-try `status` reads, so a row seen gone or finished there closes the episode, and a recovered persona no longer reports `kill failed`. A teardown's `forget` and shutdown's `close` drop it with no line. Nothing else ends it: not a kill that succeeds while the row stays live, and not `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`, which reads no row. The survivor version opens no episode, ends none and is not held back by an open one.

**After the alert.** After the ordinary version the persona is retried on its retry timer, which a condition end does not stop while the `kill-failed` cause is recorded (**Condition ends** under [Pending-only mode](#pending-only-mode-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305-srj-306)), unless it latched. A kill failure is never counted toward the restart cap. While the episode is open, a message lost for the persona reports `kill-failed` ([Inbound step 7](#inbound-slack--claude-code)). After the survivor version the caller's next step runs, and a later ordinary failure still posts its alert.

**Its lines.** Each is prefixed `[slack] persona-episodes: persona=<key> kill-failure`; with no alerts installed (unit tests) `raisePersonaKillFailureAlert` logs one line carrying the decision instead. Every line is listed in docs/engineering-guide.md, Log Messages.

#### The live-row sequence (b.jg5 SRJ-705, SRJ-717)

A persona's live row `cscb_<key>` (`pending` included) is never launched over and never deleted: it is replaced only by the live-row sequence, `runLiveRowSequence` in `src/live-row-sequence.ts`, run in the background through the dependencies the session manager's `buildLiveRowSequenceDeps` binds. Its production starters are the collision ladder's replacement sites (b.jg5 SRJ-707; Server-Managed Startup step 5, the replace step `replacePersonaRow`): a row the ladder cannot keep (`resume_enabled` false, a `cwd` that differs by real path, a `config_dir` label missing or different, at a resume or at a `pending` row, or a retired key's old life: a live row of a key recorded as retired with no "new life has begun" mark, b.jg5 SRJ-805, [Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-bjg5-srj-806-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-407)) that it last read live, `pending` and an unreadable state included. Each such request enters at step 1, seeded with the state the ladder last read, with the conversation not kept, the retired-key flag set for a retired key, a launch at the end and the alert context `recovery`, so its step 6 is a reuse spawn of the same id. The pending-row step's read-and-step entry (`readAndStepPendingRow`, b.jg5 SRJ-409, SRJ-411) starts the same request through `startRecoverySequence`, seeded `pending`, for a `pending` row that is not covered, from the restart path's `pending` deferral (a liveness probe, the re-probe, the reconnect adapter, a lost message's restart) and from a pending-only retry, with no approver lap or keystroke ([Covered and uncovered rows](#covered-and-uncovered-rows-bjg5-srj-409-srj-411)). The restart path's reconnect adapter starts the same request, with the retired-key flag, in place of its `/mcp reconnect` for a retired key with no mark whose row reads live other than `pending` (`replaceOwnRowOldLife`, `server.ts`; [Auto-Restart](#auto-restart)), and without the flag for a held own row of a key not recorded (b.jg5 SRJ-810). A dead-session path's earlier live read starts one there only when that path holds dead evidence ([Dead evidence](#dead-evidence-bjg5-srj-611); `replaceAtResumeSite`). The other starter is the ladder's not-resumable step (b.jg5 SRJ-710, SRJ-611; `spawnNotResumableAtLadder`): a `resume` that answered `ErrSpawnNotResumable` on a path holding dead evidence, whose re-read finds the row in a known live state other than `pending` (`AGENT_DIRECTOR_LIVE_STATES`), starts the same request seeded with the re-read state and with the conversation kept, so its step 6 is a `resume` when the row has a session id and the persona may resume it. `ErrSpawnNotResumable` by itself starts none: a `pending` re-read, a re-read in a state CSCB does not know (an unreadable one included), a path with no dead evidence and a finished or absent row start no sequence. The abort of CSCB's own stuck launch (b.jg5 SRJ-412; [CSCB's own stuck launch and its one abort](#cscbs-own-stuck-launch-and-its-one-abort-bjg5-srj-412)) starts one after its own checked kill succeeded (`startStuckLaunchAbortSequence`): entry at step 2, seeded `pending`, the conversation kept, ending in a launch, alert context `stuck-launch abort`, so its step 6 is a `resume` of the same session when the row has a session id and the persona may resume it. Either way the ladder answers `sequence-waiting` whatever the start entry answers, except `held`, which answers `held`. A starter passes a request: the instance id, the state it last read, the entry step, whether the persona keeps its conversation, whether its key is retired, whether the sequence ends in a launch, and the kill-failure alert's context.

**The steps, in order.**

1. **One kill**, checked, through the bounded retry (`retryPersonaKill`, site `live-row-sequence`), seeded with the state the starter last read. A success (any `kill_sent`, `ErrSpawnNotFound`, GONE, or a read between tries that found the row finished) goes on, after raising the retry's survivor decision if it has one. A non-success aborts the sequence by its class: a CONFLICT latches the persona through the latch's CONFLICT entry with the refused operation "P's next check or recovery" and the state last read, and is never sent again (SRJ-613's kill backstop: the step-1 kill of a `pending` row answering "not this launch's session" latches it); an UNUSABLE NAME latches it through the unusable-name entry; any other class ends the sequence. The retry's ordinary decision (`ErrTmuxKillFailed`, or any non-success after a survivor-naming failure in its tries) is raised after that handling. Tries the keep-going check stopped, and an `ErrInvalidFlags` whose version re-check stops the server, stop the sequence.
2. **One `get`.** A `pending` row is waited on until G past its launch start (below). A `pending` row with no launch start has no wait; a configured persona's own such row has latched the persona through the shared read (the launch-start decision, [Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)), which stops the sequence before any wait. A row read `ended`, `missing` or absent here still goes on to step 3.
3. **Up to `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_STEP3_RUNS` (3) bypassing `find-missing` runs**, the first at once and each later one `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_RUN_SPACING_MS` (5 s) after the previous run's `get`, each followed by one `get`. A `get` reading `ended`, `missing` or no row (`ErrSpawnNotFound`) goes to step 6.
4. **One more kill** as in step 1, seeded with the state step 3's last `get` read, then a `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_STEP4_PAUSE_MS` (5 s) pause, one more run and one more `get`, read as in step 3.
5. **The row still live after step 4.** When at least one run judged it, the kill-failure alert's ordinary version with no description ([The kill-failure alert](#the-kill-failure-alert-bjg5-srj-704-srj-1007)), and the sequence ends without its launch; when no run judged it, no alert, and it ends the same way.
6. **The launch**, for a request that ends in one (below). The no-launch form makes no launch and ends as "row finished".

A starter that made the first kill itself (the stuck-launch abort) enters at step 2 (`LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_ENTRY_GET`); every other starter enters at step 1 (`LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_ENTRY_KILL`). One sequence makes at most `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_MAX_RUNS` (`LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_STEP3_RUNS` + 1, 4) runs and `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_MAX_KILLS` (2) kills, each kill with its tries. Only step 3's and step 4's `get`s send the sequence to step 6.

**The wait (b.jg5 SRJ-406, SRJ-210).** The step-2 wait takes the raw launch start the step's `get` read and arms through `armPendingRowWait` (`src/pending-row.ts`, which arms `armNeverEarlyWait`) on the sequence's injected clock, passing the G accessor itself (`adGraceMsInEffect`), so G is read from the settings in effect at the arm and at every timer fire and a value raised while the wait is armed never ends it early; a G beyond the timer maximum is held by a chain of timers ([Module Map](#module-map), `ad-settings.ts`). A launch start that does not parse to a finite time is never armed: the step logs its no-wait line and goes on. A G accessor that throws or answers NaN while arming arms nothing and never ends the wait early: the step logs an arm-failed line (`liveRowSequenceWaitArmFailedLine`, the error's name and redacted message, no stack) and arms again after `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_GRACE_REARM_MS` (5 s) on the sequence's clock. The line is written at the wait's first failure, at a failure whose description differs from the last one logged, and otherwise at most once per `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_GRACE_REARM_LOG_SPACING_MS` (60 s) on that clock, per wait; with a clock whose `now()` throws, only the first and changed failures are logged. The re-arm is never skipped: it is tried until the arm succeeds or the sequence is stopped (the stop clears the re-arm timer); only the armed wait's own fire ends it. The armed line renders such a G as `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_GRACE_UNREADABLE_TEXT`, and `AD_WAIT_NEVER_ENDS` as `LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_GRACE_NEVER_ENDS_TEXT`. A launch start already older than G arms a wait that fires at once. The wait is measured from the launch start, not from the row's `started_at` ([Launch pending](#launch-pending-bjg5-srj-406-srj-408)).

**The runs and what "judged" means (b.jg5 SRJ-120, SRJ-717).** Each run is a bypassing run (`bypassingFindMissingSweep`, a new call whatever is memoized or in flight) with the persona's key as its next-step `get`, read for the instance id against the state the sequence last read (`readFindMissingRow`). A run judged the row when it put it in `ids` (marked `missing`) or in `unverified_ids` (judged and left live), or, for a row last read live other than `pending`, in neither list (judged alive). A run that puts a row last read `pending` in neither list did not judge it (the row is inside agent-director's grace period, or its launch's worker is alive): the sequence stops that episode at once, with no alert, no counted failure and no further kill, and arms the persona's retry timer with the not-judged cause. A refused run (`FIND_MISSING_REFUSED`: UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG or UNCLASSIFIED) ends the sequence at once without its launch, with the persona's retry timer armed and no further run, kill or launch; a run after which the persona is latched (`FIND_MISSING_LATCHED`) stops it; any other failed run judges nothing, and the step goes on (its `get` is still made).

**The reads (b.jg5 SRJ-114, SRJ-513).** Each `get` goes through the shared own-row read (`readPersonaOwnRow`), and each read between a kill's tries through the shared own-row `status` read. A `provenance_conflict` note on a `get` latches the persona and stops the sequence, as does an UNUSABLE NAME answer and a configured persona's own `pending` row with no launch start ([Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)). A `get` that fails otherwise, at step 2, 3 or 4, ends the sequence without its launch, with the persona's retry timer armed.

**What a step may do (b.jg5 SRJ-706, SRJ-316).** Before every agent-director call the sequence asks its stop signal (`createLiveRowSequenceStop`, set for the persona's latch, its teardown or shutdown; a kill's tries the server's keep-going query stopped because the persona is not up end the sequence stopped `not-up` without it) and the latched query, and makes no call when either holds; a wait or pause ends early once the signal is set. A result that arrives after a teardown or shutdown stop is dropped, with one line and no further call; a latch stop drops nothing: the answer is handled as for a latched persona (the sequence's own latching call included), and the sequence makes no call after it. Nor does a no-launch request's stop for its hold's end (`hold-ended`, the old-life wait, b.jg5 SRJ-811): the answer is acted on (a kill's tries that the hold's end ended go on to their success, whose survivor version is raised), and the wait makes no call after it. For a dropping stop, in full:

- a `get`, run or launch that answers after the stop is logged after the step's own line (a `get` or run line, or step 6's launch-kind line) with `the step <n> get` / `step <n> run` / `step 6 launch` `answered after the sequence was stopped — its answer is dropped; no further call`, and the sequence ends stopped;
- a kill that answers after the stop (any answer but tries the keep-going check stopped) logs its kill line, then the same line for `step <n> kill`, and the sequence ends stopped: no latch, no kill-failure alert, no retry arm. Tries the keep-going check stopped go on to the retry's log-only alert decision for a stop, which posts nothing;
- a stop set while a kill's CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME latch call runs logs the same line for `step <n> kill's latch`, and the sequence ends stopped without the ordinary kill-failure alert (the latch's own post has gone out);
- a dependency that throws after the stop logs `a step failed: <redacted failure> — the sequence ends without its launch`, then the same line for `failed step`, and the sequence ends stopped;
- a sequence whose stop signal is set arms no retry timer, whatever its last step answered.

A teardown that stops the sequence waits for the call in flight to return (the registry's `stop` resolves once the sequence settled), so the teardown's later stops of the persona's retry timer clear an arm that call made from inside its own handling (an ENVIRONMENT or CONFIG answer to a kill already in flight).

The kill retry itself asks the sequence's keep-going check once more after its tries and makes no deferred report when it answers false (**Only the outcome that stands is reported** under [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)). No kill is made, at step 1 or step 4, of a row the sequence last read `pending` while the persona's `ad-config-malformed` outage is raised: the sequence ends there without its launch. Every kill's tries are seeded with the state last read and go on only while the sequence is neither stopped nor the persona latched. In the no-launch form a kill's CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME latches nothing.

**The launch (step 6).** `decideLiveRowLaunchKind` answers `resume` only when the request keeps the persona's conversation, the key is not retired, a row was read and carries a non-empty session id, the persona is in the applied configuration with `resume_enabled` true, and the row's `cwd` and `config_dir` label match the persona (`compareRowToPersona`; a `cwd` check that cannot be made now counts as a match, and a `config_dir` that cannot be resolved gives no mismatch). Otherwise it answers a reuse spawn of the same id, with the first reason that holds, in this order: the key is retired, the persona does not keep its conversation, there is no row, the row has no session id, the persona is not in the applied configuration, `resume_enabled` is false, the row's `cwd` differs, the row's `config_dir` label is missing or differs. A persona no longer in the applied configuration is not launched at all (`not-applied`), with no call. Otherwise the launch goes through the session manager's sequence-launch entry, `launchForLiveRowSequence`, a launch call registered in the in-flight launch map:

- it waits for a launch already in flight for the persona to settle, or for the sequence's stop signal, whichever comes first; once the signal is set it makes no call and is not launched (`stopped`), with one line. It is the sequence's own launch, exempt from the `sequence-waiting` gate below;

- the `resume` leg logs `[slack] live-row-sequence: resuming <ref> (b.jg5 SRJ-705)` after the trust patch, and its outcomes are SRJ-113's through the one `resume` handler the collision ladder uses too (`resumeAtSite`; Server-Managed Startup step 5, `resume`'s outcomes), with the head `[slack] live-row-sequence:`; a success logs `[slack] live-row-sequence: resumed <ref>`. A `resume` whose answer is `ErrNoSessionId`, `ErrJsonlMissing` or `ErrJsonlNeverWritten` (by class) goes on to the no-transcript step (`noTranscriptReuse`, shared with the collision ladder), logging `[slack] live-row-sequence: <failure> on resume for <ref> — going on to a reuse spawn of the same id; nothing is deleted (b.jg5 SRJ-705, SRJ-707)`: after `ErrJsonlMissing` the lost-transcript diagnosis runs first (its `get` before the reuse; a latched or refused read ends the launch with no reuse, `latched` or `failed`, which the launch answers as `retrying` when the timer was armed), then the reuse once, and a launched outcome after `ErrJsonlMissing` carries the amnesia action (`fresh-after-amnesia` or `fresh-after-inconclusive-amnesia`), `spawned` after the other two. The sequence's launch is no start-pass launch, whichever path started the sequence (it runs detached, after its starter's `sequence-waiting` was counted, so every call passes the start flag false, the `resume` a recovery holding dead evidence ends in included), so the diagnosis writes no startup-errors entry; its line and, on success, its notice are as at the ladder. A `resume` answering `ErrSpawnNotFound` makes one plain spawn of the same id (`buildSpawnParams`, no reuse flag; agent-director's pre-spawn scan runs inside it, b.jg5 SRJ-111), logging `[slack] live-row-sequence: ErrSpawnNotFound on resume for <ref> — fresh-spawn: one plain spawn of the same id, which makes agent-director's pre-spawn scan; no spawn-failure notice for the ErrSpawnNotFound (b.jg5 SRJ-113, SRJ-111)`, with no spawn-failure notice for the `ErrSpawnNotFound` itself; that spawn takes the plain spawn's table through its one handler ([Plain spawn](#plain-spawn-bjg5-srj-111)). Its collision (`ErrInstanceIdCollision`: the row turned live) runs no get-then-act inside the sequence, which would be a second launch path for the persona while its sequence runs: it logs `[slack] live-row-sequence: the fresh spawn after ErrSpawnNotFound on resume of <ref> collided with a live row — nothing launched, no spawn-failure notice, nothing counted; the sequence ends without its launch, and the retry it arms runs get-then-act (b.jg5 SRJ-111, SRJ-705, SRJ-713)` and is not launched (`spawn-collision`): no further launch, nothing counted, and the end arms `collision`, whose retry's ladder makes the get-then-act. A `resume` answering `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` is a counted launch failure that also arms the persona's retry timer at once in pending-only mode (`armPendingOnlyAfterLaunchFailure`), and a DIRECTORY failure of the `resume` or of that plain spawn is a counted launch failure. Any other non-success ends by class (`resumeFailedAt`: a CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME latches the persona with the state last read; `ErrInvalidFlags` gets its version re-check, then UNCLASSIFIED) with no further call;
- **`ErrSpawnNotResumable` at step 6 (b.jg5 SRJ-710, SRJ-706; `sequenceNotResumable`)** never starts a second sequence. The step reads the row once more through the shared own-row read (`notResumableStep` with the sequence barred, what `get after ErrSpawnNotResumable`), logs one line, `[slack] live-row-sequence: <failure> on resume for <ref> — re-read: <re-read> — <outcome> (b.jg5 SRJ-710, SRJ-706)` (no evidence part: the sequence carries none), and the launch is not made, nothing counted:
  - the read latched the persona: `not-resumable-latched`, outcome `the persona is latched: no second sequence; the sequence stops with nothing armed`; the sequence ends stopped for the latch;
  - `pending`: `not-resumable-pending`, outcome `a launch in progress: no second sequence and no further call; the sequence ends without its launch, nothing counted or posted`; the end arms `sequence-ended-without-launch`;
  - any other state (a known live one, a state CSCB does not know or an unreadable one), no row, or a refused read (the shared read's own error rows applying): `not-resumable`, a lost race, outcome `a lost race: no second sequence and no further call; the sequence ends without its launch (cause=spawn-not-resumable-lost-race unless the persona is latched), nothing counted`; the end arms `spawn-not-resumable-lost-race`.

  The `resume` leg never deletes and never kills;
- the reuse is the session manager's reuse spawn (`reuseSpawnForPersona`, [Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)), given the state the sequence last read; after a `resume` that went on to it, the trust patch is not run again. A reuse that collides with a live row (`ErrInstanceIdCollision`), of either kind or after the `resume` leg, makes no further launch, counts nothing and is not launched (`reuse-collision`), with one line; the sequence ends without its launch;
- a success runs the after-launch step (the `pre_trust` line and the dialog approver). Any other result (`failed`, `deferred`, `latched`), or a launch that throws, ends the sequence without its launch, with no further call;
- the entry counts its launch's result once (`recordLaunchResultOutsideRestartWork`, `restart.ts`), by class: a success resets the persona's failure count; a `failed` result not marked stopping whose class is LAUNCH FAILURE (`ErrTmuxSessionCreate`) or DIRECTORY (`ErrCwdNotFound`, `ErrCwdNotADirectory`), from the `resume` or the reuse, is one counted launch failure, with the cap notice at the cap. Those results carry `countedClass` (`SpawnPersonaResult`), set where the class is handled, and the entry counts a failure only when it is set (`sequenceLaunchCounted`). Any other `failed` result and a retrying, stopping, latched, held, deferred or not-launched answer record nothing. A launch that joins the entry's launch gets every failure not marked stopping, and every not-launched answer, as `retrying` (b.jg5 SRJ-1015), so the failure is counted at most once, by the entry.

**What each end arms (b.jg5 SRJ-301).** A successful launch, a row finished in the no-launch form, every stop (latch, teardown, shutdown, not up), an abort that latched the persona, a launch that latched it or whose result says the server is stopping, and any end while the persona is latched arm nothing. The not-judged stop arms `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_SEQUENCE_NOT_JUDGED`. Every other end without the launch arms `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_SEQUENCE_ENDED`: step 5 with or without its alert, a refused `get` or run, the `ad-config-malformed` no-kill end, an abort that latched nothing, a launch not made other than a reuse collision, a plain spawn's collision (`spawn-collision`) or a lost race (`not-resumable`), and a launch that failed (`deferred` and a counted directory error included) or threw, whether or not the launch's own refusal handling armed the timer first. A reuse collision, and a collision of the plain spawn after the step-6 `resume`'s `ErrSpawnNotFound` (`spawn-collision`), arm `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_COLLISION` (`collision`), and a step-6 `resume`'s `ErrSpawnNotResumable` whose re-read found a lost race (`not-resumable`) arms `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_LOST_RACE` (`spawn-not-resumable-lost-race`), each unless the persona is latched; one whose re-read found the row `pending` (`not-resumable-pending`) arms `sequence-ended-without-launch`, and one whose re-read latched the persona arms nothing. A final launch whose `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` armed the timer at once in pending-only mode (`pendingOnlyArmed`) arms nothing more: the timer's read of the row decides, and the end line says `the retry timer armed by the launch (pending-only)`. A final launch call that succeeded (`LIVE_ROW_LAUNCH_CALL_SUCCESS_ACTIONS`) arms nothing from the sequence either: its after-launch step arms the persona's timer pending-only with the `pending-row` cause (b.jg5 SRJ-301, SRJ-409), and the end line says `no cause armed by the sequence; the launch's success arms the pending-only watch (pending-row)`. Any other end that arms nothing says `no retry timer armed` (`liveRowSequenceEndArmText`). In the old-life wait's form the dependencies' arm does nothing, so no end arms a timer for the old key (b.jg5 SRJ-1512); the wait's end handler arms the waiting personas instead ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809), **The wait's steps**). The sequence itself counts no failure toward `RESTART_FAILURE_CAP`; its final launch is counted by the sequence-launch entry (above).

**Scheduling (b.jg5 SRJ-706, SRJ-811).** Sequences run in the server's one registry (`createLiveRowSequenceRegistry`), which `main()` builds over `buildLiveRowSequenceDeps` and installs in the session manager (`setLiveRowSequenceRegistry`) before the start pass. A starter reaches it only through the session manager's start entry, `startLiveRowSequence(request)`, which the collision ladder's replace step and its not-resumable step call, the restart path's reconnect adapter for a retired key's old life, and the abort of CSCB's own stuck launch. While the installed retired-key store has the request's key recorded, marked or not (`retiredKeyReadingOf`), the start entry forwards the request with its retired-key flag set whatever the starter passed (`retiredKeyRequest`, with one line when the starter had not set it), so no sequence for such a key ends in a `resume` (b.jg5 SRJ-805).

- **In the background.** The start entry starts a sequence without awaiting it and answers at once: `started` (the sequence's first agent-director call comes after the answer), `already-running` or `closed`, and `not-installed` when no registry is installed. A refused start logs one line and starts nothing. The start pass, an apply and another persona never wait for a sequence.
- **One per instance id and per persona.** Entries are keyed by instance id and record the key and whether the request ends in a launch; a start is refused (`already-running`) while a sequence runs on that instance id, or, for a request that ends in a launch, while another such request runs for that persona. A no-launch request (the old-life wait, keyed by its old key or the instance id standing in) is refused only by its instance id: one wait runs per held id, several personas waiting on one hold never collide, a wait on another id never refuses a persona's own sequence, and a wait and a sequence never run at once on one id (b.jg5 SRJ-811). An entry is removed when its sequence settles, whatever its outcome, so a later start begins a new sequence. A sequence is one episode's replacement of the row: it ends when it launches, aborts by class, stops on a run that did not judge its row, or escalates (step 5); a later retry or tick may begin a new one.
- **Its own attempt.** Each sequence that ends in a launch runs as a recovery attempt for the persona of its own (`runDetachedRecoveryAttempt`), detached from its starter's attempt: an error it meets arms by the attempt rule there and never marks the starter's launch refused. A no-launch request runs outside every attempt (the registry's `runOutsideAttempt`, production `runOutsideAttempts`), so nothing it meets arms a timer for its old key (b.jg5 SRJ-811, SRJ-1512).
- **Every other launch for P waits.** While a sequence runs for P (`isLiveRowSequenceRunning`: from the start's answer until it settles, its step-6 launch included), every other launch path for P makes no agent-director call and reports `sequence-waiting`. `spawnForPersona` asks right after its held gate, before the in-flight join (so it joins no launch, the sequence's step-6 launch included), and a latched P goes on to the latched answer instead; `launchSession` maps the answer to the uncounted `'refused'`, and the start pass counts it neither as failed nor as succeeded. The restart work asks right after its first latched gate (`RESTART_OUTCOME_SEQUENCE_WAITING`), for a fired restart timer, a retry and a human-triggered restart; at a retry it is a refusal that re-arms the timer. The running sequence also blocks a retry and is in flight for P ([Health-Check Poller](#health-check-poller)), and a message lost meanwhile reports `restarting` ([Inbound](#inbound-slack--claude-code) step 7). When what runs on P's own `cscb_<key>` is an old-life wait, which launches no one, the refusal also arms P's retry timer with the `held-for-old-life` cause, with one line (`oldLifeWaitRefusalLine`), at `spawnForPersona` (whose `sequence-waiting` result carries `sequenceWaitingCause: 'old-life-hold'`), at the restart work's gate (`liveRowSequenceGate`) and at the start entry when a request that ends in a launch is refused for a wait on its id (b.jg5 SRJ-811).
- **Its stops.** `stop(key, reason)` stops only a sequence that ends in a launch; a no-launch request is stopped by instance id (`stopNoLaunch(instanceId, reason)`: its hold's end, reason `hold-ended`, through the hold set's end observer) and by `close()`, never by a latch or a persona's stop. `stop` sets the sequence's stop signal at once, logs `stop asked — <reason>; no further call`, and resolves once the sequence has settled, its call in flight returned and its end line logged. P's latch stops it (`stopSequenceOnLatch`, reason `latched`; [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)), P's teardown right after the approver stop (reason `teardown`; [Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-307)), and shutdown through the registry's `close()` (reason `shutdown`, after which every start answers `closed`; [Graceful Shutdown](#graceful-shutdown-sr-11-event-11)). After any of them the sequence makes no further call and leaves no timer pending.

**Its lines.** Every line starts `[slack] live-row-sequence:`: one start line, one line per kill, `get`, run and wait (a failed `get` reads `failed: class=<class> name=<reportedName> message="…"`, as a kill line reports a failure, when the classification carries a reported name or a message, else agent-director's error name and message), step 6's launch-kind line, and one end line naming the outcome, the counts and the cause armed; the registry adds a not-started line for a refused start and a stop-asked line per stop. Its calls' own lines carry the site `live-row-sequence`. Every line is listed in docs/engineering-guide.md, Log Messages.

#### Plain spawn (b.jg5 SRJ-111)

A plain spawn launches a persona's own instance id `cscb_<key>` with `buildSpawnParams`'s params unchanged: no reuse flag and no `no_pre_trust` (Server-Managed Startup step 5, the spawn params). agent-director first scans the tmux socket it resolves for a leftover of that id, inside the spawn, and writes nothing when that pre-spawn scan refuses (HO rev 15). Every plain spawn goes through one exported handler, `plainSpawnOutcomeAt(site)` in `src/session-manager.ts`, so the same answer ends in the same action whichever site made it. Its sites:

- `runPersonaLadder`'s first spawn (`<what>` `spawn`; nothing read before it, so a latch makes one latch-time `status` read);
- the ladder's retry spawn after the collision `get` answered `ErrSpawnNotFound` (`retry-spawn`; last read: no row);
- the plain spawn after `resume` answered `ErrSpawnNotFound`, at both `resume` sites, through `plainSpawnAfterResumeNotFound`: `resumeOrFreshSpawn` and the live-row sequence's step-6 `resume` leg (`fresh spawn after ErrSpawnNotFound on resume`; last read: the state the path read before the `resume`). The sequence's leg marks a DIRECTORY failure `countedClass`, since its entry counts only a marked failure.
- the latch re-check's plain spawn (`latch re-check's plain spawn`; last read: the state the re-check last read): a plain-spawn latch's retry with no row, and the finished-row retry's plain first spawn when no row is left ([The re-check](#the-re-check-bjg5-srj-505)). Its collision row is the re-check's own (`latchRecheckCollided`): no information, P stays latched, nothing more is called. It marks a DIRECTORY failure `countedClass`, and the re-check counts the result itself (`countLaunchOutsideRestartWork`). Inside the re-check a success or a definite failure clears the latch first (`clearLatchBeforeOutcome`).

A new plain-spawn site uses the same handler. The handler runs the reply-guard steps immediately before the call, makes the one spawn through `launchCallWithWindow` (which records the call's window, [A launch's window and the read after a timeout](#a-launchs-window-and-the-read-after-a-timeout-bjg5-srj-407)), and decides the outcome by class through `src/ad-error-class.ts`, never by an error's name. It makes one launch call and never a second one after a refusal; nothing in it deletes, kills or sets agent-director's finished-row option. Failures other than a collision go to the private `plainSpawnFailedAt`.

| Outcome | What follows |
|---|---|
| Success | The site's line (`spawned <ref> instanceId=…`, `retry-spawn succeeded for …`, or `fresh-spawned (after ErrSpawnNotFound on resume) for …`), then the after-launch step (`afterLaunchSucceeded`: the `pre_trust` line, the pending-only `pending-row` arm and the dialog approver on P's `pending` row; Server-Managed Startup step 5, Pre-session dialog approval); `spawned` |
| `ErrInstanceIdCollision` (by class) | Nothing was launched, so the reply-guard steps are undone, and the site's collision row answers; never a spawn-failure notice or a `spawn-failed` entry, nothing counted. The first spawn's collision is get-then-act's first run (`ErrInstanceIdCollision for <ref> — fetching current state`). A collision of the retry spawn or of `resumeOrFreshSpawn`'s plain spawn re-runs get-then-act once (`plainSpawnCollisionAtLadder`); a plain spawn's collision in that re-run makes no further call, arms P's retry timer with `collision` (`reportReuseCollisionAtSite`) and answers `retrying`. At the live-row sequence's leg the sequence ends without its launch (`spawn-collision`) and arms `collision`, and that retry's ladder makes the get-then-act ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717)) |
| CONFLICT from the pre-spawn scan ("left over from an earlier life", or "conflicting labels" at server, global or global-window scope) | P latches with the case its description gives, the refused operation `plain-spawn` and the row state last read ([Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)); `latched`. Nothing is counted and nothing is killed, and the latch's CONFLICT post is P's only post: no spawn-failure notice, no `spawn-failed` entry. agent-director wrote nothing, so no row exists afterwards and nothing is left to wait out (b.jg5 SRJ-713) |
| CONFLICT after "duplicate session" (a holder the scan did not count: "no valid instance id", "a different instance id", "another agent-director store", "conflicting labels", or "left over from an earlier life") | The same latch, nothing counted or killed. agent-director has ended the new row, so it reads `ended` afterwards, and no hook revives it: a hook applies only from the row's own launched worker. Only an end write that was not applied leaves it otherwise: `pending` after a store error, a covered row waited out through [the pending-row rule](#the-pending-row-rule-bjg5-srj-410) like the LAUNCH FAILURE row's below, or as another agent-director write left it. CSCB does not tell this CONFLICT from the scan's by its words; the row each leaves is the difference |
| A launch timeout, either form | UNAVAILABLE: a refusal, then the one `get` and its decision ([A launch's window and the read after a timeout](#a-launchs-window-and-the-read-after-a-timeout-bjg5-srj-407)); a covered `pending` row gets the approver |
| Every other UNAVAILABLE outcome | A refusal, then the one `get`, and the row is handled as the row it is. A pre-spawn scan whose lookup could not answer wrote nothing: the `get` finds no row and the retry the outcome armed launches P again (HO rev 15). "duplicate session" whose holder could not be read, or whose name more than one session matches, keeps its row as the `get` reads it. A re-lookup after "duplicate session" that could not answer (HO rev 26, below) has ended the new row |
| ENVIRONMENT (`ErrTmuxNotAvailable`) | A refusal: the wrapper raised `tmux-unavailable` and armed the timer with `environment`; no `get`, never counted, no kill, no further launch. When the session-creating call met it the row stays `pending`, a covered row, which gets no stuck-launch post while the persona's `tmux-unavailable` outage is raised ([The pending-row rule](#the-pending-row-rule-bjg5-srj-410), step 3); when the re-lookup after "duplicate session" met it the new row was ended (HO rev 26, below); when the pre-spawn scan met it no row exists |
| LAUNCH FAILURE (`ErrTmuxSessionCreate`) | One counted launch failure: the line ending `— a counted launch failure; nothing is killed and no spawn is made in its place (b.jg5 SRJ-602)`, a `spawn-failed` entry during the start pass, the spawn-failure notice, and P's retry timer armed at once in pending-only mode (`launchFailureResult`). Never a kill. The row it leaves (`pending` after a failure other than "duplicate session", a covered row; `ended` after a "duplicate session" whose holder had vanished, `pending` when that end write was not applied) is decided by the retry's read. A `pending` row is never CSCB's own launch: the failed call's window has no end (`launchCallWithWindow`), so no own-launch record is set. The retries wait it out through [the pending-row rule](#the-pending-row-rule-bjg5-srj-410): nothing before G, a bypassing `find-missing` run from G, the one held post at B and never the relaunching post or the abort, never a kill; once agent-director marks it `missing`, P is brought up (b.jg5 SRJ-713, SRJ-111). The only plain-spawn outcome that posts the spawn-failure notice |
| DIRECTORY (`ErrCwdNotFound`, `ErrCwdNotADirectory`) | `failed`; the wrapper raised `cwd-unreachable`. Counted by the restart path, and by the live-row sequence's entry through `countedClass` |
| `ErrInvalidFlags` | Exactly one immediate version re-check (the `ErrInvalidFlags` step, [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)), then UNCLASSIFIED: a `stop` answers `failed` marked `stopping`; any other answer arms `unclassified`, feeds the unclassified-error episode and answers `retrying`. No further launch, no hold (only the reuse spawn holds), no notice |
| UNUSABLE NAME | P latches with the case `unusable-recorded-name` and the refused operation `none`; `latched` |
| CONFIG (`ErrConfigMalformed`) | A refusal: `ad-config-malformed` raised, the timer armed with `config`; `retrying` |
| UNCLASSIFIED, and any STATE or GONE name the plain spawn gives no meaning | The UNCLASSIFIED refusal (`reportUnclassifiedAtSite` with the `spawn` verb): the timer armed with `unclassified`, the episode fed, one refusal line; `retrying`, no notice |

**The ended new row of HO rev 26.** A plain spawn whose session-creating call met "duplicate session" and whose re-lookup of the holder could not answer has ended its new row, and returns `ErrTmuxUnresponsive` (UNAVAILABLE) or `ErrTmuxNotAvailable` (ENVIRONMENT) whose description says "the new row was ended" (`NEW_ROW_ENDED_PHRASE`) and names a retry with `reuse_finished` once the name is free. CSCB keys nothing on those words: the class decides. After the UNAVAILABLE form the one `get` reads `ended` (`LAUNCH_UNAVAILABLE_OUTCOME_FINISHED`): P is not latched, nothing is counted, and the launch answers `retrying`. The ENVIRONMENT form takes no `get` (its refusal row above). Either way P's next attempt recovers the row as any `ended` row with no session id, with no new code: the ladder's plain first spawn collides with the row, the collision `get` reads `ended`, the `resume` answers `ErrNoSessionId`, and the no-transcript step makes one reuse spawn with `reuse_finished: true` ([Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)); with `resume_enabled` false, or for a retired key, the reuse comes straight after the `get`. No plain spawn follows the collision, and no site plain-spawns over a row. When the end write was not applied the `get` reads `pending`, a covered row, armed pending-only with no launch (`LAUNCH_UNAVAILABLE_OUTCOME_COVERED_NO_APPROVER`).

No collision reaches the spawn-failure notice (b.jg5 SRJ-713): a plain spawn's goes to its site's collision row, a reuse spawn's to its collided answer ([Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)), and a `resume`'s to `resumeCollisionAt` (Server-Managed Startup step 5, the `resume` outcomes). `remediationHint` has no collision branch, and no post calls a collision a fault. The handler's lines are listed in docs/engineering-guide.md, Log Messages.

#### Reuse spawn (b.jg5 SRJ-112, SRJ-708)

The reuse spawn brings a persona up fresh on its own instance id `cscb_<key>` and keeps its row, when it has one, as an earlier life: agent-director's `spawn` of the same id with the reuse flag. It is one launch, `reuseSpawnForPersona(persona, config, { isStartup, lastRead, trustPatchRan?, firstLaunch? })` in `src/session-manager.ts`, which every reuse site calls. Its callers are the live-row sequence's final launch ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717), step 6), the collision ladder's replace step for a finished row (`replacePersonaRow` through `reuseFinishedRow`; Server-Managed Startup step 5), a retired key's first launch (`retiredKeyFirstLaunch`, with `firstLaunch` and nothing read) and its reuse in place of a `resume` (`retiredKeyAtResumeSite`, through `reuseFinishedRow`; [Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-bjg5-srj-806-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-407)), the no-transcript step (`noTranscriptReuse`) after a `resume` that answered `ErrNoSessionId`, `ErrJsonlMissing` or `ErrJsonlNeverWritten`, at the collision ladder (Server-Managed Startup step 5), at the sequence-launch entry's `resume` leg and at the latch re-check's `resume`, and the latch re-check's retries (a reuse latch's retry, a plain-spawn latch's retry on a finished row, a finished-row retry, and a retired key's retry in place of a `resume` or a plain spawn; [The re-check](#the-re-check-bjg5-srj-505)), whose collided answer gives no information there. It runs inside its caller's launch or recovery attempt and opens none of its own; its caller registers the launch in flight and counts its result.

**Its parameters (b.jg5 SRJ-708).** `buildSpawnParams`'s params with only `reuse_finished: true` added (the client's `SpawnParams`): the same template, `cwd`, labels and `extra_env` as any launch of the persona, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION=false` included (Server-Managed Startup step 5, the spawn params). No `no_pre_trust` is set. The client emits the flag as `--reuse-finished`.

**Before and after the call.** First the launch path's `claude_config_dir` check: a directory that does not resolve goes to the deferral hook, and the answer is `deferred`, with no agent-director call. Then the pre-launch trust patch, once per launch attempt (not again when the caller ran it in this attempt, `trustPatchRan`: a `resume` that went on to the reuse), and the call made as `launchWithReplyGuard` makes it: the reply-guard steps immediately before it, then spawn detection, which reports an error by class (Server-Managed Startup step 5, the trust-patch and reply-guard bullets). The reuse runs the reply-guard steps itself, so that with `firstLaunch` (a retired key's first launch, b.jg5 SRJ-805) an `ErrInstanceIdCollision` undoes them, as the plain first spawn's collision does. A success logs one line, by the state the caller last read: with no row (`lastRead` `LATCH_ROW_STATE_NO_ROW`) the reuse is an ordinary fresh spawn and keeps no earlier life, `[slack] reuseSpawnForPersona: reuse-spawned <ref> instanceId=cscb_<key> — a new life on its own id; the id had no row when last read (an ordinary fresh spawn), so no earlier life is kept (b.jg5 SRJ-112)`; with nothing read (a retired key's first launch) `… — a new life on its own id; nothing of its row was read before it (a retired key's first launch), so any finished row is kept as an earlier life (b.jg5 SRJ-112)`, and for a forced launch through its test seam (`forcedWhat` given) the parenthesis names it instead: `(the forced reuse spawn, made through its test seam)` or, for the reuse after the forced `resume`'s no-transcript answer, `(the forced resume, made through its test seam)`; otherwise `[slack] reuseSpawnForPersona: reuse-spawned <ref> instanceId=cscb_<key> — a new life on its own id; its row is kept as an earlier life (b.jg5 SRJ-112)`. It takes the installed retired-key store's reading of the key when its launch attempt started, recorded or not, and, for a recorded key, its record generation (`recordGeneration`), from its caller (`retiredAtStart`: the collision ladder's, or the live-row sequence's request's), or reads it just before the call when the caller gave none. For a key recorded both then and at success, with its record generation unchanged, it then sets the key's "new life has begun" mark through the store's `mark` unless the mark is already set, with one line; a key recorded while the launch attempt was in flight gets no mark and answers `spawned`, with one line (`reuseSuccessAction`, b.jg5 SRJ-806 as amended by b.deo SRI-407; [Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-bjg5-srj-806-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-407)). Then it runs the after-launch step (`afterLaunchSucceeded` with `LAUNCH_VERB_REUSE_SPAWN`): the `pre_trust` line naming `reuse spawn`, then the dialog approver on the persona's row (Server-Managed Startup step 5, the pre-trust and pre-session dialog approval bullets). It answers `fresh-retired` (`SPAWN_ACTION_FRESH_RETIRED`) when it set the mark or found it set, and `spawned` for any other key.

**Its outcomes (b.jg5 SRJ-112).** `reuseSpawnFailedAt` decides each failure by class through `src/ad-error-class.ts`, with the refused operation "reuse spawn" and the caller's `lastRead` as a latch's recorded row state. A refusal logs `[slack] reuseSpawnForPersona: reuse spawn refused for <ref>: <failure> — no spawn-failure notice; nothing more is called (b.jg5 SRJ-105)` and answers `failed`, which the launch answers as `retrying` because its error armed the retry timer; a latch logs the CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME line with the same prefix ([Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)). The reuse counts nothing itself: it marks a LAUNCH FAILURE or DIRECTORY failure `countedClass`, and its caller counts a `failed` result that is not marked stopping and carries that mark as one launch failure, and nothing else.

| Outcome | What follows |
|---|---|
| Success | A new life on the id; for a key recorded before the call and at success with its record generation unchanged, the mark set; the `pre_trust` line and the approver on the persona's row; `fresh-retired` for that key, `spawned` for any other (a key recorded while the call was in flight included), which its caller records as a success |
| `ErrInstanceIdCollision` (the row is live, a launch in progress included) | `[slack] reuseSpawnForPersona: <failure> on the reuse spawn of <ref> — its row is live, so nothing was launched; no spawn-failure notice, nothing counted (b.jg5 SRJ-112)`, and the collided answer (`REUSE_SPAWN_COLLIDED`, `reuse-collided`), which is no launch result: no notice, no entry, nothing counted, nothing armed by the reuse. At the live-row sequence's final launch it is not launched (`reuse-collision`): no further launch, and the sequence ends without its launch, arming the persona's retry timer with `collision` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_COLLISION`). At a collision ladder reuse site (the replace step's or the no-transcript step's) the first collision re-runs the ladder's get-then-act once; a retired key's first-launch reuse is the attempt's first reuse collision too, so the get-then-act it goes on to is that one re-run (`run.reuseCollisionRerun`); a second ends the attempt with `retrying` (b.jg5 SRJ-1015), nothing posted or counted, and arms the same cause (`reportReuseCollisionAtSite`) |
| UNAVAILABLE, every form (`ErrCallTimeout` included) | A refusal, never counted, no notice. The reporting point has armed the retry timer with `unavailable` and started or continued the `tmux-unresponsive` condition, whose onset posts only at a later check, never at the refusal ([Its three posts](#its-three-posts-bjg5-srj-308-srj-309-srj-1006)). Nothing is assumed of the row: one `get` follows, whose row decides with no launch in the attempt, and the launch answers `retrying`, `latched` or the sequence's start result ([A launch's window and the read after a timeout](#a-launchs-window-and-the-read-after-a-timeout-bjg5-srj-407)). After a launch timeout, a covered `pending` row gets the approver, and one whose launch start lies inside the call's window is this launch's: for a recorded key the mark is set and the key's old-life hold ends there, and the launch still answers `retrying` |
| CONFLICT (`ErrTmuxSessionConflict`) | The persona latches (`conflictAt`) with the refused operation `reuse-spawn`, the case its description gives ("another agent-director store" and "conflicting labels" included) and the caller's `lastRead`; `latched`. Never a kill and never another launch |
| UNUSABLE NAME | The persona latches (`unusableNameAt`) with the case `unusable-recorded-name` and the refused operation `none`; `latched`, nothing counted |
| ENVIRONMENT (`ErrTmuxNotAvailable`) | A refusal: the wrapper raised `tmux-unavailable` and armed the timer with `environment`; never counted |
| CONFIG (`ErrConfigMalformed`) | A refusal: the wrapper raised `ad-config-malformed` and armed the timer with `config`; never counted |
| UNCLASSIFIED (an `ErrInternal` other than an unusable recorded name included) | A refusal: the timer armed with `unclassified` and the outcome reported to the persona's unclassified-error episode; never counted |
| `ErrInvalidFlags` | One immediate version re-check (the `ErrInvalidFlags` step, [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)). A re-check that stops the server answers `failed` marked `stopping`, with `[slack] reuseSpawnForPersona: reuse spawn failed for <ref>: <classification> (after one immediate agent-director version re-check: stop); no other launch`, nothing posted or counted. After any other answer (`pass`, `could-not-run`, `not-running`) the persona is held on `ErrInvalidFlags` ([The `ErrInvalidFlags` hold](#the-errinvalidflags-hold-bjg5-srj-207-srj-1008)): `[slack] reuseSpawnForPersona: reuse spawn of <ref> answered <failure> (after one immediate agent-director version re-check: <answer>) — the persona is held under agent-director version <version>; answering held: no other launch, no delete, no spawn-failure notice, nothing counted (b.jg5 SRJ-112, SRJ-207)` (`reuseInvalidFlagsHeldLine`), and `held`: nothing reported to the unclassified-error episode and nothing armed. Never another launch, a delete or a tmux-touching call |
| LAUNCH FAILURE (`ErrTmuxSessionCreate`) | A counted launch failure: `[slack] reuseSpawnForPersona: reuse spawn failed for <ref>: <failure> — a counted launch failure; nothing is killed and no spawn is made in its place (b.jg5 SRJ-112, SRJ-602)`, the spawn-failure notice, a `spawn-failed` entry (`reuse spawn failed for <ref>: <failure>`) only during the start pass, and `failed`. Whatever row the reuse was made over, the persona's retry timer is also armed at once in pending-only mode (`armPendingOnlyAfterLaunchFailure`; the result's `pendingOnlyArmed`), so the retry's read of the row decides what the failure left. Never a kill |
| DIRECTORY (`ErrCwdNotFound`, `ErrCwdNotADirectory`) | `failed`, counted; the wrapper raised `cwd-unreachable` |
| Any other name (GONE, a STATE name other than `ErrInstanceIdCollision`) | The UNCLASSIFIED row through `reportUnclassifiedAtSite`, with the refusal line |

**A reuse of an id with no row.** It is an ordinary fresh spawn: agent-director makes its pre-spawn scan, and its outcomes are the table's. A scan refusal (a CONFLICT) latches the persona with the refused operation "reuse spawn" and the recorded state "no row", and agent-director writes no row. Its `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` is counted, never followed by a kill, and arms the retry timer at once in pending-only mode, as above.

Nothing in the reuse spawn deletes or kills or makes a second launch. It reads the row after its answer only after an UNAVAILABLE outcome, with the one `get` of SRJ-407. Its lines are listed in docs/engineering-guide.md, Log Messages.

#### Launching a retired key (b.jg5 SRJ-805; b.jg5 SRJ-806 as amended by b.deo SRI-407)

A key the retired-key record holds ([retired-keys.json](#retired-keysjson-state_dirretired-keysjson)) is never resumed: its next launch starts a new life on the same instance id, and the old conversation stays in the row as an earlier life. The session manager reads the record through the one installed store (`setRetiredKeyStore`; production: `main()`'s store, installed before the start sweep) with `retiredKeyReadingOf(key)`, which answers `{ recorded, marked }`. With no store installed no key is recorded, and every launch path launches as before (b.jg5 SRJ-711). A recorded query that throws reads not recorded; a mark query that throws reads not marked, so a live row is taken as the old life; each logs one line.

**Every launch path.** The apply bring-up, the start pass, the restart path's relaunch, the lost-message trigger (through the restart path), the bring-up retries and the UNAVAILABLE retry timer's full-mode rerun all launch through the collision ladder (`spawnForPersona`, Server-Managed Startup step 5), so each applies the same rule. While the key is recorded, marked or not, the ladder makes no plain spawn and no `resume` for it:

- **First launch.** One reuse spawn of `cscb_<key>` in place of the plain first spawn (`retiredKeyFirstLaunch`, [Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)). With no row it is an ordinary fresh spawn, which makes agent-director's pre-spawn scan; on a finished row it resets the row to a new life. A collision (the row is live, `pending` included) undoes the reply-guard steps, as the plain first spawn's collision does, logs `[slack] spawnForPersona: the retired key's reuse spawn of <ref> collided — fetching current state; this is the one get-then-act a reuse collision gives (b.jg5 SRJ-805, SRJ-112)` and goes on to the collision `get`. That collision is the attempt's one reuse collision (b.jg5 SRJ-112), so the get-then-act is its one re-run: a reuse spawn there that collides too re-runs nothing, arms the persona's retry timer with `collision` and answers `retrying` (`reuseFinishedRow`).
- **The collision `get` decides** (`retiredKeyAtCollision`, after the `cwd` guard), with no further read: a finished row or no row gets the replace step's reuse (`replacePersonaRow`); a live row (`pending` and a state CSCB does not know included) with no mark is the old life, and the replace step starts the live-row sequence with the retired-key flag, the conversation not kept and alert context `recovery`, answering `sequence-waiting` (`held` for a persona held on `ErrInvalidFlags`) ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717)); a live row with the mark set is the new life and takes the ladder's live branches as any live row, never replaced by this rule.
- **No `resume` anywhere.** `resumeOrFreshSpawn`, reached from the ladder's finished branch, the dead-session routes from `waiting` and `working`, and the prompt-row recovery's finished re-read (`launchOnPromptRow`, b.jg5 SRJ-607), makes one reuse spawn of the same id first, whatever row the path last read, after the find-missing run and the unresolvable-directory deferral (`retiredKeyAtResumeSite`). The record is read again after that run's await, so a key recorded during it is never resumed; the reading taken before the run decides only the `resume_enabled` false step. A finished row or no row gets its new life, and a live row makes it collide, and the re-run of get-then-act decides as above. Nothing is deleted or killed there.
- **The live-row sequence.** Its start entry (`startLiveRowSequence`) sets the retired-key flag whatever the starter passed, so the sequence's step-6 launch is a reuse spawn, never a `resume`. Step 6 takes the flag from the request or from a fresh read of the store (P's facts, `retired`), so a key recorded while the sequence ran ends in a reuse spawn too. When the starter gave no `retiredAtStart`, the start entry forwards the store's reading of the key with its record generation (`retiredKeyAttemptStartOf`) as the attempt's start, which step 6 hands its reuse unchanged.
- **The reconnect adapter.** A recorded key with no mark whose row reads live other than `pending` is not reconnected: the adapter starts the live-row sequence with the flag and answers `'transient'` ([Auto-Restart](#auto-restart) step 3, **A retired key's old life**). A `pending` reading keeps the `pending` deferral. The `working` and `waiting` branches read the pane, which is awaited, so the adapter asks the store again right before typing `/mcp reconnect`: a key recorded meanwhile gets the same live-row sequence, with nothing typed.

**The new-life mark.** A reuse spawn compares against the store's reading of the key when its launch attempt started (`RetiredKeyAttemptStart`: recorded, marked and record generation, `retiredKeyAttemptStartOf`): the collision ladder's, taken once at its launch decision and kept for the run (`LadderRun.retiredAtStart`), which every reuse the ladder makes and every live-row sequence it starts carries; a live-row sequence's, taken when it was requested and carried to step 6 (the request's `retiredAtStart`); or, for a reuse with no attempt context, one taken just before its call. A reuse spawn that succeeds for a key recorded both when its launch attempt started and at its success, with the key's record generation (`RetiredKeyStore.recordGeneration`) the same at both reads, sets the key's "new life has begun" mark through the store's `mark`, the mark's only writer, unless it is already set, logs one line, ends the old-life hold on `cscb_<key>`, if any, with the reason `new-life`, whatever the mark's write did ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809)), and answers `fresh-retired` (`SPAWN_ACTION_FRESH_RETIRED`, `reuseSuccessAction`); a key that is not recorded answers `spawned` with nothing written. A key recorded while the launch attempt was in flight (not recorded when the attempt started, recorded again during it, or with a record generation that could not be read, so a recording during the attempt cannot be ruled out) answers `spawned` with no mark set and one line, `[slack] reuseSpawnForPersona: <ref>'s key was recorded as retired while this reuse spawn's launch attempt was in flight (<how>) — the launch was decided before that recording, so its life is the old life: no mark is set; answering spawned (b.jg5 SRJ-806, SRJ-805)`: the launch was decided before that recording, so the life it began is the one being retired, and the key's next launch decides on the record as it then stands (for a destructive modify applied during the attempt, the modify's bring-up then begins the new life, sets the mark and answers `fresh-retired`). The generation shows a re-record that writes nothing (an unmarked key recorded again), which the record itself cannot; a generation query that throws logs `[slack] retired-keys: the record-generation query for <ref> failed: <err>; a recording during the launch attempt cannot be ruled out, so no mark is set (b.jg5 SRJ-806)`. Every reuse site gets the mark this way: the first launch, the replace step, the reuse in place of a `resume`, the no-transcript step and the live-row sequence's final launch. `fresh-retired` is a success wherever `spawned` is: `launchSession` maps it to `true`, the live-row sequence's launch counts it a success (`LIVE_ROW_LAUNCH_SUCCESS_ACTIONS`), the after-launch step starts the dialog approver, and the start pass counts it in `succeeded` and under `fresh as retired keys`, never as a fresh spawn (the start summary, Server-Managed Startup step 5). The mark is durable and survives a restart, so a server that starts over a marked entry reads the key's live row as its new life; its first launch is still a reuse, never a plain spawn or a `resume`, until the entry clears.

**A reuse that timed out but launched (b.jg5 SRJ-407; b.jg5 SRJ-806 as amended by b.deo SRI-407).** The mark's second trigger: a reuse spawn that ended in a launch timeout and whose one `get` read the row `pending` with a launch start inside the call's window (this launch's row; [A launch's window and the read after a timeout](#a-launchs-window-and-the-read-after-a-timeout-bjg5-srj-407)) began the key's new life. The step runs the same mark step as a success (`setNewLifeMarkForReuse`, through `markNewLifeAfterTimedOutReuse`), against the attempt's start the reuse carried, before the cover decision: for a key recorded then and still, with its record generation unchanged, it sets the mark unless already set (a failed write held in memory, below), logs `timedOutReuseNewLifeLine` and ends the key's old-life hold with the reason `new-life`, the read named `OLD_LIFE_NEW_LIFE_AFTER_TIMEOUT_READ`; a key recorded during the attempt gets `timedOutReuseRecordedInFlightLine` and no mark, so its row is the old life and goes through the live-row sequence. The marked row is then covered and gets the approver. The launch answers `retrying`, never `fresh-retired`. A `pending` row whose launch start lies outside the window is the old life and is never marked: an unmarked recorded key's row there goes through the sequence (AC 35). The mark survives a restart like any other, and the entry clears at the first read of the new life live other than `pending` (**The clear**, below).

**A failed mark write.** The store holds a mark whose write failed in memory and reads it as set (its own one line), so this server treats the live row as the new life. Each later launch decision for a recorded, marked key calls `mark` again (`retiredLaunchReadingOf`), which writes a held mark and writes nothing for a mark already in the file; a `mark` that throws there logs one line, and the key still reads marked. A restart loses a held mark.

**The clear.** Once the mark is set, the first read of the key's own row in `waiting`, `working`, `ask_user` or `check_permission` clears its entry (**The retired-key entry clear** under [Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)), and from then on the key launches as any other.

**No stored choice carries over (b.jg5 SRJ-806 as amended by b.deo SRI-407; b.deo SRI-406, SRI-409).** The new life starts with none of the old life's stored choices: a confirmed apply's step 1 dropped them when it retired the key, and the stored-choice start rules drop them at any start where the record holds the key without its new-life mark ([channel-delivery.json](#channel-deliveryjson-state_dirchannel-deliveryjson)). A retired key's choices never apply again, so in fungible mode the new life serves each channel at `mentions` until its own agent stores a choice. The mark and its clear write nothing to the stored-choice file.

#### The old-life hold (b.jg5 SRJ-809)

An old life that may still be running holds its working directory from the moment CSCB stops owning it until agent-director shows it finished. The holds live in `src/retired-keys.ts` (`createOldLifeHoldSet`): one set per server, in memory only, which `main()` builds right after the retired-key store, hands to the reload controller (`oldLifeHolds`) and installs in the session manager (`setOldLifeHolds`) before the start sweep (Server-Managed Startup step 2). A hold is keyed by the old row's instance id and carries the old key, the held directory, its cause, the kill-failed mark and the personas recorded as waiting on it. Directories are compared by real path at query time, by the lexical path when the real path cannot be resolved. The set never reads `retired-keys.json`: whether a key is recorded without its mark is asked of the store by the hold's starters ([retired-keys.json](#retired-keysjson-state_dirretired-keysjson)).

While a directory is held, MCP admission refuses a session from it, nothing types `/mcp reconnect` into the old life, and no persona whose working directory it is is launched until the hold ends; each persona held back is retried at once when it ends (**What a hold refuses**, below). A lost message reads the hold's kill-failed mark ([Inbound](#inbound-slack--claude-code) step 7), and the wait's steps (below), which a held-back launch starts, kill and run `find-missing` on the old row to end it.

**Starts.** Each begin logs one began line ([Old-life hold lines](#old-life-hold-lines-bjg5-srj-809)):

| Cause | Where | Instance id and old key | Directory |
|---|---|---|---|
| `apply-step-1` | A confirmed apply's step 1, once the last-applied rewrite has succeeded, before the state swap and any teardown (`oldLifeHoldsToBegin`; [The apply pipeline](#the-apply-pipeline-sr-86-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-805)). A failed retired-key write or a failed rewrite begins none | `cscb_<key>` and the key, for each removed persona (a rename's old key included) and each destructive modify | The old declaration's working directory |
| `start-sweep-kill-not-succeeded` | A start-sweep kill whose record is `SWEEP_ROW_KILL_FAILED`: an absent persona's row, a live pre-persona row, a row swept for its instance id or for its `cwd` (Server-Managed Startup step 4.5). A row the listing already holds keeps its one hold | The row's id; the old key is `oldLifeKeyOf`: the `persona` label's key when the id is that key's `cscb_<key>`, else the id | The row's `cwd` |
| `start-sweep-listing` | The start sweep, after its recording and before its first kill: every row listed live (`pending` included) whose key is recorded without the "new life has begun" mark, whether the sweep then kills it, keeps it or spares it for a latch (step 4.4a). The listing's reads of its rows follow these begins, so each hold's first wait is seeded with the state its row was listed in | As above | The row's `cwd` |

A begin on an instance id already held keeps that one hold on its held directory: only the cause becomes the new one; its directory, old key, kill-failed mark and waiting personas stay, and the begin's declared directory is ignored. It logs one began-again line naming the kept directory, as `oldLifeHoldBeganLine(hold, true)` builds it:

```
[slack] old-life hold: began again on "<real path>" for oldKey=<key> (instanceId="<id>"): <cause> — one hold is kept, on its held directory (b.jg5 SRJ-809)
```

Why: the held directory may come from the row's real `cwd` (a start-sweep hold, or a re-point), and the row's real `cwd` wins over a declaration (b.jg5 SRJ-809). No hold begins once the start sweep has stopped. Only a re-point moves a held directory: a later `get` or `list` row of the held id read live with another `cwd` replaces it, with no line; a `status` read carries no `cwd`.

**Who waits.** A persona waits on a hold whose directory is its working directory by real path, and on the hold on its own `cscb_<key>` (`holdsWaitedOnBy`, `waitsOnKillFailed`). The set keeps a record of the personas a hold held back (`recordWaiting`, written by the hold step, `oldLifeHoldStep`, and, for a hold on the persona's own `cscb_<key>`, by `recordOwnRowWaiting` at a launch refused because a wait runs on that row and at the reconnect's held-row guard; `forgetWaiting`, by the teardown's `forgetOldLifeWaits`), which the end line names and the end-retry observer retries. The wait's steps compute the waiting personas from the applied configuration by the rule above (`oldLifeWaitingPersonas`), so a persona that waits but has not been held back yet is armed too.

**Ends.** A hold ends only on these, each with one end line naming what ended it and, for a read, the read (`<site>: <what>`):

- **A read of the old row as `ended` (`read-ended`) or `missing`, or no row (`read-missing`, `ErrSpawnNotFound` by class).** Every read the session manager makes of a row goes through one entry, `noteOldLifeRowRead`: the shared `get` (`readPersonaOwnRow`), the shared own-row `status` step (`applyOwnRowStatusStep`, so every kill retry's between-try read and the liveness and reconnect adapters), the persona teardown kill's and the start-sweep kill's between-try reads, the old-life wait's own `get`s and between-try reads, and every row of the start sweep's `list`. A live read also seeds the next wait's request on that id. Any other state, `pending` and a state CSCB does not know included, keeps the hold. The permission poller's and the JSONL safeguard's reads are not entries (SRJ-122).
- **A listing in a completed `find-missing` run's `ids` (`find-missing-ids`)**, whoever started the run; a memoized result reused ends nothing new.
- **The key's new life (`new-life`).** A recorded key's reuse that answers `fresh-retired` ends the hold on `cscb_<key>`, also when the mark's write failed ([Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-bjg5-srj-806-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-407)), with the read name `OLD_LIFE_NEW_LIFE_READ`. So does a recorded key's reuse that timed out but launched, once its one `get` read this launch's row and the mark was set, with the read name `OLD_LIFE_NEW_LIFE_AFTER_TIMEOUT_READ` (`spawnForPersona: get after the reuse spawn's launch timeout read this launch's row`; b.jg5 SRJ-407). Either way the end observer retries a persona waiting on the hold at once. A launch in a held directory makes no call (it answers `sequence-waiting`), so no launch timeout can happen there.

A read that settles after its caller stopped (`OwnRowReadSite.actGoes`, the start sweep's `sweepStopped`) ends nothing. **No kill outcome ends a hold** (AC 54, AC 63): not a success with `kill_sent: false`, because on a `pending` row a kill made before the launch created its session finds nothing and does not stop the launch (HO §2); not a CONFLICT, which says nothing about the process; and not any other success, `kill_sent: true` and `ErrSpawnNotFound` at the kill included. A successful teardown kill leaves the hold to the next read of the old row; a successful sweep kill leaves it to the post-kill `find-missing` run or a later read.

**The kill-failed mark (b.jg5 SRJ-812).** A persona teardown kill (`killPersonaInstanceForTeardown`), a start-sweep kill or an old-life wait's kill whose tries decided the ordinary kill-failure alert, with no stop ending them, marks its hold kill-failed (`markOldLifeHoldKillFailed`; the wait's end handler through the hold set's mark), and so does the wait's step 5 with the row still live. A success, the survivor version and a stopped kill do not, nor does a CONFLICT or an UNUSABLE NAME with no survivor-naming failure before it; after one, a CONFLICT or an UNUSABLE NAME gives the ordinary kill-failure alert and marks the hold. The mark lasts until the hold ends. A message lost for a persona waiting on a marked hold reports `kill-failed` ([Inbound](#inbound-slack--claude-code) step 7).

**The wait's steps (b.jg5 SRJ-811, SRJ-812, SRJ-1512).** To end a hold, the session manager runs the live-row sequence's kill and `find-missing` steps (steps 1 to 5 of [The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717)) on the held row's instance id, with no launch, in the background. Its one entry is `ensureOldLifeWait(instanceId)`, which the hold step calls for each hold that holds a launch back unless a wait already runs on that id (**What a hold refuses**). It reads the hold (`holdOf`) and starts the sequence's no-launch form in the server's one registry: the request is keyed by the hold's old key (or the instance id standing in for it), with the wait's reference (`oldLifeWaitRef`: `persona=<old key>` for a `cscb_<old key>` row, `instanceId=<id>` otherwise, b.jg5 SRJ-1007), seeded with the state the last read of the row gave (a start sweep's listing included, whose reads follow its holds' begins, so a row listed `pending` seeds `pending` and SRJ-316's no-kill rule applies while `ad-config-malformed` is raised; `live-unread`, `OLD_LIFE_WAIT_SEED_LIVE_UNREAD`, when none was read), entry at step 1, no conversation kept, no launch and alert context `old-life wait`. It passes the wait's own dependencies and its end handler. It answers the registry's `started`, `already-running` or `closed`; `not-held` when no hold is on the id; or `not-installed` when no registry or no wait bindings (`setOldLifeWaitBindings`, `main()`) are installed. The last two log one line each (`oldLifeWaitNotStartedLine`).

- **Never at once with a sequence on one id.** The registry refuses a no-launch request only by its instance id, so one wait runs per held id and several personas waiting on one hold never collide. A wait and a live-row sequence never run at once on one id: while either runs there, the other's start answers `already-running`. A launch of P while a wait runs on P's own `cscb_<key>` answers `sequence-waiting` with P's retry timer armed (`held-for-old-life`) and P recorded as waiting on that hold (`recordOwnRowWaiting`; not a key the installed configuration shows outside the applied set), and `launchSession` maps it to the uncounted `'refused'` ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717), **Scheduling**).
- **Outside every attempt, under the old key.** The registry runs the wait through `runOutsideAttempts`, so nothing it meets is a launch or recovery attempt's (b.jg5 SRJ-1512). Every call it makes is the old key's. Its kill tries, between-try `status` reads, plain `get`s and runs go through the outage wrapper with `armsNothing`, so they arm no retry timer, start no `tmux-unresponsive` condition and report to no unclassified-error episode for the old key (the wait's own episode, keyed by the held instance id, is reported to by its end handler); under the old key they raise an ENVIRONMENT or CONFIG outage only when the old row is a configured persona's own `cscb_<key>`. The `get`s of such a row are the shared own-row read, with that read's own wrapper call.
