- **Its dependencies (`buildOldLifeWaitDeps`).**
  - Its `get`s: for a configured persona's own row (`cscb_<key>` of a key the configured-persona query counts), the shared own-row read, so SRJ-114's and SRJ-513's row rules apply, with an UNUSABLE NAME answer routed per SRJ-1002 (`… UNUSABLE NAME met in the old-life wait: routed to the server log; nothing latches …`). For any other id, one plain `get` that applies no row rule. Every answer reaches the read entry `noteOldLifeRowRead` (`old-life-wait: get`), so a read of `ended`, `missing` or no row ends the hold.
  - Its runs: the bypassing entry, as above.
  - Each kill: the checked kill of the instance id inside the bounded retry, with the `ErrInvalidFlags` re-check. Its between-try `status` read is the shared own-row step for a configured persona's own row, its UNUSABLE NAME answer latching nothing; otherwise it is a plain read given to the read entry (`old-life-wait: status read between kill tries`). The tries' keep-going check is the sequence's stop, which also asks the latch query below, so a shutdown (the registry's `close`), the last waiting persona's teardown (reason `teardown`, through `forgetOldLifeWaits`) or the latch of a configured persona whose own row the old row is stops them. A waiting persona's latch on another id, or a persona not being up, never stops them, and the kill keeps its 3 tries (AC 64). A between-try read of a configured persona's own row that latches that persona (SRJ-114, SRJ-513) ends the tries as latched, a failure end whose ordinary alert stands. Its hold-end query (`holdEnded`, option A) ends the tries as the `hold-ended` success when the hold has ended, or when the sequence was stopped for the hold's end even though a hold has been begun again on the same id since (`stoppedForHoldEnd`): after a wait between tries (before the keep-going check, so the hold's end wins over a stop in the same window), after a read that did not find the row finished, or when a try's UNAVAILABLE outcome would stand, the last try included. That success makes no further `kill` or `status` read, writes no `persona-kill-failed` entry, and raises the survivor version when a try named a survivor.
  - The launch start: the sequence's own reader (`src/pending-row.ts`). The wait has no G wait of its own: its G wait is the sequence's step 2 ([Launch pending](#launch-pending-bjg5-srj-406-srj-408)). A `pending` row with no launch start under a key no configured persona uses gets no wait for G and latches nothing, and its kill and run follow at once (b.jg5 SRJ-408).
  - Its alerts: the kill-failure alerts with the context `old-life wait` ([The kill-failure alert](#the-kill-failure-alert-bjg5-srj-704-srj-1007), **Who raises it**), naming the old row's instance id and a session (`oldLifeWaitSession`), the first that applies: the `tmux_session_name` a `get` of the row read this round; the one the start sweep's listing gave when it began or kept the hold (`noteOldLifeHoldSession`, dropped at the hold's end); `slack_bot_<key>` for a `cscb_<key>` row; otherwise none, which the alert text renders as `"unknown"`. An instance id standing in for the old key is never named as a session.
  - Its latch query (`isLatched`, SRJ-502, SRJ-408, SRJ-513; AC 46): for a configured persona's own row, that persona's latch, so while it is latched the wait makes no kill and no call on the row; for any other id, never. Nothing latches through the wait's own answers (`latchOnKillOutcome` latches no one, so a kill's CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME holds nobody); only the shared own-row reads latch, as they do anywhere.
  - No launch, and no retry arm for the old key.
- **What a round met.** The dependencies record every CONFLICT and UNUSABLE NAME answer (at a kill try, a read between tries, a `get` or a run), the first UNCLASSIFIED answer and the last kill's result, classifying through `src/ad-error-class.ts`. An ENVIRONMENT answer raises `tmux-unavailable`, and a CONFIG answer `ad-config-malformed`, for each persona waiting on the hold, at the call. Each call of the wait that succeeds (a kill try, a between-try read, a `get`, a completed run) clears `ad-config-malformed` for each waiting persona that has it raised (`clearOldLifeWaitConfigOutage`, through `clearOutageFlag`, as a persona's own successful call does). `tmux-unavailable` is deliberately not cleared there: its clear reaches the retry controller's condition-end entry (`conditionEnded`), which would stop the held persona's retry timer and drop the `held-for-old-life` arm the wait relies on. It lasts until that persona's own calls clear it after the hold ends.

**Its results by class.** When the round settles, the end handler applies `decideOldLifeWaitEnd` (`src/old-life-wait.ts`), first match wins:

| End | The hold | Mark | Waiting personas' timers |
|---|---|---|---|
| The hold ended while the kill's tries ran, the wait was stopped for the hold's end, the row read finished (the no-launch form's end), or no hold is left at the end | Over | No | Not armed |
| Stopped by a shutdown, or by the last waiter's teardown | Nothing more | No | Not armed |
| A configured persona's own old row is latched: a read of it latched the persona (a `get`, or a between-try read that ends the kill's tries), or the persona was latched already, so no call was made | Goes on | Yes when the kill decided the ordinary alert and no stop ended its tries | Armed, except the latched persona (and, as in every row, a held or not-up one; **Arming**) |
| The kill decided the ordinary kill-failure alert with no stop | Goes on | Yes | Armed |
| Step 5: the row stayed live after runs that judged it (the ordinary version with no description) | Goes on | Yes | Armed |
| A CONFLICT or an UNUSABLE NAME answer | Goes on | No | Armed |
| A run did not judge the `pending` old row, or no run judged it (SRJ-717: no alert) | Goes on | No | Armed |
| UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG (or no kill of a row last read `pending` while `ad-config-malformed` is raised for the old key or a waiting persona) or UNCLASSIFIED | Goes on | No | Armed |
| A `get` or a run that failed otherwise, or a dependency's failure | Goes on | No | Armed |

- **Arming.** The waiting personas are armed through the retry controller with `held-for-old-life` (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_OLD_LIFE_HOLD`), never counted. They are the applied personas whose working directory is the held directory or whose own `cscb_<key>` is the held row (`oldLifeWaitingPersonas`, the hold set's `holdsWaitedOnBy` over the applied configuration). A key the applied configuration does not have is never armed (`armOldLifeWaiter`), and neither is a latched persona, a persona held on `ErrInvalidFlags` (`heldGateReadingOf`; a held query that throws counts as held) or a persona not up (`personaUpNow`, the keep-going query's `isPersonaUp`; one that throws counts as not up, and with no query installed every persona counts as up). b.jg5 SRJ-305: the timer stays stopped while P is latched, held or not up, and a persona not up is its bring-up's. Each skip logs one line: `[slack] old-life-wait: persona=<key>: latched — no retry timer armed (b.jg5 SRJ-305, SRJ-502)` (`oldLifeWaitLatchedLine`), `[slack] old-life-wait: persona=<key>: held on ErrInvalidFlags — no retry timer armed (b.jg5 SRJ-305, SRJ-207)` (`oldLifeWaitHeldLine`) or `[slack] old-life-wait: persona=<key>: not up — no retry timer armed; its bring-up owns it (b.jg5 SRJ-305)` (`oldLifeWaitNotUpLine`). So a round a configured persona's own-row latch ended arms only the waiting personas that are not latched, held or not up.
- **Entries.** Except after a stop, whose answers are dropped, each CONFLICT and UNUSABLE NAME answer the round met is one `persona-teardown-notice` entry, `<ref>, raised during its old-life wait: <notice>` (`PERSONA_TEARDOWN_NOTICE_DURING_WAIT`, `oldLifeWaitRefusalNoticeText`), latching no one (SRJ-1002, SRJ-1013). A round that keeps the hold reports its first UNCLASSIFIED answer to the wait's unclassified-error episode on the held instance id (`OldLifeWaitBindings.unclassifiedErrorEpisodes`, SRJ-313; `createOldLifeWaitUnclassifiedErrors`): the round that begins the episode writes nothing, the first round met longer than the alert threshold after it writes the episode's one `persona-unclassified-error` entry, `<ref>: <the unclassified-error alert's text>` (`oldLifeWaitUnclassifiedEntryText`, always the log-only route), and later rounds write none. Only the hold's end (`onOldLifeHoldEnd`, `UNCLASSIFIED_ERROR_END_HOLD_ENDED`) and shutdown's close end the episode; no retry stop, latch, cap or teardown does. With no episodes bound, the answer is not reported and one line is logged (`oldLifeWaitUnclassifiedNotReportedLine`). The entries are written through the startup-errors recorder, which writes the server-log line too. A kill failure and step 5 write the old key's `persona-kill-failed` entry, and a survivor its `persona-kill-survivor` entry, through the kill-failure alerts. The survivor version never marks the hold.
- **What never ends the hold.** A kill that succeeds with `kill_sent: false` goes on to the runs and ends nothing by itself, and neither does a CONFLICT (SRJ-809).
- **The end line.** The round ends with one line naming what ended it, the hold, the mark and the personas armed (`oldLifeWaitEndLine`; [Old-life wait lines](#old-life-wait-lines-bjg5-srj-811)).
- **What reaches Slack.** Nothing about the old instance is posted: its alerts and entries are log-only. Two things reach Slack through the waiting personas' own notices: the *tmux unavailable* and *agent-director refuses its config file* onsets of the outages an ENVIRONMENT or CONFIG answer raised for them, and, when the old row is a configured persona's own row, a shared own-row read that latches that persona, with its *Held:* post.

**What stops the wait.** The hold's end: the hold set's end observer (`onOldLifeHoldEnd`, registered by `setOldLifeHolds`) ends the wait's unclassified-error episode on that id and stops that id's wait through the registry's `stopNoLaunch` (reason `hold-ended`), never a sequence that ends in a launch. A configured persona's latch on its own old row stops the wait before its next call (see the table). That stop drops no answer, and the wait makes no further call. A persona teardown forgets the key's waits (`forgetOldLifeWaits`, the lifecycle's `forgetOldLifeWaits` member) and stops a hold's wait (`stopNoLaunch`, reason `teardown`) only when no persona left in the applied configuration waits on it, a destructive modify's new half, still applied under the key, counting as one that waits. Shutdown's close of the registry stops every wait. A stopped kill makes no further `kill` or `status` read and raises neither version; its one line names its stop's own cause (`oldLifeWaitStopCause`: `OLD_LIFE_WAIT_STOP_CAUSE_SHUTDOWN`, `…_TEARDOWN`, `…_LATCHED`, or `…_UNKNOWN` for a cause it does not know, never the shutdown's). A shutdown- or last-waiter-teardown-stopped kill also writes the old key's `persona-kill-failed` entry with no alert text; one the own-row persona's latch stopped writes the line only, that persona's stop (b.jg5 SRJ-702; **Latched and stopped tries**). Each `ensureOldLifeWait` runs one round; a round that keeps the hold arms the waiting personas, and a later call starts the next round.

**In flight and lost messages.** While a wait runs for a hold P waits on, P's retry is blocked (`personaRetryBlockCause`, the again-reason `old-life-wait-in-flight` and the skip line `… an old-life wait step it waits on runs …`), the health tick makes no attempt for P, and a message lost for P reports `restarting` ([Inbound](#inbound-slack--claude-code) step 7). Once the hold is marked kill-failed, a message lost for P reports `kill-failed` until the hold ends (`waitsOnKillFailedHold`, b.jg5 SRJ-812). SRJ-308's `tmux-unresponsive` onset still posts at a retry skipped for a wait step.

**What a hold refuses (b.jg5 SRJ-810, SRJ-1502, SRJ-1505).** While a directory D is held, by real path:

- **No MCP session from D is any persona's.** Session admission asks the session manager's held-directory query (`oldLifeHeldDirectory`: every hold on D in begin order, the first hold's real path as the directory; nothing before the hold set is installed) before it matches any persona, and refuses the session as `held`, whichever persona names D, with one line naming D and every held instance id ([Connection](#connection) step 3; b.av2 SR-6.3 as amended by b.jg5 SRJ-1505).
- **Nothing types `/mcp reconnect` into the old life.** `reconnectMcpWithCause` asks `isOwnRowOldLifeHeld(key)` (the hold set holds the persona's own `cscb_<key>`) after its latched check and before its `send-keys`: a held own row gets no `send-keys`, the persona is recorded as waiting on that hold (`recordOwnRowWaiting`, only for a key in the applied set), its timer is armed with `held-for-old-life` (`armOldLifeWaiter`: not for a key outside the applied set, nor a latched, held or not-up persona), one line (`reconnectHeldLine`) and `transient`. That guards every caller: the ladder's `waiting` branch, the launch's working-row wait and the restart path's reconnect adapter, which itself replaces a held own row through the live-row sequence before it would type (a recorded key's old life by the retired-key rule, SRJ-805; a key not recorded with no retired-key flag; [Auto-Restart](#auto-restart) step 3, **A held own row**). A row held under another id than a persona's own is no persona's row, so nothing reconnects it.
- **No persona whose working directory is D is launched (b.av2 SR-6.1 step 4 as amended by b.jg5 SRJ-1502: "(4) launch, which waits while an old life that may still be running holds the persona's working directory (b.jg5 SRJ-809, SRJ-810); the persona is retried on its UNAVAILABLE retry timer (b.jg5 SRJ-301) until that wait ends").** One hold step, `oldLifeHoldStep(persona, site)`, serves every launch path: `spawnForPersona`'s old-life gate (after its held and `sequence-waiting` gates, before the join check and the latched gate), which the start pass, an apply's bring-up, a bring-up retry's launch, the restart path's `launchSession` and the retry timer's rerun all reach; the sequence-launch entry's gate at a live-row sequence's step-6 launch (`launchForLiveRowSequence`, after its latched and held gates), so the sequence ends without its launch; the restart path's old-life hook (`RestartDeps.isHeldForOldLife`, site `runRestartWork`; [Auto-Restart](#auto-restart), **The old-life gate**); and a latch re-check's own launches (`latchRecheckLaunch`, site `latch-recheck`, with the step's re-check option; [The re-check](#the-re-check-bjg5-srj-505), **The retries**). For each hold on P's directory whose instance id is not P's own `cscb_<key>` (`launchHoldsOn`), with P not latched, the step makes no agent-director call (no trust patch, reply-guard step or record write either), records P as waiting on the hold (`recordWaiting`), starts the hold's wait unless one runs on that id (`ensureOldLifeWait`; one wait per id, so a second launch starts none), arms P's timer with `held-for-old-life`, uncounted (`armOldLifeWaiter`, so not for a persona held on `ErrInvalidFlags` or not up, each with its skip line, the launch line then saying `its retry timer could not be armed`), and logs one line (`oldLifeHoldLaunchLine`). The launch answers `sequence-waiting` with `sequenceWaitingCause` `old-life-hold`; `launchSession` maps it to the uncounted `'refused'`, so the timer stays armed and nothing is counted, and the start pass counts it under "waiting on a live-row sequence" (b.jg5 SRJ-1015; Server-Managed Startup step 5). A latched P meets the latched gate instead (SRJ-305), with nothing recorded or armed, except inside P's own latch re-check: there the step, asked with `{ latchRecheck: true }` (`oldLifeHoldStep(persona, site, ref, options)`), holds P back as above, recording it as waiting and starting the hold's wait, but arms no retry timer (the latch keeps it stopped; the re-check's own timer retries P), its line saying `its retry timer is not armed: it is latched, and its latch re-check retries it`.
- **Once the hold ends, each persona that waited on it is retried at once.** `main()` registers the end-retry observer (`createOldLifeHoldEndRetry`) on the one hold set right after `setOldLifeHolds`, so after the session manager's own end observer has stopped the hold's wait. For each persona recorded as waiting on the hold that ended, in key order, one still applied (`getAppliedPersona`), not latched, not held on `ErrInvalidFlags` and up is retried at once through the retry controller's run-now entry (`runNow(key, { kind: 'held-for-old-life' }, 'old-life-hold-ended')`; [UNAVAILABLE retry](#unavailable-retry-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305), **Run now**); a removed, latched, held or not-up one is not (b.jg5 SRJ-305: each stops its timer; a persona not up is its bring-up's), and a run-now that throws is named and the next persona still retried (`retryOldLifeWaiter`). The reasons are the exported constants `OLD_LIFE_HOLD_END_NOT_RETRIED_NOT_APPLIED` (`not applied`), `…_LATCHED` (`latched`), `…_HELD` (`held on ErrInvalidFlags`), `…_NOT_UP` (`not up`) and `OLD_LIFE_HOLD_END_RETRY_FAILED_PREFIX` (`its retry failed: <error>`); both lines end with `OLD_LIFE_HOLD_END_RETRY_TAG`. The one exception is a persona whose own `cscb_<key>` is the held row while the wait the hold's end stopped there has not settled yet (`pendingOldLifeHoldEndStop`): it is retried only once that stopped wait has settled, so neither its sequence gate nor its retry's block cause still finds the wait running, after the same applied, latched, held and up checks, with its own line (`oldLifeHoldEndSettledRetryLine`). One line names them all (`oldLifeHoldEndRetryLine`):

  ```
  [slack] old-life hold: ended for instanceId="<id>" — retrying its waiting personas at once: <keys|none>[; once the stopped wait on its own row has settled: <keys>][; not retried: <key> (<why>)[, …]] (b.jg5 SRJ-810)
  [slack] old-life hold: the stopped wait on instanceId="<id>" has settled — persona=<key> retried at once (b.jg5 SRJ-810)
  [slack] old-life hold: the stopped wait on instanceId="<id>" has settled — persona=<key> not retried (<why>) (b.jg5 SRJ-810)
  ```

  The observer makes no agent-director call of its own; the retry's run makes the launch.

Who waits, and the exceptions:

- **Who.** The launch gate holds back every persona whose working directory is D, except one whose own row is the held row. The wait's rounds arm, besides, the persona whose own `cscb_<key>` is held (`oldLifeWaitingPersonas`). That persona is recorded as waiting on the hold when, applied, its launch is refused because the wait runs on its own row or the reconnect's guard finds its own row held, so the hold's end retries it (once the stopped wait has settled, above), and its teardown as the last waiter stops the wait.
- **The same-key exception (SRJ-810, SRJ-805).** A destructive modify's same-key new half, whose own row is the old life, is not held back by the gate: it waits by the retired-key rule, its reuse colliding and its live-row sequence replacing the old life, the sequence's step-6 reuse made only once the old row reads `ended` or `missing` ([Destructive modify](#destructive-modify-bav2-sr-86-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-406-sri-408-sri-502)). Its launch starts no wait and records no waiter.
- **A held own row of a key not recorded** (a row the start sweep swept for its `cwd`) is replaced through the live-row sequence by the restart path's reconnect adapter or the ladder's `cwd` replace step; while the wait runs on that row, the sequence's start answers `already-running` and arms the persona's timer (SRJ-811).
- **The rename's first spawn (SRJ-711 bullet 2).** A renamed persona's new key is held back while the old key's row is live, and its plain first spawn is made by the retry at once after the hold ends, once the old row reads `ended` or `missing` ([Bring-up at apply](#bring-up-at-apply-bav2-sr-61)).
- **A persona already running from D when D becomes held** gets no reconnect, kill or launch from the restart path until the hold ends: its restart work's old-life gate starts the wait and arms its timer, and its worker is not killed. Its MCP session, already registered, stays; a new one from D is refused.
- **What stops the wait.** The hold's end, shutdown, and the teardown of the last persona waiting on the hold (`forgetOldLifeWaits`; **What stops the wait**, above). A teardown while another persona still waits leaves the wait and its kill running (AC 64).

**Server memory and the rebuild.** A restart drops every hold. The start sweep rebuilds the ones still needed from its `list` and the retired-key record: the listing start restores apply step 1's hold on a recorded key's live row, a destructive modify's same-key old life that the sweep keeps included (a `credentials_file` change leaves the row's `cwd` matching its persona), and a failed sweep kill holds its row again. A rebuilt hold carries a mark only when a sweep kill marks it again.

#### Reads of a persona's own row (b.jg5 SRJ-114)

These sites read a persona's own agent-director row (`cscb_<key>`), and all go through one shared read, `readPersonaOwnRow` in `src/session-manager.ts` (the live-row sequence's `get`s too, [The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717)):

| Site | `<site>: <what>` in its lines | After a latch (a `pending` row with no launch start, a note, or an UNUSABLE_NAME answer) |
|---|---|---|
| The collision `get` of the ladder (Server-Managed Startup step 5) | `spawnForPersona: collision get` | The ladder answers `latched` before its `cwd` and `config_dir` guards and its state branches |
| The `ErrJsonlMissing` diagnosis `get` (`diagnoseJsonlMissing`) | `spawnForPersona: ErrJsonlMissing diagnosis get` | No diagnosis is reported; the branch launches nothing (no reuse spawn); the ladder answers `latched` |
| The re-read after a `resume`'s `ErrSpawnNotResumable` (the not-resumable step, `notResumableStep`, b.jg5 SRJ-710) | `spawnForPersona: get after ErrSpawnNotResumable` at the ladder, `live-row-sequence: get after ErrSpawnNotResumable` at the sequence's step-6 `resume` | At the ladder the not-resumable line names `the read latched the persona` and the ladder answers `latched`; at step 6 the launch is not made (`not-resumable-latched`) and the sequence stops for the latch, nothing armed |
| The re-read before a resume site's replacement of a row last read live on a path with no dead evidence (`replaceAtResumeSite`, b.jg5 SRJ-609, SRJ-611) | `spawnForPersona: get before replacing` | The ladder answers `latched`; no replacement, sequence or launch |
| The one `get` after a launch call's UNAVAILABLE outcome, a launch timeout included (`afterLaunchUnavailable`, b.jg5 SRJ-407; [A launch's window and the read after a timeout](#a-launchs-window-and-the-read-after-a-timeout-bjg5-srj-407)) | `spawnForPersona: get after the launch's UNAVAILABLE outcome` (`LAUNCH_UNAVAILABLE_GET_SITE`) | The launch answers `latched`; no approver, mark or sequence, and no launch in the attempt |
| The transcript `get` of the stale-`working`-row evidence (`readPersonaTranscript`) | `readPersonaTranscript: transcript get` | No evidence. The launch's `working`-row wait ends `latched` ([a latched wait](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1)); the restart path's working-row check answers `defer` |
| The `get` after a `find-missing` run lists the row in `unverified_ids` (b.jg5 SRJ-120; one per configured persona listed, after a run the server makes, never at a memo reuse, except the row the calling path's next step reads with a `get` and the row of a persona already latched, which gets no `get` and so is never relatched there) | `<prefix>: post-sweep get`, where `<prefix>` is the run's (`escalate-dead`, `spawnForPersona: before resume`, `waitForWaitingAndReconnect`, `waitForWaitingAndReconnect: timeout`, `spawnForPersona: prompt row`, `reconnectSession: prompt row` or `reconcileOrphans`), with `<ref>` `persona=<key>` | The caller of that persona's sweep gets `FIND_MISSING_LATCHED` and calls nothing more for it (see the b.m4r note under Server-Managed Startup step 5); the restart run stops at its latch check after the escalate-dead reconnect (Auto-Restart step 3). A note on another caller's row in the result is never read or acted on |

The read makes one `get` through `withOutageDetection`, then applies the rule, and never throws. While the persona holds a "this launch's row" record after a launch timeout, every read also applies SRJ-310's third end rule to it (`checkThisLaunchRowOnRead`; [The tmux-unresponsive condition](#the-tmux-unresponsive-condition-bjg5-srj-307-srj-310)), and so does the shared own-row `status` step below. A read whose caller still goes on that reads the row live out of `pending` ends the persona's stuck-launch episode, and so does the step for a returned result ([The stuck-launch post](#the-stuck-launch-post-bjg5-srj-1017-srj-1016)).

**The start sweep's `list` rows (b.jg5 SRJ-116).** The read's act step, the unexported `actOnOwnRowRead(key, row, at, clearRetiredEntry)`, takes a row already read: `readPersonaOwnRow` applies it to its `get` row, and the start sweep (`reconcileOrphans`) to each row of its one `list` whose id is a key's own, at `START_SWEEP_LIST_SITE` (`reconcileOrphans: start sweep list`, with the persona's ref added for a configured persona). One code path for both: the same rule, latch record, notice per episode, clear and lines, with no agent-director call of its own. `readPersonaOwnRow` passes `clearRetiredEntry` true; the sweep passes false for a key the same sweep records as retired, which leaves the clear out of the read (that recording clears the mark). A latch there leaves every row of the persona unkilled for the whole pass ([Server-Managed Startup](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1) step 4).

**Latched while the read was awaited (b.jg5 SRJ-502).** A read is awaited, and the health tick's liveness read may latch the persona meanwhile (b.jg5 SRJ-315). So the collision `get`, the diagnosis `get`, the one `get` after a launch's UNAVAILABLE outcome and the two re-reads (after `ErrSpawnNotResumable` and before a resume site's replacement), unless the read answered `latched`, ask `latchedAfterOwnRowRead(key, site, what, ref)` (`personaLatchedNow`) right after it, before any other answer is handled; the prompt rows' `status` re-read (`reconcileAndReadRowState`) does the same. A persona latched then gets one line, `[slack] <site>: <ref> is latched after its <what> — nothing more is called for it (b.jg5 SRJ-502)`, and the site answers as after a latch (the table above; `FIND_MISSING_LATCHED` for the re-read). It asks the latch, not the read, so a row the read latched itself logs it too, after its own latch line. Nothing is logged when the persona is not latched. The rule is the pure `decideOwnRowRead` in `src/row-read-rules.ts`, which holds no state, logs nothing and calls nothing; the shared read does the logging and the latching.

**The rule.** It is one rule with two latch decisions and, beside them, one entry-clear decision with its own conditions (**The retired-key entry clear**, below). Neither latch decision applies unless both of these hold:

- the row is the persona's own: its `claude_instance_id` is exactly `cscb_<key>`;
- the key is a persona of the applied configuration now, as the installed configured-persona query answers. `main()` installs it (`setConfiguredPersonaQuery`) right after the latch and before the start sweep; it reads `getAppliedPersona` at each call, so an apply's added persona counts at once and a removed one stops counting at once. With no query installed, or a query that throws, no key counts and no read latches.

Then the first decision that holds decides:

1. **Launch start not recorded (b.jg5 SRJ-513).** The row reads `pending` with no launch start (`isPendingWithNoLaunchStart`, `src/pending-row.ts`): its `launch_started_at` is absent, `null`, not a string, empty, or does not parse to a finite instant (`parseLaunchStart`, a lenient RFC 3339 read: `Z` or a numeric offset, a fraction of any length). It latches with `launch-start-not-recorded`, the refused operation `none` and the recorded state `pending`, whatever the row's `cwd`, `config_dir` or note, and whatever case the persona is already latched with. A row that also carries `provenance_conflict` answers this decision only. This decision does not age the launch start: a `pending` row with a valid one goes on to the next decision (a wait on such a row is measured as [Launch pending](#launch-pending-bjg5-srj-406-srj-408) describes).
2. **Conflicting labels (b.jg5 SRJ-114).** The row's `liveness_note` is exactly `provenance_conflict` (`LATCHING_LIVENESS_NOTE`), with no prefix, substring or case-folded match.

A note that is present counts, whatever state the row reads. Every other note (`tmux_server_changed`, `process_not_seen_*`, `probe_eacces`, `tmux_session_name_*` and any note CSCB does not know) latches no one, and the site goes on. `provenance_conflict` on a row that is not a configured persona's own (another caller's id, or the `cscb_<key>` row of a key outside the applied configuration) is ignored: it is not CSCB's to act on or post about, and the site goes on. The shared read asks `decideOwnRowRead` on every row it reads. A row that latches on either decision logs one line on every read; otherwise a row with no note logs nothing; any other note logs its line once per persona per note, and again only when the note changes, after a read with no note or the latching note, or once the persona's not-connected episode is forgotten (`forgetNotConnectedEpisode`: its removal's teardown, a health-check tick that finds it deliverable, or its MCP registration) (the engineering guide's Auto-Restart, Log Messages).

**The note latch.** The read latches through the installed latch's `set` (case `conflicting-labels`, refused operation `bring-up`, the state the `get` read, session `slack_bot_<key>`, no description); the record, holds and notice are those of [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502). The read answers the row with `latched` true and the site calls nothing more for the persona (b.jg5 SRJ-502). With no latch installed, or a `set` that throws, nothing is latched and the answer is still `latched` true, as at the CONFLICT row.

**The launch-start latch (b.jg5 SRJ-513).** The read latches through the same `set` with `launchStartNotRecordedSetInput`'s input (case `launch-start-not-recorded`, refused operation `none`, state `pending`, session `slack_bot_<key>`, no description), answers the row with `latched` true, and the site does what the table gives for a latch: at the collision `get` that is before the `cwd` and `config_dir` guards, so a row of another life latches too. Its line names the reason, `its row reads pending with no launch start`, where the note latch's names the note (the engineering guide's Auto-Restart, Log Messages). The record, holds and notice are those of [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502).

**The retired-key entry clear (b.jg5 SRJ-807).** The third decision of the rule (`decideRetiredEntryClear`, folded into `decideOwnRowRead`'s `clearRetiredEntry`) removes a key's entry from the retired-key record ([retired-keys.json](#retired-keysjson-state_dirretired-keysjson)) when all of these hold:

- the row is the key's own (`cscb_<key>`), for any key: configured or not, so a key outside the applied configuration clears too;
- the row reads `waiting`, `working`, `ask_user` or `check_permission` (`RETIRED_ENTRY_CLEARING_STATES`, the live states less `pending`);
- the installed retired-key store (`setRetiredKeyStore`; production: `main()`'s one store, installed right after the configured-persona query and before the start sweep) has the key recorded with its "new life has begun" mark set (`isMarked`).

It never fires on `pending`, with or without a launch start, nor on `ended`, `missing` or a state CSCB does not know, on an unmarked or unrecorded key, or on another key's row. It sits beside the launch-start decision and never changes it: a configured persona's own `pending` row with no launch start latches whatever the key's mark, and clears nothing. It is independent of the note latch: one read can latch on `provenance_conflict` and clear. The shared reads call the store's `clear` before any latch handling, and what the read answers its site is the same whatever the clear did. The removal is durable (one whole-record write); an entry leaves the record for no other reason than this clear and a failed apply's restore.

Every site above applies it through `readPersonaOwnRow`, every `status` site through the own-row `status` step ([The shared own-row `status` read](#the-shared-own-row-status-read-bjg5-srj-115)), and the start sweep's `list` rows through the same act step, with `retiredMarked` read from the installed store, except for a key the same sweep records as `absent-at-start`, whose recording clears its mark instead (Server-Managed Startup step 4). Two reads are the exception: the start sweep's bare `status` read between kill tries (`sweepKillRead`), for a row whose id is a key's own (`cscb_<key>`, configured or not), and the persona teardown kill's `status` read between its tries (`readTeardownKillRow`); each applies no step but makes this decision itself and acts on it, latching nothing (the start sweep's names the site `START_SWEEP_KILL_STATUS_SITE`, `reconcileOrphans: status read between kill tries`, and clears nothing once the server has begun shutting down; its post-run `get` reads through `readPersonaOwnRow`). The CLI never clears: its teardown's `status` reads (the state read, the poll and the kill's read between tries) apply no step, and it installs no store and never writes the record. The reads under **Other `get`s apply no rule** clear nothing either. A clear logs one line (success or a failed write, [Retired-key record lines](#retired-key-record-lines-bjg5-srj-1013-srj-1014)); a failed write leaves the entry in memory and on disk, the site acts on its read as usual, and the next qualifying read tries again. With no store installed, or an `isMarked` that throws, nothing is cleared.

The mark is set by a reuse spawn that succeeds for a recorded key ([Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-bjg5-srj-806-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-407)), so the clear fires once the persona's new life is read live, the new life of a key that had no row included.

**Errors.** `ErrSpawnNotFound`, recognised by class, reads as absent: the collision `get` keeps its single plain-spawn retry; a re-read reads it as no row (finished: a lost race at the not-resumable step, the replace step's reuse spawn before a replacement); the diagnosis `get` reports `inconclusive` with the reason `the agent-director row is absent (ErrSpawnNotFound)`; the transcript `get` gives an `unreadable` transcript with the reason `its agent-director row is absent (ErrSpawnNotFound)`; the post-sweep `get` changes nothing. An UNUSABLE_NAME answer latches the persona with the state `unreadable` and no further read (b.jg5 SRJ-512), and the read answers `latched` (`OWN_ROW_READ_LATCHED`): each site does what the table gives for a latch; at the post-sweep `get` the persona counts among the latched ones, and its caller gets `FIND_MISSING_LATCHED`, except in the start sweep's run, where the answer is routed to the server log and latches nothing (b.jg5 SRJ-1002; see the b.m4r note under Server-Managed Startup step 5). Any other error goes back to the site unchanged, and each site handles it in its own way:

- **The collision `get` and the diagnosis `get`** take the read-error row of [Refusals at the launch and recovery sites](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104) (`refusalAt` with verb `get`): every such error is a refusal, with its one refusal line, and the attempt calls nothing more. At the diagnosis `get` a refused read reports no diagnosis and launches nothing (no reuse spawn) too. An error `refusalAt` did not refuse (not reached) logs `[slack] spawnForPersona: collision get failed for <ref>: <failure> — nothing more is called` or `[slack] spawnForPersona: ErrJsonlMissing diagnosis get failed for <ref>: <failure> — nothing more is called` and the ladder answers an unmarked `failed`: no spawn-failure notice, no `spawn-failed` entry, no diagnosis, delete or launch.
- **The re-reads** take the same read-error row (`refusalAt` with verb `get`: one refusal line, the read-error cause armed inside the attempt). The not-resumable step then ends as the lost race, with nothing counted (`the read failed` in its line; at step 6, `not-resumable`); the re-read before a replacement answers the refusal result (`failed`), nothing more called. An error `refusalAt` did not refuse (not reached) logs `[slack] <site>: <what> failed for <ref>: <failure> — nothing more is called` and is handled the same way.
- **The transcript `get`** gives an `unreadable` transcript with the reason `reading its agent-director row failed: <failure>` and no refusal.
- **The post-sweep `get`** is a refusal only for the caller whose persona's own row it read (`postRunGetRefusal`): that caller, the run's starter or a joiner, takes the read-error row of the refusals (`refusalAt` with `get`), logs `[slack] <prefix>: post-sweep get refused for <ref>: <failure> — no spawn-failure notice; nothing more is called (b.jg5 SRJ-105)` and gets `FIND_MISSING_REFUSED`; a joiner first reports the error under its own key (`reportAgentDirectorError(key, err, 'get')`), since the `get` ran in the starter's context. For any other caller the failed read is log-only: it shows as `refused (<failure>)` in the run's summary line. No failed `get` changes the run's result or its memo.

**The restart path's working-row check.** The `working`-row verdict (`workingReconnectVerdict`, `src/server.ts`) makes one `read-pane` through the shared read-pane, recording the state `working`; a CONFLICT or UNUSABLE_NAME answer latches the persona there (b.jg5 SRJ-117, SRJ-501, SRJ-512), and a persona already latched is not read. Either way, and for a persona the latch holds by the time the read answers, the verdict is `'transient'` with its evidence run forgotten, no deferral noted, no not-connected notice and nothing typed; a latch the read answered, or a persona latched before it, logs one line, `[slack] reconnectSession: persona=<key> is working and is latched — deferring; no deferral noted, nothing typed (b.jg5 SRJ-502)`. On a pane, `checkWorkingRowPane` reads the transcript with one `get` when the pane shows an idle screen and asks the latch (`personaLatchedNow`) after it: a persona latched by that `get` or elsewhere gets `defer` with its run forgotten, no deferral noted, no notice and the same line. It asks the adapter's latched gate again right before it notes a deferral and right before the `blocked-on-prompt` notice; a persona latched then gets `defer` the same way, and the gate logs its own line.

**The prompt-row paths' read.** b.jdc's prompt-row verdict (`promptRowReconnectVerdict`, `src/server.ts`) and the ladder's prompt-row action (`launchOnPromptRow`) each make one one-line `read-pane` through the shared read-pane, recording the row state they read (`ask_user` or `check_permission`); a CONFLICT or UNUSABLE_NAME answer latches the persona there (b.jg5 SRJ-117, SRJ-501, SRJ-512), and a persona already latched is not read. Either way the verdict is `'transient'`, with one line, `[slack] reconnectSession: persona=<key> is <state> and is latched — deferring; no deferral noted, no notice, nothing typed (b.jg5 SRJ-502)`, and the ladder answers `latched`, with `[slack] spawnForPersona: <ref> reads <state> and is latched — no action; nothing typed and nothing more is called for it (b.jg5 SRJ-502)`. A persona the latch holds by the time the read answers gets the same: the verdict asks the adapter's latched gate (its own line), and the ladder, after a GONE or absent answer, asks `personaLatchedNow` before its sweep (the ladder's latched line). The verdict asks the gate again right before the `blocked-on-prompt` notice.

**Other `get`s apply no rule.** The permission poller's `list` and `get` and the JSONL persistence safeguard's `get` (`jsonl-persistence-check.ts`) are not these sites and keep their own handling (b.jg5 SRJ-122): a note on the row they read, `provenance_conflict` included, and a `pending` row with no launch start latch no one, a marked retired key's row read live clears no entry, and they change nothing. They end no old-life hold either.

**The old-life hold (b.jg5 SRJ-809).** Each `get` above, once its caller still goes on (`OwnRowReadSite.actGoes`), also reports the row to the hold set's one read entry (`noteOldLifeRowRead`, with the site's `<site>: <what>`): a row read `ended` or `missing`, or `ErrSpawnNotFound`, ends an old-life hold on `cscb_<key>`, and a live row's `cwd` re-points it. The own-row `status` step does the same for every `status` it is given ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809)).

**The CLI precheck's `get` (b.jg5 SRJ-901).** The precheck of `stop --stop-bots` and `clean_restart` reads each persona's own row with one `get` (`CliDeps.directorGet`), never through `readPersonaOwnRow`, and it is the one read of a persona's own row that latches nothing and writes no record: the CLI is a short-lived process with no latch state and installs no latch, configured-persona query or retired-key store (b.jg5 SRJ-114, SRJ-115), and the CLI never writes the retired-key record (b.jg5 SRJ-801). It reads only the row's state: a finished row (`ended`, `missing`) or no row is skipped, any other state is read with one `read-pane`; a `provenance_conflict` note alone fails nothing, and a `pending` row with no launch start is read like any live row. An UNUSABLE_NAME answer fails the persona's precheck (b.jg5 SRJ-512) and latches nothing ([The CLI precheck](#the-cli-precheck-bjg5-srj-901)).

#### The shared own-row `status` read (b.jg5 SRJ-115)

Every `status` of a persona's own row (`cscb_<key>`) goes through one step, `applyOwnRowStatusStep(key, answer, at)` in `src/session-manager.ts`, whoever makes the call, with three exceptions that apply no step: the CLI's `status` reads; the start sweep's bare `status` read between kill tries (`sweepKillRead`), which latches nothing and, for a row whose id is a key's own, applies the retired-key entry clear alone (`decideRetiredEntryClear`, its line naming the site `reconcileOrphans: status read between kill tries`, `START_SWEEP_KILL_STATUS_SITE`; none once the server has begun shutting down); and the persona teardown kill's `status` read between its tries (`readTeardownKillRow`), which latches nothing and applies the retired-key entry clear alone (`decideRetiredEntryClear`, its line naming the site `persona teardown kill: status read between tries`, `TEARDOWN_KILL_STATUS_SITE`). It never throws and answers whether it latched the persona:

- **A returned result:** the row-read rule (`decideOwnRowRead`) over the result as the persona's own row, with the installed configured-persona query. A latch decision latches the persona with its case, refused operation and row state and logs one line. A `status` result carries no liveness note, so the note decision never latches here; the launch-start decision does (b.jg5 SRJ-513): a result that reads `pending` with no launch start latches the persona with `launch-start-not-recorded` and the state `pending`, relatching a persona latched with another case. The step reads the result whole, as the client returned it (the client's `StatusResult`), so its `launch_started_at` reaches the decision; every caller passes it so. A result reading `waiting`, `working`, `ask_user` or `check_permission` while the installed retired-key store has the key recorded with its mark set clears the key's entry first, configured or not and beside any latch (b.jg5 SRJ-807; **The retired-key entry clear** under [Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)); a `pending` result never clears, and what the step answers is the same whatever the clear did.
- **A thrown value:** an UNUSABLE_NAME answer (`isUnusableNameError`, by `unknownName` and phrase) latches the persona with the state `unreadable`, logs one line and makes no further read. Any other value, `ErrSpawnNotFound` included, is left to the caller.

The shared own-row `status` read, `readPersonaOwnRowStatus(key, at)`, makes one `status` through `withOutageDetection`, applies the step, and answers `state` (with the raw launch start a `pending` result shows), `absent` (`ErrSpawnNotFound`), `refused` (any other error, carried unchanged for the site's own handling) or `latched` (with the state as the latch records it). The session manager's `status` sites read through it: the launch wait's poll and timeout reads, the prompt rows' re-read after a sweep (`reconcileAndReadRowState`), the retry timer's row read (`readPersonaRowState`), the latch-time read (`latchTimeRowState`), the dialog approver's readiness read (`approvePreSessionDialogs`, what `readiness status read`) and a persona's kill retry's read between tries (`retryPersonaKill`, what `status read between kill tries`; b.jg5 SRJ-702). The liveness adapter and the reconnect adapter (`src/server.ts`) make their own `status` call and apply the step right after it, to the result or to the thrown value, so the health tick, the restart path, the re-probe, the lost-message read and the reconnect adapter's state read clear an entry the same way. The CLI's `status` reads apply no step and never clear; the two kill-retry reads above apply the clear alone.

A path whose read latched the persona calls nothing more for it: the launch wait ends `latched`; the dialog approver stops (`latched`) with nothing read or typed; the prompt rows' re-read answers `FIND_MISSING_LATCHED`, as it does for a persona latched elsewhere while it was awaited; the retry timer's read answers the state as the latch recorded it, and the retry action, asking the latched query right after the read, stops with the latch's stop reason; the liveness adapter reads `unknown`, after which `runRestartWork` stops at its latch check (after the probe and after the re-probe), the health tick asks the latch again and schedules nothing, and the lost-message routing reports `held-for-human`; the reconnect adapter answers `'transient'` with nothing typed; the kill retry's read ends the tries with no further kill, the last try's outcome standing, and the ladder answers `latched`. So a configured persona's own `pending` row with no launch start never reaches `deferPendingRow` or the pending-only retry's `pending` row: the read that found it latched first.

### Launch pending (b.jg5 SRJ-406, SRJ-408)

A `pending` row is an agent-director row whose launch has begun but whose session has not started. agent-director shows its launch start, `launch_started_at`, on `pending` rows only, from `status`, `get` and `list` alike, and counts its own grace period (G) from it. CSCB reads a launch start in one place, `parseLaunchStart` in `src/pending-row.ts` ([Module Map](#module-map)); no other module parses one.

**Accepted forms.** An RFC 3339 date-time with `Z` or a numeric offset (`±hh:mm`), with or without a fractional part of any length: agent-director shows the fraction only when it is not zero. Milliseconds are the fraction's first three digits; further digits are dropped. Fields must be in range; a leap second (`:60`) is accepted.

**No launch start.** A value that is absent, `null`, not a string, empty, malformed or not a finite instant. `isPendingWithNoLaunchStart` is true for a `pending` row with no launch start by this reader.

**Every wait counts from the launch start.** Every wait on a `pending` row is measured from its launch start, never from the row's `started_at`: a resumed row's `started_at` is its original spawn time, so a wait counted from it would act early on a fresh launch. The waits are:

- the dialog approver's pace, through `isPendingRowAged` with the G accessor ([Pre-session dialog approval](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1), **Pace**);
- the dialog approver's B once a lap keeps a launch start, armed through `armPendingRowWait` and checked before each call with `isPendingRowAged` (**B, from the launch start**, same section);
- the live-row sequence's step-2 wait for G, armed through `armPendingRowWait` ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717), **The wait**). The old-life wait has no wait of its own: its G wait is this step, in the sequence's no-launch form ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809)).

`armPendingRowWait` arms through `armNeverEarlyWait` with the derived-wait accessor itself, so the wait never ends early and a value raised while armed is honoured (see `ad-settings.ts` in the [Module Map](#module-map)). No other wait on a `pending` row exists: the pending-only arm that a covered row gets (below) is the retry timer's backoff, never a wait counted from the launch start, and the only reader of `started_at` is the transcript-loss diagnosis, which is not such a wait.

**A row with no launch start is never aged.** `isPendingRowAged` answers false for it and `armPendingRowWait` arms nothing (`PENDING_ROW_WAIT_NOT_ARMED`), so `armNeverEarlyWait` is never handed a start that is not finite. Such a row takes its own path at once instead:

- a configured persona's own row latches the persona with `launch-start-not-recorded` at every own-row read ([Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114), **Launch start not recorded**);
- a row under a key no configured persona uses gets no wait for G in the old-life wait, and its kill and run follow at once ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809));
- a row the start sweep lists is killed like any live stray, with no wait ([Server-Managed Startup](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1)).

#### Covered and uncovered rows (b.jg5 SRJ-409, SRJ-411)

A `pending` row is a launch in progress. Whether it is the persona's current life is decided in one place, `decidePendingRowCover` (`src/pending-row.ts`, pure), over the row, whether its key is a configured persona's own (`configuredReadingOf`), the retired-key store's reading of the key (`retiredKeyReadingOf`, an in-memory mark counted as set) and the one row comparison (`compareRowToPersona`, reused, never rebuilt). It answers, in this order (the ladder's; a status-only site moves 3 and 4 before 2, below):

1. **No launch start** (`PENDING_ROW_NO_LAUNCH_START`): a configured persona's own row with no launch start, whatever else is true. It is never answered covered or exempted: the read that found it latched the persona ([Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114), **Launch start not recorded**), and the step only logs `noLaunchStartPendingRowLine`.
2. **Not covered**, `cwd-mismatch`: the row's `cwd` resolves to another directory than the persona's working directory.
3. **Undecided**, `cwd-unresolved`: the `cwd` condition cannot be evaluated now (b.av2 SR-6.4). At a status-only site (below) a persona working directory with no real path makes the row undecided whatever its `cwd` (`pendingRowComparisonFor`), so the lexical comparison never makes it covered.
4. **Undecided**, `config-dir-unresolved`: the persona's `claude_config_dir` has no real path now (b.g57).
5. **Not covered**, `retired-key-old-life`: the key is recorded as retired with no "new life has begun" mark, so the row is the old life (b.jg5 SRJ-805).
6. **Not covered**, `config-dir-mismatch`: the row's `config_dir` label is missing or differs.
7. **Covered** otherwise.

That is the order at the collision ladder (`statusOnlySite` false): no-launch-start latch, `cwd` mismatch, `cwd` unresolved, config dir unresolved, retired with no mark, label mismatch, covered. The ladder's own `cwd` guard has run before its `pending` step and keeps `cwd-unreachable` (b.av2 SR-6.4). At a status-only site (`statusOnlySite` true: the restart path's deferral, its re-probe and a pending-only retry), an unresolvable working directory or `claude_config_dir` makes the row undecided before any mismatch is checked, so the order there is 1, 3, 4, 2, 5, 6, 7: no-launch-start latch, `cwd` unresolved, config dir unresolved, `cwd` mismatch, retired with no mark, label mismatch, covered. A row whose `cwd` resolves elsewhere while the persona's `claude_config_dir` cannot be resolved is therefore undecided at a status-only site and not covered at the ladder.

The session manager acts on the answer through one step, `pendingRowStep`. A covered or undecided row arms the persona's retry timer in pending-only mode with the `pending-row` cause (`armPendingRowWatch` over `armPendingOnlyForPendingRow`; a latched persona is never armed, with one line) and is never killed, reused or launched over; an undecided row gets no approver and no sequence, with one `undecidedPendingRowLine`, and the next read decides again. A row that is not covered gets one `uncoveredPendingRowLine` and goes through the live-row sequence ([The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717)) with the conversation not kept and alert context `recovery` (the retired-key flag set for an old life), never with an approver lap, a keystroke or an inline kill and launch: the sequence waits until G past the row's launch start and ends in a reuse spawn of the same id. Its step-6 launch meets the old-life hold gate like any launch.

Where each origin meets it:

- **A launch that returned success.** The after-launch step (`afterLaunchSucceeded`) arms the row's watch with no read: the row is the persona's own current life, built from its own spawn parameters (Server-Managed Startup step 5). This covers every success site, the hand-off run after a pending-only stop ([Pending-only mode](#pending-only-mode-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305-srj-306)) and the live-row sequence's final launch included.
- **A launch that ended in an UNAVAILABLE outcome** (a launch timeout included). Its one `get` reads the row and, for `pending`, runs the step with `statusOnlySite` false; a covered row gets the approver only after a launch timeout ([A launch's window and the read after a timeout](#a-launchs-window-and-the-read-after-a-timeout-bjg5-srj-407)).
- **A launch that failed with `ErrTmuxSessionCreate`.** The failure is counted (`failed`, `countedClass`) and the timer is armed pending-only at once with no `get` (`armPendingOnlyAfterLaunchFailure`); the first pending-only retry decides the row it reads (below). A covered `pending` row it left is never CSCB's own launch and is waited out through [the pending-row rule](#the-pending-row-rule-bjg5-srj-410) (**A failed launch's row**).
- **The collision ladder's `pending` step** (`ladderPendingRowStep`, `statusOnlySite` false): the `pending` branch, the not-resumable step's re-read and a resume site's re-read. Covered: armed, and at a retry of the persona's timer (full mode) the pending-row rule's one run with `withinOwnLaunch` (P's own launch in flight left out of its gate), mapped by `ladderResultOfRuleAnswer`: a refusal, the held post or a live row `no-op`; a latch `latched`; a row read gone or a refused `get` `retrying`, with one line (`ladderRuleRetryingLine`) and nothing launched in that attempt, the pending-only timer owning the persona; from any other origin `no-op`, armed only. Not covered: the replace step (`replacePersonaRow`), `sequence-waiting`. Undecided: armed, answering `deferred` for an unresolved config directory (`deferForUnresolvedConfigDir`) and `no-op` for an unresolved `cwd`. The ladder's own `cwd` guard at the collision `get` runs first, and a persona working directory with no real path fails the launch there (`cwd-unreachable`).
- **A dialog approver's stop** with its row still `pending` (Server-Managed Startup step 5, **The arm at its stop**): armed only after the stops that list names.
- **The restart path's `pending` deferral** (its first probe, b.d61's re-probe and the reconnect adapter's `pending`; [Auto-Restart](#auto-restart), **`pending` rows**) and **a pending-only retry** ([Pending-only mode](#pending-only-mode-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305-srj-306)). These hold only a `status` read, so they take the read-and-step entry, `readAndStepPendingRow(persona)`: one `get` of the persona's own row through the shared own-row read (`PENDING_ROW_STEP_GET_SITE`, so its note and launch-start latches, its retired-entry clear and its old-life read entry apply), then the step with `statusOnlySite` true. It answers covered, undecided, not covered (with the sequence start entry's answer: `startRecoverySequence`, entry at step 1, no ladder held, so the start entry reads the retired-key store itself), `latched`, `not-pending` (with the state read), `no-row` or `refused`. The adapter answers the deferral's `'pending'`, the uncounted deferral SRJ-409 calls `transient`; the retry maps the answer for the controller (`retryPendingRowStep`). A message lost for the persona reaches this path through the restart it starts.

The restart path's old life of a retired key with no mark (b.jg5 SRJ-805) that reads `pending` goes through the deferral, and so through the sequence as an uncovered row; one that reads live other than `pending` is replaced by the reconnect adapter (`replaceOwnRowOldLife`). Two rules outside these paths are their own and unchanged: the start sweep kills a swept `pending` row (an absent persona's, or one whose `cwd` is not its persona's) with no wait for G, under its own rule (b.jg5 SRJ-714; [Server-Managed Startup](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1)), and the CLI teardown of `stop --stop-bots` and `clean_restart`, run by a human, ends a persona's instance whatever its state (b.jg5 SRJ-904; [clean_restart](#clean_restart-sr-11-event-12)). The restart path's kill after a `dead` reading reads no row state, so it can end a row that would read `pending` (an `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` read as `dead`, b.jg5 SRJ-410, SRJ-314). A covered row is aged at its retries and once at the approver's stop by the pending-row rule ([The pending-row rule](#the-pending-row-rule-bjg5-srj-410)), which at B aborts CSCB's own stuck launch once per stuck-launch episode ([CSCB's own stuck launch and its one abort](#cscbs-own-stuck-launch-and-its-one-abort-bjg5-srj-412)) and makes the held post for any other row.

#### A launch's window and the read after a timeout (b.jg5 SRJ-407)

A launch that times out may have created the row, moved it to `pending` or started the session, and may be held at a startup dialog; agent-director leaves such a row `pending`. Launching again would collide with it or start a second instance, and killing it would end a start that may still succeed. So CSCB reads the row once and acts on what it shows, with no launch in that attempt.

**The window.** Every launch call (a plain spawn, a reuse spawn or a `resume`) goes through one wrapper around spawn detection, `launchCallWithWindow` in `src/session-manager.ts`: every plain spawn (through the one plain-spawn handler `plainSpawnOutcomeAt`: the first spawn, the retry spawn, the plain spawn after a `resume`'s `ErrSpawnNotFound`) and the reuse spawn (`reuseSpawnForPersona`) call it directly, and every `resume` (in `resumeAtSite`) through `launchWithReplyGuard`. It keeps the persona's latest launch call (`LaunchCallWindowRecord`, read with `launchCallWindowOf(key)`): the declared verb (`spawn` or `resume`), `startMs`, taken on the session manager's clock (`_now`; `_setNow` in tests) just before the call, and, once the call returned success or ended in a launch timeout, `endMs` and `end` (`LAUNCH_CALL_END_RETURNED`, `LAUNCH_CALL_END_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT`). The end of a timeout is taken when the error reached CSCB, after the wrapper reported it; a call that ended any other way keeps no end. A new launch call replaces the window and forgets the persona's "this launch's row" record (below) and its own-launch record ([CSCB's own stuck launch and its one abort](#cscbs-own-stuck-launch-and-its-one-abort-bjg5-srj-412)); both are absent during the call. A call that answers `ErrInstanceIdCollision` (by class), which created no row and started no launch, puts both back (`restoreLaunchRecords`), each only while that call's window is still the persona's latest (no later launch call and no `forgetLaunchCalls` came after it) and nothing set that record during the call; the window is not restored, so the collided call's window stays the latest. Every other outcome, a CONFLICT refusal included (the pre-spawn scan's refusal cannot be told from one after "duplicate session", which may leave this call's row `pending`), keeps them forgotten. They live in memory only, beside the not-interactive record ([The stuck-launch post](#the-stuck-launch-post-bjg5-srj-1017-srj-1016)); `forgetLaunchCalls(key)` forgets all four at the persona teardown's kill (`killPersonaInstanceForTeardown`, which runs once the persona's launch in flight has settled), and `_resetInFlightLaunches` clears them in tests.

**The window check.** `isLaunchStartInWindow(rawLaunchStart, window)` (`src/pending-row.ts`, pure) answers whether a row's launch start, read by `parseLaunchStart`, lies inside the window, both ends included: no earlier than the call's start and no later than its end. It answers false for no window, a window with no end, a bound that is not finite and no launch start. The check fails safe: a clock stepped between the call and agent-director's write makes this launch's row read as another launch's, which is never taken for a new life. Two readers use it: the step after a launch timeout (this launch's row and, inside the window, the own-launch record), and the dialog approver's first lap after a launch that returned success, which records the launch as CSCB's own when the kept launch start lies inside that call's window ([CSCB's own stuck launch and its one abort](#cscbs-own-stuck-launch-and-its-one-abort-bjg5-srj-412)).

**A launch timeout, by class plus phrase.** `launchTimeoutFormOf(value, call)` and `isLaunchTimeoutError(value, call)` (`src/ad-error-class.ts`) answer only for a declared launch call (`isLaunchCall`: `spawn`, plain or reuse, or `resume`), in two forms: an `ErrCallTimeout` instance (`LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_FORM_CALL_TIMEOUT`), the client's own timeout of the call; or an `ErrTmuxUnresponsive` instance whose description contains `LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_PHRASE`, "the session may have been created" (`LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_FORM_TMUX_UNRESPONSIVE`). An `ErrUnknownErrorName` whose `unknownName` is `ErrTmuxUnresponsive` is neither form; it is an unknown later name, UNAVAILABLE. Both keep the UNAVAILABLE class, so the reporting point arms the retry timer with `unavailable` and starts or continues the `tmux-unresponsive` condition as for any UNAVAILABLE launch outcome. A plain `ErrTmuxUnresponsive` (tmux unreadable, still stopping, still starting, a "duplicate session" whose holder could not be read) is no launch timeout.

**The one `get` after an UNAVAILABLE launch outcome.** Each launch call's failure handler, once its refusal handling answered a refusal for an UNAVAILABLE error (`isUnavailableRefusal`), runs one step, `afterLaunchUnavailable`, inside the launch attempt: `plainSpawnFailedAt` (behind the one plain-spawn handler: the first spawn, the retry spawn and the plain spawn after a `resume`'s `ErrSpawnNotFound` at either `resume` site), `resumeFailedAt` (the `resume` at either site) and `reuseSpawnFailedAt` (every reuse, the live-row sequence's step-6 reuse included). The triggers are a launch timeout in either form and every other UNAVAILABLE launch outcome: "still stopping", "still starting", tmux unreadable, a "duplicate session" whose holder could not be read or whose name more than one session matches (HO rev 20; for a `resume` or a reuse, whatever its restore sentence says, HO rev 28), a plain spawn's pre-spawn scan that could not answer (HO rev 15), a plain spawn's re-lookup after "duplicate session" that could not answer, whose new row agent-director ended (HO rev 26; [Plain spawn](#plain-spawn-bjg5-srj-111)), and the other UNAVAILABLE forms (an unknown later name, CSCB's `UnknownError` wrapper). A CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME latch, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG, UNCLASSIFIED, LAUNCH FAILURE and DIRECTORY keep their own rows and take no `get`. The step makes exactly one `get` of the persona's own row through the shared own-row read (`readPersonaOwnRow` at `LAUNCH_UNAVAILABLE_GET_SITE`, `spawnForPersona: get after the launch's UNAVAILABLE outcome`; [Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)), so its note and launch-start latches, its retired-entry clear and its old-life read entry apply, then asks the latch (`latchedAfterOwnRowRead`). After it, no launch call is made in this attempt, whatever it read; nothing is killed, deleted or counted. It logs one line per decision (`launchUnavailableGetLine`; [Launch-timeout lines](#launch-timeout-lines-bjg5-srj-407)).

| The `get` reads | What follows | The launch answers |
|---|---|---|
| A row that latched the persona, or the persona latched meanwhile | Nothing more | `latched` |
| No row (`ErrSpawnNotFound`) | Nothing more; the retry the outcome armed brings the persona up | `retrying` |
| A refused read | The shared read's error rows (`refusalAt` with `get`: one line; inside the attempt its own cause arms) | `retrying` |
| `ended` or `missing` | Nothing more; the next retry launches it again | `retrying` |
| Another live state | No further call and never a launch over it; the retry the outcome armed runs the restart path, whose reconnect adapter handles the row | `retrying` |
| A state CSCB does not know | Nothing more | `retrying` |
| `pending`, after a launch timeout | The window check, then the one pending-row step (`pendingRowStep`, the ladder's order, [Covered and uncovered rows](#covered-and-uncovered-rows-bjg5-srj-409-srj-411)), which arms a covered or undecided row pending-only with the `pending-row` cause. Covered: the dialog approver through its start entry with the launch-timeout origin (below). Undecided: no approver, no sequence. Not covered (a retired key's old life, a `cwd` or `config_dir` mismatch): the live-row sequence through its start entry (`startRecoverySequence`: seeded `pending`, the conversation not kept, alert context `recovery`, the retired-key flag for an old life), no approver. No launch start: the read latched the persona | Covered or undecided: `retrying`. Not covered: the start's result, `sequence-waiting` (`held` for a persona held on `ErrInvalidFlags`). No launch start: `latched` |
| `pending`, after any other UNAVAILABLE outcome | The same step, but the row is never this launch's: no window check, no mark and no approver from this rule. Covered: armed pending-only only. Undecided and not covered as above | As above |

`retrying` is the launch's refusal answered as the timer armed it (b.jg5 SRJ-1015): the step reads the attempt's last recorded error before its `get` (`currentAttemptLastError`, `src/unavailable-retry.ts`), since the `get`'s own answer replaces it, and answers `retrying` when the launch's error or the `get`'s armed the persona's timer, else the refusal's `failed` as it came. `launchSession` maps `retrying` to the uncounted `'refused'`. A launch that timed out is never routed through the after-launch step: it writes no `pre_trust` line and arms nothing there.

**This launch's row.** After a launch timeout, a `pending` row whose launch start lies inside the call's window is this launch's row. The step records it for the persona (`ThisLaunchRowRecord`: the launch start and the window; `thisLaunchRowOf(key)`) before the cover decision, and with it the own-launch record of a timed-out launch (`recordOwnLaunch` with `LAUNCH_CALL_END_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT`; an uncovered row is recorded too, but only step 3 of the pending-row rule, which runs on a covered row, reads it). For a reuse spawn, the step then runs the mark of SRJ-806's second trigger (b.jg5 SRJ-806 as amended by b.deo SRI-407; `markNewLifeAfterTimedOutReuse`, through the mark step it shares with a reuse that succeeded, `setNewLifeMarkForReuse`, against the attempt's start the reuse carried): for a key recorded when the attempt started and still, with its record generation unchanged, the "new life has begun" mark is set (a failed write held in memory by the store) with one line, and the key's old-life hold ends with the reason `new-life` ([Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-bjg5-srj-806-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-407), [The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809)); a key recorded since gets one line and no mark; any other key, nothing. Since the mark comes first, the reuse's own row is covered as the new life and gets the approver, never the sequence. A row whose launch start lies outside the window (earlier than the call, or later than its end) is another launch's: no record and no mark; covered, it still gets the approver; a recorded key's unmarked old life there is not covered and goes through the sequence (AC 35). The window check runs before the cover decision for every `pending` row read after a timeout, so a row in another directory whose launch start lies inside the window gets the record too, while it goes through the sequence. The launch answers `retrying` even when the row is this launch's and a mark was set.

The record is checked by every shared own-row read for SRJ-310's third end rule (`checkThisLaunchRowOnRead`; [The tmux-unresponsive condition](#the-tmux-unresponsive-condition-bjg5-srj-307-srj-310), **What ends it**): a read of the row live other than `pending` forgets it and ends the condition; `ended`, `missing`, no row, or `pending` with another launch start forgets it with no end; `pending` with the same launch start, or a state CSCB does not know, keeps it. A new launch call and the teardown's forget drop it too.

**Later attempts.** The retries the outcome armed read the row before anything else: a covered or undecided row's `pending-row` cause keeps the timer's last row `pending`, and a full-mode retry runs the restart path, whose `status` read defers a `pending` row (`pending-deferred`) and reconnects a live one; a pending-only retry reads with `status` ([Pending-only mode](#pending-only-mode-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305-srj-306)). While the row reads `pending` or another live state no retry launches over it, and only `ended`, `missing` or no row is launched again (AC 83); a covered `pending` row gets the pending-row rule at those retries ([The pending-row rule](#the-pending-row-rule-bjg5-srj-410)), which at B aborts the launch once when it is CSCB's own ([CSCB's own stuck launch and its one abort](#cscbs-own-stuck-launch-and-its-one-abort-bjg5-srj-412)).

#### The stuck-launch post (b.jg5 SRJ-1017, SRJ-1016)

The stuck-launch post is the single notice for a launch that does not report in (b.jg5 SRJ-405). The pending-row rule makes it at B (SRJ-410 step 3; [The pending-row rule](#the-pending-row-rule-bjg5-srj-410)). Through its production dependencies (`buildPendingRowRuleDeps`), the rule calls the relaunching poster from the abort of CSCB's own stuck launch ([CSCB's own stuck launch and its one abort](#cscbs-own-stuck-launch-and-its-one-abort-bjg5-srj-412)) and the held text's poster (`postHeld`) for any other row still `pending` at B.

**The two texts.** Both are built only in `src/pending-row.ts`, from its exported fixed pieces, and name the persona's session as `quotedPersonaSessionName` renders it (`src/persona-identity.ts`). The persona notifier adds the persona prefix.

- ***Launch stuck*** (`stuckLaunchRelaunchingText(key, launchBoundMs)`): for CSCB's own stuck launch. It says CSCB is ending that launch and relaunching it, and that nothing is needed. B is stated in whole minutes, rounded down (`wholeMinutes`), from the derived wait the caller reads at the moment of the post (`adLaunchBoundMsInEffect`): 5 minutes at the default settings, 6 with `pending_grace_seconds` 300.
- ***Session not starting*** (`stuckLaunchHeldText(key, launchStart, metNotInteractive)`): for any other `pending` row. It names the row's launch start through the one renderer (`describeLaunchStartForLog`: ISO 8601 UTC ending in `Z`, the same for both launch-start forms), says CSCB keeps checking, and lists a human's remedies: attach to the session by its exact target (`stuckLaunchAttachRemedyLine`, `tmuxExactSessionTarget`), end the launch by following agent-director's "Operator actions" (`STUCK_LAUNCH_END_LAUNCH_REMEDY_LINE`), and list what holds the session (`stuckLaunchListRemedyLine`). The human-only line closes it (`STUCK_LAUNCH_HUMAN_ONLY_LINE`). It is built only for a row with a launch start: a configured persona's own `pending` row with none latches instead.

**The attach-line variant.** When the row's current launch met a `send-keys` that answered `ErrSpawnNotInteractive` (`metNotInteractive`, read from the not-interactive record below), the head gains `STUCK_LAUNCH_NOT_STARTED_BY_CSCB_CLAUSE` and the attach line is dropped. The session holding the name was not started by that launch, so answering its prompt would put an earlier launch's worker on this row. The poster's line names this form.

**No session-ending command (b.jg5 SRJ-1001).** Neither text names a command that ends a session. The end-the-launch remedy points to agent-director's "Operator actions" by its title, and the remedies are said to be for a human only.

**The posters.** `postStuckLaunchRelaunching(deps, key, launchBoundMs)` and `postStuckLaunchHeld(deps, key, launchStart, metNotInteractive)` take injected dependencies (`StuckLaunchPosterDeps`): the server's one episodes instance, a `tmux-unavailable` query and a log. Each call:

1. While the persona's `tmux-unavailable` outage is raised (or the query throws, taken as raised with one line), posts nothing and begins no episode (`suppressed`): that outage's onset is the persona's notice.
2. Otherwise begins or keeps the persona's `stuck-launch` episode (`closed` after shutdown's `close`, nothing posted).
3. Posts its text through the episodes' sink, the persona notifier, at most once per episode under its own mark (`relaunching`, `held`): a second call in the episode answers `already-posted`. The two texts post independently, so one episode can hold both. A post a submitted teardown mutes still counts as posted.
4. Writes one line per call, and never throws: an episodes call that throws logs one line and answers `failed` (`STUCK_LAUNCH_POST_FAILED`), kept apart from `suppressed` so the abort never takes a failed post for the `tmux-unavailable` gate, nor the gate for a failed post.

The `ad-config-malformed` gate is the caller's, not the poster's. The episode and its marks live only in the episodes instance ([Module Map](#module-map), `persona-episodes.ts`), so a new episode posts both texts again.

**The episode's end (b.jg5 SRJ-1016).** The episode ends silently, with no post and one line, on any of these:

- **A live read.** A read of the persona's own row in `waiting`, `working`, `ask_user` or `check_permission` (`isStuckLaunchEpisodeEndState`) ends it. The shared own-row reads do this through the episodes `main()` installs (`setStuckLaunchEpisodes`):
  - `readPersonaOwnRow`, once its caller still goes on;
  - `applyOwnRowStatusStep`, for a returned result. That covers every own-row `status` the server makes through the step, the liveness and reconnect adapters' included.
- **A latch.** The latch's hold observer's fifth hold, `endStuckLaunch`, bound in `main()` to `endStuckLaunchEpisodeForLatch`. It runs on every set: a latch, a relatch and a same-case set.
- **A teardown or shutdown.** The persona teardown's `forget` and shutdown's `close` end it, with no step of their own.

A read of `pending`, `ended` or `missing`, no row, a failed read and a kill do not end it. Neither do the two between-try `status` reads that apply no step (the start sweep's and the persona teardown kill's) or the CLI's reads. So a row that finished after an abort and a later stuck launch share one episode. Another persona's read never ends P's episode. With no episodes installed (unit tests, the integration driver), no read ends one.

**The not-interactive record (b.jg5 SRJ-118, SRJ-412, SRJ-1017).** The session manager keeps, per persona, the launch start of its latest launch whose `send-keys` answered `ErrSpawnNotInteractive`. It sits in memory beside the launch-in-flight state (the launch-call window and the "this launch's row" record, [A launch's window and the read after a timeout](#a-launchs-window-and-the-read-after-a-timeout-bjg5-srj-407)).

- **Set.** The dialog approver's `send-keys` sets it (`recordSendKeysNotInteractive`) when the call fails with that name, keyed by the launch start the first lap kept; so does the pending-row rule's lap Enter (`sendPendingRowLapEnter`), keyed by the launch start of the row the rule runs on. It is set before the approver checks for a stop asked during the call, so it is set whatever decides the stop's reason. Only a `send-keys` answer counts: a `read-pane` or `status` answer of that name records nothing. A launch start that is absent or does not parse records nothing, and a later record replaces an earlier one.
- **Read.** `launchMetSendKeysNotInteractive(key, launchStart)` answers yes only for that instant, in either launch-start form (`launchStartInstantOf`), and no for any other launch start, another persona, or no record. The pending-row rule reads it to skip its lap and, at B, to drop the held text's attach line; the own-launch query (`isCscbOwnLaunch`) reads it too, so a launch that met it is never CSCB's own.
- **Forgotten.** The persona teardown's kill forgets it (`forgetLaunchCalls`), and `_resetInFlightLaunches` clears it in tests. A new launch call keeps it: the record names its launch by its launch start, so a new launch reads no.

Its log lines are under [Stuck-launch post lines](#stuck-launch-post-lines-bjg5-srj-1017-srj-1016).

#### The pending-row rule (b.jg5 SRJ-410)

The pending-row rule is the one place that acts on a covered `pending` row as it ages ([Covered and uncovered rows](#covered-and-uncovered-rows-bjg5-srj-409-srj-411)). It lives in `src/pending-row.ts`: the pure decisions (`pendingRowAgeOf`, `isPendingRowLapEligible`, `decidePendingRowLapPane`, `decidePendingRowLapEnter`, `readPendingRowRun`, `decidePendingRowStepThree`) and one driver, `createPendingRowRule(deps)`, whose `run(input)` runs the rule once for P on a row read the caller holds. Its dependencies are injected (`PendingRowRuleDeps`); `buildPendingRowRuleDeps` in `src/session-manager.ts` binds them to the shared entries, so `main()` and the recovery harness compose it the same way, and `setPendingRowRule({ rule, serialize, gate })` installs the one instance in `main()`, after the live-row sequence registry and before the start pass. The rule's own steps never kill, launch or reuse the row; only its own-launch slot, the abort of CSCB's own stuck launch, kills one, through the checked kill, and relaunches it through the live-row sequence ([CSCB's own stuck launch and its one abort](#cscbs-own-stuck-launch-and-its-one-abort-bjg5-srj-412)).

**Where it runs.** Only inside a retry of P's retry timer, in either mode, and once at P's dialog approver's stop:

- **At a retry.** The retry action runs inside the retry marker (`runInTimerRetry`; `isInsideTimerRetry(key)`), and `runPendingRowRuleAtRetry(persona, row, options)` runs the rule only there, at most once per retry (`claimTimerRetryRuleRun`; a second site in the same retry logs `pendingRowRuleAlreadyRanLine` and runs nothing).
