Three sites reach it, each on a row it answered covered: the pending-only retry's step (`retryPendingRowStep`, bound as the controller's `stepPendingRow`; [Pending-only mode](#pending-only-mode-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305-srj-306)), the restart path's deferral at its first probe and its re-probe (`deferPendingRow`; [Auto-Restart](#auto-restart), **`pending` rows**), and the collision ladder's `pending` step (`ladderPendingRowStep`, its not-resumable re-read included, with `withinOwnLaunch`; [Covered and uncovered rows](#covered-and-uncovered-rows-bjg5-srj-409-srj-411)). `readAndStepPendingRow`'s covered answer carries the row its `get` read, so the rule needs no second read before it starts.
- **At the approver's stop.** `queueApproverStopRuleRun`, right after the stop's pending-only arm in `runRegisteredApprover`, once the approver has left the registry ([Server-Managed Startup](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1), **The arm at its stop**).
- **Never elsewhere.** Reached from any other origin (the start pass, an apply's bring-up, a restart timer, a human-triggered restart, the lost-message trigger, the hand-off run after a pending-only stop) the deferral and the ladder's step only arm, with no call and no line from the rule. The reconnect adapter's deferral passes `mayRunRule: false`. Nothing under `runOutsideAttempts` (an approver, a live-row sequence and its ladder) is inside a retry. An undecided or uncovered row never reaches it. With no rule installed, each retry that would run it logs `pendingRowRuleNotInstalledLine` and keeps the arm only.

**The gate.** Before any call, in order, each with one gate line (`pendingRowRuleGateLine`): P latched (a throwing query counts as latched; [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)) answers latched; work in flight that blocks a retry (a launch call, a live-row sequence or an old-life wait step; at the ladder, P's own launch is left out; the one list of causes, `retryBlockCauseOf`, behind `personaRetryBlockCause` too) answers a `blocked` refusal, and a running dialog approver never blocks it; P's working directory held for an old life (`isOwnRowOldLifeHeld`, or `oldLifeHoldStep`, which records P as waiting and arms its `held-for-old-life` cause; b.jg5 SRJ-810) answers `held-for-old-life`; a row not `pending` answers `not-pending`; a row with no launch start answers `no-launch-start` (b.jg5 SRJ-408).

**Step 1, younger than G.** `pendingRowAgeOf` ages the row from its launch start through `isPendingRowAged` with the derived-wait accessors themselves (`adGraceMsInEffect`, `adLaunchBoundMsInEffect`), read at each check, so a value raised meanwhile is honoured and `AD_WAIT_NEVER_ENDS`, NaN or a throwing accessor never passes G ([Launch pending](#launch-pending-bjg5-srj-406-srj-408)). Younger than G: a refusal, with no call and no line. The rule arms no timer of its own.

**Step 2, G or older.**

1. **The lap**, only when no dialog approver runs for P and the launch has not met a `send-keys` `ErrSpawnNotInteractive` (`isPendingRowLapEligible`, the not-interactive record of [The stuck-launch post](#the-stuck-launch-post-bjg5-srj-1017-srj-1016)). One `read-pane` through the shared reader with 40 lines and `allow_pending` (`readPendingRowLapPane`; [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)) and, when the pane shows a startup dialog the approver recognises (`paneShowsStartupDialog`, the approver's own check), Enter (`sendPendingRowLapEnter`: one `send-keys` with an empty text and `allow_pending`). Each answer is read by class, one cell per SRJ-117 and SRJ-118 row: a pane with no dialog, GONE, no row, UNAVAILABLE, CONFIG and ENVIRONMENT (which raise their outages) and UNCLASSIFIED end the lap, and the run goes on; CONFLICT and UNUSABLE NAME latch P (the refused operation "P's next check or recovery", recorded `pending`) and nothing more is done; an UNCLASSIFIED whose version re-check decided that the server stops ends the round (`lap-only`). An Enter answering `ErrSpawnNotInteractive` sets the not-interactive record, so no further lap is made on that launch, and the run goes on. The latched query is asked again after every call.
2. **The run and the `get`.** One bypassing `find-missing` run (`bypassingFindMissingSweep` with P's key as the next-step `get`, read with `readFindMissingRow`; [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104), b.jg5 SRJ-120), then one `get` through the shared own-row read (`PENDING_ROW_RULE_GET_SITE`; [Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)). A refused run ends the round (`run-refused`); a run that failed otherwise is taken as not judged and the `get` follows. A refused `get` ends the round with nothing more (`read-refused`): step 3 never acts on an earlier read. No row, `ended` or `missing` answers gone; another live state answers live, with no action from this rule; a state CSCB does not know ends the round. A row still `pending` before B, measured from the `get`'s launch start, is a refusal whether or not the run judged it (`not-judged` or `still-pending`).

**Step 3, still `pending` at B or older, judged or not** (`decidePendingRowStepThree`, in this order): while P's `tmux-unavailable` outage is raised, nothing (its onset is P's notice); P latched, nothing; CSCB's own stuck launch while P's `ad-config-malformed` outage is raised, nothing, whether or not its abort is still available (`config-malformed`, neither text and no abort until it clears, with one `stuckLaunchPostSkippedLine`; b.jg5 SRJ-1017); CSCB's own stuck launch with its abort still available goes to the own-launch slot (`PendingRowRuleDeps.ownLaunch`, filled by `createStuckLaunchAbort`) for the relaunching post and the abort ([CSCB's own stuck launch and its one abort](#cscbs-own-stuck-launch-and-its-one-abort-bjg5-srj-412)), whose answer (`PendingRowRelaunchAnswer`: sequence started, latched, or kept, with no held post that round) the round returns; otherwise the held text through its poster (`postHeld`, which calls `postStuckLaunchHeld` over the one episodes instance), its attach line dropped when the launch met a `send-keys` `ErrSpawnNotInteractive`. The row is left and never killed. The poster posts the held text at most once per stuck-launch episode, so later retries at B make the same round with no second post. A launch that is not CSCB's own, whether or not `ad-config-malformed` is raised, and CSCB's own once its episode's one abort is used (a relaunch still `pending` at B included) and `ad-config-malformed` is not raised, take the held branch; for CSCB's own, the held round line follows one earlier-abort skip line. The step's queries are asked in the order `tmux-unavailable`, latched, `ad-config-malformed`, then the abort.

**What a caller does with the answer.** The answer (`PendingRowRuleAnswer`) is a refusal with its reason, gone (a `DeadRowRead`), live, latched, read-refused, held or relaunch (the abort's `PendingRowRelaunchAnswer`). The pending-only retry maps it through `pendingStepOfRuleAnswer` (a relaunch's sequence started is `sequence-started`, its latched `latched`, its kept `kept`), the ladder through `ladderResultOfRuleAnswer` (`sequence-waiting`, `latched`, `no-op`), and the deferral answers gone for a gone answer and `'pending'` otherwise, a relaunch included; see each site above. A gone row is recovered by the restart path's decision, never by the rule.

**The rows it covers.** Every covered `pending` row: one left by a launch timeout; by a fresh spawn's launch failure other than "duplicate session" (the pending-only arm on `ErrTmuxSessionCreate`); by a "duplicate session" whose end write was not applied; by a failed `resume` or reuse whose row agent-director could not restore (HO rev 28), which keeps its failure's class (an `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` counted, an UNAVAILABLE or ENVIRONMENT outcome not, a CONFLICT latched); by a launch a server restart interrupted, or one found `pending` at startup; by a dialog approver stopped by GONE, `ErrSpawnNotInteractive`, `ErrTmuxNotAvailable`, B or the one-approver rule; a `pending` row beside a leftover of an earlier launch, which `find-missing` marks `missing` past G (reason `tmux_name_held`); a row whose create reply was lost and whose worker exited while another pane keeps its labelled session, which `find-missing` counts as gone, since no pane carries its launch's per-pane label (HO rev 18); and a row whose worker's SessionStart found no pane recorded within its wait and which agent-director ignored, which stays `pending` until its pane is adopted (HO rev 24, rev 25): its live pane keeps `find-missing` from marking it, and at B step 3 applies. A `pending` row whose persona's "conflicting labels" latch has just cleared by the re-check's lap `read-pane` (b.jg5 SRJ-506) is reached the same way: the after-clear retry at once, a run of the restart path's decision with no `find-missing` first, finds the row `pending` and arms P's retry timer, whose rule waits the row out; a retired key's row with no "new life has begun" mark starts the live-row sequence instead (b.jg5 SRJ-411) ([How a latch clears and relatches](#how-a-latch-clears-and-relatches-bjg5-srj-506-srj-1005)).

**A failed launch's row (b.jg5 SRJ-713).** The `ErrTmuxSessionCreate` and unapplied-end-write rows above (and a failed `resume`'s or reuse's left `pending`) are never CSCB's own: the failed call's window has no end (`launchCallWithWindow`), so `recordOwnLaunch` never sets the record and `isCscbOwnLaunch` answers false. The timer armed at once (`launchFailureResult`) runs the rule: nothing before G, the run from G, the one held post at B, never the relaunching post or the abort, never a kill. Once the row reads `missing`, the retry hands P to the restart path's decision, which brings P up with no kill. The pre-spawn scan's refusal leaves no row to wait out, and after "duplicate session" an ended row stays ended: a leftover's hooks never revive it.

**Cadence (AC 33).** The rule has no timer: it runs only inside a retry, at most once per retry, so its laps and runs are never closer together than the retry timer's interval (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_BASE_S`, 30 s, then doubling to `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CEILING_S`, 300 s; [UNAVAILABLE retry](#unavailable-retry-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305)). The one run at the approver's stop is exempt.

**The approver-stop run.** It follows only a stop in `APPROVER_STOPS_THAT_ARM` (`approverStopArmsPendingRow`): B or the test cap, GONE, not interactive, tmux unavailable, superseded, and a loop that threw (`failed`). It never follows shutdown, a latch, the retired-key recording, a teardown or the stuck-launch abort's own stop (`stuck-launch-abort`, whose kill and sequence follow instead), and needs the approver's last `status` read to have read `pending` with a launch start that parses. It is queued in P's lifecycle serializer turn (`PendingRowRuleInstall.serialize`, `personaLifecycle.run` in `main()`), not awaited by the approver, on that last read, with origin `approver-stop`. It runs as a recovery attempt of its own (`runDetachedRecoveryAttempt`, SRD hatch A2): its UNAVAILABLE arms the timer, a tmux-touching call's UNAVAILABLE starts `tmux-unresponsive`, and its UNCLASSIFIED opens P's unclassified-error episode. When its turn starts, a run after shutdown began is dropped with one line (`pendingRowRuleApproverStopDroppedLine`). It then checks the same gate as a retry's run: `retryRunGateStop` (`src/unavailable-retry.ts`) over the installed gate (`PendingRowRuleInstall.gate`, the one `retryRunGate` object `main()` both spreads into the retry action and passes to `setPendingRowRule`), in order shutdown, P not in the applied configuration (removed by a teardown queued ahead of it), latched, held on `ErrInvalidFlags`, not up, at the restart cap. A stop reason drops the run with one line (`pendingRowRuleApproverStopGatedLine`, the reason's `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_*` text) and no `read-pane`, Enter, `find-missing`, `get`, post or kill; a gate that throws drops it too (`pendingRowRuleApproverStopGateFailedWhy`), while a latched or held query that throws counts as latched or held. With no gate installed, only the shutdown drop applies. The rule's own gates follow. Its answer is logged in one line (`pendingRowRuleApproverStopLine`); a gone row is left to the timer the stop's arm armed.

**The timer keeps running.** A retry that runs the rule on a row it leaves `pending` answers a refusal and re-arms at the next wait, with `pending` as the last row read, so neither a lap's `read-pane` that ends `tmux-unresponsive` nor one that clears `tmux-unavailable` stops the timer ([UNAVAILABLE retry](#unavailable-retry-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305), **Condition ends**).

**Never over the row.** While a covered row reads `pending`, nothing launches over it or reuses it, and the rule kills nothing but CSCB's own stuck launch at B, once per episode, through its abort (below); the abort's sequence launches only after its kill and its own reads. The restart path's kill before its relaunch, made only after a `dead` reading of `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`, reads no row state and can still end such a row (b.jg5 SRJ-314; [Auto-Restart](#auto-restart)). While P is latched the rule makes no lap, run or kill. The latch re-check's own `read-pane` on a `pending` row is not this rule's: a "conflicting labels" latch's one-line lap read with `allow_pending`, which types nothing; and a latched `resume` or reuse whose row reads `pending` gets no probe, no retry and no post (HO rev 28; [The re-check](#the-re-check-bjg5-srj-505)). A stuck-launch abort kill's CONFLICT is never retried by it either.

Its log lines are under [Pending-row rule lines](#pending-row-rule-lines-bjg5-srj-410).

#### CSCB's own stuck launch and its one abort (b.jg5 SRJ-412)

CSCB ends only a launch it started and can prove is still the one it started. At B, step 3 of the pending-row rule sends such a launch to its own-launch slot, which `buildPendingRowRuleDeps` fills with one abort instance, `createStuckLaunchAbort` (`src/pending-row.ts`), bound to the session manager's entries. The abort makes the relaunching post, stops P's dialog approver, makes one checked kill and starts the live-row sequence at its second step. Every other `pending` row, and CSCB's own once its abort is used, takes the held branch ([The pending-row rule](#the-pending-row-rule-bjg5-srj-410), **Step 3**).

**The own-launch record.** The session manager keeps, per persona, one `OwnLaunchRecord` (the launch start in epoch ms and the launch call's window; `ownLaunchRecordOf(key)`), in memory beside the launch-in-flight state: the launch-call window, "this launch's row" and the not-interactive record ([A launch's window and the read after a timeout](#a-launchs-window-and-the-read-after-a-timeout-bjg5-srj-407)). `recordOwnLaunch` sets it only when the window is still the persona's latest launch call, has the expected end, and the launch start lies inside it (`isLaunchStartInWindow`, both ends included):

- **After a launch that returned success** (`LAUNCH_CALL_END_RETURNED`): at the dialog approver's first lap that keeps a launch start (`keepApproverLaunchStart`), against the window of the launch call that started the approver (`ApproverRun.launchWindow`, captured by `startDialogApprover`; an approver run directly takes the persona's latest window). A later launch call meanwhile makes that window stale, and nothing is recorded.
- **After a launch timeout** (`LAUNCH_CALL_END_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT`): in `afterLaunchUnavailable`, beside "this launch's row". An uncovered row may be recorded too; only step 3, which runs on a covered row, reads it.

It is never set for a failed read, a window with no end, a launch start outside the window or missing, or another process's launch. It outlives the approver. It is forgotten at a new launch call (`launchCallWithWindow`), and put back, with "this launch's row", when that call answers `ErrInstanceIdCollision` (`restoreLaunchRecords`; [A launch's window and the read after a timeout](#a-launchs-window-and-the-read-after-a-timeout-bjg5-srj-407)); it is forgotten at the teardown's kill (`forgetLaunchCalls`) and by `_resetInFlightLaunches`; no read forgets it, and a server restart loses it, so a launch a restart interrupted is never CSCB's own.

**The own-launch test.** `isCscbOwnLaunch(key, launchStart)` answers yes only when all of these hold, with the launch start this round's `get` read:

1. a record is kept;
2. the launch start equals the recorded one (`launchStartInstantOf`, either form), so the launch is unchanged;
3. no `send-keys` on the row answered `ErrSpawnNotInteractive` during that launch (`launchMetSendKeysNotInteractive`, R13; [The stuck-launch post](#the-stuck-launch-post-bjg5-srj-1017-srj-1016), **The not-interactive record**).

The fourth condition, not a relaunch already made in the same stuck-launch episode, is the abort's per-episode state (`isAbortAvailable`, below). The slot is reached only from step 3, so only a covered row is ever aborted.

**The abort's steps** (`relaunch`, reached only when step 3 found P's `tmux-unavailable` not raised, P not latched, the launch CSCB's own with its abort available and `ad-config-malformed` not raised):

1. An abort of P already in progress: nothing, with one skip line.
2. The relaunching post (`postStuckLaunchRelaunching` over the one episodes instance, B in effect at the post; [The stuck-launch post](#the-stuck-launch-post-bjg5-srj-1017-srj-1016)). `posted` and `already-posted` go on; `already-posted` is a later round's retry and posts nothing. `suppressed` (`tmux-unavailable`), `closed` (shutdown) and `failed` (an episodes call threw, or no episodes are installed) make no abort, with one skip line: no abort is made without the post, and the next round that reaches step 3 posts again, since no mark was set.
3. The per-episode state is made the first time and tied to the stuck-launch episode's close (`whenClosed`). No open episode, or an abort already used, makes nothing, with one skip line.
4. The started line, then the approver stop (`stopApproverForStuckLaunchAbort`, reason `stuck-launch-abort`; [Server-Managed Startup](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1) step 5, **The stuck-launch abort's stop**). No pending-row rule run follows that stop.
5. The latch and both outages are asked again, after the stop waited on the approver's call in progress: latched answers latched; `tmux-unavailable` or `ad-config-malformed` raised makes no kill, with one skip line (SRJ-316: no kill of a row read `pending` while agent-director refuses its config file).
6. The one checked kill (`abortKillOwnStuckLaunch`, below), then by its answer: a success logs the kill line and starts the sequence (`startStuckLaunchAbortSequence`); every other answer ends the round.

At most one abort of P runs at a time. Every answer but "sequence started" and latched is kept, and step 3 makes no held post in that round. The abort never rejects: a dependency that throws ends the round as kept, with its line.

**The abort's kill.** `abortKillOwnStuckLaunch(key, ref, options)` (`src/session-manager.ts`) takes the checked kill through the bounded retry (`retryPersonaKill`, [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104), **The bounded kill retry**): seeded `pending` (`killRetrySeedOfState`), so up to `KILL_RETRY_TRIES` (3) tries `KILL_RETRY_SPACING_MS` (2 s) apart on UNAVAILABLE, each tmux-touching, with the shared own-row `status` read between tries and the server's keep-going check, on the clock the builder is given (`killRetryWait`, default `KILL_RETRY_SYSTEM_CLOCK`). It sets none of `holdEnded`, `configReadEndsTries` or `goneIsFailure`, and it is not the restart path's one-try kill. Its site is `STUCK_LAUNCH_ABORT_SITE` (`pendingRowRule stuck-launch abort`). A CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME is latched through `latchOnKillOutcomeAt` (recorded `pending`, refused operation "P's next check or recovery" for CONFLICT; [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)). The alert the tries decided is raised after that through `raisePersonaKillFailureAlert` with `KILL_FAILURE_CONTEXT_STUCK_LAUNCH_ABORT` ([The kill-failure alert](#the-kill-failure-alert-bjg5-srj-704-srj-1007)). Classes are read through `src/ad-error-class.ts`. No delete and no launch is made inside the kill.

| Kill outcome | Answer | Abort used | What follows | Alert |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kill_sent` true, false or absent; the row or the session gone; a read between tries found the row finished | `succeeded` | Yes | The live-row sequence from step 2 (or kept, with why, when the start entry answers held, not installed, closed or already running) | The survivor version after a survivor-naming failure, else none |
| `ErrTmuxKillFailed` standing after tries no stop ended (all 3 used, or a CONFIG read between tries ended them) | `kill-failed` | Yes | Kept; the held text at the next retry that reaches step 3, once | The ordinary version, once |
| CONFLICT ("not this launch's session" included) | `latched` | Yes | P latched through the latch's CONFLICT entry with its one post; the kill is never tried again | The ordinary version only after a survivor-naming failure |
| UNUSABLE NAME | `latched` | Yes | P latched through the unusable-name entry | As above |
| A read between tries latched P, or tries stopped while P is latched | `latched` | Yes | Latched | The bounded retry's latched handling |
| Another UNAVAILABLE (`ErrTmuxUnresponsive`, `ErrCallTimeout`, …) | `try-later` | No | Kept; the same abort at the next retry that reaches step 3, with no second relaunching post (Q-12) | The ordinary version only after a survivor-naming failure |
| ENVIRONMENT (`ErrTmuxNotAvailable`, which raises `tmux-unavailable`) | `try-later` | No | Kept; step 3 makes nothing until the outage clears, then the same abort | As above |
| CONFIG (which raises `ad-config-malformed`) | `try-later` | No | Kept; step 3 and the abort's own re-check hold it until the outage clears | As above |
| UNCLASSIFIED and the unlisted classes | `try-later` | No | Kept; the same abort at the next step 3 | As above |
| Tries stopped by SRJ-702's stop rule (P not up, torn down, shutdown), P not latched | `stopped` | No | Kept; once P is up, the next retry that reaches step 3 makes the same abort with no second post | Neither version; the stop's one line, or a `persona-kill-failed` entry when P was removed |
| `ErrInvalidFlags` whose version re-check stops the server | `stopped` | No | Kept | The version re-check's stop handling |

`stuckLaunchAbortKillUsesAbort` answers which answers use the abort. The ENVIRONMENT and CONFIG answers arm P's retry timer with their causes through the outage wrapper, as from any verb.

**The sequence.** After a successful kill, `startStuckLaunchAbortSequence` starts the live-row sequence through the start entry (`startLiveRowSequence`; [The live-row sequence](#the-live-row-sequence-bjg5-srj-705-srj-717)): entry at step 2 (`LIVE_ROW_SEQUENCE_ENTRY_GET`), seeded `pending`, the conversation kept, ending in a launch, alert context `stuck-launch abort`, `isStartup` false. A row with a session id ends in a `resume` of the same session, which keeps the conversation; any other ends in a reuse spawn. The sequence runs detached as its own recovery attempt. A pending-only retry answers it as `live-row-sequence-started`, and the restart path's deferral as its `pending`.

**The episode and its one abort (SRJ-1016).** The per-episode state (`used`, `inProgress`) lives in the abort instance and is disposed when the stuck-launch episode closes: on a read of the row live out of `pending`, a latch, P's teardown or shutdown. A kill and a read of `pending`, `ended` or `missing` do not end the episode, so the relaunch stays in the same episode. The relaunch's own approver records it as CSCB's own, but the abort is used: still `pending` at its B, it gets the held text once (`isAbortAvailable` answers false, a pure query that logs nothing; step 3's held branch logs the earlier-abort skip line just before its round line) and is never killed. A new episode has its abort again. `isAbortUsed(key)` reads the state for tests.

**The gates.** At most one abort per episode, made only from step 3. None while P's `tmux-unavailable` or `ad-config-malformed` outage is raised, or while P is latched: step 3 checks each first, and the abort checks the latch and both outages again after its approver stop. While `ad-config-malformed` is raised, CSCB's own stuck launch gets neither text and no abort, whether or not its abort is used (SRJ-1017), with one `stuckLaunchPostSkippedLine` per round; any other `pending` row keeps its held post. Once the outage clears, an own launch with its abort available gets the relaunching post and the abort, and one whose abort is used gets the held text once.

**A wedged tmux (SRJ-717).** A kill that answered success while tmux was slow can leave a session that shows up late. The sequence's second kill (step 4) catches it. A sequence run that does not judge the row stops that sequence with no alert and no counted failure, and arms the not-judged cause.

**Part of an attempt (hatch A2).** The abort runs inside the rule's round: at a retry, inside that retry's attempt, and at the approver's stop, inside that run's own recovery attempt. So its kill's standing UNAVAILABLE arms P's timer once, a tmux-touching UNAVAILABLE starts `tmux-unresponsive`, and an UNCLASSIFIED opens P's unclassified-error episode.

Its log lines are under [Stuck-launch abort lines](#stuck-launch-abort-lines-bjg5-srj-412).

### Health-Check Poller

A periodic backstop that runs alongside the reactive disconnect path. It catches three failure modes that the reactive `onsessionclosed` path misses: (a) sessions that die without triggering a close event (e.g., an externally-killed tmux session); (b) sessions that are alive but MCP-disconnected — an AD live-state row (`waiting` etc.) whose MCP transport is gone, read alive yet unreachable; and (c) connected-but-streamless sessions (b.9cj) — read alive and `isSessionConnected === true` in the registry, but the SDK has silently dropped the `_GET_stream` map entry, so messages cannot reach the bot. Without (c) an idle streamless session would stay broken forever, invisible to the reactive path. The tick recovers all three.

On each tick:

1. **Persona iteration** — for each persona key / working-directory pair from `HealthCheckDeps.getPersonas()` (production: `buildPersonaWorkList(personaConfig, canRelaunch)`, one entry per applied persona however many channels it lists, rebuilt every tick). The relaunch gate leaves out every persona that is not up: its bring-up is `broken` or `retrying`, or its Slack connection is not serving (never brought up, connecting, retrying its bring-up, broken or stopped). A persona a confirmed apply removed is absent too: the list is built from `personaConfig` (see the applied-set guard under Server-Managed Startup step 5). Such a persona is absent from the whole tick: no `cwd-unreachable` update, no reconnect and no relaunch, including a persona that was launched and whose connection later broke or stopped. A directory-broken persona's directory is therefore watched only by its bring-up retry, never by this tick. It rejoins the tick once it is up. The gate's one line per persona per state is described under Auto-Restart step 5. Every guard call, the disconnected streak and the `cwd-unreachable` outage flag are keyed by persona key (b.av2 SR-6.3); log lines name it as `persona=<key>`, e.g. `[slack] health-check: persona=<key> is at cap — skipping tick (SR-25.3/25.4)`:
   - **Skip if restart pending/active** — `isRestartPendingOrActive(key)` returns true: the restart owns the session. Checked first; the persona is skipped before any read, silently, and its streak is cleared.
   - **Skip if at failure cap** — checked second: `isAtCap(key, RESTART_FAILURE_CAP)` (injected as `HealthCheckDeps.isAtCap`) returns true; a persona at the consecutive-failure cap is skipped this tick before any read (SR-25.3/25.4), with its streak cleared and the line `[slack] health-check: persona=<key> is at cap — skipping tick (SR-25.3/25.4)`, including the alive-but-disconnected reconnect path — a capped persona gets no tick-driven reconnect. The cap is checked before the in-flight predicate, so a capped persona with a launch in flight logs this line too. The inbound drop branch likewise detects the cap and declines to fire a restart, so a **server restart** is the only path back — it clears the in-process counter and gives the persona a fresh attempt.
   - **No-attempt reason (b.jg5 SRJ-315)** — decided once per persona per tick, after the two skips and before any read (`noAttemptReason`, the first that holds): `latched` when `HealthCheckDeps.isLatched(key)` answers exactly `true` (b.jg5 SRJ-502; production binds the server's latch's `isLatched`; a human decides for a latched persona, and only its re-check makes a call for it, see [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)), `held` when `HealthCheckDeps.isHeld(key)` answers exactly `true` (b.jg5 SRJ-207; production binds the server's `ErrInvalidFlags` hold's `isHeld`; nothing is launched for a held persona until the binary changes, the server restarts or it is torn down, and its hold stopped its retry timer, see [The `ErrInvalidFlags` hold](#the-errinvalidflags-hold-bjg5-srj-207-srj-1008)), `in-flight` when `HealthCheckDeps.isLaunchInFlight(key)` answers true, or `tmux-unavailable` when the persona's `tmux-unavailable` outage is raised (`getOutageFlags`). In flight means anything in flight for the persona, read through the server's "in flight for P" binding (`isPersonaWorkInFlight` in `main()`), which the session-disconnect handler's `tmux-unavailable` check and the lost-message routing's read gate (`isWorkInFlight`, [Inbound](#inbound-slack--claude-code) step 7) share. It is built from the UNAVAILABLE retry timer's "blocks a retry" binding (`isPersonaRetryBlocked`), so the tick never attempts over work that holds back the retry timer, but not the reverse: a running dialog approver is in flight for the tick and never blocks a retry (b.jg5 SRJ-303, SRJ-401). It is a launch call (the session manager's `isLaunchInFlight`: a start launch parked while it waits for a `working` row, a launch after a bring-up retry, or a restart's launch; the launch owns the session, and its wait reconnects the persona or reports it), a running live-row sequence (the session manager's `isLiveRowSequenceRunning`, b.jg5 SRJ-706: the sequence owns the row until it settles; it is also in "blocks a retry"), an old-life wait step running for a hold the persona waits on (`isOldLifeWaitRunningFor`, b.jg5 SRJ-811; also in "blocks a retry", [The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809)) or the persona's running dialog approver (`isDialogApproverRunning`), which works on the `pending` row after its launch call returned. While `tmux-unavailable` is raised, the retry timer retries on its backoff, one per interval (a lost message or a session disconnect schedules no restart then; a disconnect with no timer armed arms one, as does a lost message below the restart cap, as this tick does, unless the persona is latched or work is in flight for it; see ENVIRONMENT under the UNAVAILABLE retry timer). With a reason, the persona is not skipped: the working-directory check runs and its liveness, connection and stream are read as below. A `live` persona, connected and with its stream, takes the healthy branch (step 4), so a persona that recovered on its own ends its not-connected episode and its `tmux-unresponsive` condition and clears `tmux-unavailable`. An `unknown` reading takes step 2 as usual. Any other reading (`dead`, `pending`, disconnected or streamless) clears the persona's streak: no `scheduleRestart`, no not-connected notice and, for `latched`, `held` and `in-flight`, no line and no arm. For `tmux-unavailable` that reading also arms a missing retry timer (`armMissingRetryTimer`, b.jg5 SRJ-311). Because the reason was decided before the tick awaited its reads, it is checked again (`noAttemptReason`) when arming: nothing is armed unless it is still `tmux-unavailable`, so a flag cleared during those reads (by a teardown's reset or a real clear) or a launch gone in flight meanwhile arms nothing and logs no arming line. Then, when `HealthCheckDeps.isRetryArmed(key)` answers exactly `false`, the tick logs `[slack] health-check: persona=<key> has its tmux-unavailable outage raised with no retry timer — arming one` and calls `HealthCheckDeps.armRetryTimer(key)` (production: the retry controller's `arm` with the `environment` cause, `UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_CAUSE_ENVIRONMENT`), whose own line follows (`[slack] unavailable-retry: persona=<key> armed (environment) — first retry in 30 s`). The tick still makes no attempt of its own: the timer's retry is the persona's attempt. This is needed because a raised flag does not guarantee a timer. A retry that stops as `not-up`, on a declined launch (`launch-skipped`) or because its run failed (`UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_RUN_FAILED`) leaves the flag raised, and only tmux answering clears it (a successful `status` read does not), so without this arm the persona would have no attempt at all and could stay dead indefinitely. Nothing is armed when the persona is healthy (the healthy branch clears the flag instead), when the reading is `unknown` (step 2), when the reason is `latched`, `held` or `in-flight` (all are checked before `tmux-unavailable` and win), when a timer is already armed, waiting or running, or when either member is absent (`isRetryArmed` absent, or answering anything but `false`, never arms: arming over a pending-only timer would switch it to full mode). The arm happens at most once per persona per tick, and only for a persona in the work list (up, not capped, no restart pending or active); a timer armed for a persona that is not up, not applied or at the cap by its first retry stops there through the pre-call checks, with no agent-director call. A predicate that throws ends the persona's work for the tick before any read, through the per-persona catch (`[slack] health-check: error checking persona=<key>: <error>`); one that throws at the arm-time check is logged the same way, and nothing is armed. The tick has no other no-attempt reason. Only `latched` is asked again, right after the tick's own liveness read (`latchedAfterRead`), since that read may latch the persona (an UNUSABLE_NAME answer, b.jg5 SRJ-512); the tick then schedules nothing for it.
   - **Working-directory check** — `statRoute(cwd)` on the persona's working directory clears `cwd-unreachable` for the persona when it exists and raises it otherwise.
   - **Liveness check** — `isSessionAlive(key)`, the adapter of Auto-Restart step 3, answers `live`, `pending`, `dead` or `unknown` with the same mapping; a probe that throws, or answers something that is not a reading, reads `unknown`. `live` and `pending` are read alive, but only `live` is ever counted healthy (b.jg5 SRJ-314): a `pending` row's session has not started. `isSessionConnected(key)` (b.9a7, wraps the same registry-`connected` adapter used by restart.ts) reports whether the MCP session is currently connected. `hasSessionStream(key)` (b.9cj, wraps the shared `getSessionByPersona` → `hasGetStreamKey(transport)` probe wired into both `HealthCheckDeps` and `RestartDeps`) reports whether the standalone `_GET_stream` is present.
2. **Liveness unknown (C12, b.jg5 SRJ-314)** — on `unknown` agent-director could not report on the persona, which is never read as dead. The tick logs one line and skips the persona for this tick: no restart scheduled, nothing posted and no episode ended. The tick runs outside every attempt, so its read arms the retry timer only for an ENVIRONMENT answer (`ErrTmuxNotAvailable`, which also raises `tmux-unavailable`; b.jg5 SRJ-311) or a CONFIG answer (`ErrConfigMalformed`, which also raises `ad-config-malformed`; b.jg5 SRJ-316), through the liveness adapter's own report. Its disconnected streak is cleared, as every skip clears it, so an `unknown` tick neither builds toward a restart nor proves the persona healthy.
3. **Dead session** — only on `dead`, and only with no no-attempt reason (step 1), `scheduleRestart(key, cwd)` is called at once, delegating to the same restart path used by `onsessionclosed`.
4. **Alive but not deliverable** — with no no-attempt reason (step 1), if the reading is `live` or `pending` but the session is either not connected (`!isSessionConnected`, b.9a7) **or** connected-but-streamless (`!hasSessionStream`, b.9cj), or the reading is `pending` with the session connected and its stream present, the tick tracks a per-persona consecutive-failing streak and calls `scheduleRestart(key, cwd)` only once the streak reaches **two consecutive ticks**. All these cases land in this branch and share the one streak/debounce, which suppresses the freshly-launched false positive: a booting session that connects (and re-opens its stream) between ticks is never poked. A connected-with-stream `pending` row is never healthy and never scheduled as dead: after the streak, the restart run it schedules hands it to the `pending` deferral (Auto-Restart step 3). Observing the persona as fully healthy — `live`, connected, AND stream present — (or dead) resets/consumes the streak. A tick that skips the persona clears it too: a restart pending or active, the cap, a no-attempt reason with any reading but healthy (step 1), a liveness reading of `unknown` (step 2), or the relaunch gate leaving it out of the tick's work list (not up), so a persona that comes back up starts a fresh count. `_resetHealthCheckState` clears the whole map. `restart.ts` then defers a `pending` row whatever its connection shows, reconnects a `live`-but-disconnected row (deferring a `working` row while a launch for it is in flight or the positive-idle rule has not shown it stale, never typing into a prompt or a running turn, and typing nothing on a failed status call, per Auto-Restart step 3), recovers a streamless one, or relaunches a dead one. This gives time-bounded recovery on the `health_check_interval` (default 120 s) even for idle personas that receive no inbound traffic.
   - **Two-tick exception (b.f2b).** While the reconnect adapter holds an idle run for the persona's `working` row that one more attempt can conclude (`HealthCheckDeps.hasPendingWorkingRowEvidence`, production `hasPendingWorkingRowEvidence`), the tick calls `scheduleRestart` on the first undeliverable tick. Each attempt makes one evidence read, so the next read comes one tick sooner. It never applies to a booting session: any launch for the persona forgets the run first. A prompt run doesn't count.
   - **Delay 0: the not-connected notice (b.f2b).** With `session_restart_delay` 0, `scheduleRestart` only logs `Auto-restart disabled (delay=0)` and returns, so nothing would reconnect the persona. When `HealthCheckDeps.isAutoRestartDisabled()` is true, the tick therefore also calls `HealthCheckDeps.notifyNotConnected(key, cause)` (production `notifyDisconnectedWithAutoRestartDisabled`) right after `scheduleRestart` in this branch: the `auto-restart-disabled` not-connected notice through `notifyPersonaNotConnected`, worded by `cause`, which the tick takes from the same `isSessionConnected` answer the branch used: *Not connected* (`disconnected`, cause `its connection has been down on two health checks in a row`) or *Not receiving messages* (`streamless`, `found on two health checks in a row`). A `pending` row connected with its stream gets no notice: it is neither disconnected nor streamless, so either wording would be false. A disconnected or streamless `pending` row gets it as a `live` one does. A persona with a no-attempt reason (step 1) never gets it, since the tick makes no attempt for it. One latch covers every notice text, so a notice already raised in the episode by the launch wait, a prompt report or an `unproven-idle` report counts for it. The dead branch (step 3) raises none.
   - **Healthy: the episode ends (b.f2b).** A tick that finds the persona `live`, connected and with its stream also calls `HealthCheckDeps.endNotConnectedEpisode(key)` (production `forgetNotConnectedEpisode`), as registration (`handleInitialized`) and the teardown do: the latch and the restart path's idle evidence are forgotten, so a later episode is reported again.
   - **Healthy: the tmux-unresponsive condition ends (b.jg5 SRJ-310).** The same branch calls `HealthCheckDeps.endTmuxUnresponsive(key)`, which production binds to the condition's end with reason `tick` and the reading `live`: a condition that holds ends and reaches the retry timer's condition-end entry; one that does not hold is left alone. A `pending`, `unknown` or `dead` reading, or a session that is disconnected or streamless, never ends it ([The tmux-unresponsive condition](#the-tmux-unresponsive-condition-bjg5-srj-307-srj-310)).
   - **Healthy: `tmux-unavailable` clears (b.jg5 SRJ-311, SRJ-312).** Right after, the same branch clears the persona's `tmux-unavailable` outage (`clearOutageFlag` with the reading `live`), with its all-clear when that empties the persona's flags. A real clear reaches the retry timer's condition-end entry through the cleared-flag observer (the `outage-state.ts` entry of the Module Map). It is the tick's only clear of the flag: the liveness read itself never clears it, and no other reading, and no disconnected or streamless session, does.
   - **Healthy: the slow-recovery count resets (b.jg5 SRJ-610).** Last, the same branch calls `HealthCheckDeps.resetSlowRecoveryCount(key)`, which production binds to the slow-recovery tracker's `noteHealthy`: the persona's slow-recovery count resets (logging `[slack] slow-recovery: persona=<key> count reset from <n> — a health check found the session live, connected and with its stream` only when it was above 0), and an open slow-recovery episode stays open. A throw is the persona's error for the tick (logged). Absent, nothing is called. See Auto-Restart step 3, **Slow recovery**.
5. **The tmux-unresponsive onset (b.jg5 SRJ-308)** — the tick reads its start time (`HealthCheckDeps.now`, the notice episodes' clock in production) before any of its work, and once the body ends, after all of the per-persona work and however it ends (a `finally`), calls `HealthCheckDeps.onTickEnd(tickStartedAt)` (production: the condition's `onsetAtTick(tickStartedAt)`). That check posts the *Not answering* onset for every condition still holding whose first refusal is strictly before the tick's start, a persona the tick skipped, made no attempt for (step 1) or left out included: it does not depend on any attempt, and makes no agent-director call; a condition the tick ended no longer holds, so a persona the tick found recovered gets nothing. A hook that throws is logged and changes nothing else. The tick captures its deps once, as it starts, and reads its start time and calls its end hook on those, so an `initHealthCheck` that swaps the deps mid-tick never pairs one deps' clock with another's hook. A throw outside the per-persona work (e.g. `getPersonas`) ends the body at its `catch`, which logs `[slack] health-check: the tick failed: <error>` (`describeThrownValue`) and never rethrows, so no unhandled rejection escapes the interval callback; the `finally` still runs the tick-end hook and resets the in-flight flag. A tick skipped because the previous one is still running, or during shutdown, and a tick whose start time could not be read, do not call it ([Its three posts](#its-three-posts-bjg5-srj-308-srj-309-srj-1006)).

The interval is controlled by `health_check_interval` in `config.json`. If the value is `0`, `startHealthCheck()` returns immediately and no interval is created; this stops only the health check, not the runtime version re-check, which runs every 120 s on its own timer (Server-Managed Startup step 1), nor the re-read of agent-director's timing settings, which runs after each of that re-check's timed ticks that did not stop (Server-Managed Startup step 2b), nor the UNAVAILABLE retry timer, whose retries run on their own schedule when `health_check_interval` is 0 too (Auto-Restart, [UNAVAILABLE retry](#unavailable-retry-bjg5-srj-303-srj-305)), nor a latched persona's re-check, every 120 s on its own timer ([The re-check](#the-re-check-bjg5-srj-505)). `stopHealthCheck()` clears the interval during graceful shutdown, before `cancelAllRestartTimers()` runs.

**Ordering invariant**: `startHealthCheck()` is called only after `startupSessionManager()` returns, which is once every persona has a bring-up outcome and every `up` persona's start launch has settled or been parked waiting for a `working` row (b.f2b). Moving it earlier in the startup sequence would risk the poller racing with in-progress start launches. A parked launch stays in flight until it settles, and the tick makes no attempt for a persona with work in flight (the "in flight for P" binding; it still reads it), so the poller never races it either. Bring-up retries that finish later don't delay it; their launches go through `spawnForPersona`'s one-launch-in-flight guard, which a restart the tick triggers also respects.

**Ordering invariant (reload detection)**: `reload.startDetection()` is called right after `startHealthCheck()`, for the same reason, and the controller itself refuses to arm the tick before the start bring-up pass has returned. The held credentials digests the tick compares against exist only once each persona's bring-up has read its file. A parked start launch doesn't hold the tick back: its bring-up has read its credentials, and a teardown of that persona cancels the launch's wait and waits for it to settle (b.f2b).

### Reload Detection Tick (b.av2 SR-8.2, SR-8.3)

The reload controller (`src/reload.ts`) notices edits to `config.json` and to the credentials files it references, and keeps `config.json.pending` in step with them. It also processes the operator's confirmation, `config.json.apply`, and applies a confirmed change (see [Confirmation](#confirmation-sr-85) and [The apply pipeline](#the-apply-pipeline-sr-86-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-805)). Only that apply writes the record, swaps the applied set or calls a lifecycle operation (the teardowns of step 2 and the bring-ups of step 6); its step 1 also writes the retired-key record and the stored-choice file. A detection pass reads neither of those. Detection itself creates no Slack client; a bring-up at apply does, through the connection manager.

Each pass runs in this order: derive the pending state from the files, process `config.json.apply` against it, derive the state again if the apply changed what is applied, then refresh the pending file (write it, or delete it) against that state. So a confirmation is always processed before the pending state is refreshed.

#### The timer

One serialized, self-re-arming 5 s `setTimeout` chain (`createReloadTickDriver`, `src/reload-timer.ts`), in the `cron-scheduler.ts` pattern, never `setInterval`. The next pass is armed only once the previous one has settled, 5 s after its end, so passes never overlap. There is no file watcher; each pass reads the files afresh.

`startDetection()` arms it once, after an applied start's bring-up pass returns (Server-Managed Startup step 9). A start launch the pass parked while it waits for a `working` row (b.f2b) may still be in flight then. SR-8.2's intent holds: every persona's bring-up has read its credentials, so the digests the tick compares against exist, and an apply that tears that persona down cancels the launch's wait and then waits for it to settle (`whenLaunchSettled`). `start` runs nothing itself, so the first pass runs 5 s after it. `stopDetection()` at graceful shutdown stops the driver and makes any pass still due do nothing. `stop()` is idempotent. The driver is single-use; a second `start`, or a `start` after `stop`, is logged and ignored. A pass that throws past the controller's own catch is logged by the driver (see the Reload lines table) and the chain re-arms. Nothing is armed or logged at import or construction.

#### What a pass reads

Each pass reads `config.json` once, stat-first through `readPersonaConfigBytes`, so a FIFO or device never blocks it. Unless in dry run, it then reads every distinct `credentials_file` the file names (`referencedCredentialsPaths`, parsed tolerantly, so an invalid file still names its paths) once each, through `readCredentialsFile`. It then reads `config.json.apply`, and finally `config.json.pending`. Each of these files is read once, stat-first and capped (see [Size cap](#reload-files-configjsonlast-applied-configjsonpending-configjsonapply)). The credentials bytes are dropped at the end of the pass. The preview needs a few more facts, gathered with the least extra I/O (see [The change plan](#the-change-plan-sr-86-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-203-sri-802)).

#### When a change is pending (SR-8.3)

A change is pending when either holds:

- **The configuration changed**: the bytes of `config.json` differ from the applied bytes (the record's at a start from the record).
- **Credentials changed**: the change plan lists at least one credentials-changed persona. It is the only place this is decided. Such a persona is present in both the applied set and a valid candidate, with an unchanged `credentials_file` path (by real path) and no destructive change, and has a file whose digest (`credentialsDigest`) differs from the one its bring-up holds, which is the content it connected with, is retrying with or broke with. Only digests are compared, and they are held in memory only, never written to disk. A persona that holds no digest never counts, as in dry run. A persona broken by a credentials file another applied persona shares (an SR-1.5 record-start collision; b.av2 SR-1.5 as amended by b.deo SRI-104) holds the digest of its own path's bytes, read stat-first and hashed, never parsed, with no token used. Re-saving that file with different bytes therefore makes a change pending for it. This is how the remaining persona recovers once a confirmed apply removes the collision by changing the other persona: its own declaration is unchanged, so nothing else would re-check it. While the collision stands, such a pending change can't bring either persona up.

The candidate is what a confirmation would apply. Changed bytes are validated in default mode, so a real-path collision is a validation error there; a validation failure is an `INVALID` candidate carrying the loader's message. A missing or unreadable `config.json` while a record exists is also an `INVALID` candidate. Personas added, removed or with a changed `credentials_file` path are configuration changes, not credentials changes.

In dry run no credentials file is read, and credentials never count as changed.

After a start from the record, the first pass is the SR-8.7 comparison (as amended by b.deo SRI-403, SRI-407): an edit made before the start differs from the record, so it stays pending and the pending file is written after the start.

#### The fingerprint

The pending state is identified by its fingerprint (`reloadFingerprint`, `src/reload-fingerprint.ts`). It is a SHA-256 over the configuration file's bytes plus, for each referenced credentials file in declaration order, its path and its bytes or a missing/unreadable marker. A missing or unreadable `config.json` contributes a marker and no credentials entries. In dry run it covers the configuration file alone.

#### The pending file lifecycle

`config.json.pending` exists only while a change is pending. Its first line is a fixed header (`claude-slack-channel-bots: pending configuration change (written by the server)`), its second `fingerprint: sha256:<64 hex>`, then a blank line and the preview body.

- **Pending.** The file is written through the durable write (`durableWriteFileSync`) whenever it is missing or its bytes differ from what this pass would write, without a log line. The preview is logged only when the logged state changes: from nothing pending, or to a different fingerprint. So a rewrite with the same fingerprint logs nothing, even when the preview text changed because a fact did (an added persona's working directory was created, say). The log form is under [The preview in the log](#the-preview-in-the-log).
- **Nothing pending.** The file is deleted through the durable delete (`durableUnlinkSync`). Once it is actually gone, `reload-nothing-pending` is logged once, when the state changes from pending to nothing (a revert) or when the first pass after a start actually removes a leftover pending file. It is never logged at a clean start, and a first pass that finds no file logs nothing. The line has two variants: when this pass removed the file it ends `…; no change is pending, and the pending-change file "<pending>" is removed`; when there was no file to remove (for example it had never been written, or was deleted by hand) it ends `…; no change is pending`. A pending file placed by hand while nothing is pending is deleted without a line.

#### The change plan (SR-8.6 as amended by b.deo SRI-203, SRI-802)

Every pass builds one change plan (`buildChangePlan`, `src/reload-plan.ts`) of the candidate against the applied configuration. The preview, the log lines, the pending decision and a confirmed apply all come from it (the apply uses the plan of the pass that matched the confirmation, see [The apply pipeline](#the-apply-pipeline-sr-86-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-805)), so what is applied is what was previewed. Personas are matched by key; a `name` edit that changes the key is a removal plus an addition.

| Class | A persona present in both, or a setting, when… | Effect stated |
|---|---|---|
| Added | its key is only in the candidate | brought up and launched, or why it cannot come up |
| Removed | its key is only in the applied set | `DESTRUCTIVE:` the persona will be retired: its session stopped and never resumed (b.jg5 SRJ-1510; b.jg5 SRJ-1511 as amended by b.deo SRI-406) |
| Destructively modified | `name` (same key), `credentials_file` or `working_directory` changed; paths compared by real path | `DESTRUCTIVE:` the persona will be retired and brought up fresh: its session stopped and never resumed (b.jg5 SRJ-1510; b.jg5 SRJ-1511 as amended by b.deo SRI-406, SRI-502). Listed in no other class |
| Modified in place | a setting of the candidate's section in force changed (`channelModeOf(candidate)`, never the applied mode; b.deo SRI-802). With the switch unchanged, the section is compared by resolved values: in declarative mode the set of channel IDs (`channels`), a kept channel's mode (`delivery`) and `permission_prompts`, a channel reorder being no change; in fungible mode `invited.permission_prompts` by its resolved value (`fungible_destination`), so an absent one equals `dm`. Across a switch change, the keys of the section the switch turns on are compared as written (`sections`), and a changed one is an in-place change of `channels`, `permission_prompts` or `invited.permission_prompts`. `dm.enabled` and `dm.contact` in both modes | applied in place immediately, instance kept |
| Recorded | a key of the section not in force by the candidate's switch (`RECORDED_SECTION_KEYS`: `channels` and `permission_prompts` in fungible mode, `invited` in declarative mode) changed, compared as written (`plan.recorded`; b.deo SRI-804) | recorded, with no effect until the switch selects that section; counts in no header term and goes into no apply step. A persona whose only changes are recorded is unchanged; a destructive modify gets no recorded entry, and a persona can be both modified in place and recorded |
| Changed credentials | same `credentials_file` by real path, and its current digest differs from the held one (see above); never in dry run or with nothing held | by the bring-up state and `problem` (see below): up, a new connection opens, then the old one closes; retrying, it retries with the new content; broken by its credentials now (`isCredentialsBroken`: outcome `broken` with a local credentials cause, or with Slack's refusal, `persona-credentials-refused`), it is brought up. With a `problem`, an up persona keeps its current connection, a retrying one keeps retrying with its current content and a credentials-broken one stays broken |
| Next launch | `claude_config_dir` (by real path) or `stop_hook_bootstrap` changed. It is inherited when the top-level default changed and the persona's value equalled the old default before and the new default after; otherwise it is the persona's own | takes effect at its next launch, instance kept; for `claude_config_dir`, that launch starts a new conversation: the row is replaced by a reuse spawn of the same id, with no row deleted (the conversation is not resumed; SR-6.2 as amended, b.jg5 SRJ-1504) |
| Switch | `allow_invited_channels` changed (absent and `false` are equal; `MODE_SWITCH_SETTING`), carried in `plan.settings` as `{ name, mode, personas }`, the mode it turns on and the personas present in both configurations (b.deo SRI-803) | applied in place at once, at the step-1 swap (`configInEffect`), from the next event, tool call, prompt and notice; on its own it puts no persona in any apply step, so every session is kept (b.deo SRI-203) |
| Server-wide setting | any other top-level key's resolved value changed (path settings by real path) | once applied, recorded and effective at the next server start after that; `stop_timeout` and `exit_timeout`, which only the CLI uses, are taken by the CLI from the record once applied; `agent_director_call_timeout_ms` is taken by the CLI from the record once applied and used by the running server from its next start |
| Inherited default | top-level `claude_config_dir` or `stop_hook_bootstrap` changed | lists the personas present in both, not destructively modified, whose value changes through it; takes effect at each one's next launch (a new conversation for `claude_config_dir`). With no such persona: recorded, no instance affected |

A credentials change's `problem` is why the new content is not locally valid (missing, unreadable, bad shape or prefix). For a persona that is up, the apply's credentials step (step 4) then keeps the current connection and logs `persona-credentials-change-failed`; a retrying persona keeps retrying with its current content; a credentials-broken persona stays broken. The preview's `problem` is only a forecast: step 4 checks the file again when it runs (see [Credentials change](#credentials-change-bav2-sr-86-step-4-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-805)). A persona may be both modified in place, next-launch and credentials-changed. Anything else present in both is unchanged. `no effective change` holds when every persona is unchanged and no server-wide setting changed: a whitespace or key-order edit, a key added with its default value (`allow_invited_channels: false` included), or recorded changes only (`noEffectiveChange` ignores `plan.recorded`).

The plan also carries `configDirsChanged`: whether the set of effective config directories (`effectiveClaudeConfigDirs`) differs between the applied and the candidate personas, so the apply knows to refresh the agent-director template (SR-8.6 step 5 as amended by b.deo SRI-805; see [Template refresh](#template-refresh-bav2-sr-86-step-5-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-805)). The apply selects step 5 whenever `configDirsChanged` is true, even for a plan with `no effective change` (`applyStepsFor`) (a `claude_config_dir` moved to another path that is a symlink to the same directory changes no persona but does change the template). It is compared lexically, not by real path, because the template's memory-read rules are written from the lexical paths; it is not rendered in the preview. An invalid plan carries `false`.

How the pass gathers the plan's facts:

- **Real paths**: `resolveRealPath`, memoized per pass, called only when the two path strings differ.
- **Credentials digests**: from the reads the fingerprint already made; none in dry run.
- **Bring-up state**: the injected `bringUpState`, asked only for a credentials-changed persona. It sets the change's `credentialsBroken` (`isCredentialsBroken`) and `retrying` (outcome `retrying`, or no outcome yet because its first Slack attempt is in flight). A persona held for its `claude_config_dir` (bug b.g57) is `retrying` with no connection, so its line says it retries with the new content.
- **Credentials problem**: `credentialsReadProblem` over the bytes the fingerprint already read (none in dry run), asked only for a credentials-changed persona. It becomes the change's `problem`: a token-free cause such as `credentials file does not exist` or `credentials file is invalid: …`.
- **Added personas**: `credentialsReadProblem` over the bytes already read (skipped in dry run, so the preview then gives no credentials cause), `checkPersonaWorkingDirectory` with no other personas (a valid candidate has no real-path collision), then the injected `checkConfigDir` (production: `checkLaunchConfigDir`, wired in `server.ts`), whose failure's `problem` is the cause: `claude_config_dir cannot be resolved to a real path (<errno>)`, with `: a symlink on its path points to nothing` after the errno for a dangling symlink. A directory not created yet under an existing ancestor passes. All three checks run, so one failure never hides another, and the causes are listed in that order. These are the local steps 1 and 2 of the SR-6.1 bring-up plus the `claude_config_dir` check the bring-up runs before step 3; no Slack call is made, so a token Slack would refuse is not detected. An unchanged persona is not probed.
- **Changed claude_config_dir** (bug b.g57): the same injected `checkConfigDir`, asked by the plan (`configDirProblem`) only for a persona present in both whose effective `claude_config_dir` changed (its own, through a changed top-level default, or alongside a destructive modify), with the candidate's declaration. Its `problem` becomes the change's `configDirUnresolvable`, and the line warns: a confirmed change is still applied, and the persona is then held at its next launch (at the confirmation, for a destructive modify) until the directory resolves, as the `persona-config-dir-unresolvable` hold does. A directory not created yet under an existing ancestor passes.

A fact that cannot be gathered (the bring-up state query, an added persona's checks or a changed `claude_config_dir`'s check throw) is carried as unknown (`FACT_UNKNOWN`), and the preview says so rather than claiming either answer: the added persona `is added; whether it can come up could not be checked.`, the changed `claude_config_dir` `…; whether it can come up at that launch could not be checked` (for inheriting personas `whether "<name>" (key=<key>), … can come up at that launch could not be checked`, on a `DESTRUCTIVE:` line `whether it can come up could not be checked`), the credentials-changed persona `…; whether it is broken by its credentials now could not be checked` (after `…, but it cannot be used (<cause>)` when the content is bad). The header counts are unchanged. It is logged once, and the latch re-arms after a pass that gathers every fact.

#### The preview (SR-8.4 as amended by b.deo SRI-803, SRI-804)

The preview body sits after the header and fingerprint lines and the blank line. Its `DESTRUCTIVE:` lines use the retired wording of b.jg5 SRJ-1510, which amends SR-8.4 (as amended by b.deo SRI-803, SRI-804): no preview line says "destroyed". Every line is one line (control characters escaped with `escapeCause`). Personas are named by their JSON-quoted name with the key beside it, and credentials files by path. No line carries a setting value (except the new path of a destructive path change), a token, credentials content or a digest.

A valid candidate opens with a header: `A configuration change is pending; nothing has been applied.` and the counts (`renderChangePlanCounts`). A persona modified in place or with an own next-launch change counts as modified in place; one inherited from a top-level default counts only under server-wide settings. A persona both modified in place and credentials-changed counts in both. Then come, in order: removals, destructive modifies, additions, the other affected personas in candidate order (one line each, stating every effect), then the recorded lines in candidate order, then the changed server-wide settings in the fixed top-level key order, the switch's line among them (`renderPreviewLines`, `src/reload-plan.ts`). A `no effective change` preview is its title line followed by its recorded lines, if any.

**The switch's line and the recorded line (b.deo SRI-803, SRI-804).** A change of `allow_invited_channels` renders through `modeSwitchLine(mode, personas)`, naming the mode it turns on and every persona present in both configurations, in candidate order; with none it ends `; no persona is affected.` It says nothing of instances: a persona the same change modifies destructively has its own line. A persona's changed keys of the section not in force render through `recordedLine(p)`, naming the section (fungible exactly when the keys include `invited`). Built from those builders:

```text
server-wide setting allow_invited_channels changed: turns fungible mode on, applied in place at once, from the next event, tool call, prompt and notice, for "alpha" (key=alpha), "bravo" (key=bravo).
server-wide setting allow_invited_channels changed: turns declarative mode on, applied in place at once, from the next event, tool call, prompt and notice, for "alpha" (key=alpha), "bravo" (key=bravo).
server-wide setting allow_invited_channels changed: turns fungible mode on, applied in place at once, from the next event, tool call, prompt and notice; no persona is affected.
persona "bravo" (key=bravo): channels, permission_prompts changed in the declarative section: recorded, with no effect until allow_invited_channels selects declarative mode.
persona "bravo" (key=bravo): invited changed in the fungible section: recorded, with no effect until allow_invited_channels selects fungible mode.
```

A removal, an in-place change, a credentials change, an addition that cannot come up and two settings:

```text
A configuration change is pending; nothing has been applied. personas: 1 added, 1 removed, 0 destructively modified, 1 modified in place, 1 with changed credentials; server-wide settings: 2 changed.
DESTRUCTIVE: persona "alpha" (key=alpha) is removed: the persona will be retired: its session stopped and never resumed.
persona "delta" (key=delta) is added but cannot come up: credentials file does not exist; working directory does not exist.
persona "bravo" (key=bravo): channels changed: applied in place immediately, instance kept.
persona "charlie" (key=charlie): credentials file "/srv/personas/charlie/credentials.json" changed: a new connection opens, then the old one closes, instance kept.
server-wide setting port changed: once applied, it is recorded and takes effect at the next server start after that.
server-wide setting claude_config_dir changed: inherited by "bravo" (key=bravo), "charlie" (key=charlie); takes effect at each one's next launch, which starts fresh (the conversation is not resumed), instance kept until then.
```

Other line forms:

```text
DESTRUCTIVE: persona "bravo" (key=bravo) working_directory changed to "/srv/work/bravo2": the persona will be retired and brought up fresh: its session stopped and never resumed.
persona "delta" (key=delta) is added: it will be brought up and launched.
persona "bravo" (key=bravo): stop_hook_bootstrap changed: takes effect at its next launch, instance kept.
persona "bravo" (key=bravo): claude_config_dir changed: takes effect at its next launch, which starts fresh (the conversation is not resumed), instance kept until then.
persona "bravo" (key=bravo): claude_config_dir changed: takes effect at its next launch, which starts fresh (the conversation is not resumed), instance kept until then; but at that launch it cannot come up: claude_config_dir cannot be resolved to a real path (ENOENT: a symlink on its path points to nothing).
server-wide setting claude_config_dir changed: inherited by "bravo" (key=bravo), "charlie" (key=charlie); takes effect at each one's next launch, which starts fresh (the conversation is not resumed), instance kept until then; but at that launch "bravo" (key=bravo), "charlie" (key=charlie) cannot come up: claude_config_dir cannot be resolved to a real path (EIO).
DESTRUCTIVE: persona "bravo" (key=bravo) working_directory changed to "/srv/work/bravo2": the persona will be retired and brought up fresh: its session stopped and never resumed; but it cannot come up: claude_config_dir cannot be resolved to a real path (ENOENT).
persona "charlie" (key=charlie): credentials file "/srv/personas/charlie/credentials.json" changed: it has no connection yet, so it retries with the new content, instance kept.
persona "charlie" (key=charlie): credentials file "/srv/personas/charlie/credentials.json" changed: it is broken by its credentials now, so it will be brought up.
persona "charlie" (key=charlie): credentials file "/srv/personas/charlie/credentials.json" changed, but it cannot be used (credentials file does not exist): the current connection is kept, instance kept.
persona "charlie" (key=charlie): credentials file "/srv/personas/charlie/credentials.json" changed, but it cannot be used (credentials file does not exist): it keeps retrying with its current content, instance kept.
persona "charlie" (key=charlie): credentials file "/srv/personas/charlie/credentials.json" changed, but it cannot be used (credentials file does not exist): it stays broken by its credentials.
persona "delta" (key=delta) is added; whether it can come up could not be checked.
persona "charlie" (key=charlie): credentials file "/srv/personas/charlie/credentials.json" changed; whether it is broken by its credentials now could not be checked.
server-wide setting stop_hook_bootstrap changed: once applied, it is recorded; no persona inherits it, so no instance is affected.
server-wide setting exit_timeout changed: once applied, it is recorded, and the CLI takes it from the record from then on (the running server does not use it).
server-wide setting agent_director_call_timeout_ms changed: once applied, it is recorded, the CLI takes it from the record from then on, and the running server uses it from its next start.
A configuration change is pending; nothing has been applied. no effective change: applying it would change no persona and no server-wide setting.
INVALID: loadPersonaConfig: malformed JSON in "/srv/cscb/config.json" at line 1, column 17. Nothing will be applied.
INVALID: the configuration file "/srv/cscb/config.json" does not exist. Nothing will be applied.
```

An invalid candidate is that one `INVALID:` line with the loader's full error, and no header or persona lines. A missing file reads `does not exist`, an unreadable one `cannot be read (<code>)`. The loader's error echoes no rejected value and no unknown key name that could be a token (such a key is counted, not shown).

#### The preview in the log

The preview goes to the server log once per change of the logged state (see the Pending bullet above), identified by fingerprint:

- **Valid candidate**: every body line, each as `[slack] reload-preview: <line>`. The header line also ends ` (preview in "<pending>")`. A `no effective change` preview is logged this way too.
- **Invalid candidate**: exactly one line, `[slack] reload-invalid: the pending configuration is invalid and nothing will be applied: <error> (preview in "<pending>")`. No `reload-preview` line is logged for it.

The ` (preview in …)` suffix is dropped when this pass's pending-file write failed, so the log never points at a file that doesn't hold the preview. A write whose directory sync failed counts as written. The apply-time lines are under [The apply pipeline](#the-apply-pipeline-sr-86-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-805).

#### Confirmation (SR-8.5)

The operator confirms a pending change by renaming `config.json.pending` to `config.json.apply`. Nothing else triggers an apply: no endpoint, MCP tool or CLI subcommand reads, writes or creates the confirmation (b.av2 SR-8.8).

- **Read, then delete.** Each pass reads `config.json.apply` once through `readPersonaConfigBytes`; when it is absent nothing happens. It is then deleted with the durable delete (`durableUnlinkSync`) before anything is decided or applied, so a confirmation is used once. A delete whose directory sync failed counts as removed and logs one plain line.
- **Fingerprint match.** The confirmation's fingerprint line (`parsePendingFingerprint`) is compared with the fingerprint this pass computed over the current `config.json` and credentials files (`reloadFingerprint`, see [The fingerprint](#the-fingerprint)). On a match the pass hands its own bytes and change plan to the apply (`applyConfirmed`); nothing is read again and nothing is diffed a second time.
- **Stale.** A mismatch (`config.json` or a credentials file it references changed after that preview was written), an unreadable confirmation (a directory, a non-regular file, or one over the size cap) or one with no well-formed fingerprint applies nothing and logs one `reload-stale-confirmation` line (`renderStaleConfirmationLogLine`), naming the path and the reason, never the content. The fingerprint covers only `config.json` and the credentials files, not the record, so a copy of a pending file whose change was already applied still matches while those files are unchanged: it is applied again as a no-op (`reload-noop`), not refused.
- **Undeletable confirmation.** When the delete fails, the confirmation is still acted on once (applied on a match, else the stale line), and one plain cannot-remove line is logged. The pass keeps its identity in memory (`ignoredConfirmation`: a SHA-256 of its bytes, or the fixed `UNREADABLE_CONFIRMATION_IDENTITY` for one that can't be read). A later pass that finds the same identity only retries the delete, silently; different content is processed afresh, and the memory is cleared once the file is gone. The memory is not persisted, so after a restart such a file is processed once more.
- **Pending file after a consumed confirmation.** The rename removed `config.json.pending`. When the change is still pending after the confirmation (stale, invalid, a failed record write, the stored-choice write at step 1 included, or a credentials change that step 4 could not use), the same pass writes the pending file again, without a new preview line when the fingerprint is unchanged. An invalid candidate normally gets two `reload-invalid` lines: the pending-time line when its `INVALID` preview is written, then the confirmed line when the operator confirms it. A consumed confirmation counts as the logged pending state, so the pass that consumes it never logs the pending-time line as well: when the confirmation is already there on the pass that first sees the candidate (for example the first pass after a start), that pass logs only the confirmed line.
- **Server down.** A confirmation left while the server was stopped is processed by the first pass after the next start (the SR-8.7 comparison pass, as amended by b.deo SRI-403, SRI-407). The start itself never reads it.

#### The apply pipeline (SR-8.6 as amended by b.deo SRI-805)

`applyConfirmed` in `src/reload.ts` runs the apply; the step names, their inputs and the step runner are in `src/reload-apply.ts`.

- **Invalid candidate.** A candidate that fails to parse or validate (or a `config.json` that is missing, unreadable or over the cap) changes nothing: the record is not written and one line carries the full error, `[slack] reload-invalid: the confirmed configuration is invalid, so nothing is applied: <error>`.
- **Valid candidate.** Six steps run in order. Each step completes for every persona before the next starts (`runApplySteps` awaits each step's body). A step that throws is logged (`[slack] reload: apply step <n> (<step>) failed: <thrown value>`) and the next step still runs. After step 1 the controller runs step 2 on its own (one `runApplySteps` call), and once it has settled, whatever the teardowns did, it clears the retiring keys in a `finally`, on every path out of the apply; then steps 3–6 run (a second `runApplySteps` call), so the order and failure isolation are those of one run (b.deo SRI-502). The split is the controller's; `APPLY_STEPS` and `runApplySteps` (`src/reload-apply.ts`) define the steps and run each call.

| Step | Acts on | State |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Retired keys, record and swap | The whole candidate, in one synchronous stretch with no await (b.jg5 SRJ-1511 as amended by b.deo SRI-805), over the one stored-choice store the controller asks for once, through `ReloadControllerDeps.channelDelivery()`, before the first write: when a persona the apply brings up has an unwritten drop, the stored-choice file is written first (`writeDropsBeforeBringUp`, b.deo SRI-408, see below); then the retired keys are recorded (one durable write of `retired-keys.json`, see below), then each recorded key's dialog approver is stopped (b.jg5 SRJ-808), then the record is rewritten with the candidate's exact bytes (durable write), then each recorded key's old-life hold begins (b.jg5 SRJ-809), then the retired keys' stored choices are dropped in one batch (`dropRetiredChoices`, b.deo SRI-406) and each destructive modify's key is marked retiring (b.deo SRI-502), then the controller's applied state is swapped and `onApplied` is told, which reassigns the server's `personaConfig` to `configInEffect` (the confirmed persona set and switch). The bring-up controller's applied set, the reply-guard step, the detection tick and every reader of the channel mode read the new set from then on | Implemented |
| 2. Teardowns (`teardowns`) | Removed personas (`removed`) and the old half of each destructive modify (`destructiveOld`), as the previous configuration declares them: each is torn down (see [Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-307) and [Destructive modify](#destructive-modify-bav2-sr-86-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-406-sri-408-sri-502)) | Implemented |
| 3. In-place updates (`in-place-updates`) | Personas modified in place (`inPlace`), with their previous declaration and the changed settings: each is updated in place (see [In-place update](#in-place-update-bav2-sr-86-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-802)) | Implemented |
| 4. Credentials reconnects (`credentials-reconnects`) | Personas whose credentials content changed at the same path (`credentials`, plus `credentialsBroken`) and that are not broken by their credentials when step 4 runs: each that is up is reconnected, and each that is retrying retries with the new content (see [Credentials change](#credentials-change-bav2-sr-86-step-4-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-805)). The step settles once every persona's first reconnect attempt has settled; a reconnect left retrying counts as complete, so step 5 and later ticks are not held up | Implemented |
| 5. Template refresh (`template-refresh`) | The agent-director template, once; selected only when `configDirsChanged`: its memory-read rules are rewritten for the confirmed persona set (see [Template refresh](#template-refresh-bav2-sr-86-step-5-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-805)) | Implemented |
| 6. Bring-ups (`bring-ups`) | Added personas (`added`), as the candidate declares them: each is brought up (see [Bring-up at apply](#bring-up-at-apply-bav2-sr-61)).
