Also, as a recovery bring-up, each persona whose credentials changed and that step 4 did not reconnect because it was broken by its credentials, with or without an instance; the recovery checks the state again when it runs (see [Recovery of a credentials-broken persona](#recovery-of-a-credentials-broken-persona-bav2-sr-64)). The new half of each destructive modify (`destructiveNew`), as the candidate declares it, is brought up fresh the same way as an added persona | Implemented |

**Step 1's retired keys (b.jg5 SRJ-803, SRJ-804 as amended by b.deo SRI-408; b.jg5 SRJ-1511 as amended by b.deo SRI-406, SRI-408, SRI-502).** Before any teardown and before the record is rewritten, step 1 records the keys the apply retires in the retired-key record (`retired-keys.json`, see [Configuration](#retired-keysjson-state_dirretired-keysjson)), through the server's one store (the controller's `retiredKeys`):

- **Which keys.** `retiredKeysToRecord(plan, store)`: each removed persona's key with the cause `removed` (a `name` edit that changes the key is a removal, so a renamed persona's old key is among them), and each destructive modify's key with the cause `destructive-modify` (a new `name` that keeps the key, `credentials_file` or `working_directory`). Also the key of each persona the apply adds (a key-changing rename's new key included) that the store holds only in memory after a failed write of an earlier recording, with the cause it holds, so the bring-up the apply makes never outruns that key's write; this holds for an add-only apply too, which otherwise writes no retired-key record.
- **One durable write, first.** The whole batch is one `record` call: one atomic, durable write of the whole record, through the same writer as the controller's `write` (production: `durableWriteFileSync`). It precedes the rewrite of the last-applied record, so a crash between the two writes leaves the keys retired with the old record still applied, and never a modify applied with its old life still resumable. A batch that writes nothing makes no write. With the stored-choice writes (below), an apply's writes are, in this order and each one absent when it has nothing to write: [stored-choice file (unwritten drops), retired-key record, last-applied record, stored-choice file (the retired keys' drop)].
- **Re-recording.** A key recorded with its "new life has begun" mark set is recorded again with the mark cleared; a key recorded with no mark is left as it is and writes nothing, unless the store holds it only in memory, when the batch writes the record that carries it. Either way the recording raises the key's in-memory record generation (`recordGeneration`, never written to the file), so a reuse spawn of that key whose launch attempt was in flight across the recording sets no mark and answers `spawned` ([Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-bjg5-srj-806-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-407), **The new-life mark**).
- **The stored-choice write first (b.jg5 SRJ-804 as amended by b.deo SRI-408).** Before the retired-key write, when a key the apply brings up (`plan.added`, a key-changing rename's new key included, and each destructive modify's new half in `plan.destructive`) has an unwritten drop (`hasUnwrittenDrop`), the store's record is written once (`writeUnwrittenDrops`). Nothing is written when no such key has an unwritten drop, or when the store is unreadable. When the write fails (an unsynced rename included), the store logs its own failed-write line with the error code, and one `reload-record-write-failed` line names the stored-choice file and the last-applied record (`reloadChannelDeliveryWriteFailedLine`, [Reload lines](#reload-lines-bav2-sr-87-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-403-sri-407-bav2-sr-103-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-901-sri-905)): nothing is applied, so no retired-key record is written, no approver stopped, nothing rewritten, held, dropped or marked, and the change stays pending. A successful write carries only drops already in force, so nothing later in the apply undoes it, a failed rewrite included.
- **Step 1's own write fails.** When the retired-key write fails (an unsynced rename included, whose previous bytes the store writes back, best effort), the store is restored to the record it held before the apply, as far as it can be, the last-applied record is not rewritten, nothing is applied and the change stays pending. One `reload-record-write-failed` line names the retired-key file and says how the restore went; the store logs its own `retired-keys:` line with the write's error.
- **The approver stops (b.jg5 SRJ-808).** Once the record did not fail (`RETIRED_KEYS_WRITTEN`, or `RETIRED_KEYS_UNCHANGED` for keys already recorded with no mark), the controller stops the dialog approver of each key of the batch (`stopApprover`, a required `ReloadControllerDeps` member; production `stopDialogApprover(key, APPROVER_STOP_RETIRED_KEY)`), before the last-applied rewrite, so before any teardown is submitted and before its kill. Each call is not awaited, so step 1 stays one synchronous stretch; a throw or rejection is logged as `[slack] reload: stopping the dialog approver of key=<key>, recorded as retired, failed: <thrown value>`. A failed step-1 write stops no approver, and a failed rewrite restarts none (Server-Managed Startup step 5, **The retired-key stop**).
- **The rewrite fails.** See the Record write failure bullet below: the retired-key record is restored, so a rewrite that fails leaves retired no key this apply recorded; the approvers step 1 stopped stay stopped.
- **The old-life holds (b.jg5 SRJ-809).** Once the rewrite has succeeded, and before the state swap and any teardown's kill, the controller begins one old-life hold in the server's hold set (`oldLifeHolds`) for each removed persona's key (a rename's old key included) and each destructive modify's key, on `cscb_<key>` at the old declaration's working directory, cause `apply-step-1` (`oldLifeHoldsToBegin`), each with its began line; a key already recorded with no mark, and a destructive modify whose working directory is unchanged, get theirs too. A failed retired-key write or a failed rewrite begins none. A later read of the old row as live with another `cwd` re-points the hold, and only a read of it as finished, or the key's new life, ends it ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809)).
- **The retired keys' stored choices (b.deo SRI-406).** Right after the holds begin, one `drop` batch of each removed persona's key (a rename's old key included) and each destructive modify's key, the keys `retiredKeysToRecord` records as `removed` and `destructive-modify`, drops their stored choices with the reason `retired by a confirmed change`: they stop applying at once. A failed drop write never fails the apply: it is the store's own failed-write line and leaves an unwritten drop, which the next successful write carries (an apply that brings such a key back writes it first, above). A drop that throws logs `[slack] reload: dropping the stored choices of the retired keys failed: <thrown value> (b.deo SRI-406)` and the apply goes on. The file's other drops, by the start rules, are under Configuration, [channel-delivery.json](#channel-deliveryjson-state_dirchannel-deliveryjson).
- **The retiring keys (b.deo SRI-502).** Then each destructive modify's key is marked retiring in the store (`beginRetiring`), in both modes and whether or not the store is readable, and stays so until step 2 has settled (`endRetiring` in the controller's `finally`). Meanwhile `set_channel_delivery` refuses the key with `personaNotAppliedRefusal`, so neither the old life nor anything else stores a choice under the new declaration before the new half is up. A mark or clear that throws logs `[slack] reload: <marking|clearing> the retiring keys failed: <thrown value> (b.deo SRI-502)` and the apply goes on.

Step 1's writes and restore run in one synchronous stretch over both stores, the retired-key store and the stored-choice store, so no other change of either store comes between them. A failed stored-choice write, retired-key write or rewrite drops nothing and marks nothing.

Steps 2–6 are slots (`ApplyStepSlots`). By default the controller fills them with `lifecycleApplySlots` (`src/reload-apply.ts`): step 2 fans `lifecycle.teardown` out over `removed` and `destructiveOld`, step 3 fans `lifecycle.updateInPlace` out over `inPlace` (one update per persona key), step 4 fans `lifecycle.reconnectCredentials` out over the credentials-changed personas that are not credentials-broken, step 5 calls `lifecycle.refreshTemplate` once with the confirmed configuration, and step 6 fans `lifecycle.bringUp` out over `added` and `destructiveNew` and, with `{ recovery: true }`, over the credentials-changed personas step 4 did not reconnect; production binds all five to `src/persona-lifecycle.ts`. A persona with only next-launch changes is in no step's input (see [Next-launch and server-wide settings](#next-launch-and-server-wide-settings-bav2-sr-86-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-201-sri-203)).

**Credentials-broken is decided when the step runs.** The plan splits credentials-changed personas into `credentials` and `credentialsBroken` at the preview, but a persona can become credentials-broken between the preview and the apply, for example when its bot token is refused by a Web API call. So step 4 asks the bring-up state again (`credentialsBrokenNow`, over the controller's `bringUpState` and `isCredentialsBroken`), and falls back to the plan's split only when the state can't be read. Step 4 also re-checks inside its operation: a persona found credentials-broken there resolves `{ kind: 'credentials-broken' }` and is left to step 6. Step 6 takes every credentials-changed persona step 4 did not reconnect (a per-apply set in `lifecycleApplySlots`); only when step 4 did not run in the apply does step 6 ask `credentialsBrokenNow` itself. The recovery then decides inside the persona's serializer turn: a persona no longer credentials-broken by then (a pending reconnect of an earlier change brought it up) gets the change as step 4 would have applied it, so no confirmed change is skipped by both steps. Within a step every persona's operation runs at once (each through the per-persona serializer), and the step settles once all of them have settled: one persona's rejection is logged (`[slack] reload: apply step <n> (<step>) failed for persona "<name>" (key=<key>): <thrown value>`) and never stops another. The per-step barrier holds when one apply has both: every teardown settles before step 3 starts, and the bring-ups start only after steps 3–5. The controller's `applySteps` replaces the default bodies entirely; only tests set it.

A `name` change changes the key (b.av2 SR-2.1), so the plan lists it as a removal of the old key and an addition of the new one: the old key is recorded as retired in step 1, the old persona is torn down in step 2 and the new one brought up fresh in step 6, without the old conversation.

Step 1's swap has these effects before step 2 runs, because routing, `isPersonaUp`, the permission poller, MCP admission, `/interject` and the notifier all read `personaConfig` at call time:

- **Removed persona.** It stops receiving events at once: each is dropped with `[slack] persona-routing: no applied persona with key=<key> — event not delivered to it`, and a notice for it is dropped (`persona-notifier: no applied persona with key=<key> — notice dropped`), except one raised while its teardown's notice window is open, which is written to the server log and a `persona-teardown-notice` entry, and the all-clear of an outage whose onset that window wrote (b.jg5 SRJ-1003; [Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-307)). A new MCP session from its directory matches no applied persona and is not admitted, the permission poller leaves its rows unread, and `/interject` answers 404 (`Persona not found in the applied config`). An MCP session of it that is still registered stays connected, but each tool call it makes is refused with the tool error `Tool "<name>" refused: persona key=<key> is not an applied persona.` (`personaNotAppliedRefusal`, shared by all six tools; the session's tool handler in `registry.ts` looks the persona up in the applied set at call time). It is never restarted or relaunched (see the applied-set guard under Server-Managed Startup step 5). Its instance and Slack connection still run until its teardown in step 2 removes them.
- **Kept persona.** For a change to the section in force (`channels`, `delivery` and `permission_prompts` in declarative mode, `invited.permission_prompts` in fungible mode) or `dm.*`, see [In-place update](#in-place-update-bav2-sr-86-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-802). A recorded change to the section not in force goes into no step. A change to `stop_hook_bootstrap` or `claude_config_dir` takes effect at the persona's next launch or relaunch, which reads the new declaration (`launchSession` and the bring-up retry's launch look the persona up in `personaConfig`); the running instance is untouched (see [Next-launch and server-wide settings](#next-launch-and-server-wide-settings-bav2-sr-86-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-201-sri-203)).
- **Destructively modified persona.** Its key stays applied with the new declaration, so MCP admission matches a registering session against the new `working_directory` at once, and a session from the old directory that registers again is not admitted as that persona. Its old instance still runs until step 2 tears it down (see [Destructive modify](#destructive-modify-bav2-sr-86-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-406-sri-408-sri-502)), and its key is retiring meanwhile (**The retiring keys**, above).
- **Added persona.** It is in the applied set, and step 6 brings it up.
- **Credentials change.** Nothing changes yet: the persona keeps the content it holds until step 4 (or step 6's recovery bring-up) acts on it.

- **Record write failure.** A write that fails before its rename leaves the old record intact. A write whose rename succeeded but whose directory sync failed (`DurableWriteUnsyncedError`) has the previous bytes written back, best effort. Either way the applied state is not swapped, no step runs and the change stays pending. When step 1 wrote the retired-key record, it is then restored (`restore`) to the record the store held before the apply (b.jg5 SRJ-804 as amended by b.deo SRI-408): the keys this apply recorded are removed again, keys recorded before it stay, the marks it cleared are set again, and keys and marks held only in memory before it are written with the rest; a record empty before the apply is restored by removing the file (an empty record is written when the remove fails). One `reload-record-write-failed` line is logged, and it ends with how that restore went. A failed restore is named only in that line (no Slack post, no startup-errors entry): the keys this apply recorded stay retired, which errs toward a fresh start. A stored-choice write that step 1 made before the rewrite is not undone (b.deo SRI-408).
- **Server-wide settings.** Step 1 records them; the server keeps its start-time values (`configInEffect`) until the next start, which runs the record (see [Next-launch and server-wide settings](#next-launch-and-server-wide-settings-bav2-sr-86-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-201-sri-203), which also covers the one exception, the switch `allow_invited_channels`, applied in place at the step-1 swap; b.deo SRI-201, SRI-203).
- **No effective change.** `applyStepsFor` selects no step except step 5, and that only when `configDirsChanged`. Step 1 still rewrites the record, so `config.json` and the record match byte for byte again, and `reload-noop` is logged. A candidate whose only changes are recorded ones confirms the same way: the record is rewritten, the applied state swapped and `reload-noop` logged, with no lifecycle operation (b.deo SRI-804).
- **Unchanged personas.** A persona whose declaration and credentials are unchanged is in no step's input: it is neither touched nor re-probed, and its connection, instance and held digest stay as they are.
- **Success.** After the last step, `reload-applied` is logged with the plan's counts. The pass then derives the state again against the new applied state; if nothing is pending, the pending file is deleted without a `reload-nothing-pending` line.
- **Shutdown.** When detection is stopped while a step runs, the pass ends after the apply.
- **Live-row sequences (b.jg5 SRJ-706).** No step waits for one: a bring-up's launch for a persona whose sequence runs answers `sequence-waiting` at once, and step 2's teardown stops the persona's sequence (see [Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-307)), so the apply returns while a sequence of another persona still runs.

#### Failures

- A pending-file write or delete that fails is logged once per episode and retried at the next pass. An episode ends at the next success or when the derived state changes, to nothing pending or to a different pending fingerprint: each new state logs its first failure, and a failure that keeps repeating within one state is logged only once. A write whose rename succeeded but whose directory sync failed is written again at the next pass.
- A delete whose unlink failed logs the cannot-remove line; the file stays, the logged state is unchanged and the delete is retried at the next pass, so `reload-nothing-pending` follows the removal that later succeeds.
- A delete whose unlink succeeded but whose directory sync failed (`DurableUnlinkUnsyncedError`) counts as removed: the pass logs one removed-but-unsynced line, then the removed variant of `reload-nothing-pending` when that is due, and moves to nothing pending. Nothing retries the sync (the file is gone), so the removal may not survive a crash; the next start's first pass removes any leftover.
- A pass that fails unexpectedly is logged once per episode (until a pass succeeds), and the timer carries on.
- A confirmed apply whose step-1 write fails logs one `reload-record-write-failed` line naming the file that failed: the stored-choice file (b.deo SRI-408), the retired-key record (b.jg5 SRJ-804 as amended by b.deo SRI-408) or the last-applied record. Each applies nothing and leaves the change pending, and the same pass writes the pending file again (see [The apply pipeline](#the-apply-pipeline-sr-86-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-805)).

The lines are listed under Logging, [Reload lines](#reload-lines-bav2-sr-87-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-403-sri-407-bav2-sr-103-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-901-sri-905). Every line goes to the server log only; nothing about a pending change reaches Slack.

### Bring-up at apply (b.av2 SR-6.1)

Apply step 6 brings up each added persona, and the new half of each destructive modify, through `PersonaLifecycle.bringUp` (`src/persona-lifecycle.ts`), all of them at once, each through the per-persona serializer; the same operation, with `{ recovery: true }`, brings a credentials-broken persona up again (see [Recovery of a credentials-broken persona](#recovery-of-a-credentials-broken-persona-bav2-sr-64)). It is the start procedure for one persona (Server-Managed Startup step 5), with the same outcomes and the same lines, plus the storage check:

1. **Storage check.** `runPersonaStorageCheck` (`src/jsonl-persistence-check.ts`) runs Layer 1 of the JSONL-persistence safeguard (startup step 4a-quater) for this persona's effective `<claude_config_dir>/projects` root only. A root on `tmpfs`/`ramfs` is recorded in `startup-errors.log` as `jsonl-non-persistent`, and a warning goes to this persona's destination through the notifier, held until its client is validated; a root whose fstype can't be determined is recorded as `jsonl-persistence-check-warning`, with no notice. Layer 2 doesn't run: the launch's collision ladder handles any existing row. No other persona is checked or warned.
2. **Bring-up.** The bring-up controller's `bringUp(persona, applied.personas)`: the `persona-start` line, the credentials check (the persona's credentials file only, read as it stands; nothing is read from the environment), the working-directory check against the confirmed persona set, then Slack validation and connection. The credentials check also runs against the confirmed set (b.av2 SR-1.4, apply part): a credentials file whose real path is another applied persona's makes the persona credentials-broken (`persona-credentials-invalid`, `real path is also the credentials_file of …`), and the other persona is not touched.
3. **Launch.** Only when the outcome is `up`: one `up at apply — launching` line, then `spawnForPersona` with the persona's declaration and the start-time server-wide values, as a runtime launch, so a spawn failure takes the runtime spawn-failure path. A refusal in that launch (UNAVAILABLE, ENVIRONMENT, CONFIG or UNCLASSIFIED, or a read error at the collision `get`) takes the ladder's refusal handling: no spawn-failure notice, and nothing deleted, killed to recover or launched after it. The persona's UNAVAILABLE retry timer, when the refusal armed it, retries the persona. Like the launch after a retry, it doesn't ask the relaunch gate again. The launch is b.av2 SR-6.1's step 4 as amended by b.jg5 SRJ-1502: while an old life that may still be running holds the persona's working directory (a hold on its own `cscb_<key>` excepted), `spawnForPersona`'s old-life gate makes no agent-director call, records the persona as waiting, starts the hold's wait and arms its timer with `held-for-old-life`, and the launch answers `sequence-waiting`; the persona is retried on that timer, and at once when the hold ends ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809), **What a hold refuses**). A persona added in a held directory, and a renamed persona's new key while its old key's row is live, wait so.

A `broken` or `retrying` persona is logged exactly as at start (Logging, [Persona bring-up lines](#persona-bring-up-lines-bav2-sr-103-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-901-sri-902)) and posts nothing. A `retrying` one retries on its own timers, and the operation returns without waiting for them. A new persona with missing or invalid credentials is `broken` on its own: no running persona is touched, re-probed or restarted.

**Shutdown skip.** The operation checks the server's `shuttingDown` flag (`isShuttingDown`) twice, logging `not brought up — the server is shutting down` each time it is set:

- **When the operation starts:** no storage check, no bring-up, no launch; it resolves `broken` with no failures.
- **Right before the launch** (the bring-up returned `up`): no launch; it returns the `up` result.

A recovery bring-up checks it a third time, after its preparation (see [Recovery of a credentials-broken persona](#recovery-of-a-credentials-broken-persona-bav2-sr-64)) and before the bring-up: it resolves `broken` with no failures.

Shutdown has already cancelled every bring-up and stopped every connection, so nothing started here would be released before the exit.

**The detection pass waits for it.** The pass awaits the whole apply, so it is held by the slowest per-persona operation of any of the four kinds (teardown, in-place update, credentials change, bring-up), and by step 5's one template call. A credentials change waits at most for its first reconnect attempt, which the 10 s bounds on `auth.test` and `start()` cap, plus any work already queued for the persona. A bring-up waits for its launch, which, when a leftover `cscb_<key>` row is `working`, can include `waitForWaitingAndReconnect` (up to 10 minutes, `WAIT_FOR_WAITING_TIMEOUT_MS`, then possibly a fresh spawn; about a minute when the positive-idle rule shows the row stale, b.f2b). It does not wait for the pre-session dialog approver, which starts after the launch call returns and runs on its own until the session starts, at most its bound B from the launch start (b.jg5 SRJ-404). Unlike the start pass, the apply doesn't park such a launch. A teardown queues behind any restart or retry work already submitted for its key and then waits in `whenLaunchSettled` for a launch in flight, after cancelling that launch's wait for a `working` row, so the launch settles promptly (b.f2b). An in-place update does nothing slow itself, but it too queues behind any restart or retry work already submitted for its persona, such as a restart launch waiting on a `working` row; until it runs, steps 4–6 don't start. The next pass is armed only after that, so meanwhile no pending-file refresh runs and no other confirmation is processed. Shutdown is not blocked: `stopDetection()` doesn't wait for the pass (`src/reload-timer.ts`).

### Persona teardown (b.av2 SR-6.5 as amended by b.deo SRI-307)

Apply step 2 tears down each removed persona, and the old half of each destructive modify, through `PersonaLifecycle.teardown` (`src/persona-lifecycle.ts`), all of them at once, each through the per-persona serializer. It follows b.av2 SR-6.5 as amended by b.jg5 SRJ-1507 and b.deo SRI-307, with b.jg5 SRJ-715's order: it stops everything the server runs for the persona's key first, kills its agent-director row with the bounded retry and the result checked, and keeps the row. There is no delete. There is no graceful wind-down either: nothing is paused, nothing waits for the instance to go quiet, and no exit timeout applies. A removed persona left the applied set at step 1, so meanwhile every launch, restart and retry path already refuses it (the applied-set guard, Server-Managed Startup step 5). The old half of a destructive modify is still applied; what the teardown does instead is under [Destructive modify](#destructive-modify-bav2-sr-86-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-406-sri-408-sri-502).

Before the teardown is submitted, apply step 1 recorded the key as retired and stopped its dialog approver with the reason `retired-key` (b.jg5 SRJ-803 as amended by b.deo SRI-408; b.jg5 SRJ-808; [The apply pipeline](#the-apply-pipeline-sr-86-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-805)), so no Enter reaches the old life from then on, and began the old life's hold on its working directory (b.jg5 SRJ-809, SRJ-715; [The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809)). Step 1, not the teardown, also dropped the key's stored choices and, for a destructive modify, marked the key retiring until step 2 settles (b.deo SRI-406, SRI-502). The teardown never touches the stored-choice store: a key's stored choices are dropped only when the key is retired, at apply step 1 or by a start rule ([channel-delivery.json](#channel-deliveryjson-state_dirchannel-deliveryjson)).

**At submit (b.f2b, b.jg5 SRJ-404, SRJ-715, SRJ-1003).** When the teardown is submitted, before its serializer turn, it first registers its submit with the notifier (`submitTeardown(key)`): from then until the teardown completes, the notifier's `teardownWindowState(key)` answers at least `submitted`, and the key's notice episodes post nothing to Slack (`src/persona-episodes.ts`: a post or a `postWithoutEpisode` reaches no sink, logs that it was not posted, and a post still counts as posted in its episode). That mutes every notice-episode kind posted through the episodes: the *Held: tmux session conflict*, *Held: unusable tmux session name* and *Held: launch start not recorded* notices, the *Cannot launch* alert, the *Slow recovery* notice, the `tmux-unresponsive` onset, alert and recovery, the unclassified-error alert and both versions of the kill-failure alert, so none of an old half's reaches the new half's destination. The notifier mutes the onset of the one outage that is a notice-episode kind too, `ad-config-malformed` (b.jg5 SRJ-1016; `PERSONA_NOTICE_SUBMIT_MUTED_OUTAGE_CLASSES`): one `onset for <ref> of ad-config-malformed not posted — muted, its persona teardown was submitted; its all-clear is written, never posted: <first line>` line, no post and no entry, and that outage's all-clear is written to the server log and a `persona-teardown-notice` entry, never posted. The submit's end (`settleTeardown`) runs once, when the teardown completes or when the serializer settles a turn that never ran; a registration that throws logs `registering its submit failed: <thrown value>`, and an end that throws logs `ending its submit failed: <thrown value>` and counts as a failed step. Notices outside the episodes raised between the submit and the turn (another outage's onset, such as `tmux-unavailable` or `ad-unreachable`, the stuck-prompt warning, a spawn-failure notice and the lost-message notice) route as any other: a removed key's is dropped by the notifier's rule for a key no longer applied, and a destructive modify's key's routes as any configured persona's. Then it stops the persona's dialog approver (`stopApprover`, production `stopDialogApprover(key, APPROVER_STOP_TEARDOWN)`, not awaited here), which also cancels the approver a launch in flight would start, then, right after it, stops the persona's running live-row sequence (`stopLiveRowSequence`, production `stopLiveRowSequence(key, LIVE_ROW_STOP_TEARDOWN)`, b.jg5 SRJ-706, not awaited here), and then cancels the persona's launch wait for a `working` row (`cancelLaunchWait`). Neither the teardown nor work queued ahead of it for the key (a restart that joined that launch) then waits it out. A throw is logged as `<step> before its turn failed` and the teardown still runs. The old half of a destructive modify cancels more at submit (see [Destructive modify](#destructive-modify-bav2-sr-86-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-406-sri-408-sri-502)).

**The notice window (b.jg5 SRJ-1003, SRJ-1002, SRJ-1013).** At the start of its serializer turn (`runTeardown`), after its `starting` line and with nothing awaited before or between them, the teardown forgets its outage flags silently (`resetOutageState([key])`, `resetAllToHealthy`, step label `forgetting its outage state`), so a flag raised before the teardown posts no all-clear, and opens its notice window (`openTeardownWindow(persona)`, step label `opening its notice window`), then, with nothing awaited since, cancels its destination hold (`destinationHold.cancel(key)`, step label `DESTINATION_HOLD_CANCEL_AT_WINDOW_STEP`, `cancelling its held destination notices as its notice window opens`; the hold's one line), so a notice the hold kept before the window is never retried and posted while the window is open, to a destructive modify's new half's destination included. The steps below run inside it. When they complete, whatever a step throws, it closes the window (`closeTeardownWindow(key)`, step label `closing its notice window`) and ends its submit; a step's returned promise that rejects is counted before the `complete` line, which is always last. While the window is open, every notice raised for the key goes through the notifier's window: one server-log line and one `startup-errors.log` entry naming the persona and "raised during its teardown" (`personaTeardownNoticeEntryText`: `persona "<name>" (key=<key>), raised during its teardown: <text>`), of class `persona-teardown-notice`, or `persona-kill-survivor` for the kill-failure alert's survivor version. The entry and the line carry the notice's text with Slack's control-character escapes undone (`unescapeSlackControlCharacters`), so a notice built for Slack reads as an unescaped one does. That covers an outage onset from its calls or from the launch in flight it waits for, a latch's notice or an `ErrInvalidFlags` hold's *Cannot launch* alert raised by that launch, an unclassified-error alert, every kill-failure alert (one of a context other than `persona teardown`, such as the launch in flight's `recovery` kill, prefixed `(<context>) `), a CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME its kill meets, its kill's non-success that no other notice records (step 8), a stuck-prompt warning and a lost-message notice. None reaches a Slack destination, the old half's or the new half's, and none is queued, held or dropped: the window comes before the notifier's drop for a key no longer applied, its dry-run branch, its pre-validation hold and the destination hold, so dry run routes the same way. An outage flag raised in the window is kept past the teardown, and its all-clear, whenever it comes, is written the same way, never posted (after the window has closed its entry says `the all-clear of an outage raised during its teardown`). An all-clear that lists such a class and another class is split (`allClearOf`): the window-marked classes' all-clear is written, and the rest's, listing only the other classes, is posted to the destination. A bounded retry of a launch or recovery attempt's kill that the teardown's start stops is no notice: it writes the stop's line, naming its cause (`its live-row sequence was stopped: the persona's teardown began`, or what the keep-going check answered), and for a removed persona a `persona-kill-failed` entry with no alert text, never a `persona-teardown-notice` entry ([The kill-failure alert](#the-kill-failure-alert-bjg5-srj-704-srj-1007), **Latched and stopped tries**).

The steps run in this order. A step that fails is logged and the rest still run:

1. **First, before the wait for its launch in flight (b.jg5 SRJ-715).** Its dialog approver is stopped (`stopApprover`, awaited; b.jg5 SRJ-404): a running approver makes no call after the one in progress returns, and the approver the launch in flight would start does not start. An approver still running logs `stopping the approver for <ref> (teardown): its teardown began; …` when this is the first stop asked of it (apply step 1's `retired-key` stop usually came first and logged its own), or, for one the launch had not started, `not starting the approver for <ref> (teardown): …` when that launch returns. Right after it, its live-row sequence is stopped (`stopLiveRowSequence`, awaited, step label `stopping its live-row sequence`; b.jg5 SRJ-706): the sequence logs `stop asked — the persona's teardown began; no further call` and makes no further call, and the step waits for its call in flight to return (a step-6 launch it had started included), so the retry-timer stop that follows clears any arm that call made. Then its UNAVAILABLE retry timer is stopped (`stopRetryTimer`, the controller's `stop` with the reason `the persona was torn down`, b.jg5 SRJ-305). The persona's pending `tmux-unresponsive` alert check is cancelled with it (b.jg5 SRJ-309), since its text says CSCB keeps retrying: the stop's observer calls `cancelAlert(key, reason)`, and the same binding then calls `cancelAlert(key, UNAVAILABLE_RETRY_STOP_TORN_DOWN)` itself, which cancels the check when no timer was armed; either logs `alert check cancelled — its retry timer stopped: the persona was torn down` once, and a terminal reason never lets a later refusal arm the check again. Other personas' timers stay armed. Right after that stop its old-life waits are forgotten (`forgetOldLifeWaits`, optional in `PersonaLifecycleDeps`, production the session manager's `forgetOldLifeWaits`, step label `forgetting its old-life waits` (`OLD_LIFE_WAITS_STEP`); b.jg5 SRJ-811, SRJ-810): the key leaves every hold's waiting record, so no hold's end retries it, and the wait of a hold it was recorded as waiting on is stopped (`stopNoLaunch`, reason `teardown`) only when no persona left in the applied configuration waits on that hold, a destructive modify's new half, still applied under the key, counting as one; one line per such hold (`oldLifeWaitTeardownLine`), and the step settles once each wait it stopped has settled. Then, silently, its latch is forgotten (`forgetConflictLatch`, the latch instance's `forget`, b.jg5 SRJ-504: no post, no set observer call, no line; see [Session conflict latch](#session-conflict-latch-bjg5-srj-501-srj-502)), its `ErrInvalidFlags` hold (`forgetInvalidFlagsHold`, the hold's `forget`, b.jg5 SRJ-207: nothing posted and nothing retried, one `hold forgotten` line when it was held; see [The `ErrInvalidFlags` hold](#the-errinvalidflags-hold-bjg5-srj-207-srj-1008)), and every notice episode it has open with every count kept beside them, the slow-recovery count included (`forgetNoticeEpisodes`, the episodes instance's `forget`, b.jg5 SRJ-1016, SRJ-610). A forget that throws logs its step line (`forgetting its latch failed`, `forgetting its ErrInvalidFlags hold failed`, `forgetting its notice episodes failed`), counts as a failed step, and the rest still run.
2. Its bring-up retries are cancelled and its bring-up state forgotten (the controller's `cancel`), and its pending restart timer is cancelled (`cancelRestartTimer`). A retry already running or queued ahead of the teardown finishes first, since the teardown waits for its serializer turn, and its answer is dropped. Its launch's wait for a `working` row is cancelled (`cancelLaunchWait`, production `cancelWorkingRowWait`, b.f2b), as it already was when the teardown was submitted (see above); this call catches a wait that started since. Then a launch still in flight for it is awaited (`whenLaunchSettled`), so the kill never races a launch that is bringing the row up. This covers a start-pass launch, which runs outside the serializer. A cancelled wait types nothing and its launch settles promptly, so the teardown doesn't wait up to 10 minutes for it.
3. **Again, once that launch has settled (b.jg5 SRJ-715).** Its live-row sequence is stopped again, awaited (step label `stopping its live-row sequence again, after its launch in flight settled`), its UNAVAILABLE retry timer stopped again, its old-life waits forgotten again (that launch can have recorded it as waiting), its latch forgotten silently again, and its `ErrInvalidFlags` hold and its notice episodes forgotten again (each step label ending `again, after its launch in flight settled`): that launch can have started a sequence at a collision ladder replacement site (b.jg5 SRJ-707), armed the timer, set a latch or a hold, or opened an episode after step 1. So a launch in flight that meets UNAVAILABLE during the teardown leaves no retry timer armed, and a latch or a hold it set goes, with the CONFLICT or hold episode it began. The teardown itself latches nothing (b.jg5 SRJ-1002).
4. Its Slack connection is stopped (the connection manager's `stop`), then its inbound dedupe store and its heard set, for its key only, are dropped (the routing's `forget`; b.deo SRI-307), and its ack-tracker entries are dropped (`forgetPersonaAcks`, injected as `forgetAcks`; other personas' entries stay), so a key added again starts clean and logs `persona-invited-channel` afresh for each channel it hears in fungible mode. The connection goes first, because an event for the key would create a new store.
5. Its cached DM conversation is forgotten (`personaDestinations.forget`), its destination hold is cancelled again (held notices dropped, retry timer cleared; this closes a destination episode a re-derived prompt's failure opened in the window, so it cannot hold a destructive modify's new half's first notices) and its pre-validation held notices are dropped (the notifier's `forget`, step label `dropping its held notices`, with its one line). Nothing held is posted. Only notices queued before the window opened are dropped: one raised in the window is written, never queued (b.jg5 SRJ-1003).
6. Its tracked permission prompts, their not-posted records and its wedge state are dropped (`forgetPersonaPrompts`). Their Slack messages stay as posted.
7. Its MCP session is dropped with `dropPersonaSessionAndKeepAlive`, the session drop of Disconnection, so the close schedules no restart. A `set_channel_delivery` call through the dropped session is then refused (`personaNotAppliedRefusal`), since the registry does not hold that session for the key (b.deo SRI-502).
8. **The kill (b.jg5 SRJ-715, SRJ-110, SRJ-702).** Its outage flags were reset right before the window opened, so a success posts no all-clear for a flag raised before the teardown, and a flag raised in the window is not reset again. Outside dry run, `cscb_<key>` is killed through `killInstance`, production `killPersonaInstanceForTeardown(key, { clock: KILL_RETRY_SYSTEM_CLOCK })` (`src/session-manager.ts`): the bounded kill retry (**The bounded kill retry** under [Agent-director error classes](#agent-director-error-classes-bjg5-srj-104)) over one checked kill per try (`killPersonaInstance` with `KILL_CONTEXT_TEARDOWN`, through `withOutageDetection` arming nothing; hatch A3), seeded as a live row the teardown has not read (`KILL_RETRY_SEED_LIVE_UNREAD`). An UNAVAILABLE outcome gets up to 3 tries 2 s apart, with one `status` read of the row before each further try; a read of `ended`, `missing` or `ErrSpawnNotFound` ends the tries as a success. A CONFLICT is never tried again. The read goes through `withOutageDetection` arming nothing too, with no own-row step, so it latches nothing (`readTeardownKillRow`). Of the row-read rule only the retired-key entry clear applies (b.jg5 SRJ-807, SRJ-115): a row read `waiting`, `working`, `ask_user` or `check_permission` of a key recorded with its mark set clears the key's entry, the store's clear line naming the site `persona teardown kill: status read between tries`, and what the read answers is the same whatever the clear did. A `pending` row with no launch start is a live read, and an UNUSABLE NAME answer a failed read after which the next try goes ahead. No keep-going check stops the tries: the persona teardown's own kill is never stopped early by one (SRJ-702). Neither SRJ-316's rule against starting a kill of a row last read `pending` nor a latch holds the kill's start back, so a `pending` row with no launch start (b.jg5 SRJ-513) and a latched persona's row are killed too; between tries, a CONFIG answer at a read following a read of `pending` still ends the tries, the last try's outcome standing (SRJ-702), and a CONFIG answer after any other last state read lets the next try go ahead. Each CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME answer met, at a try or at a read, is answered in the result's `refusals` and latches nothing. The kill is no launch or recovery attempt: no try or read arms a retry timer, starts a `tmux-unresponsive` condition or feeds the unclassified-error episode, nothing is reported after the tries, and an ENVIRONMENT or CONFIG answer raises `tmux-unavailable` or `ad-config-malformed` only while the persona is in the applied configuration (a destructive modify's old half; a removed persona's raises no outage, and is recorded by the kill-outcome notice below); `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` still raises `ad-unreachable`. An `ErrInvalidFlags` from a try gets its immediate version re-check (b.jg5 SRJ-104, SRJ-204) and is a non-success all the same. The outcome that stands is logged with `kill_sent` (`describeKillOutcome`) and the number of tries. A success (`killLetsNextStepRun`: any `kill_sent`, `ErrSpawnNotFound`, GONE, or a read between tries that found the row finished) passes the step; a successful `kill_sent: false` raises nothing (b.jg5 SRJ-703). Any other outcome, an answer that is not a kill outcome, or a throw fails the kill step, and the other steps still run. After any outcome the row is kept: no delete call exists (b.jg5 SRJ-715). Each CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME answer in the result's `refusals` (`teardownKillRefusalsOf` keeps only well-formed ones) is then raised as one notice through the notifier's `notify` (step label `raising the notice for the <CONFLICT|UNUSABLE_NAME> its kill met`; b.jg5 SRJ-1003, SRJ-1002), which the open window writes to the server log and a `persona-teardown-notice` entry: its text is `teardownKillRefusalNoticeText(instanceId, refusal)`, `agent-director kill of cscb_<key> refused at a try: <outcome>` or `… refused at a status read between its tries: <outcome>`, `<outcome>` being `describeKillOutcome`'s one-line rendering (its class and agent-director's redacted description). Nothing latched on it, so it carries no hold sentence and is never the CONFLICT notice's or the unusable-name notice's text. The old-life wait uses the same builder for such an answer at its kill (`oldLifeWaitRefusalNoticeText`), in an entry worded `raised during its old-life wait` that its end handler writes itself ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809), **The wait's steps**; b.jg5 SRJ-811, SRJ-1013). With no `notify` in the injected notifier the step logs `no notifier route is installed for the notice: <notice text>`. Every failed kill is recorded (b.jg5 SRJ-110): when the standing outcome is a non-success and none of the following records it, a raised kill-failure alert decision, a refusal notice for a CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME answer at a try (an answer at a read between tries does not count), or the onset of its outage written in the window (read once after the kill through the injected `outageFlags`, production `getOutageFlags`: an ENVIRONMENT outcome's `tmux-unavailable`, a CONFIG outcome's `ad-config-malformed`, `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared`'s `ad-unreachable`; with no reader, an ENVIRONMENT or CONFIG outcome counts as recorded while the key is applied and `ErrSystemInstallDisappeared` always), the next step (step label `raising the notice for its kill's outcome`) raises one notice through `notify`, which the window writes as one `persona-teardown-notice` entry: `teardownKillNotSucceededNoticeText(instanceId, outcome, tries)`, `agent-director kill of cscb_<key> did not succeed after <n> kill(s); the row is kept: <outcome>` (both builders live in `src/checked-kill.ts`, beside `describeKillOutcome`). So an ENVIRONMENT or CONFIG answer for a removed persona, an UNAVAILABLE outcome other than `ErrTmuxKillFailed`, an UNCLASSIFIED value, and a standing outcome after a read-time refusal each get an entry. Nothing latches and nothing is armed on it. When the tries decided the ordinary version and no stop ended them, `killPersonaInstanceForTeardown` marks the key's old-life hold kill-failed (b.jg5 SRJ-812; [The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809)); no outcome ends the hold, a success included, and the read between tries that finds the row finished ends it through its own read. When the retry's alert decision is `ordinary` or `survivor`, the next step raises it (`raiseKillFailureAlert`, step label `raising the kill-failure alert`; b.jg5 SRJ-704) through the server's one kill-failure alerts instance, unlatched, with the context 'persona teardown': inside the window the ordinary version goes to the server log and a `persona-teardown-notice` entry, the survivor version to the server log and a `persona-kill-survivor` entry, never to Slack ([The kill-failure alert](#the-kill-failure-alert-bjg5-srj-704-srj-1007)). In dry run no agent-director call is made, so no refusal notice, kill-outcome notice or alert is raised, and one dry-run line says the kill is skipped and the row kept. In both modes its UNAVAILABLE retry timer is then stopped once more (`stopRetryTimer`, step label `stopping its UNAVAILABLE retry timer once more, after the kill`, `TEARDOWN_RETRY_TIMER_STOP_AFTER_KILL_STEP`), so no timer stays armed after the teardown. An outage flag the kill raised (`ad-unreachable`, or for a destructive modify's old half `tmux-unavailable` or `ad-config-malformed`) is kept: its onset was written in the window, and its all-clear is written the same way when it comes (b.jg5 SRJ-1002). No second `forget` of held notices follows: none was queued in the window.
9. Its restart failure count and cap latch (`forgetFailures`), its health-check streak (`forgetDisconnectedStreak`) and its not-connected episode (`forgetNotConnectedEpisode`, b.f2b: the notice latch and the restart path's idle evidence for its `working` row) are forgotten, then its latch once more, silently (`forgetConflictLatch`, step label `forgetting its latch once more, after the kill`; b.jg5 SRJ-715, SRJ-504).
10. Its reply-guard record is deleted and its launched-with directory forgotten (`teardownPersonaReplyGuard`). The Stop-hook launch pass (`stopHookLaunchPass`) then re-evaluates the persona's configured and launched-with config directories against the personas still applied, so the managed hook stays only where a remaining persona needs it.

Step 1's approver and sequence stops and step 2's launch-wait cancel also run at submit; the old half of a destructive modify also runs step 2's cancels and step 1's retry-timer stop then. Step 1's and step 3's forgets do not run at submit: they run only at the teardown's serializer turn. Each forget that drops the persona's latch also stops its latch re-check timer, through the forget observer `bindLatchRecheck` adds (b.jg5 SRJ-505; [The re-check](#the-re-check-bjg5-srj-505)); a re-check round runs in the persona's serializer turn, so none runs during the teardown, and one due after it finds no latch and does nothing.

**Afterwards.** The row is kept, as the kill left it. The key was recorded as retired at apply step 1, so the row is the key's old life and is never resumed or reconnected: the next launch of a persona with that key, a persona added again with the same key or a destructive modify's new half, is a reuse spawn of `cscb_<key>` that resets a finished row to a new life and answers `fresh-retired` ([Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-bjg5-srj-806-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-407)). A row still live after a kill that did not succeed is replaced only through the live-row sequence with the retired-key flag, which kills it again first. Its old-life hold stays until a read shows the old row finished or the key's new life begins ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809)). A removed persona's kept row is swept at the next start like any row of an absent persona (`absent persona`, Server-Managed Startup step 4): when it is still live, the sweep holds its directory again and kills it, and keeps the row whatever the outcome. The teardown posts nothing to Slack. Every notice raised for the key while its window was open (the kill-failure alert, a CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME its kill met, its kill's non-success that nothing else recorded, an outage onset, the notices of the launch in flight, the CONFLICT notice of a latch it set during step 2 included) is a server-log line and a `startup-errors.log` entry, and none was dropped (b.jg5 SRJ-1003). After the window has closed, a notice for the key routes as any other: a removed persona's is dropped by the notifier because the persona is no longer applied, and a destructive modify's goes to the new half once it is applied. The one exception is the all-clear of an outage whose onset the window wrote (or whose `ad-config-malformed` onset the submit muted), which is written the same way whenever it comes (b.jg5 SRJ-1002); an all-clear that also lists another class is split, and only the other classes' all-clear is posted. The lines are under Logging, [Persona lifecycle lines](#persona-lifecycle-lines-bav2-sr-65-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-307-bav2-sr-61).

**Not the CLI's bot teardown, and not Graceful Shutdown.** The CLI's `teardownBots` (`stop --stop-bots`, `clean_restart`) is graceful: it pauses each persona's bot and polls its status, killing it only on escalation or timeout, and never deletes a row, so the next start can resume it. Its kill is the ordinary checked kill in the bounded retry, never with agent-director's finished-row option, and no latch holds it back: a human-initiated teardown kills a row the server would hold too, and for a `pending` row with no launch start that kill ends no session (b.jg5 SRJ-503, SRJ-513). Graceful Shutdown leaves every instance and row in place. Persona teardown acts on one removed or destructively modified persona while the server keeps running: it kills its bot without waiting and keeps its row, which is never resumed because its key is retired. No persona teardown deletes a row.

### Destructive modify (b.av2 SR-8.6 as amended by b.deo SRI-406, SRI-408, SRI-502)

A persona whose `name` (same key), `credentials_file` path or `working_directory` changed is destructively modified: previewed `DESTRUCTIVE:`, then torn down in step 2 and brought up fresh in step 6. There is no separate path. Step 2 runs the [Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-307) on the persona as the previous configuration declares it (`destructiveOld`), and step 6 runs the [Bring-up at apply](#bring-up-at-apply-bav2-sr-61) on it as the confirmed configuration declares it (`destructiveNew`). Both run through the per-persona serializer, and steps 3–5 run between them.

**Fresh.** The teardown kills `cscb_<key>` and keeps its agent-director row (b.jg5 SRJ-715), and step 1 recorded the key as retired, so the launch in step 6 is a reuse spawn of `cscb_<key>` ([Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-bjg5-srj-806-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-407)): over the kept row, once it reads finished, it resets the row to a new life (with no row, an ordinary fresh spawn), and the conversation is not resumed. When the old row still reads live (its kill did not succeed, for example), the reuse collides with it, and the collision `get` sends it through the live-row sequence with the retired-key flag, which kills it and launches only after that kill succeeds: the new half never launches over a still-live old row. The new half is not held back by the old-life gate, since the hold is on its own row (b.jg5 SRJ-810's exception): it waits by the retired-key rule, the live-row sequence's step-6 reuse made only once the old row reads `ended` or `missing` (SRJ-805), and its launch starts no old-life wait and records no waiter. Any other persona whose working directory is the held one is held back until the hold ends ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809), **What a hold refuses**). Its old-life hold, begun at step 1 on the old declaration's working directory, ends when a read finds the old row finished or the reuse begins the new life ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809)). The new half starts with no stored choices: step 1 dropped the key's choices, any unwritten drop of the key from an earlier apply is written before its bring-up (b.deo SRI-408), and its key is retiring from step 1 until step 2 settles, so `set_channel_delivery` stores nothing for it meanwhile (b.deo SRI-406, SRI-502). The bring-up reads the credentials file the new declaration names, as it stands, with a new bring-up entry. The persona then holds that file's content and digest, so nothing is pending for it until the file changes again. Whatever changed, the old life is never resumed or reconnected, at the step-6 launch or any later one, a restart included. The next start's sweep keeps such a row, as it keeps every row, and records no retired key for it, since its key is applied.

**Unlatched (b.jg5 SRJ-504).** The teardown forgets the persona's latch and its notice episodes (steps 1, 3 and 9), the CONFLICT episode included, so the latch does not carry over: the new half starts unlatched, and its launch reaches agent-director. It latches only if that launch meets a CONFLICT itself, and then posts one CONFLICT notice to its own destination, since its CONFLICT episode begins afresh.

**The key stays applied.** Unlike a removed persona, the old half's key is still in the applied set after step 1, so the applied-set guard does not stop work for it. The teardown therefore also does these things:

- **At submit.** Besides the approver stop, the sequence stop and the launch-wait cancel every teardown makes, it cancels the persona's bring-up retries and its restart timer, and stops its UNAVAILABLE retry timer, as soon as it is submitted, before its serializer turn. Work already queued ahead of it for the key (a restart timer's work, a retry's work, a bring-up retry and its launch) then finds the persona not up or cancelled and launches nothing. Otherwise that work would launch the new declaration, only for the teardown to kill it. From then until step 6, the relaunch gate and the up predicate answer not up for it.
- **After the agent-director kill.** The kill arms no retry timer, and the stop once the launch in flight settled (step 3) and the stop after the kill (step 8) leave none a launch in flight or an earlier call armed, so none retries against the new half.
- **Its notices (b.jg5 SRJ-1003).** Between the submit and the turn, the submit mutes every notice-episode kind posted through the episodes (each counts as posted in its episode) and the `ad-config-malformed` onset, whose all-clear is then written, never posted ([Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-307), at submit). Only notices outside the episodes route as any configured persona's: another outage's onset (`tmux-unavailable`, `ad-unreachable`), the stuck-prompt warning, a spawn-failure notice and the lost-message notice. From the turn until the teardown completes, every notice for its key is written by the window (the server log and a `persona-teardown-notice` entry), never posted to the old half's destination or the new half's, and never held, so none waits for the new half's client and nothing is flushed to it once it is up. This covers the CONFLICT notice of a latch the old half's launch in flight sets during the teardown, and the *Cannot launch* alert of an `ErrInvalidFlags` hold it sets. An outage onset written in the window keeps its flag, and its all-clear, even one raised after the new half is up, is written the same way, never posted to the new half's destination; the new half's own notices post to its destination.

A destructively modified persona is listed in no other class of the change plan. Its other changed settings, in-place or next-launch, come with the fresh bring-up, and a credentials change needs the same path, so it never applies.

### In-place update (b.av2 SR-8.6 as amended by b.deo SRI-802)

Apply step 3 updates each persona modified in place (a change to the candidate's section in force, `channels`, `delivery` and `permission_prompts` in declarative mode or `invited.permission_prompts` in fungible mode, or to `dm.enabled` or `dm.contact` in either; b.deo SRI-802) through `PersonaLifecycle.updateInPlace` (`src/persona-lifecycle.ts`), all of them at once, each through the per-persona serializer. It makes no lifecycle call: no kill, delete, launch, reconnect or MCP session drop, and no Slack or agent-director call. The persona's instance, agent-director row, Slack connection and Web API client, MCP session and conversation are kept, as are its restart, backoff, health, outage and retry state, its reply-guard record, its tracked prompts and its held notices.

**The new values already apply at step 1.** Step 1's swap replaced the persona's entry in `personaConfig`, and every consumer reads that entry at each use, so step 3 has no values left to push. The consumers, and when each sees the change:

- **Inbound delivery and DM intake** (Data Flow, Inbound step 4): from the next event, by the mode in force, including the cross-persona `receive_all_shared` and unclaimed-channel results. In fungible mode no persona's `channels` is read, and a changed `invited.permission_prompts` changes the loop guard's input (`fungibleDestinationsOf`) from the next event.
- **MCP tool posting scope** (`checkPersonaTarget`, Outbound step 3): from the next tool call, which reads the mode and, in declarative mode, `channels` (b.deo SRI-601).
- **Destination** (`persona-destination.ts`): from the next permission prompt, stuck-prompt warning or notice, through the one rule `personaDestinationOf` over the configuration in effect: `permission_prompts` in declarative mode, `invited.permission_prompts` (`dm` when absent) in fungible mode (b.deo SRI-701). The permission poller resolves the persona each tick, the notifier and its flush on each notice, and the destination hold on each attempt.
- **Archive evidence** (b.av2 SR-7.4 as amended by b.deo SRI-704; the `delivery: all` scope of the JSONL checks, declarative mode only; in fungible mode no channel is counted): at the persona's next launch. A launch already in flight during the apply finishes with the entry it started with.

**A switch change is not a step-3 operation (b.deo SRI-201, SRI-203).** A change of `allow_invited_channels` applies at the step-1 swap, and every consumer above reads the mode at each use ([Next-launch and server-wide settings](#next-launch-and-server-wide-settings-bav2-sr-86-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-201-sri-203)). Only a persona whose section keys also changed is in step 3's input.

**What step 3 does.** When the key is no longer applied (a later apply removed it first; its teardown owns it), it does nothing and logs nothing. Otherwise, when any of `DM_DESTINATION_SETTINGS` (`src/persona-lifecycle.ts`: `permission_prompts`, `invited.permission_prompts`, `dm.enabled`, `dm.contact`) changed, it forgets the persona's cached DM conversation (`personaDestinations.forget`), so the next post to a `dm` destination opens the DM with the current contact through `conversations.open`. The cache also re-checks the contact on each use, so this is a cheap second guard. It then logs one line naming the changed settings (Logging, [Persona lifecycle lines](#persona-lifecycle-lines-bav2-sr-65-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-307-bav2-sr-61)). It never rejects, and dry run behaves the same.

**A persona that is not up.** A `retrying` or `broken` persona gets the same update: its cache entry is forgotten when one of those settings changed, and the line is logged. Its bring-up state and retries are not touched; when it comes up, it serves with the new values.

**Posted and held items.** Prompts already posted stay where they were posted and stay answerable, including a DM prompt after DMs are turned off (b.av2 SR-5.1 exception, as amended by b.deo SRI-601; see Permission Relay, [In-memory state](#in-memory-state-sr-1)). Nothing held is dropped or moved: a prompt the destination hold is holding is derived again on a later tick and goes to the new destination, and each held notice's retry re-reads the destination, so it goes to the new one too (Permission Relay, [Destination hold](#destination-hold-bav2-sr-71-failures-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-702-sri-703)). The same holds after a switch change, which changes the destination setting in force: posted prompts stay answerable, and held items go to the destination of the mode in force (b.deo SRI-703).

### Credentials change (b.av2 SR-8.6 step 4 as amended by b.deo SRI-805)

Apply step 4 applies each confirmed change to a persona's credentials content, at the same path, through `PersonaLifecycle.reconnectCredentials` (`src/persona-lifecycle.ts`), all of them at once, each through the per-persona serializer (b.av2 SR-6.6). The operation calls the bring-up controller's `changeCredentials` (`src/persona-bringup-controller.ts`) over the connection manager's `reconnectCredentials` and `replaceRetryTokens` (`src/persona-connections.ts`). It touches no other persona and makes no agent-director call. When the server is shutting down it logs `credentials change not applied — the server is shutting down` and does nothing.

**State is decided when it runs.** The controller reads the persona's bring-up state again. A persona credentials-broken by now resolves `{ kind: 'credentials-broken' }` and is left to step 6's recovery bring-up. A persona that is neither up nor retrying, or is unknown, cancelled or no longer applied, is skipped.

**The new file is checked first.** It is read once through the same local check a bring-up runs (`checkPersonaLocalSteps`), against the applied set as it stands after step 1. When it is missing, unreadable or invalid, or its real path is another applied persona's credentials file (b.av2 SR-1.4, apply part), nothing changes: the persona keeps its connection or its retry content, one `persona-credentials-change-failed` line is logged, and the change stays pending (b.av2 SR-8.3).

**An up persona is reconnected.** The new connection opens first and the old one closes only once the new one is up (see the `persona-connections.ts` entry of the Module Map). The persona stays `up` throughout, so its MCP session is not dropped, its instance is not touched and nothing is launched.

**A persona held for its `claude_config_dir` is retrying.** It has no connection (bug b.g57; see Config-dir-unresolvable under [Server-Managed Startup](#server-managed-startup-sr-11-event-1) step 5), so it takes the new tokens and digest as a retrying persona does, opens no connection, and connects with them once the directory resolves. Its cached DM conversation is forgotten when it takes the new content. A hold that starts while an up persona's reconnect is in flight or retrying closes that reconnect with the connection; the persona keeps the new content and connects with it on its return.

**Held and live content.** The controller keeps two things per persona: the held content (tokens and `credentialsDigest`, what the reload detection tick compares against, so it decides whether the change is pending) and the live content (`live`, what the persona's own connection uses). Both are set at bring-up. Right before a swap, at the first attempt or later, both become the new file's. While the new connection retries, the held content is the new file's and `live` stays the old. A refusal, at once or later, holds `live` again, so the change is pending again. The first attempt decides what the persona holds:

| First attempt | Connection | Held content (`credentialsDigest`) | Still pending | Line |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| New connection up | The new one is in use; the old one is closed | The new file's | No | `reconnected with its changed credentials; its instance and MCP session are kept` |
| Slack refused a new token | The old one stays in use; the new clients are discarded | The live content (what its own connection uses) | Yes | `persona-credentials-change-failed`, cause `bot_token refused by auth.test: Slack error <code>` or `app_token refused by the Socket Mode open: Slack error <code>` |
| Slack unreachable (a `start()` abandoned at 10 s included) | The old one stays in use; the new one retries on its own SR-3.2 schedule | The new file's | No: it is retrying with it | `its changed credentials cannot reach Slack yet; the new connection retries and the current one stays in use` |

Each line is worded from the persona's state after the attempt. When the persona's own connection was refused while the attempt ran (it is credentials-broken now, for example after a Web API call refused its bot token), it is not said to keep that connection:

- A refused change's `persona-credentials-change-failed` line ends `it stays broken by its credentials, and the change stays pending`.
- An unreachable one logs `its changed credentials cannot reach Slack yet; the new connection retries, and it stays broken by its credentials until that connection is in use`.
- A swap logs `reconnected with its changed credentials and up again; its instance is kept`, and the persona is launched as below.

A reconnect left retrying ends later in one of four ways:

- **It swaps.** The new connection comes into use and the reconnected line is logged (`…; its instance and MCP session are kept`, or `… and up again; its instance is kept` for a persona credentials-broken meanwhile), beside the connection manager's cleared line.
- **It is refused while the persona is still up on the old connection.** The controller holds `live` again, so the change is pending again (and so is an earlier change whose retrying reconnect this one replaced), and logs `persona-credentials-change-failed` ending `the current connection stays in use, and the change stays pending`. `live` is what the connection uses when the refusal lands, which a later swap may have changed since the change was confirmed.
- **It is refused after the old connection was itself refused meanwhile** (the persona is credentials-broken). The persona stays credentials-broken, holding the confirmed content, so nothing is pending, and the refusal is logged as `persona-credentials-refused`.
- **It is cancelled** by a later confirmed credentials change or by the persona's connection being stopped (a teardown, a recovery bring-up, shutdown). Its open `persona-slack-unreachable` episode ends with a cleared line saying why (Logging, [Persona bring-up lines](#persona-bring-up-lines-bav2-sr-103-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-901-sri-902)).

A persona that was credentials-broken meanwhile and whose pending reconnect then swaps is `up` again. It is launched through its launch path's collision ladder, logging `up after its confirmed credentials change — launching`.

**A retrying persona retries with the new content.** A persona that is Slack-unreachable, directory-broken or still on its first attempt takes the new tokens and digest at once, as both held and live content, so nothing stays pending. A Slack-unreachable one gets them through `replaceRetryTokens`; a directory-broken one holds them for when its directory retry reaches Slack. It logs `it retries its bring-up with its changed credentials`. With a locally bad new file, it keeps retrying with its current content, and the `persona-credentials-change-failed` line ends `it keeps retrying with its current credentials, and the change stays pending`.

**The DM destination is forgotten before the swap.** The persona's cached DM conversation is forgotten (`personaDestinations.forget`) in the controller's `beforeSwap` hook, which the manager runs right before every swap, at the first attempt or later, while the persona still reports its old connection. So when the persona is reported up on the new connection and the notifier flushes its held notices, none goes to the old app's DM; the new credentials may belong to another app, with another DM. A throw is logged as `forgetting its cached DM conversation failed: <thrown value>`, and the swap goes ahead.

### Recovery of a credentials-broken persona (b.av2 SR-6.4)

While the server runs, a credentials-broken persona recovers only through a confirmed change to its credentials file. Credentials-broken is `isCredentialsBroken`: outcome `broken` with a local credentials cause (missing, unreadable, invalid or a real-path collision), or with Slack's refusal (`persona-credentials-refused`). Apply step 6 brings up each credentials-changed persona that step 4 did not reconnect because it was credentials-broken, whether or not an instance of it runs, through `PersonaLifecycle.bringUp(persona, applied, { recovery: true })`.

The operation checks the state again when it runs. A persona no longer credentials-broken (step 4 left it here because it was, and a pending reconnect of an earlier change has brought it up since) logs `not brought up again — it is not broken by its credentials now, so its changed credentials are applied as a credentials change` and gets the confirmed change as step 4 would have applied it: the credentials change body runs directly in the same serializer turn (not through the serializer again), with its usual lines, and the operation resolves the persona's outcome after it. Only when that change finds the persona credentials-broken again does the recovery go ahead. Otherwise it logs `broken by its credentials and its credentials file changed — bringing it up again` and clears what the broken bring-up left:

1. Its bring-up state and timers are cancelled (the controller's `cancel`).
2. Its connection is stopped (the manager's `stop`). The bring-up then builds a fresh connection entry with a fresh episode tracker, so a new refusal is logged rather than swallowed by the old episode.
3. Its cached DM conversation is forgotten.

A step that fails logs `<step> before bringing it up again failed: <thrown value>`, and the rest still run. The server's `shuttingDown` flag is checked again once these steps are done, so a shutdown that began meanwhile connects and launches nothing (`not brought up — the server is shutting down`). Then comes the same procedure as [Bring-up at apply](#bring-up-at-apply-bav2-sr-61): storage check, bring-up (a new `persona-start` line, the file read as it stands and checked against the confirmed set) and, when up, the launch. The instance and agent-director row were kept while it was down (b.av2 SR-6.4), so the launch reaches them through the collision ladder and the history is kept. A file that is still bad leaves the persona broken with the new cause logged. It then holds the new file's digest, so nothing is pending until the file changes again.

### Template refresh (b.av2 SR-8.6 step 5 as amended by b.deo SRI-805)

Apply step 5 refreshes the agent-director template once, through `PersonaLifecycle.refreshTemplate(applied)` and `refreshSlackChannelBotTemplate` (`src/agent-director-template.ts`). `applyStepsFor` selects it only when the change plan's `configDirsChanged` is true: the set of effective config directories (`effectiveClaudeConfigDirs`, compared lexically) differs between the applied and the confirmed personas. That also holds for a plan with no effective change. It runs after step 4, which settles once every reconnect's first attempt has settled, and before step 6. So a persona that step 6 brings up with a new directory launches from the refreshed template.

**Memory-read rules only.** The refresh overwrites the template with the params the boot install wrote (`installSlackChannelBotTemplate`'s `params`), with only the `allow` list derived afresh from the confirmed personas (`deriveMemoryReadAllowRules`, the boot derivation). The rules therefore keep the `projects/*/memory/**` scope and never cover a config-dir root. Every other field is kept, including `claude_args` with the start-time MCP config and system-prompt flags (the append file is not probed again), and `name`, `label`, `deny` and `relay_mode`. A changed server-wide setting behind those arguments takes effect at the next start. The refresh belongs to no persona, so it does not go through the serializer.

**Not fatal.** A rejection, either a typed agent-director error or any throw, is logged in one line and nothing else happens. No startup error is recorded, nothing is posted, no persona is touched, and the rest of the apply and later ticks run. Nothing retries it. The rules stay as last installed until a later confirmed change alters the config-dir set again, or until the next start's boot install. Meanwhile, a persona using a directory new to the set gets a permission prompt for each memory-note read. The boot install is different: a rejection there is fatal (Server-Managed Startup step 3). In dry run the refresh makes the same call the boot install makes. The lines are under Logging, [Persona lifecycle lines](#persona-lifecycle-lines-bav2-sr-65-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-307-bav2-sr-61).

### Next-launch and server-wide settings (b.av2 SR-8.6 as amended by b.deo SRI-201, SRI-203)

**`claude_config_dir` and `stop_hook_bootstrap`, own or inherited.** These get no lifecycle call at apply. Step 1's swap is all they need, and the running instance and its conversation are kept. The persona's next launch (a spawn, resume, restart or retry launch) reads the new value from the applied set. For `claude_config_dir`, that covers `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, the pre-launch directory check, the `config_dir` label, the trust patch, the reply-guard steps and the transcript diagnosis. A changed directory has a different `config_dir` label, so the ladder's `config_dir` guard replaces the row by a reuse spawn of the same id, which starts a new conversation (a live row through the live-row sequence first; SR-6.2 as amended, b.jg5 SRJ-1504), with no row deleted; the old history stays in the old directory, archived to the earlier life. A new path to the same real directory keeps the label, and the persona resumes.

For `stop_hook_bootstrap`, the reply-guard record is written at the persona's next launch (`preLaunchReplyGuard`). The apply rewrites no record, and a neighbour's launch writes only its own. The apply does not run the per-directory install rule either: the next launch's launch pass does, over the new and previous directories.

**Inherited defaults.** The top-level `claude_config_dir` and `stop_hook_bootstrap` act only through the personas that inherit them. The loader has already resolved them into each persona, so a changed default takes effect at each inheriting persona's next launch, exactly as an own change does.

**Server-wide settings.** Step 1 writes them to `config.json.last-applied`. The server then runs `configInEffect(startTime, applied)` (`src/reload.ts`): the confirmed personas and the confirmed `allow_invited_channels` switch over every other server-wide setting it started with. Except for the switch (below), running consumers keep their start-time values until the next start, which runs the record. These include the listener's `port` and `bind`, the intervals, timeouts and restart delay, `resume_enabled`, the cron paths, the template's server-wide arguments, and `ack_reaction`, `reply_chunk_limit` and `reply_chunk_mode` (read through `getReplySettings()`). The exceptions are `stop_timeout` and `exit_timeout`. Only the CLI uses them, and it reads them from the record (`readAppliedPersonaConfig`), so once applied they apply to its next `stop` or `clean_restart`. `agent_director_call_timeout_ms` is used by both: the running server keeps its start-time value (`configInEffect`) until its next start, and the CLI reads the recorded value as soon as an apply rewrites the record. The preview says so for each.

**The switch is applied in place (b.deo SRI-201, SRI-203).** `allow_invited_channels` is the one server-wide setting a confirmed change applies at once: taken from the confirmed configuration, it gives the confirmed mode from the step-1 swap, from the next event, tool call, prompt and notice, read by every consumer through `channelModeOf` at each use. It runs no lifecycle operation of its own (no teardown, bring-up, launch, reconnect or in-place operation), every session is kept, and it always matches the mode the confirmed personas were resolved in.

**Several changes at once.** A destructive change overrides everything else (see [Destructive modify](#destructive-modify-bav2-sr-86-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-406-sri-408-sri-502)). Otherwise the kinds combine. A persona can be modified in place (step 3), have its credentials content changed (step 4, after step 3) and have next-launch changes (its next launch).

### Per-persona serialization (b.av2 SR-6.6)

Lifecycle operations on one persona run strictly in sequence. Operations on different personas are independent, except that an apply finishes each step for every persona before the next step starts. The mechanism is a per-key promise chain, `createPersonaSerializer` in `src/persona-serializer.ts`. `server.ts` builds one instance at module scope (`personaLifecycle`) and hands its `run` to every user. `run(key, operation)` starts an operation only once every operation already submitted for that key has settled; a rejected operation doesn't stop the next one.

| Runs through the serializer | Doesn't |
|---|---|
| A fired restart timer's work: its shutdown and up checks, the liveness probe, reconnect, kill and launch (`RestartDeps.serialize`); a retry timer's work (`runRestartRetry`): its in-flight check first, then the same work | Scheduling a restart, the backoff, the cap, the `activeLaunches` guard and the human-trigger clamp; the UNAVAILABLE retry timer's scheduling and backoff, and its retry action's checks before the call |
