| `[slack] conflict-latch: re-check of <ref> — case=<case> step=<step> call=<call> answer=<answer>` | `latchRecheckRoundLine`: once per round. `<step>` is step 1's outcome: `clear-reported-in`, `clear-gone`, `spawn-retry` (no row, for a latch whose refused operation is a spawn: that spawn is retried), `finished-row-retry` (no row, for a "not this launch's session" latch: the finished-row retry), `step-2` (step 2's table decided), `no-information` (step 1's read failed) or `not-decided` (`RECHECK_LINE_STEP_NOT_DECIDED`: step 1's read itself relatched the persona with another case or left it not latched, so nothing was decided); the `RECHECK_STEP_*` constants hold the others. `<call>` is `none` (no call after the read), `read-pane` (the probe), `read-pane-pending` (the lap read), `plain-spawn`, `reuse-spawn`, `resume`, `restart-decision`, `finished-row-retry` (its `get` made no launch) or `finished-row-retry:<launch>`, and after a probe that found the condition cleared `read-pane+<after>`, `<after>` being `none` (no single retry, `no retry (at-cap)` for a P at the restart cap), `find-missing` (the run refused, or P no longer latched on the same case after it) or `find-missing+<call>`, with the answer `probe-cleared (<kind>); <what came of it>`. `<answer>` is `still-latched`, `no-information` (a failed read; with ` (<what>)` after a call that gave none, or a launch a gate stopped: `at-cap`, `not-up`, `held`, `sequence-waiting`; `at-cap` too for a run of the restart path's decision at the restart cap, and `observer-failed` for one that could not be made), `cleared (<step or action>)`, `relatched (case=<case>)`, `relatched-by-read (case=<case>)` (step 1 relatched; the round ends), `not-latched`, `not-applied`, or for a `read-pane` its verdict and the answer's kind (`still-latched (pane)`, `probe-cleared (gone)`, `kept (conflict)`, `config (config)`, `relatch: <latch outcome> (conflict)`, `unusable-name: <latch outcome> (unusable-name)`) |
| `[slack] conflict-latch: persona=<key> cleared — case=<case> session="<name>" reason="<reason>"; recovery notice posted` | `latchClearedLine`: once per clear (b.jg5 SRJ-506, SRJ-1014), through the clear entry; `<reason>` is SRJ-1005's, a state rendered as a description is. `recovery notice not posted (the notice episodes are closed)` once the episodes are closed at shutdown |
| `[slack] conflict-latch: persona=<key> clear step failed (<step>): <error>` | A step of the clear entry threw (`forget`, `timer stop`, `recovery post`, `episode end`); the next step still runs |

| `[slack] latch-recheck: the run of the restart path's decision failed for <ref>: <error>` | The run threw; nothing is cleared |
| `[slack] latch-recheck: the latch's set observer could not be added for <ref>'s run of the restart path's decision: <error> — its permit could not be revoked, so no run is made; the persona stays latched (b.jg5 SRJ-505, SRJ-506)` | `latchRecheckObserverFailedLine`: adding the run's set observer threw; no run, answer `observer-failed` (no information) |
| `[slack] latch-recheck: the clear hand-off failed for <ref>: <error>` | The clear hand-off threw; it is swallowed |
| `[slack] runRestartWorkInTurn: deps not initialized — skipping the re-check's run for persona=<key>` | The run before `initRestart` |
| `[slack] conflict-latch: persona=<key> re-check timer could not be set: <error> — not armed` | The clock's `setTimeout` threw |
| `[slack] conflict-latch: persona=<key> re-check round failed: <error>` | A round rejected; the next is still armed while the persona is latched |
| `[slack] conflict-latch: persona=<key> forget observer failed: <error>` | A forget observer threw; it is swallowed |
| `[slack] <site>: <what> refused for <ref>: <failure> — the persona was latched elsewhere during the call, so that latch stands: nothing is set and nothing more is called for it (b.jg5 SRJ-502)` | `latchedElsewhereDuringCall` (`latchedElsewhereDuringCallLine`): outside a re-check, a launch's CONFLICT or UNUSABLE NAME for a persona latched while its call was awaited |

### Forced-launch seam lines (b.jg5 SRJ-1306 as amended by b.deo SRI-1402 to SRI-1404; b.jg5 SRJ-1401)

The forced-launch seams' own lines (`_forceResumeForPersona`, `_forceReuseSpawnForPersona`; the `session-manager.ts` entry), to the standard error of the process that calls them, `tests/integration/fixtures/fmk-driver.ts`. `<ref>` is `"<name>" (key=<key>)`; `<what>` is `forced resume` or `forced reuse spawn`; `<failure>` is `describeAgentDirectorFailure`'s. The paths they run log their own lines as well: the forced `resume`'s handler lines carry the head `[slack] forced-launch:` (`[slack] forced-launch: resumed <ref>`, and `resumeNotFoundSpawnLine`'s pair after an `ErrSpawnNotFound`, listed in `docs/engineering-guide.md` under Log Messages), and the reuse logs its `[slack] reuseSpawnForPersona:` lines, its success line naming the forced launch ([Reuse spawn](#reuse-spawn-bjg5-srj-112-srj-708)).

| Line | When |
|---|---|
| `[slack] forced-launch: <what> of <ref> — no row state decides it (a test seam for tests/integration/fixtures/fmk-driver.ts)` | `runForcedLaunch`, just before the forced call |
| `[slack] forced-launch: launch already in flight for <ref> — no <what>; joining it` | A launch of the persona was in flight in this process: no call, its result answered |
| `[slack] dry-run: skipping the <what> of <ref> cwd=<working directory>` | Dry run: no call, `no-op` |
| `[slack] forced-launch: <failure> on the forced resume of <ref> — a reuse spawn of the same id follows; nothing is deleted (b.jg5 SRJ-707)` | The forced `resume` answered a no-transcript error: the no-transcript reuse follows |
| `[slack] forced-launch: <failure> on the forced resume of <ref> — nothing is read, killed or launched; answering retrying, no spawn-failure notice, nothing counted; the retry timer <is armed\|could not be armed> (cause=spawn-not-resumable-lost-race; b.jg5 SRJ-710)` | The forced `resume` answered `ErrSpawnNotResumable` |
| `[slack] forced-launch: the <reuse spawn\|fresh spawn after ErrSpawnNotFound on resume> of <ref> collided with a live row — nothing launched; answering retrying, the retry timer <is armed\|could not be armed> (cause=collision; b.jg5 SRJ-112, SRJ-1015)` | `forcedLaunchCollided`: the forced reuse spawn, the reuse after the forced `resume`'s no-transcript answer, or the plain spawn after its `ErrSpawnNotFound` met a live row |
| `[slack] forced-launch: counting the launch of <ref> failed: <error>` | Counting the forced launch's result threw (`countLaunchOutsideRestartWork`); the answer is unchanged |

### Clear-by-hand route and `server.port` lines (b.jg5 SRJ-510)

The `/clear-latch` route's and the `server.port` record's lines, to `server.log` only ([POST /clear-latch](#post-clear-latch), [server.port](#serverport-state_dirserverport)). Built in `src/clear-latch.ts`. A latched persona's clear logs only the clear entry's `cleared` line (above, reason `cleared by hand`); nothing is logged for a 400, 403 or 405.

| Line | When |
|---|---|
| `[slack] clear-latch: persona "<name>" (key=<key>) was not latched; nothing changed` | `clearLatchNotLatchedLine`: a 200 with `cleared` false |
| `[slack] clear-latch: no persona in the applied configuration has the requested name or key; nothing cleared` | `clearLatchUnknownPersonaLine`: a 404; the argument is never repeated |
| `[slack] clear-latch: the clear of persona "<name>" (key=<key>) failed: <error>` | `clearLatchFailedLine`: the clear by hand rejected (a 500); `<error>` through `describeThrownValue` |
| `[slack] server.port: could not write <path>; clear-latch cannot reach this server until it restarts: <error>` | `serverPortWriteFailedLine`: the record's write at start failed; the server keeps running |

### Reload lines (b.av2 SR-8.7 as amended by b.deo SRI-403, SRI-407; b.av2 SR-10.3 as amended by b.deo SRI-901, SRI-905)

The reload controller (`src/reload.ts`) and its tick driver (`src/reload-timer.ts`) log their start, detection and apply lines to `server.log` only, with the `[slack]` prefix, through the injected `log`; none goes to `startup-errors.log` or to Slack, and none carries a token, file content, credentials digest or fingerprint. Its class list is `RELOAD_DIAGNOSTIC_CLASSES`, separate from the persona classes; it holds `reload-record-write-failed`, `reload-nothing-pending`, `reload-preview`, `reload-invalid`, `reload-applied`, `reload-noop` and `reload-stale-confirmation`. A confirmed apply emits the last three, `reload-invalid` and `reload-record-write-failed`; see [Confirmation](#confirmation-sr-85) and [The apply pipeline](#the-apply-pipeline-sr-86-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-805). See Server-Managed Startup step 2a for the rules behind the start lines and [Reload Detection Tick](#reload-detection-tick-bav2-sr-82-sr-83) for the detection lines.

| Line | When | Class |
|---|---|---|
| `[slack] Starting from the last-applied record "<record>"` | A start with a valid record | — |
| `[slack] No last-applied record: recorded the configuration file "<config>" as "<record>"` | A start with no record, after the record is written | — |
| `[slack] reload-record-write-failed: cannot write the last-applied record "<record>" (<errno code>); the server does not start and nothing is applied` | A start with no record whose record write fails before the rename; the server exits 1. The errno code appears only when the error has one | `reload-record-write-failed` |
| `[slack] reload-record-write-failed: the last-applied record "<record>" was written but its directory could not be synced (<errno code>), so it may not survive a crash, and the next start will run it; the server does not start` | A start with no record whose record was renamed into place but whose directory fsync (or open) failed; the server exits 1. The errno code appears only when the error has one | `reload-record-write-failed` |
| `[slack] Fatal: configuration error — <message>` | A start with no record whose `config.json` is missing, unreadable or invalid; exits 1 | — |
| `[slack] Fatal: last-applied record error — <cause> Deleting the last-applied record "<record>" makes the next start apply the configuration file "<config>" as it stands.` | A start whose record exists but cannot be read or validated; exits 1. Unclassed: SR-10.3 (as amended by b.deo SRI-901) gives it no class | — |
| `[slack] reload-preview: A configuration change is pending; nothing has been applied. <counts, or no effective change: …> (preview in "<pending>")`, then `[slack] reload-preview: <line>` for each further preview line | A detection pass whose pending state changes to pending with a new fingerprint, for a valid candidate: every line of the preview, the same text as the pending file's body, the switch's line and the recorded lines included (their texts are under [The preview](#the-preview-sr-84-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-803-sri-804)). Only the first line carries the suffix, and it is dropped when this pass's pending-file write failed | `reload-preview` |
| `[slack] reload-invalid: the pending configuration is invalid and nothing will be applied: <error> (preview in "<pending>")` | The same, for an invalid candidate: a single line (not a multi-line preview), with the loader's full error, or `the configuration file "<config>" does not exist.` / `… cannot be read (<code>).` / `… is larger than the 64 KiB limit.`; no `reload-preview` line. The suffix is dropped when the write failed | `reload-invalid` |
| `[slack] reload-invalid: the confirmed configuration is invalid, so nothing is applied: <error>` | A matching confirmation of an invalid candidate; the same errors as above. Nothing is applied and the record is untouched. It follows the pending-time line logged when the `INVALID` preview was written; when the confirmation was already present on the pass that first saw the candidate (for example at start), that pass logs only this line | `reload-invalid` |
| `[slack] reload-applied: applied the confirmed configuration change without a restart (personas: <n> added, <n> removed, <n> destructively modified, <n> modified in place, <n> with changed credentials; server-wide settings: <n> changed); the last-applied record "<record>" now holds it` | A confirmed valid change with an effect, after step 1 and every bound later step. The counts are the preview header's | `reload-applied` |
| `[slack] reload-noop: the confirmed configuration has no effective change, so no persona and no server-wide setting changed; the last-applied record "<record>" was rewritten with it` | A confirmed `no effective change` candidate, after the record was rewritten, a candidate whose only changes are recorded ones included (b.deo SRI-804) | `reload-noop` |
| `[slack] reload-stale-confirmation: the confirmation "<apply>" <reason>; nothing is applied` | A confirmation that doesn't match the current files (`does not match the configuration as it stands (…)`), can't be read (`cannot be read (<code>)`, `is larger than the 64 KiB limit`) or has no fingerprint (`holds no well-formed fingerprint (…)`). Once per confirmation | `reload-stale-confirmation` |
| `[slack] reload-record-write-failed: cannot write the last-applied record "<record>" (<errno code>); the confirmed change is not applied and stays pending` | A confirmed apply's record write failed before the rename; nothing is applied. When step 1 wrote the retired-key record, the line ends with its restore (below) | `reload-record-write-failed` |
| `[slack] reload-record-write-failed: wrote the last-applied record "<record>" but could not sync its directory (<errno code>); <restore outcome>; the confirmed change is not applied and stays pending` | A confirmed apply's record write whose directory sync failed. `<restore outcome>` is `the previous record was written back`, `the previous record was written back, though its directory could not be synced either`, or `writing the previous record back failed too (<errno code>), so the next start may run the unapplied change`. When step 1 wrote the retired-key record, the line ends with its restore (below) | `reload-record-write-failed` |
| `…; the retired-key record "<retired-keys>" is put back to what it held before this apply: the keys this apply recorded are removed again, and keys recorded before it stay (b.jg5 SRJ-804)` | The end of either confirmed-apply line above when step 1 wrote the retired-key record and its restore succeeded. When the restore failed it ends `…; putting the retired-key record "<retired-keys>" back to what it held before this apply failed, so the keys this apply recorded stay retired (b.jg5 SRJ-804)` | `reload-record-write-failed` |
| `[slack] reload-record-write-failed: cannot write the retired-key record "<retired-keys>"; the last-applied record "<record>" is not rewritten, and the confirmed change is not applied and stays pending; <restore> (b.jg5 SRJ-803, SRJ-804)` | Step 1's own write of the retired-key record failed; nothing is applied. `<restore>` is `the retired-key record holds what this server held as retired before this apply`, or `putting the retired-key record back to what it held before this apply failed too, so a key this apply recorded that reached the file stays retired`. The store's own `retired-keys: cannot record …` line carries the write's error, so count `reload-record-write-failed` lines, not lines | `reload-record-write-failed` |
| `[slack] reload-record-write-failed: cannot write the stored-choice file "<path>" before bringing up a persona whose stored choices were dropped; the retired-key record is not written, the last-applied record "<path>" is not rewritten, and the confirmed change is not applied and stays pending (b.deo SRI-408; b.jg5 SRJ-804)` (`reloadChannelDeliveryWriteFailedLine(channelDeliveryPath, lastAppliedPath)`) | Step 1's first write, the stored-choice file's unwritten drops for a persona the apply brings up, failed (an unsynced rename included); nothing is applied, no retired-key record is written and no approver stopped. It names the two files only: the store's own `[slack] channel-delivery: cannot write the drop of …` line ([Stored-choice file lines](#stored-choice-file-lines-bdeo-sri-904-sri-905)) carries the error code | `reload-record-write-failed` |
| `[slack] reload: dropping the stored choices of the retired keys failed: <thrown value> (b.deo SRI-406)` | Step 1's drop batch threw (a failed drop write is the store's own line and does not throw); the apply goes on. Described by `describeThrownValue` | — |
| `[slack] reload: <marking\|clearing> the retiring keys failed: <thrown value> (b.deo SRI-502)` | Marking the destructive modifies' keys retiring at step 1, or clearing them once step 2 has settled, threw; the apply goes on. Described by `describeThrownValue` | — |
| `[slack] reload: cannot remove the confirmation "<apply>" (<errno code>); it was acted on once and is ignored until its content changes` | The confirmation's delete failed. Once per confirmation content; later deletes are retried silently | — |
| `[slack] reload: removed the confirmation "<apply>" but could not sync its directory (<errno code>); it may reappear after a crash` | The confirmation's unlink succeeded but its directory sync failed; counts as removed | — |
| `[slack] reload: apply step <n> (<step>) failed: <thrown value>` | A step body (2–6) threw as a whole; the next step still runs. Described by `describeThrownValue` | — |
| `[slack] reload: apply step <n> (<step>) failed for persona "<name>" (key=<key>): <thrown value>` | One persona's lifecycle operation in a default step body (2, 3, 4 or 6) rejected; the step's other personas and the next step still run. Described by `describeThrownValue` | — |
| `[slack] reload: updating the server's applied configuration failed: <thrown value>` | `onApplied` threw at step 1; the apply goes on | — |
| `[slack] reload: cannot check <what>: <thrown value>; the preview says it could not be checked` | A fact the preview needs could not be gathered: `<what>` is `whether the added persona "<name>" (key=<key>) can come up`, `the claude_config_dir of persona "<name>" (key=<key>)` (a changed one) or `the bring-up state of persona "<name>" (key=<key>)`; the preview carries it as unknown. Once, until a pass gathers every fact again. Described by `describeThrownValue` | — |
| `[slack] reload-nothing-pending: the configuration file and the credentials files it references match what is applied; no change is pending, and the pending-change file "<pending>" is removed` | Once, when the pass that removed the pending file changes the state from pending to nothing pending, or when the first pass after a start actually removes a leftover pending file (including a removal whose directory sync failed). Never at a clean start | `reload-nothing-pending` |
| `[slack] reload-nothing-pending: the configuration file and the credentials files it references match what is applied; no change is pending` | Once, when the state changes from pending to nothing pending and there was no pending file to remove | `reload-nothing-pending` |
| `[slack] reload: cannot write the pending-change file "<pending>" (<errno code>); retrying at the next check` | A pending-file write failed before its rename; once per episode. An episode ends at the next success or when the derived state changes | — |
| `[slack] reload: wrote the pending-change file "<pending>" but could not sync its directory (<errno code>); writing it again at the next check` | A pending-file write whose directory sync failed; once per episode. An episode ends at the next success or when the derived state changes | — |
| `[slack] reload: cannot remove the pending-change file "<pending>" (<errno code>); retrying at the next check` | A pending-file unlink failed; the file stays. Once per episode (an episode ends at the next success or when the derived state changes) | — |
| `[slack] reload: removed the pending-change file "<pending>" but could not sync its directory (<errno code>); it may reappear after a crash, and the next start removes it` | A pending-file delete whose unlink succeeded but whose directory open or fsync failed (`DurableUnlinkUnsyncedError`). Treated as removed: the removed variant of `reload-nothing-pending` follows when due. Once per such removal; not retried | — |
| `[slack] reload: detection check failed: <thrown value>; checking again at the next tick` | Logged by the controller (`reload.ts`): a detection pass failed unexpectedly; once per episode (until a pass succeeds). The thrown value is described by `describeThrownValue` (no message) | — |
| `[slack] reload: detection check failed: <thrown value>; checking again in 5 s` | Logged by the tick driver (`reload-timer.ts`), only for a pass that throws past the controller's own catch; every such pass, then the chain re-arms. Described by `describeThrownValue` | — |
| `[slack] reload: detection timer start() called more than once — ignoring (the timer is single-use)` (or `… called after stop() …`) | A programming error: the single-use tick driver was started twice or after stop | — |

The operator-facing entries, with fixes, are in `skills/debug-slack-channel-bots/SKILL.md`.

### Runtime version re-check lines (b.jg5 SRJ-205, SRJ-206)

The runtime version re-check (`src/ad-version-gate.ts`) logs through the `log` dependency `main()` passes it (`console.error`, so `server.log`). A passing re-check logs nothing; a run of could-not-run re-checks logs one line, at its first.

| Line | When | Also in `startup-errors.log` |
|---|---|---|
| `[<timestamp>] [ad-below-phase1-floor] <runtime floor message>` or `[<timestamp>] [ad-system-install-too-old] <runtime too-old message>` | A stop: written by `recordStartupError`, once | Yes, the same line |
| `[slack] Shutting down: the runtime version re-check refused the agent-director binary (see startup-errors.log)` | After the entry, from `shutdown` (after its timers are stopped); the usual shutdown lines follow, ending in `[slack] Shutdown complete` and exit code 1 | — |
| `[slack] Shutdown did not complete within 30 s — exiting with code 1` | The shutdown the stop ran had not exited 30 s (`SHUTDOWN_DEADLINE_MS`) after the stop callback armed the deadline (`src/shutdown-deadline.ts`); written once, in place of `[slack] Shutdown complete`, right before the process exits with code 1 | — |
| `[slack] agent-director version re-check: recording the refusal failed: <thrown value>; stopping the server anyway` | `recordStartupError` threw during a stop; the stop still runs | — |
| `[slack] agent-director version re-check: the stop callback threw: <thrown value>` | The `stop` callback threw | — |
| `[slack] agent-director version re-check: the runtime re-check could not run: <description>; the server keeps running and checks again at the next 120 s re-check` | The first could-not-run re-check (timed or triggered) after start or after a passing re-check; the rest of that run of failures logs nothing. `<description>` is the error's name (`ErrSystemInstallUnreachable (reason <reason>, binary at <path>)` for that error), the thrown value's type or `no answer within the 30 s time limit`. Never posted to Slack | No |
| `[slack] agent-director version re-check: a tick listener failed: <thrown value>; the re-check carries on` | A tick listener threw or rejected | — |
| `[slack] agent-director version re-check: a version-changed listener failed: <thrown value>; the re-check carries on` | A version-changed listener threw or rejected; the other listeners still run | — |
| `[slack] agent-director version re-check: start() called more than once …`, `… start() called after dispose() …`, `… already installed — ignoring the second install`, `… install after dispose — ignoring (the server is shutting down)` | A programming error, or an install racing a shutdown | — |

Thrown values are described by `describeThrownValue`.

### `ErrInvalidFlags` hold lines (b.jg5 SRJ-207)

The hold (`src/invalid-flags-hold.ts`) and the paths that ask it log through `console.error` (so `server.log`); nothing here is posted to Slack except the hold's one alert ([The `ErrInvalidFlags` hold](#the-errinvalidflags-hold-bjg5-srj-207-srj-1008)). A version is rendered by `describeHoldVersion` (`unknown` for none, `unreadable` for anything but a short version string). The lines that end a hold on a version change follow a passing re-check, beside the [runtime version re-check lines](#runtime-version-re-check-lines-bjg5-srj-205-srj-206).

| Line | When |
|---|---|
| `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: persona=<key> held — a reuse spawn answered ErrInvalidFlags and the version re-check did not stop the server; the hold began under agent-director version <version>; no launch is made for it until the binary's version changes, the server restarts or it is torn down (b.jg5 SRJ-207)` | A new hold (`invalidFlagsHoldSetLine`); a persona already held logs nothing |
| `[slack] reuseSpawnForPersona: reuse spawn of <ref> answered <failure> (after one immediate agent-director version re-check: <answer>) — <held>; answering held: no other launch, no delete, no spawn-failure notice, nothing counted (b.jg5 SRJ-112, SRJ-207)` | A reuse spawn's `ErrInvalidFlags` whose re-check answered `pass`, `could-not-run` or `not-running` (`reuseInvalidFlagsHeldLine`), logged after the hold's set line above (the `set` logs it). `<held>` is `the persona is held under agent-director version <version>`, `no ErrInvalidFlags hold is installed, so nothing is held` or `holding the persona failed: <error>` |
| `[slack] <site>: not launching <ref> — it is held on ErrInvalidFlags; no agent-director call (held; b.jg5 SRJ-207)` | A launch entry made no launch for a held persona (`invalidFlagsHeldNoLaunchLine`); `<site>` is `spawnForPersona`, `startLiveRowSequence`, `launchForLiveRowSequence` or `latch-recheck` (a latch re-check's own launch, for a latched persona; [The re-check](#the-re-check-bjg5-srj-505)). A held query that threw adds ` (the held query failed: <error> — taken as held)` |
| `[slack] Not scheduling restart for persona=<key> — the persona is held on ErrInvalidFlags; no timer armed (b.jg5 SRJ-207)` | `scheduleRestart` for a held persona |
| `[slack] Skipping restart for persona=<key> — the persona is held on ErrInvalidFlags; no agent-director call, nothing recorded (b.jg5 SRJ-207)` | The restart work's first held gate |
| `[slack] Restart for persona=<key> goes no further <where> — the persona is held on ErrInvalidFlags; nothing more is called for it, nothing recorded (b.jg5 SRJ-207)` | The restart work's held gate asked again (`after its liveness probe`, `after its escalate-dead reconnect`, `after its re-probe`, `before its kill`) |
| `[slack] Session relaunch for persona=<key> ended held on ErrInvalidFlags — not counted; nothing more is done for it (b.jg5 SRJ-207)` | The restart work's launch answered `'skipped'` and the persona is held |
| `[slack] unavailable-retry: persona=<key> stopped[ (pending-only)] — the persona is held on ErrInvalidFlags` | The retry timer stopped by the hold's set reaction, the pre-call held check or a `held` outcome |
| `[slack] unavailable-retry: persona=<key> the held query failed: <error> — taken as held; no agent-director call` | The retry action's held query threw |
| `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: persona=<key> hold ended — agent-director version <began> changed to <new> (b.jg5 SRJ-207)` | A passing re-check found a version different from the one the hold began under (`invalidFlagsHoldEndLine`) |
| `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: persona=<key> retried at once after its hold ended (b.jg5 SRJ-207)`, then `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: persona=<key> retry after its hold ended answered <outcome> (b.jg5 SRJ-207)` | The ended persona is still applied: one run of the retry entry, and its outcome |
| `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: persona=<key> not retried after its hold ended — it is not in the applied configuration (b.jg5 SRJ-207)` | The ended persona is no longer applied |
| `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: persona=<key> hold forgotten — it began under agent-director version <version>; nothing is posted or retried (b.jg5 SRJ-207)` | A teardown's `forget` or shutdown's `forgetAll` (`invalidFlagsHoldForgetLine`) |
| `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: persona=<key> set observer failed: <error>`, `… end observer failed: <error>`, `… retry timer stop failed: <error>`, `… alert failed: <error>`, `… ending its hold episode failed: <error>`, `… its retry failed: <error>`, and `[slack] invalid-flags-hold: ending the holds on a version change failed: <error>` | A failing observer or reaction step; the other steps still run |

Thrown values are described by `describeThrownValue`.

### agent-director settings lines (b.jg5 SRJ-209)

The settings reader (`src/ad-settings.ts`) logs through `console.error` (so `server.log`); every line starts with `AD_SETTINGS_LOG_PREFIX`, `[slack] agent-director settings:`. The startup call-timeout check (b.jg5 SRJ-213) writes the last two lines through the log its caller passes, `console.error` in `server.ts`'s start step. An accepted read logs the values line only when it is the reader's first or changes one of the nine `[tmux]` values.

| Line | When |
|---|---|
| `[slack] agent-director settings: the [tmux] values in effect from "<path>": pending_grace_seconds <n> s, stopping_window_seconds <n> s, starting_session_seconds <n> s, sweep_budget_seconds <n> s, query_timeout_ms <n> ms, action_timeout_ms <n> ms, create_timeout_ms <n> ms, pipe_close_wait_ms <n> ms, kill_exit_wait_ms <n> ms (b.jg5 SRJ-209, SRJ-1014)` | The reader's first accepted read (a missing file included, which gives the defaults) and each later accepted read whose nine `[tmux]` values differ from those in effect (`buildAdSettingsValuesLine`; the unit is `adTmuxKeyUnit`'s). `<path>` is the file's full path under the server's HOME. An unchanged read, a change of `[pause] timeout_seconds` alone and a refused read log none. Holds the path and the nine integers only. Never in `startup-errors.log`, never posted to Slack |
| `[slack] agent-director settings: the read of "<path>" was refused: <reason>; <kept> stay in effect until a read is accepted (b.jg5 SRJ-209)` | The first refused read after start or after an accepted read (`buildAdSettingsRefusedReadLine`); the rest of that run logs nothing, and the next accepted read ends the run. `<path>` is the file's full path under the server's HOME. `<kept>` is `the defaults` when no read has been accepted since start, else `the values of the last accepted read`. `<reason>` is the first broken rule, e.g. `[tmux] stopping_window_seconds is 10, below its minimum of 30`, `[tmux] query_timeout_ms is not an integer (it is a string)`, `[tmux] action_timeout_ms is too large for agent-director`, `it is not valid TOML (at line <L>, column <C>)`, `it is not valid UTF-8`, `it cannot be read (EISDIR)` or `the home directory cannot be found` (then `<path>` is `~/.agent-director/config.toml`). Never in `startup-errors.log`, never posted to Slack |
| `[slack] agent-director settings: already installed — ignoring the second install` | A programming error: `installAdSettings` called twice |
| `[slack] agent-director settings: agent_director_call_timeout_ms is <value>, at or below its need of <need> ms (the <verb> ceiling plus the 15000 ms margin): a call can time out while its verb still acts; see the README's switch-over runbook, section "Switching over to agent-director Phase 1" (b.jg5 SRJ-213)` | The startup check (`buildAdCallTimeoutWarningLine`, once per start, step 2c) when the setting is at or below the need. `<need>` is exact, in ms; `<verb>` names the row whose ceiling sets it: the `AD_CEILING_VERBS` id, or `resume/spawn-with-reuse/plain-spawn` (`AD_LAUNCH_CEILING_VERBS`) for the launch row those three share, whose `setBy` is `resume` (a tie names the earlier verb); the section title is `PHASE1_RUNBOOK_SECTION_TITLE`. Never in `startup-errors.log`, never posted to Slack; the start continues |
| `[slack] agent-director settings: agent_director_call_timeout_ms is <value>; its need is unknown: [pause] timeout_seconds holds <found>, a value that is not used, so pause's wait is not counted and the need without it is <need> ms; see the README's switch-over runbook, section "Switching over to agent-director Phase 1" (b.jg5 SRJ-213)` | The same check, in place of the line above and whatever the setting, when `[pause] timeout_seconds` is not used. `<found>` is `AdPauseTimeout`'s token-free `found`; `<need>` counts `pause` without its wait |

### Retired-key record lines (b.jg5 SRJ-1013, SRJ-1014)

The start read's refusal is written by `recordStartupError`; the store (`src/retired-keys.ts`) logs one line per change of the record and one per failed write through its `log` (`console.error` from `main()`, so `server.log`), each starting `RETIRED_KEYS_LOG_PREFIX`, `[slack] retired-keys:`. Loading the store logs nothing, and a primitive that writes nothing logs nothing. A running server's store calls are a confirmed apply's step 1 `record` and, after a failed write, its `restore` (b.jg5 SRJ-803, SRJ-804 as amended by b.deo SRI-408), the start sweep's one `absent-at-start` `record` (b.jg5 SRJ-714), and the session manager's shared own-row reads' `clear`, the start sweep's list rows included (b.jg5 SRJ-807), and the session manager's `mark` when a reuse spawn for a recorded key succeeds and at a later launch decision (b.jg5 SRJ-806 as amended by b.deo SRI-407), so it logs every line below. No line carries file content, parser text or a token. `<path>` is the file's JSON-quoted path; a key is shown as `persona=<key>`, bare when it is a persona key and JSON-quoted otherwise.

| Line | When |
|---|---|
| `[<timestamp>] [retired-keys-unreadable] The retired-key record "<path>" <problem>, so the server does not start: it never guesses which persona keys are retired. Moving the file aside (for example, renaming it) lets the server start, at the cost that the keys it held are no longer retired, so a persona whose key it held may resume the conversation of the life that was retired.` | The start read refused the record; also in `startup-errors.log`. `<problem>` is `cannot be read (<code>)` (an errno such as `EISDIR`, or `not a regular file`), `is not valid UTF-8`, `is not valid JSON at line <L>, column <C>`, or `is invalid: …` naming the first rule broken (an entry by its position in `keys`) |
| `[slack] retired-keys: recorded <key list> in <path>[; it carries the changes held only in memory for <keys>] (b.jg5 SRJ-803)` | `record` wrote a batch. Each key is `persona=<key> (cause=<cause>)`, with `, its "new life has begun" mark cleared` for a marked key re-recorded, or `(cause=<cause>, held only in memory)` for a held key it wrote |
| `[slack] retired-keys: persona=<key> marked: its new life has begun, in <path>[; it carries …] (b.jg5 SRJ-806)` | `mark` wrote the mark |
| `[slack] retired-keys: persona=<key> entry cleared from <path>[ on <read>][; it carries …] (b.jg5 SRJ-807)` | `clear` removed an entry. From a row read, `<read>` is `its row read <state> with its mark set (<site>: <what>)`, the state read and the read's site (`persona teardown kill: status read between tries` for the teardown kill's read between its tries, `reconcileOrphans: status read between kill tries` for a start-sweep kill's) |
| `[slack] retired-keys: restored the record held before the apply in <path> (b.jg5 SRJ-804)`; for an empty snapshot `… restored the record held before the apply: it was empty, so <path> was removed (b.jg5 SRJ-804)`, `…, but its directory could not be synced (<errno>), so it may reappear after a crash (b.jg5 SRJ-804)`, or `… it was empty, and removing <path> failed (<errno>), so an empty record was written (b.jg5 SRJ-804)` | `restore` succeeded |
| `[slack] retired-keys: cannot record <key list> in <path><detail>; the record in memory is unchanged (b.jg5 SRJ-803)`, or, when the batch held `absent-at-start` keys, `…; this server holds <keys> as retired in memory for its life, and the next write of the record that succeeds carries them (b.jg5 SRJ-803, SRJ-714)` | A failed `record` |
| `[slack] retired-keys: cannot mark persona=<key> in <path><detail>; this server holds its mark in memory, and its next launch decision writes it again (b.jg5 SRJ-806)` | A failed `mark`; the mark stays set in memory |
| `[slack] retired-keys: cannot clear persona=<key> from <path>[ on <read>]<detail>; the entry stays, and the next qualifying read clears it again (b.jg5 SRJ-807)` | A failed `clear`; the entry stays, in memory and in the file, and the read's answer is unchanged |
| `[slack] retired-keys: the mark query for persona=<key> failed: <failure>; nothing is cleared (b.jg5 SRJ-807)` | Logged by the session manager, not the store: the installed store's `isMarked` threw at an own-row read, which counts the key as unmarked and goes on |
| `[slack] retired-keys: cannot restore the record held before the apply in <path><detail>; the keys it could not remove stay retired (b.jg5 SRJ-804)`, or for an empty snapshot `… cannot restore the record held before the apply: removing <path> failed (<errno>), and writing an empty record failed<detail>; the keys it holds stay retired (b.jg5 SRJ-804)` | A failed `restore`; the record in memory is left as it is |

`<detail>` is ` (<errno>); the file is unchanged` for a write that failed before its rename, or `: the new record was written but its directory could not be synced (<errno>); ` followed by `the previous record was written back`, `the file, absent before, was removed again` (either with `, though its directory could not be synced either`), or `putting the previous state back failed too (<errno>), so the file holds the new record`. An errno is shown only when it is a safe errno code.

### Stored-choice file lines (b.deo SRI-904, SRI-905)

The stored-choice store (`src/channel-delivery.ts`; Configuration, [channel-delivery.json](#channel-deliveryjson-state_dirchannel-deliveryjson)) logs through its `log` (`console.error` from `main()`, so the `[slack]` stream of `server.log`) and nowhere else: no line goes to `startup-errors.log`, and nothing is posted to Slack. Its class list is `CHANNEL_DELIVERY_DIAGNOSTIC_CLASSES` (`channel-delivery-unreadable` only, `CHANNEL_DELIVERY_UNREADABLE`), a closed list kept apart from `PERSONA_DIAGNOSTIC_CLASSES` and `RELOAD_DIAGNOSTIC_CLASSES` (b.deo SRI-901). Its drop and failed-write lines start `CHANNEL_DELIVERY_LOG_PREFIX`, `[slack] channel-delivery:`, and carry no class label. Every line comes from an exported builder. A missing file, a store that drops nothing and a successful `set` log nothing here; an accepted `set_channel_delivery` call's `persona-channel-delivery-set` line is the tool's, not the store's (Data Flow, [Outbound](#outbound-claude-code--slack)). No line carries a stored choice, a token, credentials content, message text or file content; a key is shown as `persona=<key>`, bare when it is a persona key and JSON-quoted otherwise, and `<path>` is the file's JSON-quoted path.

| Line | Builder | When |
|---|---|---|
| `[slack] channel-delivery-unreadable: the stored-choice file "<path>" <what>. It is left in place, and this run neither writes it nor drops anything from it: in fungible mode every channel is served at mentions, and set_channel_delivery is refused. To fix: move the file aside, then restart the server (b.deo SRI-403, SRI-904)` | `channelDeliveryUnreadableLine(path, cause)` | Once, at the start read, when the file exists but cannot be used; the store is unreadable for the run. `<what>` is `could not be read[ (<code>)]`, where `<code>` is the read's errno code or, for a directory or other non-regular file, `not a regular file` (`CONFIG_NOT_REGULAR_FILE_CODE`, `config.ts`), `could not be parsed: it is not valid UTF-8` or `… it is not valid JSON[ at line <L>, column <C>]`, or `could not be validated: it is invalid: <problem>`, the first rule broken, naming an entry by its position, never its key or ID |
| `[slack] channel-delivery: dropped the stored choices of persona=<key> in <n> channel(s): <reason> (b.deo SRI-405, SRI-905)` | `channelDeliveryDropLine(key, n, reason)` | Once per key a drop batch removed entries from, before the batch's write; `<n> channel(s)` reads `1 channel` or `<n> channels`. `<reason>` is one of `CHANNEL_DELIVERY_DROP_REASONS`: `retired by a confirmed change` (`CHANNEL_DELIVERY_DROP_RETIRED`: apply step 1's batch, or the start rule for a key the retired-key record holds without its mark), `not an applied persona at start` (`CHANNEL_DELIVERY_DROP_NOT_APPLIED`) or `its declaration changed` (`CHANNEL_DELIVERY_DROP_DECLARATION_CHANGED`) |
| `[slack] channel-delivery: cannot <action> in "<path>"<detail>; the stored choices in memory are unchanged (b.deo SRI-404, SRI-506)` | `channelDeliveryWriteFailedLine(path, action, detail, false)`, `<action>` from `channelDeliverySetAction(key, channel)`: `store the channel delivery of persona=<key> for channel <id>` | A stored choice's write failed; memory is unchanged and the tool returns its write-failed error |
| `[slack] channel-delivery: cannot <action> in "<path>"<detail>; the dropped choices do not apply, and the next successful write of the file carries the drop (b.deo SRI-405)` | `channelDeliveryWriteFailedLine(path, action, detail, true)`, `<action>` from `channelDeliveryDropAction(keys)`: `write the drop of persona=<key>[, persona=<key> …]`, sorted and deduplicated | A drop's write, or the write of unwritten drops (apply step 1, which then logs its `reload-record-write-failed` line), failed; each key named keeps an unwritten drop |

`<detail>` is, for a write that failed before its rename, `[ (<errno>)]; the file is unchanged`. After an unsynced rename it is `: the record was written but its directory could not be synced[ (<errno>)]`, followed, for a drop or the write of unwritten drops, by `, so a crash can undo it` (nothing is written back), and, for a stored choice, by `; <put-back>`: `the previous record was written back`, `the file, absent before, was removed again` (either with `, though its directory could not be synced either`, which carries no error code of its own), or `putting the previous state back failed too[ (<errno>)], so the file holds the refused choice until the next successful write`. An errno is shown only when it is a safe errno code.

### Retired-key launch lines (b.jg5 SRJ-805; b.jg5 SRJ-806 as amended by b.deo SRI-407)

Logged by the session manager (`src/session-manager.ts`) and the reconnect adapter (`src/server.ts`) when a launch path meets a key the retired-key record holds ([Launching a retired key](#launching-a-retired-key-bjg5-srj-805-bjg5-srj-806-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-407)). `<mark words>` is `its new life has begun` or `no new life has begun yet, so any row it has is the old life`.

| Line | When |
|---|---|
| `[slack] spawnForPersona: <ref>'s key is retired (<mark words>) — its first launch is a reuse spawn of the same id, never a plain spawn or a resume (b.jg5 SRJ-805)` | A recorded key's first launch, before its reuse spawn |
| `[slack] spawnForPersona: the retired key's reuse spawn of <ref> collided — fetching current state; this is the one get-then-act a reuse collision gives (b.jg5 SRJ-805, SRJ-112)` | That reuse met a live row; the reply-guard steps are undone and the collision `get` follows, as the attempt's one re-run of get-then-act: a second reuse collision there arms `collision` and answers `retrying` |
| `[slack] spawnForPersona: <ref>'s key is retired (<mark words>; last read <state>) — not resuming: a reuse spawn of the same id first; nothing is deleted (b.jg5 SRJ-805)` | `resumeOrFreshSpawn` for a recorded key, in place of a `resume` |
| `[slack] reuseSpawnForPersona: <ref>'s key is retired and its new life has begun — answering fresh-retired; <mark> (b.jg5 SRJ-806, SRJ-112)` | A reuse spawn succeeded for a recorded key. `<mark>` is `its mark is set in the retired-key record`, `its mark was already set, so nothing is written`, or `writing its mark failed, so this server holds the mark in memory and writes it again at the key's next launch decision`. Only for a key recorded when the launch attempt started and at success with its record generation unchanged |
| `[slack] reuseSpawnForPersona: <ref>'s key was recorded as retired while this reuse spawn's launch attempt was in flight (<how>) — the launch was decided before that recording, so its life is the old life: no mark is set; answering spawned (b.jg5 SRJ-806, SRJ-805)` | A reuse spawn succeeded for a key recorded during its launch attempt. `<how>` is `it was not recorded when the launch attempt started`, `recorded again while the launch attempt was in flight`, or `its record generation could not be read, so a recording during the launch attempt cannot be ruled out`; no mark is set and the answer is `spawned` |
| `[slack] spawnForPersona: <ref>'s key is retired, so its reuse spawn answered fresh-retired — answering it, not an amnesia result; the lost-transcript diagnosis's persona notice is not posted (b.jg5 SRJ-112, SRJ-806)` | The no-transcript step after `ErrJsonlMissing`: the diagnosis held a persona notice, and the reuse answered `fresh-retired`; no amnesia result and no notice |
| `[slack] live-row-sequence: <ref>: its key is retired, so the sequence carries the retired-key flag and ends in a reuse spawn, never a resume (b.jg5 SRJ-805, SRJ-705)` | The start entry set the retired-key flag the starter had not set |
| `[slack] reconnectSession: persona=<key> is <state> and its key is retired with no new life begun — not typing /mcp reconnect into its old life; the live-row sequence replaces it (start answered <answer>); deferring (b.jg5 SRJ-805)` | The reconnect adapter met a retired key's old life; it answers `'transient'` |
| `[slack] retired-keys: the recorded query for persona=<key> failed: <failure>; taken as not recorded (b.jg5 SRJ-805)` | The installed store's `isRecorded` threw at a launch decision; the key launches as one not retired |
| `[slack] retired-keys: the mark query for persona=<key> failed: <failure>; taken as not marked, so its row is the old life (b.jg5 SRJ-805, SRJ-806)` | The store's `isMarked` threw at a launch decision |
| `[slack] retired-keys: writing the held mark of persona=<key> again failed: <failure>; this server still reads it as marked (b.jg5 SRJ-806)` | The store's `mark` threw at a later launch decision |
| `[slack] retired-keys: the record-generation query for persona=<key> failed: <failure>; a recording during the launch attempt cannot be ruled out, so no mark is set (b.jg5 SRJ-806)` | The store's `recordGeneration` threw when a launch attempt started or at a reuse spawn's success; the reuse sets no mark and answers `spawned`, with the in-flight line |

The replace step's line for a retired key carries ` (its key is retired)` (Server-Managed Startup step 5). The store's own mark and clear lines are in [Retired-key record lines](#retired-key-record-lines-bjg5-srj-1013-srj-1014).

### Old-life hold lines (b.jg5 SRJ-809)

Logged by the hold set (`src/retired-keys.ts`, `oldLifeHoldBeganLine` and `oldLifeHoldEndedLine`, through the `log` `main()` gives it: `console.error`, so `server.log`) when a hold begins or ends ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809)), each starting `OLD_LIFE_HOLD_LOG_PREFIX`. `<real path>` is the held directory's real path (its lexical path when it cannot be resolved) and `<id>` the instance id, both JSON-quoted; `<key>` is the old key, bare when it is a persona key and JSON-quoted otherwise (an instance id in its place). No line carries a token or file content. A re-point of the held directory logs nothing.

| Line | When |
|---|---|
| `[slack] old-life hold: began on "<real path>" for oldKey=<key> (instanceId="<id>"): <cause> — the old life may still be running (b.jg5 SRJ-809)` | A hold began. `<cause>` is `apply step 1 recorded its key as retired`, `its start-sweep kill did not succeed` or `the start sweep listed it live while its key is recorded as retired without the "new life has begun" mark` |
| `[slack] old-life hold: began again on "<real path>" for oldKey=<key> (instanceId="<id>"): <cause> — one hold is kept, on its held directory (b.jg5 SRJ-809)` | A begin on an instance id already held: the one hold keeps its held directory, named in the line, and takes the new cause; the declared directory is ignored, and its old key, mark and waiting personas are kept. The row's real `cwd` wins over a declaration |
| `[slack] old-life hold: ended on "<real path>" for oldKey=<key> (instanceId="<id>"): <reason>[ (<read>)]; waiting personas: <keys\|none> (b.jg5 SRJ-809)` | A hold ended. `<reason>` is `the old row read ended`, `the old row read missing, or no row`, `a find-missing run listed the old row in its ids` or `a reuse for the key began its new life`. `<read>` names the read: an own-row site's `<site>: <what>` (for example `persona teardown kill: status read between tries`, `reconcileOrphans: status read between kill tries` or `reconcileOrphans: start sweep list`), with `: no row` after it for `ErrSpawnNotFound`; a run's `<prefix>: findMissing sweep` or `<prefix>: bypassing findMissing sweep`; `reuseSpawnForPersona: reuse spawn succeeded`; or, for a reuse that timed out but launched, `spawnForPersona: get after the reuse spawn's launch timeout read this launch's row` (b.jg5 SRJ-407). `<keys>` are the personas recorded as waiting, sorted and comma-separated |
| `[slack] old-life hold: an end observer failed for instanceId="<id>": <thrown value> (b.jg5 SRJ-809)` | An end observer threw; the hold has ended and the other observers were told |
| `[slack] reload: beginning the old-life hold of <id> failed: <thrown value> (b.jg5 SRJ-809)`, `[slack] reconcileOrphans: beginning the old-life hold of instanceId=<id> failed: <thrown value> (b.jg5 SRJ-809)`, `[slack] old-life hold: noting the read of instanceId=<id> failed: <thrown value> (b.jg5 SRJ-809)`, `[slack] old-life hold: ending the hold of persona=<key> for its new life failed: <thrown value> (b.jg5 SRJ-809)`, `[slack] old-life hold: marking instanceId=<id> kill-failed failed: <thrown value> (b.jg5 SRJ-812)` | Defensive: a hold-set call threw at apply step 1, the start sweep, the read entry, the new-life end or the kill-failed mark; the apply, sweep or read goes on. Not reached in practice (the hold set never throws) |

### Old-life wait lines (b.jg5 SRJ-811)

Logged by the session manager (`src/session-manager.ts`) and built where named, through `console.error`, so `server.log`, for the old-life wait ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809), **The wait's steps**). `<ref>` is `persona=<old key>` for a `cscb_<old key>` row and `instanceId=<id>` otherwise (`oldLifeWaitRef`). The wait's sequence lines are the live-row sequence's, headed `[slack] live-row-sequence: <ref>:` (its start line reads `no launch (old-life form)` and `alert context old-life wait`; a stop for the hold's end reads `the old-life hold it serves ended`); its kill tries are the bounded retry's, headed `[slack] old-life-wait for <ref>`; its runs and own-row reads carry the site `old-life-wait`. Its entries are listed under [startup-errors.log](#startup-errorslog-claudechannelsslackstartup-errorslog). Every line is in docs/engineering-guide.md, Log Messages.

| `[slack] old-life-wait: <ref> (instanceId=<id>): ended — <what ended it>; <the hold goes on\|the hold is over\|nothing more>[; the hold is marked kill-failed]; waiting personas armed (held-for-old-life): <keys\|none> (b.jg5 SRJ-811)` | A round ended (`oldLifeWaitEndLine`, `src/old-life-wait.ts`), after its entries. The last form (`OLD_LIFE_HOLD_SKIPPED_TIMER_PHRASE`) when the arm was skipped on purpose for a persona latched, held on `ErrInvalidFlags`, not up or not applied, after that skip's own line |
| `[slack] old-life-wait: persona=<key>: not in the applied configuration — no retry timer armed (b.jg5 SRJ-1512, b.av2 SR-8.6)` | A persona to arm is outside the applied set (`oldLifeWaitNotAppliedLine`) |
| `[slack] old-life-wait: <ref>: no unclassified-error episodes are installed — the UNCLASSIFIED answer is not reported (b.jg5 SRJ-313, SRJ-811)` | A round that keeps the hold met an UNCLASSIFIED answer with no episodes in the wait's bindings (`oldLifeWaitUnclassifiedNotReportedLine`); production always binds them |
| `[slack] Restart retry skipped for persona=<key> — <a launch is in flight\|its live-row sequence runs\|an old-life wait step it waits on runs>; no agent-director call` | A retry skipped for work that blocks it (`restartRetrySkippedLine`, `src/restart.ts`) |

| `[slack] old-life-wait: persona=<key>: not up — no retry timer armed; its bring-up owns it (b.jg5 SRJ-305)` | A waiting persona to arm is not up (`oldLifeWaitNotUpLine`), at the same sites |
| `[slack] old-life-wait: persona=<key> torn down — forgotten as waiting on instanceId="<id>"; <the wait is stopped: no other persona waits on the hold\|no wait runs on it, and no other persona waits on the hold\|the wait goes on: <keys> still wait on the hold\|no wait runs on it; <keys> still wait on the hold> (b.jg5 SRJ-811)` | A persona teardown's `forgetOldLifeWaits`, once per hold the persona was recorded as waiting on (`oldLifeWaitTeardownLine`); `<keys>` are the applied personas still waiting |
| `[slack] old-life-wait: persona=<key>: forgetting its old-life waits failed: <thrown value> (b.jg5 SRJ-811)` | Defensive: `forgetOldLifeWaits` threw; the teardown goes on |

### Old-life refusal lines (b.jg5 SRJ-810, SRJ-1502, SRJ-1505)

Logged through `console.error`, so `server.log`, by what a hold refuses ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809), **What a hold refuses**). `<D>` and `<id>` are JSON-quoted, with control characters rendered; none carries a token.

| Line | When |
|---|---|
| `[slack] Session refused: its working directory "<D>" is held for an old life that may still be running (instanceId="<id>"[, instanceId="<id>" …]) — registered as no persona's session until the hold ends (b.jg5 SRJ-810, SRJ-1505)` | Session admission refused a session from a held directory (`sessionHeldRefusalLine`, `src/registry.ts`); every held id, in begin order. With `(the held-directory query failed: <thrown> — taken as held)` in place of the ids when the query threw |
| `[slack] <site>: not launching <ref> — its working directory "<D>" is held for an old life that may still be running (instanceId="<id>": wait <started\|running\|already-running\|closed\|not-held\|not-installed>[, …]); waiting on it, its retry timer is armed (held-for-old-life); no agent-director call (sequence-waiting; b.jg5 SRJ-810, SRJ-1502)` | The hold step held a persona back (`oldLifeHoldLaunchLine`): `<site>` is `spawnForPersona`, `launchForLiveRowSequence`, `runRestartWork` or `latch-recheck`, `<ref>` the persona's `"<name>" (key=<key>)` (`persona=<key>` at `runRestartWork`), and each held id carries what was done for its wait (`running` when one already ran, else `ensureOldLifeWait`'s answer). `… its retry timer could not be armed …` when the arm failed or was refused; `… its retry timer is not armed: the step skips this persona, as the line before says …` (`OLD_LIFE_HOLD_SKIPPED_TIMER_PHRASE`) when the step skipped the arm for a persona latched, held on `ErrInvalidFlags`, not up or not applied, after that skip's own line; at `latch-recheck` (the step asked inside the persona's latch re-check, which arms nothing) `… its retry timer is not armed: it is latched, and its latch re-check retries it …` |
| `[slack] Skipping restart for persona=<key> — its working directory is held for an old life that may still be running; no agent-director call, nothing recorded (sequence-waiting; b.jg5 SRJ-810, SRJ-812)`, `[slack] Restart for persona=<key> goes no further <where> — its working directory is held for an old life that may still be running; nothing more is called for it, nothing recorded (sequence-waiting; b.jg5 SRJ-810, SRJ-812)` | The restart path's old-life gate held the persona (`restartOldLifeHeldLine`, `src/restart.ts`), at its first ask or again `<where>` (`after its liveness probe`, `after its escalate-dead reconnect`, `before its kill`, `before its launch`); with ` (the old-life hook failed: <thrown> — taken as held)` after `running` when the hook threw. Follows the hold step's line |
| `[slack] reconnectMcp: <ref> — its own row instanceId="<id>" is held for an old life that may still be running: no send-keys; transient, nothing typed; its retry timer is armed (held-for-old-life) (b.jg5 SRJ-810)`, `… its retry timer could not be armed (b.jg5 SRJ-810)`, `… its retry timer is not armed: the step skips this persona, as the line before says (b.jg5 SRJ-810)` | The reconnect's guard: the persona's own row is held, so nothing is typed (`reconnectHeldLine`); an applied persona is recorded as waiting on that hold. The last form (`OLD_LIFE_HOLD_SKIPPED_TIMER_PHRASE`) when the arm was skipped on purpose, as at the hold step |
| `[slack] reconnectSession: persona=<key> is <state> and its own row is held for an old life — not typing /mcp reconnect into it; the live-row sequence replaces it (start answered <answer>); deferring (b.jg5 SRJ-810, SRJ-805)` | The reconnect adapter met a held own row of a key not recorded and started the live-row sequence (`reconnectHeldOwnRowLine`, `src/server.ts`); `<answer>` is the start entry's, `already-running` while the wait runs on the row |
| `[slack] old-life hold: ended for instanceId="<id>" — retrying its waiting personas at once: <keys\|none>[; once the stopped wait on its own row has settled: <keys>][; not retried: <key> (<not applied\|latched\|held on ErrInvalidFlags\|not up\|its retry failed: <thrown>>)[, …]] (b.jg5 SRJ-810)` | A hold ended and the end-retry observer ran (`oldLifeHoldEndRetryLine`); it follows the hold's `ended on` line. The `once the stopped wait …` part names a waiting persona whose own row is the held id while the wait the hold's end stopped there has not settled |
| `[slack] old-life hold: the stopped wait on instanceId="<id>" has settled — persona=<key> retried at once (b.jg5 SRJ-810)`, `[slack] old-life hold: the stopped wait on instanceId="<id>" has settled — persona=<key> not retried (<not applied\|latched\|held on ErrInvalidFlags\|not up\|its retry failed: <thrown>>) (b.jg5 SRJ-810)` | That persona, once the stopped wait on its own row has settled (`oldLifeHoldEndSettledRetryLine`), checked again for applied, not latched, not held and up |
| `[slack] old-life hold: retrying persona=<key> after the wait on instanceId=<id> settled failed: <thrown value> (b.jg5 SRJ-810)` | Defensive: that deferred retry threw |
