### Start sweep list lines (b.jg5 SRJ-116, SRJ-714)

Logged by the session manager's start sweep (`reconcileOrphans`, Server-Managed Startup step 4) between its `list` and its first kill. `<ref>` is `"<name>" (key=<key>)` for a configured persona and `persona=<key>` otherwise; `<keys>` are JSON-quoted and comma-separated.

| Line | When |
|---|---|
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: start sweep list for <ref>: its row reads pending with no launch start (state=pending) — <outcome>; nothing more is called for it (b.jg5 SRJ-114, SRJ-513)` | A configured persona's own listed row latched it with `launch-start-not-recorded`; `<outcome>` is `the persona latched`, `the persona relatched`, `the persona was already latched with this case`, `no latch is installed, so nothing is latched` or `latching the persona failed: <error>`, as at the shared `get` read |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: start sweep list for <ref>: its row carries the liveness note provenance_conflict (state=<state>) — <outcome>; nothing more is called for it (b.jg5 SRJ-114, SRJ-501)` | A configured persona's own listed row latched it with `conflicting-labels` |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: <ref> latched from its own listed row instanceId=<id> (case=<case>) — its own row and every row labelled with it are left unkilled (b.jg5 SRJ-116, SRJ-502, SRJ-714)` | Once per persona the latch pass latched, after the line above |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: <ref> is latched (case=<case>) — its own row and every row labelled with it are left unkilled (b.jg5 SRJ-502, SRJ-714)` | A configured persona already latched when the sweep ran |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: no retired-key store is installed, so the keys of absent personas' rows are not recorded as retired: <keys> (b.jg5 SRJ-714, SRJ-803)` | Absent personas' keys with no store installed; 0 recorded |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: recording the keys of absent personas' rows as retired failed: <error>; nothing is recorded (b.jg5 SRJ-714, SRJ-803)` | The store's `record` threw; 0 recorded, and the sweep goes on |

The list rows' other own-row lines (a non-latching note, a note not applied, a clear) are the shared read's, headed `[slack] reconcileOrphans: start sweep list for <ref>` ([Reads of a persona's own row](#reads-of-a-personas-own-row-bjg5-srj-114)); the recording's write and its failure are the store's lines ([Retired-key record lines](#retired-key-record-lines-bjg5-srj-1013-srj-1014)), the clear's `<read>` naming `reconcileOrphans: start sweep list`. The listing's old-life holds (step 4.4a) begin after the recording's line and before the first kill, each with the hold set's line, and a hold on a row listed finished then ends, still before the first kill, with its end line ([Old-life hold lines](#old-life-hold-lines-bjg5-srj-809)).

### Start sweep kill lines (b.jg5 SRJ-714, SRJ-702, SRJ-205)

Logged by the start sweep (`reconcileOrphans`, Server-Managed Startup step 4) from its kills to its end. `<row>` is `orphan instanceId=<id> persona=<persona>` for a swept row (`<persona>` as in the sweeping line) and `pre-persona row instanceId=<id>` for a row with no `persona` label; `<outcome>` is `describeKillOutcome`'s rendering. The bounded retry's own try, read and stop lines carry the same `[slack] reconcileOrphans` prefix.

| Line | When |
|---|---|
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: sweeping row (<reason>) persona=<persona> instanceId=<id> state=<state>[ cwd=<cwd>] — <it is live, so it is killed; the row is kept\|it is finished, so it is not killed (a finished row is never killed); the row is kept> (b.jg5 SRJ-714)` | A labelled row the sweep sweeps (`absent persona`, `wrong instance ID`, `wrong cwd`) |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: killing <row> state=<state> tmux_session=<session>; the row is kept whatever the outcome (b.jg5 SRJ-714)` | Before each kill of a live stray, swept or pre-persona |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: kill succeeded for <row> (<outcome>) — row kept` | The kill's success stands; a `persona-kill-survivor` entry follows when an earlier try named a survivor |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: the status read between kill tries for instanceId=<id> answered CONFIG; the row names no persona of the applied configuration, so no outage is raised — logged only (b.jg5 SRJ-110, SRJ-316)` | A between-try read answered CONFIG for a row of no configured persona |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: kill tries for <row> (start sweep) were stopped: <cause>; its last outcome's class: <class>; no kill-failure alert is raised; <descriptions> (b.jg5 SRJ-702, SRJ-714[, SRJ-205])` | `startSweepStoppedKillLine`: a stop ended a kill's tries before a success stood. `<cause>` is `the server is shutting down` (`START_SWEEP_KILL_STOP_SHUTDOWN`: a shutdown stopped the tries) or `the version re-check decided that the server stops; row kept; the sweep makes no further call` (`START_SWEEP_KILL_STOP_RECHECK`: the kill's `ErrInvalidFlags` re-check stops the server; `SRJ-205` is cited then). `<descriptions>` is `describeKillFailureDescriptions`' rendering (the latest survivor-naming description included, else `no description`); its `orphan-cleanup` entry carries no alert text, and nothing is posted |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: the server began shutting down — the sweep stops: no further kill, status read, findMissing or get, and no further latch, record write or clear; what it did stands, and the rows it left unkilled count as kept (b.jg5 SRJ-714, SRJ-205)` | Once per sweep, the first time its shutdown query answers true (`START_SWEEP_SHUTDOWN_STOP_LINE`), before the summary, also when the findMissing run then failed or the shutdown began during the post-run `get`s; never after a re-check's stop |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: the <class> answer to the <call> for persona=<key> came after the sweep stopped — no outage is raised (b.jg5 SRJ-714)` | `logSweepOutageNotRaised`: an ENVIRONMENT or CONFIG answer to a kill (`<call>` `kill`), or a CONFIG answer to a between-try read (`<call>` `status read between kill tries`), for a configured persona's row arrived after the sweep stopped: no outage is raised |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: post-sweep get for persona=<key>: the get settled after its caller stopped — not acted on: no latch, clear or episode end (b.jg5 SRJ-714)` | A post-run `get` settled after a shutdown began (`OwnRowReadSite.actGoes`): no latch, clear or episode end; the `get`s' line shows `persona=<key> not acted on (its caller stopped)` |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: findMissing sweep for the rows the start sweep killed — count=<n> ids=[…] unverified=<n> unverified_ids=[…]` | The post-kill findMissing run's own line |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: after the findMissing sweep for the rows the start sweep killed — no post-sweep get is made: its caller stopped (b.jg5 SRJ-120, SRJ-714)` | A shutdown began while the run was under way: no post-run `get` |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: findMissing after the kills of <n> row(s): missing=<n> [<ids>] still-live=<n> [<ids>] not-judged=<n> [<ids>] — a row that still reads live is killed again by the next start's sweep when it sweeps it; a not-judged row was pending and not judged by this run (retry later)` | After the run, over every row given a kill (`startSweepPostKillLine`) |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: findMissing after the kills of <n> row(s) failed — each reads as it did, and a live one is killed again by the next start's sweep when it sweeps it` | The run failed, after its failure line (`startSweepPostKillFailedLine`) |
| `[slack] reconcileOrphans: summary — listed=<n> killed=<n> kept=<n> (kill-failed=<n>) recorded-as-retired=<n> left-unkilled-for-latch=<n> (b.jg5 SRJ-714)` | The last line of every sweep that listed its rows, a stopped one included (`startSweepSummaryLine`) |

The `orphan-cleanup` entry of a kill that did not succeed is `kill did not succeed for <row> state=<state> tmux_session=<session>: <outcome>[; its tries were stopped because the server is shutting down, so no kill-failure alert is raised]; row kept, its session may still be running`, with `; kill-failure alert: instanceId=<id> (start sweep): <text>` appended when the retry decided the ordinary version and no stop ended the tries (`startSweepKillFailedEntry`). A row with no hold yet then logs the hold set's began line, cause `its start-sweep kill did not succeed`; the post-kill run's `ids` log its end lines ([Old-life hold lines](#old-life-hold-lines-bjg5-srj-809)).

### Start summary lines (b.wrb, b.fwu, b.f2b, b.jg5 SRJ-1015, SRJ-205)

Logged by the start pass (`startupSessionManager`, Server-Managed Startup step 5).

| Line | When |
|---|---|
| `[slack] startupSessionManager: complete — <N> persona(s): <n> resumed, <n> fresh-spawned, <n> fresh-after-amnesia, <n> fresh-after-inconclusive-amnesia, <n> reconnected, <n> no-op, <n> failed, <n> not brought up, <n> not reconnected, <n> latched, <n> retrying, <n> waiting on a live-row sequence, <n> held on invalid flags, <n> fresh as retired keys` | Once, when the pass returns (`startupSummaryLine`). Each launch result is counted once, in its own count; the five counts after `not reconnected` are none of them failed or a fresh spawn (step 5, the start summary) |
| `[slack] startupSessionManager: not launching <ref> — the server has begun shutting down; no agent-director call, counted in no summary count (b.jg5 SRJ-205)` | A launch the pass's launch pool did not start because a shutdown had begun (`startLaunchNotStartedForShutdownLine`); `<ref>` is `"<name>" (key=<key>)` |

### Log file locations

Both paths are rooted in `SLACK_STATE_DIR` (default: `~/.claude/channels/slack/`).

| Process | Log file |
|---------|----------|
| Server daemon (`server.ts`) | `STATE_DIR/server.log` |
| `clean_restart` subcommand | `STATE_DIR/clean_restart.log` |
| `stop --stop-bots` and `clean_restart` teardown report (`appendLogLine`, b.jg5 SRJ-909) | `STATE_DIR/server.log`, appended while the server is stopped |
| cscb_cron fire log (`cron-log.ts`) | `cron_log_path` (default `<config dir>/cron.log`) |

All three files are opened in append mode — multiple restarts accumulate in the same file rather than overwriting it; only `server.log` and `clean_restart.log` are subject to the size-based rotation above, the CLI's appended lines included. The CLI teardown also records its entries in `STATE_DIR/startup-errors.log` ([clean_restart](#clean_restart-sr-11-event-12) step 7).

## Endpoint Inventory

The HTTP server serves `/interject`, `/clear-latch` and `/mcp` only; any other path is a 404. None of them triggers or describes a reload (see Security Model, Reload is file-triggered only), and a new endpoint must not either. `/interject` and `/clear-latch` share one loopback rule (`isLocalAddress`, `src/interject.ts`).

### POST /interject

Injects a message into one persona's live Claude session without going through Slack. Localhost-only. Handler: `handleInterject` in `src/interject.ts`, wired by `server.ts`.

**Request body** (JSON, max 32 KB)

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `persona` | string | yes | Target persona's name or key (exact, case-sensitive match) |
| `message` | string | yes | Message content to inject |
| `sender` | string | no | Display name; defaults to `"interject"` |

**Success response**

`200 OK` — `{ ok: true, persona: <name> }` (the persona's name, even when the request used its key)

**Status codes**

| Status | Condition | Body `error` |
|--------|-----------|--------------|
| 200 | Notification handed to the persona's session | — |
| 400 | Invalid JSON | `Invalid JSON` |
| 400 | Missing, empty or non-string `persona` (including a body with only the old `channel` field) | `Missing or invalid field: persona (string) required` |
| 400 | Missing, empty or non-string `message` | `Missing or invalid field: message (string) required` |
| 403 | Non-localhost origin | `Forbidden` |
| 404 | No applied persona has that name or key, or there is no persona config | `Persona not found in the applied config` |
| 405 | Non-POST method | `Method Not Allowed` |
| 413 | Body exceeds 32 KB | `Request body too large (max 32KB)` |
| 503 | The persona is in the applied config but not up (broken or retrying), even when its instance is running or its session is still registered; the body also carries `persona` (its name) | `Persona is not up` |
| 503 | The persona is up but has no registered, connected session | `No active session for this persona` |

**Behavior**

- Resolves `persona` against the applied persona config (`resolvePersonaTarget`); 404 if absent
- Asks the injected `isPersonaUp` (the server's shared up predicate, `createPersonaUpPredicate`; b.av2 SR-6.4) before any session lookup. A persona that is not up gets 503 and one line, `[slack] /interject: refused for persona "<name>" (key=<key>) — the persona is not up; nothing delivered`; nothing reaches its instance
- Calls `getSessionByPersona()` with the persona's key; 503 if none or not connected
- Logs `[slack] /interject: delivering to persona "<name>" (key=<key>) sender="<label>" message="<first 80 chars>"`
- Sends `notifications/claude/channel` to that session only, with `content: message` and `meta: { user, ts }` — no `chat_id`, `message_id` or `via`. `user` is the `sender` label; `ts` is `String(Date.now() / 1000)`, which has at most three fractional digits. The absence of `via` is what the Slack Reply Guard uses to tell an injected message from a delivered Slack one (see [Slack Reply Guard](#slack-reply-guard-stop-hook)).
- Does not await the notification: a later rejection is logged as `[slack] /interject: notification to persona … failed: …`
- Does not call the Slack API

### POST /clear-latch

Clears one persona's latch by hand on the running server (b.jg5 SRJ-510, SRJ-506). Localhost-only, for the operator only: no MCP tool, MCP instruction text, tool description or notice names it (SRJ-511). Handler: `handleClearLatch` in `src/clear-latch.ts`, wired by `server.ts` after `/interject`. The route clears only through the re-check's one clear entry and after-clear sequence ([How a latch clears and relatches](#how-a-latch-clears-and-relatches-bjg5-srj-506-srj-1005)); there is no second clear path.

**Request body** (JSON, max 32 KB, `INTERJECT_BODY_CAP_BYTES`)

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `persona` | string | yes | Target persona's name or key (exact, case-sensitive match) |

**Success response**

`200 OK` — `{ ok: true, persona: <name>, cleared: true | false }`: `cleared` is whether the persona was latched (the persona's name, even when the request used its key); with `cleared` true, the persona's restart failure count has been reset by the time the route answers

**Status codes**

| Status | Condition | Body `error` |
|--------|-----------|--------------|
| 200 | The clear (and, for a latched persona, the reset of its restart failure count) has run in the persona's lifecycle serializer turn | — |
| 400 | The body could not be read | `Unreadable request body` |
| 400 | Body exceeds 32 KB | `Request body too large (max 32KB)` |
| 400 | Invalid JSON | `Invalid JSON` |
| 400 | Missing, empty or non-string `persona` | `Missing or invalid field: persona (string) required` |
| 403 | Non-localhost origin | `Forbidden` |
| 404 | No applied persona has that name or key, or there is no persona config | `Persona not found in the applied config` |
| 405 | Non-POST method | `Method Not Allowed` |
| 500 | The clear by hand rejected | `Internal Server Error` |

**Behavior**

- Checks, in order: the method, the loopback rule, the body cap, the JSON, the `persona` field, then resolves it against the applied persona config (`resolvePersonaTarget`). A persona that is not up is not refused, and a request during shutdown has no status of its own
- Makes exactly one call of the injected `clearByHand(key)`, `clearByHandOf(latchRecheck)` (`src/session-manager.ts`): `LatchRecheck.clearAndRecover(key, LATCH_RECOVERY_REASON_CLEARED_BY_HAND)`, which submits one job to the persona's serializer whose first step is the clear (`runLatchClearSequence`). The route awaits only the answer's `cleared` part, with no bound of its own (the listener's `idleTimeout` is 0), so it answers once the clear has run in the persona's turn: behind a running re-check round or any other work queued for the persona. The bypassing `find-missing` and the retry at once follow in the same job, unawaited, and the job runs to its end whether or not the caller is still waiting
- A latched persona's clear logs only the clear entry's line (`[slack] conflict-latch: persona=<key> cleared — … reason="cleared by hand"; …`) and posts one recovery notice; an unlatched persona gets nothing (no post, no call, no timer change, no reset) and one line, `[slack] clear-latch: persona "<name>" (key=<key>) was not latched; nothing changed`
- A clear that clears a latch also resets the persona's restart failure count and cap-notified latch (`forgetFailures`, `src/backoff.ts`, the counter the restart cap reads; b.av2 SR-6.3, b.jg5 SRJ-509), in the job's turn after the clear and before the route answers. So a persona that was at the restart cap is launched by the retry at once, and a new cap notice can follow only after `RESTART_FAILURE_CAP` more counted failures. An unlatched persona's count is unchanged: a persona at the cap that is not latched stays down until its teardown or a server restart. A reset that throws logs one line (`latchClearRestartResetFailedLine`) and changes nothing else: the 200, the `find-missing` and the retry go ahead. The re-check's own clears never reset the count ([The re-check](#the-re-check-bjg5-srj-505), **The restart cap**)
- A 404 logs `[slack] clear-latch: no persona in the applied configuration has the requested name or key; nothing cleared`, never repeating the argument (it may be a token typed by mistake, SRJ-509). A clear that rejects logs `[slack] clear-latch: the clear of persona "<name>" (key=<key>) failed: <error>` (through `describeThrownValue`) and answers a generic 500. Nothing is logged for 400, 403 or 405
- Does not call the Slack API itself; the recovery notice goes through the persona notifier, as every clear's does

**Reaching it.** The caller is the CLI's `clear-latch` ([clear-latch command](#clear-latch-command-bjg5-srj-509-srj-510)), which dials `127.0.0.1` at the port in the server's `server.port` record ([server.port](#serverport-state_dirserverport)), never the `bind` or `port` of the configuration, so a server whose `bind` gives it no `127.0.0.1` listener (anything but the default `127.0.0.1` or `0.0.0.0`) cannot be reached here, as the cron dispatcher cannot reach its `/interject`.

## Security Model

- **Inbound delivery** (b.av2 SR-4.2 as amended by b.deo SRI-303 to SRI-306; b.deo SRI-301, SRI-302): every inbound event goes through the receiving persona's pipeline (`src/persona-routing.ts`), whose delivery rules are in `src/delivery-decision.ts`; the mode is read once per event (`channelModeOf` over the configuration in effect). In both modes a persona receives, with `dm.enabled` on, direct messages to its own app (b.av2 SR-4.3), and a group DM (`channel_type` `mpim`) is never delivered.
  - **Declarative mode:** a persona receives its configured channels, each by its `delivery` setting. An @mention in a group DM arrives without `channel_type` and is decided by the channel rules, so it is delivered only to a persona that lists that conversation ID. The operator chooses each persona's audience.
  - **Fungible mode:** a persona receives every public or private channel its app is a member of that is not externally shared, and no persona's `channels` is read. An event takes the fungible path only when its `channel_type` is `channel` or `group` and its channel ID matches the channel-ID pattern; whether that channel counts as externally shared is then decided from the event envelope's flag alone: its `is_ext_shared_channel` flag must be present, a boolean and `false`, so a Slack Connect channel is never served, and an Enterprise Grid channel shared inside one organization is served when Slack marks it not externally shared. A fungible-mode `app_mention`, a group-DM one included, ends before the decision, so a group DM is never served. Each channel is served at the persona's channel delivery: `mentions`, unless its agent stored `all` with `set_channel_delivery` (`channelDeliveryFor`), and always `mentions` in another persona's fungible destination (the loop guard). Any channel member can invite the app, so an invite changes the persona's audience: the app's membership, not the configuration, is the exposure the operator accepts by turning the switch on. Nothing about membership is stored and no Slack call is added. The audit lines are `persona-invited-channel` (the first event a persona hears from a channel in its life) and `persona-channel-delivery-set` (each stored choice).
  - **Senders:** in both modes the persona's own messages are dropped, and that is the only sender filter: any other author, a workspace user who has never posted before included, reaches the persona wherever it receives; no list of approved senders and no per-sender approval step exists.

  The operator-facing statement of who can reach a persona in fungible mode is README.md's [Who can reach a persona in fungible mode](../README.md#who-can-reach-a-persona-in-fungible-mode).
- **Outbound scoping** (b.av2 SR-5.1 as amended by b.deo SRI-601, SRI-602): each of the five Slack tools resolves the calling session's persona, its client and the mode (`getChannelMode`) at call time. In declarative mode it may target only that persona's configured channels; in fungible mode it may target any channel ID matching `CHANNEL_ID_RE` (`C…` or `G…`), `persona.channels` is never read, and Slack enforces membership: a call in a channel the app is not in fails at Slack (for example `not_in_channel`) and returns `slackRefusalToolErrorText`'s tool error naming the persona, the channel and Slack's code; no `chat:write.public` scope is asked for. Any other non-DM target is refused before any Slack call, in fungible mode with `FUNGIBLE_TARGET_REFUSAL`. CSCB makes no Slack call to learn a channel's membership or sharing, so in fungible mode a tool acting in an externally shared channel or a group DM the app belongs to is not refused by CSCB, although neither is ever delivered from (the README's [Tools](../README.md#tools) states these known limits). `set_channel_delivery` has no Slack target: it never passes `checkPersonaTarget`, reads no client and makes no Slack call. In both modes, while its `dm.enabled` is on, a tool may also target a `D…` DM conversation or (for `reply` only) a user ID, which is opened with `conversations.open` on the persona's client before the post (`checkPersonaTarget`). With `dm.enabled` off, no tool call opens a DM (`conversations.open`) or acts on a `D…` or user-ID target for that persona, including a `chat.postMessage` to a user ID, which Slack would turn into an implicit DM open. A refused target returns a tool error naming the persona and the target, and no Slack call is made. The call posts as the persona, with no username or icon override. The server's own posts go to a persona's destination by the setting in force (`personaDestinationOf`: `permission_prompts` in declarative mode, `invited.permission_prompts` in fungible mode); they (prompts, the stuck-prompt warning, notices) are held to the same DMs switch, though not through `checkPersonaTarget`: a `dm` destination with DMs off is refused with no Slack call (`persona-destination.ts`); the one exception is an update to a prompt already posted in a DM (see [In-memory state](#in-memory-state-sr-1))
- **Who can change a channel's delivery** (b.deo SRI-501 to SRI-505; fungible mode only): in declarative mode every `set_channel_delivery` call is refused (`channelDeliveryDeclarativeRefusal`), since there the operator sets `delivery` in `config.json`. In fungible mode the persona's agent stores a choice when someone asks for it (`SET_CHANNEL_DELIVERY_DESCRIPTION`), so anyone who can reach the persona, in any channel it serves or by DM, can have it switch a channel it serves to `all`, a channel the asker is not in included; from then on every message there reaches the persona's worker. The tool accepts only a channel the persona has heard a message from on its fungible path in its life (`heardChannels`) or holds a stored choice for, so only a public or private channel that is not externally shared, and it resolves the persona and refuses a retiring key or a session the registry does not hold for the key before its own rules. The loop guard holds another persona's fungible destination at `mentions` whatever is stored. A choice is stored only by the server, in `channel-delivery.json` ([channel-delivery.json](#channel-deliveryjson-state_dirchannel-deliveryjson)), never in `config.json`; the operator removes stored choices by moving the file aside and restarting the server. The tool's resolution, refusals and line are in Data Flow, [The `set_channel_delivery` path](#the-set_channel_delivery-path-bdeo-sri-501-to-sri-507). Also in fungible mode, `fetch_messages` can read the history of every channel the app is in, so content can be carried between channels. README.md's [Who can reach a persona in fungible mode](../README.md#who-can-reach-a-persona-in-fungible-mode) is the operator-facing statement
- **File exfiltration guard**: `assertSendable()` (`src/lib.ts`) blocks uploading files from the state directory (outside `inbox/`) and every persona credentials file named by the applied configuration or by the configuration file as it currently stands (b.av2 SR-5.2), compared by real path so a symlink to one is refused too. **State-directory rule:** a file is refused when it is inside the state directory and not inside `inbox/`, by either of two checks: one on the paths as given, and the same check on the real paths of the file and of both directories. So a symlink outside the state directory that points into it (for example at a credentials-holding `.env` there) is refused, and one that points into `inbox/` is allowed. Both checks respect path-component boundaries: `<state dir>/inbox-old/x` is not in the inbox, and `<state dir>2/x` is not in the state directory. A path that does not exist gets only the as-given check. The list is rebuilt per call from the reload controller's `protectedCredentialsFiles()` (`credentialsFilesToProtect` over the applied set, which is the last-applied record's set at a start from the record, plus every `credentials_file` string in `config.json` read tolerantly now), so a credentials file named only by an unapplied edit is protected too. That read of `config.json` is one of the three reads the 64 KiB size cap does not cover (`readPersonaConfigBytes` with `uncapped`; the other two are the retired-key record's and the stored-choice file's start reads): the whole file is read, so a path named only in an oversized unapplied `config.json` is still refused. It is still opened and stat'ed first, so a non-regular file is never read (see Reload files, Size cap). Before `main()` builds the controller there is no applied set, and only `config.json`'s paths are refused. It never opens the file. `reply` checks every file up front and re-checks each one right before its upload
- **Attachment download token scope**: `download_attachment` sends the persona's bot token only to `https://files.slack.com` URLs. External (non-Slack-hosted) files are refused, and a redirect off that origin is never followed with the Authorization header, so the token cannot reach a third-party host
- **Localhost restriction**: `/interject` and `/clear-latch` are the localhost-restricted endpoints; both accept requests only from 127.0.0.1/::1/::ffff:127.*, through the one rule `isLocalAddress` (`src/interject.ts`). `/clear-latch` is for the operator only: no MCP tool, MCP instruction text, tool description or notice names it (b.jg5 SRJ-511)
- **agent-director's rows, labels, socket and sessions are its own** (b.jg5 SRJ-716, SRJ-106, SRJ-612, SRJ-601, SRJ-1101): agent-director defends against accidents only, and proves a session is a row's by the session's `@ad_owner` label and sends a row's calls to the row's recorded tmux socket, so CSCB leaves all of it alone. The build holds:
  - the server starts no tmux process: no `src/` file starts a process whose command is `tmux` (a literal in any quote style, a path ending `/tmux`, or the first word of a shell `-c` script), every `src/` process start whose command is not a literal is on a closed list with its reason, and no `src/` string names the raw tmux session-kill, session-probe or server-start sub-command (the audit's `raw-tmux-subcommand` rule); CSCB reaches tmux only through agent-director;
  - no agent-director row is ever deleted: no `src/` code calls the client's `delete`, and the row-delete helpers (`deleteInstance`, `deleteInstanceRow`, `deletePersonaInstance`, `tryDelete`, `killAndDeleteSweptRow`) appear nowhere in `src/`, in code or in a string (the source audit's `delete-helper` rule); a row is only paused or killed, keeping its `claude_session_id` for the next start's resume;
  - no call sets agent-director's finished-row option, and no `src/` text names it, as the request field or as its CLI flag (the audit's `finished-row-option` rule lists both spellings): every kill is the plain `kill` with `{ claude_instance_id }`;
  - CSCB never sets, copies, clears or reads agent-director's labels (`@ad_owner`, `@ad_pane`), and no `src/` text names `ad_owner` or `ad_pane`. With no tmux process of its own it also never judges liveness or ownership from tmux options or environments, never renames, relinks, regroups or respawns a persona's session or pane, and adds no socket option and no `TMUX` or `TMUX_TMPDIR` of its own to an agent-director call;
  - SRJ-601's removed tmux-path identifiers (the raw runner, the tmux server start, the liveness probe, the approver's raw path and its seams, the self-heal, the ladder's kill clock seam) stay absent.
  - **Pinned by `tests/fmk-source-audit.test.ts`**: one audit over every `.ts` file under `src/`, comments stripped (`stripComments`, `tests/test-helpers/source-audit.ts`), with a planted violation per rule. The rules and how to fix a finding are in the engineering guide's Source Invariants section.
- **Session scope guard**: agent-director enforces session scope via `relay_mode='on'` at spawn time. Permission requests are routed through agent-director's internal relay machinery (SR-2.1 poller), which is scoped to the spawned session. Sessions not spawned by CSCB have no relay route and no `PermissionRequest` or `PreToolUse` hook entries in `settings.json` — the `.sh` hook files are not shipped.
- **Credentials-file secrecy**: each persona's credentials file is the server's only token source (b.av2 SR-1.4, SR-10.2). The persona credentials module (`src/persona-credentials.ts`) and the bring-up checks (`checkPersonaLocalSteps` in `src/persona-start.ts`, run by the bring-up controller) read it once per persona at each bring-up (at start, at apply, and at a recovery bring-up) and once at each confirmed credentials change (apply step 4), and hand the tokens to the connection manager; the controller holds them in the persona's entry for a later directory retry and never logs, returns or re-reads them; beside them it holds only a SHA-256 digest of the bytes read (or a missing/unreadable marker). A persona whose credentials file another applied persona shares (a record-start collision) has its own path read only to be hashed: the bytes are never parsed and no token is taken from them. The reload detection tick reads each referenced credentials file every 5 s outside dry run, through the same stat-first reader, holds the bytes only for that pass (read once per path, hashed into the fingerprint), compares only digests with the held one, and drops the bytes when the pass ends; the server holds no token at module scope, and none of that code reads an environment variable. The CLI reads no token at all: it opens no credentials file. A credentials path that is not a regular file (a directory, FIFO, socket or device) is `persona-credentials-unreadable` and is never read: the file is opened non-blocking, so a FIFO cannot stall the open, and its type is checked through the same descriptor before any read. A file over the size cap is unreadable the same way and never read in full (see Reload files, Size cap). It never writes, copies, caches or persists a credentials file or any value from one; a digest is held in memory only, never written to disk or logged. It does not check or change the file mode. A bad token is described only by its key and the rule it breaks, never by its value, so no diagnostic line or failure result carries a token, and the success value redacts itself if logged.
  - **Who writes the file** (b.av2 SR-1.4; b.av2 SR-12 as amended by b.deo SRI-1101 to SRI-1110): the operator, by hand or with the setup wizard's credentials command (`## Credentials command` in `skills/setup-slack-channel-bots/SKILL.md`): one line, `claude-slack-channel-bots credentials <persona>`, which the operator runs in their own terminal once the persona is declared in `config.json` (the line stays short, so a copy from an 80-column terminal keeps it whole). The CLI finds the persona in the configuration file as it stands and runs the packaged `scripts/write-credentials.sh` with `bash` for its `credentials_file` (see the `cli.ts` and `scripts/` entries of the Module Map). That script is the only shipped writer and the only place mode 0600 is guaranteed. It turns tracing and automatic export off (`set +xa`), checks the path and that `curl` is installed before any prompt, reads both tokens without echo, and validates the bot token with `auth.test` and the app token with `apps.connections.open` (each token reaches `curl` only on its standard input, as a `--config -` header, so no token is on any command line or in the process list; a check passes only when the reply's leading field is `"ok":true`). Only then does it write exactly `bot_token` and `app_token` to a temporary file created exclusively with `mktemp` beside the target under `umask 077` and `chmod 600` (removed by a trap on any failure or interrupt), check the file is not empty, and rename it onto the target; if the target appeared, vanished, became or stopped being a symlink, or became a directory while it ran (checked again after the rename, removing the moved temporary file from a directory that appeared at the path), nothing is written. The rename replaces a symlink at the path with a regular file, leaving the old tokens in the file it pointed to. An empty answer at the replace prompt declines, and `curl -q` ignores the operator's `~/.curlrc`. The server never writes the file and never polices its mode, and the CLI process itself reads no token. No shipped skill asks for, accepts or prints a token, or displays a credentials file's content: the wizard never takes a token in chat and checks only that the file exists and its mode, and the debugging skill's shape check (`jq`) reports key names and prefixes only. Rotation is the same command for the persona, then a confirmed credentials change (see Reload).
- **Reload is file-triggered only** (b.av2 SR-8.8): a change is applied only when the operator puts a confirmation at `config.json.apply` beside `config.json`. That rename is the only trigger, made by the operator or by an agent the operator explicitly directs. No HTTP endpoint, MCP tool or CLI subcommand (listed or hidden) triggers, confirms or performs a reload, and no MCP instruction text, tool definition or CLI usage text describes it; a confirmation's content is never logged (the stale line names only its path and the reason). This is deliberate opacity, not a security boundary: the server and the persona instances run as the same OS user, so a bot could make the rename itself.
  - **The surfaces as built.** The CLI accepts only `start`, `stop` (with `--stop-bots`), `clean_restart`, `credentials` and `clear-latch`; any other first argument (`reload`, `apply` and the like included) prints the same usage text and exits 1, writing nothing. The HTTP server serves only `/interject`, `/clear-latch` and `/mcp` (see Endpoint Inventory). The MCP server lists six tools in both modes (`reply`, `react`, `edit_message`, `fetch_messages`, `download_attachment`, `set_channel_delivery`), and any other tool name is an `Unknown tool` error. `set_channel_delivery` changes no configuration and applies no reload: it stores a channel delivery in `channel-delivery.json`, never in `config.json`, and its description, input descriptions and every refusal and result text carry no reload wording (the terms in `RELOAD_TERMS`) and nothing that triggers, confirms or describes a configuration apply (b.deo SRI-501). The start, stop and clean_restart sections above describe no reload behaviour: those commands only read the last-applied record through `readAppliedPersonaConfig` and never write a reload file.
  - **Pinned by AC 74 tests.** `tests/cli.test.ts` (`unknown subcommand`) checks the usage text lists exactly the five subcommands and the one flag, carries no reload wording, and that hidden spellings take the unknown-subcommand path with the temp tree unchanged. `tests/registry.test.ts` (`tool list and instructions`) checks every tool definition, `set_channel_delivery`'s included (its description and input descriptions), and the MCP instructions carry no reload wording, and that `reload` and `apply_config` tool calls are refused. The refusal and result texts `set_channel_delivery`'s builders return are outside these checks; their author checks them by hand. The shared term list is in the testing guide's Unadvertised Reload Checks section.
- **`clear-latch` is not offered to the bots** (b.jg5 SRJ-511): the command and its route are the operator's way to end a hold, and a bot must never clear its own. No MCP tool, no tool description (`set_channel_delivery`'s `SET_CHANNEL_DELIVERY_DESCRIPTION`, `SET_CHANNEL_DELIVERY_CHANNEL_DESCRIPTION` and `SET_CHANNEL_DELIVERY_DELIVERY_DESCRIPTION` included), no refusal or result text of `set_channel_delivery`, no text of `MCP_INSTRUCTIONS`, no Slack notice (every SRJ-10xx notice builder, the "cleared by hand" recovery text included) and no text of the Reply Guard's reminder names it, in any of the spellings `clear-latch`, `/clear-latch`, `clear_latch` and `clearLatch`. Unlike reload, it is not hidden from the operator: the usage text lists it (`CLEAR_LATCH_USAGE_ENTRY`), and the README's CLI Reference and the debug skill (`skills/debug-slack-channel-bots/SKILL.md`) describe it, and nothing else that ships does. Like `/interject`, the endpoint is loopback-only, so a same-user process on the host, a bot's included, could still call it: this is deliberate opacity, not a security boundary.
  - **Pinned by AC 47 tests**, each over the terms of `tests/test-helpers/clear-latch-terms.ts` (`CLEAR_LATCH_TERMS`, from `CLEAR_LATCH_COMMAND` and `CLEAR_LATCH_ROUTE`): `tests/registry.test.ts` (`tool list and instructions`: every tool definition, `set_channel_delivery`'s included, and the instructions the session receives), `tests/shipped-docs.test.ts` (`MCP_INSTRUCTIONS` and the Reply Guard's reminder text) and `tests/notice-texts.test.ts` (the notice catalogue, one rendered text per builder and variant). The catalogue includes the permission wedge warning (SRJ-1012), through `buildWedgeWarningText`, exported from `src/permission-poller.ts`.
- **Slack notices** (b.jg5 SRJ-1001, SRJ-1508; b.av2 SR-7.2): bots read Slack posts, so a destructive step must come only from a human following agent-director's own guidance. These rules hold for every server notice posted to Slack, not only the SRJ-10xx builders; the passages on each notice link here rather than restate them.
  - **Where a notice goes.** Every server notice about a persona goes only to its destination, under its identity, through the persona notifier (the `persona-notifier.ts` entry of the Module Map): the spawn-failure and restart-cap notices, the outage onsets and all-clear, the CONFLICT notice, the unusable-name and launch-start-not-recorded posts and their recovery notices, the `tmux-unresponsive` onset, alert and recovery, the kill-failure alert, the slow dead-session recovery post, the stuck-launch post, the `ErrInvalidFlags` alert, the unclassified-error alert, the lost-message notices, the not-connected notices, the JSONL persistence safeguard's notices and the transcript-loss diagnosis notices, and the wedge warning, which the permission poller posts to the same destination through the same destination hold ([Wedge detector](#wedge-detector-bfae-f4)). These go only to the server log and a startup-errors entry: notices raised during a persona teardown, and the all-clear of an outage whose onset was raised during one, whenever it comes ([Persona teardown](#persona-teardown-bav2-sr-65-as-amended-by-bdeo-sri-307)); start-sweep notices ([Start sweep kill lines](#start-sweep-kill-lines-bjg5-srj-714-srj-702-srj-205)); CLI-teardown notices, which the CLI also prints ([stop command](#stop-command), [clean_restart](#clean_restart-sr-11-event-12)); kill failures and unclassified-error alerts for a persona no longer in the applied configuration, an old-life wait's included, and CONFLICTs and unusable names met in an old-life wait ([The old-life hold](#the-old-life-hold-bjg5-srj-809)); and the version gate's refusal of an agent-director binary, at startup or at a runtime re-check ([Runtime version re-check lines](#runtime-version-re-check-lines-bjg5-srj-205-srj-206)). A CONFLICT or an unusable name met for a persona no longer configured in any other context goes only to the server log. Broken-persona failures, reload output and those exceptions never reach Slack.
  - **The human-only sentence.** Every command a notice names is CSCB's own text. A notice names a command when its rendered text holds a code span that opens with `agent-director` or `tmux`; every notice that names one, or points to agent-director's README "Operator actions", says it is for a human only and that no bot, including any persona that sees the post, may run them (the wedge warning, the kill-failure alert's ordinary version) or may act on it (`CONFLICT_NOTICE_HUMAN_ONLY_LINE`, `src/conflict-latch.ts`, which the not-connected notices also end with). The JSONL persistence safeguard's notices name no command and carry none (b.jg5 SRJ-122).
  - **No operator action of CSCB's own.** A notice points to "Operator actions" by that quoted title and never names or describes an operator action itself. No notice names a row delete, the finished-row kill flag, a tmux command that ends a session or pane or changes a label, a process kill, a session probe, a tmux target without `=`, or `clear-latch` (below). The CONFLICT, unusable-name, launch-start and stuck-launch posts name no command that ends a session. Only the kill-failure alert's ordinary version and the wedge warning name `agent-director kill`, as a human's step whose result is checked; the alert's survivor version names no command.
  - **agent-director's words stay its own.** A description quoted from agent-director (a CONFLICT's "no kill was sent", a kill failure's "retry kill later" and "never delete this row") is its text, not CSCB's, and does not count against the rules above. It goes through the redactor and is capped at `MAX_LOGGED_MESSAGE_LENGTH` (`renderLogMessageText`, or `redactSlackLogText` and the cap) before any Slack escape.
  - **One post per episode.** No notice about one condition on one persona is posted more than once per episode, apart from its single recovery post and alert and the stuck-launch post's two texts (`persona-episodes.ts`); the kill-failure alert's survivor version has no episode.
  - **Pinned by `tests/notice-texts.test.ts`**: one catalogue (`NOTICE_CATALOGUE`) holds every Slack notice's rendered text in every variant, every SRJ-10xx builder and every other notice the file names (`NAMED_SLACK_NOTICES`), and checks these rules over it, with one redaction-and-cap row per builder that quotes agent-director. A new Slack notice joins that catalogue, never a second one; the engineering guide says how.
- **Reload output stays local** (b.av2 SR-7.2, SR-8.3): the reload detection tick's output (the pending file, the preview lines, every detection line and every apply line) goes only to `config.json.pending` and the server log, never to Slack; nothing about a pending or applied change is posted or held as a notice. Neither the pending file nor any reload line carries a token, credentials content or a digest: credentials changes are named by persona and path only, the change plan they are rendered from holds no digest, an added persona's can't-come-up cause names keys and rules only (`credentialsReadProblem`), and the pending file's fingerprint is a SHA-256 over the files, from which no content can be read back. An `INVALID` line repeats the loader's error, which echoes no rejected value, no file text and no unknown key name that isn't a plain setting name (`ECHOABLE_KEY_NAME_RE`), so a token pasted into `config.json`, even as a key, never reaches either.
- **Slack validation outcome secrecy** (b.av2 SR-10.3 as amended by b.deo SRI-901 to SRI-906): outcomes from `src/persona-slack-validation.ts` carry only the class, the token key, the check, and the Slack error code or reason kind (plus an HTTP status or `retryAfter` number). The log lines `src/persona-slack-episodes.ts` builds from them carry those fields plus the persona reference (entry position, name and key) and the credentials-file path. Neither ever carries the raw error object, its message, the request, a header or a token value. The connection manager (`src/persona-connections.ts`) uses them. The Web API auth-failure watch (`src/persona-web-api-watch.ts`, bug b.ujn) copies only the Slack error code and the method name (only when it matches `SLACK_METHOD_NAME_RE`) from a rejected call; it never logs, stores or modifies the error, the caller still sees the original rejection, and its local refusal (`WebApiCallRefusedLocallyError`) carries only that code and method name.
- **Persona Slack client error secrecy** (b.av2 SR-3.3): no persona Slack client (`src/persona-slack-clients.ts`) attaches the original request, and so the Authorization header, to its errors. `attachOriginalToWebAPIRequestError: false` is set by every option builder, so on every client the connection manager builds: the short-lived validation client (`validationWebClientOptions`), the Socket Mode client's own Web API client for `apps.connections.open` (its `clientOptions`, from the private `validationRequestLimits()`: the validation client's limits without its logger), and the long-lived Web API client (`longLivedWebClientOptions`). A credentials reconnect builds its validation, Web API and Socket Mode clients through the same factory and option sets, so it adds no token surface; the new tokens are held like the old ones and replace them only at the swap (or at once for a retrying persona). The `persona-credentials-change-failed` line carries only the persona reference, the path and a token-free cause (a credentials-check cause or the Slack classifier's refused cause). The connection manager logs a thrown value only through `describeThrownValue` (constructor name, a short `code`, the message through `redactSlackLogText` as `message="…"`, stack frames), and the exported `unhandledRejection` handler (`src/persona-connection-errors.ts`) logs the same way, so neither writes a token value. `server.ts` installs the handler once in `main()`; the event router, `connectPersonaSlack` and the bring-up controller also log thrown values only through `describeThrownValue`.
- **Slack API endpoint override is loopback only**: every persona Slack client talks to the library's default Slack API, except when `CSCB_SLACK_API_URL` holds an `http://127.0.0.1…` or `http://[::1]…` URL (literal addresses; `localhost` is refused) with no user info, query or fragment (the integration suite's Slack stub). Any other value is ignored with a warning that does not echo it. The honoured line logs only the URL's origin. The persona tokens then go only to whatever listens on that loopback port, which is trusted with them. See Environment Variables.
- **Slack library logging** (b.av2 SR-10.3 as amended by b.deo SRI-901 to SRI-906): every persona Socket Mode client is built with `socketModeSlackLogger(persona, log)` (`src/persona-slack-clients.ts`) in place of the library's console logger, which `initLogging()` would route into `server.log`. Under Bun, a failed WebSocket handshake's error text holds the full WebSocket URL, and its `ticket=` query is a short-lived bearer for the app's socket, which the library prints at its default level; "Failed to retrieve a new WSS URL" prints whatever the Web API error says. So the logger passes an explicit list of permitted lines rather than filtering out unsafe ones: only whole lines matching the library's fixed-text ping/pong timeouts are forwarded as they are, and a failed ping is forwarded as `Failed to send ping to Slack` without its runtime error text. The socket client passes the logger on to its own `apps.connections.open` client (whose `clientOptions` carry none) and its WebSocket, so their lines go through the same list. The connection manager logs every connection failure itself, through `describeThrownValue`. The validation and long-lived Web API clients get `redactingSlackLogger()`: the token travels only in the Authorization header and they don't attach the original request, but a failed request's message can hold the request URL (a `filesUploadV2` upload URL is a short-lived bearer), and a runtime's header check could echo a header value, so every argument has URL-like text replaced by `<redacted-url>` and token-like text (a deliberately wide pattern) by `<redacted-token>` before it reaches the console.
- **Persona names and paths are echoed as written** (b.av2 SR-1.2 as amended by b.deo SRI-102, SRI-202; b.av2 SR-2.2): a persona's name and its key are shown everywhere a persona is named (log lines, loader errors, previews, Slack notices, tool results, agent-director labels, the instance ID and the tmux session name). A name has no format rule and is neither rejected nor masked: the operator chooses it, and it is not a credential. Persona paths (`credentials_file`, `working_directory`, `claude_config_dir`) and `ack_reaction` are echoed as written in errors and log lines for the same reason. Unknown key names are echoed only when they are plain setting names (`ECHOABLE_KEY_NAME_RE`), since a key could be a pasted token. Message content is archived and debug-logged unfiltered. Redaction covers exactly two things: the Slack libraries' own log output (the Socket Mode logger's list of permitted lines and `redactingSlackLogger` above, and `redactSlackLogText` inside every describer of a thrown value), and CSCB's own credentials, which no loader or credentials error echoes (a bad token is named only by its key and rule).
- **No token in any output** (b.av2 SR-10.3 as amended by b.deo SRI-901 to SRI-906; b.av2 AC 20): no log line, error, server-written file (`config.json.pending`, `config.json.last-applied`, `retired-keys.json`, which holds only keys, causes and times, `channel-delivery.json`, which holds only persona keys, names, paths, channel IDs, choices and times (b.deo SRI-402), `reply-guard/<key>`, `server.port`, which holds only a PID and a port, the permission trail), preview, Slack notice or MCP tool result carries a Slack token value, credentials content or a credentials digest. The last-applied record is a byte copy of a config file that passed the loader, which rejects unknown keys, and credentials live only in the credentials files. What persona, reload and apply output may carry:
  - the persona reference (entry position, JSON-quoted name and key), paths, class labels and fixed wording;
  - Slack error codes that are safe identifiers, and Web API method names only when they match `SLACK_METHOD_NAME_RE` (the `persona-credentials-refused` "Web API call" cause from `src/persona-web-api-watch.ts`, and `WebApiCallRefusedLocallyError`);
  - errno codes, in `persona-config-dir-unresolvable` (its cleared line carries none) and the JSONL check's "transcript not checked" line; the launch's "could not be resolved" line and the restart kill adapter's "not killing" line name only the persona and the setting;
  - thrown values only through `describeThrownValue` or `describeSlackCallFailure` (the teardown's "before its turn failed" line, the connection manager's reconnect failures); `persona-credentials-change-failed` carries a credentials-check or refused cause, never a thrown value; the `template refresh:` failure line carries an agent-director error's `errName` (only when it passes `isSafeIdentifier`) and its description as `message="…"` (`describeLogMessage`), or the `describeThrownValue` description of any other value (a typed error whose `errName` fails the check included).
  - every log line, startup-error record and notice on a Slack or agent-director path (the persona connections, the permission poller and click handler, restart, the UNAVAILABLE retry timer, the health check and its stat route, the outage state, the session manager's launches and orphan cleanup, the JSONL check, the CLI's teardown and `stop --stop-bots`, `isSessionAlive`) renders a thrown value through `describeThrownValue`, never the raw error or its raw message (b.av2 SR-10.3 as amended by b.deo SRI-901 to SRI-906): the message appears only as `message="…"`, through `redactSlackLogText`, on one line and capped at 300 characters (`describeLogMessage`). An agent-director `errName` is printed, by that describer or directly, only when it passes `isSafeIdentifier`; `describeAgentDirectorFailure` (declared once in `src/ad-error-class.ts`, imported by the session manager and the episode tracker, and re-exported by the permission poller for its click handler) renders `<errName> message="<description>"` with the description through `describeLogMessage`, and any other value through `describeThrownValue`. The resume path's `ErrInvalidFlags` line is built from the classifier's answer only (`describeAdErrorClassification`, `ad-error-class.ts`): the name only when it passes `isSafeIdentifier`, the message rendered by `renderLogMessageText`, the same rendering `describeLogMessage` quotes. The session manager's startup-error records (`spawn-failed`, `orphan-cleanup*`, `jsonl-transcript-lost-on-resume`, `jsonl-diagnosis-inconclusive`) carry that description in their message, never the error itself; the JSONL diagnosis's fallback description is redacted the same way. The spawn-failure notice posted to Slack shows the checked label and the redacted description, capped at 300 characters after redaction. The CLI's `stop --stop-bots` initialization-failed line (`describeCliFailure`) prints the message of a failure CSCB built (`StartupGateFailedError`) and describes anything else. The CLI teardown's report (b.jg5 SRJ-907, SRJ-909) carries agent-director's description only as `describeReportedAdFailure` renders it, redacted and on one line, in each failure line and its `cli-teardown-failed` entry and in each failed answer-check try's line, the not-restarted alert carrying no description at all, and the kill-failure alert's text only as `src/kill-failure-alert.ts` renders it (below), on the terminal, in `server.log` and in `startup-errors.log` alike; a failed write to either file is reported through `describeThrownValue`. The permission trail keeps `raw_error_message` for forensics (SR-V-2.7), redacted by `redactSlackLogText` before it is written;
  - deliberate exceptions, which print an error's own text (the `RAW_ERROR_ALLOWED` list of the source audit in `tests/secrecy-audit.test.ts`, each with its reason): the `[slack] Fatal:` catch-alls (`src/cli.ts`, `src/server.ts`), the only text of an unexpected start failure; the CLI's config-load lines (`stop`, `stop --stop-bots`, `clean_restart`, `credentials`), which carry the loader's token-free message and, for a record, its deletion hint; the boot template install's failure, recorded verbatim; the startup gate's message, which may embed agent-director's description or a construct error and is the same text the server writes to `startup-errors.log`; and paths that touch neither Slack nor agent-director (MCP roots and connect, the message archive's open, cron, permission trail and cron log writes, cozempic, the PID read, the Stop-hook and trust patches' catch-alls);
  - MCP tool errors name the persona, the target and at most a Slack platform error code. `set_channel_delivery`'s errors are the exception (b.deo SRI-503, SRI-506): they name the persona and, for an unreadable store or a failed write, the stored-choice file's path; they echo the `channel` given only when it matches `ECHOABLE_CHANNEL_RE` (1 to 24 characters from `A-Z0-9`) and the `delivery` given only when it matches `ECHOABLE_KEY_NAME_RE`, and otherwise say the value is not shown. The store's lines name keys, channel IDs, channel counts, paths and errno codes only, never a choice (Logging, [Stored-choice file lines](#stored-choice-file-lines-bdeo-sri-904-sri-905)). The lost-message notice carries, in every one of its states, fixed wording (`STATE_WORDING`) and the sender's label only.
  - The latch notices quote agent-director's description only as the latch record holds it: redacted, on one line and capped (`renderLogMessageText`), then escaped once for Slack (`escapeSlackControlCharacters`). This holds for the CONFLICT notice (b.jg5 SRJ-1004) and for the *Held: unusable tmux session name* notice (b.jg5 SRJ-1019, `unusableNameNoticeText` in `src/conflict-latch.ts`), whose description is the classifier's message, rendered the same way. The *Held: launch start not recorded* notice (b.jg5 SRJ-1020, `launchStartNotRecordedNoticeText`) quotes no description; its session name is rendered and escaped the same way. CSCB's own text in them names no session-ending command and no label option.
  - The kill-failure alert (b.jg5 SRJ-704, SRJ-1007; `src/kill-failure-alert.ts`) quotes agent-director's descriptions only through the redactor (`renderLogMessageText`: redacted, one line, capped), escaped once for Slack after that, and takes its pid list only from `survivorPids` (`src/ad-description-phrases.ts`), never from a pattern of its own. The agent-director commands its ordinary version names are a human's next step: the text says no bot, including any persona that sees the post, may run them, and points to agent-director's README "Operator actions" for anything beyond. The survivor version names no command, and nothing in CSCB acts on a pid it lists. Its log-only routes and the CLI teardown's route carry the same redacted text, unescaped, to `server.log` and `startup-errors.log` (the CLI's also to the terminal and, for `clean_restart`, `clean_restart.log`).
  - The *Cannot launch* alert (b.jg5 SRJ-1008; `INVALID_FLAGS_HOLD_ALERT_TEXT` in `src/invalid-flags-hold.ts`) is fixed text: it quotes no agent-director description and no version. The hold's lines show a version agent-director reported only as `describeHoldVersion` renders it (a short version string, else `unknown` or `unreadable`), and a thrown value only through `describeThrownValue`; `src/invalid-flags-hold.ts` is one of the secrecy audit's source surfaces.
